# PrizeDrawsDaily — social template rework: design specification
**Date:** 2026-09-17  
**Status:** Approved by the owner 2026-09-17. **In implementation** on branch `feat/social-template-rework`. The three build-blocking criticals are settled — see *Settlements* below.  
**Approved direction:** newsprint editorial with rail-blue standing chrome ("The Verdict + The Board's chrome"), chosen by the owner from three rendered options.
**How this was produced.** Five parallel research streams (Instagram carousel, Instagram Reels, Facebook, UK competitive teardown, UK visual direction), then three orchestrated drafting rounds: twelve sections drafted and adversarially verified; nine binding rulings to reconcile cross-section conflicts and a full rewrite against them; eight settlements for residual propagation errors and a final patch. Each round ended in an independent multi-lens audit. Findings fell 77 → 39 → 21, criticals 16 → 9 → 3.
> **Provenance rule used throughout:** claims are labelled OFFICIAL (a named platform/regulator source), MEASURED (a study, with its sample), or design judgement. Claims the research identified as folklore are named as such and not built on. Caveats on soft numbers are carried forward deliberately.

---

## Known open items
These survived the final audit. They are recorded here rather than silently fixed, because each needs a decision or a re-derivation that changes numbers elsewhere. **All three criticals are build-blocking and must be settled before implementation starts.** None reopens the approved design.

**Originally 3 critical · 10 major · 8 minor. Now 0 critical · 8 major · 8 minor.**

### Settlements — applied 2026-09-17, before implementation started
The three criticals are closed in the document itself, not in a side note. Each is recorded here with the edit that closed it, because all three were propagation failures and the propagation rule is the actual fix.

**S1 — Lane C, and the rule that stops it happening a fourth time.** Criticals 1 (consistency), majors 1, 2, 5, 8 and minor 1 were one defect wearing six labels: §8 typed a copy of a rect §6.3 owns, and §6.3 moved it. The rect has now moved three times — h 272 → 285 → 346, the last when §4.4 stacked E2 on every surface and took Row C from 195px to 256px — and every typed copy in this document was wrong after at least one move. **§6.3's chrome-rect table is the sole normative source and §8 now prints no Lane C literal anywhere.** As §6.3 stands: x 0…1080, **y 661 … 1007, h 346, 373,680 px² = 18.021%**, y_c 834. The consequent chrome constants are **607px = 31.615%** expanded, photograph floor **68.385%**, ceiling `chrome_area ≤ 32%` (614.4px, 7.4px headroom); §8's scene canvas is **6.042%** collapsed, **24.063%** expanded, **22.775%** time-weighted. Two superseded sets are retired by name so neither is verified against again: 533/27.76/72.24/73.25/`≤28%` and 546/28.438/71.563/72.62/`≤29%`, alongside the retired denominators 293,760 and 307,800.
⚠ **What S1 deliberately does not do.** §8.5's eight per-scene coverage and tone figures still carry the 307,800 denominator. They are **not** rescaled here, because rescaling is the wrong operation — a taller lane lengthens every vertical stroke and admits more horizontal rules, so the ink moves with the denominator and each figure has to be recomputed from the scene's geometry. They are marked stale in §8.5 and **blocked from deriving any G3, G5 or G7 threshold** until that recomputation lands. This costs nothing now: Lane C exists only on `reel-9x16`, no still consumes it, and the recomputation is Stage D work. Inventing eight plausible percentages to clear a critical would have been the worse outcome.

**S2 — the masthead stamp.** Criticals 2 (skeptic) and 3 (compliance-and-truth) and major 3 were one defect: §10.4 assigned its LONG stamp form to carousel masthead Slot B and checked the fit against a *bare* 950px track, but Slot A occupies 480.5px of that track, so the real overlap is **−224.1px** — a §5.2 build stop on slides 2–10 of every deck, on the primary growth surface, with no step-down escape because `--fs-micro` 34px is already T3's lowest legal step. **Slot B now carries the SHORT form** (`READ 09:04`, 204.0px @34, left edge x 811.0, clearing Slot A by 265.5px), licensed by §10.4's own rule since every surface's alt text carries the full sentence under §10.7. The long form keeps Story band 1, which has no second slot and retains §7.2's 52.4px of headroom. §10.4 now states the general rule that produced the error: **a slot's free measure, not the bare track, is the fit test.** §5.2's open question is closed.

**S3 — `--meta` was never defined.** Major 7. Four sections (§4.5, §4.8, §8.4, §8.5) consumed `var(--meta)` against a §3.7 `:root` that defines `--ink-meta`. For an inherited property that is not a loud failure: it silently inherits the parent's colour, which is the exact failure class §3.7's no-double-definition assertion exists to catch, in the one direction that assertion does not look. Renamed throughout to **`--ink-meta`** (28 occurrences). §3.7 gains a seventh constraint: every `var(--x)` in an emitted stylesheet must resolve to a property defined in a lifted block, asserted at build time beside the existing check.

**Still open and deliberately so:** the eight major and eight minor items below, minus majors 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 and minor 1, which S1–S3 close. None blocks a build. Major 9 (CAP 3.7 evidence for the Trust Score numeral) is folded into Stage 0a as a `rating_checked_at` column rather than resolved by dropping the chip.

### Critical — blocking
**1. §8.3 lane table, §8.5 (all eight scene entries), §8.8 G6 clause 1 and the share-of-frame paragraph**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** §8 carries a superseded Lane C. §6.3 is the declared sole normative source — "This table is the sole normative source for both lane rects" — and its current table reads "Insert card rows | 0 … 1080 | 661 … 1007 | 346", because §4.4's stacked-E2 ruling took Row C from 195px to 256px (8 + 240 + 8) and the union from 285px to 346px. §6.3 states the consequent lane areas itself: "Lane areas: R = 1080 × 116 = 125,280 px² = 6.042%; C = 1080 × 346 = 373,680 px² = 18.021%; 498,960 px² = 24.063% combined." §8.3 still prints "Lane C (card) — §6.3's insert-card rect — currently x 0…1080, y 722…1007" and "1080 × 285 = 307,800 px² = 14.844%", and §8.8's G6 clause 1 pins the fixture card "to its expanded height, y 722…1007". This is not a cosmetic lag: every coverage and tone figure in §8.5 is computed against the 307,800 px² denominator and against 285px-tall vertical strokes (house 15,105.5 px² → 4.907%; home-garden 12,713 → 4.130%; car 7,905 → 2.568%; tech 1,573.50 → 0.511%; luxury 1,690 → 0.549%; collectibles ≈3,639), so all eight are wrong in both numerator and denominator. §8.3's derived box table is wrong for Lane C too: y_c = T + 5·round(H/10) gives 661 + 5·round(34.6) = 836, not the published 867, so tech's anchor centre line and every Lane C materialisation move. G6 clause 1 as written pins a card height the renderer no longer produces, so the loop-closure gate compares a fixture against geometry that cannot occur — it fails or passes vacuously on every build. §8.8's derived scene canvas (125,280 + 307,800 = 433,080 = 20.885% expanded, 19.825% time-weighted, ≈0.59% painted ink) is the same generation behind, and §6.3 already publishes the corrected pair (24.063% expanded, 22.775% time-weighted, ≈0.68% ink).
- **Fix:** Re-transclude Lane C from §6.3's current row and re-derive. §8.3's lane table: x 0…1080, y 661…1007, h 346, 373,680 px² = 18.021%, printed as a transclusion with the pointer, never as a typed number — which §8.3's own rule already requires ("no §8 section prints a lane literal"). §8.3's derived box table: Lane C H 346, y_c 836. §8.8 G6 clause 1: pin the fixture card to y 661…1007. §8.8's share-of-frame paragraph: scene canvas 498,960/2,073,600 = 24.063% expanded, time-weighted 22.775%, painted ink ≈0.68% — the figures §6.3 already publishes. §8.5: recompute every Lane C ink total against 346px strokes and the 373,680 px² denominator (house re-derives to ≈20,478 px² ≈ 5.48%, still inside the 6% ceiling but 0.57pp higher than published; home-garden, car, collectibles and tech all move), and re-check that house remains the heaviest and tech the thinnest before either superlative is restated. §8.5's B-relative crests (house 922/962 on Lane C) are unaffected because B is still 1007 — say so, so nobody re-derives them unnecessarily.
**2. §10.4 (stamp forms table) vs §5.2 (masthead Slot A/Slot B)**  _(found by: skeptic)_
- **Problem:** §10.4 assigns the LONG dated-stamp form to the carousel masthead — "| Long | `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` | 34 | 693.6px @34 · **897.6px @44** | Carousel masthead Slot B; Story band 1 |", and its propagation paragraph repeats it: "§5.2 and §7.2 the long form, §6.3 the short". §10.4 checks that form against a BARE 950px track ("the long form fits the 950px chrome track at either size") and never re-derives the masthead, where Slot A occupies 480.5px of it. §5.2 does the measurement and lands on a build stop: "**At the long form the two slots overlap by 224.1px, and §5.2's own rule is that where they would collide the build fails rather than shrinking either.** The short form clears by 265.5px." Arithmetic confirmed: Slot A `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` Inter 700 44px +0.08em = 480.5px, ending x 545.5; long form 34 glyphs × 20.4px (`--fs-micro` 34 × measured 0.600em) = 693.6px right-aligned to x 1015 → left edge x 321.4; 545.5 − 321.4 = 224.1px of overlap. Slot B is suppressed on slide 1 only, so on an ordinary 10-slide deck this fires on **slides 2–10, every run**. §5.2 logs it as an open question and states it cannot choose ("§10.4 must assign the short form here or delete Slot A"), so the spec as delivered ships a known, unresolved class-A failure on the primary surface — the one gate that genuinely stops a deck rendering.
- **Fix:** Change the Renders-in cell of §10.4's LONG row to "Story band 1" only, and the SHORT row to "Reel and Reel-cover top-rail right slot; **carousel masthead Slot B**; the cover's dateline (§5.4)". The short form is already licensed here by §10.4's own rule ("permitted only on a surface whose alt text carries this sentence — which is every surface, per §10.7") and clears Slot A by 265.5px (`READ 09:04` = 10 × 20.4 = 204.0px, left edge x 811.0 against Slot A ending x 545.5). Then delete §5.2's open question, publish the measured clearance (65 + 480.5 = 545.5 against 1015 − 204.0 = 811.0, gap 265.5px), and add the masthead to §10.4's consequences paragraph beside the Story band-1 and Reel rail re-derivations so the omission cannot recur.
**3. §10.4 (stamp forms) × §5.2 (masthead)**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §10.4 assigns its LONG stamp form to the carousel masthead and defends the fit against a bare track: "| Long | `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` | 34 | 693.6px @34 · 897.6px @44 | Carousel masthead Slot B; Story band 1 |" … "At a measured 0.600em the long form fits the 950px chrome track at either size." The masthead is not a bare track — Slot A occupies 480.5px of it. §5.2 measures the consequence: "§10.4 long … 693.6px | x 321.4 | −224.1px — collides" and "At the long form the two slots overlap by 224.1px, and §5.2's own rule is that where they would collide the build fails rather than shrinking either." I re-derived it: Slot A ends x 545.5; 1015 − (34 × 20.4) = x 321.4; gap = −224.1px. §5.2 raises it as an open question and explicitly declines to decide; §10.4 as delivered does not resolve it. So the delivered spec specifies a class-A build failure on every still slide except slide 1 — the primary growth surface does not render at all.
- **Fix:** §10.4 assigns the SHORT form (`READ 09:00`, 204.0px at `--fs-micro`, left edge x 811.0, clearing Slot A by 265.5px) to carousel masthead Slot B, keeping the long form for Story band 1 where §7.2 measures 52.4px of headroom. Add one sentence to §10.4's stamp table stating that a slot's occupancy, not the bare track, is the fit test, and re-check Story band 1 on the same rule. Close §5's first open question in the same edit.

### Major
**1. §8.8, share-of-frame paragraph**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** §8.8 quotes retired §6.3 constants and then asserts that another section is the only one still carrying them. It says "chrome 261/1920 = 13.594% collapsed and 546/1920 = 28.438% expanded, photograph floor 71.563%, time-weighted photograph 72.62%, assertable constant chrome_area ≤ 29%", labelled "Those constants are §6.3's and are quoted here, not owned", and then states the superseded set "was computed on §10.2's 272px card and is retired here; §10.2 is now the only section still carrying it." §6.3 as delivered supersedes that generation too: "§4.4's E2 ruling then set Row C to the stacked 240px module in a 256px row, giving 346px, 607px, 31.615% and a 68.385% floor, under a 32% ceiling. §8.8 quotes this table; §10.2's 28% / 72.24% and the interim 29% / 71.563% are both retired." §6.1 rule 6 is likewise now 32% / 614.4px, not 29%. So §8.8 attributes to §6.3 a set §6.3 has retired, and its closing claim that §10.2 is the sole remaining holder is false — §4.4, §9.3 and §10.4 hold it as well.
- **Fix:** Replace the quoted set with §6.3's current constants: collapsed 261px = 13.594% (unchanged), expanded 116 + 346 + 145 = 607px = 31.615%, photograph floor 68.385%, ceiling `chrome_area ≤ 32%` = 614.4px, and re-derive the time-weighted photograph figure from §6.4's 112 BPM configuration rather than carrying 72.62%. Delete the sentence naming §10.2 as the only holder and replace it with a list of the sections that must re-derive (§4.4, §9.3, §10.4), or drop the claim entirely — §8.8 is not the owner of who else is stale.
**2. §4.4, "Which surfaces carry which encoding" — the Reel refusal**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** §4.4's three reasons for refusing the band on the Reel are all computed on the retired 285px card. It states "§6.3's Reel chrome puts the top rail at y 269 … 385 and the insert card at y 722 … 1007 — a 285px card across two rows, with a clear photograph window of y 385 … 722 = 337px" and "§6.3's expanded chrome is 116 + 285 + 145 = 546/1920 = 28.44% against §6.1 rule 6's 29% ceiling. 28.44 + 15.32 = 43.76%." §6.3's current figures are a 346px card, a 276px clear window (y 385 … 661 — §6.3 states the change explicitly: "the clear photo window, which falls from 337px to 276px"), 607px of chrome at 31.615%, and a 32% ceiling. The conclusion survives and in fact strengthens (a 350–355px band fits a 276px window even less well than a 337px one, and 31.615 + 15.32 = 46.94%), but §4.4 publishes four numbers that no longer describe the surface it is reasoning about, and it attributes all of them to §6.3.
- **Fix:** Re-derive §4.4's Reel paragraph against §6.3's current rects: insert card y 661 … 1007 (346px), clear photograph window y 385 … 661 = 276px, expanded chrome 607px = 31.615% against §6.1 rule 6's 32% ceiling, and 31.615 + 15.32 = 46.94%. State the numbers as transclusions of §6.3 (as §4.4 already does in wording) so the next Row C change propagates automatically, and add the one-line note §10.4 already carries: if Row C grows again the refusal only gets stronger.
**3. §10.4 (stamp forms and slots) against §5.2 (masthead)**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** Two sections state incompatible things about the same slot and only one of them knows. §10.4 assigns its long form to "Carousel masthead Slot B; Story band 1" and checks it as "34 | 693.6px @34 · 897.6px @44", concluding "At a measured 0.600em the long form fits the 950px chrome track at either size, and the build steps down one step on overflow and fails if neither fits." That is a fit against a bare 950px track. §5.2 measures the slot it actually lands in: Slot A is `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` at Inter 700 44px + 0.08em = 480.5px ending at x 545.5, so the long form right-aligned to x 1015 starts at x 321.4 and "the two slots overlap by 224.1px", against §5.2's own rule that a collision fails the build rather than shrinking either. The step-down escape does not exist: `--fs-micro` 34px is already the lowest legal step for this slot under §3.5's T3. §5.2 raises it as an open question and defers to §10.4; §10.4, as the owner, does not acknowledge it and publishes a bare "fits". Left as is, the masthead cannot render on any inner still.
- **Fix:** §10.4 assigns the SHORT form (`READ 09:04`, 10 glyphs = 204.0px @34) to carousel masthead Slot B — §5.2 measures it starting at x 811.0 with 265.5px of clearance — or explicitly deletes Slot A and keeps the long form. Either way, qualify §10.4's fit sentence: the long form fits a bare 950px track, and Slot B's real measure is 1015 − (65 + 480.5 + gap), not 950. Story band 1 is unaffected: it carries no second slot, and §7.2's 897.6px / 52.4px headroom stands.
**4. §3.2 / §5.13 / §5.14 / §10.5 rule 3 — the Trust Score chip's ground**  _(found by: skeptic)_
- **Problem:** §3.2, the owner of colour semantics, has ruled: "**PDD's own computed assessments are not green.** The Trust Score is a PDD-derived rating... it renders in `--ink` on `--ground` with a `--rule` border, and the mint tint is not used behind it. This closes the collision between §3.2's absolute green rule, §5.13's mint-and-green chip and §10.5 rule 3's hard fail". §5 has not propagated it. §5.13 still specifies "the **Trust Score chip**: `PDD 4.2`, JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-micro`, `--ink` on `--verdict-tint`" and offers as its fallback "`--ink` on `--verdict-tint` with a 1px `--rule` border"; §5.14's consumed-token table still lists "`--verdict-tint` #E6F2EA | The Trust Score chip's ground". §10.5 rule 3 reads "Verdict green `#0F6B45` and mint `#E6F2EA` only on **a figure whose row satisfied §10.4's eligibility predicate**", and §10.8 makes a breach class A. A Trust Score satisfies neither §3.2(a) nor (b), so a chip rendered on mint is a class-A hit on **every draw slide and the count slide** — 8 of 10 assets on an ordinary deck. §10.5's stated block ("§3.2 widens... or §5.4 and §5.13 restyle") is now half-discharged in a way neither branch anticipated: §3.2 restyled on §5's behalf rather than widening, so the gate's enabling condition is ambiguous and a builder reading §5.13 renders the failing colour.
- **Fix:** Edit §5.13 to read "the **Trust Score chip**: `PDD 4.2`, JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-micro`, `--ink` on `--ground`, 1px `--rule` border, 6px radius, 6px/14px padding", delete the "⚠ The chip's border colour is unresolved" paragraph and its fallback, and change §5.14's row to "`--verdict-tint` #E6F2EA | not consumed by §5 — §3.2 reserves it for a block of §10.4-evidenced facts". In §10.5, replace the enabling condition with: "§3.2 has resolved this by restyling the chip (ink on ground, `--rule` border) rather than by widening the green rule; §5.4's proof-line figures are covered by §3.2(b) `drawsRendered` and §3.2(a) minimum cap. Rule 3 therefore enables with the §5/§6/§7 rewrite." Keep §10.5's separate note that G4's per-region tone baselines must be re-derived against §8's moved areas before calibration.
**5. §8.3 / §8.5 / §8.8 — Lane C and the Reel chrome constants, stale against §6.3**  _(found by: skeptic)_
- **Problem:** §6.3 is the normative source for both lane rects and has moved the insert card: with E2 stacked on every surface, Row C goes 195 → 256px and the card union becomes "**y 661 … 1007, h 346**", with the explicit instruction "§8.8's G6 clause 1 pins the fixture card to **y 661 … 1007**, not 722 and not 735." §8 still carries the superseded card everywhere: §8.3's lane table prints "§6.3's insert-card rect — currently x 0…1080, y 722…1007 | newsprint | 1080 × 285 = **307,800 px² = 14.844%**" — which also violates §8.3's own rule that "no part of §8 prints a lane coordinate as a typed number"; §8.8's G6 clause 1 repeats "pinned to its expanded height, **y 722…1007**"; §8.8's share-of-frame paragraph quotes "expanded chrome 116 + 285 + 145 = **546px of 1920 = 28.438%**", a 71.563% photograph floor and a `chrome_area ≤ 29%` ceiling, all of which §6.3 has replaced with 607px / 31.615% / 68.385% / ≤32%; and §8.8's own derived figures (scene canvas 20.885% expanded, 19.825% time-weighted, ink ≈0.59%) are computed on the 307,800px² lane against §6.3's 24.063% / 22.775% / ≈0.68%. Every per-scene coverage and tone figure in §8.5 (house 4.907%, home-garden 4.130%, car 2.568%, collectibles ≈1.18%, luxury 0.549%, tech 0.511%) is computed against the 307,800px² denominator and against stroke lengths measured on a 285px lane. No gate fails — all figures move further under their ceilings — but §8.5 publishes eight wrong numbers, §8.8's G3/G5 calibration rests on them, and the one literal §8.3 forbids is the one that went stale.
- **Fix:** In §8.3's lane table, replace the Lane C cell with a transclusion carrying no digits — "§6.3's insert-card rect (currently y 661…1007, h 346) → 1080 × h" — and add the computed area as a derived line beneath the table rather than inside it. In §8.8 G6 clause 1, change "pinned to its expanded height, y 722…1007" to "pinned to §6.3's current expanded insert-card rect". In §8.8's share-of-frame paragraph, replace the quoted §6.3 constants with 607px / 31.615% / 68.385% / ≤32% and re-derive §8's own four figures on Lane C = 1080 × 346 = 373,680px² (expanded scene canvas 24.063%, time-weighted 22.775% at 112 BPM, painted ink ≈0.68% at a 3% in-lane mean), and retire the 307,800 / 14.844% / 20.885% / 19.825% set by name as §8.8 already does for the 533px set. Re-derive every §8.5 coverage and tone figure on the 346px lane — the vertical strokes lengthen, so each is recomputed rather than rescaled.
**6. §5.10 × §10.6a Part 1**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §5.10 renders `WE LIST DRAWS. WE RUN NONE.` as "The frame's single `--fs-hero` node" and hands the string upward: "The headline above is likewise §10.6a's to ratify; §5 states only its role and its measure." §10.6a did not take it. Part 1.2b adds the closing-slide SUB-LINE only; the L1 export list is "`capFigure(n)`, `eyebrow()`, `conditional(cap)`, `legendFull(cap)`, `legendClipped(cap)`, `annotation(shown, cap)`, `proofLine(...)`, `headline(...)`, `stampLong(t)`, `stampShort(t)`, `closingSubLine()`, `signOffStrapline()`" — no closing headline. It is not in the banned list either, and §10.6a's CI grep gate only catches `ODDS`, `1 IN`, `TICKET CAP`, `SELL-OUT`, `TICKETS MAX`, none of which it contains. So the largest text element on one of ten slides is authored outside the allow-list, outside the frozen fixture, and outside the conformance test — which falsifies the claim that every rendered string sits in the permitted table. (The same class, lower stakes: §5.9's `DRAW n OF N` counter chip has no allow-list entry or owner either.)
- **Fix:** Add `closingHeadline()` to `oddsCopy`'s exports and the permitted string `WE LIST DRAWS. WE RUN NONE.` to §10.6a Part 1.2b beside the sub-line, with its measured line-box wrap on the 950px closing track (§5.10 runs the full chrome track). Add it to the frozen fixture and to `allowlist-conformance.test.mjs`'s fact-sets. Do the same for the counter chip, or state in §10.6a that fixed-structure chrome counters are out of the table's scope and name their owner.
**7. §4.5, §4.8, §8.4, §8.5 vs §3.7**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** Four sections consume a colour token named `--ink-meta` that §3.7 does not define. §4.5: "| Annotation | `--ink-meta` `#5A5F66` | 5.91:1 |". §4.8's slot table: "JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-label` 44/50, `--ink-meta`, right-aligned to x 960". §8.4's derived-alpha table carries a `--ink-meta` `#5A5F66` row, and §8.5 uses it throughout. §3.7's `:root` block defines `--ink:#14161A; --ink-meta:#5A5F66;` — there is no `--ink-meta`. `color: var(--ink-meta)` with no fallback is invalid at computed-value time and, for an inherited property, silently inherits the parent's colour. This is the exact failure class §3.2 documents for `--rail-meta` ("An undefined custom property does not throw: `var(--rail-meta)` resolves to an invalid value and the run inherits its parent's colour, silently, on the one element the ASA position makes non-negotiable") — and here it lands on the CAP 8.20/8.21 correction carrier and on §8's whole scene ink model, whose per-pixel alpha caps are derived from that hex. §3.7's six token constraints include a no-double-definition assertion but no undefined-reference assertion.
- **Fix:** Global rename: `--ink-meta` → `--ink-meta` in §4.5, §4.8, §8.4 and §8.5 (or, if §3 prefers the shorter name, rename in §3.7 and propagate). Add a seventh constraint to §3.7: every `var(--x)` in any emitted stylesheet must resolve to a property defined in a lifted block, asserted at build time beside the no-double-definition check — it is the same one-line cost and it catches the direction the existing assertion does not.
**8. §8.3, §8.5, §8.8 vs §6.3**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §6.3 moved Lane C a third time and says so: "the ruling that E2 is stacked on every surface takes Row C from 195px to 256px and the union to y 661 … 1007, h 346" and "§8.8's G6 clause 1 pins the fixture card to y 661 … 1007, not 722 and not 735." §8 has not propagated it. §8.3's lane table still reads "Lane C … y 722…1007 | 1080 × 285 = 307,800 px² = 14.844%"; all eight §8.5 coverage/tone figures are re-derived against 307,800 (house 4.907%, cash 4.19%, home-garden 4.130%, car 2.568%, collectibles 1.18%, luxury 0.549%, tech 0.511%); §8.8's G6 clause 1 says "pinned to its expanded height, y 722…1007", directly contradicting §6.8; and §8.8's share-of-frame paragraph quotes the retired interim §6.3 set ("546/1920 = 28.438% expanded, photograph floor 71.563%, time-weighted photograph 72.62%, assertable constant `chrome_area ≤ 29%`") against §6.3's current 607 / 31.615% / 68.385% / ≤32%. §8.3's own rule forbids this: "No part of §8 prints a lane coordinate as a typed number, and a lane that cannot be computed from §6.3 or §7.1 is a build error." The correct denominator is 1080 × 346 = 373,680 px² = 18.021%, so every §8.5 percentage is overstated by ~21% and the ink sums themselves move (vertical strokes lengthen, an extra horizontal rule enters most fields).
- **Fix:** Re-derive §8.3's lane row, all eight §8.5 coverage/tone figures and §8's decisions list against Lane C = y 661…1007, h 346, 373,680 px² = 18.021%, recomputing ink rather than scaling the denominator. Correct §8.8's G6 clause 1 pin to y 661…1007 and replace the quoted §6.3 chrome constants with 607px / 31.615% / 68.385% / ≤32%. Re-derive §8's own scene-canvas figures (expanded canvas, time-weighted canvas, painted-ink ≈0.59%) from the same rect, and add the retired 285/307,800/14.844% set to the by-name retirement list beside the 293,760 one so nobody re-verifies against it a third time.
**9. §5.13 × §10.4 × CAP 3.7**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §5.13 renders "the Trust Score chip: `PDD 4.2`, JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-micro`" on every draw-carrying slide, sourced from `operators.rating` (measured span 3.0–4.8, one NULL). That is a published numeric objective claim about a named third party, and CAP 3.7 requires documentary evidence held before publication. The spec builds an entire evidence apparatus for `total_entries` — §10.4's three columns, method enum, 48-hour window, selection predicate, MODEL re-check, and the wording law that `read from` is the only permitted verb — and none for `rating`. The two places the chip is discussed address only its colour: §3.2 ("PDD's own computed assessments are not green") and §5.13's own unresolved border question. There is no freshness rule, no stored method, no statement of what the score is a score of, and no on-asset or alt-text qualifier telling a viewer it is PDD's own assessment rather than a measured or third-party figure. §5.13 also calls it "the strongest 'adds material value' signal PDD has", which increases rather than reduces the substantiation exposure.
- **Fix:** Either (a) §10.4 extends its contract to `operators.rating` — a stored method and `rating_checked_at`, a freshness window, and an alt-text sentence of the form `PDD Trust Score 4.2 out of 5, PDD's own assessment, last reviewed <date>` — or (b) §5.13 drops the numeral from the frame and the score stays on-site only. If it ships, the chip must also carry a one-word attribution so the numeral cannot read as an operator-sourced or third-party rating; `PDD 4.2` already does half that work but says nothing about scale or basis. Record the decision in §10.4 rather than in §5.13, since §10.4 owns evidence.
**10. §10.6a 1.2 (`absurd-comparison`) × CAP 8.20/8.21 emphasis**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** The permitted forms are "long `{cashAlt} FOR A {price} TICKET.` / short `{cashAlt} FOR {price}.`", rendering as `£52,000 FOR A 79p TICKET.` at `--fs-hero` 150px — the largest element on the cover. The cover carries no odds figure for that draw: §5.4's board has Index/Prize/Closes columns and no cap, and the proof line's `Lowest ticket cap of the 8: 699` is the deck minimum, which is a different draw. So the frame states the upside at hero size with no probability attached to it. Nothing constrains this: §10.6 predicate 3 fires only on a unit containing `?`, and §10.6a's own ban list forbids "`only` and `just` before a cap figure — emphasis that creates an untrue overall impression" while permitting the same impression to be built by juxtaposition without the adverb. CAP's page-design guidance ("should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true") and 8.21 both bite on a value-to-stake ratio presented with no denominator. The spec is meticulous about second person and superlatives and silent on this arm beyond its data provenance.
- **Fix:** Bind the arm to its own draw's evidence: on an `absurd-comparison` day, the proof line must name the cap of the draw the `cashAlt` came from (`Ticket cap on that draw: 4,999.`) rather than the deck minimum, and §10.6 predicate 3's unit rule extends to fire on any `--fs-hero` unit containing a currency figure, not only on `?`. If that cannot be made to fit §5.4's three-line ceiling, retire the arm and let it fall through to `price-anchor` permanently — §10.8 already counts that fallback, and the arm renders on roughly 20% of selections anyway.

### Minor
**1. §9.3 and §9.11**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** §9 carries the retired Reel photograph floor. §9.3 states "§6.3 owns the photograph's share of the Reel frame and puts it at no less than 71.563% of every frame (546 px of expanded chrome out of 1920)", and §9.11 repeats the pairing. §6.3's current constants are 607px of expanded chrome and a 68.385% floor; the 86.406% open-window figure §9 also quotes is unchanged (collapsed chrome is still 261px), so only half of each citation is stale.
- **Fix:** Update both citations to 68.385% / 607px, keep 86.406% as is, and keep §9's existing caveat that the constant is §6.3's construction rather than a read of Meta's classifier. None of §9's floors move — the binding demands are still 1920px of height and 1080/1353px of width — so this is a citation correction with no arithmetic consequence downstream, and saying so in §9.3 prevents someone re-deriving the master cap.
**2. §10.4, "The stamp does not become a fourth conditions-band line"**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** The height half of the refusal is argued on retired constants: "§6.3's expanded chrome is 116 + 285 + 145 = 546px of 1920 = 28.438%, against its assertable ceiling chrome_area ≤ 29% = 556.8px — 10.8px of headroom … A 190px band takes chrome to 591px = 30.781%, over the ceiling by 1.781pp = 34.2px." At §6.3's current 346px card the arithmetic is 607px = 31.615% against a 32% ceiling = 614.4px, so headroom is 7.4px (which §6.6 independently states) and a 190px band reaches 652px = 33.958%. §10.4 already anticipates the direction ("If §6.3's Row C grows again, the chrome figure grows and this refusal only gets stronger"), so only the figures need moving.
- **Fix:** Restate as: expanded chrome 607px = 31.615% against §6.1 rule 6's 32% ceiling (614.4px), 7.4px of headroom; a 190px band takes chrome to 652px = 33.958%, over by 1.958pp = 37.6px. The Story half (883px exactly, over by the full 45px) is unaffected and needs no edit.
**3. §10.2, "38px is a named exception to §3.5's eight-step scale"**  _(found by: consistency)_
- **Problem:** §10.2 argues against a superseded §3.5 and demands an edit that has already landed. It says "The type-scale ruling proposes that this field resolve to 34px on a still and 44px on video; as the band's owner this section overrides that for this band only" and "unless 38px is enumerated as this band's exception, the type gate fails every asset on day one." §3.5 as delivered already carries `--fs-legal` 38px/45px as a ninth step, scoped verbatim to "The conditions band, on every canvas, and nothing else", lists 38 in T3's enumeration (150 / 120 / 88 / 68 / 56 / 48 / 44 / 38 / 34), and describes the scale as "eight display steps plus one legally-scoped step". The paragraph reads as a live blocker that no longer exists, and a builder chasing it goes to the wrong file.
- **Fix:** Rewrite the paragraph as a statement of the settled position rather than an override: 38px/45px is §3.5's `--fs-legal`, scoped by §3.5 to this band and enumerated in T3, and §10.2 owns only the measured fit that justified the step (44px puts L2 at 1,032.4px and L3's `none-stated` state at 1,059.4px against 950). Delete the "proposes 34px/44px" characterisation and the day-one-failure sentence.
**4. §8.3 — the count-slide scene region**  _(found by: skeptic)_
- **Problem:** §8.3's region table publishes "| Count slide | 1,458,000 − (324,000 + 65,130 + 810,000 − 48,750) = **307,620 px²** | **21.10%** |", computed on §5's pre-ruling 750px odds rect. Its own next paragraph then says the figure is a render-time computation and gives the real values under §4.4's bottom-anchored column: 745px rect at the 24-row ceiling → 312,695px² (21.45%), 740px in the clipped default state → 317,770px² (21.79%), 415px at the measured minimum cap of 99 → 647,645px² (44.42%). §5.7 records the same re-derivation. So the number §8 publishes as the count slide's region corresponds to **no state the count slide ever renders in** — and the default state (clipped, per §4.2, on roughly three days in four and on every car-draws day) is the one it is furthest from.
- **Fix:** Replace the Count-slide row's single figure with the clipped-default value as the headline — "**317,770 px² / 21.79%** (clipped default); 312,695 / 21.45% at the 24-row ceiling; 647,645 / 44.42% at the measured minimum cap" — and mark the row "computed from the descriptor at render (§4.4's bottom-anchored column), not frozen", matching the treatment the following paragraph already gives it. Delete the 307,620 / 21.10% pair by name so it is not re-verified against.
**5. §4.8 (annotation slot) × the CAP correction carrier**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** The carrier is present and legible — mandatory in the clipped state, its own 50px row, 44px mono, 5.91:1 on newsprint, ≈15.9 CSS px in feed, and a draw whose annotation cannot be composed is dropped rather than the row. But the stated CAP defence contradicts the shipped configuration. §4.8 rejects a smaller step partly because "a correction carrier set smaller than the legend it corrects is precisely the 'layout, design or format' de-emphasis CAP names and §10.5 rule 1 forbids" — and then ships the annotation at `--fs-label` 44px against a legend at `--fs-body` 48px. 44 < 48. The decision survives on its other ground (§3.5 T3 scopes 38px to the conditions band), but as written the rationale indicts the thing it is defending, which is the weakest possible footing for the one element whose job is to correct a picture that is 6.9× more favourable than the fact.
- **Fix:** Either state the compensating measurement — JetBrains Mono 700 at 44px against Inter 400 at 48px, giving cap-height and stroke-weight figures — and rest the defence on perceived prominence rather than type step, or rest the 38px rejection on §3.5 T3 alone and delete the de-emphasis clause. Do not leave both sentences standing.
**6. §10.2 and §5.14 vs §3.7**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** Both sections raise `--rail-meta` as an unowned token and instruct §3 to adopt it. §10.2: "`#B9C6D6` has no owner and must acquire one … `--rail-meta` `#B9C6D6` is not in it … §3.7 must add `--rail-meta: #B9C6D6` to its `:root` block." §5.14: "⚠ One token has no owner … has no definition in §3.7's block at all." §3.7 as delivered defines it — `--rail:#14385F; --rail-ink:#F7F5F0; --rail-meta:#B9C6D6; --rail-accent:#FFC53D;` — and §3.2 documents its 6.88:1 on rail, its 9.63:1 on the late rail, and its paper prohibition at 1.59:1. The instruction is discharged and both flags are stale. §12.1 names this exact failure mode ("an instruction to fix something already fixed sends a builder to the wrong file and spends the credibility of the MEASURED claims around it").
- **Fix:** Delete the ⚠ block from §5.14 and the "has no owner and must acquire one" paragraph from §10.2, replacing both with a one-line reference to §3.7's definition and §3.2's two prohibitions. Keep §10.2's measured 6.87:1 as a cross-check and note it agrees with §3.2's 6.88:1 to rounding.
**7. §10.3 vs §10.4**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §10.3's ban is written wider than its own reasoning supports: "in v1 no time of day renders anywhere — not in §10.2's L1, not in §6.3's Row A, not in §7.2. Everything is date-only." §10.4 mandates a rendered time in the opposite direction: the stamp forms are `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` and `READ 09:00`, and "the timestamp is mandatory", with "'checked by Prize Draws Daily' without a timestamp banned outright". §10.3's argument is entirely about a stated CLOSING time asserting a response deadline under CAP 8.22 and DMCC 2024 ("a rendered `CLOSES SUN 9PM` asserts a response deadline exactly as a ticking `04:12:38` does"), which has nothing to say about a past-tense read-at stamp. A builder reading the literal sentence strips the stamp's time and breaks §10.4's wording law.
- **Fix:** Scope §10.3's sentence: "no time of day renders anywhere as part of a closing or drawing claim — not in §10.2's L1, not in §6.3's Row A, not in §7.2. §10.4's read-at stamp is a past-tense observation time, is mandatory, and is out of scope of this ban."
**8. §5.7 (closes chip) × CAP 8.22 / DMCC 2024**  _(found by: compliance-and-truth)_
- **Problem:** §5.7 ships an urgency element with no specified string: "The closes chip survives as a photo overlay on slides 3+. Bottom-left of the photo well, x 65, `--rail-ink` on `--deadline`. It follows the Wowcher 'Wow Week' pattern … It renders only when the stored `draw_date` is within 48 hours." The gating rule is right and the arithmetic is sound (MIN_DAYS=1 confines it to the 24–48h band). But no section states what it says. §10.2 owns the band's close string; §10.3 owns the ladder and adds a `kind` argument to `closesLabel()` precisely because `draw_date` is a draw time, not an entry close, so an ungated chip could render `CLOSES TONIGHT` over a row that is a draw date. §10.6a's table does not contain it. This is the element CAP 8.22 and the DMCC false-urgency provisions target most directly, and it is the only urgency device in the spec whose wording nobody owns.
- **Fix:** State in §5.7 that the chip renders `closesLabel(draw, kind)` output verbatim under §10.3's ladder — so a draw-date-only row shows `DRAWN …` and never `CLOSES …` — and add the chip's permitted strings to §10.6a Part 1.2 so they sit inside the fixture and the conformance test with everything else. One line in each section.

## Binding decision registry
Each entry names the one section that owns the decision. Every other section references it rather than restating it — restatement was the defect that produced the first two audit rounds.

### C3 + C5 — The gutter, and re-deriving every coordinate in §5 (and §8's scene-region areas) from it

**Owner:** §3.5 — "The type scale". It is the sole normative owner of `--gutter` (65px), the 950px chrome track (x 65…1015) and the 895px content well (x 65…960). No other section publishes a gutter or a track width. §5 publishes only derivations and must show the sum from §3.5's two numbers beside each one; §4.4 continues to own the band (895px at x 65…960) derived from §3.7's `--dot-size`/`--dot-gap`, and §3.5 carries a one-line pointer saying it sized the well to that band rather than the reverse; §8 computes scene-region areas from the rects §5 supplies and publishes no coordinate of its own.

**`--gutter: 65px`. Confirmed, on every canvas. 70px is retired and may not be restated anywhere. §3.5 is the sole owner; every number below is a derivation and is published with its sum.**

THE TWO TRACKS (both from §3.5, both unchanged by this ruling — §5 now matches them)
- **Chrome track = x 65 … 1015 = 950px.** Identical on 1080×1350 and on 1080×1920. It IS Meta Safe Box A's width, so the still and the Reel/Story share one constant.
- **Content well (still slides that carry §5.9's sheet edge) = x 65 … 960 = 895px.** This is §4.4's band width to the pixel.
- **Closing slide** (no sheet edge) runs on the full 950px track, per §3.5's own 9:16 rule.

WHY 65 AND NOT 70 (the three constraints that actually decide it)
1. **Box A.** At 65 the chrome track is Box A itself (950 = 1015 − 65). At 70 it is 940px at x 70…1010 — safe inside Box A but a *different* number from the 9:16 track, so §5 carries 940 while §6/§7 carry 950. Two tracks is the exact drift that produced 64/65/70 in the first place.
2. **The band is not a free parameter.** 60×10 + 59×5 = 895px is forced by `--dot-size`/`--dot-gap` (§3.7). At 65 the well is 895 and the band fills its column: left-aligning and centring are the *same placement*, so the origin question (x 70 vs x 92.5) has nothing left to decide. At 70 the band is 45px narrower than its 940px column (35px narrower than a 930px well) and a centred origin at x 92.5 is permanently re-derivable by any author. C1/C3/C5 are that residual.
3. **The crop does not decide it.** Both clear x 33.75…1046.25. 65 gives 31.25px of headroom, 70 gives 36.25px — a 5px difference on the one slide the crop ever touches, against a permanent second track and a permanently reopenable band origin. 65 and 70 both sit on the 5px grid, so that argument kills only 64.

THE DEFINITION THAT MUST CHANGE (this is the propagation error, not the gutter)
§5.1 defines the content well as *"the gutter to §5.9's sheet-edge hairline"*. At 65 that would give 950 and contradict §3.5's 895. **The well is no longer defined by the sheet edge. The well is §3.5's 895px column (x 65…960); the sheet-edge hairline sits at x 1015 and a deliberate 55px right margin (1015 − 960) lies between them.** Nothing text-bearing crosses x 960: every left edge is 65, every right-aligned text edge is 960. Only two things cross it — the photo well (a bleed element, bounded by the hairline) and the two full-bleed chrome bands (which run type on the 950px track because the sheet edge exists only in y 180…1182, between them).

EVERY §5 COORDINATE AND WIDTH, OLD → NEW

| # | Item | §  | Old (g=70) | New (g=65) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Side margin / content origin | 5.1 | x 70 | **x 65** |
| 2 | Crop headroom, slide 1 | 5.1 | 36.25px | **31.25px** |
| 3 | Chrome track | 5.1, 5.3, 5.10 | 940px, x 70→1010 | **950px, x 65→1015** |
| 4 | Content well | 5.1, 5.4, 5.7 | 930px, x 70→1000 | **895px, x 65→960** |
