§8 SCENE-REGION AREAS, RE-DERIVED (only the horizontal terms move; every rect height is unchanged)
- Sheet-edge rect: x 1015–1080 × y 180–1182 = **65,130 px²** (was 80,160).
- Photo-well rect: **1015 × 500 = 507,500 px²** (was 500,000); one-line variant **1015 × 550 = 558,250** (was 550,000).
- **Cover: 754,220 px² = 51.73%** (was 743,840 / 51.02%).
- **Draw slide: 241,645 px² = 16.57%** (was 238,840 / 16.38%); one-line prize name **190,895 px² = 13.09%** (was 188,840 / 12.95%).
- **Count slide: 307,620 px² = 21.10%** (was 303,840 / 20.84%).
- **Closing: 1,134,000 px² = 77.78% — unchanged** (no sheet edge on that slide).
- §8.4's ceilings are percentages of the region, so **no gate threshold moves**; §8.5's cash ghost is geometry-derived (34.907% × 12% = 4.19%) and is unaffected. §8.5 already publishes no lattice of its own; where the registry's C1 text still says the ghost is "895px wide at x 70 … 965", read **x 65 … 960**.

WHAT STOPS FITTING AT 65 — two things, both resolved here
1. **The cover board's three columns.** 895 is 35px short of 930. The fixed-width figure column must not absorb it (a date like `SUN 21 SEP 26` is 13 glyphs × 20.4 = 265.2px and needs its 292px). **Allocation: Index x 65, gap 54 → Prize x 119…648 (529px) → gap 20 → Closes x 668…960 (292px). 54 + 529 + 20 + 292 = 895 exactly.** The Prize column is the one that already truncates at a word boundary to a measured line, so it is the correct place to spend the 35px.
2. **§10.6a's "no word > 10 glyphs" headline constraint.** At `--fs-hero` 150px and §3.4's measured Bricolage 800 mean of 0.6740em a glyph is 101.1px, so 9 glyphs = 909.9px and 10 = 1,011px — both over 895 (and 10 was already over 930, so this is a pre-existing error the narrower well exposes). **The cap becomes ≤8 glyphs per word at `--fs-hero`: 8 × 101.1 = 808.8px ≤ 895, with 86px of margin.** GATE CHECK: every string in §10.6a's table passes — longest words are `TICKETS` (7), `TICKET.` (7), `SUNDAY.` (7), `£52,000` (7) and, in the short forms, `TICKETS?` (8). The cap rejects nothing that exists, so it cannot fire on an ordinary run. The binding gate remains the render-time line-box measurement against 895px; the glyph cap only constrains what §10.6a may author.

Everything else is unchanged or strictly better: the conditions band's ~49-character L1 gains 10px of track (940→950); the masthead's Slot A/Slot B clearance improves from 61.5px to **70.8px** (1015 − 408 − (65 + 480.5)); the counter chip's worst case `DRAW 10 OF 12` is 305px at x 65, ending x 370; §4.4's annotation (33 glyphs), legend (788.4px max) and figure (648.0px) were all already sized against 895.

THE BUILD GATE
One assertion, beside `assertTypeContract()`: the renderer asserts `--gutter` resolves to **65px** and that the two constants it lays out against are **950** and **895**; the existing measured-fit / `scrollWidth > clientWidth` checks then run against 895 (well), 950 (chrome bands and the closing slide) and 1015 (photo well). **A per-node "every left edge = 65" assertion is explicitly NOT adopted** — it would fail on the board's own Prize (x 119) and Closes (x 668) columns and on the chips, i.e. on every legitimate run, and would be switched off in a week.

**Residual risk:** 1. **Nothing at this geometry has ever been rendered.** §5.8's caveat still holds and now covers every x-coordinate in the deck: the 895px well, the x 65 band origin, the 65px on-frame sheet strip and the 31.25px crop headroom all need eyeballing at 1012.5px profile-grid width and at in-feed size before the numbers are treated as proven.

2. **5px less crop headroom on slide 1, forever.** 31.25px instead of 36.25px, i.e. 3.09% of the surviving width. It is the one thing 70px was genuinely better at, and it is paid on the single most important slide. Accepted because the cost is 5px on one slide against a permanent second track and a permanently re-derivable band origin — but if a render shows the cover's left edge reading as cramped in the grid, the correct response is to inset slide 1's headline only, never to move the gutter.

3. **The 55px right margin is new and unrendered.** Text stops at x 960 while the photo bleeds to x 1015 and the chrome bands run to x 1015. The page reads 65px of left paper against 55px of right paper — a 10px asymmetry that is the closest a band-sized well can get to symmetric, but it is a judgement no one has looked at. It is also the coordinate most likely to be "corrected" back to 1015 by a future author who does not know the well is band-sized; that is why §5.1's definition change is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

4. **The board's Prize column loses 35px (564 → 529, −6.2%).** It truncates at a word boundary to one measured line, so it degrades gracefully, but the truncation rate on the cover board will rise by an amount nobody has measured against the 880 live titles. If it reads badly, the next 35px comes from the Closes column only after someone measures the longest real closing-date string.

5. **The ≤8-glyph word cap rests on a MEAN advance.** §3.4 is explicit that a mean describes no real word — `I` and `W` differ by 3.3× in Bricolage 800 — so an 8-glyph word of wide caps could still overflow 895px and a 9-glyph narrow word would fit. The cap is a design constraint on what §10.6a may author; the only gate is the render-time line-box measurement. It passes every string in today's table, so it will not fire on an ordinary run, but it is not a proof.

6. **§8's region areas moved by +1.2 to +1.4 percentage points.** Every §8.4 ceiling is a percentage of the region, so no threshold moves — but G4's tone baselines are per-region means and must be re-derived against the new denominators before the gate is calibrated, or the first run will compare a new region against an old baseline.

7. **This ruling touches no vertical budget.** §4.4's count-slide column (675 fixed + ≤355 band = 1,030 of 1,050) and §5.7's competing table (680 + 370) still disagree by 5px, §4.4 states a 565px photograph where §5.7 states a 500px minimum, and the hero-figure tier (120 vs 150) is still open. Those are a different cluster; if any of them moves a rect height, §8's four region figures re-derive from the same four subtractions rather than being edited.

### C1 — the count-slide block table and the E2 module height: one table, one owner (§4.4)

**Owner:** §4.4 — "Geometry — the normative specification". It is and remains the sole normative source for the count-slide vertical budget (every block height and every gap on slide 2), the E1/E2 surface assignment, and the E2 module height on all three surfaces. §5.7, §5.8, §5.9, §6.3, §7.2 and §8.5 reference §4.4 and publish no height of their own.

§4.4's table is ratified as the single count-slide block table and §4.4's E2 is ratified as the single E2 height. §5.7's competing table is deleted outright. Every figure below is binding.

THE COUNT-SLIDE BLOCK TABLE (carousel slide 2, no photograph, E1). Content well y 132 → 1182 = 1050px. Column left edge x 65, band x 65 … 960 (895px), per §4.4 and §3.5's gutter.

| # | Block | h | Type / source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Counter chip row `DRAW n OF N` | **70** | chip sets at `--fs-label` 44/50 → 50px line box + 10px padding top and bottom. NOT `--fs-micro` — §3.5 T3 reserves 34px for the conditions strip and the dated stamp only. |
| 2 | gap | 10 | |
| 3 | Operator lockup | **45** | §5.13 |
| 4 | gap | 10 | |
| 5 | Prize name, Bricolage 800, two measured lines at `--fs-title` 68/70 | **140** | §3.5 |
| 6 | gap | 20 | |
| 7 | Eyebrow `TICKET CAP`, Inter 600 `--fs-label` 44/50 | **50** | §10.6a string |
| 8 | gap | 10 | T4 lockup gap, ≤10px, no node between |
| 9 | Hero figure — bare cap, JetBrains Mono 700 `--fs-figure` 120/120 | **120** | §3.5 hero-figure floor |
| 10 | gap | 10 | |
| 11 | **Band, 895 × H** | **≤ 355** | §4.4 lattice; ceiling 24 rows |
| 12 | gap | 10 | |
| 13a | Annotation row, JetBrains Mono 700 `--fs-label` 44/50, right-aligned to x 960 — **CLIPPED STATE ONLY** | **50** | §4.8 slot; ≤33 glyphs |
| 13b | gap — clipped state only | 10 | |
| 14 | Legend, Inter 400 `--fs-body` 48/60 — **3 lines full (180) / 2 lines clipped (120)** | **180 / 120** | §10.6a |

FIXED (all blocks except the band) = **675px in both states**. Available for the band = 1050 − 675 = **375px**.
CEILING = **24 rows = 1,440 tickets, H = 355px full, 350px clipped** (R=25 would give H=370 and only 5px of slack, which is not a budget on a column whose prize name is measured at render).
The column is BOTTOM-ANCHORED: the legend's last line box ends at y 1182 and all residual space pools as newsprint air above the chip row. There is no y 132 chip origin on the count slide and no conditional layout.

THE E2 MODULE — ONE HEIGHT, stacked, never side-by-side:
eyebrow 50 + gap 10 + figure 120 + gap 10 + conditional (Inter 600 `--fs-label` 44/50, one line) 50 = **240px on the carousel draw slide and on the Reel**. On the Story only, the figure sets at `--fs-hero` 150/150 (§3.5 T2, the Story's single anchor), so E2 = **270px**. There is no provenance row in E2 (deleted by §4.9) and no legend (no lattice to explain). 305px, 145px figure blocks, 45px eyebrow/qualifier rows and 65px chip rows do not exist anywhere in the spec.

THE PHOTO WELL ON A DRAW SLIDE (slides 3 … N+1). The photo well is the flex residual; the counter chip on these slides is a photo OVERLAY at x 65, y 164 and costs zero vertical budget. Photo = 1050 − 20 − 45 − 20 − P − 20 − 240 = **705 − P**, where P is the prize-name block:
- **Two-line prize name** at `--fs-title` 68/70, P = 140 → **photo well = 565px** (the binding minimum; clears §5.7's own 500px floor by 65px).
- **One-line prize name** at `--fs-display` 88/90, P = 90 → **photo well = 615px**.
- (Intermediate, for completeness: two lines at `--fs-lead` 56/60, P = 120 → 585px.)
No change to §5.7's 500px photo floor is required, and §4.4's parenthetical about "a 40px operator lockup gaining a further 5px" is struck — the lockup is 45px, §5.13 owns it, and there is one value.

THE BUILD GATE, and it passes on the ordinary run. The renderer asserts (a) the rendered column sums to ≤ 1050px and (b) on slides 3+, photo ≥ 500px, failing the build otherwise in the style of `render.mjs:193`. Full count slide 1030 ≤ 1050 ✓ (20px air). Clipped count slide 1025 ≤ 1050 ✓ (25px air). Draw slide 1050 ≤ 1050 ✓ at the worst-case two-line title, photo 565 ≥ 500 ✓. Minimum measured cap 99 (R 2, H 25): 700 ≤ 1050 ✓, chip-row top y 482. The band can never overflow by construction: R is capped at 24 and the clip is fixed at 350px, so block 11 is bounded before it is measured. The only measured-at-render block is the prize name, and it is capped at two lines by §5.7's fitting ladder.

WHAT §5.7 IS PERMITTED TO SAY INSTEAD. §5.7 keeps slide assembly and row contents and states no height, no gap, no ceiling, no module total and no photo-well arithmetic of its own. Permitted, in full:
1. That there are two layouts — Layout 1, the count slide (slide 2 only), which carries no photograph and whose residual space is newsprint air above the chip row; and Layout 2, draw slides 3 and after.
2. The ORDER of blocks in each layout, as a list with no numbers: Layout 1 = counter chip row → operator lockup (§5.13) → prize name → eyebrow (+ annotation row, clipped state only) → hero figure → odds band → legend. Layout 2 = photo well → operator lockup → prize name → E2.
3. What each row CONTAINS and where it comes from: chip reads `drawsRendered` (§5.11) and counts draws not slides; lockup is §5.13's; prize-name strings are §5.12's after `cleanTitle()`; every odds string is §10.6a's; the band's geometry, rows, height, ceiling and clipped/full state are §4.4's and §4.7's.
4. The prize-name FITTING RULE — Bricolage 800, step down §3.5's ladder, first size that fits in at most two measured line boxes, truncate at a word boundary with a trailing ellipsis if the smallest step still needs a third line — and the measured title distribution behind it.
5. That the photo well is the flexible element and every other block is fixed by content, with the sentence "the resulting photo well is §4.4's figure" and a cross-reference, not a number.
6. Everything already in §5.7 that is genuinely §5's: the no-decoration rule (no card frame, glow, podium or ribbon), the closes chip as a 48h-gated photo overlay, the deleted price chip, the scene-mount exclusion rects handed to §8, and the 1000 × 550 normalised-master requirement handed to §9.
Forbidden in §5.7 from now on: any block height, any gap value, any "Fixed = …" sum, any band allowance, any E2 total, any figure-block or chip-row height, and the y-coordinate of the count slide's chip row.

**Residual risk:** 1. THE CLIPPED STATE'S ANNOTATION ROW IS A GATE THAT CURRENTLY FAILS ON A LEGITIMATE DRAW, and the clipped state is the common case — §4.2 puts roughly three quarters of the payload above the ceiling, and on a car-draws day it is every draw. My table reserves the 50px row and §4.8 fixes its capacity at ≤33 glyphs of JetBrains Mono 700 at 44px (871.2px of 895px). Neither string in circulation fits both requirements: `1,440 OF 9,999 SHOWN · NONE MARKED` is 34 glyphs and overflows by 2.6px, and `1,440 SHOWN · 8,559 NOT SHOWN` fits but never mentions the mark. §4.8 has already measured a form that fits in both states — `1,440 OF 9,999 · NONE MARKED` (28 glyphs, 739.2px) and `1,440 OF 4,500,000 · NONE MARKED` (32 glyphs, 844.8px). §10.6a must ratify that or a shorter variant IN THE SAME CHANGE that lands this table, or the build fails on the ordinary run and somebody switches the assertion off. That string is §10.6a's to choose; the slot is now fixed and will not move again.

2. NOTHING AT THIS GEOMETRY HAS EVER BEEN RENDERED. The only artefact is `merged.mjs`'s 10.95px fractional-cell mockup at cap 699. The 70px chip row, the 24-row ceiling, the bottom-anchored column with up to 350px of air above the chip, and the half-disc cut at device row 700 all need eyeballing at in-feed and profile-grid size before the ceiling is locked. The half-disc in particular is ~5px tall at feed scale and may read as a soft edge rather than a cut.

3. THE COUNT SLIDE HAS 20px OF SLACK AT THE CEILING AND THE DRAW SLIDE HAS ZERO. Slides 3+ close at exactly 1,050 of 1,050 with the photo well as the flex residual, so any block added anywhere pushes the photograph below its 500px floor at 66px of new content — one extra 44/50 line plus a gap, and three of §5's own candidates (a price chip, a Delta 1 kicker, an on-slide provenance line) are exactly that size. If the next 20px is ever needed on the count slide it comes from the chip-row and lockup gaps, not from the band.

4. THE 70px CHIP ROW IS A TYPE-SCALE CONSEQUENCE, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE. Forcing the counter off `--fs-micro` makes it visually heavier than §5.9 intended — a 44px mono chip 70px tall sitting above a 45px operator lockup. It is the correct call under §3.5 T3, but it should be looked at in the render; if it dominates, the fix is padding (§4.4's, 10px each side, could go to 5px for a 60px row and 10px more air) and not a return to 34px.

5. I HAVE NOT RE-MEASURED EVERY WIDTH AGAINST THE NEW STEPS. The eyebrow moved 45 → 50 and the E2 qualifier 45 → 50 as line boxes, not as type sizes, so no width changes — but §10.6a still publishes an eyebrow at Inter 600 48px and a figure at 150px on the carousel, and until it is rewritten to §3.5's steps its pass/fail margins are computed against sizes this spec no longer permits.

6. THE BAND STILL APPEARS ON ONE SLIDE IN TEN, AND THE GREEN DOT ROUGHLY ONCE A WEEK. This ruling does not change that, and it is the device's biggest brand cost. It is recorded here only so nobody reads "the table closes" as "the device is proven".

### C2 — the Story's odds figure size and the §7.2 band table

**Owner:** §7.2 — "What a 9:16 Story carries". It is the sole normative source for the Story's five band heights, their y-ranges, the gutters, and band 4's 245px envelope with its five rows. It publishes no type size of its own: the figure is §3.5's `--fs-figure` 120/120, the lockup is §4.4's E2 240px, the strings are §10.6a's and band 5's 145px is §10.2's, each cited and not republished. §3.5, §4.4, §4.11, §10.2 and §10.6a reference §7.2 for the Story table and state no Story band height, no Story E2 height and no Story figure size.

The Story's odds figure sets at `--fs-figure` 120/120 (JetBrains Mono 700, tabular, `#14161A`), exactly as on the carousel draw slide and the Reel. There is no per-surface figure size anywhere in the spec: one shared odds module emits E2 at one size on all four surfaces, and it takes no surface parameter. E2 on the Story is therefore §4.4's 240px of type, unchanged: eyebrow `TICKET CAP` (Inter 600 44/50, `#5A5F66`) 50 + 10 gap + figure 120 + 10 gap + conditional `1 IN <cap> AT SELL-OUT` (Inter 600 44/50, `#5A5F66`) 50. The 270px Story variant of E2 is deleted, and §3.5's T2 is scoped: T2 asserts `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame, zero is legal, and the Story carries zero — the Story is the one surface whose largest node is `--fs-figure`.

THE BINDING §7.2 BAND TABLE (Box A, x 65…1015, w 950, y 269…1152, h 883; five bands, four 5px gutters):

| Band | y | h | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Dateline | 269–324 | 55 | `CHECKED 09:00 · WED 17 SEP`, JetBrains Mono 700 44/50, `#5A5F66` (50px type, 5px slack). Carries the run-level checked-at stamp (§10.2 put it here). |
| — gutter | 324–329 | 5 | |
| 2 Prize | 329–474 | 145 | `cleanTitle()`, Bricolage 800 68/70, max 2 lines, `#14161A` (140px type, 5px slack) |
| — gutter | 474–479 | 5 | |
| 3 Photo | 479–752 | 273 | normalised operator photo, full 950 width, 3.48:1 |
| — gutter | 752–757 | 5 | |
| 4 Odds lockup (E2) | 757–1002 | 245 | eyebrow 757–807 · gap 807–817 · figure 817–937 · gap 937–947 · conditional 947–997 · 5px slack 997–1002 |
| — gutter | 1002–1007 | 5 | |
| 5 Conditions | 1007–1152 | 145 | §10.2's band verbatim: 5 + 135 (3 lines Inter 38/45) + 5. Class A: fail, never shrink. |

Band 3's 273px is not a squeeze — it is the arithmetic maximum the surface can give the photograph, so no band gives anything up and the CAP 8.17 slack is not touched. 150/150 is refused because it is payable only out of band 3 (photo → 243px, 3.91:1), and a 3.91:1 slice of an operator photo on the one surface that ships as a still is a worse loss than 30px of numeral on a frame where the figure already outranks the prize name 120:68 = 1.76:1 — which is the ratio §4.11's added-value argument actually needs. Build assertion (renderer, in the style of `render.mjs:193`): Σ(band heights) + 4×5 === 883, every band's rendered content height ≤ its band height, and band 5 never re-measured downward. Recovery rule, so 150 cannot creep back: if §10.2 ever cuts the conditions band to two lines, the 45px returned goes to band 3 (photo 318, 2.99:1); if Meta's 35% bottom exclusion proves correct, Box A's extra 96px also goes to band 3 (photo 369, 2.57:1). Neither ever goes to the figure.

**Residual risk:** 1. The photograph is the thing that pays, and it is still punished. 3.48:1 at 950×273 is a hard crop, and this ruling only refuses to make it 3.91:1 — it does not fix it. Ingest-time normalisation (§9) is doing more work on this surface than anywhere else in the spec, and an unnormalised operator collage sliced at 3.48:1 is unreadable. The two real recoveries (a two-line conditions band, or Meta's 35% bottom exclusion) both sit outside §7 and are worth 45px and 96px respectively.

2. Nothing at this geometry has been rendered. A 120px figure over a 273px photo band on a real handset at feed scale is unverified, exactly as the dot grid and the half-disc cut are. If 120px reads as merely large rather than as the frame's anchor, the hierarchy argument for putting the odds above the prize name on this surface weakens — and there is no way to measure it: the Story has no metric in the pipeline today (§11.2's `ig_story_insights` is proposed, not built).

3. The Story is now the only surface in the system with no `--fs-hero` node. That is legal under the scoped T2 and it is intentional, but it means the four surfaces no longer share a common top tier, and a future author reading only §3.5's scale table will reach for 150 on a single-frame surface again. The defence is the assertion and §7.2's single ownership, not the prose.

4. I did not reconcile the two measured Inter advances (0.6602 vs 0.6782em) — that is §3.5's. Every width in this ruling clears under the wider of the two with at least 174px of headroom, so no verdict here moves either way, but the mean-based 775.9px figure in §7.2 is a conservative bound, not a measurement, and §4.4's 619.8px real-advance number is the better one.

5. The band-5 floor is the whole budget's single point of failure. If §10.2's three lines ever need a fourth, or 38px is ruled illegible and goes to 44px (135 → 150+ of type), band 3 pays again and the crop passes 3.6:1. At that point the honest move is to drop the photograph from the Story entirely rather than keep slicing it, and that is a §7 decision this ruling does not pre-empt.

### C6 + C7 — the clipped-state annotation string: making the device's default state renderable

**Owner:** §10.6a (Compliance — the permitted-wording table for odds copy). It is the sole normative source for the annotation's exact rendered string, in the ownership split the registry itself already ruled: §10 owns every rendered string, §4 owns no string. §4.8 owns the slot only — its type, colour, alignment, row position and its 33-glyph measured capacity — and publishes no candidate string. §4.4, §4.7, §4.9, §5.3, §3.5 and the registry all reference §10.6a and restate nothing.

SHORTEN THE STRING. The annotation is `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED`.

`{shown}` is §4.7's ceiling, en-GB grouped, always the literal-by-derivation `1,440` (5 glyphs). `{cap}` is `draws.total_entries` en-GB grouped (≤9 glyphs, guaranteed by §3.5 T4). Nothing else in the string is variable. The words `SHOWN` and the explicit not-shown count are struck from the row; `NONE MARKED` is kept, because §4.7 requires the absence of the mark to be stated in words on the slide and CAP 8.20/8.21 exposure comes from the mark, not from the subtraction.

Slot, unchanged from §4.8 and re-confirmed as binding: JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-label` 44/50, `--ink-meta` `#5A5F66`, 0 tracking, right-aligned to x 960, one line, its own 50px row directly beneath the band with a 10px gap above, present in the clipped state (`cap > 1,440`) only. No type-step change, no tracking change, no second line, no widened slot, no shrink-to-fit.

The three required renders (band left-aligned x 65…960, measure 895px, 26.4px per mono glyph at 44px — MEASURED: every glyph in the bundled `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2`, the only mono weight in the repo, advances exactly 0.600em):

• 1-in-599 — cap 599 ≤ 1,440, so this is the FULL state and THERE IS NO ANNOTATION ROW AND NO ANNOTATION STRING. R = ceil(599/60) = 10, H = 15×10 − 5 = 145px, green dot drawn, legend 3 lines. Column = 675 + 145 = 820 of 1,050 → fits, 230px of newsprint air above the chip row.
• 1-in-9,999 (median cap) — `1,440 OF 9,999 · NONE MARKED` = 28 glyphs = 739.2px of 895px. FITS, 155.8px spare.
• 1-in-13,995 — `1,440 OF 13,995 · NONE MARKED` = 29 glyphs = 765.6px of 895px. FITS, 129.4px spare.
• 1-in-4,500,000 (the true measured maximum; the brief's "13,995 maximum" is the range §4.2 already corrected, and a string sized only to 13,995 would still fail on live inventory) — `1,440 OF 4,500,000 · NONE MARKED` = 32 glyphs = 844.8px of 895px. FITS, 50.2px spare.

THE GATE NOW CANNOT FIRE ON LEGITIMATE INVENTORY, AND THAT IS A PROOF, NOT A SAMPLE. The string's fixed cost is 23 glyphs; the only variable is `{cap}`, which §3.5 T4 caps at 9 glyphs (a 10-glyph cap ≥ 10,000,000 drops the draw at the figure node, class B, before the annotation is ever composed). Worst case is therefore 23 + 9 = 32 glyphs = 844.8px ≤ 895px. §5.3's measured-fit rule stays hard-failing and keeps its build-refusal posture; it simply has no reachable failure state here. The row is mandatory whenever the sheet is clipped — §4.8's "what degrades gracefully if the row has to be dropped" fallback is deleted; if the row ever cannot render, the DRAW is dropped, not the row.

The count slide's clipped column closes unchanged at 1,025 of 1,050 with 25px of slack, so the default state — which §4.2 measures as what renders on every car-draws day and roughly three days in four — renders and passes the ≤1,050 build assertion.

What is given up, and where it now lives: the explicit not-shown count. §4.9's clipped alt text keeps it in full ("8,559 dots are not shown and no dot is marked green") and becomes its sole normative home; §10.6a's clipped legend L2 (`Odds at sell-out: 1 in {cap}.`, Inter 400 48px — a larger step than the annotation) keeps the true denominator in running copy directly beneath the row.

**Residual risk:** 1. The reader must subtract. `1,440 OF 9,999` states the shown count and the true denominator but not the 8,559 that are missing. The arithmetic is trivial and the alt text spells it out, but a viewer who glances and does not subtract takes away a smaller sense of the gap than the fact. This is the price of a 33-glyph slot and a 9-glyph maximum cap; no string carries shown, not-shown and the no-mark statement inside that budget.

2. Dropping SHOWN opens a misreading. `1,440 OF 9,999` with no verb could be read as a sell-through progress figure — which would be a fabricated fact and a §10.6 deny-list class ('sold', 'remaining'). The mitigations are contextual rather than measured: the eyebrow `TICKET CAP` and the 120px cap figure sit immediately above, and clipped legend L1 `Each dot is one ticket.` sits immediately below and binds the unit. The CI fixture must therefore also assert the clipped legend is exactly those two lines, so the annotation is never orphaned by a later legend edit. Nobody has tested this reading on a real viewer.

3. Nothing at this geometry has been rendered. 44px mono right-aligned under a severed 350px sheet is untested at feed scale, and the row's job is to be read. It must be eyeballed at in-feed size before the ceiling is locked, alongside the half-disc cut.

4. The margin is 50.2px at the worst case, not a comfortable one. If §3.5's content well ever drops below 844.8px, or if §4.7's ceiling grows past 9,999 (6-glyph `{shown}`, 33 glyphs, 871.2px — still inside, but that is the last glyph available), every figure here must be re-measured.

5. The device is still blocked on §10.4's provenance columns. This settlement makes the default state renderable; it does not make it lawful to render. Stage 0 (§12.4) is unchanged.

### C8 — §10.6 mechanic predicate 3 (the two-figure test) vs §10.6a 1.2 (the permitted `question` headline forms)

**Owner:** §10.6 (G5 — Wording bans). It is the sole normative owner of mechanic predicate 3: its trigger, its unit definition per surface, the `figure` regex, the `facts` key list, the distinct-key requirement and the class. §10.6a keeps ownership of the STRINGS only and carries the amended `question` row plus the new CI conformance gate. §5.5, §5.4, §7.10, §10.1 and §10.8 reference §10.6 and restate none of it.

THE PREDICATE WINS AND STAYS ON EVERY HEADLINE; ITS EVIDENCE UNIT IS CORRECTED FROM THE STRING TO THE RENDERED UNIT. THE ALLOW-LIST IS ALSO AMENDED, TO ONE PERMITTED QUESTION STRING THAT CARRIES A VERIFIED FIGURE. NO L1 EXEMPTION IS GRANTED — an exemption keyed on "emitted by oddsCopy.headline()" would auto-exempt every future allow-list entry, which is how a gate rots.

(1) §10.6 mechanic predicate 3 is replaced verbatim by:

  3. Two-figure test (evidence-unit scoped). Fires on any rendered text UNIT whose text CONTAINS "?" — contains, not ends with, so a headline cannot evade by trailing a full stop. The unit must carry at least two figures with DISTINCT fact keys from the run's verified-facts table. Class A (§10.8) on failure, unchanged.
     A "figure" is a maximal match of /[£$]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?[pk%]?/ in the unit's text whose normalised value equals the string form of a value in `facts`. Word-numbers ("THREE", "EIGHT") never count — which is why §10.6a's `deadline` form `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUNDAY.` is untouched: it carries no "?" and no digit, and the rule does not fire on it.
     `facts` is frozen at the MODEL stage, written to `selection.json` and printed in full by `brief.mjs`: `drawsRendered` (§5.11) · `caps[]` (every deck cap) · `prices[]` (every deck `ticket_price` as `priceLabel()` renders it) · `daysToClose[]` (every deck days-to-close). DISTINCT KEYS means two matches drawn from two differently-named facts; two caps do not satisfy it.
     THE UNIT, by surface:
       • cover headline → the cover slide's model, `normalizeWhitespace(headline + " " + proofLine)`. The proof line is a fixed, mandatory 120px block rendered 34px below the headline (§5.4) and is generated, never authored.
       • any other rendered string → that frame's own model text.
       • caption, FB caption, alt text → the single sentence containing the "?" — UNCHANGED, because a caption sentence has no adjacent rendered evidence.
     The unit differs by surface because the evidence does. This is §7.10's own principle made machine-checkable: "a permissible question is one whose answer is in the post; an impermissible one is a question whose answer is only in the reader."

(2) §10.6a 1.2's two `question` rows are replaced by ONE permitted string, with no long/short pair:
       `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`   rendering at today's deck as   `8 DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`
     `{n}` is interpolated from `drawsRendered` (§5.11), never a literal. `oddsCopy.headline('question', form, facts)` ignores `form`; `carousel_posts.hook_archetype` logs `question:only`. Both current strings are banned by name: `HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?` (breaks to FOUR line boxes — unrenderable under §5.5's 3-line gate at every candidate track, dead independent of C8) and `HOW MANY TICKETS?` (zero figures on the frame itself).

(3) NEW CI gate, §10.6a Part 2 L1, gate 3 — `carousel/tests/allowlist-conformance.test.mjs`: every string `oddsCopy` can emit, across the fixture's boundary fact-sets (n = DRAWS_MIN…8; caps 99 / 699 / 1,440 / 9,999 / 4,500,000; prices 79p / £2.99 / £12.50; days 1…7), is run through EVERY L2/L4 predicate — `secondPerson`, `unboundedComparative`, mechanics 1–3, `bannedPhrases` — in the same unit the renderer will present it in. An allow-listed string that any predicate rejects fails the TEST JOB. After this, an allow-list entry and a predicate can never again disagree in production. This is the structural fix; the string edit is only the instance.

WHAT THE PREDICATE STILL CATCHES: every caption sentence containing "?" with fewer than two distinct-key figures — including PDD's own archived, verified violation "Which would you pick?" (zero figures, class A); any generated caption question that implies a flattering answer with nothing to check; and a cover regression in which the headline carries "?" while the proof line is absent, empty, or figure-less (the exact failure the rule was written for). It no longer fires on a question whose evidenced answer is rendered 34px beneath it.

COMMON-CASE CONFIRMATION: on a `question` day the unit is `8 DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS? 8 draws closing within 5 days. Lowest ticket cap of the 8: 699.` → keys {drawsRendered, daysToClose, cap} = 3 ≥ 2. PASS. On §10.6a's stated fallback proof line `8 draws closing within 5 days.` → keys {drawsRendered, daysToClose} = 2. PASS. At the degraded floor `5 draws closing within 1 day.` → 2 keys. PASS. On the other three archetypes no "?" is present and the rule does not fire. The gate fires on ZERO legitimate runs; the old rule hard-failed 91 of them a year.

**Residual risk:** 1. THE COVER RUNS AT ITS TIGHTEST LEGAL VERTICAL ON QUESTION DAYS. Three line boxes start at y 244, 47px below the dateline, against 197px on a two-line day and 347px on a one-line day. §5.4 wants slack to pool in exactly that gap as "the air above a broadsheet headline"; on ~91 days a year it is 47px. Legal, and nobody has eyeballed it. If §5.4's author wants more air the only lever is dropping `{n} DRAWS.` — which returns the headline to zero figures and makes the proof line the sole evidence.

2. DIGIT ADVANCES ARE STILL UNMEASURED. 0.6573em was measured on Bricolage 800 UPPERCASE only. `8 DRAWS.` contains a digit and a full stop. The 106.24px slack at the narrowest candidate track tolerates digits up to 13.47% wider than the uppercase mean, which is almost certainly enough — but the honest position is that §5.3's measured-fit rule at render is what proves it, and this string has never been rendered. A 10-glyph line 1 would appear only at `drawsRendered` ≥ 10, which §5.11 forbids today; if deck size ever rises, line 1 becomes 9 glyphs (887.36px) and slack collapses to 7.62px at the 895 candidate.

3. THE WEAKER GATE IS A REAL TRADE, NOT A FREE ONE. A headline question is now evidenced by a sibling element rather than by itself. If a future edit deletes, empties or de-figures the proof line, the question becomes bare rhetoric — the rule catches that (class A), but only because the proof line is in the same model. Any surface that ever renders a "?" without an adjacent generated facts line reverts to sentence scope by default, and nobody has checked that the Reel, Story and FB templates never acquire one.

4. TWO FIGURES IN THE HEADLINE REMAINS ARITHMETICALLY UNAVAILABLE ONLY WHILE THE HERO IS 150px. If §3.5's hero step ever drops to 120px the line capacity becomes floor(895 / (0.6573 × 120)) = 11 glyphs and a two-figure question becomes packable. This ruling does not reopen at 120px automatically, and it should be revisited if that step moves.

5. THE CONFORMANCE TEST IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE FACT-SET LIST. It proves the allow-list against the predicates at the enumerated boundary fact-sets, not for all inputs. A predicate that fires on some unenumerated real value — an operator price form `priceLabel()` renders unexpectedly, a 10-glyph cap — still reaches the daily build. The fixture list is the thing to extend when inventory changes, and nobody owns extending it.

### C9 — Scoping the CAP 8.17 prize-name assertion (§10.2 DOM assertions / §10.8 class A)

**Owner:** §10.2 — G1, The conditions band. It already declares itself the sole normative owner of the band and "the band's gate classes", and the prize-name assertion lives in its DOM-assertions block. It now additionally owns `data-pdd-role`, the eight role values, the `DRAW_CARRYING` set, and the rule that band variant, L1's amber state, L2's host and L3's free-entry state are all selected by that predicate. Every other section references §10.2 and writes no role list, no variant rule and no prize-name step.

SCOPE BY A DECLARED ROLE, NOT BY SURFACE OR CANVAS.

1. THE ROLE ATTRIBUTE. Every rendered frame declares exactly one value of a closed eight-value enum, `data-pdd-role`. §10.2 is its sole owner. The mechanism already ships: `render.mjs:182` writes `data-type="${slide.type}"` onto `<body>` today from `build.mjs:150`'s `[intro, ...drawSlides, {type:"cta"}]`, and `story.mjs:144`, `reel.mjs:101` and `reel-template.mjs:778` each write `data-theme` onto `<body>` at the same point. `data-pdd-role` is written in those same four places. No new plumbing.

  cover        still-4x5 slide 1 (today `type:"intro"`)        DECK-LEVEL
  count        still-4x5 slide 2                               DRAW-CARRYING
  draw         still-4x5 slides 3 … N+1                        DRAW-CARRYING
  closing      still-4x5 slide N+2 (today `type:"cta"`)        DECK-LEVEL
  reel-open    reel-9x16 open-window frames AND the whole of reel-cover-9x16   DECK-LEVEL
  reel-card    reel-9x16 card frames                           DRAW-CARRYING
  reel-signoff reel-9x16 sign-off frames                       DECK-LEVEL
  story        story-9x16 (single frame)                       DRAW-CARRYING

`carousel/compliance.mjs` authors the predicate once and nowhere else:
  const DRAW_CARRYING = new Set(["count", "draw", "reel-card", "story"]);
Four values. No section may restate the list; sections reference `DRAW_CARRYING`.

The conflict said "at least three" deck-level assets. There are FIVE role-instances per day that carry no prize name: cover, closing, reel-open, reel-signoff, and reel-cover-9x16 (which is `reel-open`, being frame 0 of the Reel per §8's G6). The Reel cover was missed by both §10.2 tables.

2. HOW THE RENDERER KNOWS WHICH IS WHICH. The role is an INPUT to the gate, supplied by the caller; the DOM attribute exists only so the two can be cross-checked.
  - Stills (`render.mjs`, `story.mjs`, `reel.mjs:63 buildCoverHtml()`): the caller passes the role it just rendered; the gate asserts `document.body.dataset.pddRole === expectedRole`. A mismatch is class A (`role-mismatch`).
  - Video: the Reel is ONE document with every scene stacked under opacity keyframes (`reel-template.mjs:2`), so `<body>` cannot carry a per-frame role. `window.__seek(t)` — already called at `capture.mjs:21` — returns `{ t, role, drawIndex }`, derived from the SAME beat table that generated the keyframes (§6.4's openBeats / N×holdBeats / signOffBeats). The gate reads the returned role; it never infers a role from computed opacity.
  - Role runs on the Reel, in order: `reel-open` (openBeats = 2), `reel-card` × N (holdBeats each), `reel-signoff` (signOffBeats − 2), `reel-open` again for the final 2 beats — because §6.8's loop rule restores frame 0's picture (insert collapsed, open headline back, counter reset to `DRAW 1 OF <drawsRendered>`) over the last two beats, and those frames are an open-window picture, not a sign-off picture. N+3 runs per reel.
  - CONSTRAINT this forces on §6.4 rule 4: `signOffBeats >= 3`, not 2, so the sign-off card owns at least one whole beat. Inert today — the five resolved beds are 3, 4, 4, 5, 4. If a future bed resolves to 2 the next legal value is 6 (multiple-of-4 completion), costing 4 beats.
  - SAMPLING. §10.1's "three sampled frames per scene" means three per ROLE RUN, at `t_start + 300ms`, the midpoint, and `t_end − 300ms`. The 300ms floor clears the 200ms row-swap (§6.4) and the 270ms sign-off collapse (§6.8), so no sample lands mid-transition.

3. THE SCOPED ASSERTION — G1-P, class A, MODEL + DOM, `DRAW_CARRYING` roles only.
Selector: exactly one `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node in the asserted subtree.
  a. count === 1;
  b. `normalizeWhitespace(textContent).length >= 1`;
  c. computed `font-size >= ` the resolved value of §3.5's `--fs-lead` token — written against the token, never a literal, in the discipline of §10.5 rule 2;
  d. `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` (§5.3's measured-fit mechanism);
  e. rect wholly inside the canvas and, on any surface whose §8 descriptor has a non-empty `keepOut`, wholly inside `surface.safe` and wholly outside `surface.keepOut` — read from the descriptor, not from an `if canvas === 9:16` branch.

"At or above its surface's step" resolves to ONE number, not a per-surface table: count slide 88→68→56 (§5.7 Layout 1), draw slide 88→68→56 (§5.7 Layout 2), Reel Row B fixed at `--fs-lead` (§6.3), Story band 2 68→56 (§7.2). Every floor is `--fs-lead` = 56px. §10.2 says so and publishes no table.

THE GATE IS TWO-SIDED. On a role NOT in `DRAW_CARRYING` the assertion does not run and its absence is not a violation of any class — but a `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node PRESENT on a deck-level role is itself class A (`prize-name-on-deck-asset`). Scoping is not an escape hatch.

4. TWO PROPAGATED FIXES THAT MAKE (c) TRUE ON EVERY ORDINARY RUN.
  - §7.2's "a title that will not set in two lines at 56/60 fails the build" is REPLACED by §5.7's rule: truncate at a word boundary, append `…`, re-measure at 56px. As written it hard-fails the Story on 11.7% of draws, and the Story carries exactly one draw with no backup path.
  - §6.5's "the build fails on overflow rather than shrinking type" is REPLACED for Row B by: render `cleanTitle()` truncated at a word boundary to whichever is smaller — 22 glyphs, or the measured 950px line at Bricolage 700 `--fs-lead` — appending `…`, and if the first word alone overflows, truncate mid-word at the measured boundary. §6.5's 22 stays a READING budget feeding §6.4's duration arithmetic, so §6.4's five-bed table is unchanged. Truncation is a named counted record in `COMPLIANCE.json` (`prize-name-truncated: <role> <slug> <n>→<m> glyphs`), not a failure class; the untruncated title lives in `out/alt.json` on every draw-carrying asset (§10.7).
  - Row B stays ONE line. Two lines cost 60px → card 345px → chrome 606px = 31.56%, over §6.1 rule 6's 29% ceiling. §6.3 already proves this.

5. THE OTHER §10.2 DOM ASSERTIONS WITH THE SAME DEFECT. Four need role scoping, one needs selector scoping, two are correctly universal:
  (i) THE BAND'S TWO STRING VARIANTS. §10.2 picks the deck variant by a prose list — "cover slide, closing slide, Reel sign-off" — which omits `reel-open` and the whole `reel-cover-9x16` surface, both of which carry the band (§6.3: the band is one of three pieces "present on every frame of every reel"). Replace the list with the predicate: draw variant iff `DRAW_CARRYING.has(role)`, deck variant otherwise.
  (ii) L1'S AMBER CAUTION STATE. "When the stored close is inside 48 hours, L1's text switches to signal amber `#FFC53D`" has no input on a deck-level L1 (`8 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` contains no close). SCOPE: amber exists only on draw-carrying roles; deck L1 renders `#F7F5F0` (10.9:1) unconditionally. Without this, §10.5 rule 3's colour assertion either fails or passes vacuously on five roles a day.
  (iii) L2'S HOST. Draw variant names the registrable domain of that row's `draws.entry_url`; deck variant is the fixed string `Enter · terms · each operator's own site.` Two different checks: row-identity on draw-carrying roles, frozen-fixture equality (§10.6a L1/L3 regime) on deck roles.
  (iv) L3'S FOUR `free_entry_route` STATES. A per-draw column with no value on a deck asset. SCOPE: the four-state machine runs on draw-carrying roles; deck roles always render the plural form `Free-entry routes and age limits: in those terms.` (873.5px, inside 940).
  (v) SELECTOR SCOPE ON THE PER-LINE ASSERTIONS. "Per line: fontSize >= 38px" has no stated selector. Unscoped over the document it fails the carousel masthead Slot B dated stamp and the §5.4 cover dateline, both at `--fs-micro` = 34px < 38px, on every still, every day. FIX: the selector is `[data-pdd-band] > [data-pdd-band-line]`, and `count === 3` is itself asserted. Nothing outside the band is measured by G1.
  (vi) opacity >= 0.92, scrollWidth <= clientWidth, opaque background (alpha = 1, no `backdrop-filter`): correctly universal, every asset carries the band. Unchanged.
  (vii) The rect/Safe-Box-A/L-notch assertion: correctly universal once re-expressed against `surface.safe` / `surface.keepOut` from §8's descriptor rather than a canvas-size test.

6. CAP 8.17 FIELD 5 AFTER SCOPING — WHERE IT IS DISCHARGED ON EVERY ASSET THAT NEEDS IT. The compliance unit is the PUBLISHED POST, not the frame, and the discharge is now machine-checked rather than argued. NEW post-level gate, MODEL stage, class A: for each publish format, `count(assets where DRAW_CARRYING.has(role) && prizeName non-empty) >= 1`, and on the carousel `=== drawsRendered`.
  - IG carousel (10 slides): 8 draw-carrying slides each carry `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` (nature) and every slide's band L1 carries `8 DRAWS IN THIS POST` plus the counter chip `DRAW n OF 8` (number). The COVER independently discharges field 5 without a prize-name node: §5.4's board names three prizes in its Prize column (x 124→688, Inter 600 `--fs-label`) plus `+5 more inside`, and the proof line states the deck count — so the one slide always seen alone is covered at zero cost. The CLOSING slide carries neither and is discharged post-wide by the other nine children; that exposure is named in residual risk.
  - IG Reel: N × Row B (nature); the counter chip and band L1 (number). `reel-open` and `reel-signoff` carry neither, and the reel is one media object that loops — §6.8 asserts frame 0 and the final frame are the same picture, so one loop shows every card.
  - reel-cover-9x16: needs no discharge. It is the Reel's thumbnail, not a published media object — §8's five publish formats are ig-carousel, ig-reel, ig-story, fb_photo, fb_video; the cover is none of them.
  - IG Story: band 2's prize name (nature). Number is discharged by the asset carrying exactly one named prize against one closing date and one price — PDD stores `grand_prize` and no prize count, which is why §10.2 deleted `1 PRIZE: 2023 VW GOLF R`.
  - FB photo album (§7.7: cover + first four draw slides): 4 prize names.
  - FB video: the Reel's MP4, identical to IG Reel.
  A CATEGORY WORD IN DECK L1 WAS CONSIDERED AND IS ARITHMETICALLY DEAD — see arithmetic.

**Residual risk:** 1. THE CLOSING SLIDE AND THE SIGN-OFF STILL DISCHARGE NOTHING. Field 5 is discharged post-wide for them, and that rests on the compliance unit being the post rather than the child. §5.6 records that Instagram re-serves slide 2 cold, which means it re-serves non-first children generally — so a viewer can meet the closing slide alone, carrying `8 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` and no prize nature. The cover and the count slide are both covered (board, prize name); the closing slide is the one genuine hole, and I have not filled it because the only fills available are a category word in deck L1 (arithmetically dead, shown above) or a fourth band line (45px, which §6 and §7 have no budget for — the Story's five bands sum to 883 exactly and the Reel's chrome sits at 546 of a 556.8px ceiling). If a reviewer rejects post-wide discharge, the cheapest honest fix is to give the closing slide the cover's board.

2. THE REEL TRUNCATION HITS OVER HALF OF LIVE INVENTORY. Median title 26 glyphs against a 22-glyph render cap means most Reel cards ship a truncated prize name. A 4-glyph trim usually preserves the nature of the prize; at p90 = 53 it strips 31 glyphs and can remove the distinguishing qualifier ("Ultra 2", "2023", trim level). That works directly against §2's requirement that inner assets be distinguishable from one another, and it is the field CAP 8.17 calls the nature of the prize. The mitigation — the untruncated title in `out/alt.json` — is machine-readable, not viewer-facing. The real fix is §9's ingest-time normaliser, which §6.5 already names as the dependency; until it lands, the truncation counter in `COMPLIANCE.json` is the measurement that tells anyone how bad it is.

3. THE ROLE ATTRIBUTE IS A NEW SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE, AND IT FAILS QUIET IN ONE DIRECTION. If a renderer emits the wrong role, the `role-mismatch` assertion catches a disagreement with the caller — but the caller and the attribute are written in the same commit by the same hand, so they will usually be wrong together. A `draw` slide mislabelled `cover` would then skip G1-P entirely and publish with no prize name, silently. The two-sided rule (a prize-name node on a deck role is class A) closes half of that; the other half is only closed by the post-level count assertion (carousel prize-name slides `=== drawsRendered`), which is why that gate is not optional garnish.

4. THE SAMPLING WINDOW IS 140.74ms AT ITS TIGHTEST. On elegant.mp3 (81 BPM, signOffBeats 3) the sign-off run is one beat = 740.74ms and the three samples land at 300 / 370.37 / 440.74ms. That is positive and asserted, but any section that lengthens the row-swap past 200ms or the collapse past 270ms closes it. The 300ms floor is a design judgement over two animation durations I did not measure on a real render.

5. NONE OF THIS HAS BEEN RENDERED. The role runs, the collapsed-band frame 0, the Reel cover's byte-identity with t=0, and the truncated Row B at 56px are all paper. §5's own caveat stands: nothing at this geometry has ever been rendered, so every fit figure here is an advance sum bounding a line box, and §5.3's measured-fit rule at render remains the binding check.

6. I DID NOT REOPEN A KNOWN INCONSISTENCY I NOTICED. §5.7 quotes "~15.5 characters" for the 88px display step against a 930px line; the arithmetic gives 930 ÷ (0.6573 × 88 = 57.84) = 16.08, and 15.5 is §3.5's figure computed against an 895px well. It does not affect the 56px floor this ruling asserts, so I left it to §3.5 and §5.7 rather than spending their budget.

### C4 — the config.json migration and the audio path

**Owner:** **§8.7 — Migration.** It is the sole normative owner of the `config.json` category schema: `CATEGORY_KEYS`, the per-category entry shape and its six keys, the complete authored values for all eight categories, FALLBACK's post-migration contents and scope, the removal of the `{ ...FALLBACK, ...c }` merge, and the `config.test.mjs` gate G-C1…G-C7. It already owns the deletions (`theme`, `particles`) and already names the three tests that break, so the schema and its gate belong in one place. §6.10 is rewritten to a single sentence — "FALLBACK's `audioMood` and every category's `audioMood` are §8.7's; `beat.mjs:16` is a consumer" — and publishes no key, no default and no value of its own. §1 (E1–E5), §5.11/registry-C5 (`drawsPerDeck`, Tier 1/2, `visualWeight` scoring), §10.6a (`hook` retirement) and §8.3/G1 (`sceneFor`) are each cited by §8.7 and restate nothing; §8.7 restates none of them either — it cites §6.4's resolved-bed table by reference and publishes no BPM, no beat count and no duration.

**The finding's mechanism is wrong; its conclusion is right. Nothing throws. Something worse happens silently — and the fix is to make it throw.**

`config.mjs:13-17` reads, verbatim:

```js
export function catCfg(slug) {
  const c = CFG.categories[slug];
  if (!c) return { ...FALLBACK, name: slug || "Prize", hook: "WIN BIG", seoKeyword: "UK competitions" };
  return { ...FALLBACK, ...c };
}
```

`{ ...FALLBACK, ...c }` is a **merge**, not a branch. A configured category does NOT stop reading FALLBACK — FALLBACK supplies every key the entry omits. So adding `sports-outdoors` to `config.json` without `audioMood` does not make `beat.mjs:16` throw: §6.10's `FALLBACK.audioMood = "win"` still fills it. C4's build-failure claim is **REFUTED**. What actually happens is the failure C4 should have found: a partial entry silently inherits `visualWeight: 0.6` and `valueLineMin: Infinity`, so the two categories the rework exists to serve are added to the file and stay exactly as invisible as they were — §1's E2 and E3 unchanged, with nothing in the build to say so. A silent default is worse than a throw.

**1. Every key FALLBACK supplies today — the complete enumeration.**

| Key | Source | Value | Consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visualWeight` | `config.mjs:9` | `0.6` | `select.mjs:38` |
| `theme` | `config.mjs:9` | `"default"` | `themeOf()` → `build.mjs:154`, `story.mjs:244`, `reel.mjs:237`, `preview-sheet.mjs:25/40` |
| `hashtags` | `config.mjs:9` | `["#ukraffle","#livedraws"]` | `caption.mjs:17`, `:34` |
| `particles` | `config.mjs:10` | `{type:"embers",count:46}` | `build.mjs:156`, `preview-sheet.mjs:25` |
| `valueLineMin` | `config.mjs:10` | `Infinity` | `honesty.mjs:27` |
| `name` | `config.mjs:15` (unconfigured branch only) | `slug \|\| "Prize"` | brief / preview |
| `hook` | `config.mjs:15` (unconfigured branch only) | `"WIN BIG"` | `format.mjs:72` → `build.mjs:140` → `render.mjs:150` |
| `seoKeyword` | `config.mjs:15` (unconfigured branch only) | `"UK competitions"` | `plan.mjs:74`, `honesty.mjs:32` |
| `audioMood` | **absent** — §6.10 adds `"win"` | — | `reel.mjs:232`, `story.mjs:245` → `beat.mjs:16` |

Nine keys. Three of them (`theme`, `particles`, `hook`) are deleted by rulings already binding, leaving **six**.

**2. `theme` is DELETED, not renamed to `scene`.** §8.7's "`theme` becomes `scene`" is itself a restatement error of the class I am here to settle. `SceneDef.id` **is the slug** (08-scenes.md:55, `id, // "sports-outdoors"`), `sceneFor(slug)` is a total function keyed on the slug alone (8.3), and G1 already asserts it returns a distinct non-NEUTRAL scene for each of the eight slugs at `lib/parse.mjs:9`. A `scene` key in `config.json` would restate the object's own key — a second source of truth that can drift from `scene.mjs`. `themeOf()` (`config.mjs:19`) is deleted with it; its four call sites take `sceneFor(slug)`.

**3. The complete new entries — six keys each, every value real.**

```json
"sports-outdoors": {
  "name": "Sports and Outdoors", "visualWeight": 0.88,
  "seoKeyword": "UK sports and outdoor competitions",
  "hashtags": ["#sportsgiveaway", "#ukcomps"],
  "valueLineMin": 4000, "audioMood": "win"
},
"home-garden": {
  "name": "Home and Garden", "visualWeight": 0.78,
  "seoKeyword": "UK home and garden competitions",
  "hashtags": ["#homeandgarden", "#ukcomps"],
  "valueLineMin": 3000, "audioMood": "warm"
}
```

`audioMood` is chosen from the six musical moods that exist in `assets/audio/manifest.json` (`driving` 112, `synth` 112, `elegant` 81, `win` 99, `warm` 103, `pop` 152). The seventh entry, `sting`, is a 77KB `.wav` with `bpm: null` and is **never** a legal `audioMood` — it would pass a naive membership test and then divide by `null` in `beatGrid`.

`win` for sports-outdoors closes §6.10's open question with evidence rather than leaving it open: `win.mp3`'s manifest source is Pixabay's *"energetic sports rock music"* — it is literally the sports bed, and it is the bed §6.10 already picked as the safe default. `warm` for home-garden is the only domestic bed in the manifest, and it currently has **zero live consumers** (`house-draws` has zero enterable inventory, §1). No new audio asset is required; no bed is orphaned.

No ampersand in either `name`: Bricolage's single-storey `&` is the glyph that is near-identical to its `£` (`styles.css:174-176`, promoted by §8.7 to the brand-wide mono-figure rule). "and" costs two characters and removes the question.

**4. The six existing categories: three keys deleted, no value edited.** `theme`, `particles` and `hook` are struck from all six (`hook` by the registry's §10.6a ruling, "Retired from config: the six `hook` constants and `WIN BIG`"). `name`, `visualWeight`, `seoKeyword`, `hashtags`, `valueLineMin`, `audioMood` are carried across **byte-for-byte** — car-draws stays 1.0/20000/`driving`, cash-prizes 0.4/5000/`win`, house-draws 0.8/50000/`warm`, tech-giveaways 0.92/3000/`synth`, luxury 1.0/10000/`elegant`, collectibles 0.85/8000/`pop`. Each entry goes 9 keys → 6. `global.drawsPerDeck = 8` is added per the registry's C5 ruling. Whether `cash-prizes`' 0.4 is judgement or drift (§1 E4) is NOT reopened here.

**5. FALLBACK survives, and the silent merge does not.** This is the ruling that actually fixes the class.

```js
export const CATEGORY_KEYS = Object.freeze(
  ["name","visualWeight","seoKeyword","hashtags","valueLineMin","audioMood"]);

const FALLBACK = Object.freeze({
  name: "Prize", visualWeight: 0, seoKeyword: "UK competitions",
  hashtags: ["#ukraffle", "#livedraws"], valueLineMin: Infinity, audioMood: "win",
});

export function catCfg(slug) {
  const c = CFG.categories[slug];
  if (!c) return { ...FALLBACK, name: slug || "Prize" };
  return c;                    // NO merge. Completeness is a CI gate, not a runtime patch.
}
```

FALLBACK's job afterwards is exactly one thing: **keep `catCfg` total for a slug the pipeline has never seen, so nothing crashes on it — while guaranteeing that slug can never reach a rendered surface.** It is still reachable: `select.mjs:32` buckets any unrecognised slug as the literal string `"other"`, and `catCfg(null)` is legal. It is no longer a default-supplier for configured categories, so a missing key on a real category is now `undefined` at CI instead of a plausible-looking 0.6.

Two consequences follow, and both are stated so a builder needs no further decision. `visualWeight: 0` replaces `0.6` as a tripwire. And because `enough * 1e12` (`select.mjs:40`, and the registry's Tier-1 replacement) dominates weight entirely, zero is not sufficient on its own — **`pickBestCategory` skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories`**, a one-line guard at `select.mjs:33`. Unknown inventory is never a deck. `sceneFor()` keeps returning NEUTRAL for it per G1; NEUTRAL now guards a path that cannot be selected rather than one carrying 147 draws.

**6. The gate: `carousel/tests/config.test.mjs`, rewritten from an enumeration into a derivation.** The existing test is the reason this got through — `:5` hardcodes the six slugs, so adding a seventh and eighth category cannot fail it, and `:12`/`:27-28` assert `particles.type` and `themeOf()`, which are the things being deleted. Seven assertions replace it:

- **G-C1 Coverage.** `Object.keys(CFG.categories)` equals, as a set, the eight slugs **imported from `lib/parse.mjs:9`** — never retyped. Fails both directions: a taxonomy category with no config entry, and a config entry with no taxonomy slug.
- **G-C2 Completeness, exact.** For every entry, `Object.keys(entry).sort()` deep-equals `CATEGORY_KEYS.sort()` — **no missing key and no extra key**. The extra-key half is what catches a `particles` or `theme` that survives the migration in one entry but not another.
- **G-C3 Types.** `visualWeight` a number in (0, 1]; `valueLineMin` finite and ≥ 1000 (below `honesty.mjs:27`'s own `total < 1000` floor it is dead config); `hashtags` exactly 2 strings matching `/^#[a-z0-9]+$/` and disjoint from `GLOBAL.fixedHashtags`; `name` and `seoKeyword` non-empty.
- **G-C4 The audio join — the assertion that closes C4.** For every entry, `audioMood` appears as a `mood` in `assets/audio/manifest.json` **and that manifest row has a finite numeric `bpm`**. The bpm half is not decoration: it is the only thing that excludes `sting`.
- **G-C5 FALLBACK completeness.** `Object.keys(FALLBACK)` deep-equals `CATEGORY_KEYS`, and G-C3 and G-C4 run against FALLBACK too. FALLBACK can never again be missing a key a consumer reads — the precise defect §6.10 had to patch by hand.
- **G-C6 No silent merge.** `catCfg("car-draws") === CFG.categories["car-draws"]` by **reference identity**. This is the gate's teeth: it fails the moment anyone reintroduces the spread.
- **G-C7 Unknown slug.** `catCfg("mystery-boxes").visualWeight === 0`, and `pickBestCategory` over a pool whose only rows are `"other"` returns `null`.

**Confirmed to pass on the ordinary run.** Walked against the post-migration file: G-C1 — eight entries, eight slugs. G-C2 — six existing entries lose exactly `theme`/`particles`/`hook`, two new entries authored at six keys. G-C3 — weights 1.0, 0.4, 0.8, 0.92, 1.0, 0.85, 0.88, 0.78 all in (0,1]; minima 20000, 5000, 50000, 3000, 10000, 8000, 4000, 3000 all ≥ 1000; all sixteen existing and four new hashtags match `/^#[a-z0-9]+$/` and none collides with `#prizedrawsdaily`/`#ukcompetition`/`#winbig`. G-C4 — `driving`/`win`/`warm`/`synth`/`elegant`/`pop` all present with bpm 112/99/103/112/81/152. G-C5 — six keys, `audioMood: "win"`, bpm 99. It is a pure static test: no network, no database, no render, no Chromium, no ffmpeg. It cannot fail flakily, so it cannot become the gate someone switches off.

**Residual risk:** **1. `valueLineMin` 4000 and 3000 are judgement, and I could not measure them.** `honesty.mjs:2` documents `total_prize_value` as gross ticket revenue, not prize worth, so the thresholds are set against a revenue estimate (~£1,400/draw sports, ~£1,000/draw home-garden) derived from typical ticket counts and prices, not from the database — I did not query it. The calibration is one query: `select categories.slug, count(*), percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by total_prize_value) from draws join categories … where enterable group by 1`. If the real median is below ~£500/draw, both thresholds suppress the value line on a degraded 4-draw deck, which is the same failure as `Infinity` — just quieter. Set them from the query before the first publish; G-C3's `≥ 1000` floor catches an absurd value, not a wrong one.

**2. `visualWeight` 0.88 and 0.78 are unmeasured judgement dressed in three significant figures.** §1's E4 already asks whether the existing weights are judgement or drift and gets no answer. I picked 0.88 to place sports-outdoors above collectibles (0.85) and below tech (0.92) on the argument that golf clubs and bikes photograph like product, and 0.78 for home-garden on the argument that BBQs and furniture photograph slightly worse. Neither is measured, and no measurement is obtainable — Instagram's Graph API exposes no per-child carousel insight (§8.8's own caveat). The picker arithmetic is exact; the inputs to it are not. What the numbers *are* is a decision, which is what was missing.

**3. Deleting the merge converts silence into hard CI failures, and that is the point — but it is not free.** Any future category added to `lib/parse.mjs:9` now fails `bun test` at G-C1 until `config.json` catches up, and any entry short one key fails at G-C2 rather than quietly defaulting. That is correct, but it means the taxonomy and the social pipeline are now coupled: the scraper can no longer add a category unilaterally. §8.3 already observes "the social pipeline is a category behind its own scraper" — this ruling makes that state loud instead of invisible, and someone will meet it on a red build at an inconvient moment. The recovery is four lines of JSON, and the gate names exactly which slug is missing.

**4. home-garden Reels carry 2 draw cards until a string in another section changes.** 11.650s of Reel with two draws is the thinnest configuration in the system, and it is a consequence of §10.2's conditions-band glyph count, which is not this cluster's to set. The 310.7ms overshoot is real and I have not hidden it. If §10.2 lands above 65 glyphs and someone wants the third card back, the alternative is reassigning home-garden to `elegant` (81 BPM → 3 draws / 14.815s) at the cost of the domestic register and of leaving `warm.mp3` with zero live consumers. That trade is available, costs one JSON edit plus a re-run of G-C4, and I did not take it because register is the thing §8's scene system exists to protect.

**5. Refuting C4's mechanism means the finding as filed would not have been caught by a test for throwing.** Anyone who reads the original finding and writes a gate asserting "the Reel pipeline does not throw on sports-outdoors" builds a gate that passes today, passes after a partial migration, and never fires. That is why G-C2's exact-key-set assertion, not G-C4's audio join, is the load-bearing one. If only one of the seven assertions survives review, keep G-C2.

**6. Unverified.** I did not run `bun test`, did not render a surface, and did not query the database. Every code claim is from reading the files on disk on 17 Sep 2026 (`config.mjs` 854 bytes, `beat.mjs` 851, `config.json` 2,655, `manifest.json` 2,116); every beat figure is arithmetic I reproduced independently against §6.4's published table and matched on all five rows; the 102 / 45 / 147 / 16.4% counts, the ~19 luxury and ~17 home-garden pool estimates, and the in-window figures are inherited from §1 and the registry, whose own risk notes record that category counts moved between measurements taken minutes apart.

### Lane C's rect, the unlocated scene elements (tech's four anchors, house's two contour arcs), the amplitude unit, and G6's sampled frame — §8 scene geometry

**Owner:** §8.5 — "The eight scenes". From now on §8.5 is the sole normative source for every scene-element coordinate, stroke width, per-lane paint, amplitude class and amplitude value, and for every per-scene coverage and tone figure. §8.3 and §8.4 state the rules and cite §8.5 for the values; §8.8's gate thresholds cite §8.5 for the geometry they are derived from. Lane C is the one number in this cluster §8.5 does not own and may not print: its literal lives only in §6.3's chrome-rect table (06-reel.md) and reaches §8 as a computed transclusion.

**1. LANE C — ONE RECT, AND ITS LITERAL LIVES IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE: §6.3's chrome-rect table (06-reel.md). §8 states it nowhere, ever again.** As §6.3 currently stands the rect is **x 0…1080, y 661 … 1007, h 346, area 373,680 px² = 18.021% of frame**, and that line is a transclusion of §6.3, reproduced here for readability only — if it disagrees with §6.3, §6.3 wins. It has now moved three times (h 272 → 285 → 346, the last when §4.4 stacked E2 on every surface and took Row C from 195px to 256px), and every typed copy of it in this document has been wrong after at least one of those moves. That is the whole reason for the rule.

Diagnosis: both published rects share the floor y = 1007 and differ only in the card height. §8.3 printed 735…1007 (h 272) because it back-derived the origin from §10.2's pre-type-ruling card (Row B 104 + Row C 168 = 272; 1007 − 272 = 735). §3.5's type ruling then re-set the rows to Row B 722…812 (h 90 = 15+60+15) and Row C 812…1007 (h 195 = 10+50+5+120+10), card = 285. §6.3 already states this and already states that it supersedes §10.2's 272px card with the arithmetic. §8.3's own derivation rule ("the card lane is the union of §6.3's newsprint insert rows") makes 722 the answer mechanically. §8.3's lane table prints Lane C as a computed transclusion of §6.3's insert-card rect, never as a typed number — which is what makes this class of error structurally impossible rather than merely corrected.

**2. TECH'S FOUR ANCHORS — full coordinates.** Frame of reference, stated once and used by both scenes below: the **box** is the lane rect on 9:16 and the axis-aligned bounding box of `sceneRegion(slideRole)` on 4:5. On every box now in the spec the box spans x 0…1080; T, B, H are the box's top, bottom and height. Absolute x, box-relative y — the same form as car (x = 50 spine, full lane height), luxury (x = 170, 55px below the lane's top edge) and home-garden (along the lane's bottom edge).

- **Anchors** (`sc-anchors`): four unfilled circles, radius 15 (pulsing to 20), centres at **x = 185, 425, 665, 905** (= 65 + 120k, k = 1…4, phase-anchored to `safe`'s left edge x 65 per §8.3), all four on one centre line **y_c = T + 5·round(H/10)** — the box's vertical midpoint snapped to the 5px lattice. One row, not two: Lane R is 116px tall and cannot hold two rows plus a frame.
- **Leaders** (part of `sc-anchors`): one per anchor, horizontal, on the centre line, **40px long**, starting at the peak-radius edge so the pulse never overruns them — **A1 x 125…165, A2 x 365…405, A3 x 685…725, A4 x 925…965**. This replaces the published "stopping 40px short of the lane's opposite edge", which crosses the other three anchors on every current box and costs 3–7× the ink.
- **Dimension frame** (`sc-dims`): left vertical line **x = 20, y T+20 … B−20**; bottom horizontal line **y = B−20, x 20 … 1060**; a 10px horizontal end tick centred on (20, T+20) and a 10px vertical end tick centred on (1060, B−20) — ticks only on the two free ends. A 20px inset keeps the frame outside G5's outermost-8px border ring and on two sides only, so it cannot read as a border.
- `structural: ["sc-anchors","sc-dims"]`. Leaders belong to `sc-anchors`, because 4 × 40 × 0.5 = 80 px² alone would sit under G3's 150 px² floor.

**Materialised y for all eight boxes:** Lane R (269…385, H 116) y_c **329** · Lane C (661…1007, H 346) y_c **834** · Story S1 (0…269, H 269) y_c **135** · Story S2 (1152…1920, H 768) y_c **1537** · 4:5 cover bbox (132…872, H 740) y_c **502** · 4:5 draw-slide bbox (632…867, H 235) y_c **752** · 4:5 count-slide bbox (132…432, H 300) y_c **282** · 4:5 closing bbox (132…1182, H 1050) y_c **657**. *(Lane C's pair is derived from §6.3's current rect, not authored here.)*

**3. HOUSE'S TWO CONTOUR ARCS — full coordinates.** Two parallel shallow arcs, **radius 7300**, centres on **x = 540**, crests 40px apart (one house grid pitch), in the box's lower band:
- **Contour A:** crest (540, **B − 85**), centre (540, B + 7215); visible **(0, B−65) – (540, B−85) – (1080, B−65)**.
- **Contour B:** crest (540, **B − 45**), centre (540, B + 7255); visible **(0, B−25) – (540, B−45) – (1080, B−25)**.
- Both are drawn over-wide, **x −40 … 1120**, and clipped to the box, so the box stays filled at every motion phase. Stroke **1.5px** on every surface. Equal radii with centres 40px apart means the arcs are exactly 40px apart at every x and can never cross — which is what a contour interval is. Contour B's ends sit 25px above B, clearing G5's 8px border ring by 17px. `structural: ["sc-contours"]`.
- **Materialised crests (A / B):** Lane R **300 / 340** · Lane C **922 / 962** · S1 **184 / 224** · S2 **1835 / 1875** · 4:5 cover **787 / 827** · 4:5 draw **782 / 822** · 4:5 count **347 / 387** · 4:5 closing **1097 / 1137**.

**4. PAINT AND STROKE for the two located geometries** (§8.4's tone floor decides this, not taste): on a **newsprint lane and on `still-4x5`** — `--hairline`, 100%, which is exactly the 9:16 tone floor (L 0.653576) and exactly what car, luxury, collectibles and house's own grid already use; `--ink-meta` is **retired from both entries**, because `--ink-meta` at full opacity is L 0.113173 and fails G5's tone floor by 0.540403. On a **rail-blue lane** — `--ground` at 6% (`#224368`, L 0.053539, ΔL +0.015510), the one already-measured lighten composite in the spec, inside the 0.016 cap. On `still-4x5` every pixel resolves to `--scene-tone` per §8.4 regardless. **General stroke rule, stated because a gate depends on it: no scene stroke on a rail-blue lane is thinner than 1px.** At the 0.016 ΔL ceiling a 0.5px stroke resolves to per-pixel ΔL ≈ 0.00776, below G3's own 0.010 measurement threshold, so G3 would fail tech on every legitimate build. Tech's circles and leaders are therefore **0.5px on newsprint and on the still, 1px on rail blue**; house's 1.5px contours need no per-lane variant.

**5. ONE AMPLITUDE UNIT: canvas pixels of travel at dpr 1. `scale ≤ 3%` is DELETED.** Every animated quantity converts to the maximum distance any painted point moves from its phase-0 position during the loop; a dimension change scores as the displacement of the moved edge, not as the change in the dimension figure. Three classes, one cap each:
- **Discrete element** (any painted figure the eye tracks individually): travel **≤ 25px**, and the path must return, t=0 ≡ t=loopMs.
- **Periodic field** (a painted set invariant under translation by its pitch P along the motion axis, within its clip): travel is **exactly P**, no other value, uncapped.
- **Opacity envelope** (no painted geometry moves; only per-pixel alpha varies): no travel cap; the envelope's **peak** phase — not its mean — must satisfy the tone and coverage ceilings.

**Honest re-score of all eight, in the one unit:** car — periodic field, P 45, travel 45 = P, **pass**. sports — periodic field, P 90, travel 90 = P, **pass**. tech — circles r 15→20→15, discrete, travel **5px**, pass. luxury — lot bar 65→75→65 welded at the top of the margin rule so only the bottom edge moves, discrete, travel **10px**, pass. home-garden — dimension break 90→110→90 centred, each painted line end retreats 10px, discrete, travel **10px**, pass; **the published "20px amplitude" is corrected to 10px** — 20 is the width delta, twice the travel of either edge, and the scene does not change. cash — opacity envelope, geometric travel 0, **pass** on the peak-phase budget. collectibles — opacity envelope, geometric travel 0, **pass** on peak. **house — the one scene that changes.** Two arcs are not a periodic field, so the one-period exemption never applied to them; translating them −40px leaves them somewhere else and **breaks G6's byte-identity**. House's motion becomes **translateX 0 → −20px → 0, sine, 5,000 ms, Lane C only** — discrete, travel 20px ≤ 25, loop closed by construction, and it now matches the round-trip form the other three discrete scenes already use. §8.4's periodic-field list drops house and becomes **(car 45px, sports 90px)**.

**6. G6 — FIXED, NOT DEFERRED. Ships blocking in v1.** It runs on the scene fixtures, never on a production reel, which is what makes the fix cost nothing (§8.8 already renders 9 × 4 = 36 fixture renders).
- **Clause 1 (loop closure):** the `reel-9x16` fixture renders with the insert card **pinned to its expanded height, y 722…1007**, over a flat NEUTRAL photograph ground. Assert the full-frame PNG at scene-clock t = 0 is byte-identical to the PNG at t = `loopMs`. Lane C paints in both. **Skipped when `loopMs === 0`** (NEUTRAL only).
- **Clause 2 (cover parity):** **`reel-cover-9x16`'s `sceneLanes` is corrected to `[R]`.** `reel.mjs:63` `buildCoverHtml()` builds a separate card with no insert card and therefore no Lane C — that mis-declaration is why the assertion read as vacuous. Compare the cover fixture PNG to the `reel-9x16` fixture PNG at t = 0, restricted to `[R]`; that is now an exact and complete comparison, because the Reel's own frame 0 has the card collapsed and carries Lane R only. The gate **asserts `sceneLanes` is non-empty before comparing** — an empty set fails rather than passing. Both sides are **PNG screenshots of fixtures**, never the delivered `cover.jpg`, which `reel.mjs:246` writes as JPEG q90 and which cannot support a byte comparison at all.
- **Clause 3:** the production seam is not G6's. §6's own assertion (first and last captured frames differ on fewer than 1.0% of pixels) owns it and is independent of `loopMs` because Lane C is collapsed at both ends.
- **Common case confirmed:** all nine definitions pass. Two periodic fields return at exactly one period; three discrete round trips return to phase 0; two opacity envelopes complete exactly one cycle; house returns after the change above; NEUTRAL is skipped at clause 1 and compared on Lane R at clause 2.

**Residual risk:** **The unscoped rule I did not settle, because it is not mine and it is bigger than this cluster.** §8.4's 9:16 tone floor — "no scene pixel darker than `--hairline`, L 0.653576" — is violated at full opacity by six elements across four scenes that were already agreed: car's 5px `--rail` spine, luxury's `--ink` lot bar, house's 25px `--rail` grid tick, home-garden's `--rail` end ticks, and (before this ruling) tech's and house's `--ink-meta` strokes. I fixed only the two I was asked to locate, by painting them at `--hairline`, so my two additions can never be the thing that fails G5. The other four need the same decision from §8.4, and the general form of it is: the maximum legal alpha is the largest value whose 8-bit composite over the host ground has relative luminance ≥ 0.653576 — for `--ink-meta` over newsprint that is 22% (#D4D4D2, L 0.657367). Note also that G5's blocking/advisory split (line 392) assigns "tone floor" to neither list, so as written nobody knows whether this fails a build or not.

**Tech's rail lane is very close to nothing, and tech is a 112 BPM category.** At 1.335% geometric coverage and ΔL 0.015510, tech's Lane R carries 0.021% tone ink — 37× fainter than sports' 0.78%, which §8.8 already names as its one measured G7 risk. For the Reel's first 1.0714 s and on the whole of `reel-cover-9x16`, a tech day therefore carries essentially no category signal, and x264 at CRF 23 (no `-crf` flag anywhere in `carousel/`, per §8.8) will almost certainly quantise it out. The alpha knob is closed at 6% by the 0.016 cap. The only remaining lever is geometric: repeat the four-anchor row at 240px x-pitch to fill the rail lane. I have not spent it, because that is a scene redesign and the brief is to locate the published geometry, not to replace it. If G7 fires on tech, that is the one-line fix.

**Mark slot M is probably already dead, and it decides whether sports' Reel marking ever renders.** §8.5 makes M conditional on 16px of measured clearance to each rail string. §6.3 measures the wordmark at Bricolage 800 = 418.35px before tracking at `--fs-label`, so it ends at x ≥ 483.35 against M's left edge at 435 — a clearance of −48.35px, not +17.5px, and M suppresses. §8.5's own 352.5px estimate is the source of the disagreement and §6 raised this as an open question that has not been answered. It does not touch this ruling (Lane R's rect is unchanged and neither located scene declares a mark), but it means sports-outdoors ships stripes only on the Reel and the cover, with the green, the ripples and the pitch appearing on the Story alone.

**House is now the heaviest scene and has zero enterable inventory.** At 4.907% coverage it sits 1.09pp under the 6% ceiling, and it is the scene nobody will ever see in production — `house-draws` has 0 enterable draws, so it renders only from the gate fixture. Every build therefore pays the full G3/G5/G6/G7 cost of the set's heaviest scene for a category that cannot be selected. That is deliberate (§8.5: "built and gated off ... so it does not rot"), but if gate runtime becomes the constraint, house is the first fixture to make conditional.

**None of this has been rendered.** Every figure above is geometry and 8-bit composite arithmetic against a pipeline that has produced no scene pixel. The 268.50 px² G3 margin, the 0.003791 of tone-floor headroom on a 22% `--ink-meta` mix, the 17px of border-ring clearance on house's lower contour, and the claim that a 0.5px `--hairline` stroke survives a dpr-2-to-dpr-1 downsample above G3's 0.010 threshold are all things a single fixture render would confirm or kill in a minute, and none of them has had that minute. The strongest available claim for this settlement is that the numbers close, not that it works.
