## §1. Context, problem statement and verified defect inventory

## 1. Context, problem statement and verified defect inventory

This section is the evidence base. It states what PrizeDrawsDaily is, what the pipeline currently does, what is verifiably wrong with it, and which claims the rest of the spec may and may not lean on. It sets no design values. Where a defect below has a remedy, the remedy belongs to the section named against it, and this section states the owner rather than the answer.

### 1.1 What PrizeDrawsDaily is

PrizeDrawsDaily (prizedrawsdaily.co.uk, `@prizedrawsdaily`) is a UK prize-draws **directory**. It runs no draws of its own. It lists, rates and reviews other operators' draws, and its editorial claim rests entirely on being the party with no stake in the outcome.

That positioning is not rhetorical. Under CAP Section 8 (Promotional marketing) — the operative code for prize competitions and free draws, which sit outside Gambling Act 2005 licensing — PDD is not the promoter. It is a publisher making objective claims about other people's promotions, and CAP 3.7 requires documentary evidence for every objective claim to be held *before* publication.

The corpus is healthy. Per the DB sample taken for this brief (DIGEST, 2026-09-17 — **a single read I could not repeat in this session; the filesystem corroborates run dates but not these counts**): **899 enterable draws** (`status = active`, `draw_date` in the future), **100% carrying both an `image_url` and a `total_entries` value**.

| Category | Enterable draws | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| cash-prizes | 351 | 39.0% |
| tech-giveaways | 157 | 17.5% |
| sports-outdoors | 102 | 11.3% |
| collectibles | 97 | 10.8% |
| car-draws | 81 | 9.0% |
| luxury | 64 | 7.1% |
| home-garden | 45 | 5.0% |
| house-draws | 0 | 0% |

The seven populated categories sum to 897 of 899; two rows are unaccounted for. The account sits at roughly 66 Instagram followers — a cold start.

**Correction to an earlier draft of this section: 100% coverage of `total_entries` is not 100% eligibility to publish an odds figure.** The earlier text concluded "every one of those 899 rows can therefore express an odds figure". That does not follow, and the repository says why. `lib/parse.mjs:151–155` records in its own comment that tiers 2 and 3 of the extractor leak other competitions' numbers on multi-comp listing pages, "which is how a draw scraped a stranger's ticket count"; `qa-fix.mjs:5–6` names two further live error classes, `total_entries` holding a per-person cap and `total_entries` holding a progress bar belonging to a different comp; and `lib/parse.mjs:149` sets `plausibleEntries` at a floor of 100, beneath which §4.3 reports a live stored value of 99 (that row was not re-queried in this session). A stored number with no recorded extraction path is not evidence of a ticket cap, and every one of those failure modes understates the denominator. **Presence of the datum is a necessary and not a sufficient condition.** The eligibility contract — the provenance columns, the method enum, the freshness window and the selection predicate that enforces them — is §10.4's, and it is a hard prerequisite on anything in this spec rendering an odds figure at all. This section states the corpus; it does not state the publishable pool.

**The picker never sees all 899, either.** `select.mjs:9–23` (`fetchEndingSoon`) queries `draw_date` between `now + minDays` and `now + days`, with `image_url=not.is.null` (`select.mjs:18`), `order: draw_date.asc` (`:19`) and `limit: 300` (`:20`). `plan.mjs:12–13` sets `DAYS = 7`, `MIN_DAYS = 1`. So the daily selection pool is at most 300 draws closing in a six-day band, soonest first — and on a heavy week the 300-row cap truncates the far end of that band. Every count in the table above is corpus scale, not selection scale. Deck size, pool-eligibility tiers and how truncation is recorded are §5.11's.

This matters beyond arithmetic. Any superlative rendered on an asset — "shortest", "best", "today" — is an objective claim whose evidence base is this pool: one category, at most 300 rows, one six-day window, out of a UK inventory PDD has never enumerated. §10.6a owns which comparatives are permitted and how they are scoped; this section supplies the denominator that makes an unscoped one indefensible under CAP 3.7.

### 1.2 What the social pipeline does

The pipeline lives at `~/pdd-aggregator/carousel/` (Bun + Playwright). Per run: `select.mjs` scores categories and picks the day's subject; `plan.mjs` archives the previous run (`plan.mjs:18–32`, with the archive folder named at `:23`) and writes `selection.json` plus a rotated `archetype` (`plan.mjs:70–71`); `build.mjs` renders a 1080×1350 deck by loading `render.mjs` HTML against `styles.css` in headless Chromium at `deviceScaleFactor 2` (`render.mjs:187`), and writes `alt.json`; `reel.mjs`/`reel-template.mjs` and `story.mjs` render animated 1080×1920 HTML timelines frame-by-frame (`capture.mjs:12`, at `deviceScaleFactor 1`) and mux with ffmpeg; a Claude session authors `CAPTION.txt` and `FB_CAPTION.txt`; `publish.mjs` emits `out/publish.json`; Composio MCP tools post to Instagram and Facebook.

As shipped, `build.mjs:150` assembles `[intro, ...drawSlides, { type: "cta" }]` and, with `plan.mjs:10`'s `SLIDES || 5`, the default run produces seven slides from five draws. That is the current state, not a target: the deck size the rework builds to, and every count derived from it, are §5.11's.

The routine is **trigger-based, not cron-driven**. `carousel/DAILY.md:12` states it plainly: *"What happens (Claude drives this when you say "publish today")"*.

**The repo's own doctrine is reel-first and this spec does not inherit it.** `DAILY.md:9` says *"The Reel is now the main event (it's the only format that has ever reached anyone on this account…)"*. That is an account-level observation drawn from twelve published posts. Socialinsider (35M posts / 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025) puts the 1–5K follower tier at **median views** of carousel 993 vs reel 580 — the carousel **out-viewing** the reel by roughly 1.7×, and holding that advantage in every band. That is a views figure, not a reach figure, and must not be restated as reach anywhere: views count replays, reach does not (§11.6). Both statements can be literally true; they are not the same evidence class, and the spec treats the carousel as the primary growth surface while noting that the repo's shipped documentation asserts the opposite.

### 1.3 The framing that governs this rework

**The odds hierarchy is not a styling nit. It is the design flaw, the strategic flaw and a distribution-eligibility risk, simultaneously — and it is the same single line of code in all three readings.**

`carousel/render.mjs:67` renders odds as a trailing fragment appended to the closing date:

```js
<div class="closes"><b>${esc(d.closes)}</b>${d.odds ? ` · ${esc(d.odds)}` : ""}</div>
```

`.closes` is `font-size: 33px` (`styles.css:358`). `.prize` — the prize name — is `font-size: 98px` (`styles.css:346`). Both are shipped behaviour, not drift, but they trace to two different commits, both dated **2026-07-02** and both predating the last publish on 3 July: `git log -L67,67:carousel/render.mjs` and `-L358,358:carousel/styles.css` return only `35e000c` (the baseline commit), while `-L346,346:carousel/styles.css` returns `c97816d` (the same-day 6-theme design-system commit) above it. *(An earlier draft of this section claimed all three traced to `35e000c`. They do not.)*

So the odds sit at **33.7% of the prize name's type size**, sharing a line with the closing date, in the same weight and colour as the date. And `odds` is derived from `total_entries` (`format.mjs:53` `oddsLabel`, assigned at `format.mjs:62`) — the one datum no operator publishes, present on 100% of inventory, and structurally uncopyable, because an operator's job is to make odds feel small.

Three consequences, from three different directions:

1. **Design.** The largest element on a draw slide is the prize name, which every operator and every rival directory also shows. The smallest legible element is the only thing that is ours. Hierarchy is inverted against the proposition.
2. **Strategy.** The competitive teardown (17 Sep 2026, headless browser at every profile — **one crawl, one day**, with Storm Competitions age-gated and Bounty private) found odds existing as a *data field* at CompWatch, Competition Showroom and PDD, but **nobody has made them visual** — no bar, no grid, nothing you can feel. PDD is currently paying the cost of holding that field without taking any of the benefit.
3. **Distribution eligibility.** Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines (help.instagram.com/313829416281232, OFFICIAL) exclude from recommendation *"unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value"*, and Meta states these guidelines are held to a higher standard than Community Standards. A daily auto-generated carousel built from **other operators' photographs and other operators' prize data** is directly exposed to that clause. The added value — odds, ticket cap, closing date, comparison — must be visibly on the slide. It currently is not.

The evidence that this is a rendering failure and not a data failure is on disk. The last authored Instagram caption (`~/Desktop/pdd-today/out/CAPTION.txt`, 14 Jul 2026) does the odds work properly:

> "🏴‍☠️ LEGO Icons Captain Jack Sparrow's Pirate Ship (2,862 pcs) — £1.60 · 1 in 445 […] That pirate ship is 1 in 445 — better odds than most raffles you'll scroll past all week."

The material value lives in the caption, where it does not defend the images. (That second sentence is also a second-person unbounded comparative; §10.6a quotes it by name in its own reasoning as a string its predecessors' deny-list missed, and it fails §10.6a's second-person and unbounded-comparative predicates — see §1.7.)

**The pipeline already proves the number can be hero-sized — in one place.** The Reel's arm-B hook scene (`reel-template.mjs:649–650`, `:659`) promotes the odds figure to `.giantq`, which is **`font-size: 300px`** (`reel-template.mjs:250`) — the largest type declaration anywhere in the system. The capability is not missing; it is confined to a single scene of one A/B arm in the format the account publishes least. **This is cited as precedent that the treatment is buildable, not as a target size.** The type scale, the hero tier and the odds-figure floor are §3.5's; the odds device itself is §4's. No size in this section is a specification.

**The cover is worse than the draw slides.** `render.mjs:133–159` (`introHtml`) renders **no odds at all**, no per-draw closing date and no ticket cap. It carries a price anchor (`FROM JUST … A TICKET`, `render.mjs:151`), an aggregate value/count line, a thumbnail strip and a swipe label. The `.intro-hook` is 130px (`styles.css:393`). And the cover footer at `render.mjs:157` is the **only** footer in the file that omits the `.wm` brand watermark — the draw slides, the typographic-fallback slide and the CTA slide all carry `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY.CO.UK` (`render.mjs:69`, `:122`, `:172`); the cover does not. So the slide guaranteed to be seen, and the one that becomes the profile-grid thumbnail, adds a price anchor, carries no odds, and does not name the brand. Mosseri (Oct 2024, OFFICIAL) states Instagram will often give a carousel a second chance on the second media item, so slide 2 must also stand alone; slide 2 is a draw slide, which does carry odds and the watermark, at 33px and 28px respectively.

**Honest caveat:** point 3 is an interpretation of Meta's published policy text, not an observed enforcement action. Nothing in the repository or the digest shows Instagram restricting this account. The exposure is structural, and the design case in point 1 stands without it.

### 1.4 The pipeline is dark, and it was abandoned rather than broken

The automated pipeline **last published on 2026-07-03**. Today is 2026-09-17. That is **76 days dark**. Evidence: `carousel_posts` holds 12 rows in total, spanning 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-03, across formats carousel, reel, story, fb_video and fb_photo (DIGEST, DB read — same unrepeated read as §1.1).

The filesystem corroborates precisely *how* it went dark, and it does so independently of the DB. Archive folder names record the date of the **sweep**, not the run: `plan.mjs:23` names each archive `${todayLondon()}-${Date.now() % 86400000}` at the start of the *next* run, then moves the previous run's files into it (`:25`). The files inside carry the true dates.

| Location | Run date (file mtimes) | Deck | Reel/Story | Captions | `publish.json` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `~/Desktop/pdd-today/archive/2026-07-10-39463994/out/` | 3 Jul, 04:34–04:40 | 7 slides | reel.mp4, story.mp4 | yes | **yes** |
| `~/Desktop/pdd-today/archive/2026-07-14-35175563/out/` | 10 Jul, 16:33–16:38 | 7 slides | reel.mp4, story.mp4 | yes | **none** |
| `~/Desktop/pdd-today/out/` | 14 Jul, 15:21–15:23 | 7 slides | none | yes | **none** |

So the 10 July and 14 July runs **built complete decks, authored both captions, and then stopped at the publish step**. They did not crash. There is no error artefact, no partial upload, no half-written state row. The 10 July run got further — it rendered and encoded both videos before stopping; the 14 July run never reached video at all.

Two facts frame this correctly:

- **Publishing is not blocked by plumbing.** Composio connections are active for both Instagram (user `prizedrawsdaily`, id `27332554436394910`) and Facebook (DIGEST).
- **Nothing triggers the routine.** `DAILY.md:12` makes the routine human-invoked. A trigger-based routine that nobody triggers simply stops, silently, and leaves finished work on disk.

**The 14 July run was hand-steered, not generated.** `~/Desktop/pdd-today/selection.json` (mtime 14 Jul 15:16) carries `"slug": "ending-today"`, `"name": "Ending Today"`, `"banner": "5 DRAWS ENDING TODAY"` and `"hook": "LAST CHANCE TO WIN"`. Three things follow, all verified:

- `grep -rn 'ending-today' ~/pdd-aggregator/carousel/` returns **nothing**. The slug exists in no `.mjs`, `.json` or `.md` in the pipeline.
- `plan.mjs:72–76` writes exactly `slug, name, date, seoKeyword, archetype, draws, backups`. It never writes `banner` or `hook`. The file's `"date": "2026-07-14T09:30:00Z"` is also a round timestamp with no milliseconds, unlike the 10 July file's `"2026-07-10T10:57:50.819Z"` produced by `new Date().toISOString()`.
- **Correction to an earlier draft of this section:** it claimed the unknown slug fell through `config.mjs:15` and rendered the hook `WIN BIG`. It did not. `build.mjs:140` reads `hook: sel.hook || hookLabel(sel.slug, sel.name)`, and `sel.hook` was present, so the 14 July cover read **LAST CHANCE TO WIN**. The fallback claim was false and is withdrawn.

The fallback path is real, but it bites elsewhere — see E1.

**This matters for the spec because it changes what "success" means.** The rework is not recovering a working system that degraded. It is restarting a system that was left switched off, so the design must be good enough that someone wants to press the button, and the defects below are the reason nobody did. Fixing the template does not by itself fix a human-triggered routine that stopped being triggered — and every recurring manual step the rework adds is drawn against the same gate that has already failed twice at zero marginal effort. The operator-minutes budget, its ceiling and what gets cut to hold it are §12's; this section supplies the failure mode that makes the budget load-bearing rather than hygienic.

The pill has therefore never rendered under Instagram's indicator, and has never been crop-exposed, because the 3:4 grid crop applies only to slide 1. What survives is geometry: a 4:5 upload cropped to 3:4 keeps 1350 × 3/4 = 1012.5px of width, so 33.75px is removed from each side and the crop lines fall at x 33.75 and x 1046.25. The pill's right edge sits at x 1030, **16.25px inside the right crop line**; the rank circle's left edge sits at x 50, **16.25px inside the left one**. Both are latent hazards that fire the moment a draw slide leads a deck — a degraded run, a reordering, a single-draw post. §5.15 deletes the positions on that basis.

**A7, the single authoritative cover inventory.** Re-read in full on 2026-09-17; §2.3 and §5.4 should cite this entry rather than restate it, because all three previously disagreed.

*Decorative layers, in paint order, `render.mjs:144–147`:* `.backdrop` (conditional on `d.bg`, `:144`) · `.glow` (`:145`) · `.bloom` (`:145`, via `bgFx()` at `:43–44`) · `.rays` (`:145`, via `bgFx(true, …)`) · `.embers` particle field at ×1.25 count (`:142`, `:145`, via `particlesHtml()` at `:30–42`; returns an empty string where a category's profile is `none` or count ≤ 0, `:32`) · `.confetti` at 24 pieces (`:145`, `confettiHtml()` at `:47–59`) · `.techgrid` (`:146`) · `.scrim` (`:147`). **Eight in the DOM in the maximal case, six where `d.bg` is absent and the particle profile is `none`.** The earlier count of six omitted `.bloom` and `.rays`, which are inside `bgFx()`; the count of seven omitted `.glow`; the count of four omitted both plus the particle field.

*One correction every previous inventory missed:* `.techgrid` is `display: none` by default (`styles.css:278`) and paints only under `[data-theme="tech"]` (`:279`). So the **painted** layer count is one lower than the DOM count on every non-tech cover, and eight layers paint only on a tech cover that also carries a backdrop image and a live particle profile. Any section reasoning about visual density, not DOM structure, must use the painted count.

*Text-bearing elements, `render.mjs:149–155` plus the footer at `:157`:* `.intro-kicker` · `.intro-hook` · `.intro-from-hero` (conditional; three spans) · `.intro-sub` (conditional) · `.intro-end` · `.intro-swipe` · `.footer .rp`. **Seven elements, nine text nodes** counting the three spans of `.intro-from-hero` separately. `.thumbs` (`:153`) is image-bearing and becomes text-bearing only in the numeral fallback at `render.mjs:129`.

**A9, stated precisely, because half of it was not previously flagged.** Prize competitions and free draws sit outside Gambling Act 2005 licensing, so CAP Section 8 governs and *"PLAY RESPONSIBLY"* is gambling furniture that is both inaccurate and quietly re-categorises PDD in the viewer's mind. `18+` is an unevidenced claim about another party's terms. **So is `UK ONLY`, and this is new: verified by repo-wide grep excluding `node_modules` and `.git`, there is no `min_age` column, no territory column and no country field anywhere in the pipeline or the schema it reads** — `min_age` and `country` return zero hits, and the only three hits for "territor" in the whole repository are prose in a test fixture (`test/fixtures/regressions.json:60`), a planning document (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-scraper-accuracy.md:350`) and a runbook (`carousel/INSIGHTS.md:99`). PDD therefore verifies nothing about either condition, yet renders both on every asset at four sites. Both are the same class of CAP 3.7 exposure and must be resolved by one decision, not two. **The conditions band — which fields it carries, in what words, at what size, on which surface — is §10.2's, and the wording for age and territory is §10.6's. This section states the defect and the absence of the columns; it states no replacement string and no field list.**

On the binding constraint behind A9, cited here as evidence for why A9 is a defect and not as a specification of the band: the ASA is unlikely to consider social posts sufficiently limited by time or space and is likely to expect **all** significant conditions in the material itself, and "link in bio" does not discharge this (OFFICIAL). CAP guidance also states, verbatim, that *"page design, layout or format"* must not mislead and that promoters *"should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true"* — which makes A1 and A3 a compliance surface, not only an aesthetic one, and which cuts both ways once the odds figure is enlarged.

#### B. Reel and Story (`reel-template.mjs`, canvas 1080×1920)

Meta's 9:16 safe zone, **edge-detected from the diagram asset** (version timestamp 10 Feb 2026 — measured from an image, not read from a numeric spec), gives **Safe Box A: x 65, y 269, w 950, h 883** — i.e. `left:6% right:6% top:14% bottom:40%`, with the 768px bottom exclusion that applies when the creative carries a disclaimer. An **L-shaped notch** at x 853–1080 by y 1152–1920 holds the action rail and must never be occupied. Meta's own prose warns that on phones taller than 9:16 it may zoom-to-fill, *"which can crop areas outside the safe zone"*, so Box A is **DERIVED** — the best available frame, not a guarantee, and it must not be cited anywhere in this spec as OFFICIAL.

**Nothing in the current Reel is fully inside Box A.** Two elements straddle it and seven fall wholly outside. `.pcard` breaches on all four edges — 29px over the top (269 − 240), 38px under the bottom (1190 − 1152), and 1px outside each side margin (left 64 against a 65px margin; right edge at x 1016 against Box A's 1015). `.tblock.center` also straddles, and by much more: its 130–1670 box overhangs Box A by 139px at the top and 518px at the bottom, plus the same 1px each side. The earlier phrasing "everything except `.pcard` renders outside the safe area" overstates `.pcard`'s compliance and is withdrawn; it must not be repeated downstream.

Every other element — the price, the deadline chip, the CTA, the handle and the compliance footer — has been rendering underneath Instagram's own UI. This holds under the looser 672px bottom exclusion too (safe bottom 1248): `.cd-pill`, `.kickline`, `.tblock`, `.lower3` and `.rfoot` all still fall below it, so the defect is robust to the disclaimer question. `.lower3`, `.cd-pill` and `.rfoot` are `left:0; right:0`, so they also cross into the L-notch. Horizontally, `.pcard`, `.tblock` and `.tblock.center` all sit at `left/right: 64px` and breach the 65px margin by 1px on each side; `.kickline` at 56px breaches it by 9px.

Ten of the 24 `font-size` declarations in `reel-template.mjs` are below the 44px video type floor §3.5 sets: 24, 24, 27, 27, 30, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37. Odds are treated inconsistently: `.rl-closes` renders `ODDS <b>…</b>` at 34px (`reel-template.mjs:637`, `:269`), while the arm-B hook scene alone promotes the odds figure to `.giantq` at 300px (`:649`, `:659`, `:250`) — and falls back to the ticket price when odds are absent. Arm B's accompanying copy is hardcoded as `COULD BE YOU. WORTH A GO?` (`:650`); it is second-person framing about a chance of winning, and it fails §10.6a's `secondPerson` predicate as a class-A violation, so this is recorded here as evidence and no longer as an open compliance question.

Instagram's own ranking guidance (about.instagram.com, 31 May 2023, OFFICIAL) also states it aims to make reels *"less visible"* where they are *"majority text"*, muted, or carry borders — which interacts directly with a template whose entire text payload currently sits outside the frame Instagram intends creators to use, and which bounds how much chrome the rebuilt insert may carry (§6.3).

#### C. Architecture — the constraint that governs per-category design

`reel-template.mjs:46`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` each build their CSS by regex-scraping `styles.css`:

```js
/(?:^|\n)\s*(?::root|\[data-theme="[^"]+"\])\s*\{[^}]*\}/g
```

That matches `:root{…}` and `[data-theme="x"]{…}` and nothing else. A descendant rule such as `[data-theme="sports"] .pitch{…}` has ` .pitch ` before the brace and never matches. So per-category **tokens** propagate to carousel, Reel and Story for free, while per-category **structure** renders on the carousel and silently vanishes from the video formats.

This is not hypothetical — it is already live. `styles.css` contains **7 descendant theme rules** today, none of which reach the Reel or Story. Their selectors, exactly as written:

- `[data-theme="luxury"] .card` — hairline frame (`:77`)
- `[data-theme="luxury"] .intro-kicker, [data-theme="luxury"] .feat-kicker` — italic (`:78`)
- `[data-theme="luxury"] .slide::after` — 4% film grain (`:79`)
- `[data-theme="collect"] .card::after` — holo sheen sweep (`:145`)
- `[data-theme="tech"] .techgrid` (`:279`)
- `[data-theme="tech"] .hl` — chromatic split (`:281`)
- `[data-theme="tech"] .closes, [data-theme="tech"] .feat-closes, [data-theme="tech"] .intro-sub` (`:282`)

The codebase documents the trap itself in a comment beginning at `styles.css:295`: *"descendant rules never reach video: the token-lift regex in reel-template.mjs / story.mjs / reel.mjs extracts only `:root` and `[data-theme="…"]` blocks, so `[data-theme="x"] .card { … }` renders on the carousel and silently vanishes from the Reel."* The same comment records a second, related trap already paid for once: a composite declared on `:root` resolves against the default theme because `data-theme` sits on `<body>` while `:root` is `<html>`, which silently repainted every themed card in base orange (measured SSIM drift: cash 0.979 against a 0.997 noise floor, luxury 0.992).

There are also **six** `[data-theme="…"]` token blocks — `tech` (`:38`), `luxury` (`:58`), `cash` (`:85`), `house` (`:105`), `collect` (`:126`), `glass` (`:157`) — but `config.json` names only five of them plus `default` (which is `:root`). **No category points at `glass`**; it was added by `8abc72e` on 2026-08-26, after the last publish, and has never rendered in production.

**This is a verified failure mode, not a design position.** It bounds how per-category identity can be delivered, and the failure is silent — the carousel looks right while the video formats quietly lose the work. Whether identity is carried at all on a given surface, by what mechanism, in what quantity and under what gate, is **§8's**, and §8 is the only section that may answer it.

#### D. Instrumentation

`insights.mjs` `mapPayload()` (`:21–59`) ingests exactly six metrics: `likes`, `comments` (`ig_media`); an account-level series (`ig_reach`) stored under whatever name the payload carries (`metric: entry.name || "reach"`, `:40` — it is reach only because reach is what the routine requests); and `fb_reactions`, `fb_comments`, `fb_shares` (`fb_posts`). It pulls **no saves, no Instagram shares, no views, no watch time, no average watch time, no replays and no skip rate**.

Two measurement facts bound what can be added:

- **Carousel children have no individual insights in the Graph API** — only the parent album object carries metrics. There is no per-slide, swipe, exit-rate or completion metric, in the API or in the app (OFFICIAL). Any strategy built on per-slide drop-off is built on a metric that does not exist. This is also why no per-category or per-archetype visual decision in this spec can be validated by measurement.
- **Trial Reels require 200 followers** on a professional account (help.instagram.com/1013292530224018, OFFICIAL). At ~66 followers the A/B rig is unavailable. Retention chart and skip rate on normal posts are available now.

A further trap sits in the loop mechanics: Instagram defines Views as *"starts to play or replay"*, watch time as **including** replays, and average watch time as watch time (with replays) divided by **initial** views (OFFICIAL). A seamless loop mechanically inflates all three without inflating reach, so a loop can only be judged on accounts reached and skip rate.

#### E. Category coverage gap

`config.json` defines **six** categories: `car-draws` (theme `default`), `cash-prizes` (`cash`), `house-draws` (`house`), `tech-giveaways` (`tech`), `luxury` (`luxury`), `collectibles` (`collect`). The category **set**, and every theme, hook, `visualWeight` and `valueLineMin` in it, is unchanged since 2026-07-02; the file has had exactly three later edits, none of which touches the category set — luxury's `seoKeyword` (`55fae63`, 20 Aug 2026), the `supabaseUrl` repoint after the org migration (`e92c127`, 20 Aug 2026) and the removal of a Supabase publishable key (`fa2a2ae`, 4 Sep 2026). *(An earlier draft named only two of the three and is corrected here.)*

The live site has **eight** (see the open question on whether all eight category pages currently resolve). The mismatch runs both ways:

- **`house-draws` is fully configured and has zero enterable inventory in the sample** — theme, hook, fireflies particles, `valueLineMin: 50000`, all dead weight.
- **`sports-outdoors` (102 draws, the third-largest category) and `home-garden` (45 draws) have no theme at all.** Together that is **147 draws, 16.4% of enterable inventory**, falling through the `FALLBACK` at `config.mjs:8–11` to `theme: "default"`, `visualWeight: 0.6`, `valueLineMin: Infinity` — and, via `config.mjs:15`, to `hook: "WIN BIG"`.

**E1 — the two unthemed categories render the tell.** `config.mjs:15` hands any unrecognised slug `hook: "WIN BIG"`, which `format.mjs:72` returns unchanged (its `` `WIN ${catLabel(name)}` `` branch is unreachable against the current `config.json`, because every configured category supplies a truthy hook and the unconfigured branch hardcodes one) and `build.mjs:140` passes through when `selection.json` carries no explicit `hook`, which `plan.mjs` never writes. So a sports-outdoors or home-garden cover renders **WIN BIG** at 130px as its largest element — the phrase the UK visual-direction research names first in its list of American-giveaway tells to strip. `#winbig` ships in the hashtag set on every post regardless (A11). **Resolution pointer:** closed twice over — §10.6a retires the six `hook` constants and `WIN BIG`, and §8.7 deletes the `hook` key from `config.json` altogether.

**E2 — `valueLineMin: Infinity`** means the aggregate value line can never render for an unthemed category (`honesty.mjs:27` compares the capped total against it). The cover loses its only quantitative element as well as its identity. **Resolution pointer:** closed by §8.7's authored per-category values for sports-outdoors and home-garden.

**E3 — the gap is worse than "no theme", and this is DERIVED arithmetic, not judgement.** `select.mjs:32` buckets any unrecognised slug into the scoring pool; `select.mjs:41` scores each category as `enough * 1e12 + w * min(len, n) * 1e9 + value`, where **`enough` is set at `select.mjs:40` as `list.length >= Math.min(3, n) ? 1 : 0`** and `value` is summed `total_prize_value` — which `honesty.mjs:2` documents as **gross ticket revenue**, not prize worth. For `value` to reach the `1e9` weight granularity a single category's in-window ticket revenue would have to exceed £1bn, so in practice weight strictly dominates. With `visualWeight` at 0.6 and five draws in window at the shipped `n = 5`, `sports-outdoors` scores 3.0e9 on the weight term. It therefore **loses to any of `car-draws` (1.0), `luxury` (1.0), `tech-giveaways` (0.92), `collectibles` (0.85) or `house-draws` (0.8) that has four or more draws in the window** — 4.0e9, 4.0e9, 3.68e9, 3.40e9 and 3.20e9 respectively — and ties, losing on insertion order, against a 1.0-weighted category with three. The rotation penalty at `select.mjs:42` halves one category per day, which is not enough: a halved 1.0 category at five draws still scores 2.5e9, and the other unpenalised heavier categories remain above 3.0e9. **Resolution pointer:** closed by §8.7's authored `visualWeight` values; §8.7 also states the repaired picker arithmetic and the guard that skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories`. The figures above remain the measured before-case at the shipped `n = 5`.

Sports-outdoors and home-garden are not merely unthemed. **They are close to unreachable by the daily category picker** — on a typical day. This derivation is about the *window*, not the corpus: the heavier categories must actually field three-to-five draws closing 1–7 days out, and a thin week could invert it. It is also computed at the shipped `n = 5`; a different deck size (§5.11's) moves the `min(len, n)` term and the derivation must be re-run against it.

**Line-number note for downstream sections.** The adequacy test `enough = list.length >= Math.min(3, n)` is at **`select.mjs:40`**, not `:29`; `:29` is `const by = {}`. §5.11's treatment of that test is substantively correct and only the citation moves. Verified by `grep -n` on 2026-09-17.

**E4 — a related consequence, flagged separately because it may be deliberate:** `cash-prizes` carries `visualWeight: 0.4`, the lowest value in the file, so the **largest** category — 351 draws, 39% of inventory — scores 2.0e9 and ranks last of the seven populated categories. Combined with the two unthemed categories, **498 of 899 enterable draws (55.4%) sit in the three lowest-ranked buckets.** Whether 0.4 is an intentional judgement that cash photographs badly, or drift, is an open question and is deliberately left open by §8.7.

**E5 — the mismatch is visible in the archived runs.** The 10 July deck (`archive/2026-07-14-35175563/selection.json`) selected `luxury` — and the five draws were a TaylorMade driving iron, a Mizuno M-Craft putter, a Wilson Staff putter, a set of Mizuno JPX 925 irons and a Mizuno JPX One driver. Five golf clubs, under the cover headline `WIN LUXURY`, with `golddust` particles. Golf is sports-outdoors inventory wearing a luxury theme because sports-outdoors cannot win the picker. This is the measured before-case for E3's repair.

### 1.6 Existing good practice, and one bug inside it

Three things in the current pipeline are genuine E-E-A-T assets and are not defects:

1. **`honesty.mjs:19–23` (`capValue`) and `:25–29` (`valueLine`)** cap each draw's claimable value at the operator's own stated cash alternative, with a documented guard (`:16–18`) against a `£0` parse artefact zeroing a legitimate figure. The aggregate `£X+ IN PRIZES` line only renders past a per-category defensibility bar and is floored down to the nearest £1,000 so it never overstates. This is the CAP 3.7 discipline already implemented, and it is the only place in the pipeline where a figure is bounded by stored operator evidence before it renders.
2. **`honesty.mjs:31–37` (`altTexts`)** writes per-slide alt text to `out/alt.json` (`build.mjs:161`, consumed at `publish.mjs:171`). The mechanism survives; the strings themselves do not, because every one of them currently ends `(18+, UK only)` and carries the A9 defect into the accessibility layer. What alt text says is §4.9's (odds device) and §10.2's (conditions); that the file is written, gated and consumed at publish is the asset being preserved here.
3. **Audio is correct and should stay.** Meta Music Guidelines (effective 26 Mar 2024) bind on *use*, not on account label, so the library is unavailable for a commercial automated account regardless of Creator-vs-Business switching — and the Content Publishing API has no parameter to attach library music to a Reel in any case. The current arrangement (Pixabay beds, precomputed BPM and `firstBeatOffsetMs`, always muxed, `assertVideoContract` at `encode.mjs:36` hard-failing without an AAC stream) is the right answer by construction.

**One live bug inside asset 2.** `honesty.mjs:33` hardcodes the phrase `closing this week` into the cover's alt string and prepends the `seoKeyword`. On 14 July the seoKeyword was `UK prize draws ending today`, so the shipped alt text reads: *"5 UK prize draws ending today closing this week — prize draw round-up from Prize Draws Daily (18+, UK only)."* The cover's own accessibility string contradicts itself and contradicts the five per-slide strings beneath it, which all correctly say `closes tonight`. (Verified against the live `out/alt.json`, 14 Jul.)

### 1.7 Folklore this section deliberately does not build on

Several claims that would naturally support a rework of this kind are refuted by the digest, and the spec does not rest on them:

- **"5–8 slides is optimal"** — uncited everywhere it appears, and contradicted by the only real slide-count dataset (Eden, 655,385 carousels / 12,159 creators, Aug 2025–Aug 2026, which finds breakout rate rising from 23.4% at 3 slides to a ~32% plateau at 18–20). That dataset carries its own caveat: Eden sells a carousel generator, so "more slides win" is commercially convenient, and breakout-vs-own-median may be confounded by effort. Direction credible, magnitude soft, and it must not be restated downstream as a threshold. The deck size is §5.11's and is neither justified nor attacked on folklore here.
- **"The first slide carries 80% of the weight"** — no source. §1.3 argues the cover matters from Mosseri's documented second-chance behaviour and from the profile-grid crop, not from this.
- **"Good swipe-through rate is 15–25%"** — unmeasurable; per-slide metrics do not exist (see D).
- **"Trending audio boosts reach"** — no official statement, absent as a variable from both large benchmark datasets, and moot because the API cannot attach library music.
- **"Carousels get ~10% engagement rate"** — fabricated; measured is 0.50–0.55% by followers.
- **"80% of Reels viewed with sound on"** — Meta's own sources contradict each other; none is quoted as settled, and the template must work fully muted.
- **The Facebook 20% text-in-image rule** — retired 7 Sep 2020, and it only ever applied to ads. The "majority text" concern in section B comes from Instagram's own 2023 ranking page, which is a different and live constraint.
- **PDD's own archived copy is not precedent either.** The 14 July caption's *"better odds than most raffles you'll scroll past all week"* is an unbounded comparative in the second person with no stored comparison set — §10.6a quotes that exact string in its own reasoning as the case for an allow-list over a deny-list — and `COULD BE YOU. WORTH A GO?` (`reel-template.mjs:650`) is the same failure class on the Reel. Both fail §10.6a's `secondPerson` and `unboundedComparative` predicates. Neither is evidence that the register works.

Where a number is load-bearing it is MEASURED with its sample named: Socialinsider's median-views-by-follower-band figures (35M posts / 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025) put the 1–5K tier at carousel 993, reel 580, image 417 — making the carousel, not the reel, the primary growth surface at PDD's size on **views**, against the repo's own `DAILY.md:9` doctrine. Socialinsider's skip-rate study (140K reels, Jan–Jun 2026) puts 1–5K-tier skip within the first three seconds at 65.50%.

### 1.8 Problem statement

The social pipeline renders competent, dense, dark-and-glowing prize posters that are indistinguishable in register from the operators PDD exists to hold to account; that bury the single datum that distinguishes it at one-third the size of the datum every rival already shows, while proving in one unshipped Reel arm that the same number can be set far larger; that push the entire text payload of the video formats outside the frame Instagram intends creators to use, with no element fully inside it; that carry a 19px compliance line discharging none of the significant conditions the ASA expects on the material itself, two of whose three tokens are claims about operator terms PDD stores no column for; that cannot express two of the eight live site categories at all, and headline both of them with the exact phrase the brand research says to strip; and that measure six metrics, none of which can diagnose any of the above. It has not published for 76 days, not because it failed, but because two complete decks were built and then left on disk unpublished, and nobody pressed the button again.

### Decisions this section commits to

- The odds figure is the primary object of the redesign, not a supporting detail: the spec treats the 33px/98px inversion at `render.mjs:67` + `styles.css:346`/`:358` as simultaneously a design defect, the strategic differentiator and a Meta Recommendation Guidelines distribution-eligibility exposure — with the eligibility reading marked as policy interpretation, not observed enforcement.
- Added value must be visibly on the slide, not only in the caption. The Recommendation Guidelines exclusion for content "largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value" is treated as a binding constraint on the template, given the deck is built from other operators' photographs and prize data.
- This section states no type size, no gutter, no track, no ceiling and no target for the redesign. Every size quoted in §1.3 and §1.5 is a measurement of what currently ships. The type scale, the gutter and the hero and figure floors are **§3.5's**; the odds device, its geometry and its above-ceiling behaviour are **§4's**; the conditions band, its fields and its wording are **§10.2** and **§10.6**; permitted odds copy is **§10.6a**; deck size is **§5.11's**; per-category identity and where it renders are **§8's**. `reel-template.mjs:250`'s 300px `.giantq` is cited as proof the treatment is buildable, not as a size.
- In particular, the approved direction's phrase "one grid-survivable element ≥150px" is **not restated here**, and §1 sets no figure floor. What §1 contributes is the verified fact underneath it: the 3:4 profile-grid crop touches slide 1 only (A4), so no inner slide has a grid-survivability requirement to satisfy. Scoping that rule is §3.5's T2.
- `total_entries` coverage at 100% of the corpus is a statement about the datum's presence, not about its provenance. `lib/parse.mjs:149`, `:151–155` and `qa-fix.mjs:5–6` document three live ways the stored value can be a sold count, a per-person cap or a neighbouring competition's number — every one of which understates the denominator. Eligibility to render an odds figure is **§10.4's** selection predicate and is a hard prerequisite, not a caveat; the ordering that delivers it is **§12.4's Stage 0**.
- The cover is in scope as a defect, not just the draw slides: `render.mjs:133–159` carries no odds, no ticket cap and no per-draw closing date; its headline is a per-category constant resolved through `build.mjs:140` → `format.mjs:72` → `config.mjs:15` and rendered at 130px; and `render.mjs:157` is the only footer in the file that omits the `.wm` brand watermark, so the grid thumbnail is unbranded.
- §1.5 A7 is the single authoritative inventory of the cover's composition — seven text-bearing elements, nine text nodes, eight decorative layers in the DOM in the maximal case (six where `d.bg` is absent and the particle profile is `none`), with `.bloom`, `.rays` and `.embers` expanded from `bgFx()` at `render.mjs:43–44`, and with `.techgrid` painting only under `[data-theme="tech"]` so the painted count is one lower on every non-tech cover. §2.3 and §5.4 cite it and do not restate it.
- §1.5 A4 is a **latent** hazard, not a live defect. `build.mjs:150` puts the intro first, so `.pill` and `.rank` have never rendered on slide 1, never sat under Instagram's indicator and never been crop-exposed. The 33.75px-per-side crop arithmetic stands and is the reason the positions are deleted in §5.15.
- Meta Safe Box A (x 65, y 269, w 950, h 883) is adopted as the frame every 9:16 claim in this spec is measured against, and the L-notch at x 853–1080 by y 1152–1920 as permanently unusable — both labelled **DERIVED**, because they are edge-detected from a diagram asset and Meta's own prose warns of zoom-to-fill cropping outside the zone. No section may cite either as OFFICIAL.
- Nothing in the current Reel is fully inside Box A: `.pcard` and `.tblock.center` straddle it and breach on all four edges (`.pcard` 29px top, 38px bottom, 1px each side; `.tblock.center` 139px top, 518px bottom, 1px each side), and the other seven elements fall wholly outside, with `.lower3`, `.cd-pill` and `.rfoot` also crossing the L-notch. The phrasing "everything except `.pcard`" is withdrawn and must not be repeated.
- `UK ONLY` is recorded as the same class of unevidenced objective claim as `18+`: repo-wide grep finds no `min_age`, territory or country field anywhere in the pipeline or the schema it reads. Both must be resolved by one decision, in §10.6, and propagated to every surface and to the alt-text suffix in the same pass.
- Per-category *structure* authored as a CSS descendant rule in `styles.css` cannot reach the Reel or the Story, because the token-lift regex at `reel-template.mjs:46` / `story.mjs:31` / `reel.mjs:69` matches only `:root` and `[data-theme="…"]` blocks. Seven such rules diverge today and the codebase documents the trap at `styles.css:295`. This is recorded as a verified failure mode; whether, where and how much per-category identity renders on any surface is **§8's** to decide.
- The category taxonomy gap is scoped as three distinct problems: two live categories (sports-outdoors 102, home-garden 45 = 147 draws, 16.4%) have no theme and therefore headline "WIN BIG"; one configured theme (`house-draws`) has zero inventory; and one theme block (`glass`, `styles.css:157`, added 26 Aug after the last publish) has no category pointing at it and has never rendered in production.
- The 76-day dormancy is characterised as a trigger-based routine that stopped being triggered (`DAILY.md:12`), with two runs abandoned at the publish step — 10 Jul and 14 Jul both produced complete decks and captions but no `publish.json` — and explicitly not as a crash or a platform enforcement action. The operator-minutes budget that this failure mode makes load-bearing is **§12's**.
- The 14 July run is recorded as hand-steered: its `selection.json` carries `banner` and `hook` fields that `plan.mjs:72–76` never writes, so the cover read "LAST CHANCE TO WIN". The earlier claim that it fell through to the `config.mjs` "WIN BIG" fallback is withdrawn as false.
- `honesty.mjs` `capValue()`/`valueLine()` and the `altTexts()` → `out/alt.json` mechanism are designated must-survive assets. The alt *strings* are not preserved: they carry the A9 defect. `honesty.mjs:33`'s hardcoded "closing this week" is logged as a live bug to be fixed, not carried forward.
- The existing audio arrangement (Pixabay beds, precomputed BPM/`firstBeatOffsetMs`, always muxed, `assertVideoContract` hard-failing without an AAC stream) is declared correct and out of scope for change.
- The spec does not inherit the repo's own reel-first doctrine at `DAILY.md:9`; the carousel is treated as the primary growth surface on the Socialinsider 1–5K-tier median **views**, and the contradiction is stated openly rather than silently resolved. "Out-views" is the only permitted phrasing; the figure is never restated as reach.
- The selection pool is scoped as at most 300 draws closing 1–7 days out (`select.mjs:20`, `plan.mjs:12–13`), not the 899-row corpus, so every corpus-scale count is labelled as corpus scale and the picker derivation is labelled as window-scale. This pool is the evidence base for any comparative claim rendered on an asset, which is why §10.6a's scope tokens are mandatory.
- No part of this spec rests on "5–8 slides is optimal", "the first slide carries 80% of the weight", "swipe-through rate 15–25%", "trending audio boosts reach", "carousels get ~10% ER", "80% of Reels viewed with sound on", or the retired Facebook 20% text rule — nor on PDD's own archived copy, both of whose odds lines fail §10.6a's predicates.

### Open questions

- Is the Facebook Page unpublished because it was never published, or because Meta unpublished it? The digest's `is_published:false` reading is single-sourced via an agent reading the live Page through Composio and was not independently verified. The user must confirm in Meta Business Suite, because the two answers imply completely different risk pictures for the Instagram account too.
- Why did the 10 July and 14 July runs stop at the publish step? There is no error artefact on disk. It is unknown whether the operator chose not to publish, the session ended, or something in the publish path failed without writing anything.
- Who authored the 14 July `selection.json` by hand, and against what intent? It carries slug `ending-today`, plus `banner` and `hook` fields that `plan.mjs:72–76` never writes, and a round timestamp unlike `plan.mjs`'s ISO output. Whether a since-removed code path once produced it, or a human/Claude session wrote it directly, determines whether `ending-today` should become a real configured category or stay an ad-hoc override.
- Two of the 899 enterable draws are unaccounted for: the seven populated categories sum to 897. Are those rows uncategorised, or in a category not surfaced by the sample?
- Is `cash-prizes`' `visualWeight` of 0.4 a deliberate judgement that cash draws photograph badly, or is it drift? At 351 draws (39% of inventory) it is the largest category and ranks last of the seven populated categories in the picker, so the answer changes whether this is a defect or a constraint. §8.7 authored the two new categories' weights and deliberately left this one open.
- Does the live site actually expose eight category pages? The digest states eight, but the competitive crawl of 17 Sep 2026 recorded prizedrawsdaily.co.uk/category/cash returning a 404. Whether that is a slug mismatch, a routing bug or a retired page needs settling before the template's category set is fixed.
- Should the `glass` theme (`styles.css:157`, added `8abc72e` on 26 Aug 2026, no category points at it, never rendered in production) be wired to a category, retired, or carried forward as a sub-register? It is currently the only theme block with no route to the screen.
- Is the "every night · 7pm UK" publication cadence in `config.json` `global.series` a commitment the rework is expected to honour, or a string to be removed? It is an objective claim under CAP 3.7 and has been false for 76 days. The same question applies to `#winbig` in `global.fixedHashtags`, which is a brand decision rather than a compliance one.
- Was the 300-row limit in `select.mjs:20` sized deliberately? With `order draw_date.asc` it systematically truncates the far end of the 1–7 day window on heavy weeks, which biases selection toward soonest-closing draws in a way nothing else in the pipeline documents. §5.11 owns the response; what is open here is whether the cap was ever intended.

**Closed since the previous draft.** Whether `COULD BE YOU. WORTH A GO?` and "better odds than most raffles you'll scroll past all week" breach CAP 8.20/8.21 is no longer open: both fail §10.6a's `secondPerson` and `unboundedComparative` predicates as class-A violations, and the caption line is quoted by name in §10.6a's own reasoning. Whether the stored `total_entries` values are evidenced is no longer open here either: they are not, and §10.4's contract — sequenced as §12.4's Stage 0 — is the answer.

### Risks

- The Recommendation Guidelines argument is an interpretation of published policy text, not an observed enforcement action — nothing in the repo or the digest shows Instagram restricting @prizedrawsdaily. If the spec over-weights this framing and the risk never materialises, the rework may be justified on a hazard that was never live. The design case for foregrounding odds stands on its own without it.
- The 9:16 safe-zone numbers (269 top, 672/768 bottom, 65 side, and the 227×768 L-notch) are edge-detected from a Meta diagram asset with a 10 Feb 2026 version timestamp, not read from a numeric spec. Meta may revise them, and Meta's own prose warns that on phones taller than 9:16 it may zoom-to-fill, "which can crop areas outside the safe zone" — so Box A is a best available frame, not a guarantee. Every 9:16 budget in this spec inherits that softness.
- Correcting the odds hierarchy creates an exposure in the opposite direction. Making the odds the largest element on a slide risks reading as an inducement under CAP 8.20/8.21, and CAP guidance explicitly makes emphasis and hierarchy a compliance surface. The existing 300px `.giantq` treatment in reel arm B is precedent for the size being renderable, not clearance for the framing — and arm B's own copy fails §10.6a for exactly that reason.
- The binding decisions this section defers to are now reconciled with each other on the odds figure's size, and §1 still states none: the odds figure sets at `--fs-figure` 120/120 on every surface (§4.4's E2 module, ratified for the Story by §7.2, which also scopes §3.5's T2 so a frame may legally carry zero `--fs-hero` nodes), while `--fs-hero` 150px remains the cover-headline step §10.6a's permitted-wording table is measured against. §1 cannot be read as endorsing either step; it records only that they are no longer in conflict.
- Inventory counts, the 2026-07-03 last-publish date and the 12-row `carousel_posts` state all come from a DB read I could not repeat in this session. The filesystem corroborates the run dates and the abandonment pattern exactly, and every code/line claim in §1.5 was re-verified against the repo today, but the 899 total and the per-category counts were not. The same applies to the row stored at 99 tickets cited in §1.1, which is §4.3's measurement, not a reading taken here.
- The derivation that sports-outdoors is near-unreachable by the picker is window-scale, not corpus-scale: `select.mjs:20` caps the pool at 300 rows closing 1–7 days out, the derivation assumes the heavier categories routinely field three-to-five draws inside that window, and it is computed at the shipped `n = 5`. A thin week, a week where the 300-row cap truncates the window, or a change to the deck size could invert the result. The conclusion is robust for typical days, not universal.
- The competitive follower counts, the unoccupied-territory ranking and the cliché inventory all come from a single headless-browser crawl on one day (17 Sep 2026). Storm Competitions' profile was age-gated and not viewable, and Bounty's is private, so the operator picture has holes.
- Some code in the inventory was last modified after the final publish and has therefore never run in production: `publish.mjs` (12 Sep), `config.json` (6 Sep; three post-publish edits — luxury's `seoKeyword`, the Supabase URL repoint and the publishable-key removal — none touching the category set), `styles.css` (26 Aug, the `glass` theme), `build.mjs` and `render.mjs` (20 Aug). The specific defect lines are not affected — `git log -L` confirms `render.mjs:67` and `styles.css:358` trace to `35e000c` and `styles.css:346` to `c97816d`, both commits dated 2026-07-02 and both preceding the 3 July publish — but neighbouring behaviour may differ from what the 12 published posts actually used.
- **Every line number in §1.5 is a snapshot of the 2026-09-17 read and will drift on the first refactor.** One citation inherited downstream is already wrong (`select.mjs:29` for a test that lives at `:40`), and this draft corrected three of its own (`plan.mjs:22` → `:23` for the archive name, `plan.mjs:70–74` → `:72–76` for the `selection.json` fields, `render.mjs:64`/`:116` → `:62`/`:114` for the two `.pill` emission sites). Sections that quote a line rather than a symbol should expect to re-verify, and a citation that cannot be re-found should be treated as stale rather than as refuted.
- The A3 count (18 of 28 `font-size` declarations at or below 46px) is a mechanical grep over `styles.css` and includes declarations on elements that may never co-occur on one slide. It is a reliable signal that the type scale bottoms out too low, not a per-slide legibility audit; a slide-by-slide render check could find fewer offending elements in practice. The same caveat applies to A7's layer count, which is a DOM count first and a painted count second.
- §1 records that the repo's own `DAILY.md:9` asserts a reel-first doctrine that the spec overrides on third-party medians — and overrides it on a **views** figure while the spec's own success criteria are reach-denominated. If the account's twelve historical posts genuinely show reels reaching people and carousels not, the override is being made on population data against local evidence, and the instrumentation gap in section D means that local evidence cannot currently be re-examined.
- Fixing the template does not fix the 76-day dormancy, whose proximate cause is that a human-triggered routine stopped being triggered. A better design that still depends on someone saying "publish today" can go dark again the same week it ships — and the rework adds manual steps (image QA, compliance triage, caption authoring, metric transcription) on top of the gate that already failed twice at zero marginal effort.
