## §3 Brand system: palette, type, chrome and tokens

## 3. Brand system: palette, type, chrome and tokens

This section fixes the visual constants of the approved direction — "The Verdict + The Board's chrome": newsprint editorial with rail-blue standing bands. Everything here is a flat CSS custom property, because of the architectural constraint set out in §3.7: the video templates inherit design by regex-scraping `:root` and `[data-theme]` blocks out of `carousel/styles.css`, and nothing else survives that lift.

**What this section owns, and what it does not.** §3.5 is the sole normative owner of the type scale, the gutter, both tracks, the three type floors and rules T1–T4. §3.2/§3.7 are the sole owner of the colour token table and the `:root` block, including the hex of `--rule`, `--scene-tone` and `--rail-meta`. §3.4 owns the type stack — which families and which weights exist — and the measured glyph advances. Everything else is referenced, not restated: the odds band's origin, rows, ceiling and surface assignment, the count-slide vertical budget and the E2 module's height on every surface are §4.4's and §4.7's; the conditions band's field list, strings, line count and height are §10.2's; the annotation slot's capacity is §4.8's; the evidence predicate behind verdict green is §10.4's; per-category scene geometry, area and tone floor are §8's; per-canvas rail and masthead geometry belongs to §5.2, §6.3 and §7.2. Where those sections publish a number, §3 does not repeat it.

All repo references below were checked against the working tree on 17 Sep 2026 and carry file:line. All contrast ratios are **CALCULATED** in-session (WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula). All glyph advances are **MEASURED** in-session from the bundled woff2 files with fontTools 4.62.1 (`hmtx` advance ÷ `head.unitsPerEm`), not quoted from a nominal figure.

---

### 3.1 What the palette has to do

Four jobs, in priority order:

1. **Survive the token lift.** `carousel/reel-template.mjs:46`, `carousel/story.mjs:31` and `carousel/reel.mjs:69` each run the identical regex `/(?:^|\n)\s*(?::root|\[data-theme="[^"]+"\])\s*\{[^}]*\}/g` against the stylesheet text (all three verified verbatim). A value that is not a flat declaration inside one non-nested brace pair does not reach the Reel or the Story. (`reel-template.mjs:47` additionally lifts the `.p-embers|golddust|fireflies|holo` particle skeletons — see §3.8.)
2. **Make the added value visible.** Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines exclude "unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value" (help.instagram.com/313829416281232 — OFFICIAL). PDD republishes other operators' photography daily. The ticket cap, the odds and the closing date are the added value, so the palette has to give them a colour of their own rather than leave them as grey body text.
3. **Not look like an operator.** Every direct rival observed on 17 Sep 2026 sits on dark ground with gold or orange glow — Omaze navy+gold, Elite black+red+purple, BOTB dark, and PDD's own site dark+orange. Light ground is the only unoccupied territory, and operators structurally cannot follow, because glow needs dark to work.
4. **Read at 1012.5px wide.** The profile grid centre-crops a 4:5 upload to 3:4, taking 33.75px off each side (OFFICIAL, Meta), keeping x 33.75 … 1046.25. Contrast has to hold at that size and at feed scroll speed.

---

### 3.2 The palette

Sixteen colour tokens. All hex values are the approved direction as chosen by the product owner, except `--rule`, `--scene-tone` and `--rail-meta`, which are reconciliations recorded below.

| Token | Hex | On `--ground` | Semantic rule — what it is allowed to mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ground` | `#F7F5F0` | — | The page. Newsprint warm white. The default ground of every still and every video frame. L = 0.913702. |
| `--surface` | `#FFFFFF` | 1.09:1 | A bento tile inset on the ground. Separation comes from the value step, not a stroke (see §3.6). |
| `--scene-tone` | `#F3F1EC` | 1.04:1 | **The single tone in which a scene ground renders on the still canvas, and the darkest scene pixel permitted there.** L = 0.880214; ΔL from `--ground` = 0.033488, a 3.67% luminance step. §8 owns where it paints and over how much area; §3 owns only the hex and the floor. |
| `--ink` | `#14161A` | 16.62:1 | All primary type. Never tinted, never gradient-filled, never stroked. 18.11:1 on `--surface`, 16.05:1 on `--scene-tone`. |
| `--ink-meta` | `#5A5F66` | 5.91:1 | Secondary type **on a paper ground only**: field labels, source attributions, the operator name, the cover dateline. Never a figure, never a headline, and never on a rail band, where `--rail-ink` and `--rail-meta` apply. 6.43:1 on `--surface`, 5.70:1 on `--scene-tone`. |
| `--hairline` | `#D8D3C8` | 1.37:1 | **Decorative rules only.** Non-load-bearing. Never text, never a dot, never the edge of a meaningful graphic. |
| `--rule` | `#8C8677` | 3.33:1 | **Meaning-bearing graphics.** The odds dot field's unmarked dot, chip borders, board rules, the sheet-edge hairline. Clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor for meaningful non-text content, because the field of dots *is* the message. 3.63:1 on `--surface`, 3.21:1 on `--scene-tone`. |
| `--rail` | `#14385F` | 10.95:1 | **Standing chrome only.** The fill of the top and bottom bands. Not a highlight, not an accent, never applied to a datum. |
| `--rail-ink` | `#F7F5F0` | 10.95:1 on `--rail` | Type set on a rail band. The default for every rail string. |
| `--rail-meta` | `#B9C6D6` | 6.88:1 on `--rail` | **Secondary type on a rail band only** — the conditions band's subordinate lines, as §10.2 assigns them, and any subordinate rail string. Full opacity, never a figure. **Forbidden on paper: 1.59:1 on `--ground`.** 9.63:1 on the late register's rail. |
| `--rail-accent` | `#FFC53D` | 7.56:1 on `--rail` | The amber keyline, and **at most one emphasis run per rail** — in practice the figures inside the dated stamp. Never the whole string, never outside a rail band. |
| `--verdict` | `#0F6B45` | 6.01:1 | **Checked facts only** — see the rule below. 6.54:1 on `--surface`, 5.80:1 on `--scene-tone`. |
| `--verdict-tint` | `#E6F2EA` | 1.06:1 | Fill behind a block of checked facts. Fill only. Not a bed for the dot field (see below). `--verdict` 5.69:1 on it; `--ink` 15.74:1. |
| `--deadline` | `#B3202C` | 6.10:1 | **Deadlines.** The closing date or closing time, and nothing else. Not "urgent", not "hot", not a general highlight. **Never on `--rail`: 1.79:1, measured, and forbidden.** |
| `--closing` | `#FFC53D` | 1.45:1 | **Closing state.** A draw inside the closing window §10.2 defines. On `--ground` or `--surface` it is **fill only** — at 1.45:1 amber type on newsprint is illegible, so it is an amber field with `--ink` on top (11.48:1). On `--rail` it is permitted as type at 7.56:1, which is how §10.2's closing state renders. |
| `--dot-hit` | `#0F6B45` | 6.01:1 | The one marked dot in the odds field. Same value as `--verdict` by intent, separate name by design (see below). §4.7 owns when it is drawn and when it is omitted; §3 owns only its colour. |

**What "a checked fact" means, and what may be green.** `--verdict` and `--dot-hit` paint a figure only where one of two conditions holds:

- **(a)** the figure sits on a row that satisfies §10.4's eligibility predicate — source URL, capture timestamp inside §10.4's window, and a renderable extraction method. §10.4 is normative; §3 restates none of its columns, values or window.
- **(b)** the figure is a count of PDD's own published artefacts in the same asset, checkable by the reader without leaving the post — in practice `drawsRendered` (§5.11), which the build freezes before the first PNG is written. The evidence held before publication is the build record itself.

Everything else is `--ink` or `--ink-meta`. **PDD's own computed assessments are not green.** The Trust Score is a PDD-derived rating, not an operator-sourced figure, and it satisfies neither (a) nor (b): it renders in `--ink` on `--ground` with a `--rule` border, and the mint tint is not used behind it. This closes the collision between §3.2's absolute green rule, §5.13's mint-and-green chip and §10.5 rule 3's hard fail; it does not restrict §5.4's cover proof line, whose deck count and minimum ticket cap are covered by (b) and (a) respectively.

**Why green is the scarcest colour in the system.** CAP 3.7 requires documentary evidence for an objective claim held *before* publication, and CAP 8.20/8.21 forbid exaggerating chances of winning. Binding green to §10.4's predicate makes the compliance rule visible in the render: if the pipeline cannot prove a number, it cannot paint it green. `carousel/honesty.mjs:19` already implements the equivalent logic for the value line — `capValue()` takes gross ticket revenue (`total_prize_value`) and caps it at the operator's own stated cash alternative — and that module, plus `altTexts()` at `honesty.mjs:31` (written to `out/alt.json` by `build.mjs:161`, verified), must survive the rework unchanged.

**The dot field's legal beds are `--ground` (3.33:1) and `--scene-tone` (3.21:1).** `--surface` and `--verdict-tint` are excluded. The honest reason has changed and is worth stating, because the old one is now false: the retired `#948C7C` measured **2.90:1 on `--verdict-tint`** and genuinely failed 1.4.11, whereas `#8C8677` measures **3.15:1** there and passes. The exclusion therefore survives on margin, not on failure — 3.15:1 is 5% over the floor and has never been checked after the profile-grid downscale, where `--ground` has 11% and `--scene-tone` 7%. `--surface` at 3.63:1 is excluded for a different reason: no section places the dot field in a bento tile, and two legal beds means the field's measured ratio varies by slide, which nobody can check at a glance. One bed rule, one number.

**Three retired hexes, one survivor.** `--dot-empty` `#948C7C` (§3.2, 3.06:1) and `#8B867B` (§4.5, 3.33:1) are both retired in favour of `--rule` `#8C8677` (3.33:1). `#948C7C` cannot survive any scene tone: on `#F3F1EC` it is 2.952:1, a 1.4.11 failure, so the scene ground and the dot field could not coexist. `#8B867B` and `#8C8677` are indistinguishable in ratio (3.33:1 on ground, 3.21:1 on tone, to two decimal places), so the tiebreak is that the dot field and the meaning-bearing hairline are one job and should carry one token: `--rule`. `--dot-empty` as a name is deleted outright.

**`--rule` has moved, and the failure mode was silent.** In the earlier draft `--rule` was `#D8D3C8` and meant "decorative, never a dot"; the decorative value now lives on `--hairline` and `--rule` carries the meaning-bearing graphite. The reason this had to be settled here rather than downstream: both blocks are lifted by the same regex into the same `<style>`, so a duplicate `--rule` resolves last-block-wins with no error, and a dot field authored as `var(--rule)` against the old value renders at **1.37:1** — below 1.4.11 and essentially invisible at profile-grid size. There is exactly one definition of each name, and it is in §3.7.

**`--rail-meta` is new, and it is added because it was already rendering.** §10.2 sets the conditions band's two sentence-case lines in `#B9C6D6` on every asset, and §5.14 named the token without ever defining it. An undefined custom property does not throw: `var(--rail-meta)` resolves to an invalid value and the run inherits its parent's colour, silently, on the one element the ASA position makes non-negotiable. §3.7 is the only place a token may be defined, so it is defined here. CALCULATED: **6.88:1 on `--rail`** — §10.2 and §5.14 both publish 6.87:1, the same measurement to rounding — against `--rail-ink`'s 10.95:1, which is enough hierarchy to separate the band's leading line from its subordinate ones without either dropping below AA. It is **forbidden on `--ground` and `--surface`** at 1.59:1, the exact mirror of `--deadline`'s 1.79:1 prohibition on the rail. §10.2 keeps the strings, the line count, the weight and which line takes which token; §3 adds only the name, the hex and the two prohibitions.

**`--rail-accent` and `--closing` hold the same hex deliberately.** They are separate tokens because they are separate meanings — one is chrome furniture, one is a data state — and a future divergence must not require a call-site hunt. The same applies to `--dot-hit` and `--verdict`.

---

### 3.3 Category identity carries no colour

This is a design judgement, and it goes against the natural reading of the brief ("each category its own unique design"), so the reasoning is stated in full.

Green, red and amber are semantically locked above. Blue is chrome. That leaves no uncommitted hue space for eight category colours that would not collide with a state colour. A slide that colour-codes eight categories *and* three states is asserting eleven meanings at once — which is precisely the hazard CAP names verbatim: *"Promoters should ensure that the page design, layout or format of the promotion is not misleading… should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true."*

So: **zero per-category colour tokens.** Category identity is carried by:

- **(a) §8's scene layer** — the monochrome `--scene-tone` ground on the still canvas, and the scene lanes on the three 9:16 surfaces. §8 owns the geometry, the area and the per-surface tone floor; §3 owns only the tone's hex and the rule that no scene pixel on a still may be darker than it.
- **(b) the category kicker** on draw slides, where §5 allocates one.

**The rail-band category word is withdrawn as a carrier.** The earlier draft named it, and no rail in the spec carries it: both masthead slots are spoken for by the wordmark and the dated stamp, and §10.2's stamp arithmetic leaves no third slot. Saying so costs §3.3 half a support, and that is the honest position rather than a carrier nobody delivers.

**Scenes may vary exactly one token.** `--scene-wash` — the low-chroma rgba tint the scene module lays over its background art on the three 9:16 surfaces — is the only custom property a scene definition may override. It is **not used on the still canvas**, where the ground is the single `--scene-tone` and there is no artwork to keep `--ink` legible over. §8.3's per-scene `tokens` map is closed to this one property: no `--fs-*`, no `--lh-*`, no `--gutter`, and no colour token from §3.2. A scene that needed a second token would be asserting a ninth, tenth or eleventh meaning, which is the thing this section exists to prevent.

**`--scene-wash` is bounded so the rule is checkable without the artwork.** Default `rgba(247,245,240,.86)` — the `--ground` RGB at 86%. A per-category variant may retint the RGB but must (a) keep alpha ≥ 0.86 and (b) use an RGB that itself carries `--ink` at ≥15:1. That pair guarantees legibility against *any* art, including pure black: composited over #000 at α = 0.86 the default wash resolves to ≈`#D4D3CE` and still carries `--ink` at **12.08:1** (CALCULATED). The earlier formulation — "≥7:1 against the composited result" — was unbuildable, because the composited result depends on artwork the token author has never seen.

**No scene mark may use a semantic colour.** The sports scene's pennant is `--hairline` `#D8D3C8`, not `#FFC53D`: amber inside a scene would be `--rail-accent` used outside a rail and `--closing` used as decoration rather than a state, breaching both rules in §3.2 at once. This is recorded here because the hex is §3's; the mark's geometry is §8's.

What this replaces is worth stating plainly. `carousel/config.json` defines six categories; `carousel/config.mjs:8-11` sets `FALLBACK.theme = "default"` (line 9) and 46 ember particles (line 10), `config.mjs:15` supplies the hook `"WIN BIG"` for any slug not in the file, and `"default"` is the `:root` block at `styles.css:14` — the car-draws orange fire palette. So sports-outdoors and home-garden, 147 draws and 16% of live inventory, currently render as car draws. (`house-draws` has the opposite problem: a theme and, in the sample taken, no enterable inventory.) The new system has one palette, so there is nothing to fall through to in colour — structure falls through to §8's NEUTRAL scene instead.

---

### 3.4 The type stack

| Role | Face | Weights | Bundled today? | OFL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Display — prize names, headlines, the wordmark | Bricolage Grotesque | 700, 800 | **Yes** — `carousel/assets/fonts/bricolage-grotesque-latin-{700,800}-normal.woff2` | SIL OFL 1.1 |
| Text — running copy, labels, conditions, chrome | Inter | 400, 600, 700 | **Yes** — `inter-latin-{400,600,700}-normal.woff2` | SIL OFL 1.1 |
| Figures — every numeral, every currency amount | JetBrains Mono | **700 only** | **Yes** — `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2` | SIL OFL 1.1 |

**JetBrains Mono 400 and 500 are not bundled and are no longer wanted.** The earlier draft made downloading them a prerequisite. Every figure in the reconciled spec sets in Mono 700, so the gap is closed by deletion rather than by a download: the bundle needs no new file, the "missing weight degrades to the next family and breaks tabular alignment silently" failure class (§4.10) cannot occur, and §7.2's dateline at Mono 500 is illegal rather than merely unbundled. **Mono 700 is the only weight the brand system permits.**

**Inter 500 is also retired, and that has one downstream consequence worth naming.** The stack is Inter 400/600/700. §10.2's conditions band sets L1 in Inter 600 uppercase and L2/L3 in sentence case at a weight of 500 — a weight this stack does not carry. The sentence-case lines therefore set in **Inter 400**, which is the running-copy weight everywhere else in the system and still gives the band a 400/600 hierarchy. This is §3 exercising its own ownership of the stack, not a change to §10.2's strings or line count; it is flagged as a handoff so §10.2 restates the weight rather than inheriting a face that will not load.

**The wordmark is the one display-face exception in the chrome.** `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` sets in Bricolage Grotesque 800 uppercase at `--fs-label` with `--tr-label`; everything else in a rail band is Inter. It is a wordmark, not running copy; it appears once per frame; and one face across all four surfaces is worth more than §5.2 rendering Inter 700 and §6.3 rendering Bricolage 800. MEASURED width at 44px with 0.08em tracking: **471.2px** in Bricolage 800, 480.5px in Inter 700.

**Cabin is rejected.** It was a candidate for the chrome bands as a legally bundleable Johnston/Gill relative. At 44px uppercase with wide tracking a fourth family buys almost no differentiation and costs a face, a licence entry and a load path. Inter 700 does the job for chrome copy; Bricolage 800 does it for the wordmark.

**Why every figure is mono, not display.** `carousel/styles.css:174-176` records a defect found in this repository, verbatim:

> *"Space Grotesk, not Bricolage: Bricolage's single-storey pound sign is near-identical in silhouette to its own ampersand, and 'OR £30,000' rendered as 'OR &30,000' at slide size. On a site whose whole pitch is honest, legible prices, an ambiguous £ is disqualifying."*

That is the whole argument. Bricolage is a fine display face and a bad figure face. Routing every numeral through a monospaced face fixes it structurally and buys tabular alignment for free, which is what a board needs. The stylesheet already does this once, at `styles.css:282-283`, for the tech theme's data line; the rework generalises it.

**Hard rule:** Inter and Bricolage never set a numeral. If a numeral appears in an Inter or Bricolage run it is a bug, and it is the same class of bug as the pound sign — a figure rendered in a face that was not checked for figures.

**Measured advances.** All six retained faces, read from the shipped woff2:

| Face | MEASURED advance | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| JetBrains Mono 700 | **0.600em exactly** for `0`–`9`, `,`, `.`, `£`, `$` and space | `hmtx` 600 / `head.unitsPerEm` 1000. Not nominal — measured. |
| Bricolage Grotesque 800 | uppercase A–Z mean **0.6740em** (`I` 0.3030 … `W` 1.0010); digits 0.6005em | unweighted mean over A–Z |
| Bricolage Grotesque 700 | uppercase mean **0.6648em** | |
| Inter 700 | uppercase mean **0.7011em**; upm 2048 | |
| Inter 600 | uppercase mean **0.6946em**; lowercase 0.5541em | |
| Inter 400 | uppercase mean **0.6815em**; lowercase 0.5363em | |

Three consequences a builder must not skip. First, **these run 2.4–2.5% wider than the advances quoted elsewhere in the spec** (0.6573 / 0.6487 / 0.6782), so any fit computed against those means has less headroom than stated. Second, **a mean describes no real word**: `I` and `W` differ by 3.3× in Bricolage 800. Third, and in the other direction, **a mean-derived capacity is not a verdict on a real string**, because spaces, digits and separators are narrower than the uppercase mean — §6.3's floor-row line `18+ · UK · ENTER ON OPERATOR SITE` is 33 characters, which a 0.6946em mean puts at 1,008.6px and over a 950px track, but the string itself MEASURES **794.6px at Inter 600 44px and fits**. Means are for sizing decisions; every rendered string is measured at render, and the two must not be confused in either direction.

**The glyph budget on the figure tier — and there is now only one.** At `--fs-figure` (120px) a mono glyph is exactly **72.0px**, so nine glyphs are **648.0px** against the 895px content well — 247.0px spare. `4,500,000`, the measured maximum stored ticket cap, is exactly nine glyphs. T4's nine-glyph budget therefore holds with room for an advance up to 0.8287em, 38% over the measured 0.600em. **No figure node sets at `--fs-hero` anywhere in the spec**: §7.2's settled band table puts the odds figure at `--fs-figure` 120/120 on all four surfaces and §4.4's E2 module takes no surface parameter, so the hero-tier figure arithmetic published earlier (nine glyphs = 810.0px) is retired rather than kept as a live check.

**The glyph budget on the hero display tier.** `--fs-hero` now carries Bricolage 800 headlines and nothing else. At the MEASURED 0.6740em a hero glyph is **101.1px**, so eight glyphs measure **808.8px** against the 895px well and nine measure **909.9px**, which overflows it. That advance is the input to the per-word cap §5.5 and §10.6a apply to headline strings — §3 supplies the measurement and the well, and owns neither the cap nor the strings it constrains. The direction of the correction matters: at the 0.6573em quoted elsewhere in the spec nine glyphs come to 887.4px and sit inside the well by 7.6px, so a cap derived from the older mean is the one that fails at render.

What does **not** fit is the qualifier set in the same run: `1 IN 4,500,000` is 14 glyphs = **1,008.0px** at `--fs-figure`, over the 895px well by 113.0px. That is the arithmetic behind T4's bare-numeral rule. The permitted wording of the qualifier, and where it sits, are §10.6a's; §3 states only the budget.

**OFL position.** All three families are SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Three consequences, the third of which is a reading of the licence rather than legal advice:

- OFL 1.1 §2 requires the copyright notice and licence text to accompany any redistribution of the *font software*. **`carousel/assets/fonts/` contains 17 woff2 files and no licence text at all** (verified by directory listing — the directory holds nothing but the 17 files), and **the repository is public** — `api.github.com/repos/chanakya-goyal/prizedrawsdaily-aggregator` returns `"private": false`, checked 17 Sep 2026. So this is a live §2 gap, not untidiness. The rework must add a per-family copyright line and a copy of OFL 1.1 alongside the files. `carousel/assets/audio/LICENSES.md` is the in-repo precedent and format to copy.
- The Reserved Font Name clause is not engaged **by anything PDD does**: `carousel/fonts.mjs` base64-inlines the files unmodified, subsets nothing and renames nothing. (The woff2 files are third-party Fontsource Latin subsets, redistributed as received; the notice text must be taken from each family's upstream release, not written from scratch.)
- The rendered PNG and MP4 contain rasterised glyphs, not font software, so the published social assets themselves carry no OFL obligation. The repository does, and it is public today.

**Loading stays as it is.** `carousel/fonts.mjs` inlines each face as a base64 `@font-face` with `font-display: block`, which is correct for headless capture — it removes any chance of a FOUT being screenshotted.

**Eleven faces are retired, and four of them can go today.** The eleven are the nine obviously-dead faces (Anton 400, Oswald 500/600/700, Playfair Display 700-italic and 800, Space Grotesk 700, Fraunces 900, Bungee 400) **plus Bricolage Grotesque 400 and Inter 500**, which the stack above does not use. MEASURED: the bundle is **333,628 bytes across 17 faces today**; the six retained faces total **138,608 bytes**; the retired eleven are 195,020 bytes. Because Mono 400 and 500 are no longer wanted, the end state is **138,608 bytes across 6 faces — 41.5% of today's bundle, with no new file downloaded.** **Six is the normative count**, and it reconciles with §12.1's "8 of the 17 registered" by exactly two files: §12.1 counts a family as named when any weight of it survives, so it counts Bricolage Grotesque 400 and Inter 500, which this stack does not carry. MEASURED from the directory listing: the eleven retired faces are 195,020 bytes and §12.1's nine orphans are 148,384; the 46,636-byte difference is Bricolage 400 (22,364) plus Inter 500 (24,272). The two figures are not in conflict once those two weights are accounted for — §12.1's byte total is correct for the deletion it performs, and §3.4 owns which weights exist, so the surviving-face count is six.

The eleven entries in the `FACES` array at `fonts.mjs:3-23` are what actually load them, and a face may not leave that array before its last consumer does. Re-grepped 17 Sep 2026, the reachability splits cleanly in two:

- **Four are already unreachable and leave now, at zero risk — 93,104 bytes.** Playfair Display 700-italic and 800 are named exactly once in the whole repository, at `styles.css:75` as the value of `--font-kicker`, and `--font-kicker` has **zero** `var()` consumers (see §3.7) — so no rule can resolve to Playfair today. Bricolage Grotesque is not named in any live rule at all (its only two appearances in `styles.css`, at `:174` and `:190`, are inside comments), so Bricolage 400 is dead. Inter is named only at `styles.css:178`, again as a `--font-kicker` value, so Inter 500 is dead.
- **Seven leave with their consumers — 101,916 bytes.** `'Anton'` appears **21 times** and `'Oswald'` **28 times** across `styles.css`, `render.mjs`, `reel.mjs`, `reel-template.mjs` and `story.mjs` — as hardcoded family-stack fallbacks (`var(--font-display), 'Anton', sans-serif`) and as literal families (`body { font-family: 'Oswald' … }` at `styles.css:7` and `reel.mjs:81`). Space Grotesk, Fraunces and Bungee are each reachable through `--font-display` in a theme block (`styles.css:177`, `:122`, `:143`), which is live. Deleting these faces first would silently change the display type of every legacy rule, so each leaves the array in the same commit that retires its last consumer — see §3.8, which is a schedule with a named performer per row, not a list of edits to make now.

---

### 3.5 The type scale

**§3.5 is the sole normative owner of the type scale, the gutter, both tracks, the three type floors and rules T1–T4.** No other section publishes a size, a line-height, a gutter, a track width or a legal-size list; §5.14, §6.6 and §7.2 are consumer tables that cite this section and state only what they use.

**Nine legal sizes: eight display steps plus one legally-scoped step.** Every line-height is a multiple of 5px, adopting GOV.UK's rhythm (from the UK visual-direction research). This establishes a 5px baseline unit that does not currently exist: `carousel/styles.css` contains exactly **six** `line-height` declarations in 31,541 bytes — at lines 346, 374, 393, 394, 420 and 477, all unitless, all on display type; everything else inherits `normal` (MEASURED).

| Token | Size | Line-height | Ratio | Face / weight | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--fs-hero` / `--lh-hero` | 150px | 150px | 1.000 | Bricolage 800 | **At most one node per frame; zero is legal.** Cover headline, closing headline, Reel open frame. No figure node sets at this step on any surface, and the Story carries no `--fs-hero` node at all (§7.2). |
| `--fs-figure` / `--lh-figure` | 120px | 120px | 1.000 | JB Mono 700 | **The odds figure, at this size on all four surfaces. This is the hero-figure floor.** §4.4's E2 module takes no surface parameter. |
| `--fs-display` / `--lh-display` | 88px | 90px | 1.023 | Bricolage 800 | Prize name, one line. |
| `--fs-title` / `--lh-title` | 68px | 70px | 1.029 | Bricolage 700/800 | Prize name, two lines. |
| `--fs-lead` / `--lh-lead` | 56px | 60px | 1.071 | Bricolage 700 / Inter 700 | Prize-name step 3; Reel prize title; closing URL; @handle. |
| `--fs-body` / `--lh-body` | 48px | 60px | 1.250 | Inter 400 / JB Mono 700 | **The running-copy floor on every canvas.** Proof line, ticket price, field values. |
| `--fs-label` / `--lh-label` | 44px | 50px | 1.136 | Inter 600/700 uc / Bricolage 800 uc (wordmark) / JB Mono 700 | Labels, kickers, chips, counters, the wordmark, the odds qualifier. **The editorial floor on any video canvas.** |
| `--fs-legal` / `--lh-legal` | 38px | 45px | 1.184 | Inter 400/600 | **The conditions band, on every canvas, and nothing else.** §10.2 owns the band's strings, line count and height; this step exists so the band's measured size is a legal one. |
| `--fs-micro` / `--lh-micro` | 34px | 40px | 1.176 | Inter 400 / JB Mono 700 | The still canvas's micro tier (dateline, board index, category kicker) and, **on any canvas, §10.4's dated provenance stamp**. |

Tracking: `--tr-display: -0.02em`, `--tr-label: 0.08em`, `--tr-figure: 0`.
Spacing, on the same 5px unit: **5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 60 / 90 / 120**. The 15px step is named `--sp-15` for its value rather than renumbered into the ordinal ladder, because renumbering would invalidate every existing `--sp-n` reference in §4 and §5 for no gain.

**Why 184px and 116px are gone.** Neither had a consumer anywhere in the spec: no section set a 184px node, and the prize-name ladder steps 88 → 68 → 56 without touching 116. Both shipped inside the `:root` block that three video templates lift, which is the dead-token pattern §3.7 identifies and removes. 40px is folded into 44px; nothing needed both.

**One gutter: `--gutter: 65px`, on every canvas.**

- **Chrome track** = x 65 … 1015 = **950px**, on the 1080×1350 still and on the 1080×1920 Reel and Story. It is numerically identical to Meta's 9:16 Safe Box A width, so the platform constraint and the brand constant are one number and the class of drift that produced three competing gutters is structurally closed.
- **Content well** (still slides that carry §5.9's sheet edge) = x 65 … 960 = **895px**. The well is **not** "the gutter to the sheet-edge hairline": the hairline sits at x 1015 and a deliberate **55px right margin** lies between it and the well. Nothing text-bearing crosses x 960. Where there is no sheet edge — the three 9:16 canvases and the still closing slide — the well is the full 950px chrome track.
- **Crop headroom** on slide 1: 65 − 33.75 = **31.25px each side**.
- 65 sits on the 5px grid; 64 does not.

**The content well is exactly the odds band's width, and that is the point.** §4.4 remains the sole owner of the band's origin, columns, rows, ceiling and surface assignment; §3 publishes the two cell tokens the band is derived from and one consequence of them. That consequence is this: at §4.4's 60-column geometry the band measures 60 × `--dot-size` + 59 × `--dot-gap` = 600 + 295 = **895px**, which is the still content well to the pixel. Where band width and well width are equal, left-aligning at the well's left edge and centring inside the well are the same placement — so the origin question that produced two different answers in two different sections has nothing left to decide, whatever §4.4 writes. At any other gutter the band is narrower than its column and the question reopens.

Arithmetic, shown: chrome track 1015 − 65 = 950. Well 960 − 65 = 895. Right margin on a still slide 1015 − 960 = 55px. A band filling the well ends at 65 + 895 = 960, which is 55px inside the chrome track and 86.25px inside the profile crop at 1046.25.

**The causal direction, stated once so nobody re-derives it backwards: §3.5 sized the well to the band, not the band to the well.** §4.4 owns the band and derives it from §3.7's `--dot-size` and `--dot-gap`; §3.5 chose the gutter that makes the well equal to it. §3 does not derive the band, the count-slide vertical budget or the E2 module, and it restates none of §4.4's block heights.

**The 70px gutter is retired and may not be restated anywhere.** Three constraints decide it, and none of them is taste.

1. **Box A.** At 65 the chrome track *is* Meta Safe Box A: 1015 − 65 = 950. At 70 it is 940px at x 70 … 1010 — safe inside Box A, but a different number from the 9:16 track, so the still would carry 940 while the Reel and the Story carry 950. Two tracks is the exact drift that produced 64, 65 and 70 in the first place.
2. **The band is not a free parameter, and 70 leaves a residual.** 60 × 10 + 59 × 5 = 895px is forced by `--dot-size` and `--dot-gap`. At 65 the well is 895 and the band fills its column, so left-aligning and centring are the same placement and the origin has nothing left to decide. At 70 the band is 35px narrower than a 930px well and 45px narrower than a 940px column, and a centred origin at **x 87.5 or x 92.5** stays permanently re-derivable by any author who does the division. That residual, not the gutter, is what keeps reopening.
3. **The crop does not decide it.** Both clear x 33.75 … 1046.25 — 65 leaves 31.25px of headroom, 70 leaves 36.25px. A 5px difference on the one slide the crop ever touches does not outweigh a permanent second track and a permanently reopenable band origin. Both sit on the 5px grid, so this argument kills only 64.

The cost is that 5px of crop headroom on slide 1, paid forever. The consequences, now settled rather than proposed: the band's origin question closes by itself, because the well and the band are the same width and §3 leaves the coordinate to §4.4; §5 re-derives at g = 65 throughout (chrome track 940 → **950**, content well 930 → **895**, every left edge x 70 → **x 65**); §5.9's sheet-edge hairline moves x 1000 → **x 1015** with the 96px strip at x 1015 … 1111, **65px on-frame and 31px off**; and §8 recomputes its still scene-region areas from the rects §5 supplies. §5 publishes derivations of the two numbers above, never a gutter or a track of its own.

**Four hard rules, all mechanically checkable.**

- **T1 — the odds inversion.** The odds figure sets at `--fs-figure` (120px) and is **never smaller than the prize name on the same frame**. Guaranteed by construction: the prize name's largest step is 88px, so the ratio is ≥ **1.36**. Today `render.mjs:67` appends odds as a trailing fragment inside `.closes` at 33px (`styles.css:358`) against `.prize` at 98px (`styles.css:346`) — a ratio of **0.337**. `render.mjs:120` carries the identical defect on the feature layout (`.feat-closes` 32px, `styles.css:382`, against `.feat-name` 96px, `styles.css:374`) — **0.333**. This is a distribution-eligibility fix under the Recommendation Guidelines, not a preference.
- **T2 — one anchor at most, and zero is legal.** T2 is `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame. It is an **upper bound, never "exactly one"**, and `assertTypeContract()` must implement it as one. The node is the cover headline on a surface that has a cover: carousel slide 1, the closing slide, the Reel open frame. **A carousel draw slide, a Reel card and the Story carry no `--fs-hero` node at all** — the Story's largest node is the odds figure at `--fs-figure` 120/120. The earlier assignment, "and the odds figure where it does not [have a cover]", is withdrawn: it prescribed a 150px Story figure, which is payable only out of §7.2's photograph band — a cost §7.2 has measured and refused. §3 does not restate that band's heights. That is now a settled reading of T2 rather than a departure from it. Asserted at node level, never at line-box level — a three-line 150px headline is one node. The earlier rule ("every slide needs a ≥150px element inside the crop") mis-generalised a slide-1 requirement: only the first child of a carousel is ever profile-grid cropped (§5.1), so inner slides have no grid-survivability requirement to satisfy.
- **T3 — nine legal sizes, three floors.** Every computed `font-size` in the rendered DOM is one of 150 / 120 / 88 / 68 / 56 / 48 / 44 / 38 / 34, subject to: **48px is the running-copy floor on every canvas; 44px is the editorial floor on any video canvas; 34px exists on a still for the micro tier and, on any canvas, for §10.4's dated stamp; 38px is the conditions band and nothing else.** The two sub-44px exceptions on video are named, measured and both are fixed-position standing chrome whose re-read cost after the first card is near zero — the same ground §6.5 already uses to exclude the counter from its read budget. Everything editorial on a video canvas is ≥44px. **No tenth step was created for §4.8's clipped-state annotation row**: it stays at `--fs-label` 44px, and §10.6a shortened the string to fit the slot §4.8 measures instead. The slot's capacity is §4.8's figure and is not restated here. `--fs-legal` remains the conditions band's and nothing else's; `--fs-micro` remains the still micro tier's, plus §10.4's dated stamp on any canvas. Today **18 of 28** `font-size` declarations in `styles.css` are ≤46px and **10 of 24** in `reel-template.mjs` are below 44px (MEASURED).
- **T4 — the glyph budget.** The `--fs-figure` figure node carries the **bare numeral only, at most 9 glyphs**. The qualifier sets at `--fs-label` in the same lockup, directly above, with a gap of at most `--sp-1` (10px) and no node between. At 10 or more glyphs the build does not shrink the figure and does not abbreviate it — the draw is dropped, per §10.6a. The permitted wording of every string in that lockup is §10.6a's; §3 states the budget and the adjacency, not the words. The "qualifier at ≥50% of the figure's type size" rule is retired and replaced by this adjacency rule, because at 120px it would demand a 60px qualifier that no layout in the spec affords.

**The assertion ships in v1, hard-failing, in the same commit as the §5/§6/§7 rewrite.** `assertTypeContract()`, modelled on `assertVideoContract` at `carousel/encode.mjs:36` (verified: its guard clauses at `:45–50` throw on `codec_name !== "h264"`, `pix_fmt !== "yuv420p"`, wrong dimensions and `codec_name !== "aac"`, and it is called from `reel.mjs:265` and `story.mjs:273`). T3 is an enumeration check on computed style; T4 is a `textContent.length` check on one node with 247px of measured margin; T1 is a two-node comparison guaranteed by construction (88 < 120); T2 is a node count, evaluated as an upper bound. None is content-dependent. **It must not land before the surface sections are on this scale** — an assert that fails every legitimate render is switched off on day one, which is how the spec acquired three scales in the first place. The measured-fit and overflow checks (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`) are a separate class and stay report-only for the first week, because they depend on real line-breaking of live operator titles.

**One further assertion ships beside it, and it is the gutter's.** The renderer asserts that `--gutter` resolves to **65px** and that the two constants the layout runs against are **950** and **895**; the measured-fit checks then run against 895 (the well), 950 (the chrome bands and the closing slide) and 1015 (the photo well). A per-node "every left edge is 65" assertion is **explicitly not adopted** — it would fail on the cover board's own Prize and Closes columns and on every chip, which is to say on every legitimate run, and an assertion that fails on every legitimate run is switched off within a week.

---

### 3.6 Standing chrome

The chrome's **colour, type and content contract** are brand constants and live here. Its **geometry does not**: the masthead's height and slot layout are §5.2's, the Reel's rails are §6.3's, the Story's bands are §7.2's, and the conditions band — its height, line count, field list and exact strings on every canvas — is **§10.2's**. §3 previously published `--rail-h-top` and `--rail-h-bottom` as brand constants and they are deleted from the token block, because a value that every canvas overrides is not a constant, and shipping one guaranteed that §3 and §5 would disagree.

The carousel is the reference implementation because it is the primary growth surface (Socialinsider, 35M posts / 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025: median views at the 1–5K tier, carousel 993 vs reel 580).

**Top rail — content and type contract.** Filled `--rail`. It carries exactly two things and no third: the **wordmark** left, Bricolage Grotesque 800 uppercase at `--fs-label` / `--lh-label` with `--tr-label`, in `--rail-ink`; and the **dated stamp** right, its label words in `--rail-ink` and its figures permitted in `--rail-accent` (7.56:1) as the single emphasis run the rail allows. The stamp's face is JetBrains Mono 700 — the only bundled Mono weight. Its size, its exact string and whether it is suppressed on slide 1 are §5.2's and §10.4's; §3 states only that the top-right 180 × 180px on slide 1 must stay clear of content, because that is where Instagram's multi-image indicator sits. This replaces `.pill` at `top: 52px; right: 50px` (`styles.css:328`), which currently sits directly under that indicator.

**Bottom rail — content and type contract.** Filled `--rail`, with a 6px `--rail-accent` keyline along its top edge, carrying the CAP 8.17 significant-conditions strip in Inter at **full opacity**. Two rail type tokens are available to it — `--rail-ink` (10.95:1) and `--rail-meta` (6.88:1) — and which line takes which, like every other property of the band, is §10.2's. Today's equivalent is `.footer .rp` at 19px in `rgba(255,255,255,.55)` (`styles.css:367`) — a fifth the size at half the opacity. The band's fields, strings, line count, per-canvas height and type size are **§10.2's**, and §3 restates none of them; the only constraint §3 imposes is T3, which is why `--fs-legal` (38px) exists as a legal step. The closing state on this band renders `--closing` as type on `--rail` at 7.56:1; `--deadline` is **forbidden** there at a measured 1.79:1.

**Why the rail is standing chrome and not an optional strip.** The ASA is unlikely to consider a social post sufficiently limited by time or space, and expects all significant conditions in the material itself; "link in bio" does not discharge it. A template that cannot render without this band is the design response, and it is why the band is a permanent structural element in §3 rather than a per-slide decision in §5. What goes in it is still §10.2's.

**Why the rail carries no decoration.** A Verizon Media/Publicis study (5,616 US adults, fielded April 2019) measured −12% ad memory when logos crowd the screen alongside captions. That is a seven-year-old US study of *paid* creative and its transfer to an organic UK carousel is unproven, so it is treated as a reason to keep the rail informational rather than as a measured constraint. No second logo, no repeated handle on inner slides, no ornament.

**The per-canvas override mechanism, for the sections that need it.** In all three video templates the lifted token `<style>` is emitted *before* the template's own `<style>`: the lift is at `reel.mjs:76`, `reel-template.mjs:773` and `story.mjs:140`, and each template's own CSS follows at `reel.mjs:78`, `reel-template.mjs:776` and `story.mjs:143`. A later `:root{…}` in the template's own CSS therefore wins on cascade order. That is how a canvas overrides a token. **No §3 token relies on it today** — the rail heights that did are gone — but §5, §6 and §7 do, and the contract is implicit and untested: reordering those style tags, or moving the token lift later, would silently restore the wrong values with no error.

**On the demotion for reels that "contain borders".** Meta's guidance targets a border on the delivered frame, not a card edge inside the composition. That reading is inherited and unverified — Meta publishes no geometry for what counts as a border — so to stay clear of the ambiguity rather than rely on the reading, bento tiles separate by the `--surface`/`--ground` value step rather than a stroke, and `--hairline` rules appear only where a genuine table rule is doing work.

---

### 3.7 The token contract

The complete brand system fits in one `:root` block. Every declaration is flat and every value is a literal. This is the single source: any token §4–§10 needs exists here, exactly once.

```css
:root{
  /* Colour — 16 tokens. §3.2 is normative for what each one is allowed to mean. */
  --ground:#F7F5F0; --surface:#FFFFFF; --scene-tone:#F3F1EC;
  --ink:#14161A; --ink-meta:#5A5F66;
  --hairline:#D8D3C8; --rule:#8C8677;
  --rail:#14385F; --rail-ink:#F7F5F0; --rail-meta:#B9C6D6; --rail-accent:#FFC53D;
  --verdict:#0F6B45; --verdict-tint:#E6F2EA; --deadline:#B3202C; --closing:#FFC53D;
  --dot-hit:#0F6B45;
  /* Dot cell. §4.4 derives the odds band, the count-slide vertical budget and the E2
     module FROM these two values, never the reverse, and these tokens restate none of
     §4.4's block heights. Editing either one moves the band on every surface.
     No brace in this comment. */
  --dot-size:10px; --dot-gap:5px;
  --font-display:'Bricolage Grotesque'; --font-text:'Inter'; --font-figure:'JetBrains Mono';
  --font-chrome:'Inter';
  --fs-hero:150px;   --lh-hero:150px;
  --fs-figure:120px; --lh-figure:120px;
  --fs-display:88px; --lh-display:90px;
  --fs-title:68px;   --lh-title:70px;
  --fs-lead:56px;    --lh-lead:60px;
  --fs-body:48px;    --lh-body:60px;
  --fs-label:44px;   --lh-label:50px;
  --fs-legal:38px;   --lh-legal:45px;
  --fs-micro:34px;   --lh-micro:40px;
  --tr-display:-0.02em; --tr-label:0.08em; --tr-figure:0;
  --gutter:65px;
  --sp-0:5px; --sp-1:10px; --sp-15:15px; --sp-2:20px; --sp-3:30px;
  --sp-4:40px; --sp-5:60px; --sp-6:90px; --sp-7:120px;
  --scene-wash:rgba(247,245,240,.86);
}
```

**This block is ADDED to `:root`, not substituted for it.** The video templates consume **32 distinct custom properties** defined in the current `:root` (MEASURED by intersecting every `var()` reference in `reel-template.mjs`, `story.mjs` and `reel.mjs` with every declaration in `styles.css`; `--accent-rgb` alone is referenced 21 times across the three). The legacy block therefore stays live until each of its consumers is retired. §3.8 schedules those removals and names who performs each one.

**The block declares 54 properties, and 53 of those names have never existed in this repository.** MEASURED, re-grepped 17 Sep 2026 across every `.css`, `.mjs` and `.js` file with exact-name matching: 53 of the 54 have **zero** definitions and **zero** `var()` references — `--rail-meta` and the literal `#B9C6D6` included, which have zero occurrences anywhere in `carousel/`, so coexistence with the legacy block is safe and no rename is needed to achieve it. **`--font-display` is the single exception** — it is defined four times in code (`styles.css:34` in `:root`, and `:122`, `:143`, `:177` in the `house`, `collect` and `glass` theme blocks) and referenced 20 times. It is not a collision to be tolerated but the migration lever described below: the new value **re-points `styles.css:34` in place** and is never added as a second declaration, and the three per-theme redeclarations leave with their theme blocks. Every other name in the block above is genuinely new.

**Six constraints.** The first four are consequences of `\{[^}]*\}`; the fifth is a separate, measured trap already documented in the repo; the sixth is new and follows from the comments above.

1. **No `@media`, no `@supports`, no nesting** inside a token block. The match stops at the first `}`.
2. **A descendant rule is not a token.** `[data-theme="sports"] .pitch{…}` has a space before the brace and never matches. It would render on the carousel and vanish silently from the Reel and Story. The stylesheet already says this to itself at `styles.css:295-299`.
3. **No `}` inside a value.** An SVG data-URI token containing a literal or percent-decoded brace truncates its own block and every declaration after it, in all three video templates at once, with no error. `styles.css:81` already carries such a data-URI for the luxury grain — it is safe only because it sits in a descendant rule (`styles.css:79-82`). Any texture moved into a token must be brace-free.
4. **Each template holds its own copy of the regex.** Three separate literals at `reel-template.mjs:46`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` (verified). There is no shared helper, so a fix or relaxation applied to one does not reach the others.
5. **No token value may reference another token.** `:root` is `<html>`, but `data-theme` sits on `<body>` (`render.mjs:182`, verified). A composite declared on `:root` substitutes the *default* theme's values and inherits down already resolved — which silently repainted every themed card in the base orange, measured in-repo at SSIM 0.979 for cash against a 0.997 noise floor (`styles.css:295-305`). So `--verdict-tint` is the literal `#E6F2EA`, never a `color-mix()` of `--verdict` and `--ground`; a computed tint would also bake the light register into the dark sub-register below. Defaults that must compose belong in inline `var()` fallbacks at the use site.
6. **No `}` inside a comment, either.** The comments in the block above are safe because they contain no brace; `/* 60 x 10 { … } */` would truncate the block exactly as a value would. The regex does not parse CSS, it counts braces.

**No custom property may be defined twice across the lifted blocks.** Last-block-wins is silent, and the `--rule` collision described in §3.2 is what it looks like in practice: a dot field at 1.37:1 instead of 3.33:1, correct on the carousel and wrong in every video, with no error and no failing test. This is the cheapest assertion in the system and it belongs beside `assertTypeContract()`. Note that `--font-display` is the one name where satisfying it means editing a legacy declaration rather than simply adding a new one.

**The migration lever.** `--font-display` already exists at `styles.css:34` and is consumed **11×** in `styles.css`, **6×** in `reel-template.mjs`, **2×** in `story.mjs` and **1×** in `render.mjs` (MEASURED, re-counted 17 Sep 2026) — re-pointing it moves the whole display register in one edit. `--font-kicker` is a **dead token**: it is defined three times (`styles.css:35` in `:root`, `:75` in the luxury block, `:178` in the glass block) and read by nothing — **zero** `var(--font-kicker)` references anywhere in the repository, re-grepped 17 Sep 2026 and confirmed. It is deleted outright, at no call-site cost, and replaced by `--font-text` and `--font-chrome`. Its death is also what makes Playfair Display and Inter 500 unreachable (§3.4). Anton and Oswald, by contrast, are genuinely live — 21 and 28 references — which is why §3.4 schedules those faces rather than deleting them.

**Reserved dark sub-register.** "The Late Board" was rejected as the primary direction and is retained only as a possible sub-register for dark live formats. It is reserved as `[data-theme="late"]`, defined but not built, and it is explicitly **not** dark-plus-gold — the semantic four keep their meanings and are lifted for dark legibility:

```css
[data-theme="late"]{
  --ground:#101418; --surface:#171C21; --ink:#EDEAE4; --ink-meta:#9AA1A8;
  --hairline:#2A3138;
  --rail:#0B1F33; --rail-ink:#EDEAE4; --rail-accent:#FFC53D;
  --verdict:#3FBF87; --verdict-tint:#12281F; --deadline:#FF6B72; --closing:#FFC53D;
}
```
CALCULATED, on `--ground`: `--ink` 15.41:1, `--ink-meta` 7.08:1, `--verdict` 7.94:1, `--deadline` 6.69:1, `--closing` 11.72:1. On `--rail`: `--rail-ink` 13.90:1, `--rail-accent` 10.58:1. On `--surface`: `--ink` 14.28:1, `--ink-meta` 6.56:1. `--verdict` on `--verdict-tint` 6.68:1. `--rail-meta` needs no override either: `#B9C6D6` measures **9.63:1** on the late rail `#0B1F33` (CALCULATED), so the band's subordinate lines keep one hex in both registers. **`--rule` and `--scene-tone` are deliberately not overridden here**, because the dark register has no dot-grid design and no scene ground yet; building the sub-register requires designing both first.

---

### 3.8 The "no" palette — a schedule, not a commit

Each entry names the code it removes and **who performs the removal**, so the prohibition is enforceable rather than aspirational, and so that no deletion lands before the section that retires its consumers does. §3 decides what goes; the surface sections decide when.

| Banned | What it removes | Performed by | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No gold** | `--gold-1`, `--gold-2`, `--gold-3`, `--gold-rgb`, `--gold-deep-rgb` (defined `styles.css:32-33`, re-defined "cooled to platinum" inside the glass block at `styles.css:217-218`). And CAP 8.22 forbids claiming a response deadline that does not exist, while the DMCC Act 2024 consumer provisions (in force 6 Apr 2025) ban fake countdown timers outright. The two Playfair faces do **not** wait for it — they are already unreachable (§3.4) and leave `FACES` now. | This is the category's centre of gravity, top to bottom. A directory that looks like it cannot be a neutral one. |
| **No glassmorphism** | The `[data-theme="glass"]` block (`styles.css:157-219`), `--card-blur` (`:183`), `--card-bg` (`:181`), the four-layer `--card-shadow` (`:184`), and the `--block-*`/`--pill-*` glass tokens. | §8.7. | On a static PNG the blur buys nothing, because nothing moves behind it; it costs legibility at thumbnail size; and it is the most dated-looking choice available in 2026. |

"Play responsibly" is gambling vocabulary: it is inaccurate here and re-categorises PDD in the viewer's mind. **§3 deletes "PLAY RESPONSIBLY" and states no replacement wording** — what stands in the conditions band for age and territory is §10.2's, informed by §10.6's finding that PDD stores neither a `min_age` nor a territory field and therefore verifies neither. |

One further exclusion: **no cartoon, mascot, game-like or toy-like treatment.** CAP 16.3.12's "strong appeal" test does not formally bind PDD, but rules 1.3 and 8.8 do, and designing as if it bound costs nothing here.

### 3.9 What is not a token, and who owns it instead

Anything that is not a flat custom property cannot reach the video templates through the lift, and therefore is not part of the brand system. The earlier draft handed all of it to "the scene-module section", which owns almost none of it. The actual owners:

| Not a token | Owner |
|---|---|
| The odds dot grid — band origin, columns, rows, ceiling, surface assignment, the count-slide vertical budget and every block height in it, the E2 module's height on every surface | **§4.4** |
| The above-ceiling encoding and the marked-dot rule | **§4.7** |
| The clipped-state annotation slot — its row, alignment and measured glyph capacity | **§4.8** |
| The permitted wording of every odds string | **§10.6a** |
| The conditions band — field list, strings, line count, per-canvas height | **§10.2** |
| The evidence predicate behind verdict green | **§10.4** |
| Per-canvas masthead and rail geometry, the bento layout, the board, the slide block tables | **§5.1–§5.9** (still), **§6.3** (Reel), **§7.2** (Story) |
| The broadcast insert system's expand-hold-collapse chrome | **§6.3** |
| Per-category scene art, scene lanes, scene region, ink budgets and the tone floor's area | **§8** — scene art and the scene module only |
| Asset normalisation of scraped operator photography | **§9** |
| Deck size and `drawsRendered` | **§5.11** |

The division is the point. This section fixes what every format shares — colour, type, the two tracks, the four type rules and the token contract. Every other section fixes what its format does with them, and states none of §3's numbers back.

---

### Decisions this section commits to

- Palette is **16 colour tokens** on a newsprint ground: `--ground` #F7F5F0, `--surface` #FFFFFF, `--scene-tone` #F3F1EC, `--ink` #14161A (16.62:1), `--ink-meta` #5A5F66 (5.91:1), `--hairline` #D8D3C8 (1.37:1), `--rule` #8C8677 (3.33:1), `--rail` #14385F (10.95:1), `--rail-ink` #F7F5F0, `--rail-meta` #B9C6D6 (6.88:1 on rail), `--rail-accent` #FFC53D (7.56:1 on rail), `--verdict` #0F6B45 (6.01:1), `--verdict-tint` #E6F2EA, `--deadline` #B3202C (6.10:1), `--closing` #FFC53D, `--dot-hit` #0F6B45. All ratios calculated in-session.
- `--rail-meta` #B9C6D6 is **added**, because §10.2 already renders it on every asset and §5.14 named it with no definition anywhere — an undefined token does not throw, it inherits, on the CAP 8.17 band. 6.88:1 on `--rail`, 9.63:1 on the late register's rail (so no override there), and forbidden on paper at 1.59:1. §10.2 keeps the strings, the weight and the line assignment.
- `--rule` is the meaning-bearing graphite #8C8677 (dot field, chip borders, board rules, sheet-edge hairline); the decorative value #D8D3C8 moves to `--hairline`. `--dot-empty` #948C7C and the alternative #8B867B are both retired. One hex, one name, one definition — a duplicate `--rule` across two lifted blocks resolves last-block-wins and drops the dot field to 1.37:1 with no error.
- `--scene-tone` #F3F1EC is added as the still canvas's single scene tone and the darkest scene pixel permitted there. L = 0.880214, ΔL from `--ground` = 0.033488. §8 owns its area and placement.
- The dot field's only legal beds are `--ground` (3.33:1) and `--scene-tone` (3.21:1). The exclusion of `--verdict-tint` now rests on margin, not failure: the retired #948C7C measured 2.90:1 there and failed WCAG 1.4.11; #8C8677 measures 3.15:1 and passes. `--surface` at 3.63:1 is excluded because no section puts the dot field in a tile and a second legal bed makes the ratio slide-dependent.
- Verdict green paints only (a) a figure on a row satisfying §10.4's eligibility predicate, or (b) a count of PDD's own published artefacts in the same asset (`drawsRendered`, §5.11). PDD's own computed assessments — the Trust Score — are not green and not on mint; they render in `--ink` with a `--rule` border.
- `--deadline` is forbidden on `--rail` (measured 1.79:1). The closing state on a rail renders `--closing` as type at 7.56:1. On `--ground`/`--surface` `--closing` stays fill-only (1.45:1), an amber field with `--ink` on top at 11.48:1.
- Category identity carries zero colour. Carriers are §8's scene layer and §5's category kicker; the rail-band category word is withdrawn, because both masthead slots are spoken for. Scenes may override exactly one property, `--scene-wash`, and it is not used on the still canvas. `--scene-wash` default `rgba(247,245,240,.86)`, alpha ≥ 0.86, RGB carrying `--ink` at ≥15:1; composited over pure black it still gives `--ink` 12.08:1.
- Scene marks may not use a semantic colour: the sports pennant is `--hairline` #D8D3C8, not #FFC53D.
- Type stack: Bricolage Grotesque 700/800 display and the wordmark, Inter 400/600/700 text and chrome, **JetBrains Mono 700 only** for every figure. Mono 400 and 500 are no longer wanted, so the bundle needs no new file and §7.2's Mono 500 dateline is illegal rather than merely unbundled. Inter 500 is retired, so §10.2's sentence-case band lines set in Inter 400 — handed to §10.2 rather than left to resolve silently.
- Bricolage and Inter never set a numeral, grounded in the defect at `styles.css:174-176`.
- MEASURED advances from the bundled woff2 (fontTools 4.62.1): JetBrains Mono 700 **exactly 0.600em** for digits, comma, full stop, £, $ and space — closing the open question; Bricolage 800 uppercase mean 0.6740em, Bricolage 700 0.6648em, Inter 700 0.7011em, Inter 600 0.6946em, Inter 400 0.6815em. These are 2.4–2.5% wider than the figures quoted elsewhere in the spec. Means size decisions; strings are measured at render, in both directions — `18+ · UK · ENTER ON OPERATOR SITE` is 1,008.6px by the mean and 794.6px measured, and fits.
- Wordmark is Bricolage Grotesque 800 uppercase at `--fs-label` with `--tr-label`, measured 471.2px for `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` (Inter 700 would be 480.5px).
- Bundle end state: **138,608 bytes across 6 faces**, 41.5% of today's 333,628 bytes across 17. Six is the normative count; §12.1's "8 of the 17 registered" counts Bricolage 400 and Inter 500, which this stack does not carry, and the 46,636-byte gap between the eleven retired faces (195,020) and §12.1's nine orphans (148,384) is exactly those two files (22,364 + 24,272). Eleven faces retired. Four leave `FACES` now at zero risk (Playfair Display 700-italic and 800, Bricolage Grotesque 400, Inter 500 — 93,104 bytes, all reachable only through the dead `--font-kicker` or not named in any live rule). Seven leave with their consumers (101,916 bytes): 21 `'Anton'` and 28 `'Oswald'` references are live across five files, and Space Grotesk, Fraunces and Bungee hang off `--font-display` in the `glass`, `house` and `collect` theme blocks.
- The repository is PUBLIC (`api.github.com` reports `"private": false`, checked 17 Sep 2026), so shipping 17 OFL woff2 files with no licence text is a live OFL 1.1 §2 gap. Per-family copyright lines plus a copy of OFL 1.1 must sit in `carousel/assets/fonts/`, using `carousel/assets/audio/LICENSES.md` as the precedent.
- Type scale is **eight display steps plus one legally-scoped step**, every line-height a multiple of 5px: 150/150, 120/120, 88/90, 68/70, 56/60, 48/60, 44/50, 38/45, 34/40. 184px, 116px and 40px are deleted — the first two had no consumer anywhere in the spec, the third folds into 44.
- `--fs-legal` 38/45 exists solely so §10.2's measured conditions band is a legal size. It is scoped to that band on every canvas and is legal nowhere else.
- One gutter: `--gutter: 65px`. Chrome track x 65 … 1015 = 950px on every canvas, identical to Meta's Safe Box A width. Content well on a still slide carrying the sheet edge x 65 … 960 = 895px, exactly the width §4.4's 60-column band derives from §3's two cell tokens (60×10 + 59×5 = 895), with a 55px right margin between the well and the hairline at x 1015. Any surface without a sheet edge — the three 9:16 canvases and the still closing slide — runs on the full 950px track. Crop headroom 31.25px each side. **64px and 70px are both retired and may not be restated**: 70 puts the still on a 940px track against the Reel's 950, and leaves the 895px band 35–45px narrower than its column, so a centred origin at x 87.5 or x 92.5 stays re-derivable forever. §3.5 sized the well to the band, not the band to the well, and leaves the band's own coordinate to §4.4.
- The gutter ships with its own build assertion beside `assertTypeContract()`: `--gutter` resolves to 65px and the layout's two constants are 950 and 895, with measured-fit checks running against 895, 950 and 1015. A per-node "every left edge is 65" assertion is explicitly not adopted — it would fail on the cover board's Prize and Closes columns and on every chip.
- `--rail-h-top` and `--rail-h-bottom` are deleted from the token block. Rail geometry is per-canvas and belongs to §5.2, §6.3, §7.2 and §10.2.
- T1 — the odds figure sets at 120px and is never smaller than the prize name; guaranteed by construction at ≥1.36 against an 88px maximum prize step. Today `render.mjs:67` gives 0.337 and `render.mjs:120` gives 0.333.
- T2 — `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame, asserted at node level as an **upper bound; zero is legal**. The anchor is the cover headline on a surface that has a cover. A draw slide, a Reel card and the Story carry none — the Story's largest node is the odds figure at `--fs-figure` 120/120, per §7.2's settled band table. The earlier "the odds figure where the surface has no cover" assignment is withdrawn; it prescribed a 150px Story figure payable only out of the photograph band.
- T3 — nine legal sizes with three floors: 48px running copy on every canvas; 44px editorial floor on video; 38px conditions band only; 34px still micro plus §10.4's dated stamp on any canvas. The two sub-44px exceptions on video are named, measured, and both are fixed-position standing chrome. No tenth step was created for §4.8's clipped-state annotation row: it stays at `--fs-label` 44px and §10.6a shortened the string to fit §4.8's measured slot instead.
- T4 — the figure node carries the bare numeral, at most 9 glyphs; the qualifier sets at `--fs-label` in the same lockup with a gap of at most 10px and no node between. At 120px nine glyphs measure 648.0px against an 895px well. No figure node sets at `--fs-hero` on any surface, so there is no second tier to check. `1 IN 4,500,000` is 14 glyphs = 1,008.0px at 120px and cannot fit, which is why the anchor is bare. Wording is §10.6a's. The "qualifier ≥50% of the figure" rule is retired and replaced by this adjacency rule.
- `assertTypeContract()` ships hard-failing in v1, in the same commit as the §5/§6/§7 rewrite and never before it, modelled on `assertVideoContract` at `encode.mjs:36` (guard clauses `:45–50`, called from `reel.mjs:265` and `story.mjs:273`). Measured-fit/overflow checks stay report-only for the first week.
- The `:root` block is ADDED to the legacy one, not substituted. The templates consume 32 distinct custom properties defined in the current `:root` (MEASURED; `--accent-rgb` 21×). Of the 54 properties the new block declares, 53 have zero definitions and zero references in the repo today — `--rail-meta` and `#B9C6D6` included; `--font-display` is the only shared name and is re-pointed at `styles.css:34` in place rather than declared twice. §3.8 is a schedule with a named performer per row.
- Six token constraints: no `@media`/`@supports`/nesting; a descendant rule is not a token; no `}` in a value; no `}` in a comment either; each template holds its own copy of the regex; no token may reference another token. Plus: no custom property may be defined twice across the lifted blocks, asserted at build time.
- `--font-kicker` is deleted outright — re-grepped 17 Sep 2026, zero `var(--font-kicker)` references against three definitions (`styles.css:35`, `:75`, `:178`). Its death is what makes Playfair Display and Inter 500 unreachable. `--font-display` is the migration lever, consumed 11× / 6× / 2× / 1×.
- `[data-theme="late"]` is reserved but not built, explicitly not dark-plus-gold. `--rule` and `--scene-tone` are deliberately not overridden there, so building it requires designing a dark dot grid and a dark scene ground first.
- "PLAY RESPONSIBLY" is deleted from all 7 render call sites and 3 test assertions. §3 states no replacement wording for age or territory; that is §10.2's, informed by §10.6.
- `carousel/honesty.mjs` survives unchanged: `capValue()` at `:19` and `altTexts()` at `:31`, written to `out/alt.json` by `build.mjs:161`.

### Open questions

- **Does JetBrains Mono's pound sign pass the silhouette test that Bricolage failed?** The £/& collision is documented at `styles.css:174-176`; the equivalent check has not been run on the face that now sets every currency figure. Width is settled — £ measures exactly 0.600em, identical to every digit, so the tabular grid is safe — but the test is about shape, not advance. Render `£ & 8 0 O S 5` at 120px in JetBrains Mono 700 and compare silhouettes at profile-grid scale.
- **Does the `--scene-tone` ground survive the profile-grid downsample?** ΔL 0.033488 is a 3.67% luminance step. At feed size it resolves; in the profile grid the 1012.5px crop displays at roughly 120px, an 8.4× downsample, where line-work scenes average into a uniform wash. If it vanishes, the correct response is to delete the still scene rather than darken the tone — there is no value between #F3F1EC and #D8D3C8 that is both visibly stronger and keeps the dot field at 3:1.
- **Is there an ASA-legible size floor the 34px and 38px tiers can be tested against?** The ASA expects all significant conditions to be present and legible but publishes no numeric threshold. 38px is §10.2's measured fit, not a compliance-verified figure, and 38px is 13.7 CSS px on a 390px-wide phone. Both should be eyeballed on a real handset before the T3 gate lands.
- **Does the reserved `[data-theme="late"]` sub-register ship at all, and for which format?** It is defined so the token surface exists, but building it re-enters the category's most crowded territory and now requires designing both a dark dot grid and a dark scene ground, neither of which exists.
- **Which OFL notice text goes with each family?** The bundled woff2 files are third-party Fontsource Latin subsets with no accompanying metadata in the repo, so the copyright lines must be taken from each family's upstream release rather than reconstructed.
- **Handed to §10.2, not open here:** the band's sentence-case lines were specified at Inter 500, a weight this stack retires. They resolve to Inter 400 unless §10.2 argues Inter 500 back into the bundle, which costs 24,272 bytes and a seventh face.

### Risks

- **The gutter is settled, and two of its costs are permanent.** 70px is retired and the registry's gutter clauses are superseded, so the number will not move again — but slide 1 now has 31.25px of crop headroom instead of 36.25px, forever, on the one slide the profile grid touches; and the 55px right margin between the well at x 960 and the hairline at x 1015 is new, unrendered, and the coordinate most likely to be "corrected" back to 1015 by a future author who does not know the well is band-sized. That is why §3.5 states the causal direction explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred. If a render shows the cover's left edge reading as cramped, the correct response is to inset slide 1's headline only, never to move the gutter.
- **The measured advances invalidate published fits elsewhere.** `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` at 44px is 471.2px, not the 352.5px assumed in the scene-lane arithmetic. On a 9:16 rail with the wordmark at x 65 and `CHECKED 09:00` (Mono 700, 343.2px measured) right-aligned to x 1015, the gap between them is **135.6px, not 254.3px** — so the 220px-wide rail mark slot published for the Reel does not fit and overlaps the wordmark by 101px. §8's scene ruling has since reached the same verdict from the other side — it suppresses mark slot M on a clearance of −48.35px, computed against the untracked 418.35px wordmark rather than the tracked 471.2px one — so the suppression is corroborated by two independent measurements rather than merely handed on; §8 must re-derive or suppress it. §10.4's stamp is the other casualty: at 44px it measures 1,045.2px against a 950px track and overflows by 95.2px, rather than fitting by 0.8 of a character as published — which strengthens rather than weakens the case for rendering it at 34px (measured 807.6px).
- **T3 now has two named sub-44px exceptions on video.** 38px for the conditions band and 34px for the dated stamp. Both are measured and both are standing chrome, but it means the same CAP 8.17 text renders at two sizes across formats and that the "44px video floor" is a floor with holes. If anyone wants one number, the honest move is 38px everywhere, which costs the still conditions band nothing and the video floor its label tier.
- **`--rail-meta` is the second token whose ground is a prohibition rather than a preference.** At 1.59:1 on newsprint it is illegible on paper, exactly as `--deadline` is illegible on the rail at 1.79:1, and nothing in CSS stops either. The palette now carries two tokens that are correct in one place and invisible in another, and the only guard is §3.2's semantic rule and a reviewer reading it.
- **Adding `--fs-legal` breaks the eight-step scale on its first contact with §10.** The step exists because §10.2's measured band does not fit at 44px and sits below its own derived legibility floor at 34px. It is scoped, but it is a ninth value in a scale that was argued down to eight, and it is a warning about how firmly the enumeration will hold under the remaining sections.
- **Zero per-category colour still contradicts the brief.** With the rail-band word withdrawn, the whole burden of differentiation sits on §8 — a monochrome 3.67% ground on the still and stripe fields inside chrome on 9:16. If §8 underdelivers, or if the tone vanishes in the profile grid, all eight categories look identical and the product owner may reasonably read this section as having quietly overruled them.
- **Retiring the `--gold-*` tokens breaks 15 template references and 19 in-stylesheet consumers.** A missed reference does not throw: `var(--gold-2)` with no definition resolves to an invalid value and the element renders transparent or falls back to initial — a silent regression visible only in the encoded MP4, the least-inspected output. The tokens are also re-declared inside the glass block at `styles.css:217-218`, so deleting only the `:root` definitions leaves a second live definition behind. Scheduling the removals per-consumer reduces this risk; it does not remove it.
- **`--font-display` is the one place the no-double-definition assertion is satisfied by editing, not adding.** Every other new name is absent from the repository, so the additive rule is safe by construction. `--font-display` is not: if the new block is pasted in whole while `styles.css:34` still says `'Anton'`, the assertion fires on day one — or worse, does not, and last-block-wins silently decides the display face of every legacy rule.
- **Standing chrome is roughly a fifth of the still slide** (§5.2 owns the figure). If the Verizon Media/Publicis finding transfers from 2019 US paid creative to 2026 UK organic carousels, the rail is precisely the crowding it warns about. The mitigation — the rail carries only required information — is untested.
- **Light ground plus unnormalised operator photography may look worse than dark did.** Operator artwork is mostly dark, saturated and collage-like; the rendered mockup at `~/Desktop/pdd-directions/D-merged-01-cover.png` shows a darts collage and a gold iPhone tile sitting badly in one strip. A white `--surface` tile is far less forgiving than a dark card. Asset normalisation (§9) is a hard dependency of this palette, not an optional companion change.
- **The lift regex truncates a token block at the first `}`** — now including one inside a comment, which the block above deliberately avoids. If anyone later moves a texture into a token as an SVG data-URI containing a brace, every declaration after it disappears from the Reel, the Story and the Reel cover at once, with no error and no failing test, because the carousel reads the stylesheet directly. The regex exists as three independent literals, so hardening one does not harden the others.
- **Constraint 5 is easy to violate and impossible to see in review.** `color-mix()` or a `var()` inside a token value looks correct on the carousel and silently resolves against the default theme everywhere else. The in-repo evidence is an SSIM measurement, not a test — nothing currently fails the build when someone reintroduces it.
- **T1 is a genre inversion with no precedent and no measurement.** The distribution-eligibility argument is a sound reading of official policy, but it is a reading: Meta publishes no per-post signal confirming that added value was recognised, and there is no per-slide or swipe metric in the Graph API, so the change cannot be measured at slide level even after the fact.
- **The `--fs-display` 88px step is nearly dead.** At a measured 0.6740em, 88px fits about 15 characters on the 895px well, so the one-line prize step will fire on a minority of draws. It is not dead, so it stays, but it is the next candidate for retirement if nine steps ever need to become eight.
- **T4 drops draws rather than shrinking figures.** A ticket cap of 10 or more glyphs (≥10,000,000 tickets — not present in today's inventory, whose measured maximum is 4,500,000) removes the draw from every surface. That is the correct failure, but it is a failure on legitimate inventory and it will read as a bug the first time it fires.
- **The dot field at 3.33:1 has not been checked after encoding.** The ratio holds on a full-size render; it has not been verified after the profile-grid downscale to 1012.5px or after JPEG/H.264 chroma subsampling, where a 10px dot at 3:1 may not survive. `encode.mjs:30` passes no `-crf`, so video runs at libx264's default 23.
- **`--rail-accent` and `--closing` carry identical hex**, so an amber rail keyline and an amber closing run can appear in one frame and read as a single system. Position is the only cue separating chrome from data state, and that distinction is invisible to a first-time viewer.
- **Seven retired faces remain registered in `FACES` until their consumers go.** Removing an entry is trivial; leaving one in is also trivial, and an unused Anton or Oswald keeps the old typographic register one line of CSS away from returning.
- **The cascade-order override is an implicit contract with no test.** No §3 token depends on it now, but §5, §6 and §7 do. Reordering the style tags, or moving the token lift later, would silently restore the wrong values.

**Decisions this section commits to**
