## §4 — The odds device: making the number visible

## 4. The odds device: making the number visible

### 4.1 Why this device carries the whole system

Three separate constraints converge on one component, which is why it earns the largest budget on the slide it renders on.

**It is the distribution-eligibility argument.** Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines (OFFICIAL, help.instagram.com/313829416281232) exclude "unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value". A daily carousel built from other operators' photographs and prize copy is squarely in that category. The added value has to be *visible on the slide*.

Note the precise form of the claim, because the draft version of this section overstated it. Operators **do** publish their ticket caps — that is exactly where `lib/parse.mjs` scrapes them from. What no operator publishes is the *normalised, comparable* figure across a set of draws, and what the 17 Sep 2026 competitive crawl found is that no directory renders it as anything but a table cell. The material value PDD adds is the normalisation and the rendering, not the discovery of a secret number.

**It adds that value without adding text weight.** The same OFFICIAL source (about.instagram.com, 31 May 2023) says Instagram aims to make certain reels "less visible" when they are "majority text". That rule is written about reels, not carousels. On the carousel the band is a graphic rather than a text block, so it raises the information density of the slide without raising the text-to-photo ratio — one of the few levers that does both, though not the only one. On the video canvases the point is now moot rather than argued: under §4.4's surface assignment the full grid never renders on 9:16 at all, so the "majority text" exposure it would have created on the Reel is zero. See §4.4 for why that is a consequence of the budget rather than a concession.

**Nobody in the category has it.** The 17 Sep 2026 crawl found odds existing as a data *field* at CompWatch, Competition Showroom and PDD, and found no bar, grid or other visual encoding on any profile crawled. It is unoccupied territory #6, sitting on top of #5 (typography as the only ornament) and #2 (the scoreboard, not the poster). The direction research's argument that an operator structurally cannot copy it — their commercial job is to make the odds feel small — is a strategic judgement, not a measured fact, but it is the right one.

### 4.2 Correction to the digest's odds range — the fallback is the primary renderer

The brief states that odds run "from roughly 1 in 599 to 1 in 13,995 in the live data". MEASURED against the live database on 17 Sep 2026, that range describes a narrow sample, not the inventory.

Query: `status=eq.active`, `draw_date >= now()`, all rows, paginated (n = 880; 880 of 880 have `total_entries > 0`, zero nulls). Percentiles are nearest-rank on the sorted array, so they will move by a step or two under a different estimator.

| Statistic | Ticket cap |
|---|---|
| min | 99 |
| p25 | 1,500 |
| median | 9,999 |
| p75 | 69,999 |
| p90 | 300,000 |
| p99 | 1,599,999 |
| max | 4,500,000 |

The digest reports 899 enterable draws on the same day; this query returns 880. Two snapshots hours apart with a slightly different `draw_date` boundary — treat both as ~880–900, not as a discrepancy.

**The population that actually renders is narrower and smaller than the draft assumed.** `plan.mjs:39` calls `fetchEndingSoon(DAYS, MIN_DAYS)` with `DAYS = 7` and `MIN_DAYS = 1` (`plan.mjs:10–13`), and `select.mjs:20` caps the result at `limit=300`. So the real payload is **the 300 nearest-closing draws in the 1-to-7-day window that have an image** (`select.mjs:18`, `image_url=not.is.null`), not the full window.

MEASURED on that exact payload (n = 300): **77 draws (25.7%) have a cap at or below 1,500.**

The draft corroborated that with "on the untruncated 1–7 day window (n = 493) it is 127 (25.8%)". **That corroboration is withdrawn.** §5.11 re-measured the window at 483 rows and records the 493 figure as wrong; §5.6 and §5.8 use 483. The claim now rests on the 300-row payload alone, which no other section contradicts.

| Category (real 300-row payload) | n | visualWeight | ≤ 1,500 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cash-prizes | 110 | 0.4 | 18 (16%) |
| tech-giveaways | 56 | 0.92 | 23 (41%) |
| sports-outdoors | 40 | **0.88** | 3 (8%) |
| collectibles | 33 | 0.85 | 18 (55%) |
| car-draws | 28 | 1.0 | **0 (0%)** |
| luxury | 20 | 1.0 | 8 (40%) |
| home-garden | 12 | **0.78** | 7 (58%) |
| (uncategorised) | 1 | — (never scored) | 0 |

The rows sum to 300 and the ≤1,500 column sums to 77. §5.11's own per-category figures for the same payload (~114 cash-prizes, ~17 home-garden) are a *proportional estimate* scaled from the untruncated window and are explicitly labelled as such in its residual-risk note; the table above is a direct query of the 300-row payload. Do not reconcile the two by averaging — prefer this one and cite §5.11 only for the untruncated window.

The two weights the draft read as FALLBACK are now authored values: **§8.7 owns `config.json`** and sets sports-outdoors to 0.88 and home-garden to 0.78, retires the 0.6 default, and makes `pickBestCategory` skip any slug absent from the config — which is why the uncategorised row can no longer be scored at all. The `≤ 1,500` column is a property of the data and does not move with them, and neither does the winner below.

That column is measured at ≤ 1,500. §4.4's ceiling is **1,440**, so every count in it is an upper bound on the count at the ceiling. Inventory-wide, §5.8 measured both thresholds directly: **212 of 880 at ≤ 1,440 (24.1%)** against 222 of 880 at ≤ 1,500 (25.2%) — the ceiling change costs **1.1 percentage points**, ten draws in 880. The equivalent figure on the 300-row payload has not been queried and is owed; until it is, quote 25.7% as the ≤1,500 payload share and 24.1% as the ≤1,440 inventory share, and do not blend them.

**The decisive measurement.** A post does not render a cross-section of that payload — `pickBestCategory` (`select.mjs:27–51`) picks **one** category and `plan.mjs:40` takes the deck's draws from it. Re-running that scoring function against today's real payload (`score = enough·1e12 + visualWeight·min(len,n)·1e9 + Σ total_prize_value`), the winner is **car-draws**, whose 28 eligible draws include **zero** at or below 1,500 and therefore zero at or below 1,440. §8.7's authored weights do not disturb that: at 0.88 and a full pool, sports-outdoors scores below both categories tied at the top.

So a deck built today would render a clipped sheet and not one full grid. The two categories tied at the top of `visualWeight` are car-draws (0%) and luxury (40%); the category with the deepest inventory, cash-prizes, is held down by `visualWeight: 0.4` and is itself only 16%.

**The above-ceiling treatment is the device's default appearance and must be designed as a first-class state, not a degraded one.** The full "one dot per ticket" sheet is the exception, concentrated in collectibles, home-garden, luxury and tech.

One flourish the draft claimed is now retired: the ceiling no longer "lands exactly on the measured p25". At 1,440 it sits just below it. The ceiling is derived from the count slide's vertical budget (§4.4), not from the percentile, and the coincidence was rhetoric rather than evidence.

### 4.3 What the figure is — and why its safety property is conditional, not structural

The number is **`draws.total_entries`**, read at `carousel/format.mjs:62`. It is currently formatted by `oddsLabel()` at `format.mjs:53`, which returns `1 IN 9,999` with en-GB grouping. **`oddsLabel()` is retired from every rendered surface by §10.6a**, which replaces it with the bare, en-GB-grouped cap; it may survive only inside `brief.mjs`'s non-rendered facts table. PDD has no sell-through data and the `draws` table has no column for it. Columns verified in-session by selecting `*`:

`affiliate_url, category_id, category_source, created_at, draw_date, entry_url, featured, grand_prize, id, image_url, operator_id, prize_description, prize_value, slug, status, ticket_price, title, total_entries, total_prize_value, updated_at`

The draft version of this section then asserted a structural safety property: *"a cap can only ever overstate the denominator, so the device is structurally incapable of exaggerating the chance of winning."* **That assertion does not survive contact with the repo, and correcting it is the single most important change in this section.**

`total_entries` is *intended* to be a cap at every extraction tier in `lib/parse.mjs`. The ladder, which is where §10.4's method enum comes from, runs: an operator-specific override pattern; a clean labelled cap in the operator's own per-product API description; a clean labelled cap anywhere on the page ("Total Entries: 5000"); `ltyCap`, the scoped sum of a lottery-for-woocommerce progress bar's sold-plus-remaining; and last, the noisy whole-page grab, which the file itself calls the last resort. Four separate places in the repo document that ladder going wrong, or document a path that must never be trusted:

- **`lib/parse.mjs:151–155`**, the `strict` flag's own comment: *"no progress bars, no bare 'N tickets' … multi-comp listing pages leak other comps' numbers into tier 2/3, **which is how a draw scraped a stranger's ticket count**."*
- **`qa-fix.mjs:5`**, naming the first of three reported error classes: *"total_entries = the per-person cap, or a progress bar belonging to a DIFFERENT comp."*
- **`plausibleEntries` (`lib/parse.mjs:149`) admits only `n >= 100`** — yet one live active row, `win-a-lego-lamborghini-countach-5000-quattrovalvole-redline-competitions-2` (Redline Competitions), stores `total_entries = 99`. One row in 880 is not a crisis, but it proves the column is not uniformly parser-produced and that nothing records which path wrote any given value.
- **`lib/parse.mjs:670–682`** records that the Woo/Shopify API stock count was *removed* from the chain on purpose, because it is tickets REMAINING and drifts daily (1p Gaming 1,382,267 → 1,381,767; Flash Cash 998,574 → 998,291), concluding that `apiStock` "must never stand in for a cap". This is why §10.4's method enum has no `operator-api` value: a remaining count is the error direction the device cannot tolerate, and the draft's enum listed it as renderable.

The direction of error matters. A *cap* mistaken for something else overstates the denominator and the graphic is conservative. A **sold count** or a **per-person cap** mistaken for a cap **understates** it — and a smaller denominator means the graphic shows better-than-real chances, which is the exact failure CAP 8.20 and 8.21 name.

**Therefore, corrected:** the device is safe *when the stored value is the operator's published ticket cap*, and the repo documents several ways it currently may not be.

**Where the safety mechanism now lives.** §10.4 is the normative owner of the evidence and provenance contract — the column names, the method enum and its renderable allow-list, the freshness window and the enforcement point. Under that ruling the check is a **selection predicate**, not a render gate: a draw without fresh, method-qualified provenance is never selected, so it cannot be dropped at render, cannot collapse a slot and cannot consume a backup. §4 states no column name, no enum value and no window of its own. The sequencing consequence is unchanged in force and changed in wording: **nothing in this section may be built before Stage 0 (§12.4) ships.**

The corollary that does survive unchanged: the device must never present the figure as the viewer's personal chance. The proven mockup does exactly that — `merged.mjs:83` labels the block **"Your odds"** — and every second-person framing is banned by §10.6a's allow-list, which is generated rather than filtered (see §4.8).

> **Where `merged.mjs` lives.** Every `merged.mjs` citation in this section refers to the rendered design-session mockup held in the spec scratchpad, **not** to a file in `~/pdd-aggregator`. Its line numbers were re-verified in this session against that file; a builder grepping the aggregator repo for it will find nothing, which is expected. Every other file path in this section (`carousel/*`, `lib/*`, `manager/*`, `qa-fix.mjs`) is in `~/pdd-aggregator` and was re-verified there in this session.

### 4.4 Geometry — the normative specification

**§4.4 is the sole normative source for the lattice, the band, the ceiling, the surface assignment (E1 versus E2), the count-slide vertical budget and the E2 module height on every surface.** No other section publishes a column count, a dot diameter, a gap, a pitch, a band width, a band origin, a row count, a band height, a ceiling, a count-slide block height or an E2 total. §5.7's competing block table is deleted outright: it keeps slide assembly and row contents and states no height, no gap, no ceiling, no module total and no photo-well arithmetic of its own. §5.8, §5.9, §6.3, §7.2 and §8.5 reference this section and specify only what is theirs: the chip's appearance, band heights, row heights and scene ink.

What §4.4 does **not** own, and references instead:

- the gutter, both tracks, the type scale, the hero-figure floor and rules T1–T4 — **§3.5**;
- the token literals, including `--dot-size`, `--dot-gap` and the dot's colour value — **§3.7** (see §4.5);
- every rendered string — **§10.6a**;
- the evidence contract — **§10.4**;
- the conditions band's height and content — **§10.2**;
- the Story's five bands and their y-ranges — **§7.2**;
- the Reel's chrome rects and row heights — **§6.3**;
- the deck's draw count — **§5.11**.

All values are CSS px on the 1080-wide canvas; stills render at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` (`carousel/render.mjs:187`).

#### The lattice and the band

| Property | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| Columns | **60** | fixed, never varies |
| Dot diameter | **10px** | `--dot-size`, §3.7 |
| Gap, both axes | **5px** | `--dot-gap`, §3.7 |
| Cell pitch | **15px** | both axes |
| Band width | **895px** | 60 × 10 + 59 × 5 = 600 + 295 |
| Band origin | **x = 65**, left-aligned | the band runs x 65 … 960 |
| Rows | `R = ceil(cap / 60)` | the data |
| Band height, full | `H = 15R − 5` | the data |
| Band height, clipped | **350px**, constant | 15 × 24 − 10 |
| **Ceiling** | **24 rows = 1,440 tickets, H = 355px** | the count-slide budget below |

**The band is left-aligned to §3.5's content well, not centred.** The 895px is forced by §3.7's `--dot-size` and `--dot-gap` and is not a free parameter; §3.5 then sized the still content well to it, at `--gutter: 65px` and x 65 … 960 = **895px**, so the band fills its column exactly rather than floating inside it. The band therefore shares its left edge with the prize name, the hero figure, the operator lockup, the legend and the counter chip, and the origin question is closed by construction: at a zero residual, left-aligning and centring are the same placement. The draft's centred origin at x 92.5 put a 22.5px offset between the band and every other left-edge element on the slide, which reads as a defect rather than as composition.

Every edge is an integer at both scales. At `deviceScaleFactor: 2` the band spans device px 130 … 1920; the pitch is 30 device px, the dot 20, the gap 10. This is the whole reason the geometry is 10/5/15 and not the proven mockup's 10.95px cell (`merged.mjs:56` `.pad{padding:0 64px}` → a 952px band; `merged.mjs:61` `.grid{gap:5px}` with 60 `1fr` columns → `(952 − 59 × 5) / 60 = 10.95px`), which lands off the device-pixel grid and antialiases unevenly across a row.

**The three rival lattices are deleted, and here is the arithmetic that kills them.**

- **§5.8's 74 columns / 8px dot / 4.05px gutter on an 888px track is deleted.** Its own derivation gives `(888 − 74 × 8) / 73 = 296 / 73 =` **4.0548px**, which is 8.1096 device px at `deviceScaleFactor: 2`. Every dot after the first in each row lands off the device-pixel grid — the exact antialiasing defect the integer 10/5/15 cell exists to prevent. Its module arithmetic is separately inconsistent (`45 + 213 + 45 = 303`, stated as 301).
- **§8.5's "8px dots on a 15px pitch, 60 columns, 900px wide, x 90–990" is corrected, not kept.** `59 × 15 + 8 =` **893px**, not 900, so the published width was wrong on its own figures; and an 8px dot is an element dimension below §8.4's own 5px floor only by grace. §8.5's *pitch* was already right; its width and dot size are replaced by this section's 10px dot at x 65 … 960, and the ghost renders as an echo of the master lattice at 12% ink across that same span, never as a fourth geometry.
- **§6.3's 240 × 120 Reel slot is deleted** — see the surface assignment below for the three independent reasons.

**The grid's height is the datum.** `R = ceil(cap / 60)` and `H = 15R − 5`; the row count is the only thing that varies and there is no per-slide rescaling, ever. A short band is a fact, not a layout failure. The honest caveat the draft did not need and this ruling does: **with one full band per deck (below) there is no second band beside it to compare it to.** The within-post comparison now rests on digit count in the hero figure across the other draw slides — which is the same fallback §4.7 argues for above the ceiling, so the argument is consistent, but it is a smaller claim than the draft made.

Worked examples: cap 99 → R 2, H 25. Cap 599 → R 10, H 145. Cap 699 (the proven render) → R 12, H 175. Cap 1,440 → R 24, H 355, last row complete. Cap 1,439 → R 24, H 355, 59 of 60 cells filled in the last row; the last row is left-aligned and partial, and empty cells render as nothing, not as placeholder dots. Cap 1,441 → clipped (§4.7).

**Coverage, recomputed at the ceiling.** A full sheet at R 24 is 1,440 dots in 895 × 355: `π·5²·1440 ÷ (895 × 355) = 113,097 ÷ 317,725 =` **35.60%**. The clipped sheet is 1,380 whole dots plus 60 half-discs in 895 × 350: `π·5²·1410 ÷ (895 × 350) = 110,741 ÷ 313,250 =` **35.35%**. The draft's 35.6% calibration — "the density at which the lattice still reads as discrete objects rather than a grey slab" — is preserved unchanged, because coverage is nearly scale-free in R when the last row is full. That figure is design judgement calibrated against the proven mockup, not a threshold anyone has measured. A full sheet is 1,440 DOM nodes.

#### Which surfaces carry which encoding

**E1 — the full band with its lockup and legend — renders on exactly one slide: the carousel count slide.** Nowhere else. **E2 — the numeral lockup, no grid — renders on every other draw slide, on the Reel and on the Story.**

The arithmetic that forces it, done against §10.2's conditions band and §3.5's type scale:

The carousel's real budget is not 1350px. §5.2's standing chrome takes 132 (masthead) + 168 (conditions band, §10.2) = 300px, so the content well is **1050px**, running y 132 → 1182. On a draw slide that well must also carry a photograph, the operator lockup (§5.13), the prize name and three 20px gaps — 105px of gaps and lockup, plus the prize name, before any odds module at all.

E1's own stack is eyebrow 50 + 10 + figure 120 + 10 + band + 10 + legend 180 = **380 + H**. At the ceiling that is 735px, and the photograph gets `1050 − 105 − 140 − 735 =` **70px**. Even at the proven 699-ticket render (H 175) the stack is 555px and the photograph gets **250px** — half of §5.7's own 500px floor, which §5.7 already concedes does not dominate even when it is met.

**So on 1080×1350 you can have the photograph or the band, not both.** The only question is which slide gives up its photograph, and §5 answers it: §5.6 Delta 2 already routes the lowest-`total_entries` draw to slide 2, precisely to raise the chance a full grid lands there, and §5.4's cover already carries no photograph, so a photoless slide is inside the template's register. Slide 2 is also the slide Mosseri (OFFICIAL, Oct 2024) confirms Instagram re-serves by auto-advancing — the one shown cold — and the band is the strongest "adds material value" artefact in the system. Giving the band the slide that is re-served cold is the best available use of it.

**The Reel carries E2 only. This is explicit and final.** Three independent reasons, each arithmetic:

1. §6.3's Reel chrome puts the top rail at y 269 … 385 and the insert card at y 722 … 1007 — a **285px** card across two rows, with a clear photograph window of y 385 … 722 = **337px** between them. The band at the ceiling is 355px full and 350px clipped. It does not fit the card, and taking it from the photograph consumes the entire window and then some.
2. An 895 × 355 band is 317,725px² = **15.32%** of the 1080 × 1920 frame added to chrome. §6.3's expanded chrome is 116 + 285 + 145 = 546/1920 = **28.44%** against §6.1 rule 6's 29% ceiling. 28.44 + 15.32 = **43.76%**. The band breaks the Reel's only quantified defence against the "majority text" demotion by more than half again. (The 533px / 27.76% pair the draft quoted from §10.2 was computed on a 272px card and is superseded by §6.3's rects.)
3. The draft's 240 × 120 slot cannot hold an honest reduced encoding. At the finest lattice that survives h.264 — 6px dot, 2px gap, 8px pitch — it holds 30 × 15 = **450 cells**. Showing 450 of a 9,999 cap is a picture **22× more favourable than the fact**, which is precisely the CAP 8.20/8.21 failure §4.7's no-mark rule exists to prevent. There is no named reduced encoding because none is honest: any grid that fits 240 × 120 either rescales the lattice (forbidden above) or sub-samples the cap (forbidden by §4.7).

**The Story carries E2 only.** §7.2's re-cut Story is five bands and four 5px gutters filling Box A exactly, with every band at its minimum legal height, so none is free for a grid: E2's 240px stack sits in band 4, the conditions band is fixed by CAP 8.17 at §10.2's height, and the photograph band is the arithmetic residual rather than a discretionary allocation. Those band heights are §7.2's and are not restated here; §4 depends only on there being no spare band. §7.2's band-5 proportional bar is deleted by §10.2 and by §4.7; it was §4.7's own Candidate A shipped without even §5.8's clamp disclosure, at a fill of 0.095px on the median draw.

**Box A, correctly labelled.** Meta's safe box for 9:16 is x 65 … 1015 by y 269 … 1152, **DERIVED** — measured by edge detection from the diagram at facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490 (version 10 Feb 2026), not published as numbers. The draft tagged it OFFICIAL and that is wrong. §7.1 is also right that the 40% bottom exclusion is a decision rather than a derivation: whether Meta's "disclaimer" category covers a CAP 8.17 significant-conditions line is not established, and 40% is adopted conservatively because the cost of being wrong in the safe direction is 96px of layout. Since E1 no longer renders on any 9:16 surface, Box A no longer constrains the band at all; the band's width would fit it (x 65 … 960 sits flush on Box A's left edge and 55px inside its right), and that is recorded as evidence should the surface assignment ever be reopened, not as a live requirement.

Carousel slide 2. It is the draw with the lowest `total_entries` (§5.6 Delta 2, unchanged and now load-bearing), it carries **no photograph**, and it carries E1. There is no conditional layout and no second variant.

Content well y 132 → 1182 = **1050px**. Column left edge x 65, band x 65 … 960. Type steps are §3.5's; strings are §10.6a's.

Fixed — every block but the band — is **675px in both states**. Full: `70 + 10 + 45 + 10 + 140 + 20 + 50 + 10 + 120 + 10 + 10 + 180 = 675`. Clipped: the same 675, minus 60px for the legend's third line, plus rows 13a and 13b at 50 + 10 — which is the point of putting them in the table. Available for the band = 1050 − 675 = **375px**.

(The previous draft of this section published 670 and 380 here. Both were wrong by 5px — the block heights sum to 675 — and §4.11's own total of 1,030 was already computed against the correct 675. The conclusion is unaffected, but the intermediate figures are not, so they are corrected rather than carried.)

`H = 15R − 5 ≤ 375` gives R ≤ 25, but R = 25 yields H = 370 and only **5px** of slack. **The ceiling is 24 rows, H = 355, slack 20px.** Zero or near-zero slack on a column whose prize name is measured at render is not a budget; §5.12 measures a 7.2% title-residue swap rate, and the prize name is the one block here that can move.

**The clipped column closes at 1,025 of 1,050** — 675 fixed plus a 350px band — with **25px of slack**, looser than the full state's 20px. That is the device's default state (§4.2), and it is costed with §10.6a's annotation row in it, so the build assertion does not fire on an ordinary draw.

**The column is bottom-anchored**: the legend's last line box ends at y 1182 and all residual space pools as newsprint air above the counter chip. At the ceiling that air is 20px (chip-row top y 152); in the clipped state 25px (y 157); at the measured minimum cap of 99 (R 2, H 25) it is 350px (y 482). One layout, one anchor, no branch, and no fixed y-origin for the chip row.

**The renderer asserts the column sums to ≤ 1050 and fails the build otherwise**, in the style of `render.mjs:193` — *"refusing to ship a degraded slide"* — and on slides 3 onward it asserts the photograph against §5.7's 500px floor in the same place.

§3.5 hands this section a derived constraint: "with a two-line prize name the draw slide affords the grid at most 210px of height = 14 rows". That figure was computed for a band sharing a slide with a 500px photograph. Under this ruling the band never renders on a photographed slide, so the constraint is discharged rather than violated, and the binding budget is the count slide's 375px.

E2 carries no legend, because there is no lattice to explain; §10.6a's conditional does that work in one line. It carries no provenance row, which §4.9 deletes.

**E2 is 240px on every surface — the carousel draw slide, the Reel and the Story.** One shared module, one size, no surface parameter: the figure sets at `--fs-figure` 120/120 everywhere. The 270px Story variant the previous draft published, which set the figure at `--fs-hero` 150/150, is **deleted**. §3.5's T2 is an upper bound — `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame, and zero is legal — so a coverless surface is not obliged to carry a hero node, and the Story carries none: its largest node is the odds figure at 120px. The arithmetic is §7.2's and it is decisive: 150/150 is payable only out of the Story's photograph band, and §7.2 measures the cost as that band's crop going from 3.48:1 to 3.91:1, on the one surface that ships as a still. The band heights behind that ratio are §7.2's.

**E2 is stacked on every surface, never a side-by-side lockup.** Widths below are MEASURED in this session with fontTools directly against the bundled `inter-latin-600-normal.woff2` and `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2`, summing real glyph advances rather than applying a per-character mean — see §4.8 for why a mean is unsafe for Inter. At the measured maximum cap of 4,500,000:

- figure, 9 glyphs of JetBrains Mono 700 at 120px = **648.0px** (the face is 0.6000em for every glyph, measured, so the mono arithmetic is exact);
- stacked conditional `1 IN 4,500,000 AT SELL-OUT` at Inter 600 44px = **619.8px**.

Both clear the 895px well and the 950px chrome track stacked, with room to spare. Side by side the **figure** lockup does not: 648.0 + a 24px gap + `1 IN 4,500,000` at 315.8px = **987.8px** against a 950px track, over by 37.8px. §10.6a sized the Reel's Row C lockup against a **100px** figure, where 9 glyphs are exactly 540px and exactly fill its 540px slot with zero margin; §3.5's `--fs-figure` floor of 120px retires that size, and at 120px the side-by-side form stops fitting. E2 is therefore stacked, which fits everywhere.

**One claim from the previous draft is withdrawn as a measurement error.** It stated that §10.6a's Story single-line form (`TICKET CAP` left, `1 IN <cap> AT SELL-OUT` right, 24px minimum gap) overflows a 950px track by 148.2px. MEASURED, it does not overflow: 264.2 + 24 + 619.8 = **908.0px**, or **943.1px** once the eyebrow's 0.08em tracking is applied — inside 950px, with 6.9px of margin at the maximum cap. §10.6a's own estimate reached the same verdict by a different route. The line is thin enough that §5.3's measured-fit rule must govern it, but it is not a defect, and §7.2's re-cut Story deletes that band on other grounds anyway. The error came from applying a single 0.6782em per-character figure to a string that is mostly narrow characters.

**Consequence handed to §6.3.** E2's 240px of type plus §10.2's 8px row paddings is **256px**, and §6.3 consumes Row C whole at that height rather than re-cutting the module into two lines. §4 states the module's height and content; the row, the photograph window that funds it and the card's rect are §6.3's, and this section publishes none of them.

**Consequence on the carousel draw slide (slides 3 onward).** The photograph is the flex residual and every other block is fixed by content: well 1050 = photo + 20 + lockup 45 + 20 + prize name + 20 + E2 240, so photo = 705 − (prize name). At a two-line name at `--fs-title` 68/70 (140px) the well is **565px**, clearing §5.7's own 500px minimum by 65px with no change to §5.7 required and passing the renderer's floor assertion at the worst case; at two lines of `--fs-lead` 56/60 (120px) it is **585px**; at a one-line `--fs-display` 88/90 (90px) it is **615px**. The counter chip on these slides is a photo overlay and costs no vertical budget. The operator lockup is 45px and §5.13 owns it; there is one value and no variant.

### 4.5 Colour and contrast

Tokens from the approved direction: newsprint ground `#F7F5F0`, ink `#14161A`, meta grey `#5A5F66`, verdict green `#0F6B45`. Ratios computed in-session against the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula.

| Element | Colour | Contrast vs `#F7F5F0` | Standard |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Unmarked ticket dot | **`--rule` `#8C8677`** | **3.33:1** | WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 (3:1, non-text) — pass |
| Marked ticket dot | `--verdict` `#0F6B45` | 6.01:1 | pass |
| Datum cross rules | `--verdict` `#0F6B45` | 6.01:1 | pass |
| Figure and legend | `--ink` `#14161A` | 16.62:1 | SC 1.4.3 — pass |
| Annotation | `--ink-meta` `#5A5F66` | 5.91:1 | SC 1.4.3 — pass |

**One hex, one token name.** The draft specified `#8B867B`; §3.2 shipped `--dot-empty: #948C7C`; §5.14 shipped `--rule: #8C8677`. §8's ruling settles it on measurement: `#948C7C` is 3.06:1 on paper and **2.952:1 on `--scene-tone` `#F3F1EC`**, an SC 1.4.11 failure that no scene tone can rescue, while `#8C8677` measures 3.33:1 on paper and 3.21:1 on the scene tone. `#8B867B` and `#8C8677` both round to 3.33:1 on paper (computed: 3.327 and 3.328), so the switch costs this section nothing and gains the scene layer its floor. **§3 owns the hex; the dot references `--rule`.** `--dot-empty` is retired, `--hairline` `#D8D3C8` carries the decorative rules that `--rule` used to name in §3.2, and §3.2's "never a dot" clause goes with it.

`#8C8677` against `#0F6B45` measures **1.80:1**, which confirms the working grey cannot separate from the green on luminance and hands the entire marking load to the datum cross.

**Why the mark cannot be carried by hue — corrected reasoning.** The draft claimed a brute-force sweep found that *no* neutral grey clears 3:1 against both the paper and the green, then contradicted itself by quoting black at 3.21:1 against the green and calling it a failure. Re-run in-session: verdict green sits at relative luminance 0.1105, newsprint at 0.9137, and **exactly 12 of the 256 neutral greys clear 3:1 on both sides — `#000000` through `#0B0B0B`** (`#0B0B0B`: 18.06:1 vs paper, 3.01:1 vs green; `#0C0C0C` falls to 2.99:1 on the green side). The brand's own ink `#14161A` measures 2.77:1 against the green and does not qualify; meta grey `#5A5F66` measures **1.02:1** — effectively identical luminance.

So hue *could* carry the mark, but only by painting 1,440 unmarked dots in near-black. That is rejected on design grounds, and the grounds are specific: at 35.6% coverage a near-black field reads as a solid slab rather than a lattice, it inverts figure and ground so the marked ticket becomes *lighter* than its neighbours, and it is the opposite of the approved light direction. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 (Use of Colour) forbids colour-alone regardless of ratio. **The marked ticket is identified by a shape difference, specified in §4.6.** The conclusion is the draft's; the reasoning is now true.

**The proven mockup's locator fails and must not be carried forward.** `merged.mjs:59` uses `#CFCABE` for unmarked dots (**1.50:1** against the paper — below the 3:1 floor) and `merged.mjs:60` adds `box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px rgba(15,107,69,.22)` as the halo, which composites over newsprint to `#C4D7CA` at **1.38:1**. Both are invisible in greyscale and to a viewer with a green deficiency.

### 4.6 The marked ticket

The marked ticket exists in one state only — the full band on the count slide, with `cap ≤ 1,440`. It is **the same 10px dot at the same pitch**, filled `--verdict` `#0F6B45`. It is never enlarged. Enlarging it would make one ticket occupy more area than the others, which is the graphical form of the thing CAP guidance bans verbatim: "Promoters should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true."

It is located by a **datum cross**, borrowed from the British Rail / Kinneir register the direction research identifies as the authentically British and authentically neutral one:

- a 2px `#0F6B45` horizontal rule spanning the full 895px band width at the marked row's centre;
- a 2px `#0F6B45` vertical rule spanning the full band height at the marked column's centre;
- both drawn **behind** the dots, so every ticket in the row and column stays fully visible and the rules read as dashed where dots occlude them — no ticket is ever hidden by the locator;
- **both rules terminate at the band edges.** The draft specified a 20px tick extending past the right edge carrying a label; there is no external tick and no external label, and the legend carries the explanation. (The band's right edge is x 960 and §5.9's sheet-edge hairline sits at x 1015, so the band clears it by **55px**. That 55px is §3.5's deliberate right margin between a band-sized well and the sheet edge, not spare room: a right-hand tick and label would have to live in it and cannot.)

The cross reads at 6.01:1 in greyscale, so the information survives desaturation and a green deficiency. It never renders on a video canvas, because E1 never does — and, per §4.7, it never renders anywhere above the ceiling, on any layer, including §8.5's scene ghost. Verdict green in this device belongs to the E1 mark and its cross alone.

§5.8's contrary sentence — "the winner dot is **not** ringed, highlighted or enlarged … it is meant to be hard to find" — is superseded. The dot is not enlarged and not ringed; it is *located*, which is a different act, and the alt text depends on it being findable.

**Position rule, fully specified.** The mockup hard-codes `Math.floor(cap * 0.37)` (`merged.mjs:47`), putting every mark on every slide at the same relative spot — visibly a template. Replace with a deterministic hash so the same draw renders identically wherever it is drawn:

```js
// FNV-1a, 32-bit, over the UTF-8 bytes of draw.slug
let h = 2166136261 >>> 0;
for (const b of new TextEncoder().encode(slug)) {
  h = (h ^ b) >>> 0;
  h = Math.imul(h, 16777619) >>> 0;
}
const i = eligible[h % eligible.length];   // 0-based cell index
const row = Math.floor(i / 60) + 1;        // 1-based
const col = (i % 60) + 1;                  // 1-based
```

`eligible` is built once as every `i` in `[0, cap)` whose 1-based `col ∉ {1, 60}` — so the cross always has grid on both sides — and, **when `R >= 4`**, whose `row ∉ {1, R}`: a mark in the first row reads as "the first ticket wins" and one in the last reads as "the last". When `R < 4` the row exclusion is dropped. If `eligible` comes out empty (only possible for a cap below 60, which `plausibleEntries`' own floor of 100 would reject, but the fallback must be total), it falls back to every `i` in `[0, cap)`.

**The position carries no claim**, and §10.6a's legend line 3 says so on the slide in words.

### 4.7 Above the ceiling: the encoding and the marker

**§4.7 is normative for the above-ceiling encoding on every surface.** Three rivals are deleted rather than demoted: §5.8's Encoding B rail, §7.2's band-5 bar and §8.5's thousand-blocks. No section publishes a fallback encoding of its own.

No linear encoding survives this inventory. The measured range is 99 to 4,500,000 — four and a half orders of magnitude. At this geometry a literal sheet would be **3,505px** tall at a cap of 13,995 (`ceil(13995/60) = 234` rows; 2.6 carousel slide heights) and **1,124,995px** tall at the maximum cap (75,000 rows; 833 slide heights). The question is not how to compress the sheet; it is what the graphic should encode once it cannot encode every ticket.

**Candidate A — proportional bar. Rejected.** A single 895px bar with `1/cap` filled. MEASURED: at 1 in 1,501 the fill is 0.596px; at the median cap of 9,999 it is 0.0895px (0.179 device px at 2×); at the maximum cap, 0.0002px. It renders as literally nothing across most of the render window, collapsing every long-odds draw into one indistinguishable empty rectangle, and an empty rectangle reads to a first-time viewer as a rendering bug rather than as a fact.

*The kill-shot the draft did not have, and which is why the bar is deleted rather than re-argued.* §5.8 clamped its green segment to `max(2px, 888/cap)`. 888/444 = 2.0, so **every cap above 444 renders the identical 2px mark**; §7.2's 950px Story rail crosses over at 475. The measured median cap is 9,999 and the measured p25 is 1,500, so the great majority of live draws clamp to one constant picture that reads as roughly 1 in 444 — a 23× flattery at 1 in 9,999 and four orders of magnitude at the maximum. That is not a clamp needing disclosure; it is a constant masquerading as a measurement, and a 34px line admitting the graphic is wrong does not discharge CAP's page-design rule. (The share of inventory at or below 444, where the bar would not clamp, has not been queried; the measured minimum cap is 99, so it is not zero. "100% of live draws clamp" would be an overstatement.)

This is worth stating plainly because the mockup already reaches for it. `merged.mjs:45` returns a bar for `cap > 1500`, and `merged.mjs:63` sets `.barfill{width:6px}` — a **constant** 6px regardless of cap, so a cap of 2,000 and a cap of 4,500,000 render with an identical fill, under a label reading `N tickets · 1 is yours`, a second-person claim §10.6a bans. Known weakness (d) in the rendered mockups is more accurately "the fallback is an unlabelled placeholder" than "there is no fallback".

**Candidate B — logarithmic odds ladder. Rejected on compliance grounds, not on comprehension.** A marker on a log axis from 1 in 100 to 1 in 5,000,000. MEASURED positions: 1 in 999 at 21.3%, 1 in 9,999 at 42.6%, 1 in 1,000,000 at 85.1%. A draw with ten times the cap looks exactly twice as bad; a draw with a thousand times the cap looks four times as bad. A log scale systematically *flatters long odds*, landing directly on CAP 8.20/8.21 and the page-design guidance. The one encoding that most efficiently spans the range is the one PDD may not use. The comprehension objection is separately decisive: the premise of the device is "one dot = one ticket, and you can feel it"; a marker on an unlabelled abstract axis is a bar with extra steps.

**Candidate C — the clipped sheet. Selected.** The lattice, the dot size, the pitch and the 60 columns are all unchanged. The band renders exactly one full sheet at the ceiling — 60 × 24 = 1,440 dots — and is cut. It is accompanied by the hero figure (the bare cap, §4.4's E1 lockup), the annotation row (§4.8's slot, §10.6a's string) and §10.6a's two-line clipped legend.

**How the truncation is signalled — corrected twice.** The original draft had the sheet bleed off the slide edge, which is unavailable and was withdrawn. Its replacement — "the final row is full and complete, where a natural grid's last row is almost always partial" — is also withdrawn, on the draft's own evidence: its risk register conceded that "nothing about a complete final row is self-evidently a cut to a first-time viewer". That is correct and it is fatal to the tell.

**The tell is a half-disc cut, interior to the band.** Twenty-four rows are laid out at the 15px pitch. Row 24 occupies y 345 … 355 within the band, with its equator at y 350. The band is clipped at exactly **350px**, which cuts all 60 dots of row 24 precisely through their equators, leaving a row of 60 half-discs on a hard flat 895px edge. No natural lattice ends mid-glyph, so the cut cannot be read as a design choice. And because the cut is *interior* to the band rather than at a canvas edge, it needs no bleed, touches no exclusion zone and is identical wherever the band is drawn.

There is **no fade, no gradient mask, no terminal rule, no rounded corner and no ellipsis.** Decoration would make the truncation look like a design choice rather than a measurement. At `deviceScaleFactor: 2` the clipped band is 700 device px and the cut lands on device row 700 — an integer, like every other edge in §4.4.

**And no green dot.** This is the decisive rule. Drawing one marked ticket among 1,440 visible dots when the true ratio is 1 in 9,999 shows a picture 6.9× more favourable than the fact. A viewer who takes in the graphic and not the annotation would form an impression that is not true — the exact failure CAP's page-design guidance names.

**The marker rule, stated once:** the marked ticket is drawn **iff every ticket in the cap is on the card — that is, iff `cap ≤ 1,440`.** Hard-edged, no tolerance band, and above it there is no green dot, no clamped green segment, no clamped green tile and no ghosted green dot on any layer, including §8.5's scene ghost. The omission is stated in words on the slide — **§10.6a's annotation string, in the row §4.8 sizes** — and in the alt text (§4.9), never left to be inferred. That string's `NONE MARKED` clause is this rule's on-slide discharge and may not be dropped for space: the row is mandatory in the clipped state, and a draw whose annotation cannot be composed is dropped, never the row.

The rule is deliberately slightly over-cautious at the boundary: at a cap of 1,441 the visible 1-in-1,440 picture is wrong by 0.07%, and the mark is dropped anyway. A second regime with a tolerance band would be marginally more accurate and much easier to get wrong, and it would mean the presence of a green dot no longer reliably meant "every ticket is on this card". One rule, one meaning.

**Monotonicity check.** Band height is `15·ceil(cap/60) − 5` capped at 355 full / 350 clipped: monotone non-decreasing in cap, so a longer-odds draw is never shorter than a shorter-odds one. The green dot exists only below 1,441, so its presence always means "better than 1 in 1,440" and never the reverse. The clipped state simultaneously carries maximum height, a severed edge and no mark — three signals all pointing the unfavourable way. There is no inversion anywhere in the measured range 99 → 4,500,000. The bar, by contrast, flattens everything above 444 into one flattering constant.

**What this costs, stated plainly.** Above the ceiling the device loses within-post comparability — 1 in 2,000 and 1 in 4,500,000 produce the same picture. The comparison is carried instead by the hero figure, set in tabular mono at a fixed size so digit count itself is the comparison: `2,000` against `4,500,000` is visibly a different object at 120px, and E2 puts that same figure on every other draw slide. That is the "beautifully set number" the teardown flagged as available (unoccupied territory #5), and it is the reason the figure is specified in mono rather than in Bricolage. Given §4.2, this is what the count slide looks like on roughly three quarters of days, and on every day `pickBestCategory` lands on car-draws.

**On the swipe cue.** The draft argued that a bleeding sheet doubles as the evidence-backed swipe cue (NN/g: arrows are read as *tap* affordances; a partial element crossing the slide edge is the cue that works) and should retire the `SWIPE TO SEE ALL … →` string at `render.mjs:155`. There is no bleed, and `render.mjs:155` renders on the **cover** (the intro slide), not on a draw slide, so that string is §5's call. Withdrawn.

### 4.8 The slots, their measured capacities, and the wording law

**Every rendered string in this device is §10.6a's.** §4.8 publishes no wording table and no candidate string; it owns the slots, their type steps (from §3.5), their alignment and their measured capacities, and it keeps the CAP reasoning that produced the ban list.

| Slot | Type | Measure | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eyebrow | Inter 600, `--fs-label` 44/50, `--ink-meta`, 0.08em tracking | 895px, left | E1 and E2 |
| Hero figure | JetBrains Mono 700, tabular, `--fs-figure` 120/120, `--ink` | 895px still / 950px video, left | E1 and E2 |
| Annotation | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-label` 44/50, `--ink-meta`, right-aligned to x 960 | 895px, one line, own row | E1, clipped state only — string: §10.6a |
| Legend | Inter 400, `--fs-body` 48/60, `--ink` | 895px, three lines in-grid / two clipped | E1 only |
| Conditional | Inter 600, `--fs-label` 44/50, `--ink-meta` | 895px still / 950px video, one line | E2 only |
| Provenance | **deleted from the device** — §10.4 | — | — |

**How these capacities were measured, and why the previous draft's were wrong.** Every width below was computed in this session with fontTools, summing the real `hmtx` advances of the actual glyphs in the bundled woff2 files — not by multiplying a character count by a per-character mean.

That distinction is load-bearing, because the registry contains **three different figures for the same face**: §3.5 measured Inter 600 uppercase at 0.6782em, §10.2 measured it at 0.6602em, and the plain A–Z mean in `inter-latin-600-normal.woff2` is 0.6946em. All three are defensible over different sample sets, and **all three are unsafe as a budget**, because Inter's space is 0.2520em and its comma 0.3188em, so a real string's effective per-character advance ranges from 0.51em to 0.61em depending on how many spaces and commas it holds. There is no flat per-character number for Inter that is both safe and useful. Build-time measurement is the only correct gate, which is what §5.3's measured-fit rule already provides.

JetBrains Mono 700 is the opposite case and is now settled beyond doubt: MEASURED, **every** glyph in the bundled file — A–Z, a–z, digits, comma, hyphen, middot, em dash and space — advances exactly 600/1000 units. §3.5 closed this for digits, comma and sterling; it holds for the whole Latin set, so all mono arithmetic below is exact.

Measured capacities:

- **Eyebrow** `TICKET CAP` at Inter 600 44px: **264.2px** bare, **299.4px** with the specified 0.08em tracking.
- **Figure**: 72.0px per glyph at 120px, on every surface — there is no per-surface figure size and no Story variant. §3.5's T4 caps it at 9 glyphs, and `4,500,000` — the measured maximum stored cap — is exactly 9: **648.0px** against 895px, 247px spare, and against 950px, 302px spare. At 10 or more glyphs the build does not shrink the figure; the draw is dropped. The draft's `1 IN 9,999` form is retired by §10.6a for exactly this reason: `1 IN 4,500,000` is 14 glyphs = 1,008px at 120px and does not fit the band, and the bare cap is the only form that survives the measured inventory at the figure floor.
- **Annotation**: 26.4px per glyph at 44px. Capacity on 895px is **33 glyphs** (871.2px; a 34th takes it to 897.6px and overflows).
- **Legend**: §10.6a's longest in-grid line, `We do not know which ticket wins.`, measures **788.4px** at Inter 400 48px; `Odds at sell-out: 1 in 4,500,000.` measures **728.2px**; `Each dot is one ticket.` measures **500.2px**. All clear 895px. Three lines × 60px = the 180px §4.4 budgets. (The previous draft quoted 798.3px for the sell-out line from a derived 24.19px/character rate; the real figure is 70px narrower, and the rate itself was the weakest number in that draft.)
- **Conditional**: `1 IN 4,500,000 AT SELL-OUT` at Inter 600 44px = **619.8px**, inside both measures with wide margin. (The draft's 775.9px was the same flat-rate error: 26 glyphs × 0.6782em × 44px.)

**The annotation has its own row.** The draft, and the geometry ruling that replaced it, both put the annotation on the eyebrow line right-aligned. At §3.5's legal type steps that is impossible: the eyebrow is 299.4px with its tracking and §10.6a's annotation is 739.2px at the median cap, so the pair needs **1,038.6px** of an 895px measure before any gap at all. The annotation therefore occupies its own 50px row directly beneath the band, right-aligned to x 960, present in the clipped state only, and §4.4's clipped column is costed with it and its 10px gap.

**The slot cannot overflow, and that is now a proof rather than a sample.** §10.6a has ratified `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED`. Its fixed cost is 23 glyphs; `{shown}` is §4.7's ceiling, always the literal `1,440`, and the only variable is `{cap}` in its en-GB grouped form, which §3.5's T4 bounds at 9 glyphs — a 10-glyph cap drops the draw at the figure node before the annotation is ever composed. The bounded worst case is therefore 23 + 9 = **32 glyphs = 844.8px** at the measured maximum cap, against the slot's 33 glyphs / 871.2px; at the median cap it is 28 glyphs = **739.2px**, with 155.8px spare. §5.3's measured-fit rule keeps its hard-failing posture and simply has no reachable failure state on this row. The word `SHOWN` is struck from the string deliberately — at the maximum cap it costs six glyphs the slot does not have — and the explicit not-shown count moves to §4.9's clipped alt text, which is now its sole normative home. The row is mandatory whenever the sheet is clipped: there is no graceful degradation and no fallback in which it is dropped, because it carries §4.7's no-mark statement. A draw whose annotation cannot be composed is dropped; the row never is.

**No new type step was created to make this fit, and none was needed.** `--fs-legal` 38px stays scoped to the conditions band and `--fs-micro` 34px to the still micro tier plus §10.4's dated stamp, per §3.5's T3; the annotation stays at `--fs-label` 44px. A correction carrier set smaller than the legend it corrects would in any case be the "layout, design or format" de-emphasis CAP names.

**Why the ban list exists, and where it now lives.** The reasoning stays here; the enforcement is §10.6a Part 2's allow-list, CI fixture and DOM identity check, which is a stronger control than the lint this section originally specified. A deny-list cannot enumerate second-person framings — `Your odds`, `your chances`, `you have a 1 in`, `1 is yours` is four of an unbounded set, and PDD's own archived caption already shipped `better odds than most raffles you'll scroll past all week`, two violations with zero deny-list hits. The classes and their grounds:

- **Every second-person framing.** A ticket cap is a property of the draw. A viewer's odds depend on how many tickets they hold and are undefined at zero, so `YOUR ODDS AT THE CAP` is false for every viewer who has not bought exactly one ticket; under CAP 8.21 it implies the reader is already in the draw, and under 8.20 it converts a published cap into a personal probability claim. `merged.mjs:83` ships `Your odds` and `merged.mjs:45` ships `1 is yours`.
- **Bare superlatives about odds quality** — `Best odds`, `shortest odds`, `better odds than`, `great odds`. `merged.mjs:107` ships `Best odds tonight`. A superlative scoped to "today" cannot be evidenced under CAP 3.7: the pool is one category, truncated at 300 rows, from an inventory PDD has never enumerated.
- **`only` and `just` before a cap figure** — emphasis that creates an untrue overall impression.
- **Any comparison to the National Lottery, EuroMillions, lightning strikes or similar.** The category's oldest cliché, a second objective claim needing its own CAP 3.7 evidence, and its whole rhetorical function is to make the odds feel good.
- **`sold`, `remaining`, `left`, `selling fast`, `X% sold`.** PDD holds no sell-through data. Using any of them fabricates a fact and, under the DMCC Act 2024 consumer provisions (in force 6 Apr 2025), manufactures false scarcity.
- **`verified`, `audited`, `guaranteed`, `confirmed`, `approved`, `fair`.**

`carousel/config.json:13`'s `global.bannedPhrases` array is the precedent for the mechanism, and §10.6a correctly notes it is not a control today: verified in-session, its only consumer in the whole repository is `brief.mjs:11`, which prints it into a Markdown briefing.

**The draft's one permitted comparative is withdrawn.** `SHORTEST TICKET CAP OF THE SIX BELOW — 1 IN 599` used a banned superlative form, hard-coded a deck size that §5.11 has changed, and reintroduced the `1 IN` hero the figure arithmetic rules out. §10.6a replaces it with a cover proof line whose count is interpolated from §5.11's `drawsRendered` and whose comparative is about a *cap* rather than about odds quality. §4 states no cover copy. The mockup line at `merged.mjs:108` — *"Every odds figure checked against the operator's own cap"* — is retired as unlocated, untimed, and, per §4.3, not reliably true.

### 4.9 Provenance and alt text

**§10.4 is the normative owner of the evidence and provenance contract** — the three columns, the method enum and its renderable allow-list, the freshness window, and the rule that enforcement is a selection predicate in `fetchEndingSoon` rather than a render gate. §4 publishes none of it. The draft's column definitions, its five-value enum (including the `operator-api` value `lib/parse.mjs:670–682` shows must never render), its 48-hour render-refusal paragraph and its on-slide provenance line are all deleted from this section.

**The on-device provenance line is deleted.** §10.2's conditions-band stamp and the masthead's dated stamp are the only rendered provenance, and §10.4 sets their content. Three independent constraints kill the on-device line, and any one is sufficient: §3.5 reserves the 34px step for the conditions strip and the dated stamp and forbids it elsewhere, so the line has no legal type size on the device; at 44px it measures well over 1,100px at a typical host and over 1,300px at the longest live entry domain (`thecollectorsclubcompetitions.com`, 33 characters) against an 895px band; and CAP 3.7 requires evidence *held* before publication, not evidence displayed adjacently. Deleting it frees the ~50px line box and its gap, which is part of what funds the 24-row ceiling and §10.6a's third legend line.

This closes the audit's "mandated but rendered nowhere" finding in the only honest direction: no surface renders a per-figure line, and none is required to.

**What §4.9 keeps: the wording law and the alt text.**

The stamp, wherever it renders, **may claim only** that PDD read this specific number from that specific host at that specific time, with the hostname rendered as a bare registrable domain — never a full URL, never a link.

It **may not claim**, and the DOM identity check must block:

- that PDD verified the draw, the operator, the odds or the fairness of anything — **"read from" is the only permitted verb**;
- that the figure is current *now*: the stamp is a past-tense reading, which is why the time is mandatory and why "checked by Prize Draws Daily" without a timestamp is banned outright;
- that PDD knows how many tickets have sold;
- endorsement, approval, partnership or any relationship with the operator.

**Alt text.** `carousel/honesty.mjs:31–37` (`altTexts`, written to `out/alt.json` at `build.mjs:161`) currently omits odds entirely — verified in-session: its per-draw template carries title, price and closing date only, and neither the intro line nor the closing CTA line mentions odds. The odds figure is the primary claim on the slide, so it must be described, both for screen readers and because `out/alt.json` is an existing E-E-A-T asset the rework must preserve. Alt text has no space budget, so it carries the full statements the slide cannot fit. Three required forms, one per state:

- **E1, full band** — `Dot grid: 699 dots, one per ticket, 60 to a row. One dot is marked green and crossed by two rules; it stands for one ticket and its position is arbitrary — we do not know which ticket wins, or how many have sold. Ticket cap read from <host> at <HH:mm>, <D MMM YYYY>.`
- **E1, clipped** — `Dot grid: 1,440 of the 9,999 tickets this draw is capped at, 60 to a row, cut off after 1,440 — the last row of dots is cut in half to show the sheet is not complete. 8,559 dots are not shown and no dot is marked green. We do not know how many tickets have sold. Ticket cap read from <host> at <HH:mm>, <D MMM YYYY>.`
- **E2, numeral lockup** — `Ticket cap 9,999 tickets, so the odds are 1 in 9,999 if this draw sells out. No dot grid on this card. We do not know how many tickets have sold. Ticket cap read from <host> at <HH:mm>, <D MMM YYYY>.`

The clipped form is, by ruling, **the only place the not-shown count is stated**: the on-slide annotation carries shown-of-cap and the absence of the mark, and the alt text carries the subtraction. It is therefore not an optional enrichment of the row and must not be trimmed alongside it.

`<host>` is the bare registrable domain of the provenance URL §10.4 stores, never a link.

### 4.10 Where the device must live in the codebase

This is a hard architectural constraint, not a preference. The three video renderers build their CSS by regex-scraping `styles.css` — verified in-session, line by line:

- `reel-template.mjs:46` lifts `:root` and `[data-theme="x"]` blocks — **and `reel-template.mjs:47` lifts a second set**, `.p-(?:embers|golddust|fireflies|holo)`, so the digest's "and NOTHING ELSE" is true of the token regex but not of that file's total lift;
- `story.mjs:31` lifts the token blocks only;
- `reel.mjs:69` lifts the token blocks only.

`reel-template.mjs:43` states the intent outright: *"Descendant rules are intentionally skipped."* The conclusion is unchanged and the particle exception does not rescue it: a `.odds-grid{…}` rule added to `styles.css` matches neither regex in any of the three files, so it would render correctly on the carousel and **silently vanish from the Reel and the Story**, with no error.

The device must be a **shared module that emits its own markup and its own scoped CSS** — both E1 and E2 — imported by `render.mjs`, `reel-template.mjs` and `story.mjs` alike, and not a stylesheet rule that one renderer scrapes out of another's text. Only the colour tokens may live in `:root`, because those are the things the regex is designed to carry. This constraint binds even though E1 now renders on the carousel alone: E2 renders on all three, at one height and one figure size with no surface parameter, so a single emitter is the correct shape and a module that emits only one of the two encodings will be extended into the other by whoever ships next.

**Font gap.** The direction specifies JetBrains Mono 400/500/700 for every figure. `carousel/fonts.mjs:20` registers **only weight 700**, and `carousel/assets/fonts/` contains `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2` and no other mono file (directory listed in-session: 17 files, one mono). `fonts.mjs:32` swallows a missing file in a bare `catch`.

One correction to the draft's account of the consequence: that `catch` carries the comment *"missing font file -> skip; CDN link is the fallback"*, but **the comment is stale** — grepping `render.mjs`, `reel-template.mjs`, `reel.mjs`, `story.mjs` and `fonts.mjs` in this session finds no `fonts.googleapis`, `fonts.gstatic` or any CDN reference. There is no fallback. A missing weight degrades to the next family in the CSS font stack, which for a mono stack is a system mono, breaking tabular alignment silently and emitting no warning.

Either the 400 and 500 woff2 files are bundled, or the device is specified mono-700-only. The spec assumes **JetBrains Mono 700 throughout the device**, with size and colour — not weight — carrying the hierarchy. The draft's outstanding instance of this, §7.2's `JetBrains Mono 500` dateline, is discharged: §7.2's settled band 1 sets it at 700.

### 4.11 Hierarchy budget

For contrast with the defect this replaces: today the odds are a trailing fragment, at `render.mjs:67` on the standard draw slide and `render.mjs:120` on the featured one — `<div class="closes"><b>${esc(d.closes)}</b>${d.odds ? ` · ${esc(d.odds)}` : ""}</div>` — rendered in `.closes` at 33px (`styles.css:358`) and `.feat-closes` at 32px (`styles.css:382`), beside `.prize` at 98px (`styles.css:346`) and `.feat-name` at 96px (`styles.css:374`). The one datum that justifies the post is set at a third the size of the prize name that every competitor also shows.

**The reworked ordering.** On the count slide, in descending area and size: the band (895 × up to 355) → the hero figure at 120px → the prize name at 68px, two lines → the eyebrow and, in the clipped state, the annotation at 44px → the legend at 48px, three lines full and two clipped. On every other draw slide: the photograph (565px) → the hero figure at 120px → the prize name at 88px one line or 68px two → E2's eyebrow and conditional at 44px.

The figure is the largest **text** element on every draw slide. §3.5's T1 guarantees it by construction rather than by assertion: the prize name's largest step is 88px and the figure's floor is 120px, a ratio of **1.36:1**. Today that ratio is 0.34 at `render.mjs:67`. On the Story the margin is wider still — §7.2's band 2 sets the prize name at 68px against the same 120px figure, **1.76:1** — and it is bought with no `--fs-hero` node at all.

Under CAP's own guidance, type size and hierarchy are a compliance surface, and this ordering is the compliant one. The draft additionally claimed this is "the same ordering Instagram's 'adds material value' test rewards" — that is an inference, not a finding. The Recommendation Guidelines require the added value to be present and visible; they say nothing about type size. The hierarchy argument rests on CAP's page-design guidance alone, and it does not need the second prop.

**The space this costs, audited.** The draft's "the device reserves 864px, leaving 486px for the photograph" was wrong twice over: the 864px budget was computed against Meta's Box A on a canvas the band no longer occupies, and the 486px omitted §5.2's 300px of standing chrome. The true figures, all summing exactly:

- **Count slide, full state** (no photograph): 70 + 10 + 45 + 10 + 140 + 20 + 50 + 10 + 120 + 10 + 355 + 10 + 180 = **1,030** of a 1,050px well, 20px of air.
- **Count slide, clipped state** (the default, §4.2): 70 + 10 + 45 + 10 + 140 + 20 + 50 + 10 + 120 + 10 + 350 + 10 + 50 + 10 + 120 = **1,025** of the same well, 25px of air, with the annotation row and its gap costed in and the legend at two lines.
- **Every other draw slide**: 565 + 20 + 45 + 20 + 140 + 20 + 240 = **1,050** exactly, with the photograph the largest element on the slide at 53.8% of the well and clearing §5.7's own 500px floor by 65px.

The draft's open question — does the space left for the photograph satisfy the direction's requirement that it dominates — is closed in §5's favour on every draw slide except one, and answered honestly on that one: the count slide has no photograph at all, by design, and that is the price of the band.

One further note for §5: Mosseri (OFFICIAL, Oct 2024) confirms Instagram often gives a carousel "a second chance" by auto-advancing to the second media. Slide 2 must therefore stand alone. The count slide does — it carries brand, recency via the chip, premise via the prize name and the single most material fact in the system — but §5.6's Delta 1 day-angle kicker is deleted from it (80px of repeated cover copy competing with the figure, and §3.5's T2 permits at most one anchor per frame), so it no longer states the day's angle. That is a real weakening of the cold-entry case and it is listed as a risk.

### Decisions this section commits to

- The lattice is 60 columns of 10px dots on a 5px gap, 15px pitch, band **895px** wide, **left-aligned at x 65** to §3.5's content well (x 65 … 960). The 895px is forced by §3.7's `--dot-size`/`--dot-gap`; §3.5 sized the well to it, so the band fills its column with zero residual and left-aligning and centring are the same placement. Only the row count varies. Every edge is an integer at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` (device px 130 … 1920, pitch 30, dot 20, gap 10). The draft's centred origin at x 92.5 is retired.
- **§3.5 is the sole owner of the gutter and both tracks**, and has settled them: `--gutter: 65px` on every canvas, a 950px chrome track and an 895px content well. §4.4 publishes a derivation of those numbers and no rival value; the earlier 70px/940px pairing is retired, and no figure in this section is derived from it.
- §4.4 is the **sole normative source** for columns, dot, gap, pitch, band width, band origin, the rows formula, the ceiling, the E1/E2 surface assignment, the count-slide budget and the E2 module height on all surfaces. §5.7's competing block table is deleted; §5.8, §5.9, §6.3, §7.2 and §8.5 reference this section and publish none of those numbers. §3.5 owns the gutter, the tracks, the type scale and the hero-figure floor; §3.7 owns the token literals; §10.6a owns every string; §10.4 owns the evidence contract; §10.2 owns the conditions band; §7.2 owns the Story's bands; §6.3 owns the Reel's rows and rects; §5.11 owns the deck's draw count.
- **Three rival lattices are deleted by name.** §5.8's 74 columns / 8px dot / 4.05px gutter on 888px: `(888 − 592)/73 = 4.0548px` = 8.11 device px at dsf 2, fractional at both scales, and its module sums to 303 not the stated 301. §8.5's "60 columns of 8px dots at 15px pitch, 900px, x 90–990": `59 × 15 + 8 = 893`, so the published width was wrong; the ghost becomes a 12%-ink echo of the master lattice at x 65 … 960. §6.3's 240 × 120 slot: deleted outright.
- `R = ceil(cap/60)`; full band `H = 15R − 5`; clipped band a constant **350px**. The grid's HEIGHT is the datum, and there is no per-slide rescaling, ever — with the honest caveat that with one band per deck there is no second band to compare it to.
- The ceiling is **24 rows = 1,440 tickets = 355px**, derived from the count slide's 375px band allowance (1,050px well − 675px of fixed blocks) with 20px of slack. 25 rows would leave 5px, which is not a budget on a column whose prize name is measured at render. (The previous draft published 670/380/10px here; the block heights sum to 675, so the correct trio is 675/375/5px.)
- **The count-slide fixed blocks are 675px in BOTH states.** The clipped state loses the legend's third line (−60) and gains the annotation row and its gap (+60), which is why the table now carries rows 13a and 13b explicitly rather than in prose. Full column 1,030 of 1,050 (20px air, chip-row top y 152); clipped column 1,025 (25px air, y 157); at the measured minimum cap of 99, 700 (350px air, y 482).
- **The counter chip row is 70px** — a 50px `--fs-label` 44/50 line box with 10px of padding top and bottom. The chip has no access to `--fs-micro`: §3.5's T3 scopes 34px to the conditions strip and §10.4's dated stamp. §4.4 owns the row height; §5.9 owns the chip's appearance and restates its type step to match.
- **E1 (the full band) renders on the carousel count slide and nowhere else. E2 (the numeral lockup, 240px) renders on every other draw slide, on the Reel and on the Story — one module, one size, no surface parameter.** On 1080×1350 you can have the photograph or the band, not both; slide 2 is the slide that gives up its photograph, because §5.6 Delta 2 already routes the lowest-cap draw there and it is the slide Instagram re-serves cold. E1's own stack is 380 + H, so at the ceiling the photograph on a draw slide would be 70px and at the proven 699-ticket render 250px.
- **The 270px Story variant of E2 is deleted.** The odds figure sets at `--fs-figure` 120/120 on every surface. §3.5's T2 is an upper bound of one `--fs-hero` node per frame and zero is legal; the Story carries zero, and 150/150 is payable only out of §7.2's photograph band, at a crop §7.2 measures going from 3.48:1 to 3.91:1. The band heights behind that ratio are §7.2's and are not restated here.
- The Reel carries no grid: the band is 355px full / 350px clipped against §6.3's 337px clear photograph window (y 385 … 722) and a 285px insert card; it adds 15.32% of frame to a chrome budget already at 546/1920 = 28.44% against §6.1 rule 6's 29% ceiling, for 43.76%; and the deleted 240×120 slot holds 450 cells at the finest h.264-survivable lattice — 22× more favourable than a 9,999 cap. The Story carries no grid: §7.2's five bands and four gutters fill Box A exactly, with every band at its minimum legal height.
- The count-slide column is **bottom-anchored** — the legend ends at y 1182 and residual space pools as newsprint air above the counter chip. There is no fixed y-origin for the chip row. The renderer asserts the column sums to ≤ 1,050 and, on slides 3+, the photograph against §5.7's 500px floor, failing the build otherwise in the style of `render.mjs:193`; every state passes, so the assertion does not fire on an ordinary draw.
- E2 is **stacked** on every surface, never a side-by-side lockup: MEASURED, a 120px figure plus a 24px gap plus an inline `1 IN 4,500,000` needs 987.8px of a 950px track. §10.6a sized that lockup against a 100px figure, which exactly fills its 540px slot with zero margin and which §3.5's 120px floor retires. §6.3 consumes the module whole — 240px of type plus §10.2's 8px row paddings = 256px — rather than re-cutting it into two lines.
- **The draw slide's photograph is the flex residual**: photo = 705 − (prize-name block), giving 565px at a two-line `--fs-title` name, 585px at two lines of `--fs-lead` and 615px at a one-line `--fs-display`. The operator lockup is 45px and §5.13 owns it; there is one value.
- **Correction to the previous draft:** §10.6a's Story single-line lockup does **not** overflow. MEASURED it is 943.1px with the eyebrow's 0.08em tracking (908.0px without) against a 950px track, fitting with 6.9px of margin at the maximum cap. The earlier 148.2px overflow claim came from applying a flat 0.6782em per-character rate to a string that is mostly narrow glyphs, and is withdrawn.
- All Inter widths in this section are MEASURED per string from the bundled woff2, not multiplied out from a mean. The registry holds three different means for Inter 600 uppercase (§3.5's 0.6782em, §10.2's 0.6602em, the plain A–Z mean of 0.6946em) and none is safe as a budget, because the space is 0.2520em and the comma 0.3188em. JetBrains Mono 700 is exactly 0.6000em for every glyph in the bundled file — verified across A–Z, a–z, digits, comma, hyphen, middot, em dash and space — so all mono arithmetic here is exact.
- Unmarked ticket dots take `--rule` **`#8C8677`** (3.33:1 vs `#F7F5F0`, 1.80:1 vs `#0F6B45`). `--dot-empty` `#948C7C` is retired — it fails SC 1.4.11 at 2.952:1 on `--scene-tone` — and `#8B867B` is dropped because it and `#8C8677` both measure 3.33:1 on paper, so the switch is free. §3 owns the hex. The mockup's `#CFCABE` (1.50:1) and its `rgba(15,107,69,.22)` halo (composites to `#C4D7CA`, 1.38:1) are rejected as failing.
- Hue does not carry the mark. Exactly 12 neutral greys clear 3:1 against both `#F7F5F0` and `#0F6B45` — `#000000` through `#0B0B0B` — so it is possible but only with a near-black field, which at 35.6% coverage reads as a slab, inverts figure and ground, and contradicts the light direction. SC 1.4.1 forbids colour-alone regardless. The mark is carried by shape.
- The marked ticket stays the same 10px size and is located by a datum cross: 2px `#0F6B45` rules at full band width and height, drawn BEHIND the dots so no ticket is ever hidden, both terminating at the band edges. The band's right edge is x 960 and §5.9's sheet-edge hairline is x 1015, so the cross clears it by 55px — a margin §3.5 leaves deliberately, not spare room for a tick and label. §5.8's "not ringed, highlighted or enlarged … meant to be hard to find" is superseded: the dot is not enlarged, it is located. Verdict green in this device belongs to the E1 mark and its cross alone.
- The marked index is FNV-1a 32-bit (basis 2166136261, prime 16777619, over UTF-8 bytes of `draw.slug`, `>>>0`) mod `eligible.length`, where `eligible` excludes columns 1 and 60 always and rows 1 and R when R ≥ 4, with a total fallback to all cells if empty. The mockup's fixed `Math.floor(cap*0.37)` (`merged.mjs:47`) is dropped.
- Above 1,440 tickets the encoding is the **clipped sheet**, and §4.7 is normative for it on every surface. §5.8's Encoding B rail, §7.2's band-5 bar and §8.5's thousand-blocks are deleted, not demoted.
- **The truncation tell is a half-disc cut, interior to the band.** Row 24 spans y 345 … 355; clipping at exactly 350px severs all 60 dots through their equators onto a flat 895px edge. No fade, gradient, terminal rule, rounded corner or ellipsis. The draft's bleed was unavailable and its "complete final row" replacement was conceded illegible by its own risk register; both are withdrawn.
- **No green dot above 1,440**, on any surface or layer including §8.5's scene ghost. One mark among 1,440 visible dots at a true cap of 9,999 shows odds 6.9× better than fact and breaches CAP 8.20/8.21. Hard-edged with no tolerance band, accepting slight over-caution at 1,441 so that a green dot always means "every ticket is on this card".
- The proportional bar is rejected on two grounds: the fill measures 0.0895px at the median cap (0.179 device px at 2×), and §5.8's own `max(2px, 888/cap)` clamp crosses over at a cap of 444, so the great majority of live draws render one identical picture reading as ≈1 in 444. The mockup's bar (`merged.mjs:45,63`) is not even proportional — `.barfill` is a constant 6px, so a cap of 2,000 and a cap of 4,500,000 render identically.
- The logarithmic ladder is rejected on compliance grounds: 1 in 999 at 21.3% and 1 in 1,000,000 at 85.1% of the axis systematically flatters long odds. A literal sheet is not an option either: 3,505px at a cap of 13,995 (2.6 slide heights) and 1,124,995px at the maximum (833 slide heights).
- The figure's safety property is **conditional, not structural**. `lib/parse.mjs:151–155`, `qa-fix.mjs:5`, the live row at 99 below `plausibleEntries`' floor of 100, and `lib/parse.mjs:670–682`'s deleted API-stock path all document non-caps reaching the column. A sold count UNDERSTATES the denominator and flatters the odds. The safety mechanism is §10.4's selection predicate, and nothing in §4 may be built before Stage 0 (§12.4) ships.
- §4 publishes **no provenance column, no method enum, no freshness window and no on-device provenance line.** All four are §10.4's. Deleting the on-device line frees its ~50px line box and is forced independently by §3.5 (34px is conditions-strip-only), by measurement (well over 1,100px at a typical host against an 895px band at 44px) and by CAP 3.7 requiring evidence held rather than displayed adjacently.
- §4 publishes **no wording table and no candidate string.** §10.6a owns every string. §4.8 keeps the CAP 8.20/8.21 reasoning and the six ban classes, and owns the slots and their MEASURED capacities: eyebrow 264.2px bare / 299.4px tracked, figure 648.0px at 9 glyphs on every surface, annotation 33 glyphs on 895px, legend longest line 788.4px, conditional 619.8px.
- The annotation occupies **its own 50px row** beneath the band, right-aligned to x 960, clipped state only. It cannot share the eyebrow line at §3.5's legal type steps (299.4 + 739.2 = 1,038.6px of an 895px measure, before any gap). §10.6a's ratified `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED` costs 23 fixed glyphs plus a cap T4 bounds at 9, so the worst case is 32 glyphs / 844.8px and the median 28 / 739.2px — the slot cannot overflow while T4 holds, and the row's measured-fit gate has no reachable failure state. The row is mandatory; a draw whose annotation cannot be composed is dropped, never the row. The explicit not-shown count now lives in §4.9's clipped alt text alone.
- The draft's permitted comparative `SHORTEST TICKET CAP OF THE SIX BELOW — 1 IN 599` is withdrawn: banned superlative form, a hard-coded deck size §5.11 has changed, and a `1 IN` hero the figure arithmetic rules out. §10.6a's proof line replaces it, with the count interpolated from §5.11's `drawsRendered`. `merged.mjs:108`'s "Every odds figure checked against the operator's own cap" is retired.
- `oddsLabel()` at `format.mjs:53` is retired from every rendered surface by §10.6a and replaced by the bare, en-GB-grouped cap. The 33px `.closes` fragment at `render.mjs:67`/`styles.css:358` and the 32px `.feat-closes` at `render.mjs:120`/`styles.css:382` are replaced by a 120px figure.

E2 takes no surface parameter, so one emitter is the correct shape.

The clipped form is the sole normative home of the not-shown count.

As delivered §4 is internally consistent at a 1,440 ceiling, an x 65 origin, E1 on the count slide only and a single 240px E2. ### Open questions

- **The ≤1,440 share of the 300-row render payload** has not been queried. 25.7% is measured at ≤1,500 on the payload and 24.1% at ≤1,440 inventory-wide; the payload figure at the actual ceiling is owed before either number is quoted as the device's coverage.
- **How should a multi-prize draw be represented?** The `draws` table has no prize-count field, so a draw with five winning tickets still shows one green dot. That understates rather than overstates and is safe under CAP 8.20/8.21, but drafting a legend clause without a prize-count field means guessing, and §10.6a's three in-grid lines are full.
- **Should JetBrains Mono 400 and 500 be bundled into `carousel/assets/fonts/`?** `fonts.mjs:20` registers 700 only, `fonts.mjs:32` swallows a missing file, and there is no CDN fallback despite the comment. Until answered the device is mono-700-only.
