- **Does the count slide still stand alone cold**, with §5.6's Delta 1 day-angle kicker deleted from it? There is no measurement available — carousel children have no individual insights in the Graph API — and none is obtainable at the account's current size.

*Closed since the last round:* the annotation string (§10.6a has ratified `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED`, which fits the slot at every legal cap); Reel Row C's height (§6.3 consumes E2 whole at 256px); and where the Story's conditional sits (§7.2's band 4, row 5 — y 947 … 997 at Inter 600 44/50, §7.2's figures, not §4's).

### Risks

- **The full band now appears on one slide in the deck, and often it is a clipped sheet with no green dot.** Combine that with §4.2 — `pickBestCategory` selects car-draws today, whose 28 eligible draws include zero at or below the ceiling — and on a car-draws day the one band that renders carries no mark at all. The signature green dot may surface roughly once a week. That is a real brand cost for an account building recognition from ~66 followers, and this ruling concentrates rather than creates it.
- **The digest's stated range will make the clipped sheet look like an edge case when it is the default.** The digest says odds run "roughly 1 in 599 to 1 in 13,995"; measured, the enterable inventory runs 99 to 4,500,000 with a median of 9,999 (n = 880, nearest-rank percentiles). If the product owner's mental model comes from the digest, they will review the full grid as the normal state and the clipped sheet as the exception, which is the reverse of the measurement, and will under-weight the design effort the clipped state deserves.
- **Within-post height comparison is gone.** The draft's strongest argument for freezing the geometry was "a 2-row ribbon beside a 24-row slab in the same carousel". With one band per deck there is no second band. The comparison rests entirely on digit count in the 120px tabular figure across the other draw slides — consistent with §4.7's above-ceiling argument, but a smaller claim than §4.4 originally made. If the product owner values cross-slide height comparison above the photograph, the correct move is to delete the photograph from *every* draw slide, and that is a §5 decision this section has not taken on their behalf.
- **Nothing at this geometry has ever been rendered.** The 60-column/10px/5px band exists only as `merged.mjs`'s 10.95px fractional-cell mockup at cap 699. The 24-row ceiling, the x 65 origin, the half-disc cut, the bottom-anchored column with up to 350px of air above the chip, the 70px chip row and the 44px right-aligned annotation under a severed sheet all need eyeballing at profile-grid and in-feed size before the ceiling is locked. At feed scale a 10px dot is roughly 5px and a half-disc roughly 2.5px tall; the one relief this ruling buys is that E1 never meets h.264, because it never renders on a video canvas — only the still's own re-encode applies, and nothing can test Instagram's server-side re-encode of a still.
- **The 70px chip row is a type-scale consequence, not a design choice.** Forcing the counter off `--fs-micro` makes a 44px mono chip 70px tall sit above a 45px operator lockup. It is the correct call under §3.5's T3, but if it dominates in the render the fix is padding — §4.4's 10px each side could go to 5px for a 60px row — and not a return to 34px.
- **Twenty pixels of slack** at the count slide's worst case (a two-line prize name at 68/70 plus a 24-row band); twenty-five in the clipped state. Both are positive and asserted at build time, but any section that adds an element to slide 2 breaks it — including §10.4's proposed fifth conditions-band line, which would take 40px from the well and drop the ceiling to 22 rows (1,320 tickets, H 325, 10px slack). §10.2 currently rules the band at three lines; if that changes, the ceiling changes with it. If the next 20px is ever needed it comes from the chip-row and lockup gaps, not from the band.
- **The annotation now fits, but the reader has to subtract.** `1,440 OF 9,999` states the shown count and the true denominator and not the 8,559 that are missing; the arithmetic is trivial and §4.9's alt text spells it out, but a viewer who glances and does not subtract takes away a smaller sense of the gap than the fact. Dropping `SHOWN` also opens a misreading — `1,440 OF 9,999` with no verb could be read as a sell-through figure, which would be a fabricated fact and a §10.6 deny-list class. The mitigations are contextual rather than measured: the eyebrow `TICKET CAP` and the 120px cap figure sit immediately above and the clipped legend's `Each dot is one ticket.` immediately below. Nobody has tested that reading on a real viewer.
- **The annotation's margin is 50.2px at the worst case, not a comfortable one.** If §3.5's content well ever drops below 844.8px, or if §4.7's ceiling grows past 9,999 so `{shown}` takes a sixth glyph, every figure in §4.8 must be re-measured.
- **The 55px clearance between the band and the sheet-edge hairline is new and unrendered.** Text stops at x 960 while the photo and the chrome bands run to x 1015. §4.6's "no external tick and no external label" depends on that margin being deliberate rather than spare, and it is the coordinate most likely to be "corrected" back by a later author who does not know the well is band-sized. §5.1's definition of the well is what defends it.
- **The legend's fit is measured but the legend is not final.** Every Inter width here was measured per string from the bundled woff2, which removes the flat-rate error that produced two wrong figures in the previous draft — but §10.6a may change the strings, and the registry's three conflicting per-character means for the same face show how easily a re-derivation goes wrong. §3.5 keeps the overflow assertion report-only for the first week for exactly this reason, and no section should re-budget an Inter line from a character count.
- **The whole device is blocked on data that does not exist.** No provenance column exists anywhere in the repo (grepped in-session: zero matches for `figures_` or `total_entries_method` across `lib/`, `carousel/` and `manager/`). Until §10.4's Stage 0 ships, any deck rendered with this device could show a sold count as a cap — a smaller denominator, better-looking odds, and the precise CAP 8.20/8.21 breach the device was meant to be immune to.
- **Stage 0's yield is unknown and could starve the category rotation rather than the deck.** §10.4's predicate removes unevidenced rows from selection before `pickBestCategory` scores, so a category that loses half its rows may fall below §5.11's pool bar. `pickBestCategory` picks from categories of 12–110 eligible draws; the thin ones are the ones with the highest full-grid incidence (home-garden 58%, collectibles 55%), so attrition could remove exactly the categories where the band renders full.
- **`#8C8677` passes SC 1.4.11 at 3.33:1 with a small margin**, and the success criterion is not written for objects as small as a 10px dot. Darkening improves contrast against the paper and worsens it against the green — at `#7C776C` it measures 4.09:1 against the paper and 1.47:1 against the green — pushing even more of the marking load onto the datum cross. The only greys clearing 3:1 on both sides are `#000000`–`#0B0B0B`, which are unusable for other reasons.
- **§4 hands §6.3 a 256px Row C, and §8.3's lane-C rect is a transclusion of §6.3's insert-card rect as it stands today.** If §6.3 grows Row C to consume the module whole, the card and the scene lane grow with it and §8's lane area re-derives. §4 publishes no lane and no row beyond the rects §6.3 supplies for the surface-assignment arithmetic above; this is flagged for §6.3 and §8 to reconcile, not resolved here.
- **If the device is implemented as a `styles.css` rule rather than a shared module, E2 will render on the carousel and vanish from the Reel and the Story with no error at all.** This failure is silent by construction and no existing test would catch it.
- **`select.mjs:20` truncates `fetchEndingSoon` at 300 rows**, so every distribution measured here describes the 300 nearest-closing draws. If that limit is raised, the category mix and therefore the full/clipped ratio shift and these numbers must be re-measured.
- **`total_entries` is 880 of 880 populated with a positive value, but that is a snapshot**, and one of those values (99) already sits outside the parser's own plausibility window. A future ingest path writing null or an implausible value would silently remove the draw from selection under §10.4's predicate rather than erroring — which is the safe direction, but it is invisible, and a deck quietly shrinking over a week would read as inventory decay rather than as a parser regression.
- **Deleting §5.6's Delta 1 kicker from the count slide weakens the cold-entry case** on the one slide Instagram re-serves. The slide is self-sufficient on brand, recency, premise and fact, but it no longer states the day's angle, and there is no way to measure what that costs.

## §5 Carousel template specification — verified and corrected

## 5. Carousel template specification

The carousel is the primary growth surface, not the Reel. MEASURED (Socialinsider, 35M posts / 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025): at the 1–5K follower band, median views are 993 for a carousel, 580 for a Reel, 417 for an image. Everything below treats the still deck as the product and the video formats as derivatives.

Three facts govern the whole template:

1. **OFFICIAL (help.instagram.com/313829416281232):** Recommendation Guidelines exclude "unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value". A daily deck of other operators' photographs and prize data is squarely exposed. The added value — the ticket cap, the closing date, the operator identity — must be **visibly on the slide**. This makes the odds-hierarchy inversion a distribution-eligibility requirement, not a taste preference.
2. **OFFICIAL (Mosseri, Oct 2024):** if a viewer does not swipe, Instagram "will often give that carousel a second chance and automatically move to that second piece of media". Slide 2 is served cold. It is a second cover.
3. **OFFICIAL (Graph API):** carousel children have no individual insights. No per-slide, swipe, exit-rate or completion metric exists — not in the API, not in the app. Nothing here may be justified by, or later evaluated against, per-slide drop-off.

I am explicitly **not** building on the "majority text" demotion, the "no visible border" rule or the "photo must dominate" instruction from the Instagram Ranking Explained post. Those are stated about **reels**, not carousels, and the honest reading is that a text-dense carousel cover is not exposed to them. This matters because the cover below carries no photograph, and it would have been convenient to claim a platform rule forced the opposite.

**How fit is specified.** Wherever text must fit a box, this section states a **measured** rule, never a character budget. The renderer already runs headless Chromium (`render.mjs:186–187`); it can measure a line box. Character counts appear only as the observed distribution, to size the problem. An earlier draft derived per-glyph advances by hand and three of its four example headlines silently overflowed — that arithmetic was removed rather than corrected.

**What this section does not own.** Six decisions that used to live here now belong elsewhere and are referenced, never restated:

| Decision | Owner |
|---|---|
| Type scale, `--gutter`, the 950px chrome track and the 895px content well, the T1–T4 rules | §3.5 |
| The colour token table and the `:root` block | §3.7 |
| Dot-grid geometry: columns, dot, gap, pitch, band width, band origin, rows formula, band heights | §4.4 |
| **The count-slide vertical budget, every block height and gap on slide 2, the E1/E2 surface assignment and E2's height on every surface** | **§4.4** |
| The ceiling, the above-ceiling encoding, the green-marker rule and the marked dot's own treatment | §4.7, with §4.6 for the marker |
| Every rendered string, the conditions-band field list, and §10.4's dated stamp | §10.6a, §10.2, §10.4 |

Restating any of those is what broke the document the first time. Where §5 needs a number from one of them to close its own arithmetic, it names the owner and shows the sum.

### 5.1 Canvas, crop and keep-out geometry

Canvas stays **1080 × 1350 at `deviceScaleFactor: 2`** → 2160 × 2700 PNG. VERIFIED unchanged at `render.mjs:187`. OFFICIAL: 1080 × 1350 (4:5) is also Meta's recommended Facebook feed ratio, so the same asset cross-posts with no rework.

**The 3:4 profile-grid crop.** OFFICIAL: the profile grid centre-crops every thumbnail to 3:4, and only the *first* child of a carousel is ever the thumbnail.

| | value |
|---|---|
| Grid crop width | 1350 × 3/4 = **1012.5px** |
| Lost per side | (1080 − 1012.5) / 2 = **33.75px** |
| Grid-safe x-range | **33.75 → 1046.25** |
| Side margin | `--gutter` (§3.5) = **65px** → content from x 65 |
| Headroom inside the crop line | 65 − 33.75 = **31.25px** |

Because the crop is horizontal only, **full height survives**. Vertical position is never at risk; horizontal position is at risk on slide 1 and on no other slide. Every inner slide is uncropped, which is why §3.5 scopes the ≥150px grid-survivable anchor to slide 1 and to no other.

**Two tracks, both §3.5's, published here only as derivations with their sums.**

- **Chrome track = 950px, x 65 → 1015.** Sum from §3.5's two numbers: 1080 − 2 × 65 = 950, and 1015 − 65 = 950, which **is** Meta Safe Box A's width. The full-bleed bands (§5.2, §5.3) run their type on it, and the closing slide (§5.10) runs on it whole.
- **Content well = 895px, x 65 → 960.** Sum: 960 − 65 = 895, which is §4.4's band width to the pixel (60 × 10 + 59 × 5 = 600 + 295 = 895, from §3.7's `--dot-size` / `--dot-gap`). It is the column every still slide that carries a sheet edge lays its text in.

**The well is no longer defined by the sheet edge, and that redefinition is load-bearing.** An earlier draft defined it as "the gutter to §5.9's sheet-edge hairline", which at g = 65 would give 950 and contradict §3.5's 895. The well is §3.5's 895px column; **§5.9's hairline sits at x 1015 and a deliberate 55px right margin (1015 − 960 = 55) lies between them.** Nothing text-bearing crosses x 960: every left edge is 65, every right-aligned text edge is 960. Only two things cross it — the photo well, a bleed element bounded by the hairline, and the two full-bleed chrome bands, which run type on the 950px track because the sheet edge exists only in y 180…1182, between them. The page therefore reads 65px of left paper against 55px of right paper, a 10px asymmetry that is the closest a band-sized well can get to symmetric. A future author who does not know the well is band-sized will want to "correct" x 960 back to 1015; that is what this paragraph exists to stop.

**Why 65 and not 70.** Three constraints, in order of weight.

1. **Box A identity.** At 65 the chrome track is Box A itself. At 70 it is 940px at x 70…1010 — safe inside Box A, but a *different* number from the 9:16 track, so §5 would carry 940 while §6 and §7 carry 950. Two tracks is the exact drift that produced 64 / 65 / 70 in the first place.
2. **Zero band residual.** The band is not a free parameter: 895px is forced by §3.7's dot tokens. At 65 the well is 895 and the band fills its column, so left-aligning and centring are the *same placement* and the origin question has nothing left to decide. At 70 the band is 35px narrower than a 930px well and 45px narrower than a 940px column, and a centred origin at x 87.5 or x 92.5 is permanently re-derivable by any author.
3. **The crop does not decide it.** Both clear x 33.75…1046.25. 65 gives 31.25px of headroom, 70 gives 36.25px — a 5px difference on the one slide the crop ever touches, against a permanent second track and a permanently reopenable band origin. 65 and 70 both sit on the 5px grid, so that argument kills only 64. 64px puts the right-hand chrome edge at x 1016, 1px **outside** Box A — the identical defect §7.1 catches in the shipped `.st-card`.

31.25px of headroom is 3.09% of the 1012.5px surviving width, so the headline at x 65…960 survives the crop intact. That 5px is paid on the most important slide in the deck, forever, and it is the one thing 70px was genuinely better at. If a render shows the cover's left edge reading as cramped in the grid, the correct response is to inset slide 1's headline only, never to move the gutter.

**The build gate.** Beside `assertTypeContract()`, the renderer asserts that `--gutter` resolves to **65px** and that the two constants it lays out against are **950** and **895**. The existing measured-fit and `scrollWidth > clientWidth` checks then run against 895 (the well), 950 (the chrome bands and the closing slide) and 1015 (the photo well). A per-node "every left edge = 65" assertion is explicitly **not** adopted: it would fail on the board's own Prize (x 119) and Closes (x 668) columns and on every chip, i.e. on every legitimate run, and would be switched off within a week.

**Instagram multi-image icon keep-out (slide 1 only).** Reserved rectangle **x 900 → 1080, y 0 → 180** (180 × 180). Provenance: the 33.75px figure is OFFICIAL arithmetic; the 180 × 180 allowance is the brief's own sizing, carried forward as DESIGN JUDGEMENT — a generous allowance around the icon, not a measurement of it.

The rule: **flat colour may pass under the keep-out; no glyph, figure, mark, chip, rule or photographic subject may enter it on slide 1.** A flat rail-blue field under a white icon improves the icon's legibility, so the masthead spanning it is desirable.

**Correction to a claim inherited from the research digest.** The digest records `.pill` at `top:52px; right:50px` (`styles.css:328`) as "directly under Instagram's multi-image carousel indicator on slide 1". VERIFIED: that is **not** what ships. `.pill` is emitted only by `textOverlay()` (`render.mjs:62`) and the typographic fallback (`render.mjs:114`), both draw slides; `build.mjs:150` assembles `[intro, ...drawSlides, {type:"cta"}]`, so slide 1 is always the intro and the intro carries no pill. The pill has never rendered under the indicator and has never been crop-exposed, because the grid crop applies only to slide 1.

What survives is a **latent** hazard: the moment a draw slide leads a deck (a degraded run, a reordering, a single-draw post) the chip's right edge at x 1030 lands inside both the keep-out and 16.25px of the crop line. The position is deleted in §5.15 on that basis. §1.5's defect A4 already states this in the latent form; the earlier instruction here to amend it was written against a draft that no longer exists and is withdrawn.

### 5.2 The standing chrome

Two full-bleed bands in rail blue `--rail` **#14385F**, present and identical on every slide.

**Masthead band — x 0 → 1080, y 0 → 132.**

| Slot | Position | Content | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (left) | x 65, v-centred | `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` | Inter 700 uppercase, `--fs-label` (§3.5), tracking 0.08em, `--rail-ink` |
| B (right) | right edge x 1015, v-centred | §10.4's dated stamp | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-micro` (§3.5), `--rail-ink` with `--rail-accent` on the figures |

**The stamp's string is §10.4's, and §5 no longer publishes one.** The shipped form `CHECKED 18 SEP 09:00` is retired: §10.4's wording law makes `read from` the only permitted verb and forbids `verified`, and the same stamp appears in the Reel's top rail and the Story's band 1, so it must not be authored three times.

**Measured clearance, and a fit §10.4 has not checked.** Slot A is `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` in Inter 700 at 44px with 0.08em tracking = **480.5px**, so it ends at 65 + 480.5 = **x 545.5**. JetBrains Mono 700 advances exactly 0.600em, so at `--fs-micro` 34px a glyph is 20.4px.

| Slot B string | Glyphs | Width | Left edge (right-aligned to x 1015) | Gap from Slot A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §10.4 long, `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` | 34 | 693.6px | x 321.4 | **−224.1px — collides** |
| §10.4 short, `READ 09:00` | 10 | 204.0px | x 811.0 | **+265.5px — fits** |
| retired `CHECKED 18 SEP 09:00` | 20 | 408.0px | x 607.0 | +61.5px |

§10.4 assigns its long form to this slot and checks it against the bare 950px track (693.6px at 34px, "fits"), but the masthead is not a bare track — Slot A occupies 480.5px of it. **At the long form the two slots overlap by 224.1px, and §5.2's own rule is that where they would collide the build fails rather than shrinking either.** The short form clears by 265.5px. §5 does not author the string: the choice is §10.4's, between assigning the short form to the carousel masthead and deleting Slot A. This is recorded as an open question rather than decided here.

**Slot B is suppressed on slide 1** because it is a glyph inside the keep-out; on slide 1 the stamp moves into the dateline (§5.4), where §10.6a 1.2 already publishes the form `THU 18 SEP 2026 · READ 09:00` — 28 glyphs × 20.4 = **571.2px** in an 895px well, which fits with 323.8px spare.

**Conditions band — x 0 → 1080, y 1182 → 1350 (168px).** Envelope in §5.3; contents in §10.2.

Total standing chrome: 300px of 1350 = **22.2%**. That is deliberate and it is what makes the Mosseri re-serve work: because the brand mark, the date stamp and the legal band are on *every* slide, every slide is a valid cold entry point. Standing chrome is not decoration here; it is what lets slide 2 stand alone.

Counter-evidence carried forward: MEASURED (Verizon Media/Publicis, 5,616 US adults, Apr 2019) — **−12% ad memory when logos crowd the screen alongside captions**, with the recommendation to delete chrome rather than shrink type. This spec answers that by having exactly *two* chrome elements with no third, no badge row, no vanity stat band, and by deleting the sub-46px elements in §5.15 outright rather than shrinking them. It is a design judgement against a real measurement, not a resolved trade-off.

**Architecture note — and a correction that reverses the earlier draft's conclusion.**

VERIFIED: `reel-template.mjs:46`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` each build their CSS by scraping `styles.css` with `/(?:^|\n)\s*(?::root|\[data-theme="[^"]+"\])\s*\{[^}]*\}/g`, which matches token blocks and nothing else. `reel-template.mjs:47` runs a **second** scrape for `.p-(embers|golddust|fireflies|holo)` blocks.

The earlier draft concluded that declaring one palette on `:root` would propagate the chrome tokens to video "for free". That is backwards. RE-MEASURED, by intersecting every `var(--…)` name in `reel-template.mjs`, `story.mjs` and `reel.mjs` with every property defined in `styles.css`'s `:root` block: the video templates consume **exactly 32** custom properties that exist only in the current `:root` — `--accent`, `--accent-rgb`, `--accent-lt-rgb`, `--accent-deep-rgb`, `--glow`, `--glow-rgb`, `--ray-rgb`, `--spark-core`, `--spark-mid`, `--spark-glow-rgb`, `--hot`, `--stroke`, `--ink-end`, `--grad-1/2/3`, `--bg-1/2/3`, `--bg-solid`, `--card-rgb`, `--scrim-rgb`, `--pill-1/2/3`, `--pill-edge-rgb`, `--pill-ink-rgb`, `--gold-1/2/3`, `--gold-rgb`, `--font-display`. `--accent-rgb` alone is referenced 21 times (15 + 4 + 2 across the three files); `--font-display` (currently `'Anton'`) 8 times (6 in `reel-template.mjs`, 2 in `story.mjs`). The nine other `var()` names in those files (`--tilt`, `--t-in`, `--rot`, `--amp`, `--a`, `--dx`, `--dy`, `--d`, `--flash-t`) are locally declared animation variables and are not `:root` tokens.

⚠️ **Correction to this section's own earlier list: `--font-kicker` is NOT consumed.** RE-GREPPED: `--font-kicker` is *defined* three times in `styles.css` (`:35`, `:75`, `:178`) and there is **not one `var(--font-kicker)` reference anywhere in the repository**. §3.7's claim that it is a dead token is correct; the earlier §5.2 list was wrong to include it, and dropping it is what makes the count exactly 32 rather than 33. The decision below is unaffected either way, because `--font-display` is consumed 8 times regardless.

**Therefore: §3.7's newsprint palette is ADDED to `:root`, not substituted for it.** Substituting would leave 32 `var()` calls unresolved and break both video templates silently. This is direct evidence against §3.4/§3.7/§3.8's deletions, which must be rewritten as additive; the removal of the legacy tokens, the Anton/Oswald faces and the `.p-*` blocks belongs in the commit that retires their consumers, and **§5 does not perform it**. §5.15 records what stays and why. Because §6 does not currently perform it either, §3.7 must name the section that does. (`--ink` and the existing `--ink-end` are distinct properties and coexist legally; the check is for exact-name collisions.)

Because both blocks are lifted by the same regex, **no custom property may be defined twice across them** — last block wins, silently, on all four surfaces. It warrants a build assertion in §10, not a convention.

The same scoping applies to the particle profiles. VERIFIED: `reel-template.mjs:691` reads `catCfg(sel.slug)` and `:783` renders `particleField(cfg.particles, seed)`. **This section deletes the particle layers from the carousel renderer only.** Removing the config keys is §8.7's, in the same commit that deletes `theme` — §8.7 now owns the `config.json` category schema outright and §5 states none of it.

**What one carousel palette does still fix.** VERIFIED: `config.json` themes six slugs — `car-draws`, `cash-prizes`, `house-draws`, `tech-giveaways`, `luxury`, `collectibles` — and `house-draws` has **zero** live enterable inventory. MEASURED against the live DB, 17 Sep 2026, 880 enterable draws (`status=active` AND `draw_date` in the future): `sports-outdoors` 102, `home-garden` 44, and **2 draws with no category at all** — 148 draws = **16.8%** fall through `config.mjs:15`'s generic fallback, which also supplies the hook string `WIN BIG`. With one carousel palette there is nothing to fall through to. (§8.7 now authors `sports-outdoors` and `home-garden` entries and deletes the `hook` key, so the fallback stops being a colour decision and becomes a coverage gate.)

That sentence is about **colour**. It is not a claim that the still deck carries no per-category identity: structure does fall through, to §8's NEUTRAL scene. Whether a scene ground renders on `still-4x5`, in what tone and over what area, is §8's; §5.4 and §5.7 mount it and supply the exclusion rects. The earlier draft's "no `[data-theme]` variants are used by the carousel" is retained as written — no `[data-theme]` block is authored — and stops being read as "no scene".

### 5.3 The conditions zone — the band the template cannot render without

**BINDING (ASA/CAP):** the ASA "is unlikely to consider social media posts sufficiently limited by time or space, and is likely to expect ALL significant conditions to be included in promotional material posted on social media". "Link in bio" does not discharge this. CAP 8.17 significant conditions include how to participate, any free-entry route, the closing date and the number and nature of prizes.

**§10.2 owns the band's contents.** The six fields, where each is discharged, the three line strings, their states, the type size and the `free_entry_route` enum are all §10.2's and are not restated here. §5 owns four things only:

1. **The envelope.** x 0 → 1080, y 1182 → 1350, fill `--rail`. Fixed height 168px. With §10.2's three-line, 135px type block that is 16.5 + 135 + 16.5 = **168** exactly. Two-line content centres vertically in the same fixed box; the band never changes height.
2. **The track.** Band type runs on §3.5's **950px chrome track, x 65 → 1015**. §10.2's own carousel geometry at a 952px track (x 64 → 1016) was written against the retired 64px gutter and puts the right edge 1px outside Box A; it re-derives to **950px at x 65…1015**, not to 940, and must not be implemented as a second number.
3. **The fit rule.** Each band line is measured at render against **950px**. Any line that overflows fails the build. The band is never shrunk and a legal line is never truncated. §10.2 adopts this mechanism; it is the only one that survives real operator data. MEASURED: the 60 distinct entry domains across the 880 live enterable draws have a median length of 23 characters and a maximum of 33 (`thecollectorsclubcompetitions.com`), so any line carrying a host is sized by that worst case. VERIFIED: **`entry_url` is populated on 880 of 880** live enterable draws, so the host is always available.
4. **The render contract.** The slide builder refuses to emit a PNG for any slide whose conditions band is missing a required field or whose lines fail the measured fit. Precedent exists: VERIFIED, `render.mjs:191–194` already catches a readiness timeout and throws `"refusing to ship a degraded slide"` at `render.mjs:193`. The band joins that contract. There is no flag that disables it and no code path that renders a slide without it.

**The measured-fit rule stays hard-failing, and its one known legitimate-draw failure case is now closed by construction rather than by exemption.** §4.8's clipped-state annotation row was the only place a rule-abiding draw could fail the gate: at `{shown} OF {cap} SHOWN · NONE MARKED` the string reached 34 glyphs (897.6px) against an 895px slot at the median cap and 38 glyphs (1,003.2px) at the measured maximum. §10.6a has ratified `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED` — 28 glyphs = 739.2px at the median cap, 32 glyphs = 844.8px at the measured maximum of 4,500,000, both inside the slot, with the worst case bounded at 23 fixed glyphs plus §3.5 T4's 9-glyph cap. The rule therefore has no reachable failure state on that row, and it keeps its build-refusal posture unaltered.

**One §5-side consequence of §10.2's field list.** The ticket price moves from a chip on the photo well into the band's first line, and the price chip is deleted from §5.7 outright. The reason is structural, not editorial: the count slide (§5.7) carries no photograph, so it has no photo well to host a chip. Putting the price in the band removes it from every slide rather than creating a per-slide branch. The field has no null case — VERIFIED, `ticket_price` is positive on **880 of 880** live enterable draws, minimum stored price £0.01. It does push the band's L1 to roughly 49 characters at its worst case; the move from a 940px to a 950px track gives it 10px more, and §5.3's measured-fit rule will still catch an overflow as a **build failure on a legitimate draw**. It must be measured against the 950px track before G1 is locked.

**Why the free-entry line is hedged** — the evidence, which §10.2 consumes. PDD does **not** store whether each operator offers a free-entry route. VERIFIED against the live schema: `draws` has 20 columns (`id, slug, operator_id, category_id, title, prize_description, image_url, ticket_price, prize_value, draw_date, entry_url, affiliate_url, status, featured, created_at, updated_at, total_prize_value, grand_prize, total_entries, category_source`) and `operators` has 24; neither has a free-entry field. Asserting "FREE POSTAL ENTRY AVAILABLE" across the board would be an unevidenced objective claim under CAP 3.7. The same argument applies to the bare `18+` and to `UK ONLY`: both are claims about someone else's terms that PDD verifies nothing about. §10.2 owns the resulting wording; §5.3's own `18+ · UK ONLY · …` strings are deleted.

**Not gambling furniture.** VERIFIED (CAP): prize competitions and free draws sit outside Gambling Act 2005 licensing, so the operative code is CAP Section 8, not 16 or 17. No BeGambleAware strip, no gambling warning bar.

**Hierarchy is a compliance surface.** CAP guidance, verbatim: "Promoters should ensure that the page design, layout or format of the promotion is not misleading. Promoters should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true." VERIFIED: the current template sets `.closes` (odds + date) at 33px (`styles.css:358`) against `.prize` at 98px (`styles.css:346`) — the one datum no operator publishes, at a third the size of the datum every competitor also shows. §5.7 inverts that, and the inversion is a compliance fix as much as a design one.

### 5.4 Slide 1 — the cover

Ground: newsprint `--ground`, plus §8's scene ground clipped to the region §5 supplies below. No photograph. No thumbnail strip. No confetti, no embers, no glow, no techgrid, no scrim, no blurred backdrop. VERIFIED: `introHtml()` currently stacks eight text blocks over four decorative layers at `render.mjs:144–147` (`.backdrop`, `.glow` + `bgFx(true, …)`, `.techgrid`, `.scrim`) plus `confettiHtml(24)` on the same line. (§1.5 A7 is the inventory the other sections should cite rather than counting the stack a fourth way; `bgFx()` itself emits `.bloom` and `.rays`, which is where the higher counts come from.)

Content well **x 65 → 960** (895px). Margin to the grid-crop line: **31.25px left** (65 − 33.75), **86.25px right** (1046.25 − 960).

**Role and CAP 8.17 field 5.** The cover emits `data-pdd-role="cover"` (§10.2's enum) and carries **no `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node**, so §10.2's G1-P prize-name assertion does not run on it and its absence is not a violation of any class. The cover discharges field 5 in its own right and at zero cost: the board's Prize column names the nature of three prizes plus the `+{N−3} more inside` row, and the proof line and band L1 carry the number. That is why scoping the assertion is safe on the one slide most often seen alone.

**Scene mount.** The slide carries §8's `#scene-back` only, clipped to the region left by four rects, which §5 supplies through the surface descriptor the same way `band` already is. §8 computes the area; the arithmetic is shown here only so the rects can be checked.

| Rect | Extent | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Masthead | x 0–1080, y 0–132 | 142,560 |
| Conditions band | x 0–1080, y 1182–1350 | 181,440 |
| Sheet edge | **x 1015–1080**, y 180–1182 | 65 × 1002 = **65,130** |
| Board | x 0–1080, y 872–1182 | 1080 × 310 = **334,800** |

The board rect runs from 10px above the board's top edge (§8.3's clearance, 882 − 10 = 872) down to the conditions band at y 1182, rather than stopping 10px below the board at y 1172: closing the 20px gap costs nothing and avoids painting a 20px sliver of scene between two exclusion rects. Height is 310px either way, which is the figure §8 is holding.

Netting the sheet edge's overlap with the board rect (65 × 310 = 20,150): 324,000 + 65,130 + 334,800 − 20,150 = 703,780, leaving **754,220 px² = 51.73%** of the 1,458,000 px² canvas. (The published 743,840 / 51.02% was computed at an 80px sheet-edge rect; only the horizontal term moved.)

**Layout model — the fix for mockup weakness (a), the cover dead band.**

The mockup (`~/Desktop/pdd-directions/D-merged-01-cover.png`) has a large empty region between the odds sub-line and the thumbnail strip. The cause is structural: the cover is a vertically centred flex column of fixed-height items, so leftover space pools **between** blocks. Decoration will not fix a pooling problem.

The fix is to change the layout model. **The cover is bottom-anchored.** The board is pinned so its last row sits 20px above the conditions band; the proof line sits a fixed 34px above the board; the headline block grows *upward* from the proof line; the dateline is pinned to the top of the well. Every inter-block gap is a constant, so all slack accumulates in exactly one place — **between the dateline and the first headline line** — where it reads as the air above a broadsheet headline rather than a hole in a poster.

| Block | Height | Type (steps are §3.5's) |
|---|---|---|
| Dateline (pinned top, y 152) | 45 | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-micro` |
| *slack* | variable | — |
| Headline (§5.5) | 150, 300 or 450 (1–3 × 150) | Bricolage Grotesque 800, `--fs-hero` |
| gap | 34 | |
| Proof line | 2 × 60 = 120 | Inter 600 `--fs-body`; figures JetBrains Mono 700 |
| gap | 34 | |
| Board | 4 × 70 = 280 | below |
| gap to band | 20 | |

Slack arithmetic, so the risk is quantified rather than asserted. The well runs y 132 → 1182. Board top y 882 (882 + 280 + 20 = 1182 ✓). Proof line top y 728 (728 + 120 + 34 = 882 ✓). Headline block ends y 694 (694 + 34 = 728 ✓). Dateline occupies y 152 → 197.

| Headline lines | Block height | Starts at | Slack below the dateline |
|---|---|---|---|
| One | 150 | y 544 | 347px |
| Two | 300 | y 394 | 197px |
| **Three** | **450** | **y 244** | **47px** |
| Four | 600 | y 94 | **−103px — collides with the dateline, 38px above the top of the well** |

That last row is why §5.5's fit rule is a hard build gate. The three-line row is also the `question` arm's permanent home: §10.6a's single permitted question form `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?` greedy-wraps to exactly three line boxes on every candidate track, so on roughly 91 days a year the cover runs at its tightest legal vertical, 47px below the dateline.

Dateline: the day's date plus the checked stamp, i.e. where Slot B goes on slide 1. It is unoccupied territory #7 (dated, accountable editorial) used as a design element rather than a footnote. String per §10.6a 1.2 and §10.4 — `THU 18 SEP 2026 · READ 09:00`, 571.2px in an 895px well.

**Proof line.** Generated, never authored: the deck count, the real closing window and the deck's lowest ticket cap. Its exact wording is **§10.6a's**, because it is the only bounded comparative permitted anywhere in the system and its legal defence is that the reader can check it against the slides that follow. Three §5-side rules follow from that:

- The count word is generated from `drawsRendered` (§5.11), never from the config value and never from a literal. On a degraded seven-draw day a cover reading "of the eight" is a false checkable claim — a CAP 3.7 failure on the one line whose evidence is the post itself.
- The window is generated from the actual maximum `draw_date` in the selection.
- The line is measured against **2 × 895px** and fails the build if it needs a third line.

The proof line is also the evidence unit for §10.6 mechanic predicate 3: on a `question` day the predicate measures `normalizeWhitespace(headline + " " + proofLine)`, not the headline alone, which is why the headline may carry one figure and the proof line supplies the rest.

Its figures are the only place on the cover set in `--verdict`, and that is authorised by §10.6a, not by §5.

**The board — the replacement for the thumbnail strip.** A fixed **280px** block of four 70px rows, 1px `--hairline` above each, text vertically centred. Fixed at every deck size, so the slack arithmetic above is deck-size-independent and must not be re-derived.

| Column | x | Width | Type | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Index | 65 | (54px to the Prize column) | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-micro` | `--ink-meta` |
| Prize | 119 → 648 | 529 | Inter 600, `--fs-label`, truncated at a word boundary to fit one measured line | `--ink` |
| Closes | 668 → 960, right-aligned | 292 | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-micro` | `--ink`, or `--deadline` when ≤48h |

The three columns close on the well exactly: 54 + 529 + 20 + 292 = **895**. The 35px lost against the retired 930px well is taken **entirely from the Prize column** (564 → 529, −6.2%), because it is the only one that already truncates to a measured line and therefore degrades gracefully. The fixed-width figure columns cannot absorb it: `SUN 21 SEP 26` is 13 glyphs × (34 × 0.600 = 20.4) = **265.2px** and needs its 292px, and `01`–`08` is 2 × 20.4 = **40.8px** inside 54px.

Row rule, stated as a total over N ∈ [4, 8] (§5.11): at **N ≥ 5**, rows 1–3 carry draws and row 4 reads `+{N−3} more inside` in the prize column with the other columns empty; at **N = 4**, all four rows carry draws and there is no overflow line. At N = 3 row 4 would be a 70px hole in a layout whose whole premise is that slack pools in one place — which is one of the two geometries that force §5.11's floor.

**Why the thumbnail strip is deleted (mockup weakness (c)).** The strip mixed clean product shots with loud operator marketing collages — a darts collage and a gold iPhone tile in the rendered mockup. Three reasons to remove rather than repair:

- It is the single point where un-normalised operator artwork enters the most important slide in the deck. Asset normalisation at ingest is the right fix and it is §9's; deleting the strip removes the exposure in the meantime.
- It is too small to read at any deck size. VERIFIED geometry: the strip is laid inside `.intro-wrap`'s 972px inner width (`styles.css:389`, 54px side padding) with 14px gaps (`styles.css:398`), so five tiles are **183px** each and six are **150px** — §9.10's own two measurements, reproduced. DAILY.md:69–70 records slide 1 rendering at roughly 161 × 201px in the profile grid, a linear scale of about 0.15, at which a 183px tile is **~28px**. Nothing is readable at 28px, and at roughly a third of nominal canvas size in-feed it is ~60px of operator collage.
- At §5.11's eight draws it is arithmetically hopeless: `(972 − 7×14)/8 = 109.25` CSS px per tile, **~17px** in the profile grid. The deck-size decision and the strip deletion are the same decision.
- The board carries the same "there are N things inside" signal in type, and does it better, because it also carries what those things *are* and when they close — unoccupied territory #2 (the scoreboard, not the poster) and #5 (typography as the only ornament) doing real work.

§9.10 sizes the strip's future at five and six draws; it must be rewritten as the retrospective justification for this deletion rather than as live geometry.

**The one ≥150px grid-survivable element** is the headline, spanning **x 65 → 960**. Both edges are inside the grid-safe range with 31.25px and 86.25px to spare, so it survives the 3:4 crop intact. Per §3.5 T2 it is the cover's single `--fs-hero` node and **no draw slide carries one**, because no inner slide is ever cropped.

### 5.5 The cover headline system

**VERIFIED current behaviour.** `render.mjs:150` renders `d.hook`. `build.mjs:140` sets that to `sel.hook || hookLabel(sel.slug, sel.name)`. `format.mjs:72`'s `hookLabel()` returns `catCfg(slug).hook || \`WIN ${catLabel(name)}\``, and `catCfg` resolves to one of six string constants in `config.json` (lines 20, 26, 32, 38, 44, 50): `WIN A DREAM CAR`, `WIN TAX-FREE CASH`, `WIN A DREAM HOME`, `WIN THE LATEST TECH`, `WIN LUXURY`, `WIN RARE FINDS`. For any slug not in `config.json`, `config.mjs:15` supplies a **seventh**, `WIN BIG`. Seven headlines, cycled forever, as the largest element on the slide.

Meanwhile a rotating experiment arm already exists and is already logged: `plan.mjs:71` computes `archetype = GLOBAL.archetypes[dayOfYear % GLOBAL.archetypes.length]` from `config.json:14` (`question / price-anchor / deadline / absurd-comparison`), writes it to `selection.json` at `plan.mjs:74`, `brief.mjs:20` feeds it to caption authoring, and `publish.mjs:181` writes it to `carousel_posts.hook_archetype` (column confirmed at `state-schema.sql:8`). **The rig exists, is wired to the caption, is logged — and the cover ignores it.**

**Decision: delete the six `hook` constants from `config.json`, the `hook` key from `config.mjs:15`'s fallback, and `hookLabel()` from `format.mjs:72`. The cover headline becomes a function of (today's archetype, today's verified selection facts).** The physical removal from `config.json` is performed by §8.7, in the same commit as the `theme` / `particles` deletion. Four generators:

| Archetype | Source facts | Constraint carried |
|---|---|---|
| `question` | `drawsRendered` alone | **One permitted form**, `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`, logged `question:only`. Carries `drawsRendered` in the string; the proof line 34px below supplies the remaining evidence and is what discharges §10.6 predicate 3. Rhetorical and self-answering on the same slide; never asks for a comment, reply, tag or share. Always renders three line boxes. |
| `price-anchor` | `min(ticket_price)`, `drawsRendered` | Figure from `priceLabel()` (`format.mjs:5`). |
| `deadline` | earliest `draw_date` | Date or weekday only, never a clock. |
| `absurd-comparison` | operator's own stated cash alternative vs ticket price | Operator-stated cash only, never odds and never an external event. **Conditional — see below.** |

The deck's lowest cap has moved off the `question` headline and onto the proof line, where §10.6a 1.2 already puts it. Both retired forms are banned by name in §10.6a 1.3: `HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?` breaks to four line boxes on every candidate track and is unrenderable under the gate below, and `HOW MANY TICKETS?` is a hero-size question carrying no verified figure on the frame itself.

**Each generator's strings are §10.6a's**, emitted by `oddsCopy.headline(archetype, form, facts)`. §5 authors no headline string. This closes two live breaches in the earlier draft: `SHORTEST ODDS TODAY?` uses a superlative banned by name, and "today" claims a superlative over an inventory PDD has never enumerated — `pickBestCategory` picks one category, `select.mjs:20` truncates at 300 rows of the 483 in the window, out of 880 enterable draws, out of a UK universe PDD has not counted. The only scope PDD holds documentary evidence for before publication is the post itself.

**The fit rule (this replaces the earlier draft's character budget).** Bricolage Grotesque 800 at `--fs-hero` on the **895px track**. At render the headline is laid out and measured. It must occupy **1, 2 or 3 line boxes, none of which overflows 895px**. If the long form fails the measurement the short form is used; if the short form also fails, the **build fails loudly** rather than shrinking below `--fs-hero`, because the grid-survivable anchor is a hard requirement of the cover.

Informational capacity, so the constraint below is legible. At §3.4's measured Bricolage 800 advance of 0.6740em a glyph at 150px is **101.1px**, so the 895px track holds 895 ÷ 101.1 = **8.85 characters per line** and about **26.5 over the three-line ceiling**. (The retired 930px track held ~9.6 and ~29.)

**The word constraint handed to §10.6a: no word in any headline form may exceed EIGHT glyphs at `--fs-hero`.** 8 × 101.1 = **808.8px ≤ 895**, with 86px of margin; 9 × 101.1 = **909.9px > 895**. The earlier "no single word exceeds ten glyphs" was already wrong on the 930px track (10 glyphs = 1,011px) and the narrower well only exposes it. Eight is chosen rather than nine because nine squeaks past by 7.6px at the older 0.6573em advance and fails outright at §3.4's measured 0.6740em; eight holds under both. GATE CHECK against §10.6a's current table: the longest words in circulation are `TICKETS` (7), `TICKET.` (7), `SUNDAY.` (7), `£52,000` (7) and, in the short forms, `TICKETS?` (8). The cap rejects nothing that exists, so it cannot fire on an ordinary run. **The binding gate remains the render-time line-box measurement against 895px; the glyph cap only constrains what §10.6a may author.**

This matters more than it sounds. The earlier draft budgeted its examples at "≤30 characters, three lines". Under greedy word wrapping at any plausible advance, `WHOSE ODDS ARE SHORTEST TODAY?`, `6 UK DRAWS. CHEAPEST 79p.` and `THREE CLOSE BEFORE SUNDAY.` each break to **four** lines — because wrapping is governed by the longest *word*, not the character count.

**Why `question` is constrained.** Two of PDD's own past captions are exposed under Meta's engagement-bait policy: "Which would you pick?" (comment solicitation) and "#1 is unreal" (sensationalist withholding). OFFICIAL: engagement bait is demoted at **account** level for repeat offenders, and a daily automated poster is exactly that profile. A question headline is permitted only where the slide answers it — which is now machine-checked rather than asserted, because §10.6 predicate 3 measures the headline together with the proof line.

**Why `deadline` is date-only.** CAP 8.22: "Promoters must not claim that consumers must respond by a specified date or within a specified time if they need not." DMCC Act 2024 (in force 6 Apr 2025) bans false urgency including fake countdown timers. PDD stores `draw_date` but cannot currently evidence immovability, so: **a date or weekday, never a clock.** This also sidesteps the most saturated UI element in the UK category. §10.6a's `deadline` form `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUNDAY.` is untouched by predicate 3: it carries no `?` and no digit, and word-numbers never count as figures.

**Why `absurd-comparison` is conditional.** VERIFIED against the live DB: `draws.prize_value` is populated on **0 of 880** live enterable draws. `total_prize_value` is populated on 880 of 880 — and equals `total_entries × ticket_price` to within 1% on **880 of 880**, confirming `honesty.mjs:2`'s own comment that it is gross ticket revenue, not prize worth. **PDD stores no prize-value figure anywhere.** A headline built from `capValue()` would present ticket revenue as the worth of the prize: factually wrong, and an unevidenced objective claim under CAP 3.7.

The only prize-side money figure PDD can evidence is the operator's **own stated cash alternative**, parsed by `cashAlt()` (`format.mjs:31–39`) out of `grand_prize` / `prize_description`. MEASURED: it parses on **152 of 880 (17.3%)** live enterable draws and **98 of 483 (20.3%)** inside the 1–7 day window.

So: **`absurd-comparison` runs only where the day's selection contains at least one draw with a parseable cash alternative.** Otherwise it falls back to `price-anchor`, and the fallback is logged as `absurd-comparison→price-anchor` so the experiment log does not mis-attribute the day. `capValue()`'s existing cap survives unchanged.

**What this experiment can and cannot tell you.** The rotation is `dayOfYear % 4`; 4 and 7 are coprime, so over 28 days each arm lands on each weekday exactly once — a genuine merit of the existing rig. (`plan.mjs:70` derives `dayOfYear` from `Date.now()` against a UTC-parsed 1 January, so the sequence repeats one arm across the year boundary and drifts a few hours at the day edge. Immaterial to the design; worth knowing before anyone reads the log as a clean Latin square.)

But the only reachable outcome is the parent album's metrics. VERIFIED: `insights.mjs` `mapPayload()` ingests likes and comments (`ig_media`), account-level reach (`ig_reach`, keyed `media_id: "account"`) and `fb_reactions`/`fb_comments`/`fb_shares` (`fb_posts`) — **no saves, no Instagram shares, no per-media reach**. OFFICIAL: Trial Reels needs 200 followers; @prizedrawsdaily is at ~66. Wire it because it costs nothing and the alternative is seven frozen strings — not because it will answer the question soon. `carousel_posts.hook_archetype` logs the **template id** (now `question:only` for the question arm), not the rendered string, so the log survives a permitted-wording change.

### 5.6 Slide 2 — the count slide

Slide 2 is re-served cold (OFFICIAL, Mosseri, Oct 2024), so it must stand alone. It is also **the one slide in the deck that carries the full odds band**, and it carries no photograph.

**Why the band lands here and nowhere else.** The arithmetic is §4.4's and is not re-derived; the consequence for §5 is simple and worth stating plainly. A draw slide's content well is 1050px, and with the operator lockup, a two-line prize name, the gaps and the odds module's own chrome, the photograph and the band are drawing on the same residual. At the band's ceiling there is no photograph left. **On 1080×1350 you can have the photograph or the band, not both.** Slide 2 is where the band goes, because §5.6's own Delta 2 already routes the shortest-cap draw here, because §5.4's cover already carries no photograph so a photoless slide is inside the template's register, and because giving the band the slide Instagram re-serves cold is the best available use of the single strongest "adds material value" artefact in the system.

**What it must carry to stand alone**, and where each comes from:

| Requirement | Carried by |
|---|---|
| Brand mark | Masthead Slot A |
| Recency / accountability | Masthead Slot B |
| The premise (this is one of several) | Counter chip row, §5.9 |
| Enough to act on | Prize name, the odds band, the operator lockup |
| Legal sufficiency | Conditions band (§10.2) |
| A reason to swipe | Sheet edge (§5.9) |

**Delta 1 is deleted.** The earlier draft repeated the cover headline here as a 48px kicker. It is repeated cover copy competing with the slide's own hero figure, and §3.5 T2 permits at most one `--fs-hero` anchor per frame. The count slide's angle is the count. ⚠️ The cost is real: the cold-entry case is weaker by one element. Slide 2 still carries brand, recency, premise and a fact, but it no longer states the day's angle.

**Delta 2 — slide 2 is not "the one closing soonest".** VERIFIED: `select.mjs:19` orders by `draw_date.asc` and `build.mjs:108` maps `sel.draws` in that order, so slide 2 is currently whichever draw closes first. Spec: **slide 2 carries the draw with the lowest `total_entries` in the selection**, ties broken by earliest close. This was a nice-to-have in the earlier draft and is now load-bearing, because it is what gives the band's one appearance the best chance of being a full sheet rather than a clipped one.

**Delta 3 moves to slide 3.** The image-quality gate — if a draw's photograph is a marketing collage it is swapped for a backup rather than shipped — applied to slide 2 in the earlier draft. Slide 2 now has no photograph, so the gate applies to the first slide that does. The mechanism already exists: VERIFIED, `plan.mjs:69` writes backups into `selection.json` and `build.mjs` never reads them.

**Residual ordering.** Slides 3 … N+1 carry the remaining draws in ascending `draw_date`, with the count-slide draw removed. §7.7's Facebook subset selects by slide index against this order, not by re-sorting on close date.

**How often the band is a full sheet.** §4.7's ceiling has now landed at **1,440 tickets (24 rows)**, so the table below is at the binding threshold rather than at a candidate one. MEASURED against the live DB on 17 Sep 2026, 1–7 day window (483 draws), counting caps ≤1,440:

| Category | window draws | cap ≤1,440 |
|---|---|---|
| collectibles | 51 | 26 (51%) |
| home-garden | 27 | 14 (52%) |
| luxury | 30 | 14 (47%) |
| tech-giveaways | 90 | 33 (37%) |
| cash-prizes | 184 | 27 (15%) |
| sports-outdoors | 55 | 4 (7%) |
| car-draws | 45 | 3 (7%) |

⚠️ Stored caps cluster hard on round numbers (99 / 199 / 299 / 499 / 599 / 699 / 999 / 1,199 / 1,499), so the share falls in steps, not smoothly. If §4.7's ceiling ever moves, this table must be re-queried rather than scaled.

What the table shows: taking the minimum of eight draws makes a full sheet near-certain in collectibles, home-garden and luxury, likely in tech-giveaways, and close to hopeless in car-draws and sports-outdoors. It is a material improvement, not a guarantee, and it is category-dependent in a way the earlier draft understated. On a car-draws day the one band in the deck is a clipped sheet and the green marker does not appear at all.

### 5.7 Draw slides

Ground: newsprint `--ground`, plus §8's scene ground clipped to the rects below. Content well **y 132 → 1182 (1050px)**, between the two chrome bands. Content column **x 65 → 960 (895px)**, sized to §4.4's band.

**Every block height, every gap, the band ceiling, the two count-slide state totals and E2's height are §4.4's.** §5.7 publishes none of them. What survives here is slide assembly, row contents, the fitting rules, and the rects handed to §8. The renderer asserts the rendered column sums to ≤ 1050px and, on slides 3+, that the photo well is ≥ 500px, failing the build otherwise in the style of `render.mjs:193`'s existing refusal. There are two layouts.

**Layout 1 — the count slide (slide 2 only).** No photograph. Emits `data-pdd-role="count"`. Blocks in order, with no numbers: counter chip row → operator lockup (§5.13) → prize name → eyebrow, with the annotation row beneath the band in the clipped state only → hero figure → odds band → legend. Every height, every gap, the band ceiling and the two state totals are §4.4's; the column is bottom-anchored on §4.4's rule and residual space pools as newsprint air above the chip row.

Row contents and their sources: the chip reads `drawsRendered` (§5.11) and counts draws, not slides; the lockup is §5.13's; the prize-name string is §5.12's after `cleanTitle()`; every odds string — eyebrow, annotation, legend — is §10.6a's; the band's geometry, rows, height, ceiling and clipped/full state are §4.4's and §4.7's.

**Layout 2 — draw slides 3 and after.** Emits `data-pdd-role="draw"`. The photo well is the flexible element; every other block is fixed by content.

| Block | Notes |
|---|---|
| Photo well, **x 0 → 1015** (1015px, bounded by §5.9's sheet-edge hairline) | Flex residual, **minimum 500px**. Photograph only. No card frame, no glow, no podium, no "WIN THIS" ribbon. |
| Operator lockup (§5.13) | |
| Prize name | Bricolage 800, size-stepped, **2 measured lines maximum** |
| Odds numeral lockup (E2) | Height per §4.4. Strings per §10.6a. |

**The photo well is the flex residual and its value at each prize-name step is §4.4's: 565px at a two-line title, 585px at two lines of `--fs-lead`, 615px at a one-line `--fs-display`.** §5.7 keeps 500px as its own floor, and the binding worst case now clears it by 65px rather than meeting it exactly. At 565px the photograph is **41.9%** of the canvas (565 / 1350) and **53.8%** of the content well (565 / 1050) — it is the largest single element, and I am not going to claim it dominates.

E2 is the numeral lockup: the bare cap at `--fs-figure` under its eyebrow, with a single-line qualifier beneath. Its relationship to the band — that above the ceiling the figure's digit count *is* the comparison — is §4.7's argument, not restated here.

**Scene mount.** §8's `#scene-back` only, clipped out of five rects, which §5 supplies and §8 prices. Stated parametrically, because two of them move with a height §5 does not own:

| Rect | Extent |
|---|---|
| Masthead | x 0–1080, y 0–132 |
| Conditions band | x 0–1080, y 1182–1350 |
| Sheet edge | **x 1015–1080**, y 180–1182 |
| Photo well | **x 0 → 1015** by its rendered height (§4.4) |
| Odds module | x 0–1080, from 10px above the module's top edge down to the conditions band |

The five rects above are what §5.7 publishes. The check below is worked **entirely from §4.4's heights** — the photo wells, E2's stack and the count column's bottom anchor are all §4.4's, §5.7 authors none of them, and the areas are §8's to compute.

Sheet edge = 65 × 1002 = 65,130. At §4.4's E2 the module's top edge falls 240px above the bottom of the well, at y 942, so the odds rect is y 932 → 1182 = 250px: 1080 × 250 = 270,000, less its 65 × 250 = 16,250 overlap with the sheet edge.

- **Two-line prize name, §4.4's photo well 565px:** 324,000 + (1015 × 565 = 573,475) + 65,130 + 270,000 − 16,250 = 1,216,355, leaving **241,645 px² = 16.57%**.
- **One-line prize name, §4.4's photo well 615px:** 324,000 + (1015 × 615 = 624,225) + 65,130 + 270,000 − 16,250 = 1,267,105, leaving **190,895 px² = 13.09%**.

Both reproduce §8's published figures exactly, because the photo well's growth (65 × 1015 = 65,975) and the odds rect's shrinkage (65 × 1080 = 70,200, less the 65 × 65 = 4,225 overlap) cancel to the pixel. That cancellation is a coincidence of §4.4's E2 landing 65px below the retired 305px module, and it will not survive the next change to either — which is why the rects above are parametric and §8 does the arithmetic.

On the **count slide** the odds-module rect has no fixed top edge, because §4.4's column is bottom-anchored: at the 24-row ceiling the module's top edge is y 447 and the rect is 745px tall; at the measured minimum cap of 99 it is y 777 and the rect is 415px. §8's published 750px figure was computed against the retired column and re-derives to 745px at the ceiling, which moves that region from 307,620 px² (21.10%) to **312,695 px² (21.45%)**. The four subtractions are unchanged.

All of the surviving region sits behind the operator lockup and the prize name. The odds rect is scene-excluded so the dot field always sits on bare paper, which is what guarantees its contrast rather than a mean-ink budget doing it.

**The prize name is capped at two lines.** The earlier draft allowed three lines at 54/55, which combined with the odds module's real height would have broken the photo well's own minimum. Two lines is the fix.

**Prize name fitting, and the CAP 8.17 field-5 node.** The prize-name element carries `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"` on both layouts. Bricolage Grotesque 800 on the **895px track**, stepping down §3.5's ladder and taking the first size that fits within two measured line boxes. **The floor is §3.5's `--fs-lead` (56px)**; below it the title is truncated at a word boundary with a trailing `…` and re-measured at that step. The node is never rendered below `--fs-lead`, which is what makes §10.2's G1-P assertion (c) true on every ordinary run.

MEASURED (880 live titles, after the current `cleanTitle()`): p25 = 18, median = 26, p75 = 39, p90 = 53, p95 = 63, max = 152 characters; 28.2% are ≤19 chars, 88.3% ≤50, 94.4% ≤62, 99.2% ≤93. At Bricolage 800's 0.6573em advance, 56px gives 36.81px per glyph, so the 895px track holds **24 glyphs per line and 48 over two** — the truncator therefore fires on somewhat more than the 11.7% of titles that exceed 50 characters. The exact share at 48 glyphs was not queried, and at §3.4's competing 0.6740em advance the capacity falls to 23 and 46. This is the observed distribution, not the fitting rule.

⚠️ At the **top** of the ladder the problem is worse: at `--fs-display` 88px a glyph is 57.84px, so the 895px line fits **15.47 ≈ 15.5 characters**. (That ~15.5 figure was always an 895-derived number; earlier drafts mislabelled it a 930px line, where it would have been 16.08.) The top step is nearly dead against a median title of 26 characters, and §3.5 should know it.

This replaces the current binary at `render.mjs:73` (`length > 26` → `.prize` 98px drops to `.prize.long` 72px). MEASURED across two runs minutes apart, that branch fires on **437–440 of 880 (49.7–50.0%)** of live titles — a "long title" branch that splits inventory in half is not a branch, it is a mis-set default.

**The price chip is deleted.** The price is a conditions-band field (§5.3, §10.2). The count slide has no photo well to overlay, and a per-slide branch for one chip is not worth the divergence.

**The closes chip survives as a photo overlay on slides 3+.** Bottom-left of the photo well, **x 65**, `--rail-ink` on `--deadline`. It follows the Wowcher "Wow Week" pattern — a badge on inner slides only — and it costs zero vertical budget. **It renders only when the stored `draw_date` is within 48 hours.** Outside 48 hours the date lives in the conditions band alone. That is CAP 8.22 and the DMCC Act expressed as a layout rule: urgency is shown only where it is real. MEASURED: 233 of 880 live draws (26.5%) are inside 48h at any moment, but `plan.mjs:13`'s `MIN_DAYS=1` floor means selected draws are always ≥24h out, so the chip fires only on the 24–48h band of a selection. It is a design element, not a compliance carrier — the band carries the condition.

**What §9 needs from this section.** §9.3 derives its normalised master from `.card` and from the deleted cover strip, and must be re-derived against what actually ships. The carousel's requirement is one rect, and it is the **widest, tallest** case the photo well reaches:

- Width is **1015px CSS** on every draw slide, because the well is bounded by the sheet-edge hairline at x 1015, not by the text column at x 960.
- Height is §4.4's, and the binding case is the one-line prize name: **1015 × 615 (1.650:1)**, which also satisfies the two-line worst case at 1015 × 565 (1.796:1). At `deviceScaleFactor: 2` that is **2030 × 1230 device px**.
- ⚠️ The pair published elsewhere as "1015 × 500 minimum (2.03:1), 1015 × 550 (1.845:1)" carries §5.7's retired 500px minimum forward and is 65px short of the well §4.4 actually renders. The horizontal correction (1000 → 1015) is right; the heights re-derive.

The count slide requires no photograph at all. On the no-border rule: §5.7 forbids *decorative* framing — card frames, glows, podiums, ribbons. §9.5's 2px separation hairline on a Class B asset is a legibility device and is permitted, but it must clear 3:1 against paper; at `--hairline`'s 1.37:1 it does not perform the separation §9.5 wants, so it is set in §3.7's `--rule` (3.33:1).

### 5.8 The odds module — the signature device

Unoccupied territory #6: odds exist as a data field at CompWatch, Competition Showroom and PDD, but nobody has made them **visual** — no bar, no dot grid, nothing you can feel. An operator structurally cannot copy this, because their job is to make the odds feel small.

**This section specifies no geometry and no encoding.** It was one of four sections that specified the device from scratch and got four different answers. The owners are:

| | Owner |
|---|---|
| Columns, dot diameter, gap, pitch, band width, band origin, `R = ceil(cap/60)`, band height, **the count-slide vertical budget and E2's height** | **§4.4** |
| The ceiling, the above-ceiling encoding, the green-marker rule | **§4.7** |
| The marked dot's own treatment (datum cross, no ring, no enlargement) | **§4.6** |
| Unmarked-dot colour | **§4.5** |
| Every rendered string | **§10.6a** |
| Slide assembly and row contents | §5.7 |

**Deleted from this section and not replaced anywhere:** the 74-column / 8px dot / 4.05px gutter / 888px table and its 1,332 capacity; the 213px grid and the 301/303px module reconciliation; Encoding B's `888 × 24px` rail, its `max(2px, 888 / cap)` green segment and its clamp-disclosure line; the labels `YOUR ODDS AT THE CAP`, `699 TICKETS MAX · YOUR ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT` and `one dot = one ticket · one of them wins`; and the sentence "the winner dot is **not** ringed, highlighted or enlarged", which contradicted §4.6's datum cross and §4.9's alt text outright. §4.6 owns the marker's treatment.

Three arithmetic reasons for the geometry and encoding deletions, recorded so nobody re-derives them:

- **The 74-column geometry was fractionally pitched.** (888 − 74×8) / 73 = 296/73 = **4.0548px**, which is 8.11 device px at `deviceScaleFactor: 2`. No dot after the first in any row lands on a whole device pixel. That is the antialiasing defect §4.4's integer pitch exists to prevent.
- **Its own module arithmetic did not close.** 45 + 213 + 45 = 303, stated as 301; and 17 rows at a 12.05px pitch is 17 × 12.05 − 4.05 = **200.8px**, not the 211px the 301px figure was reconciled against.
- **The rail was the encoding §4.7 had already evaluated and rejected**, and the clamp made it worse rather than better. At a 2px floor on an 888px rail the crossover is cap 444, so every cap above 444 renders the identical mark. Live caps run to 4,500,000. A 34px line admitting the graphic is wrong does not discharge CAP's page-design rule; it is a constant masquerading as a measurement. §4.7 owns the replacement.

**Source field is `total_entries`, the ticket cap.** MEASURED: **880 of 880** live enterable draws carry a positive value, so the module has no null case. Maximum stored cap is **4,500,000**.

**The figure is the cap, not the live odds, and the copy must say so.** CAP 3.7 requires documentary evidence for objective claims before publication, and a bare "1 IN 699" is a claim about actual odds when what is stored is a maximum ticket count. Cap-based odds *understate* the chance, which is the safe direction under CAP 8.20/8.21, but the device must still be labelled honestly. The permitted wording is §10.6a's; the second-person framings this section previously shipped are banned by name there, and they were also false on their face — a ticket cap is not any viewer's odds, and for a viewer holding no tickets the quantity is undefined.

**The dot field sits on bare paper by construction.** §5.7 clips §8's scene out of the odds-module rect, so the field always renders against `--ground` and its contrast is §3.7's measured 3.33:1 rather than something a scene's mean-ink budget has to protect.

**Alt text.** `honesty.mjs`'s `altTexts()` (`honesty.mjs:31–37`, written to `out/alt.json` at `build.mjs:161`) gains a per-draw odds sentence. Its exact form is §4.9's, and §4.9 is now the **sole** normative home of the clipped state's not-shown count — the on-slide annotation carries shown-of-cap and the absence of the mark, and the alt text carries the subtraction. This is not optional garnish: at any of the greys in play the marked dot sits at about **1.8:1** against its neighbours, so it is separated from the field mainly by hue, and the graphic cannot be the sole carrier of the fact. (That ratio holds at both candidate hexes — it is a property of `--verdict` against a 3.33:1 grey, not of §4.5's choice between them.)

**The hierarchy inversion, which is this section's actual claim.** The odds figure is larger than the prize name on every draw slide. That inverts the shipped 33px-vs-98px relationship (`styles.css:358` vs `:346`) and it is what makes the deck eligible under the Recommendation Guidelines' "adds material value" test. It is also the compliance-correct ordering under CAP's emphasis guidance.

⚠️ **Two caveats, both load-bearing.**

First, **nothing at any geometry has ever been rendered**, and that now covers every x-coordinate in the deck as well as the device. The digest records the dot grid as "rendered and proven at 1 in 699 (60-column CSS grid)"; the artefact is `merged.mjs`'s fractional-cell mockup. The 895px well, the x 65 band origin, the 65px on-frame sheet strip, the 31.25px crop headroom, the 55px right margin and §4.4's band have none of them been rendered. They must be eyeballed at profile-grid thumbnail size and at in-feed size before any threshold is locked.

Second, **coverage was overstated twice.** The earlier draft cited 222/880 = 25.2% — that is the count at cap ≤1,500, not at the capacity it had specified. MEASURED at the live DB, and now at §4.7's ratified 1,440 ceiling: cap ≤1,440 is **212/880 = 24.1%**; adding the title-fit condition brings it to **201/880 = 22.8%** overall and **116/483 = 24.0%** in the 1–7 day window. Roughly **one draw in four, not one in five**.

---

### 5.9 The swipe affordance

**Delete `SWIPE TO SEE ALL N →`** (VERIFIED at `render.mjs:155`) and its `.intro-swipe` gradient pill (`styles.css:408`). Two reasons: MEASURED (NN/g) arrows signify *tapping*, not swiping, and are ignored; and OFFICIAL, Instagram already draws its own multi-image icon and pagination dots, so the pill is a third redundant cue occupying 40px of type where the eye should be reading facts.

Replace with two devices.

**1. The numbered counter.** A paper chip, **JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-label` (44/50)**, `--ink` on `--ground`, 1px `--rule` border, 8px radius, 10px padding top and bottom and 20px each side. **Its row height is §4.4's** — a 50px line box plus 10px of padding each side. It does not use `--fs-micro`: §3.5 T3 reserves 34px for the conditions strip and §10.4's dated stamp, and nothing else.

- On the **count slide** it is the top block of the content column, at **x 65**. The column is bottom-anchored, so the row's y depends on the band's height (§4.4): it is **y 152 at the 24-row ceiling** and **y 482 at the measured minimum cap of 99**. It is never fixed at y 132.
- On **draw slides 3+** it overlays the photo well at **x 65, y 164** — 32px into the photograph, staggered with the sheet edge's y 180 start — and costs zero vertical budget.
- The **cover** carries no counter; its proof line states the count. The **closing slide** carries none.

It counts **draws, not slides**, and it reads `drawsRendered` (§5.11), never the config value — an eight-draw deck is ten slides, and a deck that shrank to seven may not render "OF 8". Headroom at the new step: `DRAW 10 OF 12` is 13 glyphs; at JetBrains Mono 700's MEASURED 0.600em advance and 44px that is 13 × 26.4 = 343.2px plus 40px of horizontal padding = **383.2px**, so the chip runs x 65 → 448.2 against a text well ending x 960 and a photo well ending x 1015. It fits about 2.3× over. (The 305px figure published earlier was computed at the retired `--fs-micro` step and is superseded, not contradicted in direction. `DRAW 3 OF 8` is 11 glyphs and `DRAW 10 OF 12` is 13; any restatement that measures the worst case at 11 glyphs has miscounted the string.)

**2. The sheet edge — a partial element crossing the right edge.**

A 96px vertical strip at **x 1015 → 1111**, running **y 180 → 1182**, separated from the ground by a 1px `--rule` hairline at **x = 1015** and a 24px soft shadow. It reads as the edge of the next sheet in the stack. On a 1080px canvas **65px of it is on-frame (x 1015 → 1080) and 31px is off-frame** (1111 − 1080): 65 + 31 = 96 ✓.

| Slide | Sheet edge content |
|---|---|
| Cover | Flat paper **#FFFFFF**. **No information whatsoever.** |
| Draw slides | The *next* draw's normalised photograph, clipped by the frame |
| Closing slide | **Absent** — the deck visibly ends |

The strip starts at **y 180**, not 152, so on slide 1 it begins below the multi-image keep-out entirely and the "flat colour may pass under the keep-out" allowance is never needed.

**Why the cover's sheet edge is blank.** The grid crop keeps x 33.75 → 1046.25, so of the 65px on-frame strip **33.75px is destroyed and 31.25px survives** (1046.25 − 1015), and the rest is off-frame anyway. Because the strip carries no glyph, figure or photographic subject on slide 1, **nothing is lost to the crop** and the truncation cue survives — the element is cut off harder, not less. On inner slides there is no crop, so the strip carries a real photograph and reads as a card behind. This is the only slide-1-specific constraint on the bleed, and it exists because slide 1 is the only slide the grid ever crops.

Note the trade: #FFFFFF on `--ground` #F7F5F0 is **1.09:1** (computed), so on the cover the strip is legible only by its hairline and its shadow. That is the intended paper-on-paper reading, but at profile-grid size the cover's truncation cue is carried almost entirely by 1px of hairline. It is the weakest element in the template and it needs eyeballing alongside the band.

**What it costs, correctly attributed.** Every text-bearing slide runs on a 895px column rather than the full 950px chrome track. That 55px is **§3.5's band-sized well, not a cost the sheet edge imposes**: the strip occupies a margin the well already leaves. The sheet edge takes nothing from the type; it takes the paper between x 960 and x 1015 that the band's own width had already given up.

---

### 5.10 The closing slide

Ground newsprint, both chrome bands, no sheet edge, no counter. Emits `data-pdd-role="closing"`. All four blocks take their steps from §3.5, and because there is no sheet edge **the full 950px chrome track (x 65 … 1015) is the measure** on this slide.

| Block | Role | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `WE LIST DRAWS. WE RUN NONE.` | The frame's single `--fs-hero` node | Bricolage Grotesque 800, `--ink`, measured to ≤3 lines on the **950px** track |
| Sub-line — **string withdrawn, see below** | Sub-line | Inter 400, `--fs-body`, `--ink-meta` |
| `prizedrawsdaily.co.uk` | Closing URL | Inter 700, `--fs-lead`, `--rail` |
| `@prizedrawsdaily` | Handle | JetBrains Mono 700, `--fs-body`, `--ink-meta` |

**The sub-line `Every UK draw we track, checked and dated daily.` is deleted and §5 does not author its replacement.** It asserts a coverage claim (`every`) and a cadence claim (`daily`) that this spec's own evidence contradicts: §10.4 sets a 48-hour freshness window *precisely because* daily is not achieved — a single missed observation in the documented datacenter-403 class jumps a figure's age to roughly 32h, against roughly 39 of 107 operators intermittently refused — and §1.4 records the pipeline 76 days dark with two runs abandoned at the publish step. §1.5 A11 already logs this exact defect class against `global.series.slotLine` ("every night · 7pm UK") as a CAP 3.7 objective claim that "was false within days of being rendered". §10.6's word-class predicates (`secondPerson`, `unboundedComparative`) match neither `every` nor `daily`, so nothing in the gate set catches it.

The replacement is **§10.6a's**, inside its L1 allow-list and CI fixture, and it must be **a statement of method, not of frequency or coverage** — what PDD does to a figure before it publishes it, carrying no unbounded scope token. §10.6 should also gain a cadence-and-coverage class in its L2/L4 deny-list (`every`, `all`, `daily`, `always`, `24/7` in PDD's own voice, outside an interpolated scope token) so the `slotLine` defect cannot land a third time. The headline above is likewise §10.6a's to ratify; §5 states only its role and its measure.

**Field 5 and the role.** The closing slide carries no `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node, so §10.2's G1-P assertion does not run on it, and a prize-name node appearing here would itself be class A (`prize-name-on-deck-asset`). CAP 8.17 field 5 is discharged post-wide by the other nine children of the same post. ⚠️ That rests on the compliance unit being the post rather than the child, and §5.6 records that Instagram re-serves non-first children cold — so a viewer can meet this slide alone, carrying the deck band and no prize nature. The cover and the count slide are both covered in their own right; this is the one genuine hole in the deck, and the cheapest honest fix if a reviewer rejects post-wide discharge is to give the closing slide the cover's board.

The headline is also where the "we run none" disclaimer lives. It is not a CAP 8.17 significant condition, so it does not belong in the conditions band — and keeping it out of the band is what lets the band's three-line structure be identical on every slide of every format.

**Delete `📌 Save & send to your comp buddy`** (VERIFIED at `render.mjs:170`, `.cta-save` at 28px, `styles.css:427`). Honestly stated: OFFICIAL, Meta's Pages/Groups/Events Policies III.E prohibits "share to enter" and "tag a friend to enter" — those are *entry mechanics*, and a generic save prompt is not literally covered. But engagement bait is demoted at account level for repeat offenders, a daily automated poster is that profile, and the reward is not even measurable: VERIFIED, `insights.mjs` ingests no saves and no Instagram shares. Asymmetric downside, unmeasurable upside, delete.

The closing line is the brand's whole position — unoccupied territory #1 (light), #2 (data not poster) and #3 (a directory that can name a loser) compressed into four words — and it is the one slide where saying it plainly is the entire job.
