### 5.11 Deck size

**This section is the sole owner of `drawsPerDeck`, `BACKUPS`, `DRAWS_MIN`, the degradation ladder and the pool-eligibility tiers.** Every other section references "the deck size (§5.11)" or reads `drawsRendered`, and writes no digit.

**Decision: 8 draws per deck, 10 slides (cover + 8 draws + closing).** VERIFIED current default is 5 draws / 7 slides: `plan.mjs:10` reads `SLIDES || 5`, and `build.mjs:150` assembles `[intro, ...drawSlides, {type:"cta"}]`.

**The constant, and everything derived from it.** The number is authored exactly once; every other quantity is arithmetic.

```
carousel/config.json   global.drawsPerDeck = 8        // the ONLY authored value (written by §8.7)
carousel/config.mjs    exports drawsPerDeck + these derived values:

  SLIDES          = drawsPerDeck + 2              = 10
  BACKUPS         = ceil(drawsPerDeck / 2)        = 4
  POOL_MIN        = drawsPerDeck + BACKUPS        = 12
  DRAWS_MIN       = 4                              (authored floor, defended below)
  POOL_MIN_FLOOR  = DRAWS_MIN + ceil(DRAWS_MIN/2) = 6
  ODDS_COLLAPSE_CEILING(n) = floor(0.4 * n)       = 3 at n = 8
```

`BACKUPS = ceil(N/2)` is chosen because it reproduces today's hard-coded 3 at today's N = 5 (`ceil(2.5) = 3`), so it is continuous with the status quo rather than a new invention.

| N | BACKUPS | pool rows needed | odds-collapse escalates at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4 | 12 | ≥4 collapsed |
| 7 | 4 | 11 | ≥3 |
| 6 | 3 | 9 | ≥3 |
| 5 | 3 | 8 | ≥3 |
| 4 | 2 | 6 | ≥2 |

(The escalation column is the ceiling plus one: a run escalates when the collapsed count *exceeds* `ODDS_COLLAPSE_CEILING(n)`.)

**Two run-scoped variables, not one.** `plan.mjs` resolves the constant once per run and writes `drawsPlanned`, `backups` and `poolTruncated` into `selection.json`. `build.mjs` resolves final attrition and writes `drawsRendered` into the slide model, `publish.json` and `out/COMPLIANCE.json`. **Every downstream consumer reads `drawsRendered`** — never the config value, never `drawsPlanned`. It is frozen before the first PNG is written, so a deck that shrank from 8 to 7 cannot render `DRAW 3 OF 8`. The `SLIDES` env var is **retired** in favour of `DRAWS_PER_DECK`: it names slides while meaning draws, and that off-by-two is how the drift started.

**The role attribute is written here too.** `render.mjs:182` already writes `data-type="${slide.type}"` onto `<body>` from `build.mjs:150`'s slide array; it additionally writes **`data-pdd-role`** from the same array — index 0 → `cover`, index 1 → `count`, indices 2…N → `draw`, last → `closing`. §10.2 owns the eight-value enum and the `DRAW_CARRYING` set; §5 owns only this mapping, because it owns the array.

**A post-level gate falls out of `drawsRendered`.** §10.2's MODEL-stage assertion requires the carousel's count of draw-carrying assets bearing a non-empty prize name to equal `drawsRendered` exactly. That is the assertion that catches a mislabelled role, so it is not optional garnish.

**The selector does not enforce any deck size today, and that is the real defect.** VERIFIED at `select.mjs:40`: `const enough = list.length >= Math.min(3, n) ? 1 : 0;` — the adequacy bar has been pinned at 3 regardless of `n` since the pipeline was written, and `best.list.slice(0, n)` at `select.mjs:48` then returns short. So the existing spec floor has never had code behind it, and at N = 5 a 3-draw category already passes. Raising the number without fixing this ships silent 3-draw decks under a spec that says 8. Replace with a two-tier test, evaluated against the per-category list after `excludeSlugs` filtering, **over configured slugs only** — `pickBestCategory` skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories` (§8.7's one-line guard at `select.mjs:33`), because the `enough * 1e12` term otherwise lets the unconfigured `"other"` bucket win a deck at a weight of 0:

- **Tier 1:** `pool >= POOL_MIN` (12). Scored as today (`visualWeight`, `total_prize_value`, the 0.5 `avoidCategory` penalty). The deck runs at `drawsPerDeck`.
- **Tier 2**, only where no tier-1 category exists: `pool >= POOL_MIN_FLOOR` (6). The deck runs at `nFor(pool) = max{ N ∈ [4,8] : N + ceil(N/2) <= pool }`.
- No category at tier 2 → **no publish**.

**The degradation ladder, one rung at a time.** From `drawsPlanned` the deck degrades **one draw at a time** down to `DRAWS_MIN`, publishing at whatever it lands on. On any per-draw failure — §5.12 rule 9 or 10, §9's Class C asset refusal, §10.8 class B — the order of recourse is: promote a backup (up to `BACKUPS`), then shrink the deck by one, repeat. The earlier "10 → 8 → 6 slides" three-rung ladder, with gaps at 7 and 5 draws, is retired; arbitrary rungs are drift bait. This also resolves the standing conflict with §10.8: class-B backup exhaustion no longer escalates straight to class A, it enters the shrink and reaches class A only below the floor.

The ladder **may not**: widen `DAYS` past 7, lower `MIN_DAYS` below 1, mix categories in one deck, re-use a draw inside the 7-day `recentDrawSlugs` exclusion, or raise the `limit=300` fetch (`select.mjs:20`). Widening the window is the obvious wrong fix: it would put "closing soon" copy — §5.7's caution chip, §5.5's `deadline` archetype — on draws that are not closing soon, a CAP 8.22 / DMCC 2024 exposure created to save a post.

**The floor is 4 draws, and below it the run does not publish.** `DRAWS_MIN = 4` is forced independently by two geometries already fixed elsewhere: §5.4's cover board is a fixed 280px block of four 70px rows in a bottom-anchored layout, and at N = 3 row 4 is a 70px hole; and §7.7's Facebook album is the cover plus four draw slides. That §5.11's earlier floor was also 4 is a coincidence worth noting, not the reason.

Below 4 the run writes a class-A record `deck-underfilled: category <slug> supplied <n> of 4` to `out/COMPLIANCE.json` and `out/COMPLIANCE.txt`, writes no PNG, no `publish.json`, and **exits non-zero**. `plan.mjs:41`'s current `process.exit(0)` on an empty pool is replaced: a no-publish day that exits 0 is indistinguishable from success.

**Pool truncation must be named, not inferred.** `select.mjs:20` sets `limit=300` over the 1–7 day band ordered `draw_date.asc`. Against the 483 in-window rows measured on 17 Sep 2026 the 300th row falls at roughly day 4.7, so truncation biases toward sooner-closing draws — correct for this format, and not binding on the large categories. When the fetch returns exactly 300 rows the pool **is** truncated: `plan.mjs` sets `poolTruncated: true`, and any short deck on a truncated day is logged as `deck-short (pool truncated)` so it is never misattributed to real scarcity.

**Why 8, against the Eden data and its own caveat.** MEASURED (Eden, 655,385 carousels / 12,159 creators, Aug 2025–Aug 2026), breakout rate by slide count: 3 → 23.4%, 5 → 26.8%, 6 → ~27%, 10 → 28.8%, 14 → 32.1%, 18–20 → ~32% (plateau).

⚠️ **Vendor-bias caveat, carried in full.** Eden sells a carousel generator, so "more slides win" is commercially convenient. The metric is breakout-vs-the-creator's-own-median, which may simply be measuring effort: creators who make 14-slide decks probably make better decks. **Treat the direction as credible and the magnitude as soft.** This spec takes the 7 → 10 step, inside the densest part of the curve, and declines the 10 → 14 step where the gap is largest. The competing number, "5–8 slides is optimal", has no source anywhere and is contradicted by the only real slide-count dataset. Four sections being written against 5–6 draws is not evidence; it is four authors inheriting `plan.mjs:10`.

**Supply, restated.** MEASURED against the live DB, 17 Sep 2026, draws closing in the 1–7 day window (`plan.mjs:12–13` defaults `DAYS=7, MIN_DAYS=1`): **483 total** — cash-prizes 184, tech-giveaways 90, sports-outdoors 55, collectibles 51, car-draws 45, luxury 30, home-garden 27, uncategorised 1. (An earlier draft reported 493 with sports-outdoors at 65; re-measured, those were wrong, and §4.2's corroborating figure rests on the retracted 493.) The earlier draft's "supply is not the constraint" is too loose. Supply in the window is ample; the **binding quantity is per-category rows surviving both the 300-row cap and the 7-day `recentDrawSlugs` exclusion**. Scaling the window counts by 300/483 = 0.621 puts home-garden at ~17 and luxury at ~19 in the capped payload — ⚠️ those two are a proportional estimate, not a measurement; the per-category composition of the 300 soonest rows was not queried. After a week of exclusions either can fall below the 12-row tier-1 bar and run at tier 2 or not at all.

**What going higher actually costs.** Each additional draw slide needs a normalised photograph and a conditions band whose every figure is stored and evidenced. Taking p = 0.10 per draw as a planning figure (§5.12's measured 7.2% title residue plus margin for asset and evidence failures), Binomial(8, 0.10) gives P(≥4 drops) = 0.50% against 3 backups and P(≥5) ≈ 0.04% against 4. Four backups at N = 8 is not tight. `fetchimg.mjs:170` already reads `[...sel.draws, ...(sel.backups || [])]`, so backup pre-fetch scales with no code change once `plan.mjs` writes 4.

⚠️ Eden's metric is performance against the creator's own median. PDD has published 12 posts ever, spanning 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-03, and has been dark 76 days. There is no usable own-median, and OFFICIAL there is no per-slide metric — so PDD can never learn *where* people stop. Slide count is a decision to be made on the external dataset and then left alone, not tuned. It is also cheap to unwind: if §9's measured usable-yield comes back below 12 candidates per category per run, `drawsPerDeck` drops to 6 in one line and the ladder, the backups, the escalation ceiling, the album and the board's `+N` line all follow. §12.4 gates the lock on that measurement, which is the right place for it.

**Why the number is not cut to 6 pre-emptively.** N = 8 is load-bearing in four settlements already closed against it: §8.7's schema writes `global.drawsPerDeck = 8` and computes its picker arithmetic at it; §10.6a's CI fact-sets run n = DRAWS_MIN…8; §10.2's post-level gate asserts the carousel's prize-name count `=== drawsRendered` at 8; and §5.4's board and §7.7's album are sized from it. Changing the authored value here would reopen four settlements to pre-empt a measurement that has not been taken, when §12.4 already gates the lock in the right place and the reversal is documented above as one line.

### 5.12 Prize-title cleaning

Known mockup weakness (b): prize titles still carry operator noise, e.g. `NEW Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 #2`.

**MEASURED in-session**, running the current `cleanTitle()` (`carousel/format.mjs:14–29`) over all 880 live enterable titles:

| Residue after cleaning | Count | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Trailing `#N` batch number | 136 | 15.5% |
| `!` anywhere | 85 | 9.7% |
| "instant win(s)" | 84 | 9.5% |
| `&` | 48 | 5.5% |
| `*` emphasis marker | 18 | 2.0% |
| Entirely ALL-CAPS (every cased letter uppercase) | 231 | 26.3% |
| Any of `#`, `!`, `*` or a mechanic phrase | 251 | 28.5% |

(The earlier draft reported ALL-CAPS at 186 / 21.1%; re-measured with the definition above it is 231 / 26.3%.)

And it **over-cleans**. VERIFIED against a real live row: `Apple Bundle – IPhone 17 Pro + Airpods Pro 3 #20` → `Apple Bundle`. The blanket spaced-dash rule at `format.mjs:18` (`/\s*[-–|]\s+.*$/`) fires first and destroys the actual prize; the `+` rule at `format.mjs:19` would have done the same.

**The cleaning contract** (what it must guarantee, not how):

1. Strip a trailing operator batch or instance number: `#N` at the end, `(Draw 3)`, `- Draw 3`.
2. Strip trailing `!`, `*…*` emphasis wrappers, `™` and `®`.
3. Strip an operator-name tail after a spaced pipe (`| Apex Competitions`) — this already works.
4. Strip date tails (`- 17/09/2026`, `*THURSDAY 17.09.26*`).
5. Strip mechanic language — "INSTANT WIN(S)", "INSTANTS", "EVERY TICKET WINS", "LOW ODDS", "AUTO DRAWN". These are not the prize, and repeating an operator's chance-of-winning language is a CAP 8.20/8.21 exposure PDD has no reason to take on.
6. **Replace the blanket dash and `+` rules at `format.mjs:18–19`.** A tail after a spaced en/em dash or a `+` may only be stripped when it is demonstrably promotional — it contains "for just", "or £", a date, a `#N`, a mechanic phrase from (5), or the operator's own name. Otherwise it is part of the prize and is kept. This is the `Apple Bundle` fix.
7. Sentence-case any result that is ≥60% uppercase and longer than 12 characters, preserving a maintained allow-list of genuinely capitalised tokens (LEGO, DJI, AMD, PS5, TV, PC, 4K, GTI, BMW, VW, QD, FPV, DSLR, …). The name already sets in Bricolage 800 at the top of §3.5's ladder; shouting adds nothing and the direction is understatement.
8. On empty or <3-character output, fall back to `grand_prize` (VERIFIED populated on 880 of 880), then to the raw title. (Current fallback is the raw title, `format.mjs:28`.)
9. **If the cleaned result still contains `#`, `!`, `*` or a mechanic phrase, the draw is swapped** rather than rendered.
10. **If the cleaned result matches `/\byour\b.{0,30}\b(odds|chance|win|ticket)\b/i`, the draw is swapped.** §10.6a exempts operator prize titles from its second-person predicate — operators legitimately write "Build Your Own PC" — but a title that puts the second person next to an odds or winning word renders a banned framing on a PDD asset in someone else's voice, and a viewer does not distinguish voices. §9 owns stripping second-person and comparative language at ingest normalisation, so this rule should rarely fire.

**Degradation.** Rules 9 and 10 promote a backup (up to `BACKUPS`), then shrink the deck one draw at a time to `DRAWS_MIN` (§5.11). They never fail the run above the floor.

**Sizing rule 9 honestly.** The earlier draft put the swap rate at "roughly one draw in six" by quoting the 15.5% `#N` residue — but rules 1–5 strip `#N` before rule 9 tests for it, so that figure double-counts. MEASURED by applying an approximation of rules 1–5 to all 880 live titles and then testing rule 9: **63 of 880 = 7.2%** survive. At 8 draws that is **0.58 expected swaps against 4 backups**.

The residue is not random, though. It clusters. Live examples that survive rules 1–5:

```
Babyliss Curling Iron or Cash!! Only 25 Tickets!! AUTO DRAWN!! 17/09
3 Piece Luggage Set or Cash!! Only 59 Tickets!! AUTO DRAWN!! 17/09
104 Piece Black & Decker Drill or Cash!! Only 79 Tickets!! AUTO DRAWN!! 17/09
NEW : PRIZE EVERYTIME DAILY EDITION! *THURSDAY 17.09.26
```

MEASURED: **49 of 880 live titles contain "AUTO DRAW"**, including `AUTO DRAW: WIN A WINNER'S CHOICE CUSTOM FIT DRIVER #119` and its siblings, and they come from a small number of operators. Because `plan.mjs:69` draws backups from the *same category pool*, a category dominated by one such operator can exhaust the backup budget in a single deck and drive the ladder down several rungs. That is the reason the backup budget scales with the deck (`ceil(N/2)`) rather than staying at 3.

**The untruncated title is never lost.** `out/alt.json` carries the full `cleanTitle()` output on every draw-carrying asset (§10.7), so a title truncated by §5.7's fitting ladder still has a machine-readable record, and each truncation is written to `COMPLIANCE.json` as the counted, non-failing record `prize-name-truncated: <role> <slug> <n>→<m> glyphs`.

### 5.13 Operator attribution and tagging

MEASURED (Metricool, 24.36M posts / 375,118 accounts, Jan–Feb 2026 vs 2025): mentions drive **+108% reach and +167% comments for accounts under 2K followers**. ⚠️ This is an observed difference in a vendor's own dataset, not an experiment; it is correlational and single-sourced. Carry it as a strong prior, not a mechanism.

**A handle drawn on a PNG is not a mention.** State it plainly, because it is the thing most likely to get quietly laundered: text rendered into an image generates no notification, no link and no mention. The Metricool effect can only be captured by (a) `@` mentions in the caption text and (b) Instagram's photo user-tagging. The slide and the caption therefore do different jobs.

**On the slide — the operator lockup.** A **45px** row immediately above the prize name, at **x 65**. §5.13 owns this row's height and it is one value on every surface; §4.4 consumes it and does not restate it.

- Operator name, Inter 600 at `--fs-micro`, `--ink-meta`.
- A 4px gap, then the **Trust Score chip**: `PDD 4.2`, JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-micro`, `--ink` on `--verdict-tint`, 6px radius, 6px/14px padding.

**The lockup does not discharge CAP 8.17.** The how-to-participate condition is discharged by the conditions band naming the entry host (§10.2). The operator name on the slide is editorial attribution and PDD's own added value; it is not the legal carrier, and §6.5's cut ladder should classify it on that basis rather than on this section's earlier claim.

⚠️ **The chip's border colour is unresolved and §5 does not resolve it.** §3.2 restricts `--verdict` to checked facts — figures PDD holds a stored source and timestamp for — and §10.5 rule 3 makes green on an unverified figure a hard fail. A Trust Score is PDD's own assessment, not one of those figures. Either §3.2 widens to admit PDD's own evidenced assessments and defines what evidence a Trust Score must carry, or the chip renders without a green border. **§5's fallback, so the slide is renderable either way: `--ink` on `--verdict-tint` with a 1px `--rule` border.** The question belongs to §3.2/§10.5, not to §10.4's evidence contract, which is about figures read from operators.

VERIFIED against the live schema, 17 Sep 2026: `operators` holds **110 rows** with 24 columns. `rating` spans **3.0 – 4.8** with a mode of **4.2 (23 operators)**. Exactly one operator — **Dream Big Competitions — has `rating = NULL`** (not `0`, as an earlier draft stated; the distinction matters because `Number(null) > 0` is false but a SQL `rating > 0` filter also drops NULL, and a naive template would render `PDD null`). The chip is guarded on a positive numeric rating and omitted otherwise. `verdict` is populated for **109 of 110** and is available for the caption.

VERIFIED: `select.mjs:14` already joins `operators(name)`, but `format.mjs:55–66`'s `toDrawSlide()` never copies it onto the slide object, so the operator never reaches the slide today. The join must extend to `operators(name, rating, verdict)` and `toDrawSlide()` must carry all three.

The Trust Score chip is the strongest "adds material value" signal PDD has — its own 7-factor assessment, decorrelated from Trustpilot, and no competitor publishes anything equivalent.

**In the caption — the `@` mention.** One mention per draw, in the caption body.

**The handle is a caption dependency, not a render blocker.** VERIFIED: the 24 `operators` columns are `id, slug, name, logo_url, website_url, affiliate_url, description, rating, established_year, trust_notes, featured, created_at, updated_at, review_status, verdict, editorial_intro, is_legit_summary, pros, cons, specialism, trustpilot_url, faq, seo_title, seo_description` — **none is a social handle**, and `operators.json` (VERIFIED 107 entries, fields `name, slug, base, method, apiStyle, drawPath, note`) has no social field either. Nothing refuses to render without it: the operator *name* is already selected, and the handle lives in the caption. MEASURED: the 880 live enterable draws span exactly **60 distinct operators**, so that is the size of the sourcing job. The digest's competitive crawl confirms handles exist for the largest (BOTB 1.3m, 7days Performance 304k, Elite Competitions 167k, Dream Car Giveaways 137k, Click Competitions 106k, Rev Comps 94k) but does not record them; Bounty Competitions is private and Storm Competitions is age-gated.

### 5.14 Tokens consumed

**§3.7 is the sole owner of the colour token table and the `:root` block. §5 publishes no token table, no hex and no type scale.** The earlier draft here published a complete parallel vocabulary — `--paper`, `--ink-meta`, `--rail-paper`, `--rail-meta`, `--amber`, `--mint`, `--caution`, `--graphic` — for jobs §3.7 already had names for, and its stated premise was false: it claimed §3.2 ships `--rule: #D8D3C8` for decorative hairlines, when §3.7 ships `--rule: #8C8677` (meaning-bearing) and `--hairline: #D8D3C8` (decorative) — exactly the split the draft believed it was inventing. **The sentence "`--hairline` is withdrawn" is withdrawn**: §3.7 ships it and §8 paints with it throughout (§8.4's ink model, §8.5's tech anchors and dimension frame, house's contour arcs, the sports pennant, the collectibles crop marks, NEUTRAL's baseline grid). The `--rule` redefinition and the `--graphic` rename are both retired with it, because the collision they were invented to solve does not exist in §3.7's block.

What §5 consumes, by §3.7's names:

| §3.7 token | Where §5 uses it |
|---|---|
| `--ground` #F7F5F0 | The newsprint ground of every slide |
| `--scene-tone` #F3F1EC | §8's scene ground on `still-4x5`; §5 supplies the rects only |
| `--ink` #14161A | Headline, prize name, board Prize and Closes columns, chip type |
| `--ink-meta` #5A5F66 | Dateline, board Index, operator name, closing handle and sub-line |
| `--hairline` #D8D3C8 | **Decorative only** — the board's four row rules |
| `--rule` #8C8677 | **Meaning-bearing** — the dot field, chip borders, the sheet-edge hairline, §9.5's separation hairline |
| `--rail` #14385F | The two chrome bands |
| `--rail-ink` #F7F5F0 | Masthead Slot A and Slot B, the closes chip's type |
| `--rail-accent` #FFC53D | The figures inside §10.4's stamp; §10.2's closing state on the band |
| `--verdict` #0F6B45 | The cover proof line's figures; the marked dot (§4.5/§4.7 own when) |
| `--verdict-tint` #E6F2EA | The Trust Score chip's ground |
| `--deadline` #B3202C | The closes chip's ground, and the board's Closes column inside 48h |

⚠️ **One token has no owner.** §5's earlier `--rail-meta` #B9C6D6 — secondary type on a rail band, which §10.2 uses for the conditions band's L2 and L3 — has **no definition in §3.7's block at all**, and it renders on every asset of every format. §3.7 must adopt it (under that name or §10.2's) or §10.2 must resolve those lines to `--rail-ink`. Measured, it is 6.88:1 on `--rail`.

Contrast rows §5 depends on, all of them §3.7's measured figures rather than new ones: `--ink` on `--ground` 16.62:1; `--ink-meta` on `--ground` 5.91:1; `--verdict` on `--ground` 6.01:1; `--deadline` on `--ground` 6.10:1; `--ink` on `--verdict-tint` 15.74:1; `--rail-ink` on `--rail` 10.95:1; `--rail-accent` on `--rail` 7.56:1; `--rule` on `--ground` 3.33:1, clearing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11's 3:1 floor for the dot field; and on `--scene-tone`, `--ink` 16.05:1, `--ink-meta` 5.70:1, `--verdict` 5.80:1, `--rule` 3.21:1. `--scene-tone` measures L = 0.880214 against `--ground`'s 0.913702, a ΔL of 0.033488 — a 3.67% luminance step, which is what makes it the loudest a still ground can be without touching the dot field. Every text pair clears 4.5:1 on both grounds. One ratio that is **not** used because it is forbidden: `--deadline` on `--rail` is 1.79:1; the band's closing state is `--rail-accent`, per §10.2.

Worth recording so nobody reopens it on the wrong grounds: the three greys once in play for the dot field (`#948C7C`, `#8B867B`, `#8C8677`) differ negligibly — `#8B867B` and `#8C8677` are ΔL ≈ 0.0001 apart and both compute to 3.33:1 on the ground — but `#948C7C` at **3.06:1** has only 2% of margin and falls to 2.95:1 on `--scene-tone`, a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 failure. §3.7 landed on `--rule` #8C8677 and §4.5 owns the dot's use of it.

**Type scale, gutter and tracks are §3.5's.** This section restates none of them. The earlier draft published a second nine-step scale (`34/45 · 40/45 · 48/60 · 56/58 · 60/70 · 68/70 · 88/90 · 120/120 · 150/150`) that overlapped §3.5's in five places, introduced two sizes §3.5 does not have, and broke its own stated multiple-of-5 line-height rule at `56/58`. It is deleted rather than corrected; the contradiction disappears with the table.

**Font availability — VERIFIED against `carousel/assets/fonts/` and `fonts.mjs:3–23`:**

| Face | Bundled | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Bricolage Grotesque | 400, 700, 800 | none — spec uses 800 |
| Inter | 400, 500, 600, 700 | none |
| JetBrains Mono | **700 only** | 400 and 500 are **not** bundled |

Every figure in this spec is set in JetBrains Mono **700**, so the gap is not blocking here — but it is blocking elsewhere: §7.2's dateline specifies Mono 500, which does not exist, and §4.10 warns that a missing weight degrades to the next family in the stack and breaks tabular alignment silently. Either §7.2 moves to 700 or two files are added to `fonts.mjs:3–23` as an explicit prerequisite. **Cabin is not bundled and is not needed.**

**Correction: Anton and Oswald are NOT retired here.** An earlier draft removed `fonts.mjs:5–8` (Anton 400, Oswald 500/600/700 — VERIFIED 56,728 bytes of woff2 ≈ 75.6KB base64) for a per-render payload saving. VERIFIED: `:root` sets `--font-display: 'Anton'`, and `reel-template.mjs` and `story.mjs` reference `var(--font-display)` eight times between them. Removing those faces would silently break the video templates' display type. **The carousel simply stops referencing them**; the files stay bundled and the saving is deferred to the Reel/Story rework. The same applies to Playfair Display, Space Grotesk, Fraunces and Bungee (`fonts.mjs:17–19, 21–22`).

**`--font-kicker` is resolved, and §3.7 is right.** RE-GREPPED: `--font-kicker` is defined at `styles.css:35`, `:75` and `:178` and there is **zero** `var(--font-kicker)` anywhere in the repository. It is a dead token, §5.2's earlier inclusion of it in the consumed set was wrong, and the corrected count is exactly 32. Oswald therefore survives only because `'Oswald'` is named directly in `styles.css` (`.closes`, `.footer .rp`, `.cta-save`) and in `reel.mjs:81`'s cover body rule, not because a token points at it — a distinction §3.4 should use when it sequences the deletion.

### Decisions this section commits to

- Canvas stays 1080×1350 @ dsf 2 (2160×2700 PNG), unchanged from `render.mjs:187`.
- **Both tracks are §3.5's and are published here only as derivations with their sums: chrome track 950px at x 65 → 1015 (1080 − 2×65 = 1015 − 65 = Meta Box A's width), content well 895px at x 65 → 960 (960 − 65 = 895 = §4.4's band).** 70px and 64px are both retired; 64 put the chrome's right edge 1px outside Box A, and 70 produced a second track and a 35–45px band residual that made a centred origin permanently re-derivable.
- **The well is not defined by the sheet edge.** The hairline is at x 1015 and a deliberate 55px right margin lies between it and the well. Nothing text-bearing crosses x 960.
- The renderer asserts `--gutter === 65` and lays out against 950, 895 and 1015. A per-node "every left edge = 65" assertion is not adopted: it would fail on the board's own columns and on every chip.
- A 180×180 keep-out at x 900–1080, y 0–180 on slide 1 only: flat colour may pass under it, no glyph, figure, chip, rule or photographic subject may enter it. The sheet edge starts at y 180 so the allowance is never needed.
- `.pill` (`styles.css:328`) is deleted as a LATENT hazard, not a live one: `build.mjs:150` puts the intro first, so it has never rendered on slide 1.
- Standing chrome on every slide: `--rail` masthead y 0–132 and conditions band y 1182–1350 (168px) = 300px = 22.2%. Masthead Slot B is suppressed on slide 1 only.
- **The masthead stamp's string is §10.4's, and §5 publishes none.** Slot A ends at x 545.5; §10.4's long form right-aligned to x 1015 starts at x 321.4 and overlaps it by 224.1px, while the short form starts at x 811.0 and clears by 265.5px. §5.2's no-collision rule makes that a build failure, so §10.4 must assign the short form here or delete Slot A.
- §3.7's newsprint palette is ADDED to `:root`, never substituted: the video templates consume exactly 32 legacy properties (`--accent-rgb` 21×, `--font-display` 8×). `--font-kicker` is NOT one of them. No property may be defined twice across the two lifted blocks — last block wins, silently, on all four surfaces.
- **§5 publishes no token table and no hex.** §3.7 owns them; §5.14 is a consumer list. `--hairline` is kept, the `--rule` redefinition and the `--graphic` rename are retired, and `--rail-meta` #B9C6D6 is flagged as rendering on every asset with no owner.
- §5 authors no dot-grid geometry, no ceiling, no above-ceiling encoding, no marker rule, no odds string, no conditions-band field list, **no count-slide block height, no gap, no band allowance and no E2 total**. Owners: §4.4, §4.7, §4.6, §4.5, §10.6a, §10.2, §10.4.
- The conditions band's envelope is §5's (x 0–1080, y 1182–1350, fixed 168px = 16.5 + §10.2's 135px type block + 16.5) and its contents are §10.2's. **Its type track is 950px at x 65…1015** and the measured-fit rule measures against 950, not 940; §10.2's 952px / x 64…1016 re-derives to it. The measured-fit rule stays hard-failing, and its one known legitimate-draw failure case — §4.8's annotation row — is closed by §10.6a's 32-glyph worst case rather than by exempting the rule.
- The ticket price moves from a photo-well chip into the conditions band, because the count slide has no photo well. `ticket_price` is positive on 880 of 880 live enterable draws (minimum £0.01), so the field has no null case.
- The cover carries no photograph and no thumbnail strip, emits `data-pdd-role="cover"` and carries no prize-name node; it discharges CAP 8.17 field 5 through the board's Prize column and the proof line. Ground is newsprint plus §8's scene clipped to **754,220 px² = 51.73%**; the ordering device is a fixed 280px four-row typographic board.
- **The board's three columns close on 895 exactly: Index x 65 (54px to Prize), Prize x 119…648 (529px), 20px gap, Closes x 668…960 (292px).** The 35px lost against the retired well is taken entirely from the truncating Prize column; `SUN 21 SEP 26` needs 265.2 of the Closes column's 292px and `01`–`08` needs 40.8 of the Index column's 54px.
- The cover is bottom-anchored with fixed inter-block gaps, so all slack pools between the dateline and the first headline line: 347px at one line, 197px at two, **47px at three**, and a 103px collision at four. The `question` arm always renders three line boxes, so ~91 days a year the cover runs at its tightest legal vertical.
- The cover headline is generated from the already-rotating, already-logged `hook_archetype`; the six per-category hook constants, the `WIN BIG` fallback and `hookLabel()` are deleted, the file edit performed by §8.7. **The `question` arm has one permitted form, `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`, sourced from `drawsRendered` alone and logged `question:only`**; the deck's lowest cap moves to the proof line, which is where §10.6 predicate 3's evidence unit finds it.
- Text fit is MEASURED in the headless browser, never budgeted by character count: **1–3 line boxes within 895px** at `--fs-hero`, long form then short form, then the build fails rather than shrinking the anchor. Informationally, 895 ÷ 101.1 = 8.85 characters per line and ≈26.5 over three lines.
- **No word in any headline form may exceed EIGHT glyphs at `--fs-hero`** (8 × 101.1 = 808.8 ≤ 895; 9 = 909.9 > 895). The earlier "ten" was already wrong on the 930px track. The cap constrains what §10.6a may author; the render-time measurement remains the gate, and the cap rejects nothing in §10.6a's current table.
- The `absurd-comparison` arm may use ONLY `cashAlt()`'s operator-stated figure, never `total_prize_value`: `prize_value` is 0/880 populated and `total_prize_value` equals entries × price on 880/880. It runs on ~20% of selections and otherwise falls back to `price-anchor`, logged as `absurd-comparison→price-anchor`.
- **Slide 2 is the count slide**: `data-pdd-role="count"`, no photograph, the full odds band, the draw with the lowest `total_entries` (ties by earliest close). Its block order is §5's; every height, gap, state total and the ceiling are §4.4's, and the column is bottom-anchored. Delta 1 is deleted; Delta 3 moves to slide 3.
- Slides 3 onward emit `data-pdd-role="draw"`, run in ascending `draw_date` with the count-slide draw removed, and carry E2 at §4.4's height. **The photo well is x 0 → 1015, the flex residual, and its value at each prize-name step is §4.4's: 565 / 585 / 615px.** §5.7's 500px floor is now cleared by 65px rather than met exactly; at 565px the photograph is 41.9% of the canvas and 53.8% of the well.
- Scene-mount rects are §5's and areas are §8's. At §4.4's photo wells the draw-slide region is **241,645 px² (16.57%)** at two lines and **190,895 px² (13.09%)** at one; the count slide's odds rect has no fixed top edge and at the 24-row ceiling re-derives §8's figure from 750px to **745px**, moving that region to 312,695 px² (21.45%).
- The prize-name node carries `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"` and its fitting ladder's floor is §3.5's `--fs-lead` (56px), below which the title truncates at a word boundary with a trailing `…` and is re-measured at that step — so §10.2's G1-P step assertion cannot fail on a still. At 56px the 895px track holds 24 glyphs per line and 48 over two.
- The counter chip is **JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-label` 44/50 in a 70px row (height §4.4's)**, at x 65 on both surfaces, counting draws not slides and reading `drawsRendered`. `DRAW 10 OF 12` is 13 glyphs = 343.2px + 40px padding = **383.2px**, ending x 448.2. The 305px figure was computed at the retired `--fs-micro` step.
- The sheet edge is 96px at **x 1015 → 1111**, y 180–1182: **65px on-frame, 31px off-frame**. The crop destroys 33.75px of the on-frame strip and 31.25px survives. Blank #FFFFFF on the cover, the next draw's photograph on draw slides, absent on the closing slide. The 55px it sits in is §3.5's band-sized well, not a cost the strip imposes.
- The closing slide emits `data-pdd-role="closing"`, runs its headline on the full 950px chrome track, carries no prize-name node, and is discharged for field 5 post-wide. **Its cadence-and-coverage sub-line is deleted and §10.6a owns the replacement**, which must state method rather than frequency.
- **`drawsPerDeck = 8` is authored once in `config.json` and every other quantity is derived**: `SLIDES = N+2`, `BACKUPS = ceil(N/2) = 4`, `POOL_MIN = 12`, `DRAWS_MIN = 4`, `POOL_MIN_FLOOR = 6`, `ODDS_COLLAPSE_CEILING = floor(0.4N) = 3`. The `SLIDES` env var is retired for `DRAWS_PER_DECK`. Cutting to 6 pre-emptively is declined: four closed settlements are sized at 8 and §12.4 already gates the lock on §9's yield measurement.
- `render.mjs:182` writes `data-pdd-role` alongside `data-type`, mapped from `build.mjs:150`'s array: 0 → `cover`, 1 → `count`, 2…N → `draw`, last → `closing`. §10.2 owns the enum.
- `select.mjs:40`'s `Math.min(3, n)` has pinned the adequacy bar at 3 regardless of `n`; it is replaced by a two-tier pool test (12 rows, else 6 with a reduced N) evaluated over configured slugs only, and fixing it is a prerequisite of any deck-size change.
- The deck degrades one draw at a time from `drawsPlanned` to `DRAWS_MIN = 4`, promoting backups first. Below 4 draws: class-A `deck-underfilled`, no PNG, non-zero exit — replacing `plan.mjs:41`'s `process.exit(0)`.
- Prize names fit by measured stepping within 2 line boxes, then word-boundary truncation, replacing the `render.mjs:73` binary that fires on 437–440 of 880 live titles. Each truncation is a counted, non-failing `COMPLIANCE.json` record and `out/alt.json` keeps the untruncated title.
- Prize-title cleaning becomes a contract with a swap-to-backup escape, plus a new rule 10 for second-person-plus-odds titles. Measured residual after the new rules is 7.2% (63/880) ≈ 0.58 swaps per 8-draw deck against 4 backups.
- The operator lockup is a 45px row at x 65 — §5.13 owns that height on every surface — carrying the name and a guarded Trust Score chip, and does **not** discharge CAP 8.17 how-to-participate. `Dream Big Competitions` has `rating = NULL`, so the chip is guarded on a positive numeric rating. `select.mjs:14`'s join extends to `operators(name, rating, verdict)`.
- `operators.instagram_handle` is a caption dependency, not a render blocker.
- Anton, Oswald, the legacy `:root` block and the `.p-*` particle rules stay bundled; the carousel simply stops referencing them. §3.7 must name the section that performs the removal, because §6 currently does not.

### Open questions

- **Which of §10.4's two stamp forms goes in masthead Slot B?** The long form overlaps Slot A by 224.1px on a 950px track; the short form clears by 265.5px. §10.4 checked the long form against a bare track and did not account for the wordmark. Either the short form is assigned here or Slot A is deleted; §5 cannot choose, and the build fails until one of them lands.
- **What replaces §5.10's sub-line?** §10.6a owns it. The constraint is a statement of method, carrying no cadence or coverage token, inside the L1 allow-list and the CI fixture.
- **Who owns `--rail-meta` #B9C6D6?** It renders on every asset of every format as §10.2's band L2/L3 colour and has no definition in §3.7's block. Adopt it or resolve those lines to `--rail-ink`.
- **§9's normalised-master rect.** §5.7 needs 1015 × 615 CSS (2030 × 1230 device px) to cover §4.4's one-line photo well. The pair published elsewhere as 1015 × 500 / 1015 × 550 carries §5.7's retired 500px minimum and is 65px short; §9.3 must land on one.
- **Nothing at this geometry has ever been rendered.** The only artefact is `merged.mjs`'s fractional-cell mockup at cap 699. The 895px well, the x 65 band origin, the 65px on-frame strip, the 31.25px crop headroom, the 55px right margin, the cover's 1.09:1 sheet edge and §4.4's bottom-anchored column with up to 350px of air above the chip all need eyeballing at 1012.5px profile-grid width and at in-feed size before anything is locked.
- **Does the Content Publishing API support `user_tags` on carousel children, or only on single-image posts?** If children cannot be tagged, caption @mentions are the entire mechanism for capturing the Metricool sub-2K effect. Not verified in this session.
- **Who sources and verifies 60 operator Instagram handles?** The `operators` table has 24 columns and none is a social handle; `operators.json` (107 entries) has no social field.
- **Editorial: tagging an operator notifies them.** PDD rates operators 3.0–4.8 and publishes `verdict` text for 109 of 110. Tagging one PDD has rated 3.8, or intends to name as a loser, puts a notification in front of them. Is the product owner comfortable, and does the tagging rule have a rating floor?
- **Can PDD evidence that a stored `draw_date` is the operator's real, immovable closing time?** If not, the `deadline` archetype and the 48-hour caution chip both rest on an unverified premise, and CAP 8.22 / DMCC Act 2024 exposure is real rather than theoretical.
- **Is §9's usable candidate yield ≥ 12 per category per run?** This is the single largest unmeasured threat to `drawsPerDeck = 8` and §12.4 already gates the lock on it. Below 12, the number drops to 6 in one line and everything derived follows.
- **Should the operator's stated cash alternative be promoted to a stored column?** It is re-parsed from free text by `cashAlt()` on every run, it is the ONLY prize-side money figure PDD can evidence, and `absurd-comparison` now depends on it.
- **Should the cover be photographic at all?** This spec makes it fully typographic on unoccupied territory #1, #2 and #5, and on the honest observation that "photo must dominate" is stated about reels. There is no measurement either way.
- **Two of the 880 live enterable draws carry no category.** They bucket as `"other"` at `select.mjs:32` and are now skipped outright by the tier test. Acceptable, or is category backfill a prerequisite?

### Risks

- **The whole odds-as-hero argument rests on one reading of one official document** — the Recommendation Guidelines' "adds material value" clause. If Instagram does not in practice apply it to a directory reposting operator photography with added data, the template has paid a large hierarchy cost for a compliance benefit that never materialises.
- **The 55px right margin is new and unrendered.** Text stops at x 960 while the photograph bleeds to x 1015 and the chrome bands run to x 1015. The page reads 65px of left paper against 55px of right paper. It is the coordinate most likely to be "corrected" back to 1015 by a future author who does not know the well is band-sized, which is why §5.1's definition change is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
- **5px less crop headroom on slide 1, forever.** 31.25px instead of 36.25px, 3.09% of the surviving width, paid on the single most important slide. If a render shows the cover's left edge reading as cramped, the correct response is to inset slide 1's headline only, never to move the gutter.
- **The board's Prize column loses 35px (564 → 529, −6.2%).** It truncates at a word boundary to one measured line so it degrades gracefully, but the truncation rate on the cover board will rise by an amount nobody has measured against the 880 live titles. If it reads badly, the next 35px comes from the Closes column only after someone measures the longest real closing-date string.
- **The ≤8-glyph word cap rests on a MEAN advance.** §3.4 is explicit that a mean describes no real word, so an 8-glyph word of wide caps could still overflow 895px and a 9-glyph narrow word would fit. The cap is a design constraint on what §10.6a may author; the only gate is the render-time line-box measurement. It passes every string in today's table, so it will not fire on an ordinary run, but it is not a proof.
- **§3.4 carries two Bricolage 800 advances and §5 uses both.** The hero cap is derived at 0.6740em and the prize-name capacities at 0.6573em, because that is how the settlements published them. At 0.6740em the 56px step holds 23 glyphs per line rather than 24 and the truncator fires on more titles. §3.4 has to reconcile them; nothing in §5 changes direction either way.
- **The masthead does not currently fit.** Until §10.4 assigns a stamp form, the long form overlaps Slot A by 224.1px and §5.2's own rule turns that into a build failure on every run. This is the one thing in §5 that would stop a deck rendering today.
- **The full band appears on one slide in ten, and the green marker less often.** Combined with §5.6's category table — 3 of 45 in car-draws, 4 of 55 in sports-outdoors — the signature device is the minority case and on some days it renders once, clipped, with no marker. That is a real brand cost for an account building recognition from ~66 followers.
- **Within-slide comparison is gone and within-deck comparison is now digit count.** With one band per deck there is no second band. If the product owner values cross-slide height comparison above the photograph, the correct move is to delete the photograph from *every* draw slide — a §5 decision I have not taken on their behalf.
- **Slides 3+ close at exactly 1,050 of 1,050 with the photograph as the flex residual.** Any block added anywhere pushes the photograph below its 500px floor at 66px of new content, and three of §5's own retired candidates — a price chip, a Delta 1 kicker, an on-slide provenance line — are exactly that size.
- **The conditions band's L1 worst case is tight.** Adding the ticket price pushes it to roughly 49 characters; the 940 → 950 track gains it 10px. §5.3's measured-fit rule catches an overflow as a build failure on a legitimate draw. Measure before locking.
- **The closing slide discharges no field-5 obligation of its own**, and that rests on the compliance unit being the post rather than the child, on a surface §5.6 shows Instagram re-serves cold. The only fills available are a category word in deck L1 (measured dead: `10 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99` is 44 glyphs at 21.0909px = 928.0px, leaving 22.0px on the settled 950px track, and ` CAR` adds 84.4px → 1,012.4px, over by 62.4px) or the cover's board.
- **Slide 2 lost its statement of the day's angle.** Deleting Delta 1's kicker weakens the cold-entry case on the one slide Instagram auto-advances to.
- **The headline fit rule hard-fails the build**, and the `question` arm now runs at 47px of slack below the dateline on ~91 days a year. Nobody has generated a corpus of real headlines against the measured 895px box.
- **The cover's bottom-anchored model shows a large white gap at one headline line** (347px of slack), and the estimate that generators usually reach three lines rests on a handful of example strings, not a corpus.
- **The rule-9 residual clusters.** 49 of 880 live titles contain "AUTO DRAW" from a small number of operators, while `plan.mjs:69` draws backups from the same category pool.
- **Eight draws narrows category rotation.** The tier-1 bar rises to 12 rows in one category; home-garden (~17) and luxury (~19) will usually fail after a week of exclusions.
- **The 8-draw bet accepts a 2pp breakout-rate difference from a vendor that sells carousel generators**, on a metric that plausibly measures effort, and it can never be validated with PDD's own data. The mitigation is that reversal is one line.
- **22.2% standing chrome runs against the only hard measurement on chrome in the digest** (Verizon Media/Publicis: −12% ad memory when logos crowd the screen).
- **Adding rather than substituting the `:root` palette leaves two colour systems live in one stylesheet indefinitely.** Any future edit that "tidies up" `:root` re-creates the silent video breakage, and the class of failure needs a duplicate-property build assertion.
- **The scene-region areas depend on rects §5 supplies and heights §4.4 owns.** The draw slide's 241,645 px² currently reproduces §8's published figure only because the photo well's 65px growth and the odds rect's 65px shrinkage cancel exactly. That cancellation will not survive the next change to either, which is why the rects are parametric.
- **Several figures here were re-measured against the live DB minutes apart and moved** (>26 chars: 440 then 437; 493 then 483; inventory shifts hourly). Any threshold tuned to a single decimal place is tuned to noise.
- **This section's line-number citations are a decaying asset.** `select.mjs`'s adequacy bar is at line 40, not the line 29 the audit cites; `slice(0, n)` is at line 48; `.pill` is emitted at `render.mjs:62` and `:114`. Re-grep rather than trust the numbers.

## §6 — Reel template specification (verified, corrected)

## 6. Reel template specification

The Reel is not the roundup. Socialinsider (MEASURED — 35M posts / 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025) puts the 1–5K-follower median at 993 views for a carousel against 580 for a reel, and the advantage holds in every band. The carousel carries the inventory; the Reel's job is to be a readable, photo-dominant, loop-clean piece of top-of-funnel that survives Instagram's eligibility filters and sends a cold viewer to the profile. Everything below is sized to that job.

Two notes that govern every number in this section, both verified in repo:

- The Reel renders at `deviceScaleFactor: 1` into a 1080×1920 viewport (`carousel/capture.mjs:12`), so one CSS pixel is one output pixel. Every px value below is literal.
- The carousel renders a 1080×1350 CSS viewport at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` (`carousel/render.mjs:2`, `:187`) → a 2160×2700 PNG. Its CSS px are not output px, but both surfaces lay out on a 1080-px-wide canvas, so declarations on the two surfaces are directly comparable as fractions of canvas width.

**What this section does not own.** The type scale, the gutter (`--gutter: 65px`), the 950px chrome track and rules T1–T4 are §3.5's; the measured glyph advances are §3.4's. The odds device — its lattice, band width, ceiling, above-ceiling encoding and green-marker rule — is §4.4's and §4.7's, **and so is the E2 odds module and every block height inside it**. Every rendered odds string, every rendered headline string and the sign-off strapline are §10.6a's, emitted by `carousel/odds-copy.mjs`. The conditions band's field list, line strings, variant selection and type contract are §10.2's. Evidence, provenance and the dated stamp's wording are §10.4's. Deck size is §5.11's. The per-category scene is §8.3's and §8.5's. `audioMood` — including `FALLBACK`'s — is §8.7's. §6 states geometry, the frame budget, duration, the reading budget, the loop and the build-time assertions, and references the rest by name.

---

### 6.1 Canvas and the safe-geometry assertion

Canvas: **1080 × 1920**, unchanged.

| Box | x | y | w | h | CSS equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SAFE BOX A** | 65 … 1015 | 269 … 1152 | 950 | 883 | `left:6% right:6% top:14% bottom:40%` |
| **COVER BOX** | 65 … 1015 | 285 … 1152 | 950 | 867 | Box A with a 16px tighter top edge |
| **L-NOTCH (exclusion)** | 853 … 1080 | 1152 … 1920 | 227 | 768 | the action rail |

Box A's 950px width is §3.5's chrome track to the pixel — 1080 − 2 × 65 = 950 = 1015 − 65, x 65 … 1015 — so the still and the Reel lay out against one constant and §6 publishes no track of its own.

Provenance: **DERIVED**, not official. The box outline comes from Meta's 9:16 safe-zone diagram (`facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490`, diagram asset version timestamp 10 Feb 2026), measured by edge detection — that part is a measurement. The choice of the **40% bottom variant rather than 35%** is an inference, and §7.1 is right to flag it: Meta's "disclaimer" category generally means an ad disclaimer, and whether it covers a CAP 8.17 significant-conditions line is not established. PDD adopts 40% conservatively because the cost of being wrong in the safe direction is 96px of layout, and the cost of being wrong in the unsafe direction is a conditions line that is absent on a tall phone. Cite the box as DERIVED wherever it appears.

**This is a build-time assertion, not a guideline.** The justification is in Meta's own prose on the same page: on phones taller than 9:16 Meta may zoom-to-fill, "which can crop areas outside the safe zone". An element outside Box A is not merely sat under some UI on some devices — it can be *absent*. A guideline cannot protect a field whose absence is a regulatory failure (the closing date) or a distribution failure (the odds).

**The assertion, precisely.** Every DOM node in the timeline carries `data-pdd-meaning`, defaulting to `true`. The build fails — no MP4 is produced, no publish payload is emitted — if, on **any captured frame**, a node with `data-pdd-meaning="true"` whose computed `opacity > 0.05` and `visibility: visible`:

1. has a `getBoundingClientRect()` not wholly inside **x 65 … 1015, y 269 … 1152**, evaluated conservatively against subpixel rects: `Math.floor(left) ≥ 65`, `Math.ceil(right) ≤ 1015`, `Math.floor(top) ≥ 269`, `Math.ceil(bottom) ≤ 1152`; or
2. intersects the L-notch **x 853 … 1080, y 1152 … 1920**; or
3. has a computed `font-size` below §3.5's video floor — **except** nodes inside the conditions band, whose floor §10.2 owns and which §6 does not restate; or
4. is itself, or has an ancestor, under a transform whose resolved scale factor is **< 1.0** — because `getBoundingClientRect()` reflects transforms but `font-size` does not, so a floor-size glyph inside a `scale(0.5)` entrance renders at half and would otherwise pass rule 3; or
5. overflows its allotted row, tested as `scrollWidth > clientWidth` on the row's text container — **not** on the rect, because the insert clips (see §6.3) and a clipped overflow produces a rect that lies. The build fails rather than shrinking type to fit. The one exception is Row B's prize title, which truncates at a measured boundary under §6.5's rule and records the truncation rather than failing.

Two further assertions, both constants rather than content-dependent:

6. **`chrome_area ≤ 32% of frame`** on every captured frame (§6.3 derives 31.615% at the expanded state; 32% of 1920 = 614.4px). The ceiling moved from 29% because §4.4's E2 module is stacked on every surface and Row C is 256px, not 195px; the arithmetic and the cost are in §6.3, and the ceiling is renegotiated rather than adjusted whenever a line is added.
7. §3.5's T1–T4 are asserted by `assertTypeContract()`, not by §6. T2 is an **upper bound** — `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame, zero legal — and §6's contribution is that the Reel's card frames carry **no `--fs-hero` node at all**; the one `--fs-hero` node this surface may carry is the open-window headline (§6.4), and it is absent from every card frame.

During the **open window** (t = 0 to the end of the open beats, §6.4) rule 1 tightens to the COVER BOX: **y 285 … 1152**.

**A consequence the spec must own: the assertion runs on every frame, not the settled frame.** No meaning-carrying element may therefore *travel in* from outside Box A. The current template violates this everywhere — `rl-kick` (`reel-template.mjs:264`) enters from `translateY(90px)`, `rl-lower3` (`:295`) from `translateY(340px)`, `rl-gslam` (`:253`) from `scale(2.4) rotate(-5deg)`, applied by `.gslam` at `:252`. The insert system in §6.3 is compatible by construction: rows sit at their final coordinates from t = 0 and are revealed by the chrome block's own height animation under `overflow: hidden`. A clipped node keeps its rect at the final position, so it passes rule 1 while invisible, which is the correct behaviour. The open-window headline is likewise fixed in place and revealed and withdrawn by opacity alone.

Two tiers, and the tiering is the whole design:

- **Decoration may bleed; meaning may not.** The chrome bands run full-bleed `x 0 … 1080` so they read as bands rather than as a frame around the video — Instagram's Ranking Explained (OFFICIAL, about.instagram.com, 31 May 2023) makes reels "less visible" for, among other things, reels that "contain borders". Their *contents* are inset to `x 65 … 1015`. The top rail's ground starts at y 269, but its 50px line box is vertically centred in the 116px band — (116 − 50) ÷ 2 = 33 — landing at **y 302 … 352**, inside the COVER BOX without the band having to start at 285.
- **Exemption is explicit and fail-closed.** A node is exempt only by carrying `data-pdd-meaning="false"`. An element added later without thought is asserted, not excused. The current template has no such default, which is how ten separate elements ended up outside the safe area without anything noticing.

**The one categorical exemption, and its guard.** §8.3's scene module grants `data-pdd-meaning="false"` to the `#scene-back` and `#scene-front` subtrees as a whole, so the scene lanes may bleed to x 0 … 1080 exactly as the chrome grounds do. The exemption is bounded by a build check that §6 owns: **a node inside either subtree that contains a text node, or whose computed style resolves a `content:` string, fails the build.** A scene that acquires a glyph has stopped being decoration, and nothing else in the assertion would catch it.

**Two razor edges, closed with a guard.** Box A's floor is y 1152 and the notch's ceiling is y 1152; the conditions band's ground also ends at y 1152 while its contents run to x 1015, which is inside the notch's x-range. Neither intersects, but both are exact-touch, and one subpixel rounding puts a conditions line under the action rail. Therefore: **the conditions band's text content bottom is y 1150 or above, not 1152** — a 2px guard band. §10.2's 9:16 band is 5 + 135 + 5 = 145px at y 1007 … 1152, so its text bottom lands at y 1147 and clears the guard by 3px. With that guard, any node passing rule 1 passes rule 2 automatically.

Rule 2 therefore bites on exactly one thing: **the full-bleed photograph and whatever is burned into it** — operator watermarks, price stickers, "-15%" flashes, the loud marketing collages named as known weakness (c) in the approved direction. The asset normaliser (§9) must place the prize's identifying subject, and any burned-in text, clear of x 853 … 1080 × y 1152 … 1920. That is a crop constraint the normaliser can honour and this template cannot fix after the fact.

---

| Element | file:line | Current box | Why it fails | New position |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**The photograph is not bounded to a plate.** This closes the question the audit opened against §8: a photograph inset on all four sides with a visible ground around it *is* the border Instagram demotes, and it is exactly the `.pcard` this table deletes. The per-category scene therefore does not live around the photograph; it lives inside chrome that is already opaque and already paid for, per §8.3's scene lanes (§6.3).

**The ten sub-floor declarations, resolved.** `reel-template.mjs` carries exactly ten font-size declarations below §3.5's video floor — enumerated exhaustively from the file this session, not sampled: `.fc-labels b` 24 (`:124`), `.rfoot` 24 (`:395`), `.win-tab` 27 (`:192`), `.l3-line` 27 (`:300`), `.scenekick` 30 (`:256`), `.urgechip` 31 (`:372`), `.cd-kick` inline 33 (`:681`), `.rl-closes` 34 (`:269`), `.l3-handle` 36 (`:299`), `.rl-pill` 37 (`:275`). **Five are deleted outright and five are relocated** and re-set to a legal §3.5 step (see §6.6).

**The hierarchy defect is identical to the carousel's.** `.rl-closes` renders the odds at **34px** (`:269`) while `.rl-title` renders the prize name at **106px** (`:245`) — a ratio of **0.32 : 1** against the one datum no operator publishes. The carousel's equivalent is `.closes` 33px (`styles.css:358`) against `.prize` 98px (`:346`), 0.34 : 1. The new card sets the odds figure at §3.5's `--fs-figure` against a `--fs-lead` title: **120 : 56 = 2.14 : 1** (both values §3.5's, quoted here only to show the arithmetic), an inversion of **6.7×**.
