### 6.3 The insert system

**One persistent chrome. It expands, holds, swaps and collapses. It never cuts between layouts.**

Three permanent pieces plus two scene mounts, present on every frame of every reel:

| Piece | x | y | h | Ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Top rail** | 0 … 1080 (contents 65 … 1015) | 269 … 385 | 116 | Rail blue `#14385F`, opaque |
| **Insert card rows** | 0 … 1080 (contents 65 … 1015) | **661 … 1007** *(expanded)* / h 0 *(collapsed)* | **346** / 0 | Newsprint `#F7F5F0` |
| **Conditions band** | 0 … 1080 (contents 65 … 1015, text bottom y 1147) | 1007 … 1152 | 145 | Rail blue `#14385F`, opaque. Content, strings, variant and type: **§10.2** |
| **Scene lane R** *(decoration)* | 0 … 1080 | 269 … 385 | 116 | = the top-rail rect. §8.3 is normative for what renders in it |
| **Scene lane C** *(decoration)* | 0 … 1080 | **661 … 1007** | **346** | = the union of the newsprint rows. §8.3 is normative for what renders in it |

**This table is the sole normative source for both lane rects.** §8 transcludes them and prints no lane literal of its own, per the scene-geometry ruling; when a row moves here, the lane moves with it mechanically and every §8 figure derived from it re-derives. That is the whole mechanism, and it has now fired twice: §8.3's original y 700 … 1048 was a four-row card, its corrected y 722 … 1007 was the 285px two-row card at §3.5's type sizes, and the ruling that E2 is stacked on every surface takes Row C from 195px to 256px and the union to **y 661 … 1007, h 346**. Lane areas: R = 1080 × 116 = 125,280 px² = **6.042%** of frame; C = 1080 × 346 = **373,680 px²** = **18.021%**; 498,960 px² = **24.063%** combined when expanded. All of it is already counted as chrome below, so the scene adds no opaque area and moves none of §6's constants. §8.8's G6 clause 1 pins the fixture card to **y 661 … 1007**, not 722 and not 735.

Between y 385 and the top of the expanded insert there is a guaranteed clear window of **276px minimum** (y 385 … 661) and **622px** when the insert is collapsed (y 385 … 1007). That window is not a lane and carries no scene. It is not a box you place things in; it is the photograph's — with the two exceptions this section names explicitly, the counter chip and the open-window headline, both of which are transparent-ground elements and neither of which adds chrome area.

The block grows upward from a fixed floor at y 1007 under `overflow: hidden`, so the rows are revealed rather than flown in (§6.1).

**Roles, and where they are written.** Every frame this surface emits declares one of §10.2's eight `data-pdd-role` values: `reel-open` for the open-window frames and for the whole of `reel-cover-9x16`, `reel-card` for the card frames, `reel-signoff` for the sign-off. The Reel is one document with every scene stacked under opacity keyframes (`reel-template.mjs:2`), so `<body>` cannot carry a per-frame role: `window.__seek(t)` — already called at `capture.mjs:21` — returns `{ t, role, drawIndex }` derived from §6.4's beat table, and the gate reads that rather than inferring a role from computed opacity. The Reel cover is a separate document (`reel.mjs:63` `buildCoverHtml()`), so it writes `data-pdd-role="reel-open"` on `<body>` at the point `reel.mjs:101` already writes `data-theme`; `reel-template.mjs:778` is the equivalent site in the timeline document. All four file:line sites were re-read this session. `buildCoverHtml()` builds no insert card, so the cover's `sceneLanes` is `[R]` and it carries no card-lane scene — stated here because §6 owns the rect that would otherwise be assumed.

**The band's variant follows the role, not a prose list.** §10.2's draw variant renders iff `DRAW_CARRYING.has(role)`; the open window, the sign-off and the Reel cover are all `reel-open`/`reel-signoff` and therefore all render the deck variant, with L1's amber caution state, L2's entry host and L3's four free-entry states all rendered in their deck forms. §6 states no band string.

**A weight constraint the repo imposes.** `carousel/assets/fonts/` bundles Bricolage Grotesque 400/700/800, Inter 400/500/600/700 and **JetBrains Mono 700** — plus the legacy display faces the current template still uses (Anton, Bungee, Fraunces, Oswald 500/600/700, Playfair, Space Grotesk, which is why `.rfoot` is Oswald 600). **There is no Mono 400 or 500 woff2** — re-verified by directory listing this session: 17 files, one Mono weight. Every Mono setting below is therefore **JetBrains Mono 700**. If the approved direction's Mono 400/500 are wanted, the woff2 files must be added to that directory and registered in `carousel/fonts.mjs` first; §6 does not assume they exist.

**Measurement, not estimation.** Every width in this section was measured from the bundled woff2 files with fontTools, by summing real glyph advances over the real string. That method replaces the per-character em estimates the earlier draft used, and it also replaces the three disagreeing "mean uppercase advance" figures now in circulation for Inter 600 — 0.6602em (§10.2), 0.6782em (§3.5) and my own A–Z mean of 0.6946em. They disagree because they average different character sets, and all three are the wrong instrument: a real string contains spaces (0.2520em) and digits (mean 0.6116em), so any A–Z mean overstates it. **§6 budgets by measured string sum, and the build measures at render and fails on overflow.**

**Top rail contents** (one line, 950px track):

| Slot | Content | Type | Colour | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| left, x 65 | `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY` | Bricolage Grotesque 800 at `--fs-label`, ls 1.5px | `#F7F5F0` | 418.35px + 22.5px tracking (15 glyphs × 1.5) = **440.85px** |
| right, to x 1015 | §10.4's **short** dated-stamp form, `READ 09:00` | JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-label` | Signal amber `#FFC53D` | 10 glyphs × 26.4px = **264.00px** |

The string changed from `CHECKED 09:00` because §10.4 owns the stamp and its wording law is explicit: `read from` is the only permitted verb, the timestamp is mandatory, `verified` is forbidden, and the short form is the one assigned to the Reel and Reel-cover top-rail right slot. Every clearance below is re-derived from 264.00px; none was carried. The substitution frees 343.20 − 264.00 = **79.2px**, which is §10.4's own stated figure for the short form.

The stamp must be rendered from a stored verification timestamp in Europe/London, never a constant string. CAP 3.7 requires documentary evidence for objective claims to be held *before* publication; a "read at" stamp that is a hard-coded decoration is a claim without evidence. It is also unoccupied territory #7 from the teardown — no UK operator or directory publishes an accountability stamp as a design element. §10.4 now owns the field (`figures_checked_at`) and the string; §6 owns the slot. Note for the implementer that nothing in the carousel pipeline supplies this today: `carousel/freshness.mjs` reads `carousel_posts.posted_at` on a 36h dead-man's switch, which is a run-level liveness check, not a per-figure stamp.

**And the slot is the binding constraint on which string can go there.** The right slot runs from the wordmark's right edge plus a 24px minimum gap to x 1015: 1015 − (65 + 440.85 + 24) = **485.15px**, which at Mono 700 `--fs-label` (26.4px per glyph, exact — §3.5's step × a measured 0.600em) is **18 glyphs**. `READ 09:00` is 10 and fits with **221.15px spare** (it was 141.95px at the retired string). §10.4's long form, `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP`, is 34 glyphs and measures **897.60px** in Mono 700 — it does not fit the rail at any step legal on a video canvas. (The 42-glyph / 1,108.8px figure in circulation was measured on a longer string form and is withdrawn.) If the long form must render on the Reel it has to be a conditions-band line, which is §10.2's and §10.4's call; §6 supplies the measurement rather than the decision.

**Three consequences of the same measurement, all re-derived on the short stamp rather than carried.**

- **There is still no room for a category word in the rail.** §3.3 names the category word set in the rail band as carrier (a) of category identity. The free run inside the right slot is 485.15 − 264.00 = **221.15px**, and the shortest live category label (`TECH GIVEAWAYS`, 404.70px at Inter 600 `--fs-label`) is **183.55px** over it. **On the Reel, carrier (a) is withdrawn**; category identity on this surface is carried entirely by §8.3's scene lanes. §3.3 should record that the Reel supports only carrier (b). The shorter stamp widens the residual by 79.2px and does not change the verdict.
- **§8.3's rail mark slot M is still suppressed, but by 6.85px rather than by a 70.85px overlap — and the conclusion is now conditional, which it was not before.** Right-aligned to x 1015, the stamp's left edge is x 751.00; the measured wordmark ends at x 505.85; the free run between the two rail strings is **245.15px** (it was 165.95px). M is 220px wide and §8.3's own suppress-never-shrink rule wants 16px of clearance each side, so it needs 252px — **short by 6.85px**, i.e. a per-side clearance of (245.15 − 220) ÷ 2 = **12.575px** against a 16px requirement. Removing the wordmark's 1.5px letter-spacing recovers 22.5px, ends the wordmark at x 483.35 and opens the run to **267.65px**, at which M fits with 15.65px to spare and 23.825px of clearance per side. So M as *published* at x 435 … 655 overlaps the wordmark in every case (by 70.85px tracked, 48.35px untracked) and must be re-originated wherever it renders; whether it renders at all now turns on a tracking decision that is §3.4's. §6's contribution is the measured run at both settings; the redraw and the origin are §8.3's and §8.5's.
- **The face of the wordmark is not settled here.** §3.4/§3.6 set chrome in Inter 700 and this section renders Bricolage Grotesque 800. §3.4 owns it. The numbers so §3 can decide with arithmetic rather than taste: Bricolage 800 = 418.35px, Inter 700 = 427.71px, both at `--fs-label` before tracking. The choice costs 9.36px — and with the short stamp it is no longer inert, because at Inter 700 **tracked** (450.21px) the wordmark ends at x 515.21, the free run falls to **235.79px** and M is short by 16.21px, while **untracked** (427.71px) it ends at x 492.71, the run is **258.29px** and M fits by 6.29px with 19.145px of clearance per side. Under both faces the tracking decision, not the face, is the one that moves M — it is worth 22.5px against a 6.85px deficit, where the face is worth 9.36px.

**Expanded card rows**, two rows in 346px:

| Row | y | h | Contents | Type | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B** | 661 … 751 | 90 | Prize title, normalised, one measured line, box y 676…736. Carries `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"` | Bricolage Grotesque 700 at `--fs-lead` | `#14161A` on `#F7F5F0` |
| **C** | 751 … 1007 | **256** | **§4.4's E2 odds module, stacked**, occupying y 759 … 999, inside 8px of §10.2's row padding top and bottom. Every block height, gap and type step inside the module is §4.4's; every string is §10.6a's | §4.4's | §4.4's; the figure in verdict green `#0F6B45` |

Row B's internals are padded, not flush: 90 = 15 + 60 + 15. Row C is 8 + **§4.4's 240** + 8 = 256. **90 + 256 = 346**, and 661 + 346 = 1007.

**Row C is consumed, not specified.** The earlier draft laid E2 out as two lines in 195px — eyebrow label and sell-out conditional sharing one line above a figure — and argued the case on measured width (264.17 + 619.76 = 883.93px of 950px, a 66.07px gap). **That arrangement is retired**, and it is recorded as superseded rather than deleted silently, because the measurement behind it was sound and only the ruling changed. §4.4 is the sole owner of the E2 module and has ruled it stacked on every surface, at one height, with no surface parameter; §6.3 states the row height and the photograph window that funds it and states no eyebrow, figure, gap or conditional height of its own. The cost is **61px** (195 → 256) and it is paid entirely out of the clear photo window, which falls from 337px to 276px.

**What §6 still owns on this row is the horizontal fit, and all three runs clear the 950px track on their own lines**, left at x 65:

- eyebrow label `TICKET CAP` — 264.17px, 685.83px spare;
- figure, the bare ticket cap at ≤ 9 glyphs — **648.00px** exactly, 302.00px spare;
- sell-out conditional `1 IN 4,500,000 AT SELL-OUT` — 619.76px measured, 330.24px spare.

The stacked form is therefore horizontally comfortable; the constraint was only ever vertical, and §4.4's "the figure may never sit beside the conditional" (648.00 + 24 + 619.76 = 1,291.76px against a 950px track) is honoured by construction.

**Rows A and D are deleted, not squeezed.** Row A carried the counter and the closing date; Row D carried the price. The closing date and the price are CAP 8.17 significant conditions and now sit on §10.2's band L1, which is where they were always supposed to be. What remains of Row A is the counter, which is chrome, and it becomes a paper chip laid over the photograph at zero vertical cost.

**Counter chip.** §5.9's chip, at §4.4's **70px** row height — one step and one row height across all four surfaces, settled in §4.4's count-slide table, and §6 restates neither the step nor its decomposition. §6 states only its position on this surface and the width probe that proves it clears the notch: **x 65, y 405 … 475**, ink `#14161A` on `#F7F5F0`, 1px `--rule` border, 8px radius, 20px horizontal padding. Content is `DRAW <n> OF <drawsRendered>` per §5.11 — no deck-size digit is written here. Sized against a two-digit worst case as a width probe: `DRAW 10 OF 12` is 13 glyphs × 26.4 = 343.20px, so the chip is **383.2px wide, declared max 384px**, running x 65 … 449: inside Box A, inside the COVER BOX, inside the 276px clear photo window (405 sits 20px below the rail, 475 sits 186px above the card), and 404px clear of the L-notch.

**Why the figure is the bare cap.** `1 IN 4,500,000` at `--fs-figure` is 14 glyphs = 1,008px and does not fit the 950px track at all; `1 in 100,000` at the old 100px setting needed 720px against a 680px slot. Moving `1 IN` out of the figure and into §10.6a's conditional — where §4.4's stacked module already puts it — leaves the figure at ≤ 9 glyphs, which fits with 302px of headroom, and is also the better typographic answer: unoccupied territory #5 is a brand whose hero element is a beautifully set number. JetBrains Mono 700's advance is **exactly 0.600em** for digits, comma and sterling (hmtx 600 / upm 1000, measured), so 9 glyphs are **648.00px** and `4,500,000` — the measured maximum stored cap — is exactly 9 glyphs at exactly 648.00px. The build fails above 9 glyphs rather than shrinking; §10.6a drops the draw at 10+.

**Row B's cap is a glyph count, not a width guarantee.** At `--fs-lead` a real 22-glyph title measures 795.48px (`SAMSUNG GALAXY WATCH U`, from which Bricolage 700's uppercase mean derives as 795.48 ÷ 22 ÷ 56 = 0.6457em), but 22 glyphs of the widest uppercase in Bricolage 700 (W, 0.9860em) measure **1,214.75px** — **264.75px over the track**. The build measures the real string; where it overflows, §6.5's truncation rule fires rather than the assertion. Two related measurements: at `--fs-title` the same live title measures **965.94px and overflows the 950px track**, which is why §3.5 sets the Reel's title step at `--fs-lead` and why 68px is not available on this surface. **Row B stays one line**: a second line costs 60px, takes the card to 406px and chrome to 116 + 406 + 145 = **667px = 34.740%**, past §6.1 rule 6's 32% ceiling (614.4px) by 52.6px.

**Verdict green appears in Row C's figure and nowhere else in the Reel**, per the approved direction's "CHECKED FACTS ONLY" rule. **§6 states no eligibility gate of its own.** §10.4 makes provenance a PostgREST selection predicate inside `fetchEndingSoon` — a draw without a fresh source, timestamp and renderable method is never a candidate, so it cannot be dropped at render, cannot collapse a slot and cannot fail the Reel. The earlier draft's "fewer than three draws clear the gate, the Reel is not built" rule is retired: the Reel carries `min(N_bed, drawsRendered)` draws in deck order, where N_bed is §6.4's resolved count for the bed and `drawsRendered` is §5.11's. §5.11's `DRAWS_MIN` is at or above every N_bed in §6.4's table — the largest is 3 — so the minimum does not bind today, but it would if that floor ever fell, and that is the dependency, stated rather than assumed.

**The counter is the swipe/progression cue.** NN/g finds arrows signify *tapping* and are ignored; a numbered counter is the evidence-backed alternative. It is chrome, and §6.5 excludes it — and §10.6a's fixed eyebrow label — from the reading budget.

**The scene ground is resolved once per run, not once per card.** The card is one continuous mount across row swaps, so a ground that changed when a draw changed would paint and unpaint a translating field mid-loop — an entry animation, which §8.4 forbids outright. §6 therefore requires lane C's ground to be constant for the whole reel; the resolution grain (a deck-level reduction where §8.5's variants change the ground, rather than `variantOf(draw)`) is §8.3's to state, and the consequence of a gym-dominant sports deck rendering NEUTRAL throughout is §8.5's to accept or fix. §6's contribution is the constraint the mount imposes; it does not rule on another section's scene set.

**The conditions band is not §6's to fill.** §6 fixes the zone (x 0 … 1080, contents 65 … 1015, y 1007 … 1152, 145px = 5 + §10.2's 135px type block + 5), the 2px guard on its text bottom, its opacity and its non-suppressibility: **the render fails if the band is absent, empty, occluded by any other node, or if any of its lines overflows its measured track.** Its field list, its exact strings, its variant selection, its four free-entry states and its type size are §10.2's, and §6 restates none of them — which also disposes of the earlier draft's two hardcoded strings and its "≤ 36 characters per line" capacity claim.

That claim was wrong on its own terms, and no replacement capacity figure is safe either. §10.2's 0.6602em mean gives 32.7 uppercase characters on a 950px track at `--fs-label`; this section's own A–Z mean (0.6946em) gives 31.1; and the actual string `18+ · UK · ENTER ON OPERATOR SITE` measures **794.62px across 33 glyphs — 24.08px each, or 0.547em**, because the string is full of spaces, digits and middots. Every mean-uppercase capacity overstates a real line. It fitted by accident rather than by budget. It is moot now, because the line is §10.2's and neither string survives — §10.2's band names the entry host, folds the age condition into a pointer rather than asserting `18+`, and hedges the free-entry route rather than asserting one. Two breaches the earlier floor row carried are closed by deferring, not by rewording.

**The propagation rule has changed, and it is worse than it was.** §10.2's band is a 135px type block plus this surface's 5px padding. If §10.2 lands a fourth or fifth content line the band grows by 45px per line and the card's fixed floor moves up with it — but **Row C can no longer absorb the loss.** Row C is §4.4's E2 module at a fixed 240px in which no row is optional, so the growth is paid entirely out of the clear photo window and entirely in chrome. **One extra line takes chrome to 652px = 33.958% and already breaks §6.1 rule 6's 32% ceiling**, where under the old 195px Row C the first extra line was absorbable; two lines reach 697px = **36.302%**, and the clear photo window falls from 276px to 231px at one line and 186px at two. That is the propagation path; §6 does not pre-authorise it, and the first extra band line is now a ceiling renegotiation rather than a row adjustment.

**Sign-off card.** The closer reuses the same 661 … 1007 block rather than introducing a layout. All newsprint, three elements, 346px. It carries no `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node — it advertises no specific prize — and under §10.2's scoped field-5 assertion its absence is no violation of any class; a prize-name node appearing here would itself be class A (`prize-name-on-deck-asset`).

| Element | box y | h | Type | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| top padding | 661 … 669 | 8 | — | — |
| Strapline (§10.6a's string) | 669 … 719 | 50 | Inter 600 at `--fs-label`, `#5A5F66` | slot affords one measured 950px line |
| gap | 719 … 794 | 75 | — | — |
| `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY.CO.UK` | 794 … 864 | 70 | Bricolage Grotesque 800 at `--fs-title`, `#14161A` | **873.94px** |
| gap | 864 … 939 | 75 | — | — |
| `@prizedrawsdaily` | 939 … 999 | 60 | Inter 700 at `--fs-lead`, `#14385F` | **497.08px** |
| bottom padding | 999 … 1007 | 8 | — | — |

8 + 50 + 75 + 70 + 75 + 60 + 8 = 346. The paddings match Row C's 8px convention; the elements and paddings are 196px, so the 150px of residual the taller card frees is split equally between the two gaps at 75px each. The closer is the one card carrying no data, so air is the right place to spend it.

Three things the measurement settles here. The URL was set at 80px on an assumed 0.50em advance, needing "~840px"; the real advance puts it at **1,028.16px** (873.94 × 80 ÷ 68), which overflows the 950px track by 78.16px — `--fs-title` is the largest legal step that fits, at 873.94px with 76.06px spare. The strapline was `EVERY LIVE UK DRAW, CHECKED DAILY`, which does fit at 857.12px but makes an objective claim of exhaustive UK coverage PDD cannot evidence. **And its replacement, `UK PRIZE DRAWS, CHECKED DAILY`, is withdrawn too**: `DAILY` is a cadence claim of exactly the class §1.5 A11 already logs against `global.series.slotLine` ("every night · 7pm UK") as an objective claim under CAP 3.7 that was false within days of being rendered, and §10.4's own 48-hour freshness window exists precisely because daily is not achieved — a single datacenter-403 refusal jumps a figure's age to roughly 32h, against roughly 39 of 107 operators intermittently refused, and §1.4 records the pipeline 76 days dark. **§6 therefore publishes no strapline string.** The slot renders §10.6a's, inside its L1 allow-list and CI fixture so a predicate can see it, and the two banned forms are named above. For sizing: the withdrawn string measured 758.16px across 29 glyphs — 26.14px per glyph on that composition — so a replacement of roughly 36 glyphs of similar composition fits the 950px track (950 ÷ 26.14 = 36.3), and the build measures rather than counts.

**The motion argument.** A cut between per-draw layouts resets the viewer's spatial model every few seconds; they must re-find where the price is. An insert that expands in place keeps every field in the same slot for the whole reel, so from card 2 onward the viewer reads by position rather than by search — which is why §6.5's reading rate is a floor and not a target. Motion then creates temporary hierarchy: the only thing that moves is the thing that just changed. Today the opposite holds, and it is verifiable in four places — `reel-template.mjs:780` runs `rl-shakes` across the entire duration, `.bp` beat-pulses `infinite` (`:447`), the particle field runs `animation-iteration-count:infinite` (`:312–313`) and the light sweep loops every 4800ms (`:206`). When everything moves, nothing is emphasised. §8.3's rail lane is frozen at phase 0 for the same reason; only the card lane animates, and only while the card is open.

**The same structure is the "majority text" defence**, and this is the part a cut-based design cannot reproduce. Instagram's Ranking Explained (OFFICIAL, 31 May 2023) makes reels "less visible" if they are "majority text". The Recommendation Guidelines (OFFICIAL, `help.instagram.com/313829416281232`) separately exclude content "largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value" — which is what a daily auto-generated reel of other operators' photographs is, unless the added value is visibly on the frame. The two pull in opposite directions: show more data, but do not become text. A single persistent chrome with exactly two states resolves it with a constant:

| State | Chrome area | Photograph share |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed (116 + 145 = 261px full-bleed) | 13.594% | **86.406%** |
| Expanded (116 + **346** + 145 = **607px** full-bleed) | **31.615%** | **68.385%** |

**No frame of any reel is ever less than 68.385% photograph**, and that is assertable at build time because the chrome heights are constants, not content-sized: `chrome_area ≤ 32% of frame` is a number a build step can hold. Time-weighted over the 112 BPM configuration in §6.4 — 2 collapsed open beats = 1.0714s of 15.000s, 13.9286s expanded, travel frames ignored — it is **69.672%**: (1.0714 × 86.406 + 13.9286 × 68.385) ÷ 15.000 = (92.575 + 952.508) ÷ 15.000. The scene's own painted ink is a fraction of that again: its time-weighted canvas is **22.775%** of frame — (1.0714 × 6.042 + 13.9286 × 24.063) ÷ 15.000 — and, at §8.5's typical ~3% in-lane mean, **≈0.68% of frame is actually painted**. State the ink figure, not the canvas figure, whenever the majority-text defence is argued.

**These constants supersede every earlier set, and the reason is arithmetic, not disagreement.** §10.2's band ruling computed a 272px card (Row B 104 + Row C 168) and published `chrome_area ≤ 28%` with a 72.24% photograph floor (chrome 533px). §3.5's type ruling re-set the rows to 90 + 195 = 285px, giving 546px, a 28.438% share, a 71.563% floor and a 29% ceiling. §4.4's E2 ruling then set Row C to the stacked 240px module in a 256px row, giving 346px, **607px, 31.615% and a 68.385% floor**, under a 32% ceiling. §8.8 quotes this table; §10.2's 28% / 72.24% and the interim 29% / 71.563% are both retired, named here with their arithmetic so §8.8 updates rather than treating either as a competing claim. The defence cost **3.18 percentage points** of photograph (71.563 − 68.385) to put the odds module in one form on all four surfaces, and that is the trade, stated rather than absorbed.

The card geometry is **identical on every bed and every draw count** — there is no 3-field / 4-field variant and no per-bed row set — so the 68.385% floor holds regardless.

CAVEAT carried forward: Meta publishes no threshold for "majority text" and no definition of what it counts. 68.385% is an area calculation of opaque chrome, which is my own construction. If the classifier counts glyph coverage rather than band area, the figure is conservative.

### 6.4 Duration and the open window

The Instagram Reels Chaining system card (OFFICIAL, `transparency.meta.com/features/explaining-ranking/ig-reels-chaining/`, updated 11 Nov 2025) discloses nine prediction heads, including an abandonment head (watch under 3 seconds, dismissals, skip rate, sound-on views) and — the operative disclosure — **watch duration measured relative to peer reels of similar length**. You are compared inside your own length cohort. "Longer banks more seconds" is wrong and "shorter wins on completion" is not automatic. **Pick the length the content genuinely fills, and beat that cohort. Never pad.**

Today's template does the opposite in two ways, both verified in repo:

- `reel-template.mjs:700–702` sets the duration by arm: `A` = `min(18000, max(14000, coldEnd + N×2600 + 2400))`, `B` = 7500, `C` = 10000. `reel.mjs:181–182` rotates the arm by day-of-year. **The account therefore scatters itself across three different length cohorts on a three-day cycle**, and can never accumulate a record in any of them.
- Arm A pads. With 3 draws the raw length computes to 12,200ms, is floored up to 14,000ms, and `reel-template.mjs:720` sets `nScenes = max(N, ceil(M / 3000))` where `M = repriseStart − coldEnd ≈ 11,600ms — which for N = 3 yields 4` — while `:731` fills them with `slides[i % N]`. The same draw is shown twice to reach a duration the content does not fill. That is the padding the system card penalises.

**The replacement mechanism.** One structure, no arms. Duration is an *output*:

1. `readFloor = charBudget ÷ 20` seconds (§6.5).
2. `holdBeats = ceil((readFloor + 0.20) ÷ beatSec)`, where 0.20s is the row-swap during which the card is not readable.
3. `openBeats = 2`.
4. `signOffBeats` = the smallest value in **3 … 7** that makes `openBeats + N×holdBeats + signOffBeats` a **multiple of 4** (one bar), so the loop seam lands on a bar line, not merely a beat. The floor is 3, not 2, because §10.1 samples three frames per role run and §6.8's loop restore reclaims the last two beats for the `reel-open` role — at 2 the sign-off run is zero beats long and has no sampling window at all. If a future bed's smallest legal value would be 2, the next is 6 (multiple-of-4 completion), costing 4 beats.
5. **Maximise N** subject to `total ≤ 16.0s`; then spend any surplus beats on a *richer field set* before spending them on a longer sign-off; then drop a draw if nothing fits.
6. **Hard assertions:** every card's hold ≥ its read floor; total ≤ 16.0s; total ≥ 8.0s.

The 12–16s band is an *expected output range*, not a gate. The gate is the read floor.

**The 3-beat sign-off floor is inert on the five resolved beds and is NOT free elsewhere — this is stated because the constraint arrived from §10.2's role ruling, not from §6, and its cost lands here.** The five resolved beds are 3, 4, 4, 5, 4, so nothing in the table below moves. But a sign-off of 2 was load-bearing in exactly two configurations, and both are now closed: `pop.mp3`'s four-draw arrangement at 40 beats (2 open + 4×9 hold + **2**) and the 112 BPM five-field arrangement at 28 beats (2 + 3×8 + **2**). Both are re-derived under the floor below. Anyone reading "verified inert" as "costless" would restore them and fail rule 4.

**Role runs.** The reel emits **N + 3** role runs, in order: `reel-open` (the 2 open beats) · `reel-card` × N (holdBeats each) · `reel-signoff` (signOffBeats − 2) · `reel-open` again for the final 2 beats, because §6.8's loop restore reinstates frame 0's picture there and those frames are an open-window picture, not a sign-off picture. `window.__seek(t)` returns the role for a given t, derived from this same beat table rather than restated anywhere else, and §10.1 samples each run at `t_start + 300ms`, its midpoint and `t_end − 300ms` — a floor that clears the 200ms row-swap and the 270ms sign-off collapse.

**Rule 5's field-enrichment clause is inert in v1, and that must be said rather than implied.** §10.2's band ruling deleted Rows A and D, so the card has exactly two rows and no slot into which a fifth field could be spent. Surplus beats therefore go to the sign-off. Restoring a field row would cost 80px of chrome (607 → 687px = **35.781%**), which is 3.78 percentage points past §6.1 rule 6 as it now stands. That is a costed option, not a closed door, and it is more expensive than it was.

**The open window is a named scene, and it is where retention is actually won.** The benchmark this template is judged against is 65.50% skip within the first three seconds, and for the first two beats the frame is 86.406% photograph with no claim on it. That is not sufficient, and the earlier draft argued only for the opener's brevity, never for its content.

| Element | Geometry | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open headline | x 65 … 1015, bottom-anchored with a 40px gap above the band: bottom y 967; 1 line y 817…967, 2 lines y 667…967, 3 lines y 517…967 | Bricolage Grotesque 800 at `--fs-hero`, `#F7F5F0` | The **one `--fs-hero` node this surface may carry**. §3.5's T2 is an upper bound — `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1`, zero legal — which is what makes the card frames' zero legal rather than a departure |
| Scrim | x 0 … 1080, y 507 … 1007, `linear-gradient(rgba(20,22,26,0) → rgba(20,22,26,0.62))` | — | `data-pdd-meaning="false"`. Not opaque and edge-free, so it is not counted as chrome — declared as my construction, on the same footing as the 68.385% figure |

The headline's **string is §10.6a's**, drawn from its permitted headline forms and carrying no odds claim, because a `--fs-hero` node carries no qualifier in its own run (§10.6a rule 1.0). It is a **deck-level statement** — deck size, closing window, lowest cap — and therefore never repeats a draw shown later, which answers the question the audit asked about repetition.

Capacity, measured: Bricolage Grotesque 800's A–Z mean is **§3.4's 0.6740em**, so at `--fs-hero` (§3.5's 150px step) a glyph averages 101.1px and a 950px line holds **9 glyphs** (950 ÷ 101.1 = 9.396), giving a 3-line ceiling of **≈28 glyphs**. The build measures and fails on a fourth line. §10.6a's authoring cap of **≤ 8 glyphs per word** at `--fs-hero` is set against the still's 895px content well (8 × 101.1 = 808.8 ≤ 895; 9 = 909.9 > 895) and is therefore one glyph inside this surface's own line capacity — **it binds on the still and never on the Reel.** A second cap of nine glyphs is in circulation from the two-figure-test ruling; it was computed on the older 0.6573em advance (98.595px/glyph) against the retired 930/940px tracks, and since both 8 and 9 sit at or under this surface's 9-glyph line, the disagreement is inert here and is §10.6a's to close.

The single permitted `question` form, `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`, renders on this surface as `8 DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`: 26 characters greedy-wrapping to `8 DRAWS.` / `HOW MANY` / `TICKETS?`, three lines of 8 glyphs, 808.8px each against the 950px track with **141.2px of slack**, landing at y 517 … 967. Both of the strings it replaces are dead here, and for two different reasons: `HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?` greedy-wraps to **four** line boxes and cannot render under the 3-line ceiling at any candidate track, while `HOW MANY TICKETS?` wraps to two 8-glyph lines that fit comfortably and is banned solely for carrying no verified figure on the frame. Both are banned by name in §10.6a 1.3.

**How the open frame discharges §10.6 predicate 3, and the dependency that keeps it discharged.** Predicate 3 fires on any rendered unit containing `?` and requires two figures with distinct fact keys; on this surface the unit is the frame's own model text, and **the Reel has no generated proof line** — the proof-line unit rule is the cover's, not this surface's. The headline alone carries one key (`drawsRendered`). It passes because the conditions band is on **every** frame of every reel by §6.3's non-suppressibility rule, and on a `reel-open` role the band renders §10.2's deck variant, whose L1 carries the deck count and the lowest ticket price — keys {`drawsRendered`, `prices`} = 2 distinct. **The dependency is exact: if §10.2's deck L1 ever drops its price run, the `question` archetype becomes unrenderable on the Reel**, because there is no vertical budget for a proof element and the headline cannot honestly carry two figures at `--fs-hero` (the shortest legible two-figure line, `8 DRAWS. 699`, is 12 glyphs = 1,213.2px against a 950px track). §6 records the measurement and raises the dependency as an open question; the string set and the predicate are §10.6a's and §10.6's.

Contrast, computed: `#F7F5F0` (relative luminance 0.9137) over the scrim at its darkest point, over a pure-white photograph — the worst case — composites to `#6D6F71` = (109, 111, 113), relative luminance 0.1582, giving **4.63:1**. That clears WCAG AAA-large (4.5:1) at a 150px glyph, with 0.13 of ratio to spare. Over any darker photograph it improves.

The headline reaches opacity 0 on the first frame of the card's expand and is never occluded. It returns over the final two beats alongside the photograph's cross-dissolve, because §6.8's loop assertion requires the last frame to be frame 0's picture — which also means **the counter chip must reset to `DRAW 1 OF <drawsRendered>` during the closing collapse.** Both are loop requirements the earlier draft missed, and both are why those two beats carry the `reel-open` role.

Beat lengths come from `carousel/assets/audio/manifest.json`, which stores a measured `bpm` and `firstBeatOffsetMs` per bed (both fields verified present on all six musical entries this session; three of the six offsets are 0). Resolved configurations at the **68-glyph four-field floor** (§6.5 → 3.40s read floor → 3.60s hold requirement):

| Bed | BPM | Beat | Categories (live inventory) | Draws | Hold | Open | Sign-off | Beats | **Duration** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `elegant.mp3` | 81 | 740.741ms | luxury (64) | 3 | 5 beats / 3.704s | 2 | 3 | 20 | **14.815s** |
| `win.mp3` | 99 | 606.061ms | cash-prizes (351), **sports-outdoors (102)** | 3 | 6 / 3.636s | 2 | 4 | 24 | **14.545s** |
| `warm.mp3` | 103 | 582.524ms | house-draws (0 live), **home-garden (45)** | **2** | 7 / 4.078s | 2 | 4 | 20 | **11.650s** |
| `driving.mp3` / `synth.mp3` | 112 | 535.714ms | car-draws (81), tech-giveaways (157) | 3 | 7 / 3.750s | 2 | 5 | 28 | **15.000s** |
| `pop.mp3` | 152 | 394.737ms | collectibles (97) | 3 | 10 / 3.947s | 2 | 4 | 36 | **14.211s** |

The Categories column is §8.7's assignment, not §6's: `win` gains sports-outdoors and `warm` gains home-garden under the config-schema ruling, and every `audioMood` — including `FALLBACK`'s — is §8.7's to publish. §6 owns the beat arithmetic and nothing else in that column.

**This table has moved once, and the cause is §10.3, not a change of mind.** The earlier draft budgeted the closing date at 14 glyphs on `CLOSES SUN 9PM`. §10.3 measures that `lib/parse.mjs` manufactures a 20:00 time at four sites when the operator's page prints none, with nothing recording the substitution, and forbids any time-of-day claim in v1. The date-only form is longer, and the price run's worst case is longer than the draft's `£2.50 A TICKET`. The floor rises from 59 to 68 glyphs, which pushes `driving`/`synth` from 4 draws to 3, `pop` from 4 to 3, and `warm` from 3 to 2.

**The table is sensitive to §10.2's band strings, and the sensitivity is worth publishing — but it is not symmetric, and the earlier "one glyph either way" framing was wrong.** The two band-carried runs are §10.2's to finalise. Re-derived under rule 4's 3-beat sign-off floor:

- At **≤ 65 glyphs**, `warm` (103) returns to **3 draws** / 6-beat hold / 24 beats / **13.981s**. At 103 BPM, 6 beats measure 3,495.1ms against a 3.60s requirement — short by 104.9ms — and the 7th beat is what costs the third draw. **This is the genuine one-glyph-class recovery**, and if §10.2's L1 resolves the close to §10.3's 17-glyph absolute form (`CLOSES SUN 21 SEP`) rather than a 21-glyph relative form, the floor lands at 64 and this row recovers.
- **`pop`'s fourth draw is not one glyph away, and the claim that it was is withdrawn.** At ≤ 67 glyphs pop's hold does drop from 10 beats to 9, but N stays at **3** (2 + 27 + 3 = 32 beats = 12.632s); the four-draw arrangement needs 2 + 4×9 + signOff ≡ 0 (mod 4), and the only completion in 3 … 7 is 6, giving 44 beats = **17.368s**, past the 16.0s ceiling by 1.368s. The 40-beat / 15.789s configuration that made the old claim true required a **2-beat** sign-off and is closed by rule 4's floor. Pop's fourth draw now requires the hold to fall to 8 beats, i.e. a read floor ≤ 2.958s, i.e. **≤ 59 glyphs**, at which 2 + 32 + 6 = 40 beats = 15.789s. That is a nine-glyph cut from today's floor, not one.
- No other bed changes draw count anywhere in 64 … 68 glyphs.

**`warm.mp3` is now a live configuration, not a mechanism check.** The earlier draft excused its 2-draw row on the ground that `config.json` assigned it only to house-draws, which has zero enterable inventory. §8.7's schema ruling assigns it to **home-garden (45 draws)** as well — the only domestic bed in the manifest — so the thinnest configuration in the system ships for a real category. The arithmetic that forces it: at a 7-beat hold, N = 3 is 2 + 21 = 23 beats, and the smallest legal sign-off completing a bar is 5, giving **28 beats × 582.524ms = 16,310.7ms = 16.311s**, which breaks the 16.0s ceiling by **310.7ms**. 27 beats is not a whole bar, so there is no intermediate. Home-garden Reels therefore carry **2 draws / 20 beats / 11.650s** until §10.2's band L1 lands at ≤ 65 glyphs. It is a bounded, one-glyph-away cost on the thinnest of the eight categories, and it is stated rather than excused.

**The five-field claim, corrected twice.** The earlier draft stated "no bed reaches a five-field card … in every case the resulting total exceeds 16.0s even at N = 3." **That was arithmetically false as published**: against the 59-glyph floor it assumed and the 2-beat sign-off then permitted, 112 BPM reached a five-field card at N = 3 in 28 beats / 15.000s and 152 BPM at N = 3 in 40 beats / 15.789s, both inside the ceiling. The false claim was load-bearing — it was the stated justification for dropping the operator name — so it is recorded rather than quietly repaired.

Re-derived at the corrected **86-glyph** five-field floor (4.30s read, 4.50s hold) and under rule 4's 3-beat sign-off floor, **every bed falls to N = 2**: elegant 7/4/20 = 14.815s · win 8/6/24 = 14.545s · warm 8/6/24 = 13.981s · driving·synth 9/4/24 = 12.857s · pop 12/6/32 = 12.632s. At N = 3 the cheapest completions are 28 beats (81 BPM) = 20.741s, 32 (99) = 19.394s, 32 (103) = 18.641s, 32 (112) = 17.143s and 44 (152) = 17.368s — all past 16.0s. **The earlier draft's conclusion is therefore true again at the corrected floor, though its reasoning was wrong when written**, and the previously-published exception ("only 152 BPM reaches a five-field card at N = 3 … there the fifth field is free") is **withdrawn**: it depended on the 40-beat / 2-beat-sign-off arrangement rule 4 now forbids.

**The operator name still does not appear on the frame in v1, and now for three stated reasons rather than an impossibility claim that was false:** every bed loses a draw to carry it; §10.2's band ruling leaves no slot without adding a row and 80px of chrome; and CAP 8.17's how-to-participate condition is discharged on every frame by the entry host on §10.2's band L2 (draw-carrying roles) or its frozen deck-level equivalent, so the operator *brand name* is attribution rather than a significant condition. §5.13's "not a courtesy" framing is satisfied by the host, not by the brand. Attribution lives in the caption and in `out/alt.json`, the per-slide alt text the digest names as an existing E-E-A-T asset to preserve.

**Non-uniform pacing** (fast on photo-only beats, held on number beats) is deliberately *not* specified. The digest calls it the single most testable open question, and the mechanism above already supports it — `holdBeats` is per-card and can differ. A uniform hold is v1; the non-uniform variant is the first comparison to run once skip rate is captured. It must be labelled a sequential comparison, not a controlled test: Trial Reels require 200 followers for a professional account (OFFICIAL, `help.instagram.com/1013292530224018`) and @prizedrawsdaily is at ~66.

### 6.5 Field budget per card

The Netflix English Timed Text Style Guide specifies **20 characters per second** for adult subtitles and 42 characters per line, max 2 lines. Applied here it gives a floor, and the discipline it enforces is: **cut fields, not seconds.** Every on-frame run below is a single line under 42 characters, so the second Netflix constraint binds nowhere.

| Field | Glyph budget | Where it renders | Cuttable? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prize title (normalised) | 22 | Row B | **No** | CAP 8.17 — the nature of the prize. This is also the only carrier of "number and nature of prizes": PDD stores no prize count, and §10.2 rules that no count renders where none is stored |
| Ticket cap figure | 9 | Row C, §4.4's E2 | **No** | The entire added value; removing it re-exposes the reel to the Recommendation Guidelines' repurposed-content exclusion |
| Ticket price | 16 (`£129.99 A TICKET`) | §10.2 band L1 | **No** | The entry condition, and DMCC Act 2024 bans drip pricing — the headline price must be the real one |
| Closing date | 21 (`CLOSES TOMORROW (WED)`) | §10.2 band L1 | **No** | CAP 8.17 significant condition. **Date-only**: §10.3 forbids a time of day in v1 |
| Sell-out conditional | — (excluded, below) | Row C, §4.4's E2 | **No** | §10.6a places it at the top of the never-cut list, above price and cash alternative |
| Operator name | 18 | no slot in v1 | Yes | Attribution; the entry host discharges CAP 8.17 on band L2 |
| Cash alternative | 16 | no slot in v1 | Yes | Already capped by `honesty.mjs` `capValue()` (`:19`) |

| Configuration | Glyphs | Read floor | Hold requirement (+0.20s swap) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **4 fields** (floor, v1) | 68 | 3.40s | 3.60s |
| 5 fields (+ operator) | 86 | 4.30s | 4.50s |
| 6 fields (+ cash alt) | 102 | 5.10s | 5.30s |

The cut ladder is **6 → 5 → 4, and it stops at 4**. Below four fields the card no longer carries a significant condition the ASA expects to be in the post, so the correct move is to drop a *draw*, never a fifth field. In v1 the ladder never runs — the card has two rows and the band is non-suppressible, so every reel renders the four-field floor — but the ordering is stated so that a future slot cannot be filled in the wrong order.

**Price and closing date are counted although they render on the band.** The budget measures what a first-time viewer must read on the frame, not which box it sits in. The band's *structural* words (`Enter · terms ·`, the free-entry and age pointer), the entry host and the dated stamp are excluded, on the same ground as the counter: fixed position, fixed structure, unchanged across cards, near-zero re-read cost after the first, and the reel loops.

Four exclusions from the budget, all DESIGN JUDGEMENT and stated as such:

- The `DRAW n OF N` counter chip is chrome and positionally fixed.
- §10.6a's eyebrow label is likewise fixed and never changes across cards.
- **§10.6a's sell-out conditional.** Its structure is fixed and its only changing content is the cap digits, which restate the figure counted directly above it. This is the most convenient of the four exclusions and it is the one most likely to be wrong: it is a 26-glyph run that a viewer meets for the first time on card 1. **If it is counted, the floor becomes 94 glyphs → 4.70s → 4.90s hold, and every bed falls to 2 draws** (re-derived under rule 4: elegant 7/4/20 = 14.815s, win 9/4/24 = 14.545s, warm 9/4/24 = 13.981s, driving 10/6/28 = 15.000s, pop 13/4/32 = 12.632s; every N = 3 completion exceeds 16.0s). That is the single largest sensitivity in §6.4 and §6.5, and it is the same trade §10.2 records as its own residual risk 1.
- The Netflix rate is for continuous prose read while watching action. A repeating, positionally-fixed data card is read faster after the first instance. I have **not** discounted for this — the conservative rate is used throughout. If the first real skip-rate read shows no retention cost, a faster rate is the justified revision and a fourth draw follows on several beds.

**The 22-glyph title cap is a READING budget, and Row B truncates rather than failing.** The earlier rule — "the build fails on overflow rather than shrinking type; it does not truncate silently" — failed the build on the ordinary case: the measured median live title after `cleanTitle()` is **26 characters**, so over half of live inventory would have hard-failed every day. Row B therefore renders `cleanTitle()` truncated at a word boundary to whichever is smaller — **22 glyphs, or the measured 950px line at Bricolage 700 `--fs-lead`** — appending `…`; if the first word alone overflows, it truncates mid-word at the measured boundary. Truncation is a named counted record in `COMPLIANCE.json` (`prize-name-truncated: reel-card <slug> <n>→<m> glyphs`), **not** a failure class, and `out/alt.json` carries the untruncated title on every draw-carrying asset so the record is never lost.

**Holding the reading budget at 22 is what keeps §6.4's five-bed table unchanged**, and that is the reason not to raise it to the measured median. At 26 glyphs the floor rises to 72 → 3.60s read → 3.80s hold, and `elegant.mp3` (81 BPM) needs 6 hold beats: 2 + 18 + 4 = 24 beats = **17.778s**, past the 16.0s ceiling, dropping it to N = 2. The budget and the render cap are deliberately different numbers doing different jobs.

The truncation depends on the ingest-time normaliser stripping operator noise (known weakness (b): `NEW Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 #2`) for its quality, not for its safety — a bad normaliser now produces a poorer prize name, not a failed build. That is the correct failure mode on a surface carrying two to three draws, and it moves the risk from the pipeline to the copy, where §10.7's alt text and the truncation counter can both see it.

### 6.6 Type floor and hierarchy

**§3.5 owns the type scale, the gutter, the three floors and rules T1–T4. This section states none of them and restates no size.** What §6 consumes is the video floor, which §3.5 sets at `--fs-label`; the running-copy floor at `--fs-body`; and the rule that `--fs-micro` does not exist on a video canvas. §6's own contribution is the arithmetic that justifies a video floor distinct from a still's, and it survives: on a 1080-wide canvas rendered to a ~390 CSS-px-wide phone viewport (scale ≈ 0.361), `--fs-label` lands at ≈15.9 CSS px, the conventional body-text floor (DESIGN JUDGEMENT; the arithmetic is mine). A still can be pinch-zoomed and dwelt on indefinitely; a Reel frame can be paused but not zoomed and is on screen for ~3s. That is the whole of the difference, and it is one scale with a per-canvas floor rather than two scales.

The conditions band is a named exception to the video floor, owned by §10.2 and asserted through §6.1 rule 3's carve-out. §6 does not publish the band's size.

The relocations — five of the ten sub-floor declarations:

| Old | Old size | New home | New size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.rfoot` conditions | 24px | §10.2's conditions band | §10.2's |
| `.l3-line` strapline | 27px | Sign-off strapline | `--fs-label` |
| `.l3-handle` | 36px | Sign-off `@prizedrawsdaily` | `--fs-lead` |
| `.rl-pill` price | 37px | §10.2's band L1 | §10.2's |
| `.rl-closes` odds | 34px | **Row C, inside §4.4's E2** | §4.4's |

**The floor is met by deleting elements, never by shrinking type.** Verizon Media / Publicis (MEASURED — 5,616 US adults, fielded Apr 2019) found **−12% ad memory** when logos crowd the screen alongside captions. The other **five** of the ten sub-floor declarations are therefore deleted outright rather than resized — the flip-clock labels (`:124`), the win tab (`:192`), the scene-kick span (`:256`), the urgency chip (`:372`) and the countdown kicker's inline 33px (`:681`) — and the progress bar and the price-stamp furniture go with them, although neither carries a type declaration of its own.

**Hierarchy is a compliance surface, not taste.** CAP guidance, verbatim: "Promoters should ensure that the page design, layout or format of the promotion is not misleading. Promoters should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true." Setting the prize name at 106px and the odds at 34px is precisely that emphasis. The new ratio — §4.4's figure step against a title at `--fs-lead`, **120 : 56 = 2.14 : 1** (both values §3.5's, quoted only to show the arithmetic) — is the only hierarchy that is both compliant and, per the Recommendation Guidelines, visibly value-adding.

**The Reel carries the numeral only. There is no dot grid on this surface, and no bar.** The earlier draft allotted the device a 240 × 120px slot at x 775 … 1015, y 828 … 948. **That slot is deleted**, its width returns to Row C's track, and §4.4's band does not replace it. Three reasons, each arithmetic and each in this section's own terms:

1. **There is no vertical room that is not the photograph's.** The only free window inside Box A is the clear photo window, now y 385 … 661 = **276px**, and §6.3 assigns it to the photograph. Putting a band there does not add a band; it replaces the photograph with one.
2. **There is no chrome budget, and there is less of it than there was.** §6.1 rule 6 caps chrome at 32% of frame = 614.4px. Chrome is 607px. **The frame has 7.4px of unallocated chrome height** — down from 10.8px under the 195px Row C and the 29% ceiling. No band at any specification in §4.4 fits in 7.4px, and the 32% ceiling is the spec's only quantified defence against the majority-text demotion — a rule that *is* written about reels.
3. **A 240 × 120 slot cannot hold an honest reduced encoding.** At the finest lattice that survives H.264 at this scale (6px dot, 2px gap, 8px pitch) it holds 30 × 15 = **450 cells**. Showing 450 cells against the measured maximum cap of 4,500,000 — or against a typical four-figure cap — is a picture orders of magnitude more favourable than the fact, which is the CAP page-design failure the no-green-dot rule in §4.7 exists to prevent. There is no named reduced encoding here because none is honest.

The device's ceiling, its above-ceiling encoding and its green-marker rule are **§4.7's**, and §6 restates no ceiling value, no row count and no fallback. What carries the comparison on this surface is the digit count of the tabular figure — which is exactly the fallback §4.7 already argues for above the ceiling, so the argument is consistent rather than improvised. What is given up is unoccupied territory #6 (nobody in the category has made odds *visual*), and that loss is recorded in the risks rather than hidden.

### 6.7 Encode

Current state, verified this session: `reel.mjs:18` sets `FPS = 30` (and `reel-template.mjs:51` mirrors it); `encode.mjs:28–32` passes `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v high -g fps*2 -flags +cgop -r fps` (the codec flags are on `:30`) with **no `-crf` flag at all** — a `grep crf encode.mjs` returns nothing — so the stream is encoded at x264's default **CRF 23**.

| Parameter | Now | New | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame rate | 30fps | **30fps — held** | The earlier draft moved to 60fps on Instagram's 9 Apr 2026 creator guidance (OFFICIAL), which asks for 2K / HDR / 60fps exports and names 30fps only as the minimum. It is withdrawn. 60fps doubles a 15.0s reel from 450 to 900 frames against `capture.mjs:20`'s fixed `5 * 60000`ms budget, and §8's scene lane rasterises a clipped transform-animated field on every one of them — so the guidance bought a smoother 0.33s insert travel at the price of making a budget change in another file a hard prerequisite, on the account's secondary format (580 median views against the carousel's 993). Revisit only if §11's skip-rate readings show abandonment inside the insert travel |
| Rate control | implicit CRF 23 | **CRF 18** (19 permitted when the frame is photo-dominant and the file would otherwise be large) | The chrome is large flat fields of newsprint `#F7F5F0` and rail blue `#14385F` with hard type edges — exactly the content x264 smears at CRF 23 (ringing on glyph edges, banding across the flat grounds). The scene lanes make this sharper still: §8.3's rail lane paints at a luminance delta of 0.0155, which is the first thing a quantiser discards. Instagram then re-encodes on top, and Ranking Explained makes **low-resolution** reels less visible (OFFICIAL), so the upload should hand Instagram the cleanest available source. The *direction* is standard x264 practice for synthetic graphics; the exact value 18 is DESIGN JUDGEMENT, not a measured PDD result |
| GOP | `-g fps*2` | unchanged (`-g 60` at 30fps) | Keeps the 2-second GOP |
| Everything else | `yuv420p`, `profile:v high`, `+cgop`, `+faststart`, AAC 48kHz 160k | unchanged | Already correct |

**`assertVideoContract()` gains one check, records two values and tightens one.** It currently verifies codec, pixel format, dimensions, audio codec, sample rate, duration and moov position (`encode.mjs:36–52`) — but **never the frame rate**. Add: `r_frame_rate === "30/1"` — the value asserted is the value shipped, and the check is one line that catches a silent FPS drift in either direction. Tighten: `maxDurS` from the 20 passed at `reel.mjs:265` to **16.0**, matching §6.4's ceiling. **No file-size assertion ships yet** — the Content Publishing API's Reels size ceiling is not in the research digest, and asserting an invented number is worse than asserting none. Instead the contract *records* `bytes` and `bitrate` into the publish payload so the ceiling can be set from real data once sourced.

**The capture budget leaves the critical path but does not leave the risk register.** At 30fps a 15.0s reel is 450 frames, which `capture.mjs:20`'s fixed `5 * 60000`ms budget accommodates today at an observed screenshot cost in the low hundreds of milliseconds. What is new is per-frame cost, not frame count: §8.3's lane C rasterises a clipped, transform-animated field inside an already-animating `overflow:hidden` block on every expanded frame. Nobody has measured that cost, so the budget is a **watch item** — if the first real build trips it, the fix is to scale the budget with frame count, and the failure will look like a Playwright problem rather than a budget problem. This is the half of the 60fps risk that holding 30fps does not remove, and it is retained deliberately rather than dropped with the frame-rate change.

### 6.8 The loop rule, and the KPI correction

**The loop rule.** Frame 0 and the final frame must be the same picture: the insert collapsed to the conditions band, the top rail present with its scene lane static at phase 0, the open headline and its scrim at full opacity, the counter chip reading `DRAW 1 OF <drawsRendered>`, and draw 1's photograph behind. The closer therefore does four things in its last beats — collapses the sign-off insert back over 0.27s, cross-dissolves the photograph back to draw 1's over the final 2 beats, restores the headline and scrim, and resets the counter chip. Those final two beats carry the `reel-open` role, because the picture they restore is an open-window picture. Assertion: the first and last captured PNG must differ on fewer than 1.0% of pixels at a per-channel tolerance of 4/255 (DESIGN JUDGEMENT on the thresholds; the mechanism is a build step).

**This is the production seam, and it is clause 3 of §8.8's G6, not clause 1.** The only animated scene lane is lane C, which lives inside the insert card, and the card is collapsed on both frame 0 and the final frame — so lane C paints zero pixels at the seam. Lane R is static at phase 0 by §8.3's rule. **The 1.0%-pixel-diff assertion is therefore independent of any scene's `loopMs`**, and no scene loop period needs deriving from the beat grid on this surface. G6's own loop-closure clause (clause 1) runs on the `reel-9x16` **fixture** with the insert card pinned to its expanded height — **y 661 … 1007** under this section's current rows — over a flat NEUTRAL photograph ground, which is what makes it a comparison of two painted frames rather than a blank against a painted one. Its cover-parity clause (clause 2) compares fixture PNGs restricted to `reel-cover-9x16`'s declared lanes, which is `[R]` alone, because `reel.mjs:63` `buildCoverHtml()` builds no insert card — so the comparison is exact and complete rather than vacuous, and it is never run against the delivered `cover.jpg`, which `reel.mjs:246` writes as JPEG q90. The incommensurability between §8.5's 3,000–5,200ms loops and §6.4's 11.650–15.000s totals is real and has no effect on either.

The audio seam is clean **by construction**: the bed is trimmed to `firstBeatOffsetMs` (`reel.mjs:260`, correctly — `loudnorm` otherwise amplifies silent intros) and §6.4 forces the total to a whole number of **bars** measured from that first beat, so the loop point lands on a bar line. CAVEAT: the manifest stores `bpm` and `firstBeatOffsetMs` but no phrase length, so a 4-beat-multiple total guarantees rhythmic alignment, not harmonic alignment. A bed whose phrase is 8 or 16 bars will still step harmonically at the seam.

**The KPI correction — judge a loop ONLY on accounts reached and skip rate.** Instagram's own metric definitions (OFFICIAL, `help.instagram.com/202865988324236`) are unambiguous:

| Metric | Definition | Effect of a seamless loop |
|---|---|---|
| Views | "starts to play **or replay**" | **Inflated** |
| Watch time | **Includes replays** | **Inflated** |
| Average watch time | watch time (incl. replays) ÷ **initial** views | **Inflated** — the numerator counts replays, the denominator does not |
| Accounts reached | unique accounts | Not inflated |
| Skip rate | per-impression abandonment | Not inflated |

All three of the obvious video metrics are contaminated by the thing being tested. A loop that improves nothing will still raise views, watch time *and* average watch time. They may be logged as descriptive data; they must be **excluded from the loop's success criteria**. The criteria are reach and skip rate, and nothing else.

**And the pipeline cannot measure either of them today.** Verified this session: `insights.mjs` `mapPayload()` (`carousel/insights.mjs:21–59`) ingests only likes, comments, `ig_reach`, `fb_reactions`, `fb_comments`, `fb_shares`. Skip rate is absent entirely. More importantly, the `ig_reach` branch writes `media_id: "account"` (`insights.mjs:35–44`) — the pull it maps is the **account-level daily reach time-series**, not per-media reach, and `INSIGHTS.md:86–91` already warns that its Pacific-anchored `end_time` bucketing makes any arm-vs-reach comparison accurate to ±1 day at best. So the pipeline's only reach figure is the wrong reach figure for this decision. The loop's acceptance requires **per-media reach** from the media insights edge plus skip rate, which is available in-app on normal posts now and is the priority instrumentation ask.

Until both are captured, the loop ships on its design rationale and its measurement stays an open item — not on a views number that the loop itself produced.

### 6.9 The audio contract — unchanged

Keep it exactly as it is. It is already correct, and for structural reasons rather than preference:

- **Pixabay beds, always muxed.** `assertVideoContract()` hard-fails without an AAC stream (`encode.mjs:48`). Ranking Explained makes muted reels less visible (OFFICIAL), so a silent render must never be publishable.
- **Baked audio is not a choice.** The Content Publishing API for Reels has no parameter to attach Instagram library music, so an automated pipeline cannot use it. Meta's Music Guidelines (effective 26 Mar 2024) bind on *use*, not on account label — commercial and non-personal use of the library requires licences, and Creator-vs-Business switching does not change that. Every manifest entry carries a Pixabay Content License line, which is the correct footing. The trending-audio question is closed by construction, and "trending audio boosts reach" is FOLKLORE in any case: no official Meta statement supports it and the two largest benchmark datasets do not include audio as a variable, so no part of this section rests on it.
- **Precomputed BPM and `firstBeatOffsetMs` per bed**; `trimToOnsetMs = firstBeatOffsetMs` (`reel.mjs:260`). §6.4's entire duration mechanism is built on these fields, so they become load-bearing rather than decorative.
- **`loudnorm I=-16:TP=-1.5`, `amix`, `alimiter`, `apad`** — unchanged.
- **The stings re-point, the contract does not change.** They currently fire at `stampTimesMs` (`reel.mjs:262`), the price-stamp landings. There is no stamp any more, so they fire at each insert expand and each row swap. Same file, same mix, same assertion.
- **Design for sound off.** No information may exist only in the audio; the stings mark a change the eye can already see. Meta's own creative guidance says design for sound off, and the "80% of Reels viewed with sound on" figure is FOLKLORE — Meta's own sources contradict each other (a 2022 sales page says 80%; Mosseri in Jun 2024 says roughly half of watch time is sound-off). None is quoted here as settled, and no part of this template depends on the viewer hearing anything.

One correction for the record, re-verified this session: `dropMs` is `null` on **all seven** entries in `assets/audio/manifest.json`, so `reel-template.mjs:699`'s `audioMeta?.dropMs ?? 2000` has always resolved to 2000 and the inline comment "scene 1 lands on the drop when it's early enough" has never described real behaviour. §6.4's fixed 2-beat open removes the dead branch.

### 6.10 What this section does not decide, and the one thing it must

The odds device's lattice, band, ceiling, above-ceiling encoding, marker rule **and the E2 module's every block height** are **§4.4's and §4.7's**. Every rendered string — the open headline, the odds runs and the sign-off strapline — is **§10.6a's**. The conditions band's fields, strings, variant and type are **§10.2's**. Evidence, provenance and the dated stamp's wording are **§10.4's**. Deck size is **§5.11's**. The prize-title normaliser and the operator-photo crop rules are **§9's**. The per-category scene, its lane paints, its ground grain and its mark are **§8.3's and §8.5's**. `audioMood` is **§8.7's**. This section fixes the geometry they must land in, the floors they must clear, the frame budget they must fit inside, and the assertions that fail the build when they do not.

**The Metricool mention effect is a payload decision, not a frame decision.** Metricool's +108% reach / +167% comments for mentions is correlational across a 24.36M-post benchmark corpus, not a controlled test on PDD, and it measures *tagged mentions*, which live in the publish payload. §6.4's arithmetic and §10.2's band ruling both put the operator name off the frame in v1, which removes the temptation to put a name in a card row and quote a number that was never about on-frame text.

**The audio default is no longer §6's, and the earlier draft's decision is withdrawn.** The earlier draft observed that `config.json` defines `audioMood` for six categories only, that `config.mjs:8–11`'s `FALLBACK` supplies none, and that `beat.mjs:16` throws `no audio in manifest for mood="undefined"` — and then set `FALLBACK.audioMood: "win"` itself so the pipeline could not fail closed. **Every `audioMood`, including `FALLBACK`'s, is §8.7's.** `beat.mjs:16` is a consumer and asserts nothing. §8.7's gate G-C4 — which asserts that every entry's mood appears in `assets/audio/manifest.json` *and* that the manifest row's `bpm` is a finite number, which is the half that excludes the `sting` entry whose `bpm` is `null` — guarantees this section can never again be handed a mood the manifest does not carry or one that cannot produce a beat grid. §6 keeps §6.4's resolved-bed table, which is its own, and consumes the assignment.

One note for the record, because the earlier draft's mechanism was wrong even though its conclusion was right: `config.mjs:13–17` returns `{ ...FALLBACK, ...c }`, a **merge** and not a branch — re-read on disk this session — so a configured category short of a key inherits FALLBACK silently rather than throwing. Adding a category to `config.json` without `audioMood` therefore produces a silent `visualWeight: 0.6` and `valueLineMin: Infinity`, not a build failure. §8.7 deletes the merge; that is the fix, and it is not §6's. Anyone writing a gate that asserts "the Reel pipeline does not throw on sports-outdoors" builds a gate that passes today, passes after a partial migration, and never fires.

**A structural dependency that governs the scene as well as the insert.** `reel-template.mjs:46`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` build the video CSS by regex-scraping `styles.css` for `:root{…}` and `[data-theme="…"]{…}` blocks only; `reel-template.mjs:47` adds a second, hard-coded allowlist for `.p-embers|golddust|fireflies|holo`. Both regexes were re-read this session and are unchanged. Any new styling written into `styles.css` as a descendant rule — `[data-theme="cash"] .insert-row-b { … }` — will render on the carousel and **silently vanish from the Reel**. Therefore: every colour the insert and the scene lanes use must be declared as a token inside a `:root` or `[data-theme]` block (which the regex does lift), and every structural rule must live inline in `reel-template.mjs` or in a shared scene module both renderers import. §8.3's module already emits its tokens inline on `<body>`, so the lane paints are token-driven and cannot be lost to the scrape — that is recorded here so it is not undone. This is not optional hygiene; it is the exact failure mode the digest names, and it is silent, so it passes every unit test that renders a still.

**Decisions this section commits to**

- §6.4's `pop.mp3` four-draw recovery is WITHDRAWN as a one-glyph sensitivity. Under rule 4's newly-tightened 3-beat sign-off floor the 40-beat arrangement (2 open + 4×9 hold + 2 sign-off) is illegal; the only legal completion at a 9-beat hold is 44 beats = 17.368s, past the 16.0s ceiling. Pop's fourth draw now requires an 8-beat hold, i.e. a read floor ≤ 2.958s, i.e. ≤59 glyphs — a nine-glyph cut, not one. `warm.mp3`'s three-draw recovery at ≤65 glyphs survives and is the only genuine one-glyph-class recovery in the table.
- §6.4's five-field exception ("only 152 BPM reaches a five-field card at N=3 … there the fifth field is free") is WITHDRAWN for the same reason: it depended on a 2-beat sign-off. At the 86-glyph five-field floor EVERY bed falls to N=2 (elegant 20 beats, win 24, warm 24, driving 24, pop 32). The earlier draft's conclusion is therefore true again although its reasoning was wrong when written — recorded as a double correction rather than a quiet repair, and the operator-name decision now rests on three stated reasons instead of one false impossibility claim.
- Rule 4's 3-beat sign-off floor is declared inert on the five RESOLVED beds and explicitly NOT costless elsewhere. §6.4 now names the two configurations it closes (pop's 40-beat four-draw arrangement and the 112 BPM 28-beat five-field arrangement), because the settlement's "verified inert" finding was scoped to the resolved table only and would otherwise be read as costless.
- §6.3's wordmark-face paragraph: the Inter 700 UNTRACKED free run is 258.29px (751.00 − 492.71), not 252.29px, so mark slot M fits by 6.29px with 19.145px of clearance per side, not by 0.29px. The verdict is unchanged — tracking (22.5px) moves M, the face (9.36px) does not — but the margin is 20× larger than published and the conclusion is restated on the corrected figure.
- §6.2's sub-floor census is corrected from "six deleted, four relocated" to FIVE and FIVE. The ten declarations were re-enumerated exhaustively from the file (every font-size under 44px in reel-template.mjs) and the split is: deleted = .fc-labels b, .win-tab, .scenekick, .urgechip, .cd-kick; relocated = .rfoot, .l3-line, .l3-handle, .rl-pill, .rl-closes. §6.6's "six" counted the progress bar and the price-stamp furniture, neither of which carries a type declaration; they are now named separately.
- §6.4's `HOW MANY TICKETS?` width figure (1,523.1px) is withdrawn as unreproducible from §6's own 101.1px/glyph advance and replaced with the derivable fact: it greedy-wraps to two 8-glyph lines of 808.8px, FITS comfortably, and is banned solely for carrying no verified figure. The two banned strings are now distinguished by reason — one is unrenderable (four line boxes), one is renderable and non-compliant.
- §6.4's open-frame contrast is restated as 4.63:1 with the composite shown (#6D6F71 = 109,111,113; L 0.1582), re-derived rather than carried at 4.65:1. The AAA-large verdict is unchanged with 0.13 of ratio to spare.
- The 8-vs-9-glyph headline word cap is declared INERT on this surface rather than arbitrated. §10.6a's ≤8 (set on the still's 895px well at §3.4's 0.6740em) and the two-figure ruling's 9 (computed on the older 0.6573em against the retired 930/940px tracks) both sit at or under the Reel's own 9-glyph line, so neither binds here; closing the disagreement is §10.6a's.
- §6.3's counter-chip paragraph no longer restates §4.4's 70px decomposition. It previously said "§6 restates neither" in the same sentence that restated the 44/50 + 10px derivation; the pointer is kept and the decomposition is dropped.

**Open questions**

- Does §10.2's deck-variant L1 keep its ticket-price run? It is the ONLY thing discharging §10.6 predicate 3 on the Reel's open frame. The Reel has no generated proof line, so if the price run is dropped the `question` archetype becomes unrenderable on this surface and there is no vertical budget for a replacement. §6 raises the dependency; it cannot fix it.
- §3.4 must settle the wordmark's 1.5px tracking. At 0px, mark slot M fits the Reel rail (267.65px run, 15.65px spare, Bricolage 800); at 1.5px it is suppressed by 6.85px. The face choice (Bricolage 800 vs Inter 700, 9.36px) does not decide it; the tracking (22.5px) does. §8.3/§8.5 then own whether to redraw M, re-originate it from its published x 435…655 (which overlaps the wordmark under every setting), or give the other seven scenes a Story mark instead.
- §10.6a must reconcile the two headline word caps it has been handed — ≤8 glyphs from the gutter ruling and ≤9 from the two-figure ruling — and record which advance (0.6740em or 0.6573em) it measures against. The disagreement is inert on the Reel and binds only on the still.
- Does §10.2's band L1 land at ≤65 glyphs? Home-garden Reels ship 2 draws / 11.650s until it does — the thinnest configuration in the system, now on a live category.
- Nobody has measured the per-frame cost of rasterising lane C's clipped, transform-animated field. `capture.mjs:20`'s fixed 5-minute budget is a watch item at 450 frames, and a trip would present as a Playwright failure rather than a budget failure.

**Risks**

- NOTHING AT THIS GEOMETRY HAS BEEN RENDERED. Every width is an advance sum bounding a line box; §5.3's measured-fit rule at render is the binding check. The 346px card, the 276px clear photo window, the 70px counter chip over a full-bleed photograph and the truncated Row B at `--fs-lead` are all paper.
- THE 32% CHROME CEILING HAS 7.4px OF SLACK, down from 10.8px. Chrome is 607px against 614.4px. One extra conditions-band line (45px) breaks it outright — where under the 195px Row C the first extra line was absorbable — so the next band line is a ceiling renegotiation, not a row adjustment. The photograph floor has fallen 3.18 percentage points (71.563% → 68.385%) to buy one E2 form across four surfaces.
- THE REEL TRUNCATES OVER HALF OF LIVE INVENTORY. Median title 26 glyphs against a 22-glyph render cap. At p90 = 53 the trim strips the distinguishing qualifier, which is the field CAP 8.17 calls the nature of the prize. The mitigation (untruncated title in out/alt.json plus a COMPLIANCE.json counter) is machine-readable, not viewer-facing; the real fix is §9's ingest normaliser.
- THE SIGN-OFF RUN IS ONE BEAT AT ITS TIGHTEST (elegant.mp3, 740.74ms), leaving a 140.74ms sampling window after §10.1's 300ms floors. Any section that lengthens the row-swap past 200ms or the sign-off collapse past 270ms closes it, and the 300ms floor is a judgement over two animation durations nobody has measured on a real render.
- THE SELL-OUT CONDITIONAL'S EXCLUSION FROM THE READING BUDGET IS THE LARGEST SINGLE SENSITIVITY IN §6.4 AND §6.5. Counting it takes the floor to 94 glyphs and drops EVERY bed to 2 draws. It is a 26-glyph run a viewer meets for the first time on card 1, and the exclusion is convenience, not measurement.
- G6 CLAUSE 2 IS NOW EXACT BUT NARROW. The Reel cover declares sceneLanes [R] because buildCoverHtml() builds no card, so the thumbnail carries only the rail lane — which §8's own risk flags as possibly sub-threshold at 0.78% tone ink. The comparison is non-vacuous; the category signal in the thumbnail may still be invisible.
- HOLDING 30fps REMOVES THE FRAME COUNT FROM THE CAPTURE-BUDGET RISK BUT NOT THE PER-FRAME COST. It also leaves G7's actual blocker untouched (encode.mjs:2 hardcodes /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg), and §6.7's CRF 18 is unaffected by whichever way §8 rules on its gate set — §6 declines to rule on another section's gates.
- THE 68.385% PHOTOGRAPH FLOOR IS AN AREA CALCULATION OF OPAQUE CHROME, MY OWN CONSTRUCTION. Meta publishes no threshold for "majority text" and no definition of what it counts. If the classifier counts glyph coverage rather than band area the figure is conservative — but nobody knows.
