## §7 Story and Facebook specification — verified, three corrections

## 7. Story and Facebook specification

These are the two secondary surfaces. Neither earns a bespoke design system. The Story reuses the Reel's safe box and the carousel's still renderer; Facebook reuses the Instagram deck outright. The work here is mostly subtraction — removing a video render that buys nothing, removing a publishing decision that an agent has already got wrong once, and removing three caption mechanics that expose the account to account-level demotion.

Everything marked **verified in-session** was checked against `~/pdd-aggregator` or against the live Composio tool schemas on 17 Sep 2026. Everything else carries its provenance.

**What this section owns, and what it only consumes.** §7 owns: the Story's band envelope inside Box A (the five band heights, their y-ranges, the four gutters, and band 4's 245px envelope with its five rows), the Story's still-vs-video decision, the countdown gate, the Facebook post path, the album composition, and the caption-mechanic ban's *reasoning*. It owns none of the following and restates none of their values — where a number below is theirs, it is cited, not republished:

| Not ours | Owner |
|---|---|
| The odds device: geometry, ceiling, above-ceiling encoding, the green marker | §4.4 (geometry), §4.7 (ceiling, encoding, marker) |
| The E2 odds module and its height on every surface | §4.4 |
| The exact odds wording on any surface | §10.6a |
| The conditions band: fields, strings, line count, type size, height | §10.2 |
| The type scale, the gutter, both tracks, the type floors, rules T1–T4 | §3.5 |
| The dated read-time stamp: its permitted verb, its two forms, their glyph counts and widths | §10.4 |
| `data-pdd-role`, the `DRAW_CARRYING` predicate, the G1-P prize-name assertion | §10.2 |
| Deck size, backups, the degradation ladder | §5.11 |
| Where the per-category scene renders on 9:16, and the lane and mark-slot rects | §8.3 (lanes and slots), §8.5 (scene elements) |
| Whether Story insights are retrievable | §11 |
| Evidence/provenance columns, the freshness window, the eligibility predicate | §10.4 |

**One measurement this section depends on is contested upstream.** Two rulings publish different *measured* mean uppercase advances for the same bundled `inter-latin-600-normal.woff2`: **0.6602em** (stated method: mean over A–Z, space and digits) and **0.6782em** (no method stated). §7 cannot reconcile them — that is §3.5's — so every Inter figure below is computed at the **wider 0.6782em** and the narrower value is given alongside. Every conclusion in §7.2 survives both, and after the §10.4 correction to band 1 the §7.1 category-word conclusion now survives both as well, so the dispute no longer changes a single verdict in this section. For band 4's sell-out conditional, §4.4 publishes a **real-advance measurement** (glyph-by-glyph rather than a mean) which supersedes both means for that one string; it is used below and the mean-based figure is kept as a conservative bound. JetBrains Mono 700 (0.600em for every glyph, measured) and Bricolage 800 uppercase (0.6573em) each have a single measured value and are used as published.

---

### 7.1 The Story reuses Box A, unchanged

The Story canvas is 1080×1920, identical to the Reel. It therefore inherits **Derived Safe Box A** unchanged:

```
Box A   x 65 … 1015   (w 950)
        y 269 … 1152  (h 883)
        CSS: left:6%  right:6%  top:14%  bottom:40%
L-notch NEVER place anything at x 853…1080 by y 1152…1920
```

**The gutter is settled, and it makes Box A and the chrome track one number.** §3.5 has landed `--gutter: 65px` on every canvas and is the sole owner of it. `1080 − 2×65 = 950` and `1015 − 65 = 950`, so §3.5's chrome track and Derived Safe Box A are **the same 950px constant at the same x-origin on both the 1080×1350 still and the 1080×1920 Story and Reel**. §7 publishes neither the gutter nor the track; it records only that the two now coincide, which is why the Story needs no column of its own.

(One correction, because getting it wrong is what keeps re-seeding this conflict: the still's narrower 895px *content well* is **not** caused by §5.9's sheet edge. §3.5 sizes that well to §4.4's dot band, and the sheet edge then occupies a margin the band-sized well already leaves. Nothing on the Story is sized to the dot band, because no band renders on 9:16 at all — see §7.2 — so the Story runs the full 950px chrome track. The well's derivation and its value are §3.5's and are not §7's to restate beyond this pointer.)

The box is **DERIVED, not official**: it was obtained by edge detection from Meta's own 9:16 safe-zone diagram (facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490, diagram asset version timestamp 10 Feb 2026). Meta publishes no numeric table. Meta's prose states that 9:16 Feed video uses the same guidance as Reels and Stories, so one box governs all three. Any section citing Box A should label it DERIVED; §4.4, §6.1 and §8.3 currently do not.

**On the bottom exclusion, be careful.** Meta's measured bottom exclusion is 672px (35%) normally and 768px (40%) "if the creative carries a disclaimer". Whether Meta's "disclaimer" category covers a CAP 8.17 significant-conditions line is **not established** — Meta's usage generally means an ad disclaimer, not a promotional T&Cs line. So 768px is **adopted as the operating figure** on the grounds that PDD's creative always carries a conditions line and the cost of being wrong in the safe direction is 96px of layout, while the cost of being wrong in the unsafe direction is a compliance line under Instagram's reply bar. Box A's `bottom:40%` is a decision, not a derivation, and §7.2's photo band is the element that pays for it (open question below).

**The current Story breaches the box almost everywhere.** Measured by arithmetic from `carousel/story.mjs` against Box A — every line number and value verified in-session:

| Element | Source | Rendered y | Inside Box A? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.st-kick` (closing date) | `story.mjs:53` `top:120px`, `left:56px;right:56px` | ~120–161 | No — inside the 269px top exclusion, and x 56–1024 is 9px outside the margin each side |
| `.st-name` (prize title, 58px) | `story.mjs:59` `top:190px` | ~190–250 | No |
| `.st-breathe` / `.st-card` (photo) | `story.mjs:68` `top:310px; height:820px` | 310–1130 | Vertically yes; `left:64px;right:64px` puts x at 64–1016, 1px outside the margin each side |
| `.st-stamp` (ticket price) | `story.mjs:102` `top:46%`, 430px, `margin:-215px` | 668–1098 | Yes |
| `.st-clock` (flip countdown) | `story.mjs:91` `top:1170px` | from 1170 | No — top edge sits 18px past the boundary |
| `.st-link` (`LINK IN BIO · @prizedrawsdaily`) | `story.mjs:95` (CSS), `story.mjs:152` (markup) | ~1560–1600 | No |
| `.rfoot` (compliance line) | `story.mjs:107` `bottom:36px`, `story.mjs:155` (markup) | ~1855–1884 | No — and being full-width it crosses the L-notch's x-range |

The photo card's 64px is now a settled 1px error rather than a rounding question: §3.5's gutter is 65px, so `left:64px;right:64px` misses the margin by exactly one pixel each side and the fix is a literal, not a judgement.

(The previous draft published `.rfoot` at "~1884–1908". That is arithmetically wrong: `bottom:36px` on a 1920px canvas puts the element's **bottom** edge at y 1884, so a 24px line occupies roughly 1855–1884. The conclusion — outside Box A, inside the notch band — is unchanged.)

Same defect shape as the Reel: only the photo card and the price stamp are inside the box. The countdown, the CTA and the compliance line have been rendering underneath Instagram's own UI.

The compliance line is the serious one. A CAP 8.17 conditions line that Instagram's reply bar and action rail sit on top of is not "included in the promotional material" in any practical sense, and the ASA is unlikely to accept that a social post is limited by space. Separately the wording itself is wrong — see §7.10.

**Type sizes below the floor.** The Story is a video canvas, so §3.5's **44px video floor** binds. Four rendered sizes are below it: `.st-kick` 34px (`story.mjs:54`), `.st-link` 32px (`story.mjs:96`), `.rfoot` 24px (`story.mjs:108`), and `.fc-labels b` 24px (`reel-template.mjs:124`, imported into the Story via `flipClockCss()` at `story.mjs:20`). The imported `.fc-time` at 148px (`reel-template.mjs:118`) is not a floor violation — it is more than three times the floor — and it is not a T2 violation either: T2 is now scoped to `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame with **zero legal**, it bounds a node *count* rather than banning a size, and the Story is the surface that carries zero. The point is moot in practice in any case, because §7.2 gates the flip clock off and the node does not render. Separately, three current sizes (`.st-name` 58px, `.st-typo .st-title` 100px, `.fc-time` 148px) are not steps on §3.5's scale at all; that is §3.5's T3 to police, not §7's. The conditions line is the one sanctioned exception to the video floor, and §10.2 owns both the exception and the size it sets.

Two smaller defects found in-session and not in the research digest:

- `story.mjs:148` renders `⏳ <b>${closes}</b>` — an emoji used as layout furniture, which the approved direction strips (the American-giveaway tell list names siren/fire/money-bag emoji specifically; the hourglass is the same move). It goes.
- `story.mjs:125` reads `const closeIso = draw.draw_date || nowIso;`. A draw with a null `draw_date` therefore renders a flip clock counting to *build time* — a live draw shown at 00:00:00. This is not hypothetical safety margin; it is a wrong number on a compliance-sensitive element. §10.3 deletes this fallback outright and rules the flip clock out of v1 entirely; §7.2's gate is the same conclusion reached from the other direction.

**The exclusion bands are the Story's scene lanes.** The 269px top exclusion and the 768px bottom exclusion are filled with flat rail blue `#14385F` — the approved direction's standing chrome bands. Instagram's own progress bar, avatar and reply bar then sit on brand colour, and nothing of PDD's is lost to them. This also neutralises Meta's documented zoom-to-fill behaviour on phones taller than 9:16: cropping flat colour costs nothing.

Those two bands are **§8.3's Story scene lanes S1 and S2**, and §8.3 is normative for their rects and for what paints in them; §8.5 is normative for every scene-element coordinate inside them. §7 publishes neither. Three consequences bind here:

- The Story's per-category identity lives entirely in S1 and S2, **outside Box A**. No band in §7.2 is shortened to make room for a scene, and band 3's photograph is untouched by the scene system. The scene ruling confirms this explicitly.
- Both lanes render **static, at phase 0** — the Story ships as a still (§7.3), and §8.3's freeze rule defines a still as the loop sampled at a phase.
- A scene *ground* may pass under the L-notch; a scene *mark* may not. §8.3 places the Story's single mark slot inside S2, clear of both the notch and the conditions band's bottom edge; the coordinates are §8.3's and are not repeated here.

One consequence §7 must record rather than fix: §6.3 measures the Reel rail's real inter-string gap and **suppresses mark slot M on the Reel and the Reel cover**, so the Story is currently the only surface in the system on which a scene mark can render at all — and the Story is a still. Of the eight scenes, only sports-outdoors defines any `front()` content, so today that amounts to one mark, on one surface, with no motion. Whether the remaining seven scenes get a mark in the Story slot or `#scene-front` and both mark slots are deleted is **§8's decision, not §7's**; §7 records only that the Story is where the answer lands, and that if the mark survives it survives on a static surface.

The bands remain **story-only** and must not be carried into the Reel, where Instagram's own ranking guidance names "reels that … contain borders" as a demotion trigger (about.instagram.com, 31 May 2023). That boundary has to be enforced in code, not remembered.

**The category word.** §3.3 names the rail band as carrier (a) of category identity. On the Story it cannot be carried, and after §10.4's stamp correction the arithmetic is no longer close.

Band 1 carries §10.4's **long** stamp form, which §10.4 itself assigns to "Carousel masthead Slot B; Story band 1": 34 glyphs, JetBrains Mono 700 at `--fs-label` 44px, 0.600em measured = 26.4px per glyph, **34 × 26.4 = 897.6px** of the 950px track. That leaves **950 − 897.6 = 52.4px**. Appending ` · <CATEGORY>` at Inter 600 uppercase costs, over the **eight** category names `config.json` carries after §8.7's migration (the six shipped today plus `sports-outdoors` "Sports and Outdoors" and `home-garden` "Home and Garden", neither of which uses an ampersand):

| Suffix | Glyphs | @0.6782em | Line total | @0.6602em | Line total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ` · LUXURY` | 9 | 268.6 | 1166.2 | 261.4 | 1159.0 |
| ` · CAR DRAWS` | 12 | 358.1 | 1255.7 | 348.6 | 1246.2 |
| ` · CASH PRIZES` | 14 | 417.8 | 1315.4 | 406.7 | 1304.3 |
| ` · HOUSE DRAWS` | 14 | 417.8 | 1315.4 | 406.7 | 1304.3 |
| ` · COLLECTIBLES` | 15 | 447.6 | 1345.2 | 435.7 | 1333.3 |
| ` · TECH GIVEAWAYS` | 17 | 507.3 | 1404.9 | 493.8 | 1391.4 |
| ` · HOME AND GARDEN` | 18 | 537.1 | 1434.7 | 522.9 | 1420.5 |
| ` · SPORTS AND OUTDOORS` | 22 | 656.5 | 1554.1 | 639.1 | 1536.7 |

**All eight overflow the 950px track, under both contested Inter advances, by at least 209px.** The shortest suffix in the set, ` · LUXURY`, needs 268.6px (261.4px at the narrower advance) against 52.4px of remaining track — an overflow of 216.2px, or 209.0px. There is no coin toss left: the previous draft's 5.0px-versus-2.2px result was computed against a 26-glyph `CHECKED 09:00 · WED 17 SEP` that §10.4 has since retired, and the correct 34-glyph string settles the question by 40× the margin the dispute was about. Under the measured-fit rule a standing element that fails the build on eight categories out of eight is not a standing element, and there is no second rail on this surface to move it to. **The Story's category identity is therefore carrier (b), the scene lanes above.** §3.3 must either accept that carrier (a) is undelivered here or find it a slot; §7 states the arithmetic and takes no decision on §3.3's behalf.

(Two corrections are folded into that table. The previous draft ran the test against ` · CASH PRIZES` and called it "the shortest real category suffix"; it is not — `LUXURY` is four glyphs shorter. And it ran against the wrong stamp string, which is the correction that converts a 5px coin toss into a 216px refusal.)

### 7.2 What a 9:16 Story carries

One draw — the soonest-closing. `story.mjs:196–200` already selects it correctly (minimum `draw_date`, ties keep original order); that logic survives unchanged.

The Story emits **`data-pdd-role="story"`** and is a member of §10.2's `DRAW_CARRYING` set, so the band-2 prize name carries `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"` and the G1-P assertion runs on it. The role enum, the predicate and the assertion are §10.2's; §7 declares the value and nothing else.

**Five bands inside Box A.** Band heights sum to 863px, plus four 5px gutters = 883px exactly. The 883px envelope is not a judgement; the split between bands is, except where a band's height belongs to another section.

| Band | y | h | Contents | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Dateline | 269–324 | 55 | §10.4's **long** stamp form — the run-level read-time stamp. §10.4 owns the string and the wording law; §7 owns the slot | JetBrains Mono **700**, 44/50 (§3.5 `--fs-label`), `#5A5F66`. 50px of type, 5px slack |
| 2 Prize | 329–474 | 145 | `cleanTitle()` output (`format.mjs:14`), max 2 lines, carrying `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"` | Bricolage Grotesque 800, 68/70 → 56/60, `#14161A`. 140px of type at 68/70, 5px slack |
| 3 Photo | 479–752 | 273 | normalised operator photo, full 950 width | — |
| 4 Odds lockup | 757–1002 | 245 | §4.4's E2 module, 240px of type, consumed whole. Strings per §10.6a | see below. 5px slack |
| 5 Conditions | 1007–1152 | 145 | **§10.2's conditions band. Not specified here.** | §10.2 |

`55 + 145 + 273 + 245 + 145 = 863`; `863 + (4 × 5) = 883`. Positions chain exactly: `269+55=324`, `+5=329`, `+145=474`, `+5=479`, `+273=752`, `+5=757`, `+245=1002`, `+5=1007`, `+145=1152` — flush with the top of the L-notch, nothing inside it.

**The build asserts the table rather than trusting it.** In the style of `assertVideoContract` (`encode.mjs:38–48`), the renderer asserts that `Σ(band heights) + 4 × 5 === 883`, that **every band's rendered content height is ≤ its band height**, and that **band 5 is never re-measured downward**. A failure is a build failure, not a shrink.

**Band 1.** JetBrains Mono **700**, not 500: §3.4 records that only `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2` is bundled, and §4.10 warns that a missing weight degrades to the next family in the stack, breaking tabular alignment silently. §10.4's long form is 34 glyphs; at 0.600em × 44px = 26.4px per glyph that is **897.6px** — the figure §10.4 itself publishes — leaving **52.4px** on the 950px track. The slot affords 35 glyphs (`35 × 26.4 = 924.0px`); a 36th reaches 950.4px and overflows by 0.4px. So band 1 ships with **one glyph of headroom**, which is a risk rather than a comfort (below).

The operator name is **removed** from this band. At the corrected string and size the dateline alone is 897.6px, and the shortest real operator suffix (` · REV COMPS`, 12 glyphs, 316.8px) takes the line to **1,214.4px** — 264.4px over the track. Operator attribution is the conditions band's host line (§10.2), which is also the field CAP 8.17 actually requires. (The previous draft computed this at 48px against the retired string and got 748.8px + 345.6px; the size and the string were both wrong, the conclusion was right.)

**Band 2.** The prize type steps 68/70 → 56/60, both a maximum of two lines, both fitting the 145px band (140px and 120px of type). The previous draft argued at length against 72px; that argument is moot, because 72 is not a step on §3.5's eight-step scale at all. The band-fit arithmetic survives as corroboration — 72px over two lines cannot fit 145px at any leading ≥ 1.01, and the multiple-of-5 leading rule pushes it to 75px leading = 150px, which overflows. Both shipped steps are §3.5 values (`--fs-title`, `--fs-lead`); §7 publishes no scale.

Capacity, measured at Bricolage 800 uppercase 0.6573em against the 950px track: `0.6573 × 68 = 44.6964px` per glyph → `950 ÷ 44.6964 = 21.25` → **21 glyphs per line at 68px, 42 over two lines**; `0.6573 × 56 = 36.8088px` → `950 ÷ 36.8088 = 25.81` → **25 glyphs per line at 56px, 50 over two lines**.

**A title that will not set in two lines at 56/60 is truncated, not refused.** The previous rule — fail the build — is replaced by §5.7's: truncate at a word boundary, append `…`, and re-measure at 56px. Against the measured distribution of 880 live `cleanTitle()` outputs, 88.3% are ≤ 50 characters, so the truncator fires on **11.7% of draws**. The old rule therefore hard-failed the Story on roughly one draw in nine, on a surface that carries exactly one draw and has no backup slot — a legitimate draw taking out the whole asset. Truncation is a counted, non-failing record (`prize-name-truncated`) and §10.7 keeps the untruncated title in `out/alt.json`, so nothing is lost from the record. The title still does not shrink to a third step and does not spill into band 3.

**Band 3** at 950×273 is a **3.48:1 crop**. That is punishing, and it is the price of two other sections' decisions rather than a §7 preference — see the ledger below. **273px is the arithmetic maximum the surface can give the photograph, not a discretionary squeeze**: bands 1, 2, 4 and 5 are each at their minimum legal height, so nothing else can be taken. It is why ingest-time asset normalisation (§9) matters more for the Story than for any other format: a 3.48:1 slice of an unnormalised operator marketing collage is unreadable.

**Band 4 — the odds lockup. There is no dot grid and no bar on the Story.**

§4.4 is normative for the odds device's geometry and for the E2 module; §4.7 for the ceiling, the above-ceiling encoding and the green marker. §7 states only which encoding this surface carries, and the answer is: **the numeral lockup, on its own.** The full dot band does not render on 1080×1920 at all.

Band 4 consumes **§4.4's E2 whole, at 240px**, and adds the 5px of slack that makes the 245px envelope. E2 is one module at one size on all four surfaces and takes no surface parameter; §7 publishes none of its sub-block heights and states the rows only so the envelope is auditable:

| Row | y | h | Content | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eyebrow | 757–807 | 50 | `TICKET CAP` (§10.6a) | Inter 600 44/50, `#5A5F66`. 10 glyphs = 298.4px (290.5 at the narrower advance) |
| gap | 807–817 | 10 | | |
| Figure | 817–937 | 120 | the bare ticket cap, en-GB grouped, ≤ 9 glyphs (§10.6a) | JetBrains Mono 700, tabular, `--fs-figure` 120/120, `#14161A`. 9 glyphs × 72.0 = 648.0px |
| gap | 937–947 | 10 | | |
| Conditional | 947–997 | 50 | `1 IN <cap> AT SELL-OUT` (§10.6a) | Inter 600 44/50, `#5A5F66`. 26 glyphs = **619.8px measured** (§4.4's real-advance measurement); 775.9px under the conservative 0.6782em mean |

`50 + 10 + 120 + 10 + 50 = 240` in a 245px band. Every row clears the 950px track at the measured worst case (`4,500,000`, the maximum stored cap). Under §4.4's real advances the widest row in the band is the **figure at 648.0px** (302.0px of headroom); under the conservative mean it is the conditional at 775.9px (174.1px of headroom). Both clear, so the unresolved Inter measurement changes no verdict here.

The rows stack vertically rather than setting the figure and the conditional side by side. Side-by-side does not fit: `4,500,000` at 120px is 648.0px and `1 IN 4,500,000` at Inter 600 44px is 417.8px, which with a 24px gap is 1,089.8px against a 950px track. §6.3's Reel Row C has the same collision at the same measured advances and it is flagged here because the arithmetic is identical, not because §7 is fixing it.

**§10.6a's strings are adopted unchanged; its illustrative Story geometry has been deleted at source.** §10.6a used to sketch this content as a 150px figure in a 170px band 4 plus a single 44px line in a 57px band 5. That band 5 no longer exists — §10.2's conditions band occupies y 1007–1152 — and §10.6a's own band-4 and band-5 geometry is now deleted and replaced by a pointer to this section's band 4. §10.6a owns the wording and §7 owns the surface geometry; nothing in the permitted-wording table changes.

**Why the figure is 120 and not 150 — settled, not a departure.** There is **one shared odds module emitting E2 at one size on all four surfaces**, and it takes no surface parameter: the Story's figure sets at §3.5's `--fs-figure` 120/120, exactly as on the carousel draw slide and the Reel. The 270px Story variant of E2 is deleted, and §3.5's T2 is scoped to `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` per frame with **zero legal** — so the Story is the one surface whose largest node is `--fs-figure`, and `assertTypeContract()` implements T2 as an upper bound, never as "exactly one". The previous draft framed this as "a deliberate departure from one line of §3.5's own commentary"; that framing is withdrawn. It is now the ruled position, and §4.4's "270px on the Story", §4.8's hero-figure parenthetical and §10.6a's 150px sketch are all struck in the same change.

The arithmetic is what decides it. Three of the five bands are fixed by owners other than the figure: band 5 = 145 (§10.2, three lines, class A), band 2 = 145 (2 × 70 + 5), band 1 = 55 (44/50 + 5, and it cannot be deleted — §10.2 put the checked-at stamp there). Fixed + gutters = `145 + 145 + 55 + 20 = 365`, leaving `883 − 365 = 518` for bands 3 and 4 together:

- at E2 240 → band 4 = 245 → band 3 = `518 − 245 = 273` → **3.48:1**
- at E2 270 → band 4 = 275 → band 3 = `518 − 275 = 243` → **3.91:1**

So 150/150 is payable only out of the photograph, at 30px, and a 3.91:1 slice of an operator photo on the one surface that ships as a still is a worse loss than 30px of numeral on a frame where the figure already outranks the prize name **120 : 68 = 1.76:1** — which is the ratio §4.11's added-value argument actually needs.

**The recovery rule, so 150 cannot creep back.** Any height this surface ever gets back goes to band 3, never to the figure. If §10.2 cuts the conditions band to two lines, the 45px returned takes the photograph to 318px (**2.99:1**). If Meta's 35% bottom exclusion proves to be the correct variant, Box A's extra 96px takes it to 369px (**2.57:1**). Neither goes to the figure.

**Why the odds get the largest type on the frame at all.** This is the positioning argument, and it is not interchangeable with the compliance one. The odds are the datum no operator publishes; unoccupied-territory item 6 in the teardown is that nobody in the category has made odds visual. That is why the figure outranks the prize name here, and it is an editorial claim, not a legal one.

**The Story renders no per-figure provenance line.** §10.4 is the normative owner of the evidence contract and makes provenance a PostgREST selection predicate rather than a render-time element — a draw without fresh, method-stamped figures is never selected, so nothing on this surface can fail for want of a provenance row. The run-level read-time stamp lives in band 1 and the deck-wide one in §10.2's band. There is no provenance row in E2 and no legend; both were deleted at source, and any carousel allocation for them does not reach this surface.

**Band 5.** §10.2 owns the conditions band on every surface: its fields, its lines, their exact strings and states, its type contract and its 145px 9:16 height at y 1007–1152. §7 supplies the y-range and nothing else. The render must **fail** rather than shrink it — the conditions are the one thing that cannot be traded for layout — and that rule is §10.8's class A, not a §7 invention. The competing 190px five-line variant is closed: the 145px band is the ratified figure and §10.2's own five-band Story table is demoted to non-normative narrative, binding only on the band's y-range and on the checked-at stamp living in band 1.

Note what band 5 does **not** say. Odds are not among CAP 8.17's significant conditions; they are PDD's editorial value-add. §10.2 holds the list of what the significant conditions are and carries that statement normatively — §7 does not enumerate them. The proposition is repeated here once because it is the reason band 4 exists as editorial type rather than growing band 5, and because keeping the two justifications separate is what stops an editorial choice being laundered into a legal requirement.

**How this surface discharges CAP 8.17 field 5.** Band 2's prize name carries the *nature* of the prize. The *number* is discharged by the asset carrying exactly one named prize against one closing date and one price — PDD stores `grand_prize` and no prize count, which is why §10.2 deleted a `1 PRIZE:` prefix. The post-level gate (`count(assets where DRAW_CARRYING && prizeName non-empty) >= 1`) therefore passes on the Story with one asset, and the strings behind it are §10.2's.

**The proportional bar is deleted.** The previous draft gave band 5 a 950×24 rail with the single-ticket share marked in verdict green. §4.7 evaluated that encoding, rejected it by name, and the rejection is correct on this surface twice over.

- At the measured median cap of 9,999 the true fill is `950 / 9,999 = 0.095px` — 0.19 device px at `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, i.e. nothing.
- Clamped to §5.8's stated 2px minimum, the mark reads as `950 / 2` = **1 in 475**. Clamped instead to a width actually visible at feed scale — 24px, the bar's own height — it reads as roughly **1 in 40**. Either is a picture one to two orders of magnitude more flattering than the fact, and either is the CAP page-design breach §5.8 identified and then specified anyway.

The Story had no room for the clamp disclosure that would have been the minimum mitigation, and no disclosure wording is permitted for it in any case (§10.6a). It is removed, not relabelled. An independent check reaches the same place from the other direction: the deleted band was 57px, and a 699-ticket sheet at §4.4's 60 columns is 12 rows, so even the dot grid would have run at a 4.75px pitch there — roughly a 1px dot on a phone, which is the point at which the encoding stops being feelable at all.

**The trade, stated plainly, with the ledger that balances it.** The baseline is **§10.2's 340px photo table** — band 3 was 340px, a 2.79:1 crop. It is 273px here, and the 67px is fully accounted for:

| Released | px | Demanded | px |
|---|---|---|---|
| Band 1, 63 → 55 (48px type → 44px) | 8 | §10.6a eyebrow row (50 + 10 gap) | 60 |
| Band 2 slack, 148 → 145 | 3 | §10.6a sell-out conditional row (50 + 10 gap) | 60 |
| Band 5's bar, deleted | 57 | §10.2's band, 80 → 145 | 65 |
| One gutter (six bands → five) | 5 | | |
| Band 4's own slack, 20 → 5 | 15 | | |
| Figure, 150 → 120 | 30 | | |
| **Total released** | **118** | **Total demanded** | **185** |

`185 − 118 = 67`, which is exactly what band 3 pays. The previous draft's narrative named only the conditions growth and the conditional row and so accounted for 52 of the 67; the missing 15 is the eyebrow row that §10.6a also requires and that the old band 4 did not carry. None of the three demands is §7's to overturn, and **band 3 = 273px is the arithmetic maximum available, not a squeeze** — every other band sits at its minimum legal height.

**The registry's 392px photo band is dead arithmetic, and it is worth saying why so nobody claims it back.** An earlier ruling redistributed the deleted bar into a 392px band 3 and a 90px conditions band. Band 3 = 392 leaves `518 − 392 = 126px` for band 4, and E2's smallest legal stack is 240px — no row in it is optional, and 120 is §3.5's hero-figure floor. That is **114px short**; deleting band 1 outright (+55) still leaves it 59px short. The 392 was computed against a 90px conditions band and a bare 170px figure band, i.e. before §10.2's three-line 145px band (+55) and before §10.6a's eyebrow and conditional rows (+75). The conditions band did not give its slack back — it grew by 55px. That registry line is marked superseded.

**The countdown is conditional, and does not ship.** `story.mjs:151` renders a live flip clock to `closeIso` unconditionally. CAP 8.22 forbids claiming consumers must respond by a specified date when they need not, and the DMCC Act 2024 consumer provisions (in force 6 Apr 2025) ban fake countdown timers outright. `draw_date` comes from the scraper and operators do extend. A clock therefore ships **only** where the close time is stored as real and immovable. No such flag exists — `select.mjs:14` lists the exact columns the pipeline selects and there is no confirmation or source field among them (verified in-session; the live `select` string is `slug,title,grand_prize,prize_description,image_url,ticket_price,total_prize_value,total_entries,draw_date,entry_url,categories(slug,name),operators(name)`). §10.3 reaches the same conclusion from the gate side and rules the HH:MM:SS flip clock out of the first implementation entirely, on the independent ground that its own condition 4 — two fetches agreeing on the *time* — is unsatisfiable while `README.md:19–22`'s agreement compares only the draw *day*. Until both change, the clock does not render and the closing date is carried in §10.2's band as a date. This is the single highest-regulatory-risk element in the pipeline, because it currently renders every day with no gate and, per §7.1, renders a zeroed clock when `draw_date` is null.

### 7.3 How the Story differs from the Reel

| | Reel | Story |
|---|---|---|
| Audience | recommended to non-followers via Reels chaining | delivered to existing followers, 24h life |
| Ranking | nine prediction heads including abandonment; watch duration measured relative to peer reels of similar length (transparency.meta.com, 11 Nov 2025) | not in the chaining system; no length cohort |
| Draws carried | `drawsRendered` (§5.11) | exactly one, the soonest-closing |
| Audio | mandatory — Instagram makes muted reels less visible | not required |
| Motion | broadcast insert system: chrome expands → holds → collapses | none by default; §8.3's scene lanes render static at phase 0 |
| Recommendation-eligibility risk | high; added value must be visible on-frame | low; not a recommended surface |
| "Majority text" demotion | applies | does not apply |
| Link | none (link in bio) | none (no sticker parameter) |
| Metric the pipeline records | per-media likes + comments (`ig_media`), plus account-day reach | nothing today; §11.2 adds `ig_story_insights` — see §7.4 |

**Decision: the Story ships as a single still by default.** The grounds are four, and none of them is "it cannot be measured":

1. The Reel is video because Instagram's recommendation machinery ranks it as video and a muted reel is demoted. None of that applies to a Story, which is not in the chaining system and has no length cohort.
2. The 12s render (`story.mjs:126`) costs a full headless-Chromium frame capture plus an ffmpeg encode plus a music-licensing surface (Meta Music Guidelines, effective 26 Mar 2024, bind on use, so the pipeline muxes Pixabay beds). A still uses the same renderer as the carousel at a 1080×1920 viewport and costs one PNG.
3. Its only motion is a 1.00→1.02 breathe (`story.mjs:70`) and a flip clock that §7.2 and §10.3 both gate off. A video whose only moving element has been removed is a still with an encode attached.
4. §8.3's scene lanes render static at phase 0 on this surface, so the still carries the same per-category identity the video variant would — nothing is lost on that axis.

A video variant remains permitted on two conditions **together**: the close time is stored as verified-immovable (so the clock is lawful), and the Reel already rendered that day (so the clip is a free derivative rather than a second render).

This is design judgement. There is no measured evidence that a still Story under-performs a video Story at this account size. It is now *potentially* answerable rather than structurally unanswerable — see §7.4 — and the decision is reopened when §11.7's B10 coverage criterion is met for a run of days long enough to compare, not before.

### 7.4 API Stories carry no link sticker, and what follows from that

`carousel/story.mjs:4–6` states this in its own header comment: API-posted stories cannot attach a tappable link. It is consistent with the digest's finding that the Content Publishing API exposes no parameter for Instagram library music on Reels either — the publishing API takes media, not interaction furniture. Carried forward with the caveat that this was **not** re-verified against Meta's API reference in this session; it rests on the repo's own assertion plus the parallel music finding.

Three consequences the template must respect:

1. **No fake tap targets.** The only navigable affordance on an API-posted Story is Instagram's own header, which sits inside the 269px top exclusion. The creative must not draw anything that looks tappable. The current `.st-link` line reads `LINK IN BIO · @prizedrawsdaily` at 32px in the bottom exclusion — both unreachable and suggestive of a tap. It is removed; the dateline in band 1 is the only editorial type that replaces it, and the handle is not restated on the frame.

2. **The Metricool mention effect is not available here.** Metricool (24.36M posts / 375,118 accounts, Jan–Feb 2026 vs 2025) measured mentions driving +108% reach and +167% comments for accounts under 2K followers — on *posts*. A mention rendered as pixels in a PNG is not a mention object, so a Story cannot capture that effect however the operator's name is typeset. Since §7.2 removes the operator name from band 1 and hands attribution to §10.2's host line, nothing on the Story may be justified as a growth mechanic on those grounds.

3. **The Story has no metric in the pipeline as built, and §11 owns whether that is permanent.** Verified in-session: `insights.mjs:14` defines `KINDS = ["ig_media", "ig_reach", "fb_posts"]`. `mapPayload()` emits `ig_media` rows keyed by a real media id (likes, comments) and `ig_reach` rows hard-coded to `media_id: "account"` — an account-day figure that cannot be attributed to the Story. So today there is no story completion, no taps forward or back, no exits, no replies, and no story-level reach. That is a statement about the code, not about the platform, and the previous draft overreached by treating it as a statement about what is obtainable. **§11.2 adds an `ig_story_insights` kind** (`reach`, `replies`, `exits`, `taps_forward`, `taps_back`) pulled same-day at `window='t24'` only, because Story insights expire with the Story, and **§11.7 B10** sets the coverage criterion at "a number exists for ≥ 80% of published Stories", diagnostic only and never a gate. §11 is the instrumentation authority and owns whether B10 is deliverable — its own open question is whether a Composio action for Story insights exists and whether the 24-hour pull can be run every day.

   The design position that follows: the Story ships because it is nearly free once it is a still, and it is currently unmeasured. If B10 lands, §7.3's still-by-default decision and any future bespoke render budget become arguable on evidence. If §11 concludes B10 is undeliverable, the fallback holds: at ~66 followers a Story's ceiling is ~66 people, and an unmeasured surface gets no render budget.

---

### 7.5 Facebook posts one multi-photo feed post, via one named tool

**Decision: the daily Facebook action is a single multi-photo feed post via `FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST`.** Verified in-session against the live Composio schema. Its own description:

> "Publish one Facebook Page feed post containing one or more photos from public URLs. The action first uploads every photo with published=false, then creates one /feed post with those photo IDs as attached_media. If any upload fails, the feed post is not created; earlier uploads can remain unpublished on Facebook temporarily. This action publishes immediately and does not add photos to an existing album."

Required inputs are `page_id` and `photo_urls` (array, minItems 1); `message` is optional. Three things the description settles: it is a multi-photo **feed post**, not a Facebook Album object (so "album" below is shorthand for the collage the feed renders); it **publishes immediately** with no `scheduled_publish_time`, so the `primeWindowsUK` slots at `config.json:11` must be hit by running the routine in the window, not by scheduling; and it carries **no comment parameter** (see §7.7).

This decision is final, not provisional. §12.6's Q2 ("is the target end state a true multi-photo album or the single hero photo the code currently describes") is **answered here and closes**, and §12.2's Facebook scope line becomes "album" rather than deferring to it.

This **replaces `FACEBOOK_UPLOAD_PHOTOS_BATCH`**, which caused the 28–29 June 2026 regression: from roughly 28 June the pipeline stopped making album posts and instead fired 5–7 separate single-photo posts within the same second, with the caption attached as a self-comment on one of them, so six of seven posts carried no text. Composio's own tool description warns of exactly this — the live text, verified in-session:

> "Uploads up to 50 independent photos to a Facebook Page or Album using the Graph batch API. **With published=true, each page photo may create its own feed story; this action does not create one post containing all photos. Use FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST for one multi-photo feed post.**"

Meta's spam policy names high-frequency repetitive posting. A daily automated Page firing seven near-identical photo posts per second is that profile.

**Where the bug actually entered, verified in-session.** `FACEBOOK_UPLOAD_PHOTOS_BATCH` appears **nowhere** in `~/pdd-aggregator` (full-tree grep, `node_modules` excluded) — and neither does `FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST` or `FACEBOOK_CREATE_COMMENT`. The committed runbook at `DAILY.md:123–136` specifies `FACEBOOK_CREATE_VIDEO_POST` as primary and `FACEBOOK_CREATE_PHOTO_POST` as fallback — both single-object posts. `publish.mjs:169` computes `heroUrl = urls[0]`, `publish.mjs:172–173` writes it into `publish.json`, and `publish.mjs:233` prints a prose next-step naming `FACEBOOK_CREATE_PHOTO_POST`. So `publish.json` — the machine-readable contract — carries **no Facebook tool name and no photo array**, only a single hero URL, and the tool is chosen by an agent reading prose. That is the hole the regression came through, and fixing a tool name in prose alone leaves it open.

`publish.json` must therefore carry an explicit Facebook block that names both tools, the array and the prohibitions:

```json
"facebook": {
  "tool": "FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST",
  "pageId": "1106603652538117",
  "photoUrls": ["…01.jpg", "…02.jpg", "…03.jpg", "…04.jpg", "…05.jpg"],
  "message": "<FB_CAPTION.txt body, no URL>",
  "commentTool": "FACEBOOK_CREATE_COMMENT",
  "firstComment": "https://prizedrawsdaily.co.uk/category/<slug>",
  "forbiddenTools": ["FACEBOOK_UPLOAD_PHOTOS_BATCH", "FACEBOOK_CREATE_LINK_POST"]
}
```

`pageId` is already at `config.json:4` as `fbPageId: "1106603652538117"` (verified). `photoUrls` is a **five-element array at every deck size** — see §7.7; it does not track `drawsRendered`.

**Naming the tool is necessary but not sufficient — and the control that would make it sufficient has nothing to run in.** §10.1's PUBLISH gate runs inside `publish.mjs`, and an agent session then reads `publish.json` and calls Composio itself, which is how a caption can be edited, an alt array dropped or a different tool chosen while `COMPLIANCE.json` still reads pass. §10.7 proposes a SHA-256 binding: `publish.mjs` writes a hash of each caption file into `publish.json`, and the posting step re-hashes what it is about to post and refuses on mismatch.

**§7 does not claim that closes the hole, because §7 is the section that establishes there is no posting step.** None of the three Facebook tool names appears anywhere in the repository; "the posting step" is a model reading a runbook, which is precisely the control class that is rejected by name elsewhere in this spec ("a control defined in editable JSON, read only by a briefing, is not a control"). So the hash as specified is **written but not evaluable**, and a class-A failure whose trigger nothing can evaluate is not enforcement. Two honest endings exist and both are §10's to choose, with a cost line in §12.2 either way: scope a real posting step — a Bun script that reads `publish.json`, re-hashes, and calls the Graph API directly with a stored token — or restate §10.1's PUBLISH row and §10.8's class-A entry as **detection after the fact** via post-publish Graph reconciliation. The `forbiddenTools` array above is the same idea applied to the tool choice and inherits the same limitation. §10 owns the mechanism; §7.5 is the documented incident that justifies building one, and the record that today there is nothing for it to hook into.

Three knock-on changes, all verified against the files:

- **State row renames `fb_photo` → `fb_album`.** `state-schema.sql:3` types `format` as free text, so there is no migration, and `cleanup.mjs:26–30` is format-agnostic (it checks that every row for today is terminal, whatever it is called). The rename touches `publish.mjs:184–188` (the write-ahead upsert), the log line at `publish.mjs:227`, and **seven** lines in the runbook — `DAILY.md:92, 128, 131, 136, 138, 205, 206`. (The previous draft listed `DAILY.md:134` among them; line 134 carries `fb_video`, not `fb_photo`. The count of seven is right, the list was not.) A half-done rename leaves a write-ahead row nobody marks terminal, and `DAILY.md:128` already documents the consequence verbatim: *"the photo mirror never posts on a video day, so its write-ahead row needs a terminal status too, or `cleanup.mjs` would wait on it forever."*
- **`fb_video` is retired from the daily routine.** Facebook does one thing per day. This is not only a runbook edit: `publish.mjs:209–226` is a live block that write-aheads an `fb_video` row whenever `reelUrl` resolves. That block is deleted, along with the `+ fb_video` fragment in the log line at `publish.mjs:227`. In the runbook, `fb_video` is named at `DAILY.md:95–96` (the write-ahead description), `123–136` (the whole Facebook step, primary/fallback/carousel-only paths), `138–139` (the cleanup gate) and `205–208` (the formats-seen note) — four blocks, not one.
- **The stale comments go too.** `publish.mjs:163–165` and `caption.mjs:23–26` both name `FACEBOOK_CREATE_PHOTO_POST` in prose, and `publish.mjs:3` already contradicts them by describing the output as "IG carousel + FB album". One description, in one place.

### 7.6 The `child_attachments` carousel is available, free, and still wrong

Facebook's link-carousel format exists on the Page API, costs nothing, and looks like the closest structural analogue to the Instagram carousel. It is the wrong build, for one structural reason: **every card in a `child_attachments` carousel requires a link**. A post with links on its cards is a link post, and the link post is the worst-performing organic format Facebook has — 0.05% engagement rate and roughly 200 views against roughly 1,125 for a photo post (Socialinsider, 25M posts).

The mechanism behind that number reinforces it rather than softening it. Meta publishes no link-penalty demotion category, but ranking predicts outbound-click likelihood and weighs "the ratio of the popularity of a domain on Facebook versus the Internet as a whole" — a ratio a small UK directory domain loses by construction. Separately, 98.9% of US Facebook feed views in Q2 2026 contained no outbound link at all.

So the format that superficially matches PDD's content shape would convert a photo post into the format that reaches roughly one sixth as many people. It is not built.

### 7.7 The album: count, dimensions, caption and link placement

**Five photos: the cover plus the first four draw slides in deck order.** They are a strict subset of the Instagram deck — `build.mjs:150` composes `[intro, ...drawSlides, {type:"cta"}]` (verified in-session) — so there is no separate render and no separate design QA.

Three things about that selection are deliberate:

- It is by **slide index, not by close date**. §5.6's Delta 2 puts the draw with the lowest `total_entries` on slide 2, so "the four soonest-closing" no longer identifies slides 2–5. The album inherits §5.6's ordering and applies no second sort.
- It is **five at every deck size**. The count does not track §5.11's `drawsRendered`. Its only deck dependency is `drawsRendered ≥ 4`, which §5.11's `DRAWS_MIN = 4` guarantees; below that the run does not publish at all, so no Facebook branch is needed.
- The previous draft derived the five from "a default five-draw day renders seven slides and the album takes five of them". That premise is retired — §5.11 owns deck size and the album never depended on it.

Provenance, stated plainly: five is design judgement, not a measured optimum. The only real slide-count dataset in the digest is Eden's (655,385 carousels / 12,159 creators, Aug 2025–Aug 2026), which measures **Instagram** carousel breakout rate and shows it rising to a plateau around 14–20 slides. That dataset is Instagram-only and Eden sells a carousel generator, so "more slides win" is commercially convenient to them. It is not extrapolated to Facebook here, where the post renders as a fixed collage rather than a swipeable sequence and every extra photo shrinks every tile. Five is chosen because fewer tiles means larger tiles, which is what gives the odds figure a chance of surviving the collage, and because at roughly 30 people reached the marginal value of photos six through eight does not repay the QA.

**Dimensions need no rework.** 4:5 at 1080×1350 is Meta's own recommended Facebook feed ratio (1440×1800 ideal), and `publish.mjs:57–69` already produces exactly that JPEG.

There is a free upgrade available. `render.mjs:2` and `render.mjs:187` render each slide at a 1080×1350 viewport with `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, i.e. a 2160×2700 PNG; `publish.mjs:63` then hard-codes a 1080×1350 canvas and throws the extra pixels away. A 1440×1800 Facebook variant is one additional canvas size from a source that already has the resolution — not a re-render and not a redesign. One caveat if it is taken: `publish.mjs:64` fills the canvas with `#07060a`, which is `--bg-solid` from the old dark direction (`styles.css:25`). Under the approved newsprint direction the ground is `#F7F5F0`, and the moment source and target aspect ratios differ that fill becomes a visible black hairline. It changes to `#F7F5F0` in the same breath.

One cross-reference correction, recorded here because it names §7: §9.4 cites "§7.6's optional 1440 variant". The variant is **§7.7's**, and it is an output-canvas size for the Facebook JPEG, not a photo-well dimension — so §9's photo-well range re-derivation does not depend on it and should not be sized from it.

**Caption in the body, link in the first comment.**

Today the link is in the body twice over: `caption.mjs:32` and `caption.mjs:33` both build `👉 See every live UK draw: https://prizedrawsdaily.co.uk` (the list and no-list branches), and `brief.mjs:32` instructs the authoring agent to write "a fuller FB caption (with the clickable link https://prizedrawsdaily.co.uk in the body)". All three change.

Be precise about what this decision rests on, because the two halves have different evidential weight:

- **Removing the body link is supported by measurement.** The measured same-format cost of a body link is −30% to −60%. That is a real number about a real choice.
- **Putting it in the first comment is an untested hypothesis.** There is no controlled experiment behind link-in-first-comment for reach. It has a genuine compliance rationale — comment links are excluded from Meta's own link accounting and are exempt from the December 2025 two-link-per-month test — but a rationale is not a result.

**The first comment is a second Composio call, verified in-session.** `FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST` exposes no comment parameter. The comment is posted by `FACEBOOK_CREATE_COMMENT` with `object_id` set to the **composite `pageId_postId`** the post returns (the tool's schema is explicit that a bare numeric id may not resolve) and `message` set to the category URL. Composio's own documented pitfall for that tool: *"May fail with HTTP 400 policy rejection for certain external links; retries typically require changing/removing the URL."* So the routine must treat a failed comment as a named, recorded outcome — the album is already live and cannot be un-posted — and must not silently retry a rejected URL. Whether PDD's Page connection holds the engagement permission this call needs was not verified; see open questions.

The digest recommends A/B testing the placement. **This spec recommends not scheduling that A/B**, and the reason is arithmetic rather than reluctance: at a median of 30 people reached per post, detecting an effect of the size in question would need a sample a daily cadence will not produce in a year. Running it would generate a number that looks like evidence and is not. The placement is adopted on the compliance rationale and on the measured cost of the alternative, and the question is reopened only if median reach per post passes roughly 300 — a tenfold improvement, and a judgement threshold, not a powered one.

### 7.8 Blocking prerequisites

Nothing in this section ships until three things are resolved, in order.

1. **Publish the Page.** It appears to be unpublished — `is_published:false`, 1 follower, zero engagement across 29 sampled days, last post 3 July 2026. Carry the caveat: this was read from the live Page by an agent via Composio and was **not** independently verified. The owner must confirm it in Meta Business Suite.
2. **Establish whether Meta unpublished it, or whether it was simply never published.** These are different situations with opposite responses. If the owner never published it, publishing it and resuming is correct. If Meta unpublished it, resuming daily automated posting before understanding the restriction risks repeating whatever triggered it — and the 28–29 June burst of five to seven posts in one second is precisely the profile Meta's spam policy names. One new datum, verified in-session and cutting the other way: the Composio Facebook connection `facebook_olinia-brooky` (alias `prizedrawsdaily`) was **created 2026-06-28T19:52:28Z** — the same day the burst began. A fresh connection changing which tool an agent reached for is at least as plausible an explanation for the burst as anything Meta did. That is a correlation and nothing more; it does not tell us whether the Page was unpublished, and it does not relax this prerequisite.
3. **Set a vanity username.** Without one there is no clean URL to print on the creative, no `@` target for an Instagram cross-post to name, and nothing memorable for a viewer who sees the Page once.

### 7.9 Honest expectations, and the effort ceiling

**Expect roughly 30 people reached per post.** Buffer's benchmark (52M+ posts, updated 13 Sep 2026) puts median reach per post in the 0–1K follower tier at 30. Socialinsider (872,075 posts, published 3 Sep 2026) puts organic reach at 4.35% for 1–5K Pages, falling to 0.50% at 100K–1M. A freshly published Page with one follower should expect ~30, not 300. Every decision in §7.5–§7.7 is sized to that number.

**Recommended effort ceiling for Facebook:**

- Zero bespoke renders. The album is a subset of the Instagram deck, optionally at the free 1440×1800 resolution.
- Zero bespoke design QA. Facebook inherits the Instagram gates or it does not ship.
- **One caption, mechanically derived.** `brief.mjs:32` currently asks the authoring agent for two captions every day — two authored artefacts for a channel reaching ~30 people. The Facebook caption becomes a transform of the Instagram one: strip the hashtags entirely (Metricool found hashtags correlated with −31.70% views, correlational not causal; Eden found a 2.6pp spread across hashtag counts with 65% of creators using none — on this evidence hashtags are not worth a second authoring pass anywhere, least of all here), strip "link in bio", strip the URL.
- **Exactly two Composio calls per day** — `FACEBOOK_CREATE_MULTI_PHOTO_POST`, then `FACEBOOK_CREATE_COMMENT` on the returned composite post id. No third.
- One review, at 60 days, against one number: median reach per post across the album posts. If it is still around 30, stop posting to Facebook.

**Instagram deserves the effort, and this should be said plainly.** Instagram out-reaches and out-engages Facebook at every measured Page size on the same content — 3.20% versus 1.25% overall, 6.65% versus 4.35% at the 1–5K tier. And the competitive position is not symmetrical. On Instagram the entire UK prize-draw *directory* category totals roughly 13,000 followers, of which 12,100 belong to one person (Di Coke / SuperLucky); excluding her, every directory in Britain totals under 900, and PDD at 66 is already third. That is a measured, uncontested opening, observed directly on 17 September 2026. No equivalent opening has been measured on Facebook Pages.

There is a real UK comping audience on Facebook, but it lives in **Groups**, and the largest — SuperLucky's Lucky Learners, ~23,000 members — bans competition links outright while welcoming scam warnings and win stories. A Page cannot reach that audience at all; a person posting a scam warning can. That is a different programme, run by a human, and it is out of scope for a template specification. It must not be used to justify Page investment.

---

### 7.10 Banned caption mechanics

Two distinct classes, with different consequences.

**Class A — prohibited outright.** Meta's Pages, Groups and Events Policies III.E prohibit "share to enter" and "tag a friend to enter". PDD runs no draws, so it can never set these mechanics itself. The real exposure is **reproducing an operator's mechanic** in a PDD caption or on a slide: the moment PDD restates "share this post to enter", PDD's Page is carrying it. Rule: PDD never restates an operator's entry mechanic verbatim. It states the route and the existence of the free-entry route, which is what CAP 8.17 requires anyway and which §10.2 words.

**Class B — demoted at account level.** Engagement bait is demoted at *account* level for repeat offenders. A daily automated poster is exactly the repeat-offender profile. The banned mechanics are comment solicitation, share or send solicitation, tag solicitation, vote or react solicitation, and sensationalist withholding.

**Three live exposures, two named in the research and one found in the code.**

1. **"Which would you pick?"** — bare comment solicitation. The root cause is systemic, not accidental: `config.json:14` defines `archetypes: ["question", "price-anchor", "deadline", "absurd-comparison"]`, `plan.mjs:70–71` rotates them by `dayOfYear % GLOBAL.archetypes.length` (= 4), and `brief.mjs:20` hands the day's archetype to the authoring agent naming all four but defining none. The question archetype therefore fires roughly 91 times a year with no guard.

2. **"#1 is unreal"** — sensationalist withholding, the classic curiosity gap. It is also a claim with no stored source, which sits badly against CAP 3.7's requirement to hold documentary evidence for claims before publication.

3. **`carousel/brief.mjs:24`, found in this session and not in the research digest** — the briefing mandates a send-CTA **every single day** (verified verbatim in-session):

   > `- One send-CTA, fresh wording each day (never verbatim-repeat "send this to your comp buddy").`

   A send or share solicitation is Class B engagement bait, and requiring one daily is precisely the repeat-offender pattern. This is the most consequential of the three because it is committed code rather than an ad-hoc caption, and because its only guard is against repeating the *wording*, not the *mechanic*. **It is removed outright** — not softened.

**Why the existing guard cannot be extended to cover this.** `config.json:13` holds `bannedPhrases`, injected into the briefing at `brief.mjs:11`. All eight entries — "don't miss out", "amazing prizes", "you could win", "once in a lifetime", "hurry now", "act fast", "what are you waiting for", "incredible opportunity" — are hype tells. None is an engagement-bait pattern. More fundamentally, a string blocklist cannot govern a generator explicitly instructed to vary its wording each day; "fresh wording" defeats string matching by construction. And a control defined in editable JSON whose only consumer is a Markdown briefing is not a control at all.

**The guard is therefore an allow-list plus a mechanic ban, and §10 enforces both.** §10.6a owns the permitted-wording table and the four enforcement layers; §10.6 owns the predicates, and its `bannedPhrases` is demoted to a backstop and rewritten as word-class regexes. The three predicates this section's analysis produced, ported there rather than duplicated here, are:

- No imperative verb directed at the reader's social graph: *share*, *send*, *tag*, *comment*, *vote*, *react*, *double tap*.
- No claim whose subject is withheld — a numbered reference ("#1", "the third one") may not appear without the thing it refers to being named in the same sentence.
- **The question archetype is redefined rather than deleted.** *A permissible question is one whose answer is in the post; an impermissible one is a question whose answer is only in the reader.* That principle survives verbatim, and it is now **§10.6's mechanic predicate 3 and specifically its unit rule**: the predicate fires on any rendered text unit containing `?`, and on the cover the unit is the headline **plus the generated proof line 34px beneath it**, because that is where the evidenced answer is rendered. §10.6a's permitted `question` form is now the single string `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`, with `{n}` interpolated from `drawsRendered`; both previous forms are banned by name — `HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?` because it breaks to four line boxes and cannot render under the 3-line gate, and `HOW MANY TICKETS?` because it is a hero-size question carrying no verified figure on the frame itself.

  The previous draft's own example, *"A 1-in-699 shot at a £40,000 car, or a 1-in-13,995 shot at £2,000 cash — which is the better £10?"*, remains **withdrawn**: it is a comparative about odds quality and it fails §10.6a's unbounded-comparative predicate. The two-figure test that produced it was the right instinct and the wrong output — it checked that a question was *evidenced* without checking that it was *bounded*.

  **The claim the previous draft made here is withdrawn in full.** It read "§10.6a's allow-list supersedes it, because a headline that renders at 150px cannot be retracted from a published image." The allow-list supersedes nothing: §10.6 is the predicates' owner, no string is exempt because it is allow-listed, and an exemption keyed on "emitted by `oddsCopy.headline()`" would auto-exempt every future allow-list entry, which is how a gate rots. What actually resolves the conflict is the unit correction plus a new CI conformance gate that runs every string `oddsCopy` can emit through every predicate in the unit the renderer will present it in, so an allow-list entry and a predicate fail the **test job** rather than the daily build. On today's deck the `question` unit carries three distinct fact keys and passes; the old rule would have hard-failed roughly 91 legitimate runs a year, and the corrected one fires on none.

The reply sweep at `DAILY.md:144–145` ("reply to comments with a question back") is unaffected. Replying is conversation; soliciting in the post to game ranking is bait. They are different acts, even though the same instinct produced both that instruction and exposure 1.

**One further wording change, on every surface.** The compliance line `18+ · UK ONLY · PLAY RESPONSIBLY` is replaced by §10.2's conditions band. Three things are wrong with the current string and all three are fixed by handing it to one owner:

- "Play responsibly" is gambling furniture on a promotion that sits outside Gambling Act 2005 licensing — CAP Section 8 applies, Sections 16 and 17 do not.
- It omits the significant conditions CAP 8.17 actually requires. §10.2 holds that list; §7 does not restate it.
- The bare `18+` and `UK ONLY` are themselves unevidenced objective claims about another party's terms. PDD stores no `min_age` and no territory field, so both assert something PDD has not checked — the CAP 3.7 defect §10.6 identifies for `18+` and which applies identically to territory. §10.2's free-entry/age pointer replaces both with a pointer to the operator's own terms. The previous draft's line that "'18+' stays where an operator's own terms require it" is withdrawn: nothing in the pipeline reads those terms.

The line is **not** in one place. Verified in-session, it is hard-coded at seven render sites and asserted by three tests:

| Site | What it is |
|---|---|
| `story.mjs:155` | Story footer markup |
| `reel.mjs:105` | Reel footer markup |
| `reel-template.mjs:789` | Reel template footer markup |
| `render.mjs:69, 122, 157, 172` | carousel intro / draw / cta / other slide footers |
| `caption.mjs:35` | the lower-case variant in the FB caption body |
| `brief.mjs:26` | the briefing instruction that tells the agent to end with it |
| `tests/story.test.mjs:26`, `tests/render.test.mjs:20`, `tests/reeltemplate.test.mjs:18` | assert the exact string |

The three tests are part of the change, not collateral of it — they are rewritten to assert §10.2's new conditions band and, in `story.test.mjs`'s case, to stop asserting the things this section removes: `story.test.mjs:27` asserts `durationMs === 12000`, and `story.test.mjs:30–35` asserts the html contains "link in bio" and "@prizedrawsdaily" (all three verified in-session). Both encode decisions §7.3 and §7.4 reverse. A change that leaves them standing will look like a regression to CI.

### Decisions this section commits to

- The Story reuses Derived Safe Box A (x 65–1015, y 269–1152, 950×883). The box is DERIVED, not official, and `bottom:40%` (768px) is ADOPTED rather than derived — whether Meta's "disclaimer" category covers a CAP 8.17 conditions line is unestablished, and the cost of erring safe is 96px of layout.
- §3.5's gutter is settled at 65px, so §3.5's 950px chrome track and Derived Safe Box A are the same constant at the same origin on both canvases. The Story's bands run that track. §7 publishes neither the gutter nor the track, the previous draft's "if §3.5 resolves a narrower column" hedge is deleted, and the previous draft's explanation of the still's narrower content well is corrected: that well is §3.5's band-sized column, NOT a cost §5.9's sheet edge imposes — the sheet edge occupies a margin the band-sized well already leaves.
- Every Inter figure in §7 is computed at the wider of the two contested measured advances (0.6782em), with the narrower (0.6602em) given alongside. §3.5 owns the reconciliation. After the §10.4 stamp correction, no verdict in §7 turns on which is right.
- The 269px top exclusion and 768px bottom exclusion are §8.3's Story scene lanes S1 and S2, rendered static at phase 0. Their rects and the Story mark slot's coordinates are §8.3's and are not restated here. They stay story-only and are never carried into the Reel, where "contains borders" is a demotion trigger.
- Because §6.3 suppresses mark slot M on the Reel and the Reel cover, the Story is the only surface on which a scene mark can render at all — and it is a still. Whether the other seven scenes get a mark or `#scene-front` is deleted is §8's decision; §7 records only where it lands.
- The Story emits `data-pdd-role="story"`, is a member of §10.2's `DRAW_CARRYING` set, and its band-2 prize name carries `data-pdd-claim="prize-name"`. The role enum, the predicate and the G1-P assertion are §10.2's.
- The Story carries exactly one draw (the soonest-closing, already selected at `story.mjs:196–200`) across FIVE bands inside Box A: Dateline 55 · Prize 145 · Photo 273 · Odds lockup 245 · Conditions 145 = 863, plus four 5px gutters = 883 exactly.
- The build asserts `Σ(bands) + 4×5 === 883`, that no band's rendered content exceeds its height, and that band 5 is never re-measured downward.
- Band 1 carries §10.4's LONG stamp form (34 glyphs, 897.6px at JetBrains Mono 700 44px, 0.600em measured), not the retired `CHECKED 09:00 · WED 17 SEP`. §10.4 owns the string, its forms and the wording law; §7 owns the slot and restates none of them. Headroom is 52.4px of the 950px track; the slot affords 35 glyphs and ships with one to spare. The operator name is removed — ` · REV COMPS` would take the line to 1,214.4px — and attribution is §10.2's host line.
- Band 2's prize ladder is 68/70 → 56/60, both two lines maximum, both inside the 145px band. Measured capacity on the 950px track: 21 glyphs per line at 68px (42 over two), 25 at 56px (50 over two). A title that will not set in two lines at 56/60 is TRUNCATED at a word boundary with a trailing `…` and re-measured at 56px — it does not fail the build. 88.3% of 880 live titles are ≤ 50 characters, so the truncator fires on 11.7%; the untruncated title lives in `out/alt.json` (§10.7). 72px is not a step on §3.5's scale and the question does not arise.
- Band 4 consumes §4.4's E2 module WHOLE at 240px and adds the 5px of slack that makes the 245px envelope. §7 publishes no sub-block height of its own: eyebrow 50 + 10 + figure `--fs-figure` 120/120 + 10 + sell-out conditional 50. Strings are §10.6a's, adopted unchanged; §10.6a's illustrative Story band-4/band-5 geometry is deleted at source and replaced by a pointer here; geometry, ceiling, above-ceiling encoding and the green marker are §4.4's and §4.7's, none restated.
- The Story's odds figure sets at `--fs-figure` 120/120 — the same size as the carousel draw slide and the Reel. There is ONE shared odds module emitting E2 at ONE size on all four surfaces, with no surface parameter; the 270px Story variant of E2 is deleted. §3.5's T2 is scoped to `count(nodes at --fs-hero) <= 1` with zero legal, and the Story carries zero. This is the ruled position, not a departure — the previous draft's "deliberate departure from one line of §3.5's own commentary" framing is withdrawn.
- 150/150 is refused because it is payable only out of band 3 (photo 273 → 243, 3.91:1). The figure still outranks the prize name 120 : 68 = 1.76:1, which is the ratio §4.11's added-value argument needs.
- RECOVERY RULE: any height this surface gets back goes to band 3, never to the figure. Two lines of conditions returns 45px (photo 318, 2.99:1); a 35% bottom exclusion returns 96px (photo 369, 2.57:1).
- The odds carry the largest type on the frame on POSITIONING grounds — the odds are the datum no operator publishes, and unoccupied-territory item 6 is that nobody in the category has made odds visual — never on compliance grounds.
- The Story renders no per-figure provenance line: §10.4 makes provenance a selection predicate, not a render-time element. There is no provenance row in E2 on any surface.
- Band 5 is §10.2's conditions band, 145px at y 1007–1152. §7 supplies the y-range and nothing else. The competing 190px five-line variant is CLOSED; §10.2's own five-band Story table is non-normative narrative binding only on that y-range and on the checked-at stamp living in band 1.
- CAP 8.17 field 5 is discharged on this surface by band 2's prize name (nature) and by the asset carrying exactly one named prize against one closing date and one price (number). The post-level gate passes with one asset.
- **Band 5's proportional bar is DELETED.** At the measured median cap of 9,999 its true fill is 0.095px (0.19 device px at dsf 2); clamped to §5.8's 2px minimum it reads as 1 in 475, and clamped to a mark visible at feed scale (24px) as roughly 1 in 40. Either is a CAP page-design breach. §4.7 rejected this encoding by name and §7 no longer ships it. Corroboration: the deleted band was 57px, so even a 699-ticket sheet at §4.4's 60 columns would have run 12 rows at a 4.75px pitch.
- The Story's photograph is 950×273 = 3.48:1 against a baseline of §10.2's 340px photo table (2.79:1). The ledger balances exactly: 118px released (bar 57, figure 150→120 = 30, band 4 slack 15, band 1 8, band 2 slack 3, one freed gutter 5) against 185px demanded (§10.6a's eyebrow row 60 and conditional row 60, §10.2's band growth 65) — shortfall 67px, paid by the photograph. 273px is the ARITHMETIC MAXIMUM available: bands 1, 2, 4 and 5 are each at their minimum legal height.
- The registry's 392px band 3 / 90px conditions redistribution is dead arithmetic and is marked superseded: 392 leaves 126px for band 4 against E2's 240px minimum — 114px short, and 59px short even with band 1 deleted. It was computed before §10.2's three-line band (+55) and §10.6a's eyebrow and conditional rows (+75).

- The Story ships as a single still by default, on four stated grounds — no Reels ranking, no music-licensing surface, no remaining motion once the clock is gated, one PNG instead of a capture-and-encode — and explicitly NOT on the ground that it cannot be measured. A video variant is permitted only when the close time is stored as verified-immovable AND the Reel already rendered that day.

- The pipeline as built records NO story-level metric (verified: `insights.mjs:14` `KINDS = ["ig_media","ig_reach","fb_posts"]`, with `ig_reach` hard-coded to `media_id: "account"`). §11 owns whether Story insights are retrievable; §11.2 adds `ig_story_insights` at `window='t24'` and §11.7 B10 sets the ≥80% coverage criterion. §7.3's still-by-default decision reopens if and when B10 lands.

The previous 5.0px-versus-2.2px `LUXURY` coin toss was an artefact of the retired stamp string and is gone. The Story's category identity is carrier (b), §8.3's scene lanes.

- Banned Class A (prohibited): share-to-enter and tag-a-friend, including any verbatim restatement of an operator's own entry mechanic.
- Banned Class B (account-level demotion): comment, share/send, tag and vote solicitation, and sensationalist withholding. §7 supplies the reasoning and the three predicates; §10.6a owns the permitted-wording allow-list, §10.6 owns the predicates, and `bannedPhrases` is a backstop only.
