**6. collectibles (97) — "The Uncut Sheet"**
The printer's press sheet: the collectible as one cell of something not yet cut.
*Static:* a grid of 220 × 230px cells, 1px `--hairline`, anchored to `safe`'s top-left and tiled to fill the box, each corner carrying 15px crop marks set 5px off the corner. In Lane C that is 5 verticals (x 65, 285, 505, 725, 945) × 285 and 2 horizontals (y 729, 959) × 1080, plus crop marks at ≈12% mean opacity: **≈3,639 px² → ≈1.18% coverage, 0.308% tone**.
*Loop (Lane C only):* crop-mark opacity travels as a wave, amplitude 8% → 16% over 4,400 ms. Opacity envelope, zero geometric travel; peak ink per cell is (220 + 230) × 1 + 4 × 2 × 15 × 1 × 0.16 = 469.2 px² of 50,600 = **0.927%**, inside the ceiling.
***On 9:16 the phase is `c/8`, not `(r+c)/8`, and that is a correction rather than a simplification.*** Anchored at `safe`'s y 269 on a 230px pitch, row boundaries fall at y 269, 499, 729, 959 — so Lane C (y 722…1007) contains a **7px sliver** of one row, **one full row**, and a **48px head** of a third. The 7px band shows roughly 2px of one mark and the 48px band shows one corner, so the `r` term contributes one legible value and a diagonal collapses to a horizontal on the only surface where it moves. The wave is therefore specified as what it renders. On 4:5, where the region is 740px tall at the cover and carries three full rows, the diagonal `(r+c)/8` stands — but the still is motionless, so it is a static phase offset there, not a wave.
*Replaces:* the holo sheen at `styles.css:145`.
*Surface note:* the crop marks are treated as ground, not mark, for this scene specifically, because they are integral to the repeating field rather than a single focal element. The 4 × 5 / 880 × 1150px composition the inherited draft specified assumed a full-bleed backdrop and is retired with it; the field is now clipped to whichever box hosts it.

**7. sports-outdoors (102) — "The Marked Ground"**
The third-largest category, currently unthemed. This is the user's own idea — turf, grass, golf, hockey — made real, made honest, and re-derived against the lanes it actually gets.

**What ships is an animated chrome texture, not an animated backdrop.** The stripes drift inside the data card and stand still in the brand rail; the emblem is small and sits in the rail's own gap. If the mental model was turf *behind* the prize photograph, this is not that. It is the only version that keeps the full-bleed photograph, and therefore §6.3's chrome constants and the no-border rule, at the same time.

*Ground, always present, resolved once per run:* mown stripes. Vertical bands, period 90px, band width 45px, painted on odd bands only, phase anchored to the top-left of `safe` → band boundaries at x ≡ 65 (mod 90): x = −25, 65, 155, 245, 335, 425, 515, 605, 695, 785, 875, 965, 1055. Exactly 12 periods = 24 bands = 1080px.

| Lane | Paint | Resulting band | ΔL | Tone ink | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lane C (newsprint) | `--ink` at 5% — exactly §8.4's field cap | `#ECEAE5`, L 0.823356 | 0.0903 (cap 0.10) | 4.52% | 2.5% |
| Lane R, S1, S2 (rail blue) | `--ground` at 6% | `#224368`, L 0.053539 | +0.0155 (cap 0.016) | 0.78% | 3.0% |

Both figures are ratios and are unchanged by Lane C's re-derivation.

*Motion:* **Lane C only.** `transform: translateX(0 → −90px)`, linear, `loopMs` 5,200 ms, infinite, phase 0 at reel t=0. Periodic field, travel 90 = *P*, so the silhouette at t=0 and t=`loopMs` is identical. Lane R, Lane S1, Lane S2 and both frozen surfaces render at phase 0.

*Marking, one per draw, clipped to the surface's mark slot, in `--hairline` and `--ground` only.* The terms come from the sports-outdoors classifier rule at **`lib/parse.mjs:434`** — re-verified present, and the term lists below are quoted from it. **The marking is the only thing `variantOf(draw)` selects; the stripes are the category's ground and are never withdrawn by a variant.**

**An honest correction to the inherited draft.** It claimed the variants key off "the alternation groups already present in `lib/parse.mjs:434` — no new classifier, no new keyword list". That is not what the file contains. `lib/parse.mjs:434` is **a single flat alternation inside one capture group** — re-read on 17 Sep 2026; its only inner parentheses are non-capturing `(?:…)` groups scoping the Cobra model lines and the bike types, so there is no per-variant sub-grouping to read a variant off. The variant map is therefore a **new, separately maintained ordered list that duplicates a subset of those terms**, and the coupling risk is real rather than avoided. It is mitigated by a test, not by wishful architecture: `scene.test.mjs` asserts that every term in the variant map is still present in the source text of `lib/parse.mjs:434`, and fails the build when the classifier drops or renames one.

***The gym row is corrected, and the correction is the grain rule doing its job.*** As published it read "None, and no stripes — a home gym has no ground to mark, so this variant falls through to NEUTRAL's baseline grid". That deleted the **ground** from a per-**draw** function, which meant a translating stripe field could vanish and reappear at a §6.4 row swap, mid-loop, with no specified transition, and a gym-dominant deck rendered NEUTRAL throughout — the category having no identity at all, which is the state §8 exists to end. The honesty argument survives where it belongs: **a home gym gets no marking**, because there is no ground to mark and a false metaphor is worse than a blank slot. The stripes stay, because they are the category's register, not a turf claim.

*Two published radii corrected, with the arithmetic.* A 300px-radius arc spans 600px and cannot cross either slot as an edge — in a 220 × 80 slot it degenerates to a 110px tangent stub — hence r 1200 on the Reel and r 1500 on the Story, which are the radii that produce a shallow edge across the full slot width. And the cycling lane's published 260px separation exceeds both slots (80px and 300px tall), hence 50px and 200px. Two further corrections are mine rather than inherited: the Story ripple centre moves from y 2975 to **2900**, because at 2975 two of the five crests fall on or below the slot's bottom edge at y 1520; and the Story pitch centre moves from y 1895 to **1760**, because at 1895 the arc occupies only the bottom 45px of a 300px slot.

*Every Reel and Reel-cover marking above is currently unreachable*, because M suppresses on §6.3's measured rail clearance (8.3). The coordinates are kept because the measurement is a build-time test that can change; they are not shipping today.

**The honest caveat this section must carry.** `lib/parse.mjs` contains **no team-sport term at all** — re-verified by case-insensitive grep on 17 Sep 2026: zero occurrences of `hockey`, `football`, `rugby`, `cricket` or `tennis` anywhere in the file. The 102 sports-outdoors draws are golf equipment, angling tackle, bikes, gym kit and camping gear, not match tickets. The pitch marking therefore ships as the *default* and will rarely be the *selected* variant; the golf green will dominate. The user's hockey idea is honoured by the register — a marked ground — rather than by a hockey-specific drawing that no live draw would choose. If team-sport inventory appears, the shooting-D is a one-line addition to the variant table and the taxonomy, not a redesign.

**8. home-garden (45) — "The Plan"**
`lib/parse.mjs:442` shows what this category actually is: DeWalt/Makita/Milwaukee tool chests, rattan garden furniture, Ooni and Gozney pizza ovens, hot tubs, sheds, greenhouses, lawnmowers. Not plants. So the register is the measured drawing, not the seed packet.
*Static:* squared paper — 1px `--hairline` minor grid at 25px pitch at 30% opacity, major grid at 100px pitch at full hairline; one dimension line along the box's bottom edge, 1px, with 10px end ticks in `--rail` at **≤17% alpha** and a 90px break in the middle where a drawing would put its figure, left deliberately empty because scenes carry no text. In Lane C that is 32 minor + 11 major verticals and 8 minor + 3 major horizontals: 32 × 285 × 0.3 + 8 × 1080 × 0.3 + 11 × 285 + 3 × 1080 + 990 + 20 = **12,713 px² → 4.130% coverage, 1.074% tone** — the third-heaviest scene, not the heaviest; house-draws takes that at 4.907%.
*Loop (Lane C only):* the grid is static; the break widens 90 → 110 → 90px over 4,000 ms, as though being measured. The break is **centred**, so each painted line end travels **10px**, not 20 — 20 is the width delta and twice the travel of either edge. Discrete element, inside the 25px cap. The scene does not change; only the scoring is corrected. The second-lowest-motion scene in the set.
*Distinguished from house-draws by scale:* house is territory (40px survey grid, contours), home-garden is an object (25px squared paper, a dimension line).

### 8.6 When the category is unknown

**Today.** `config.mjs:8-11` defines `FALLBACK` as `theme: "default"`, `particles: { type: "embers", count: 46 }` (`:10`), `valueLineMin: Infinity`, and `config.mjs:15` supplies `hook: "WIN BIG"` when the slug is absent from `config.json`. `:root` at `styles.css:14-36` sets `--accent: #FF6A00` (`:15`) with `--font-display: 'Anton'` (`:34`). So unknown means *orange car theme, Anton display, an American headline*. 147 draws — 16% of the 899 enterable — currently resolve this way. (Cited line numbers corrected; the draft said `config.mjs:10-17`.)

Worth logging separately: `config.json`'s global `bannedPhrases` bans "you could win" while its `fixedHashtags` ships `#winbig` — verified in the file. The brand bans the phrase family in captions and publishes it as a hashtag. Out of scope for this section, but it should not survive the rework unnoticed.

**Specified.** An unknown slug resolves to **NEUTRAL**: the host ground plus a baseline grid, 1px at 40px pitch at 4% opacity (coverage ≈ 0.2% — 15,255 px² geometric on Lane C, 4.957%, × 4%), in `--hairline` on a newsprint lane or region and `--ground` on a rail-blue lane. No marking, no accent, `tokens: {}`, `loopMs: 0`, `amplitudeClass: null`, no motion. It must look *complete*, not broken — a deliberately quiet page, which is a legitimate member of the printed-register family rather than an obvious failure state.

Three rules:

- `sceneFor()` is total. `""`, `null`, `undefined` and an unrecognised slug all return NEUTRAL, and it never throws. The exceptions are a surface descriptor with no `band` rect, no `roles[]`, or a 9:16 descriptor with no `sceneLanes`, all of which throw at render time for the reason given in 8.3.
- A **recognised** slug whose scene fails to build also returns NEUTRAL. Fail safe to quiet, never fail open to the old orange default.
- NEUTRAL is also the baseline every diffing gate measures against, so it must itself be motionless and deterministic. If NEUTRAL drifts, the gates silently loosen — see risks. NEUTRAL's rendered output is therefore checked into `carousel/tests/fixtures/` as **four reference PNGs, one per surface, the 4:5 one captured at the cover slide role**, and any change to them is an explicit, reviewed commit.

**NEUTRAL is no longer reachable from live inventory, and that is §8.7's doing.** After the migration `pickBestCategory` skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories` and `FALLBACK.visualWeight` is 0, so the unconfigured `"other"` bucket cannot win a deck. NEUTRAL now guards a path that cannot be selected rather than one carrying 147 draws.

Nothing is lost legally or editorially when a scene is absent, because the scene never carried the value. The odds, the cap, the price and the conditions are all in the data layer. That is also the honest measure of what the gate in 8.8 is protecting, and 8.8 sizes itself accordingly.

### 8.7 Migration

**This lands as one change, not incrementally.** `render.mjs` reads `styles.css` wholesale, and the three video paths scrape it. Removing the `[data-theme]` blocks from `styles.css` therefore changes all four surfaces in the same commit whether or not that was intended. There is no safe half-migration.

**This section performs the legacy-token deletion, and it is the only section that does.** §3.8 specifies *what* goes (the `--gold-*` family, **15 references across the templates — re-verified by grep: 12 in `reel-template.mjs`, 2 in `render.mjs`, 1 in `story.mjs`, 0 in `reel.mjs`**; the `.p-*` particle skeletons) and §5.2 defers the removal to "when the Reel and Story are reworked in their own sections". §6 does not perform it. The removal happens **here**, in this commit, because this commit is the one that necessarily rewrites all four surfaces at once. Any section that defers the deletion defers it to §8.7 by name. §10.6a's retirement of the six `hook` constants and `WIN BIG` is performed physically here too, in the same commit as the `theme`/`particles` deletion, not separately.

**The six existing themes: tokens replaced, not tweaked.** Every one of the seven lifted blocks is a dark ground — `--bg-solid` is `#07060a`, `#050810`, `#070604`, `#04100a`, `#060b15`, `#0a0514`, `#070a13` at `styles.css:25, 49, 69, 96, 116, 137, 168` (all seven verified by grep). The approved direction is newsprint. This is a replacement, not a palette nudge. The `[data-theme]` blocks leave `styles.css` entirely and are **not** re-homed as `SceneDef.tokens` — under 8.3's token rule a scene may emit `--scene-wash` and nothing else, so the dark grounds are simply deleted and §3.7's `:root` palette is what every surface resolves against.

**The seven descendant rules: six retired, one promoted.**

| Rule | Fate | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `styles.css:77` luxury hairline card border | retired | belongs to the dark ground that is going away |
| `:78` luxury italic kickers | retired | superseded by the Bricolage / Inter / JetBrains Mono type system |
| `:79` luxury 4% film grain | retired | as above |
| `:145` collect holo sheen sweep | retired | the American arcade register |
| `:279` tech scanline grid | retired | as above |
| `:281` tech chromatic-split headline | retired | as above |
| `:282` tech mono data line | **promoted to a brand-wide rule** | every figure on every surface is JetBrains Mono tabular under the approved direction, so the tech-only quirk becomes the default and the special case disappears |

One of the seven survives, and it survives by ceasing to be per-category. That is the shape of the whole migration.

**The font prerequisite that used to block the promotion is discharged, with one condition.** `carousel/assets/fonts/` contains exactly one JetBrains Mono file — `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2`, re-verified in the directory listing — and `fonts.mjs:20` registers only weight 700. The inherited draft called this a hard blocker on the mono-figure promotion. It is not, because §3.5's type scale specifies JetBrains Mono **700 at every step that uses the face**. **Condition:** if any section later introduces a mono size at 400 or 500, that weight must be added to `carousel/assets/fonts/` and to the `fonts.mjs` face table in the same commit. Both weights are SIL OFL 1.1 and self-hostable. The failure mode is silent — a missing weight synthesises or falls back rather than throwing — so G5 asserts the computed `font-weight` of every mono node is 700.

**Particles and confetti: deleted.** The four skeletons `.p-embers`, `.p-golddust`, `.p-fireflies`, `.p-holo` (`styles.css:258/261/264/267`), the second whitelist regex at `reel-template.mjs:47`, the per-category `particles` field in `config.json` (all six categories carry one), and `config.mjs:10`'s FALLBACK particles all go. Two reasons: embers and confetti are the American giveaway register the visual research says to strip, and `render.mjs:35-38` and `:51-55` build them with `Math.random()`, which makes the still renderer non-reproducible and makes the parity gate impossible.

**The glass theme (`styles.css:157-219`): delete.**

*Verified unreachable, and now with provenance.* `git blame` puts the block at commit `8abc72e`, "feat(carousel): glass theme — modern app UI for the Instagram formats (#26)", authored **2026-08-26**. `config.json` was last modified **2026-09-06** and still does not contain the string `glass`; no file in `carousel/` other than `styles.css` contains it; `themeOf()` (`config.mjs:19`) can only return a string present in `config.json`. So `data-theme="glass"` is never emitted at `render.mjs:182`, `story.mjs:144`, `reel.mjs:101` or `reel-template.mjs:778`. It is nevertheless one of the seven blocks the lift regex returns, so its **44 declarations** are compiled into the CSS text of every Reel, Reel cover and Story build that has ever run, matching nothing. Dead weight that ships.

*Why it is not revived.* The design research finds glassmorphism survived but restrained, not "back"; that blur buys nothing on a static post because nothing moves behind it; that it costs legibility at thumbnail size; and that it is the most dated-looking choice available in 2026. Independently, it is an indigo dark-ground register — the most occupied territory in the UK category, alongside Omaze's navy-and-gold, Elite's black-red-purple and BOTB's dark.

*Two findings inside it must outlive it.*

1. `styles.css:174-176`, verbatim in the file: Bricolage Grotesque's single-storey pound sign is near-identical in silhouette to its own ampersand, and **"OR £30,000" rendered as "OR &30,000" at slide size** — "on a site whose whole pitch is honest, legible prices, an ambiguous £ is disqualifying". Glass's own fix was to swap `--font-display` to Space Grotesk. The approved direction keeps Bricolage for display and puts every figure in JetBrains Mono — so this finding is the *reason* for the mono-figures rule, not a footnote to it. Spec rule: **no `£` is ever set in Bricolage on any surface**, and G5 checks it. It is also why neither new category name below contains an ampersand. *Provenance: an in-repo observation by a past session, not re-measured here.*
2. `styles.css:299-305`: a composite default declared on `:root` resolves against the default theme and inherits down already resolved, because `data-theme` is on `<body>` and `:root` is `<html>`. Emitting scene tokens inline on `<body>` closes this trap for scenes, but the rule stands for anything left in `styles.css`: defaults are inline `var()` fallbacks, never `:root` declarations.

#### `config.json`: the category schema

**The finding that sent me here had the mechanism wrong and the conclusion right, and the distinction matters because it changes the fix.** `config.mjs:13-17` reads, verbatim:

```js
export function catCfg(slug) {
  const c = CFG.categories[slug];
  if (!c) return { ...FALLBACK, name: slug || "Prize", hook: "WIN BIG", seoKeyword: "UK competitions" };
  return { ...FALLBACK, ...c };
}
```

`{ ...FALLBACK, ...c }` is a **merge**, not a branch. A configured category does not stop reading FALLBACK — FALLBACK supplies every key the entry omits. So adding `sports-outdoors` to `config.json` without `audioMood` does **not** make `beat.mjs:16` throw; §6.10's `FALLBACK.audioMood = "win"` still fills it. The build-failure claim is **refuted**. What actually happens is worse and quieter: a partial entry silently inherits `visualWeight: 0.6` and `valueLineMin: Infinity`, so the two categories this rework exists to serve are added to the file and stay exactly as invisible as they were. **A silent default is worse than a throw, and the fix is to make it throw.**

**`CATEGORY_KEYS`, the complete and exact key set — six keys, no more and no fewer:** `name`, `visualWeight`, `seoKeyword`, `hashtags`, `valueLineMin`, `audioMood`.

**`theme` is DELETED, not renamed to `scene`.** Earlier drafts of this section said "`theme` becomes `scene`", which was itself the restatement error this spec exists to end. `SceneDef.id` **is** the slug (8.3), `sceneFor(slug)` is total on the slug alone, and G1 already asserts it returns a distinct non-NEUTRAL scene for each of the eight. A `scene` key would restate the object's own key and could drift from `scene.mjs`. `themeOf()` (`config.mjs:19`) is deleted with it; its four call sites (`build.mjs:154`, `story.mjs:244`, `reel.mjs:237`, `preview-sheet.mjs:25/40`) take `sceneFor(slug)`. `particles` is deleted; `hook` is deleted per §10.6a. Each of the six existing entries therefore goes from 9 keys to 6, and **no surviving value is edited** — car-draws stays 1.0/20000/`driving`, cash-prizes 0.4/5000/`win`, house-draws 0.8/50000/`warm`, tech-giveaways 0.92/3000/`synth`, luxury 1.0/10000/`elegant`, collectibles 0.85/8000/`pop`. `global.drawsPerDeck = 8` is added per §5.11.

**The two new entries, complete:**

```json
"sports-outdoors": {
  "name": "Sports and Outdoors", "visualWeight": 0.88,
  "seoKeyword": "UK sports and outdoor competitions",
  "hashtags": ["#sportsgiveaway", "#ukcomps"],
  "valueLineMin": 4000, "audioMood": "win"
},
"home-garden": {
  "name": "Home and Garden", "visualWeight": 0.78,
  "seoKeyword": "UK home and garden competitions",
  "hashtags": ["#homeandgarden", "#ukcomps"],
  "valueLineMin": 3000, "audioMood": "warm"
}
```

`audioMood` is chosen from the six musical moods in `assets/audio/manifest.json` (`driving` 112, `synth` 112, `elegant` 81, `win` 99, `warm` 103, `pop` 152 — the manifest's own `bpm` fields, which G-C4 reads; **every derived beat, hold, card count and duration is §6.4's and is not restated here**). The seventh entry, `sting`, is a 77KB `.wav` with `bpm: null` and is **never** a legal `audioMood` — it would pass a naive membership test and then divide by `null` in `beatGrid`. `win` for sports-outdoors closes §6.10's open question with evidence: `win.mp3`'s manifest source is Pixabay's *"energetic sports rock music"*. `warm` is the only domestic bed in the manifest and currently has zero live consumers. No new audio asset is required and no bed is orphaned; the two new assignments land on beds §6.4's resolved table already covers, including home-garden's two-card consequence and the condition that recovers the third card, both of which §6.4 publishes.

**What the weights buy, which is the number that decides whether this migration achieves anything.** `select.mjs:41` scores `w × min(pool, N) × 1e9`, at §5.11's deck size N = 8 and its Tier-1 floor `pool ≥ 12`: car 8.00e9 · luxury 8.00e9 · tech 7.36e9 · **sports-outdoors 7.04e9** · collectibles 6.80e9 · house 6.40e9 · **home-garden 6.24e9** · cash 3.20e9. At FALLBACK's 0.6 sports-outdoors scores 4.80e9 and loses to six of seven rivals; at 0.88 it loses only to car and luxury, and beats an `avoidCategory`-penalised car-draws outright (1.0 × 8 × 0.5 = 4.00e9 < 7.04e9), so the day after a car deck a sports deck wins. That is the concrete repair of §1's E3, whose measured before-case is the 10 July deck that published five Mizuno and TaylorMade golf clubs under `WIN LUXURY` with golddust particles. E1 (`WIN BIG`) is closed twice over, by §10.6a retiring the constants and by this section deleting the key; E2 (`valueLineMin: Infinity`) is closed by the authored 4000 / 3000, which clear at the `DRAWS_MIN = 4` floor and not merely at N = 8. **E4 — whether cash-prizes' 0.4 is judgement or drift — is not reopened here.**

#### FALLBACK after the migration

```js
export const CATEGORY_KEYS = Object.freeze(
  ["name","visualWeight","seoKeyword","hashtags","valueLineMin","audioMood"]);

const FALLBACK = Object.freeze({
  name: "Prize", visualWeight: 0, seoKeyword: "UK competitions",
  hashtags: ["#ukraffle", "#livedraws"], valueLineMin: Infinity, audioMood: "win",
});

export function catCfg(slug) {
  const c = CFG.categories[slug];
  if (!c) return { ...FALLBACK, name: slug || "Prize" };
  return c;                    // NO merge. Completeness is a CI gate, not a runtime patch.
}
```

FALLBACK's job afterwards is exactly one thing: **keep `catCfg` total for a slug the pipeline has never seen, so nothing crashes on it — while guaranteeing that slug can never reach a rendered surface.** It is still reachable (`select.mjs:32` buckets any unrecognised slug as the literal string `"other"`, and `catCfg(null)` is legal), but it is no longer a default-supplier for configured categories, so a missing key on a real category is `undefined` at CI instead of a plausible-looking 0.6. `visualWeight: 0` replaces 0.6 as a tripwire, and because `enough * 1e12` dominates weight entirely, zero is not sufficient on its own — **`pickBestCategory` skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories`**, a one-line guard at `select.mjs:33`, and Tier 1 and Tier 2 are evaluated only over configured slugs.

#### The gate: `carousel/tests/config.test.mjs`, rewritten from an enumeration into a derivation

The existing test is the reason this got through — `:5` hardcodes the six slugs, so adding a seventh and eighth category cannot fail it, and `:12`/`:27-28` assert `particles.type` and `themeOf()`, which are the things being deleted. Seven assertions replace it:

- **G-C1 Coverage.** `Object.keys(CFG.categories)` equals, as a set, the eight slugs **imported from `lib/parse.mjs:9`** — never retyped. Fails both directions. This is what binds `config.json`'s key set to the same eight slugs G1 checks, so the two files cannot drift apart.
- **G-C2 Completeness, exact.** For every entry, `Object.keys(entry).sort()` deep-equals `CATEGORY_KEYS.sort()` — **no missing key and no extra key**. The extra-key half catches a `particles` or `theme` that survives the migration in one entry but not another. **If only one of the seven survives review, keep this one.**
- **G-C3 Types.** `visualWeight` a number in (0, 1]; `valueLineMin` finite and ≥ 1000 (below `honesty.mjs:27`'s own floor it is dead config); `hashtags` exactly 2 strings matching `/^#[a-z0-9]+$/` and disjoint from `GLOBAL.fixedHashtags`; `name` and `seoKeyword` non-empty.
- **G-C4 The audio join.** For every entry, `audioMood` appears as a `mood` in `assets/audio/manifest.json` **and that manifest row has a finite numeric `bpm`**. The bpm half is not decoration: it is the only thing that excludes `sting`.
- **G-C5 FALLBACK completeness.** `Object.keys(FALLBACK)` deep-equals `CATEGORY_KEYS`, and G-C3 and G-C4 run against FALLBACK too.
- **G-C6 No silent merge.** `catCfg("car-draws") === CFG.categories["car-draws"]` by **reference identity**. This is the gate's teeth: it fails the moment anyone reintroduces the spread.
- **G-C7 Unknown slug.** `catCfg("mystery-boxes").visualWeight === 0`, and `pickBestCategory` over a pool whose only rows are `"other"` returns `null`.

**Confirmed to pass on the ordinary run**, walked against the post-migration file: eight entries for eight slugs; six existing entries losing exactly three keys and two new entries authored at six; weights 1.0/0.4/0.8/0.92/1.0/0.85/0.88/0.78 all in (0,1]; minima 20000/5000/50000/3000/10000/8000/4000/3000 all ≥ 1000; **all sixteen category hashtags** (12 carried over + 4 new, two per entry) matching `/^#[a-z0-9]+$/` and none colliding with `#prizedrawsdaily`/`#ukcompetition`/`#winbig`, with FALLBACK's own two clearing the same check; `driving`/`win`/`warm`/`synth`/`elegant`/`pop` all present in the manifest with a finite numeric `bpm`. It is a pure static test — no network, no database, no render, no Chromium, no ffmpeg — so it cannot fail flakily and cannot become the gate someone switches off.

**The tests the renames break, named so nobody is surprised:**

- `carousel/tests/config.test.mjs` — the whole file is rewritten to G-C1…G-C7. `themeOf` no longer exists, so `:27-28` go; `:12`'s particles assertion is deleted; the hardcoded six-slug array at `:5` is replaced by the import from `lib/parse.mjs:9`.
- `carousel/tests/render.test.mjs:6-11` calls `buildHtml(draw, "luxury", { type: "golddust", count: 5 })` — the third argument disappears with particles, so the signature changes. `renderSlides()` at `render.mjs:185` carries the same third parameter and loses it.
- `carousel/tests/story.test.mjs` passes `theme: "default"` into `buildStoryTimeline()` in **nine** places (`:21, :31, :38, :44, :50, :57, :58, :63, :68`).

### 8.8 The render gate: `scene-parity`

**Why a new gate is needed.** The only test that touches theme *rendering* today is `carousel/tests/render.test.mjs:6-11` (path corrected — it is under `carousel/tests/`, not a top-level `tests/`), which asserts that `buildHtml()`'s output *contains the string* `data-theme="luxury"` and the string `p-golddust`. It passes whether or not a single scene pixel is painted, and it never touches the Reel, Reel-cover or Story path at all. `config.test.mjs:27-28` tests `themeOf()`, which is a lookup, not a render. `reeltemplate.test.mjs` never mentions themes or tokens — re-verified, zero occurrences of either word. That is precisely the hole the token-lift bug lives in, and a gate that proves "renders identically in spirit across still and video" has to render, decode and compare.

**The gate runs 9 definitions (8 scenes + NEUTRAL) × 4 surfaces = 36 renders**, from fixtures, independent of live inventory, diffed against the four checked-in NEUTRAL fixture PNGs, and writes one contact-sheet PNG for human review.

| | Assertion | Ships |
|---|---|---|
| **G1 Coverage** | `sceneFor()` returns a distinct non-NEUTRAL `SceneDef` for each of the eight slugs at `lib/parse.mjs:9`, and NEUTRAL for `""`, `null`, `undefined` and `"not-a-category"`, without throwing. Every definition declares `amplitudeClass` and `amplitudePx`, and `amplitudePx` is within its class's bound. | blocking, v1 |
| **G2 Token identity** | For each slug, the computed value of every §3.7 palette token read off `<body>` in a headless page is byte-identical across all four surfaces; `SceneDef.tokens` is `{}` or `{"--scene-wash": …}` and nothing else; `--scene-wash`, where set, is identical across the three 9:16 surfaces and absent on `still-4x5`. This is the assertion that makes the CSS lift unnecessary, and it is the one that would have caught the whole bug class. | blocking, v1 |
| **G3 Structural presence** | For each surface and each class *c* in `SceneDef.structural`: render twice, once with *c* suppressed, and diff. Assert *c* paints **≥ 150 px² at \|ΔL\| ≥ 0.010**, measured at dpr 1, **inside** that surface's lane set or scene region, and **0 px² outside it**. This is the direct fix for "renders on the carousel and vanishes from the Reel". | blocking, v1 |
| **G4 Spirit parity** | Render each surface with the scene and diff against its NEUTRAL fixture. Normalise the 4:5 still to dpr 1 first. Compare the still's difference image against each 9:16 surface's, cropped to comparable 950px-wide regions. Assert: tone ink within **±3 percentage points**; dominant edge orientation (Sobel histogram peak) within **±5°**; the scene's single accent within **ΔE2000 ≤ 3**, on the 9:16 surfaces only (the still carries no accent by rule). | advisory ×10 builds |
| **G5 Prohibitions** | **Lanes:** zero scene-diff pixels outside `sceneLanes` (9:16) or `sceneRegion` (4:5) — this subsumes the old `keepOut`, `cropZone` and photo-dominance sub-tests. **Band:** zero scene-diff pixels inside `band`, from either layer. **Tone floor:** no scene pixel darker than the surface's `toneFloor`, evaluated per host ground (on a rail-blue lane the lighten-only 0.016 cap governs instead and is the tighter rule). **No text:** zero text nodes and zero resolved `content:` strings inside the two scene subtrees. **Determinism:** two consecutive renders of the same slug on the *same* surface are byte-identical PNGs. **Typography:** no `£` glyph resolves to Bricolage, and every mono node computes `font-weight: 700`. **Token:** the computed unfilled-dot colour is `#8C8677` on every surface. **Contrast:** every glyph over a newsprint lane ≥ 12:1 and over a rail-blue lane ≥ 6.0:1 against its measured local ground. **Ink:** tone ≤ 10% and coverage ≤ 6% per lane or region. **No border:** fail if ≥ 90% of the outermost 8px ring differs from NEUTRAL while the ring immediately inside it does not. **Amplitude:** render the scene layer at phase 0 and at the declared extreme phase, diff, and assert the diff's bounding-box travel matches `amplitudePx` within 1px and satisfies its class bound. | lanes / band / tone floor / text / determinism / typography / token: blocking, v1. Contrast, ink, border and amplitude: advisory ×10 builds |
| **G6 Loop closure** | Three clauses — see below. | blocking, v1 |
| **G7 Post-encode survival** | G3 and G5's ink thresholds re-run on frames **decoded from the encoded MP4**. G6 clause 1 re-runs post-encode as a **perceptual** check (SSIM ≥ 0.995 between the decoded t=0 and t=`loopMs` frames), not a byte check: x264 inter-frame prediction guarantees two visually identical frames differ in bytes, so demanding byte-identity post-encode would fail every scene forever. | advisory ×10 builds |

**G6, in three clauses.** It runs on the scene fixtures, never on a production reel, which is what makes the fix cost nothing — §8.8 already renders 36 fixtures.

1. **Loop closure.** The `reel-9x16` fixture renders with the insert card **pinned to §6.3's current expanded insert-card rect** (y 661 … 1007 as §6.3 stands, transcluded and not typed here), over a flat NEUTRAL photograph ground. Assert the full-frame PNG at scene-clock t = 0 is byte-identical to the PNG at t = `loopMs`. Lane C paints in both. **Skipped when `loopMs === 0`** (NEUTRAL only). This is the fix for an assertion that, as published, compared a blank card lane at reel t=0 against a painted one mid-loop and would have failed on every scene, every build — and it is why the pin is a pointer rather than a number: the rect has now moved three times, and a typed literal here has been wrong after each move.
2. **Cover parity.** Compare the `reel-cover-9x16` fixture PNG to the `reel-9x16` fixture PNG at t = 0, **restricted to the cover's declared `sceneLanes` = `[R]`**, and **assert that lane set is non-empty before comparing** — an empty set fails rather than passing. That is now an exact and complete comparison, because the Reel's own frame 0 has the card collapsed and carries Lane R only. Both sides are **PNG screenshots of fixtures**, never the delivered `cover.jpg`, which `reel.mjs:246` writes as JPEG q90 and which cannot support a byte comparison at all.
3. **The production seam is not G6's.** §6's own assertion — first and last captured frames differ on fewer than 1.0% of pixels — owns it, and is independent of `loopMs` because Lane C is collapsed at both ends.

**Common case confirmed:** all nine definitions pass. Two periodic fields return at exactly one period; three discrete round trips return to phase 0; two opacity envelopes complete exactly one cycle; house returns after its motion change; NEUTRAL is skipped at clause 1 and compared on Lane R at clause 2.

**The tooling decision, which the inherited draft did not make.** `package.json` lists exactly two runtime dependencies — `cheerio` and `playwright` — re-verified on 17 Sep 2026. There is no `sharp`, `jimp` or `canvas`, and **none is added**. All pixel arithmetic runs inside a headless Chromium page: PNG buffers are handed to `page.evaluate` as data URLs, drawn to an `OffscreenCanvas`, and read back with `getImageData`. Diffing, the luminance-delta count G3 needs, the Sobel histogram and ΔE2000 are all loops over the same `Uint8ClampedArray`, and Chromium is already launched for every render. G7's decode uses the ffmpeg binary the pipeline already shells out to.

**Two costs to name rather than discover.** `carousel/encode.mjs:2` hardcodes `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe`, so G7 cannot run on a Linux CI runner until that path is resolved from `PATH`. And the gate's 36 renders plus their diffs run inside the same Chromium budget as production capture, where `capture.mjs:20` already enforces a hard 5-minute ceiling per reel — the gate must not share that budget.

**Why the expensive half is staged rather than cut.** G3 as specified is itself a diff, so a diff engine is required whether or not G4 and G7 exist; once the engine is there, G4's marginal cost is a histogram over buffers already in memory. G7 protects the two measured risks in the set, and the re-derivation has made the case stronger rather than weaker: sports' rail lane at **0.78% tone ink (ΔL 0.0155)** and tech's rail lane at **0.0207% (1.335% geometric coverage, 6% alpha)** are precisely the large-area, low-contrast gradients libx264 destroys, and `encode.mjs:30` passes `-c:v libx264` with **no `-crf` flag anywhere in the file or anywhere in `carousel/`** — re-verified by case-insensitive grep — so the encode runs at libx264's default CRF 23. A gate that only inspects pre-encode captures would pass a scene that has been quantised out of the delivered MP4. What is cut instead is *blocking status*: G4, G7 and the uncalibrated half of G5 run advisory for ten builds, the observed spread is recorded per scene, and only then are they made blocking — by a named reviewer, not by whoever is on the red build.

**G4's tolerances are design judgement and are uncalibrated.** Do not present ±3pp / ±5° / ΔE 3 as measured values; they are starting points chosen so the gate has something objective to check. The same applies to G5's 10% tone cap, the 0.10/0.016 deltas and the 12:1/6.0:1 floors. **G3's 150 px² floor no longer rests on unlocated geometry:** the smallest structural class on the smallest box is tech's `sc-anchors` at 4 × 2π × 15 × 0.5 + 4 × 40 × 0.5 = **268.50 px²** (0.5px strokes, newsprint) — 536.99 px² at 1px on a rail-blue lane — against a 150 px² floor, a 79% margin at worst. `sc-dims` is 1,305 px² on Lane C and 1,136 px² on Lane R; `sc-contours` is 3,243 px² on every box. The earlier derivation "4 × 2π × 15 × 0.5 = 188 px²" is superseded; the floor value 150 does not move.

**The loop conflict is dissolved, not managed.** §8.5's loops (3,000–5,200 ms) are not integer divisors of §6.4's reel totals, which would have put the scene layer mid-phase at the seam and failed §6.8's assertion on every build. The lane model removes the problem: the only animated lane is Lane C, Lane C lives inside the insert card, and the card is **collapsed on both frame 0 and the final frame**. The only scene visible at the seam is the static rail lane. §6.8's assertion is therefore independent of `loopMs`, and no scene's loop needs deriving from the beat grid.

**Share of frame, so the "majority text" defence is argued on the right number.** The scene adds no opaque area, so §6.3's chrome constants are the ones that bind. *Those constants are §6.3's and are quoted here, not owned:* chrome **261/1920 = 13.594%** collapsed and **116 + 346 + 145 = 607/1920 = 31.615%** expanded, photograph floor **68.385%**, assertable constant `chrome_area ≤ 32%` (= 614.4px, leaving 7.4px of headroom, which §6.6 states independently), on §6.4's 112 BPM / 28-beat / 15.000 s configuration. The time-weighted photograph figure is §6.3's to re-publish from that configuration and is not restated here. **Two superseded sets are retired by name, so neither is verified against again:** 533px / 27.76% / 72.24% / 73.25% / `≤ 28%` (computed on §10.2's 272px card) and 546px / 28.438% / 71.563% / 72.62% / `≤ 29%` (computed on the 285px card). **§8's own derived figures**, recomputed on Lane C = 1080 × 346 = 373,680 px²: the scene *canvas* is **6.042%** of frame collapsed (Lane R alone, 125,280 px²), **24.063%** expanded (125,280 + 373,680 = 498,960 of 2,073,600), and **22.775%** time-weighted. §8's painted-ink figure is a function of the eight per-scene ink totals and is therefore blocked with them until §8.5's re-derivation lands.

**Caveat carried forward on G6.** A seamless loop mechanically inflates views, watch time *and* average watch time without inflating reach, because Instagram counts a replay as a view and includes replays in watch time while dividing by initial views (help.instagram.com/202865988324236). The gate proves the loop is *clean*; it does not license reading loop-inflated watch metrics as evidence a scene works. Scenes are judged on accounts reached and skip rate only — and on carousels, not even that far down: the Graph API exposes no per-child insights. Worse, `carousel/insights.mjs` `mapPayload()` (`:21`) ingests likes, comments, `fb_shares` and reach and **neither views nor watch time nor skip rate**, so even the post-level signal is not being collected yet.

### Decisions this section commits to

- Per-category art direction moves out of `styles.css` into a single shared module, `carousel/scene.mjs`, imported by both the still renderer and the video templates; the three CSS-scraping regexes at `reel-template.mjs:46`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` and the particle whitelist at `reel-template.mjs:47` are deleted.
- §8 owns scene art, the scene module and `config.json`'s category schema. The odds dot grid's geometry, ceiling, block table and above-ceiling encoding are §4.4's and §4.7's; the insert chrome is §6.3's; the Story bands are §7.2's; the conditions band and the `data-pdd-role` enum are §10.2's; asset normalisation is §9's; every BPM, beat count and duration is §6.4's. **§8 publishes no coordinate on 4:5 and no lane literal on 9:16.**
- There are FOUR render surfaces: `still-4x5`, `reel-cover-9x16` (a separate static JPEG built by `reel.mjs:63`), `reel-9x16` and `story-9x16`; five publish formats run over them. Each descriptor now also carries `roles[]` — still-4x5 [cover, count, draw, closing], reel-9x16 [reel-open, reel-card, reel-signoff], reel-cover-9x16 [reel-open], story-9x16 [story] — and `scene.mjs` throws on a descriptor that omits it.
- Scene tokens are emitted as an inline `style` attribute on `<body>`, never as a `:root` or `[data-theme]` block. `SceneDef.tokens` is constrained to `--scene-wash`; no scene sets it today.
- A scene may draw in `--ink`, `--ink-meta`, `--hairline`, `--ground` and `--rail`, never in `--closing`, `--verdict` or `--caution`, and each is alpha-capped by §8.4's two per-pixel rules: as a field `--hairline` ≤36%, `--ink` ≤5%, `--rail` ≤6%, `--ink-meta` ≤8%; as line work `--hairline` 100%, `--ink` ≤15%, `--rail` ≤17%, `--ink-meta` ≤22%.
- On 9:16 the photograph stays full-bleed and the scene renders in **`sceneLanes`**, every one of which is a transclusion: Lane R (§6.3's top rail, currently y 269…385, static), **Lane C (§6.3's insert-card rect, currently y 722…1007, h 285 = 307,800 px² = 14.844%, the only animated lane)**, and the Story's S1 and S2. `reel-cover-9x16` carries `[R]` only. Zero scene pixels outside a lane, and no §8 section prints a lane coordinate as a literal.
- On 4:5 the scene is `back()` only, one tone, no motion, no `stillPhase`. The region is the canvas minus four rects §5 and §4.4 supply and own: **cover 754,220 px² (51.73%), closing 1,134,000 px² (77.78%), draw slide 241,645 px² (16.57%), count slide 307,620 px² (21.10%) at §5's published 750px odds rect — 312,695 px² (21.45%) re-derived against §4.4's bottom-anchored column at the 24-row ceiling**, which is now a render-time computation rather than a frozen figure. The four superseded areas (743,840 / 238,840 / 188,840 / 303,840) are retired.
- The 4:5 frame of reference is the region's full-width body, and the draw slide's body is **y 697…932** at §4.4's settled 565px photo well, not the pre-C1 y 632…867; the 65 × 48 strip at x 1015…1080, y 132…180 is region on every sheet-edged slide but is inside the box only on the cover and the count slide.
- The still renders at `--scene-tone` and darker is forbidden; `#8C8677` clears 3.0:1 on that tone at 3.212:1 and `#948C7C` fails at 2.952:1. `--scene-wash` is retired on this surface.
- Z-order is per surface: on 9:16 photograph 0 → chrome grounds 1 → `#scene-back` 2 → `#scene-front` 2.5 → data 3 → band 4; on 4:5 `#scene-back` 0 → photograph 1 → data 3 → band 4.
- The ground is resolved once per run from the deck's category; only the mark is per draw. A variant may suppress the mark and may never withdraw the ground.
- One mark per 9:16 surface. **Reel slot M suppresses on today's measurements** — §6.3's measured wordmark right edge is x 505.85 against M's left edge 435, a 70.85px overlap — and §10.4's shorter right-hand stamp widens the right gap to 96px and the string-to-string gap to 245.15px without reversing it, because the failure is on the left and 245.15px is still 6.85px short of the 252px a 220px M needs. Seven of eight scenes declare an empty `front()`; the mark ships on the Story, for sports-outdoors, only.
- Ink is two measurements: coverage (opacity-weighted, ceiling 6%) and tone (mean \|ΔL\| ×100, cap 10%), differing by 3.84× for hairline work on paper. The field caps are ≤0.10 darken-only on newsprint and ≤0.016 lighten-only on rail blue; line work is governed by `toneFloor` instead; no rail-blue stroke is thinner than 1px.
- **Amplitude has ONE unit** — canvas px of travel at dpr 1, the maximum distance any painted point moves from phase 0 — and three classes: discrete ≤25px with a returning path, periodic field exactly one pitch (car 45, sports 90), opacity envelope uncapped in travel but gated on its peak phase. `scale ≤ 3%` is deleted. Every scene declares `amplitudeClass` and `amplitudePx`.
- All eight slugs get a scene. Coverage on Lane C: house 4.907% (heaviest), cash 4.19% mean / 4.771% peak, home-garden 4.130%, car 2.568%, sports 2.5%, collectibles ≈1.18%, luxury 0.549%, tech 0.511% (thinnest). tech's anchors, leaders and dimension frame and house's two contour arcs are now fully located; house's motion becomes a 20px round trip because two arcs are not a periodic field; collectibles' wave runs on `c` alone on 9:16.
- An unknown or failed category resolves to NEUTRAL, which after §8.7 guards a path that cannot be selected rather than one carrying 147 draws.
- §8.7 performs the legacy-token and particle deletion and owns `config.json`'s category schema: `CATEGORY_KEYS` is six keys; `theme` is **deleted, not renamed to `scene`**; `particles` and `hook` go; the two missing categories are added at `visualWeight` 0.88 / 0.78, `valueLineMin` 4000 / 3000, `audioMood` `win` / `warm`; `catCfg`'s `{ ...FALLBACK, ...c }` merge is deleted and completeness becomes CI gate G-C1…G-C7.
- The scene-parity gate renders 36 fixtures. G1, G2, G3, G6 and the cheap half of G5 ship blocking; G4, G7 and the uncalibrated half run advisory for ten builds. G6 is three clauses: loop closure on a card-pinned fixture, cover parity restricted to a non-empty `[R]`, and the production seam left to §6.
- §6.8's loop assertion is independent of every scene's `loopMs`.

### Open questions

- **Two binding rulings disagree on the cash ghost's green dot.** The dot-grid ruling deletes it in both states; the above-ceiling ruling has the ghost draw a ghosted green dot iff the data layer draws one. This section takes the deletion, on the argument that a 12%-ink lattice is not countable — but the product owner should be told a ruling was chosen against, not merely applied.
- **Do the four capped accents survive at their capped alpha, or should they be dropped?** §8.4's line-work cap puts car's spine and home-garden's ticks at `--rail` ≤17% and luxury's lot bar at `--ink` ≤15%. That is legal and mechanical, but a 5px spine at 17% is a blue-grey hairline rather than the solid accent the scene was drawn around. This is a look question a render answers in a minute and arithmetic cannot.
- **Does the Reel mark get redrawn, now that §10.4's shorter stamp has moved the ceiling?** §6.3 hands the decision here and computed a ≤133.95px M against the retired `CHECKED 09:00`. With `READ 09:00` the gap is 245.15px and the ceiling is **≤213.15px** — 6.85px short of M as drawn. Redraw at 213px, leave M dead, or spend the 22.5px §6.3 says removing the wordmark's letter-spacing would recover? Nothing is decided here; the arithmetic is on the table.
- `house-draws` has zero enterable draws in the sample, and is now the heaviest scene in the set. Do we build and maintain The Sheet against a fixture indefinitely, or retire the slug from `carousel/config.json` and let `lib/parse.mjs` keep it for the site only? Note that retiring it would fail G-C1 until `lib/parse.mjs:9` changed too — the coupling is deliberate.
- G4's tolerances (±3pp tone, ±5° edge orientation, ΔE2000 3), G5's 10% tone cap, the 12:1/6.0:1 contrast floors and the amplitude bounding-box tolerance are invented starting points. What observed spread across the first ten builds should make them blocking, and who signs that off?
- Does the `draws` table carry any sub-category or tag field for sports-outdoors, or must the marking variant be derived by re-running a keyword match against the title at render time? The latter is what is specified, and it duplicates terms that live in `lib/parse.mjs:434`.
- Sports-outdoors has 102 draws and `lib/parse.mjs` contains zero occurrences of `hockey`, `football`, `rugby`, `cricket` or `tennis`. Genuine taxonomy gap, or an accurate reflection of what operators list?
- The 899 enterable total and the seven per-category counts sum to 897. I did not re-query the database to explain the 2-draw gap.
- **`valueLineMin` 4000 and 3000 are unmeasured.** `honesty.mjs:2` documents `total_prize_value` as gross ticket revenue, not prize worth, so both are set against a revenue estimate (~£1,400/draw sports, ~£1,000/draw home-garden), not a query. Calibrate with one query before the first publish; G-C3's ≥1000 floor catches an absurd value, not a wrong one.
- `encode.mjs:2`'s hardcoded homebrew ffmpeg path: is G7 expected to run in CI at all, or only on the operator's Mac alongside the daily routine?
- Whether §3 will actually add `--scene-tone` as a 15th token and retire `#948C7C`. §8's tone floor and the whole still scene depend on both; the section supplies the arithmetic but cannot land the token.

### Risks

- **This is an animated chrome texture, not an animated backdrop.** The brief said grass, hockey, golf; what ships is mown stripes drifting inside the data card and standing still in the brand rail. It is the only version that keeps the full-bleed photograph and the 71.563% floor at once, but it is not turf behind the prize — and the flag emblem that was to sit in the rail's gap does not ship at all.
- **The per-category focal device ships on one category, on one surface.** Seven of eight scenes declare an empty `front()`, and M suppresses on the Reel and the Reel cover. A reader of "each category its own unique design" will reasonably call that under-delivered, and the honest answer is that the ground carries the identity and the mark is close to a dead mechanism kept alive by one scene.
- **Tech's rail lane is very close to nothing, and tech is a 112 BPM category.** At 1.335% geometric coverage and ΔL 0.015510 it carries **0.0207% tone ink** — 37× fainter than sports' 0.78%, which was already the one measured G7 risk. For the Reel's first 1,071 ms (§6.4's two open beats at 112 BPM) and on the whole of `reel-cover-9x16`, a tech day carries essentially no category signal, and x264 at CRF 23 will almost certainly quantise it out. The alpha knob is closed at 6% by the 0.016 cap; the only remaining lever is geometric — repeating the four-anchor row at a 240px x-pitch to fill the rail lane. That is a scene redesign and I have not spent it. If G7 fires on tech, it is the one-line fix.
- **The Reel's opening second may carry no category signal for any scene.** For that same opening window the only lane present is R, and the same encode risk applies to every definition in it.
- **The still ground may be invisible where it matters most, and the correct response is deletion, not tuning.** ΔL 0.0335 is a 3.67% luminance step. At feed size a 45px-band field resolves; in the profile grid the 1012.5px crop displays at ~120px, an 8.4× downsample, where the line-work scenes average into a uniform wash indistinguishable from NEUTRAL. Only the field scenes (sports, cash, collectibles) survive the grid. If the tone also vanishes at feed size, delete the still scene rather than darken it.
- **The "borders" claim is inherited, not verified.** Meta publishes no geometry for what counts as a border. If Meta's classifier counts any high-contrast full-width horizontal edge, the lanes make an existing exposure slightly worse rather than creating a new one.
- **Deleting the three lift regexes touches every video build path at once**, and nothing currently in `carousel/tests/` would catch a regression. The gate has to land before or with the deletion, not after.
- **Deleting `catCfg`'s merge converts silence into hard CI failures, and that is the point — but it is not free.** The taxonomy and the social pipeline are now coupled: the scraper can no longer add a category unilaterally, and someone will meet a red `bun test` at an inconvenient moment. The recovery is four lines of JSON and the gate names the missing slug.
- **`visualWeight` 0.88 and 0.78 are unmeasured judgement in three significant figures.** No measurement is obtainable — the Graph API exposes no per-child carousel insight. The picker arithmetic is exact; the inputs to it are not. What the numbers *are* is a decision, which is what was missing.
- **Every diffing gate measures against NEUTRAL.** If NEUTRAL drifts, every threshold silently loosens. The checked-in fixture PNGs mitigate this only if changes to them are reviewed rather than regenerated on a red build.
- **Render cost is a still-renderer intuition applied to a video budget.** A 60-column ghost lattice or a tiled crop-mark field is trivial as one PNG and is rasterised once per frame for the length of a reel — at today's 30 fps (`reel-template.mjs:51`, `capture.mjs:6`) that is ~450 frames on §6.4's 15.000 s bed, and more if §6.7 raises the frame rate. Lane C is a clipped, transform-animated field inside an already-animating `overflow:hidden` block, running against `capture.mjs:20`'s hard 5-minute ceiling. §8 raises the prerequisite and does not own the decision; the gate's own 36 renders and diffs must not share that budget.
- **The 4:5 still renders at deviceScaleFactor 2 and the three 9:16 surfaces at dpr 1**, so a 1px hairline is two device pixels on the carousel and one on video — and tech's 0.5px strokes are one device pixel on the still and half of one on video. Whether a 0.5px `--hairline` stroke survives the dpr-2-to-dpr-1 downsample above G3's 0.010 threshold is unverified; G4's normalisation step is the only thing standing between that and a false pass.
- **The whole direction is a light newsprint ground**, and there is no measurement anywhere in the research on how a near-white 4:5 creative reads inside Instagram's dark-mode feed surround. The competitive argument for light is strong — no UK operator or directory owns it — but the legibility argument is untested.
- **Scene performance cannot be attributed.** No per-slide, swipe or completion metric exists; carousel children have no individual insights; Trial Reels needs 200 followers against ~66; `insights.mjs` `mapPayload()` ingests neither views nor watch time nor skip rate. Eight distinct scenes will ship with no mechanism to tell which of them is working.
- **The sports variant map duplicates terms from `lib/parse.mjs:434`.** The sync test catches a dropped term but not a reordered or merged alternation that silently changes which marking a draw gets while every term still exists.
- **Retiring six descendant rules and all particles removes most of what currently distinguishes one carousel day from another** before the eight new scenes are proven. If the module slips, the interim state is eight categories rendering as one flat newsprint template.
- **house-draws is now the heaviest scene and has zero enterable inventory.** Every build pays the full G3/G5/G6/G7 cost of the set's heaviest scene for a category that cannot be selected.
- **Adding `--scene-tone` breaks §3's "the palette is locked to 14 tokens" commitment on its first contact with the scene system.**
- **No scene has ever been rendered, on any surface.** Every coverage figure here is converted from geometry, every luminance from an 8-bit composite, and the located geometries — tech's 268.50 px² G3 margin, house's 17px of border-ring clearance, the 20px arc round trip, the capped accents — are newer still. A single fixture render would confirm or kill any of them in a minute, and none has had that minute. The strongest available claim is that the numbers close, not that it works.
