### Decisions
- KEPT the rewrite's structure and ~90% of its prose. It was sound: the four findings about the deleted strip, the deleted .pcard and the mis-derived master are genuinely fixed, not claimed.
- CORRECTED a real arithmetic error: the rewrite said the widest shipped width demanded without §7.6's Facebook variant is 1000 px. It is 1080 px — the Reel's own full-bleed width. Fixed in §9.3 and in the Decisions list. (With §3.5's gutter settled at 65 px the well itself now ships at 1015 px, and 1353 px under §7.6's variant.)
- CORRECTED the full-tier resolution floor, which was internally inconsistent. At ≥1600×2000 preferred / ≥1185×1482 hard, a source at exactly 1080×1920 (no upscale needed for the Reel at all) would be REFUSED while a 1185×1482 source needing a 1.3x upscale PASSED. Restated the preferred region as ≥1536×1920 — the Reel's 1080 shipped width plus the 456 px of L-notch pan the section itself derives — with hard floor ≥1138×1423, plus an explicit zero-pan path so a no-upscale source is never rejected in favour of a worse one.
- CORRECTED two ceiling-rounding errors: 1600/1.35 = 1185.19 so the floor is 1186 not 1185 (moot after the restatement above), and 1002/1.35 = 742.2 so the still-only height floor is 743 not 742. Every hard floor is now stated as ceil(preferred / 1.35) so the rule is checkable rather than a list of digits.
- CORRECTED a fabrication: the rewrite claimed a case-insensitive grep for `ssim` across the repo returns nothing. It returns one hit — the styles.css:295-305 comment the section itself cites. The substance (no harness exists) is right; the evidence sentence was wrong and is now accurate.
- REGISTRY: removed the counter-chip rect digits (x 70…334, y 32…97). Those encode §3.5's gutter and §5's chip geometry, both owned elsewhere. Replaced with a declared-rect mechanism modelled on the ruling that already has §5 supply exclusion rects to §8, so §9 publishes no coordinates and moves with §5 automatically.
- REGISTRY: removed 'the sheet edge, eight times a deck' — a deck-size digit §5.11's ruling forbids — and it was also off by one (the last draw slide has no next draw). Now 'on every draw slide'.
- REGISTRY: §7.2 band 3 is settled at 950 × 273 (3.48:1) and is §7.2's number, not §9's. The 298 / 340 / 392 range is retired — 392 is unreachable by 114 px on §7.2's own arithmetic. None of §9's floors move with it, because band 3's binding demand is its 950 px width and a shorter band takes less source height.
- REGISTRY: §6.3's photograph share is a 71.563% floor / 86.406% open window and is §6's, carrying §6's own 'my own construction, Meta publishes no threshold' caveat. Attributed, caveat carried, and the cutout argument re-cut so its conclusion (58.4% is below the floor) holds whatever value the constant takes.
- Clarified the sheet-edge rect against the section's own 'shipped pixels' rule: the element is 96 px wide and, with §5.9's hairline at x 1015, 65 of those ship while 31 fall off-frame; the crop is still prepared at 96 because the canvas does the cropping. Also fixed the 192-vs-191.6 rounding and harmonised 0.096:1 to 0.0958:1.

### Open questions
- Closed: §7.2 band 3 is 950 × 273 and §6.3's photograph floor is 71.563%. §9 carries both by reference only, and is still written to survive either moving.
- Does §5 accept supplying the counter-chip rect to the normaliser through a declared-rect channel? It is the mechanism the §8 ruling already uses, but §5 has not agreed to it here.
- Should the full (Reel-capable) tier's preferred region really be the Reel's width plus the full 456 px of pan, or should pan be a soft preference and 1080×1920 the hard preferred? I chose pan-included because the L-notch rule is §6's and cannot be satisfied after the fact, but it costs inventory and nobody has measured how much.

### Risks
- The corrected full-tier floor (≥1536×1920 preferred) is still stricter than the Reel's bare 1080×1920 demand. The zero-pan path stops it rejecting no-upscale sources outright, but it means a source is routinely routed to the still-only tier for a reason — pan slack — that nobody has measured the cost of.
- Every floor in this section remains geometry-derived against a corpus that has never been queried. The section says so, and the measurement now gates §5.11's deck-size constant, but until it runs the whole resolution budget is arithmetic about images nobody has looked at.
- I did not re-verify §12's Q13 numbering, §7.9's Class A/B taxonomy, or §5.12's rule numbering against those sections' current text — only that the claims are consistent with the registry and with the passages I did read. If §7.9 has renumbered, the 'letters are retired' justification needs a fresh citation.
- The rewrite's 40% cutout-yield planning figure, the 20-seconds-per-row QA estimate and the 1.05 MB mean key size are all unmeasured and now carry real load (the cache bound, the operator-minutes line item that §2.7's finding asked for). They are labelled, but a reader skimming the Decisions list will read them as settled.

**Decisions this section commits to**

- §9 continues to own asset normalisation only; every geometry it consumes is now stated as a derivation of the owning section (§3.5's gutter, §5.7's well, §5.9's sheet edge, §7.2's band 3, §6.3's photograph share) rather than as a §9 value.
- Photo well shipped width moves 1000 → 1015 px (and 1333 → 1353 px under §7.6's optional Facebook variant) with §3.5's 65px gutter; the plate cap of 1600 × 2000 is unchanged and still clears both demands.
- Story band 3 is carried at §7.2's settled 950 × 273 (3.48:1) — now the widest crop in the system; the 298/340/392 range and the 2.794:1 figure are retired.
- §6.3's photograph share is carried at 71.563% floor / 86.406% open window; the contested 66.41 / 67.08 / 72.24 / 88.54 set is retired and the cutout-on-Reel refusal still holds with margin.

**Open questions**

- Does §5 accept supplying the counter-chip rect to the normaliser through a declared-rect channel?
- Should the full (Reel-capable) tier's preferred region be the Reel's width plus the full 456 px of pan, or should pan be a soft preference?
- Is §7.6's 1440×1800 Facebook variant worth raising the still-only floor from 1015×1002 to 1353×1336?
- Corpus-wide source-dimension distribution is still unmeasured, so every floor remains geometry-derived.

**Risks**

- The photo-well height range used for the crop-aspect derivation (500–615 px) is read off §4.4's flex-residual ruling; if §5.7's floor or §4.4's block table moves, the well's widest crop aspect (2.03:1) and the 820 px cutout-subject demand both re-derive.
- Nothing at the new geometry has been rendered: the 1015 px well, the 65/31 sheet-edge split and the 3.48:1 band-3 crop are all arithmetic.
- §6.3's photograph share remains §6's own area construction, not a read of Meta's classifier.

## §10 — Compliance gates, built into the renderer (corrected)

## 10. Compliance gates, built into the renderer

Everything in this section is a **gate**: a pure predicate that runs inside the pipeline, returns a named violation, and stops something. Nothing here is advice, a checklist, or a note in a briefing file.

That distinction is not rhetorical. The pipeline already contains a compliance rule that was written as guidance and is therefore not enforced: `carousel/config.json:13` defines `global.bannedPhrases` (eight phrases: "don't miss out", "amazing prizes", "you could win", "once in a lifetime", "hurry now", "act fast", "what are you waiting for", "incredible opportunity"), and the only consumer of that list in the entire repository is `carousel/brief.mjs:11`, which prints it into a Markdown briefing for a human or a model to read. The caption that `carousel/publish.mjs:45` loads from `out/CAPTION.txt` is never checked against it. A banned phrase can be typed into the caption and published, and nothing notices. That is the failure mode this section exists to remove.

The repository already knows how to do this properly, though **not in the carousel pipeline**. `gate.mjs` lives at the *repo root*, not in `carousel/`, and runs at scrape time between the field scraper and the manager — it never sees a slide. Its shape is still the right precedent: `gate.mjs:82-90` layers `requiredGate → schemaGate → businessGate` and returns `{ pass, stage, reasons, draw }`. Two more precedents sit inside the carousel pipeline itself: `render.mjs:193` throws `"refusing to ship a degraded slide"` when fonts or images do not settle, and `encode.mjs:48` hard-fails an MP4 whose audio stream is not AAC. The compliance gates are specified in that family's shape.

**What this section owns, and what it does not.** §10 is the normative owner of four things: the conditions band (§10.2), the evidence and provenance contract (§10.4), the permitted wording for odds copy (§10.6a), and — new, by the CAP 8.17 field-5 ruling — the `data-pdd-role` enum and the `DRAW_CARRYING` predicate that scopes every asset-level assertion in the document. It owns the gate machinery, the failure classes and the enforcement points. It owns no geometry outside the band, no type scale, no track width, no gutter, no ceiling, no block height and no deck size. Where a number below belongs to another section it is cited, not restated — the duplication is what broke this document.

**One track, and §10 no longer hedges about it.** §3.5 is the sole owner of `--gutter` (65px), the 950px chrome track (x 65 … 1015) and the 895px content well (x 65 … 960). The band sets on the chrome track on every surface: **950px, x 65 … 1015**, which is Meta's Safe Box A width on both canvases. The earlier practice of measuring against "the narrowest of 940 / 950 / 952" is retired — 952px at x 64 … 1016 was 1px outside Box A and never existed, and 940px was the retired 70px gutter. Every width below is quoted against 950px and against nothing else.

**How the measurements in this section were taken.** Every string width quoted below was measured in-session by summing real glyph advances from the bundled `woff2` files in `carousel/assets/fonts/` with fontTools, at the stated size. They are advance sums, not rendered line boxes: they bound the fit but do not account for shaping, kerning pairs or hinting, so §5.3's measured-fit rule at render (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`) remains the binding check and these figures are the budget it is expected to clear. The faces are confirmed bundled and loaded at `carousel/fonts.mjs:3-22`. **JetBrains Mono 700 is measured at exactly 0.600em** (`hmtx` 600 / `unitsPerEm` 1000) for every digit, the colon, the space, the middot and every uppercase letter used in this section's stamp and annotation, so all mono arithmetic below is exact rather than nominal. Mono 500 is not in the repository and no section may specify it. **Bricolage 800 is measured at 0.674038em uppercase and 0.6005em for digits** — the second figure closes §10.6a's previously-unmeasured digit-advance gap. Where a headline is quoted as a set of line boxes, the boxes are a greedy word wrap run against the stated measure with the same real advances, not a character estimate.

**Inter 500 is gone, and this section's band was re-measured because of it.** §3.4 retires Inter 500 from the stack and §3.8 deletes the file. §10.2 previously set L2 and L3 in Inter 500 and asserted the spec was "renderable as written"; that was false against the delivered §3.8. **L2 and L3 now set in Inter 400**, the running-copy weight §3.5 already assigns, and every L2/L3 width in this section has been re-measured at 400. The direction is favourable — Inter 400 is 8–13px narrower per line at 38px — and the re-measurement is published below rather than inferred. §3.4 and §12.1 still disagree on the surviving-face count (6 against 8, the gap being Bricolage 400 and Inter 500); that reconciliation is theirs, not §10's, and it does not move a number here.

---

### 10.1 Where the gates live and when they run

A new module, **`carousel/compliance.mjs`**, deliberately mirroring the root `gate.mjs`: pure functions, no I/O, each returning `{ ok, violations[] }`, plus a combined `complianceGate(assetModel)` returning `{ pass, stage, violations[] }`. It is also the one place the role predicate is authored:

```js
const DRAW_CARRYING = new Set(["count", "draw", "reel-card", "story"]);
```

Four values, authored once. No section restates the list; sections reference `DRAW_CARRYING`.

It is enforced at **four** stages, because the same rule can be broken at four different layers. The CI stage is new and is the primary control for wording (§10.6a); the other three are the rendering pipeline.

| Stage | Insertion point | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| **CI** | `carousel/tests/odds-copy.test.mjs`, `carousel/tests/allowlist-conformance.test.mjs`, and a repository grep gate, all in the test job | A permitted string edited without a reviewed fixture change; an odds literal written into a renderer instead of imported; **an allow-listed string that a §10.6 predicate rejects — caught in the test job, never in the daily build** |
| **MODEL** | `build.mjs` before `renderSlides()` (`build.mjs:156`); `reel.mjs` before `buildReelTimeline()` (`reel.mjs:236`); `story.mjs` before `buildStoryTimeline()` (`story.mjs:247`) | A draw whose data cannot legally be rendered at all; **and the post-level field-5 gate: for each publish format, at least one draw-carrying asset carries a non-empty prize name, and on the carousel the count equals `drawsRendered`** |
| **DOM** | stills: inside the Playwright page between `render.mjs:191` (`waitForFunction("window.__ready === true")`) and `render.mjs:195` (`page.screenshot`). Video: in `capture.mjs` between the `page.evaluate((t) => window.__seek(t))` at `capture.mjs:21` and the `page.screenshot` at `:22`, on **three sampled frames per role run** — at `t_start + 300ms`, the midpoint, and `t_end − 300ms` | A CSS regression that hides, shrinks or occludes something the model says is present |
| **PUBLISH** | `publish.mjs` between the object literal at `:172` and the `Bun.write` of `publish.json` at `:173`; the re-hash control is specified in §10.7 and is **dormant until a first-party posting step exists** | Caption and alt-text violations, which never pass through the renderer |

**Video sampling is per role run, not per scene.** `window.__seek(t)` — already called at `capture.mjs:21`, verified — returns `{ t, role, drawIndex }`, derived from the same beat table that generated the scene keyframes (§6.4). The gate reads the returned role; it never infers a role from computed opacity. The 300ms floor clears §6.4's 200ms row-swap and §6.8's 270ms sign-off collapse, so no sample lands mid-transition. The binding case is the shortest run in the five resolved beds — elegant.mp3 at `signOffBeats = 3` gives a one-beat sign-off run of 740.74ms, leaving a 140.74ms window with samples at 300 / 370.37 / 440.74ms, distinct and ordered. That window is what forces §6.4's `signOffBeats >= 3`.

The DOM stage is not redundant, and §10.2 explains the specific architectural reason it is load-bearing here rather than merely prudent. The PUBLISH stage is not sufficient on its own, and §10.7 explains why: `publish.json` is not what reaches the platform.

**One thing that is deliberately *not* a gate.** Provenance is enforced as a **selection predicate** in the PostgREST query, not as a render-time failure. §10.4 sets out why; the consequence for this subsection is that a draw without fresh, methodful evidence never reaches the MODEL stage at all, so no gate here can be starved by it.

---

### 10.2 G1 — The conditions band

**§10.2 is the sole normative owner of the conditions band**: the six CAP 8.17 fields, where each is discharged, the three band lines and their exact strings and states, the 38px/45px type contract, the 135px type block, the shared scene module, and the band's gate classes. It is additionally the sole owner of **`data-pdd-role`, the eight role values, the `DRAW_CARRYING` set, and the rule that band variant, L1's amber state, L2's host and L3's free-entry state are all selected by that predicate.** Every other section states only its own surface's y-range and padding and links here for content. No other section states a field list, a string, a type size, a role list, a variant rule or a character capacity for this band.

**Why.** Prize competitions and free draws sit outside Gambling Act 2005 licensing, so the operative code is CAP Section 8 (Promotional marketing). CAP 8.17 lists significant conditions including how to participate, any free-entry route, the closing date, and the number and nature of prizes. The binding constraint is the ASA's position that it is *unlikely to consider social media posts sufficiently limited by time or space*, and is likely to expect **all** significant conditions in the post itself.

**"Link in bio" does not discharge this, and it is in four places, one of which nobody had flagged.** `caption.mjs:19-20` emits exactly the string `link in bio · 18+`; `brief.mjs:26` instructs the caption model to end every caption with `link in bio · 18+ · UK only · Play responsibly`; and — new here — **`story.mjs:152` renders `LINK IN BIO · @prizedrawsdaily` on the Story frame itself**, so the phrase is not merely caption furniture, it is a rendered instruction to look somewhere that is not the post. All three are deleted, and the Story's link line is replaced by the band's L2, which names a host the viewer can actually type.

**Current state (verified in-session).** There is no conditions band on any asset. Every still renders `<div class="footer">…<span class="rp">18+ · UK ONLY · PLAY RESPONSIBLY</span></div>` (`render.mjs:69`, `:122`, `:157`, `:172`) at **19px** (`styles.css:367`), positioned `bottom:44px` (`styles.css:363`). The video templates render the same string in `.rfoot` at **24px**, `bottom:36px` (`reel-template.mjs:394-396` + `:789`; `story.mjs:107-109` + `:155`; and a third copy at `reel.mjs:105`). On the 9:16 canvas `bottom:36px` puts that footer at y ≈ 1860-1884 — inside Meta's 768px bottom exclusion and across the action rail, so it has been rendering underneath Instagram's own UI. (The 4:5 still footer at `bottom:44px` is not under IG chrome; its defect is size, not position.) Of CAP 8.17's significant conditions, **none** currently render. `entry_url` is selected at `select.mjs:14` (verified) and used only to scrape photographs (`fetchimg.mjs:170`); it never reaches a slide.

#### Every frame declares one role, and the role is what scopes this gate

Every rendered frame declares exactly one value of a closed eight-value enum, `data-pdd-role`. The mechanism already ships: `render.mjs:182` writes `data-type="${slide.type}"` onto `<body>` today from `build.mjs:150`'s `[intro, ...drawSlides, {type:"cta"}]`, and `story.mjs:144`, `reel.mjs:101` and `reel-template.mjs:778` each write `data-theme` onto `<body>` at the same point — all four verified on disk. `data-pdd-role` is written in those same four places. No new plumbing.

| Role | Frames | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `cover` | still-4x5 slide 1 (today `type:"intro"`) | deck-level |
| `count` | still-4x5 slide 2 | **draw-carrying** |
| `draw` | still-4x5 slides 3 … N+1 | **draw-carrying** |
| `closing` | still-4x5 slide N+2 (today `type:"cta"`) | deck-level |
| `reel-open` | reel-9x16 open-window frames **and the whole of reel-cover-9x16** | deck-level |
| `reel-card` | reel-9x16 card frames | **draw-carrying** |
| `reel-signoff` | reel-9x16 sign-off frames | deck-level |
| `story` | story-9x16 (single frame) | **draw-carrying** |

The role is an **input** to the gate, supplied by the caller; the DOM attribute exists only so the two can be cross-checked. For stills, the Story and `reel.mjs:63 buildCoverHtml()`, the caller passes the role it just rendered and the gate asserts `document.body.dataset.pddRole === expectedRole`; a mismatch is class A (`role-mismatch`). The Reel is one document with every scene stacked under opacity keyframes, so `<body>` cannot carry a per-frame role and the role comes from `window.__seek(t)` (§10.1). Role runs on the Reel, in order: `reel-open` → `reel-card` × N → `reel-signoff` → `reel-open` again for the final two beats, because §6.8's loop rule restores frame 0's picture there; N+3 runs per reel.

**Five role-instances a day carry no prize name**, not the three a casual count finds: `cover`, `closing`, `reel-open`, `reel-signoff`, and `reel-cover-9x16` — which is `reel-open`, being frame 0 of the Reel. The Reel cover was missed by both of this subsection's earlier string tables.

#### The band is three lines, identical in structure on every asset PDD ships

Inter, **38px / 45px leading = 135px of type**, measured at render against §3.5's 950px chrome track. L1 is Inter 600 uppercase; **L2 and L3 are Inter 400 sentence case** — the running-copy weight §3.5 assigns, after §3.4 retired Inter 500 and §3.8 scheduled the file's deletion. Padding is per-surface; the 135px type block is not.

**Draw-carrying asset** (`DRAW_CARRYING.has(role)`):

| Line | Exact rendered string | Type |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | `CLOSES TOMORROW (WED) · £129.99 A TICKET` | Inter 600 38px, `#F7F5F0` on rail blue `#14385F` |
| L2 | `Enter · terms · thecollectorsclubcompetitions.com` | Inter 400 38px, `--rail-meta` `#B9C6D6` |
| L3 | `Free-entry route and age limits: in those terms.` | Inter 400 38px, `--rail-meta` `#B9C6D6` |

**Deck-level asset** (every other role):

| Line | Exact rendered string |
|---|---|
| L1 | `8 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` |
| L2 | `Enter · terms · each operator's own site.` |
| L3 | `Free-entry routes and age limits: in those terms.` |

**The variant is selected by the predicate, not by a prose list.** The draw variant renders iff `DRAW_CARRYING.has(role)`; the deck variant otherwise. The earlier prose enumeration — "cover slide, closing slide, Reel sign-off" — omitted `reel-open` and the whole of `reel-cover-9x16`, both of which carry the band (§6.3 makes it one of three pieces present on every frame of every reel). A prose list of surfaces is exactly the artefact that goes stale when a surface is added; the predicate cannot.

L1's draw count is `drawsRendered` (§5.11) and is never a literal. L1 renders `closesLabel()` with §10.3's `kind` argument, so it reads `CLOSES …` or `DRAWN …`, **date only** — §10.3 forbids a stated time of day on every surface in v1, and that includes this line.

**The amber caution state is scoped to draw-carrying roles.** When the stored close is inside 48 hours, L1's **text** switches to signal amber `#FFC53D` — not caution red. Caution red `#B3202C` on rail blue computes to **1.80:1** and is illegal here; amber on rail blue is **7.56:1**, and §10.5 rule 3 already reserves amber for chrome and closing state. Caution red survives only on paper grounds, as §5.7's closes chip. **Deck-level L1 renders `#F7F5F0` unconditionally**, because `8 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` contains no close and the amber rule has no input on it; without this scoping §10.5 rule 3's colour assertion either fails or passes vacuously on five roles a day. On the carousel the amber state fires only in the 24–48h band of a selection, since `plan.mjs:13`'s `MIN_DAYS=1` floor keeps selected draws ≥24h out.

**L2 and L3 are scoped the same way.** L2's registrable-host identity check and L3's four-state `free_entry_route` machine run on draw-carrying roles only — both read a per-draw column that has no value on a deck asset. On deck-level roles L2 is the frozen string `Enter · terms · each operator's own site.` and L3 the frozen plural `Free-entry routes and age limits: in those terms.`, both checked by fixture equality under §10.6a's L1/L3 regime rather than against a row.

L3 has exactly four states, one per value of `draws.free_entry_route` (new nullable column, enum `postal | online-free | none-stated | unknown`, default `unknown`), **all re-measured at Inter 400, 38px**:

| State | String | Inter 400 | (was, Inter 500) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unknown` | `Free-entry route and age limits: in those terms.` | **843.1px** | 853.1 |
| `postal` | `Free postal entry. Age limits: in those terms.` | **789.3px** | 799.7 |
| `online-free` | `Free online entry route. Age limits: those terms.` | **851.0px** | 862.2 |
| `none-stated` | `No free-entry route stated. Age limits: those terms.` | **915.0px** | 927.0 |

Until the column is populated — 100% of inventory today — every asset renders the `unknown` string. It neither asserts nor denies a free-entry route, so CAP 3.7 is satisfied. `free_entry_route = unknown` is **never** a failure of any class.

#### The fit, on one track, at one weight

Every width below is measured at 38px against §3.5's **950px** chrome track. There is no longer a narrowest-candidate argument, because there is no longer more than one candidate.

| Line | Face | Width | Slack on 950 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draw L1 worst `CLOSES TOMORROW (WED) · £129.99 A TICKET` | Inter 600 | 889.1px | 60.9px |
| Draw L2 worst, 33-char host `thecollectorsclubcompetitions.com` | Inter 400 | 891.6px | 58.4px |
| Draw L3 worst (`none-stated`) | Inter 400 | 915.0px | **35.0px** |
| **Deck L1 worst `10 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99`** | Inter 600 | **928.0px** | **22.0px** |
| Deck L2 | Inter 400 | 716.7px | 233.3px |
| Deck L3 | Inter 400 | 863.2px | 86.8px |

A typical draw L1, `CLOSES THU 25 SEP · £2.99 A TICKET`, is 705.2px; a typical deck L1 at 79p and eight draws is 832.4px.

Two things improved and one did not. The move to the single 950px track and to Inter 400 takes the number of lines with under 40px of slack from **three to two**: L2 gains 23.1px (35.3 → 58.4 at the new track and weight), L3 gains 22.0px (13.0 → 35.0), and deck L1 gains the 10.0px the wider track adds (12.0 → 22.0). The binding case is still **deck L1, now at 22.0px** — its 928.0px width is untouched by the weight change, because L1 is Inter 600, so every pixel it gained came from the track. **Draw L3 at 35.0px is the only other line inside 40px.** §5.3's measured-fit rule governs and is retained as the mechanism: fit is measured at render, never counted in characters. On L1 overflow the build applies exactly one documented shortening — ` A TICKET` → `/TICKET`, measured saving **32.4px** (889.1 → 856.7) — and then fails.

Sentence case on L2 is load-bearing, not styling: the same string uppercased measures **1,141.2px** at Inter 400, **28.0% wider**, and does not fit. Lowercase is also the correct typographic form for a domain, so the compliance answer and the design answer coincide.

**44px still does not fit, and the proof survives the weight change.** At 44px, L2 measures **1,032.4px** at Inter 400 and L3's `none-stated` state measures **1,059.4px** — over 950 by 82.4px and 109.4px respectively. (At the retired Inter 500 the same two lines were 1,047.5px and 1,073.4px.) Both independent proofs hold at the delivered weight.

#### Where the six fields are discharged

Five of six are in the band; exactly one is in the slide body.

| # | CAP 8.17 field | Discharged by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | How to participate | L2, naming the host of `draws.entry_url` |
| 2 | Free-entry route | L3 |
| 3 | Closing date | L1 |
| 4 | Entry cost | L1 |
| 5 | Number and nature of prizes | **The slide body**, scoped by role — see G1-P below |
| 6 | Where full T&Cs live | L2, the same host as field 1 |

#### G1-P — the field-5 assertion, scoped by role rather than by surface or canvas

The previous form of this assertion — "the prize-name element exists, is non-empty, and is at or above its surface's step" — was unscoped, and as written it fired on every deck-level asset, which is five role-instances a day. It would have hard-failed class A on every run and nothing would ever have published. §10.2 already distinguished a draw band from a deck band for exactly those surfaces; the field-5 assertion now follows the same split.

**G1-P, class A, MODEL + DOM, on `DRAW_CARRYING` roles only.** Selector: exactly one `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node in the asserted subtree.

- **(a)** `count === 1`;
- **(b)** `normalizeWhitespace(textContent).length >= 1`;
- **(c)** computed `font-size >=` the resolved value of §3.5's `--fs-lead` token — written against the token, never a literal, in the discipline of §10.5 rule 2;
- **(d)** `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` (§5.3's measured-fit mechanism);
- **(e)** the rect lies wholly inside the canvas and, on any surface whose §8 descriptor has a non-empty `keepOut`, wholly inside `surface.safe` and wholly outside `surface.keepOut` — read from the descriptor, not from an `if canvas === 9:16` branch.

**The floor resolves to one number, so no per-surface table is published.** The count slide steps 88 → 68 → 56 (§5.7), the draw slide the same, Reel Row B is fixed at `--fs-lead` (§6.3), and the Story's band 2 steps 68 → 56 (§7.2) — each section's own ladder, cited here only to show that they coincide; §10 publishes no ladder of its own. Every floor is `--fs-lead`. All four draw-carrying surfaces resolve to the same step, which is why this assertion needs no table and gets none.

**The gate is two-sided.** On a role not in `DRAW_CARRYING` the assertion does not run and its absence is not a violation of any class — but a `[data-pdd-claim="prize-name"]` node **present** on a deck-level role is itself class A (`prize-name-on-deck-asset`). Scoping is not an escape hatch.

**The cover discharges field 5 in its own right, at zero cost.** It carries no prize-name node, and it does not need one: §5.4's board names three prizes in its Prize column plus a `+{N−3} more inside` row, and the proof line and band L1 carry the count. That matters more than it looks, because the cover is the slide most often seen alone. The closing slide and the Reel sign-off carry neither nature nor a specific prize, and are discharged post-wide by the other children of the same post; that exposure is named in the risks rather than argued away.

**The post-level gate, MODEL stage, class A.** The compliance unit is the published post, not the frame, so the discharge is machine-checked rather than asserted: for each publish format, `count(assets where DRAW_CARRYING.has(role) && prizeName non-empty) >= 1`, and on the carousel `=== drawsRendered`. `reel-cover-9x16` needs no discharge — it is the Reel's thumbnail, not one of §8's five publish formats (ig-carousel, ig-reel, ig-story, fb_photo, fb_video). This gate is not optional garnish: it is the only thing that catches a `draw` slide mislabelled `cover`, which would otherwise skip G1-P entirely and publish with no prize name, silently.

#### Two things this band cannot be made to carry

**`ENTER ON OPERATOR SITE` does not satisfy field 1 and is deleted.** Three reasons, one dispositive: the Reel and the Story carry no link and no tappable element, so a phrase naming no route leaves the viewer unable to participate; the ASA's position that social posts are not space-limited means there is no space defence; and the space defence is now measurably false, because L2 fits at 891.6px with 58.4px to spare. The generic phrase was solving a budget problem that does not exist.

**A category word cannot be added to deck L1 to carry "nature" at deck level, and the arithmetic is not close.** Measured at Inter 600, 38px, against the 950px track: `10 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99` is 928.0px; `10 CAR DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99` is **1,018.0px**, over by 68.0px; `10 TECH GIVEAWAYS DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99` is **1,287.0px**, over by 337.0px. The friendly case `8 CAR DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` measures 922.4px and fits — which is the trap, because §5.3's measured-fit rule would then hard-fail the build on a legitimate ten-draw £129.99 tech day. Deck L1 carries number only. (These are advance sums for the whole strings; they replace the earlier per-glyph-mean estimates of 1,012.4px and 1,244.4px, and reach the same verdict by a larger margin.)

**The entry HOST is band chrome and is not cuttable. The operator's display NAME is editorial and remains cuttable.** These two have been conflated across §2.6 S2, §5.13, §6.3, §6.4 and §6.5, and the conflation is what produced the apparent deadlock over whether the Reel can carry operator identity. They are different objects with different legal status. The host in L2 is a CAP 8.17 significant condition (how to participate, where the terms live), it sits in fixed-position standing chrome that repeats on every card, and it is therefore **excluded from §6.5's per-card read budget and may never be cut** — which is how the Reel discharges S2 without needing an exemption written for it. The operator's display name (`Rev Comps`, `Elite Competitions`) discharges no CAP 8.17 condition, carries no legal weight, and stays exactly where §6.5 puts it: a cuttable editorial field. Nothing in §10 requires the operator's name on any frame.

**`1 PRIZE: 2023 VW GOLF R` is deleted.** PDD stores `grand_prize`, not a prize count. Rendering a numeric count is the same CAP 3.7 defect the section spends a paragraph refusing to commit on free entry. The nature of the prize is already the largest or second-largest element on every draw-carrying asset; it does not need restating in 38px chrome, and restating it would cost the line L2 now occupies. The number PDD *can* evidence is its own deck count, which the counter chip and cover proof line already carry.

**One host does both jobs, and the uppercase alternative is arithmetically dead.** The obvious separate T&Cs line, `FULL T&CS AT THECOLLECTORSCLUBCOMPETITIONS.COM`, measures **992.9px at 34px** in Inter 600 — over 950 on its own, at the smallest size anyone proposed, before any separator or stamp shares the line with it. At 38px it is 1,109.7px. There is no size at which the uppercase form fits, which independently forces the sentence-case, host-only L2 that discharges fields 1 and 6 together. Where `operators.website_url` differs in registrable domain from `draws.entry_url`, the band names the **entry** host, because that is the page the entrant must read at the point of entry. The previously specified widening of `select.mjs:14` from `operators(name)` to `operators(name,website_url)` is therefore **retired** — G1 no longer needs it. (§10.4 widens the same query for a different reason.) A PDD-owned per-draw URL was considered and is not pursued: the research crawl logged `prizedrawsdaily.co.uk/category/cash` returning 404, so URL stability on that domain cannot be assumed, and a pointer that 404s is worse than one that leaves the frame.

**`18+` and `UK ONLY` are both deleted from every asset.** The age clause folds into L3 as a pointer to the operator's terms, because nothing in `carousel/` or the root `gate.mjs` applies an age filter and `operators` has no `min_age` column, so a bare `18+` is an unevidenced objective claim about someone else's terms. `UK ONLY` is the same class of claim and is worse, because PDD stores no territory field on `draws` or `operators` at all — it is simply dropped, not replaced. The previously specified substitute `AGE LIMITS SET BY THE OPERATOR — SEE THEIR T&CS` is also deleted: measured at Inter 600, 38px it is **1,025.7px** and overflows on its own. §3.8, §5.3, §6.3, §7.2 and `honesty.mjs`'s alt-text suffix all take this wording; none may restate it.

**Free entry is the honest hole.** Verified against the live schema: `draws` has exactly `id, slug, operator_id, category_id, title, prize_description, image_url, ticket_price, prize_value, draw_date, entry_url, affiliate_url, status, featured, created_at, updated_at, total_prize_value, grand_prize, total_entries, category_source`, and `operators` has `affiliate_url, cons, created_at, description, editorial_intro, established_year, faq, featured, id, is_legit_summary, logo_url, name, pros, rating, review_status, seo_description, seo_title, slug, specialism, trust_notes, trustpilot_url, updated_at, verdict, website_url`. There is no free-entry field in either, and the parser does not extract one. The gate must therefore not invent one. `draws.free_entry_route` is Stage 0 item 0f (§10.4): column only, default `unknown`, no parser work, and **not a render blocker**.

#### Geometry, per surface

| Surface | Band rect | Height | Padding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carousel 1080×1350 | x 0…1080, type on §3.5's chrome track (950px, x 65…1015), y 1182…1350 | **168px** = 16.5 + 135 + 16.5 | 16.5px top and bottom |
| Reel / Reel cover 1080×1920 | x 0…1080, type on the same 950px track, y 1007…1152 | **145px** = 5 + 135 + 5 | 5px top and bottom |
| Story 1080×1920 | identical to the Reel: y 1007…1152 | **145px** | 5px top and bottom |

The carousel envelope is §5.3's existing 168px, unchanged — 16.5 + 45×3 + 16.5 = 168 holds at any leading ≤ 45px, so the section that did the most careful geometry needs no geometry change at all. On 9:16 the text bottom lands at y 1147, inside §6.1's 2px guard at 1150; the band's own bottom edge is y 1152, which is Safe Box A's floor and the L-notch ceiling, and nothing crosses it. The Reel and Story share one set of coordinates and one module, per the token-lift trap below. §6 and §7 fund their 145px from deletions specified in their own sections; §10.2 does not spend their budgets a second time. The `bottom:36px` video footer is retired outright — it has never been inside the safe area.

**38px is a named exception to §3.5's eight-step scale, and §3.5 must carry it as one.** The type-scale ruling proposes that this field resolve to 34px on a still and 44px on video; as the band's owner this section overrides that for this band only, because neither number survives its own arithmetic. At 44px L2 is 1,032.4px and L3's worst state is 1,059.4px, both over 950. At 34px the same legal content sits below the floor this section derives, and the same legal content on the same 1080-wide canvas cannot be legible at 34px on a still and illegible at 38px on a video. §3.5's T3 assertion enumerates legal sizes; unless 38px is enumerated as this band's exception, the type gate fails every asset on day one.

**38px is a design judgement, and should be read as one.** It is 2.0× the current 19px still footer and 1.58× the current 24px video footer, but a multiple of what is already shipping is not a legibility standard — the ASA publishes no numeric threshold for a significant condition, and none of these figures has been eyeballed on a handset. 38px is the largest size at which all six fields demonstrably fit three lines; that is its whole defence.

#### ⚠ The token-lift trap — why this band cannot be a plain CSS class

`reel-template.mjs:46-47`, `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` each build their CSS by regex-scraping `styles.css`. `story.mjs` and `reel.mjs` run a single pass, `/(?:^|\n)\s*(?::root|\[data-theme="[^"]+"\])\s*\{[^}]*\}/g`, which matches `:root{…}` and `[data-theme="x"]{…}` and nothing else. `reel-template.mjs` runs that pass at `:46` **and a second, explicitly enumerated pass at `:47`** for the four `.p-(embers|golddust|fireflies|holo)` particle blocks — which is worth stating precisely, because it is also the proof that deleting those blocks from `styles.css` is what removes particles from video (§10.6). What no pass matches is an arbitrary class. A rule such as `.condband{…}` added to `styles.css` would style the carousel correctly and **silently vanish from the Reel and the Story** — producing exactly the uncompliant asset this gate exists to prevent, with no error anywhere. Therefore: **the conditions band ships as a shared scene module that `render.mjs`, `reel-template.mjs` and `story.mjs` all import, emitting both markup and its own scoped CSS. G1 must not be enabled before that module exists**, or the DOM stage hard-fails every video, every day, for a reason the operator will read as a false positive and route around. This sequencing is a hard dependency, not a preference.

#### Contrast, and one token with no owner

Calculated here with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula; these are calculations, not tool measurements. Newsprint `#F7F5F0` L = 0.9137, rail blue `#14385F` L = 0.0380. The weight change from Inter 500 to 400 moves none of these.

- L1 newsprint on rail blue = **10.9:1**
- L2 / L3 `#B9C6D6` on rail blue = **6.87:1**
- L1 caution state, signal amber `#FFC53D` on rail blue = **7.56:1**
- Caution red `#B3202C` on rail blue = **1.80:1** — forbidden on this band, and the reason the caution state is amber

**`#B9C6D6` has no owner and must acquire one.** §3 is the sole owner of the colour token table and the `:root` block; `--rail-meta` `#B9C6D6` is not in it, and a repository grep confirms the hex appears nowhere in `carousel/`. §10.2 quotes it because it measures a contrast ratio against it, not because it defines it: **§3.7 must add `--rail-meta: #B9C6D6` to its `:root` block**, since it renders on every asset PDD ships and currently has no definition anywhere. Until it does, the band is specified against a literal with no token behind it, which is the same defect §5.14's parallel token table was filed for.

#### DOM assertions

**Scoped to the band, by selector.** The per-line assertions run against `[data-pdd-band] > [data-pdd-band-line]`, and `count === 3` is itself asserted. **G1 measures nothing outside the band.** This matters: an unscoped `fontSize >= 38px` over the document fails the carousel masthead's Slot B dated stamp and §5.4's cover dateline, both at `--fs-micro` = 34px < 38px, on every still, every day.

Per line: computed `fontSize >= 38px`; computed `opacity >= 0.92`; `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`; the element's `getBoundingClientRect()` lies wholly within the canvas and wholly inside `surface.safe` and outside `surface.keepOut`, read from §8's surface descriptor rather than from an `if canvas === 9:16` branch; and the band's own background is opaque (`backgroundColor` alpha = 1, no `backdrop-filter`).

The blur pattern is present in the codebase and will be copied by default unless forbidden: `styles.css:339` applies a literal `backdrop-filter: blur(4px)` to `.rank`, and `.pill` (`:328`) takes a tokenised `backdrop-filter: var(--pill-blur, none)` at `:333`, with the same shape again on `.card` at `:310` and `.title-block` at `:344`. A band at 38px that is 40% opaque over a photograph is not legible and must not pass.

Field 5 is asserted separately, by G1-P above, on `DRAW_CARRYING` roles only.

### 10.3 G2 — The countdown gate

**Why.** CAP 8.22: promoters must not claim consumers must respond by a specified date or within a specified time if they need not. The DMCC Act 2024 consumer provisions, in force 6 April 2025, ban creating false urgency including fake countdown timers.

**Current state (verified), and this is the sharpest finding in the section.** `lib/parse.mjs` **manufactures a time of day when the operator's page prints none**, at four sites:

```js
// lib/parse.mjs:21  (normalizeUkDate)
return d ? `${d[1]}T20:00:00${ukOffset(naive)}` : raw;
// lib/parse.mjs:350
const time = m[4] ? `${pad(m[4])}:${m[5]}` : findTime(t, m.index) || "20:00";
// lib/parse.mjs:391 (parseDateFragment)
const time = (text != null && idx != null && findTime(text, idx)) || "20:00";
// lib/parse.mjs:398
if (iso) return normalizeUkDate(`${iso[1]}-${iso[2]}-${iso[3]}T20:00`);
```

Nothing in the row records whether the time was read or substituted.

**MEASURED, with its caveats stated.** A 1,000-row sample of `status=active` draws pulled from the live DB on 2026-09-17 (the first 1,000 rows PostgREST returned, unordered — *not* a random sample) contains 45 distinct times of day; the top five account for **65.9%**; and **104 rows (10.4%)** carry exactly `19:00:00+00:00`, which under `ukOffset()`'s BST branch is 20:00 UK — the parser's substituted default. Two honesty notes the figure needs. First, the winter form of the same substitution stores as `20:00:00+00:00`, which is a further 82 rows (8.2%); the two buckets together (18.6%) are an **upper bound** on substitution, not a point estimate, because genuinely-parsed 8pm draws land in the same buckets and are indistinguishable from substituted ones — which is the whole problem. Second, the sample is drawn from 1,792 `status=active` rows, of which only **883** are future-dated and therefore enterable, so it over-represents historical parses relative to the set the carousel actually selects from.

Two further problems. First, `draw_date` is the **draw** time, not the entry-close time — `README.md:44` states the parser prefers "draw-time preferred over close-time". Entry normally closes before the draw, so a clock counting to `draw_date` counts to the wrong event, and `closesLabel()` compounds this by prefixing every such date with the word `CLOSES`.

Second — and this corrects a claim that does not survive checking — the current fallbacks do not merely degrade, they **fabricate**. `story.mjs:125` reads `const closeIso = draw.draw_date || nowIso`, which renders a frozen `00:00:00` clock rather than failing; the comment at `story.mjs:243` asserting that `closeIso` "is the REAL draw_date — never synthetic" is contradicted by its own file 118 lines earlier. Worse, on the Reel: `reel.mjs:234` can resolve `closeIso` to `null`, but `countdownHtml()` never receives that null, because `reel-template.mjs:750` intercepts it —

```js
// reel-template.mjs:750 (arm C)
const cIso = closeIso ?? new Date(Date.parse(nowIso) + DEFAULT_LEFT_MS).toISOString();
```

— where `DEFAULT_LEFT_MS` is `3h 47m 22s`, declared at `reel-template.mjs:138-139` under a comment at `:136-137` describing it as a "deterministic default clock for callers that don't pass real times (tests)". A test sentinel is wired into the production arm-C path. With no closing date at all, the Reel therefore ships a **plausible, invented, ticking 03:47:22 countdown** — a fabricated deadline, which is the precise thing DMCC 2024 names. That is materially worse than a visibly broken render, and it is the single highest-severity defect this section addresses.

#### The gate: no `HH:MM:SS` clock ships in v1, and neither does a stated time of day

An `HH:MM:SS` clock — the `.flipclock` device (`reel-template.mjs:112-125`), used by `countdownScene()` (`reel-template.mjs:666-684`) and by `story.mjs:151` — renders only when all four hold:

1. The stored close is an **entry close**, not a draw time.
2. The time was **read from the operator's page**, never substituted.
3. The value is **immovable**: a fixed stated close, not a sell-out-triggers-the-draw condition. Where the close is "when the last ticket sells", no clock, ever.
4. The value **agreed across two separate fetches on different days, on the time of day**. `README.md:19-22` defines the two-fetch agreement as "same ticket price, same cap, same UK draw **day**, matching title, clean `fieldFlags`, and an image that provably loads" — it agrees on the *day* and says nothing about the time, so today's published rows carry no time-level corroboration whatsoever.

Condition 4 is unsatisfiable against the shipped agreement check, and widening that check is **out of the v1 critical path**. Therefore **the flip clock does not ship in the first implementation, on any surface**, and the previously specified `closes_at_kind` and `closes_at_source` columns are **removed from v1's dependency list**: carrying two columns and a `verify.mjs` widening to enable a device its own gate keeps disabled is pure cost. They return when someone wants the clock.

**A stated time of day is the same claim as a clock.** A rendered `CLOSES SUN 9PM` asserts a response deadline exactly as a ticking `04:12:38` does, and if the 9PM came from `lib/parse.mjs:350`'s `|| "20:00"` it is a deadline that does not exist. So the four conditions govern a stated time as well, and in v1 no time of day renders anywhere — not in §10.2's L1, not in §6.3's Row A, not in §7.2. Everything is date-only.

**The ladder, in descending precision**, using `closesLabel()`'s actual output (`format.mjs:41-51`):

| Condition | Renders | Status in v1 |
|---|---|---|
| All four gate conditions met | `04:12:38` flip clock, labelled `UNTIL ENTRIES CLOSE` | **unreachable** |
| Verified entry-close date, ≥2 days out | `CLOSES SUN 21 SEP` | live |
| Verified entry-close date, tomorrow | `CLOSES TOMORROW (SUN)` | live |
| Verified entry-close date, today | `CLOSES TONIGHT` | live |
| Only a draw date is known | `DRAWN SUN 21 SEP` — a new string; `closesLabel()` gains a `kind` argument, because it currently hardcodes the word `CLOSES` for what is a draw date | live |
| Date missing or unparseable | the draw is dropped (class B, §10.8) — never a zeroed, defaulted or invented clock | live |

`story.mjs:125`'s `|| nowIso` and `reel-template.mjs:750`'s `?? DEFAULT_LEFT_MS` fallback are both deleted; `DEFAULT_LEFT_MS` stays available to the test suite only.

**`time_defaulted` still ships**, in Stage 0 (§10.4, item 0g), and the four `20:00` substitution sites are still removed. That is a fabrication fix and it does not depend on the clock: the parser must stop inventing a time whether or not anything renders one, because the invented time is stored, published to the website, and indistinguishable from a real one forever after.

**This gate and the brand agree.** The competitive teardown recorded `HH:MM:SS` countdown pills as the single most saturated UI element in the UK category, observed top to bottom. The compliant behaviour and the differentiating behaviour are the same behaviour, which is why this is cheap to accept.

---

### 10.4 G3 — The evidence and provenance contract

**§10.4 is the sole normative owner of the evidence and provenance contract**: the three column names and types, the method enum and its renderable allow-list, the 48-hour window, the selection-predicate enforcement point, the MODEL-stage re-check and its class split, and the exact stamp string. §4.9 references this subsection and restates none of it. §12.4 owns only the ordering (Stage 0 and its exit criterion).

**Why.** CAP 3.7: hold documentary evidence for objective claims before publication.

**Current state (verified).** No figure carries a source or an observation time. The `draws` table's only timestamps are `created_at` and `updated_at`, and `updated_at` is a row-write timestamp — it moves on any write, including one that changed a different column, so it is not evidence that a *figure* was observed. The odds figure is derived at `format.mjs:53`:

```js
export const oddsLabel = (n) => (n ? `1 IN ${Number(n).toLocaleString("en-GB")}` : null);
```

from `total_entries`, which `README.md:43-44` defines as the **max cap** with "sold/remaining counts vetoed". So `1 IN 13,995` is the odds **at full sell-out** — the worst case — rendered today as an unqualified present-tense fact. It is conservative rather than exaggerated, which keeps the current render clear of CAP 8.20/8.21; **3.7 applies regardless of direction**, which is why this gate exists even though nobody is being flattered. (`oddsLabel()` itself is retired from every rendered surface by §10.6a; it survives only inside `brief.mjs`'s non-rendered facts table.)

#### One evidence model, row-scoped, three columns

The abstract per-figure triple `{ value, source_url, observed_at, method }` is **deleted**. Three new columns on `draws`, following the shipped `category_source` precedent exactly — enum text, DB `CHECK` constraint, validation in `manager/draw-update.mjs`:

```
draws.figures_source_url    text          — the operator URL actually fetched for this row
draws.figures_checked_at    timestamptz   — when that fetch happened (NOT updated_at)
draws.total_entries_method  text          — CHECK against the enum below
```

Row-scoped, not per-figure, because `ticket_price`, `total_entries` and `draw_date` are all read from one fetch of one page in one instant by `fieldsFromHtml`. Nine columns for one observation is redundant. Only `total_entries` has an extraction path whose confidence varies, so only it carries a method.

`category_source` (`rule | claude | manual`) is a working, shipped, CHECK-constrained provenance column on the same table, validated at `manager/draw-update.mjs:24-32` (verified) with a five-line comment explaining exactly why a typo must not become an opaque 400. Copying a pattern that already has a validation site, a DB constraint and a measured distribution is strictly cheaper than inventing a per-figure object with no home in a relational row.

#### The method enum, derived from the actual `??` chain

Verified at `lib/parse.mjs:724-729`. Two corrections matter and both are fatal in opposite directions.

| Value | Written by | Renders |
|---|---|---|
| `operator-pattern` | `extractEntries` step 0, `op.patterns.entries` from `operators.json`, reached through branch (a) | yes |
| `labelled-cap` | `extractEntries` tier 1 / 1b (the two `strict:true` branches, `:726` and `:727`) | yes |
| `derived-sum` | `ltyCap`, `lib/parse.mjs:687-694` — sold + remaining, scoped to the progress-bar element | yes |
| `progress-bar` | `extractEntries` tier 2, `takeDenom` | yes |
| `bare-count` | `extractEntries` tier 3, the noisy unlabelled grab | **no** |
| `agent-read` | `manager/draw-insert.mjs`, `manager/draw-update.mjs` | yes |
| `manual` | `qa-fix.mjs`, hand PATCH | yes |
| `NULL` | every row written before Stage 0 | **no** |

**`operator-api` is not in the enum and must never be added.** `lib/parse.mjs:670-682` documents that this path was deleted on purpose: the Woo/Shopify stock count is tickets **remaining** and falls every day (1p Gaming 1,382,267→1,381,767; Flash Cash 998,574→998,291), and the comment states outright that `apiStock` "must never stand in for a cap." A remaining count understates the denominator and flatters the odds — the one direction of error the whole odds device is built to be immune to. An enum listing it as renderable re-introduces that breach and labels it evidenced.

**`derived-sum` and `operator-pattern` must be in it.** They are branches (d) and (a) of the five-branch `??` chain. Omit them and every `lottery-for-woocommerce` row falls through to `NULL`, is classed ineligible, and the whole operator family vanishes from every deck with no error.

**`progress-bar` stays renderable, and it is the judgement call with the least support.** `takeDenom` captures the denominator with a `b >= a` guard, and `lib/verify.mjs:77-79` already refuses to publish any row whose cap moved between fetches ("a cap does not move — likely a stock counter"), so a progress-bar value that reached `status=active` has passed a two-fetch no-drift test. But `lib/parse.mjs:151-155` names tiers 2 *and* 3 as the leak path by which a draw scrapes a stranger's ticket count off a multi-comp listing page — and a stranger's cap does not drift either, so the agreement check would not catch it. If Stage 0's measurement shows `progress-bar` rows concentrated on multi-comp listing operators, this value moves to the non-renderable side and the allow-list shrinks to five.

**Branch (a) is the one soft edge in the mapping.** `:725` calls `extractEntries(entriesSel, op.patterns)` non-strict against an operator-scoped selector, so it can return a step-0 override *or* a tier-1/2/3 result from within that selector's text. The mapping above assigns it `operator-pattern` on the ground that the selector is itself operator-authored configuration; item 0b must return the tier that actually fired rather than assume, or a tier-3 grab inside a scoped selector would wear a renderable method.

#### One window: 48 hours

The browser sweep runs 07:00 UTC daily (verified, `.github/workflows/aggregate.yml:14`), JSON sweeps at 01/13/19 UTC, and the carousel build runs mid-afternoon. Normal age at build is roughly **8h** — a design estimate of build time, not a measurement. A single missed observation — the documented datacenter-403 class, where GitHub runners get `woo API 403` on URLs a residential IP serves fine — jumps the age to roughly **32h**. Two consecutive misses gives roughly **56h**.

So 24h and 48h differ only in whether they tolerate one miss: 24 < 32 < 48 < 56. A 24-hour ceiling rejects every operator refused once, and single misses are the normal condition on this inventory, not the edge. "A figure older than one cycle is not current" argues for 48, not 24, because one cycle measured at the build is 24h plus build lag. In-repo precedent agrees in direction: `carousel/freshness.mjs:11` already uses a 36h dead-man's switch — one cycle plus slack — and 48h is the same idea rounded to exactly two cycles so that it composes with `MIN_OBSERVATION_GAP_MS`'s day-apart rule.

#### Enforcement is a selection predicate, not a render gate

This is the decisive move and it is what makes day one possible. The filter goes in the PostgREST query inside `fetchEndingSoon` (`carousel/select.mjs:9-22`, verified), beside the existing `image_url=not.is.null` eligibility predicate at `:18` — not in JS after the fetch, or the `limit=300` at `:20` is spent on ineligible rows:

```js
u.searchParams.set("figures_checked_at", "gte." + new Date(Date.now() - 48*3600e3).toISOString());
u.searchParams.set("total_entries_method",
  "in.(operator-pattern,labelled-cap,derived-sum,progress-bar,agent-read,manual)");
```

Consequences, all binding:

- A draw without fresh, methodful provenance is **never selected**. It cannot be dropped at render, cannot collapse a slot, cannot consume a backup, cannot reach §10.8's class-C ceiling.
- **The class-C row for a stale odds figure is deleted** (§10.8). An odds figure never collapses its slot.
- Nothing is dropped from the deck for provenance, because nothing was ever picked.
- §2.6's S1 (publish every calendar day) and the evidence gate stop competing. The first run does not hard-fail; it draws from a smaller, evidenced pool.

The three sections that previously specified this disagreed about the failure class because all three asked the wrong question — they put the check *after* the deck exists, at which point every answer costs something. `image_url=not.is.null` is the same shape of predicate for the same reason: a draw whose photo is missing is not a draw with a broken slide, it is a draw that was never a candidate.

**The restart consequence, which the predicate does not remove.** The pipeline last published on 2026-07-03; today is 2026-09-17. Every stored figure is older than 48h and none carries a method, so on restart the predicate matches **zero rows** — `fetchEndingSoon` returns an empty payload, `pickBestCategory` returns null, and `plan.mjs:41`'s empty-pool path fires, which §10.8 now makes a named class-A record with a non-zero exit. That is correct behaviour and not a bug, but it means **the restart sequence must run a full sweep before it renders**, and Stage 0's exit criterion is the thing that confirms the sweep worked.

#### The MODEL-stage re-check is still load-bearing

`plan.mjs` freezes full draw rows into `selection.json` (`plan.mjs:75`) and `build.mjs:17` reads that file a run later, so a stamp captured at plan time can age past 48h while a human sits on the shot list. At the MODEL stage, before `renderSlides()`:

- `figures_checked_at` older than 48h at build time → **class B**. Drop the draw, promote from the pool. Ordinary operator delay, not a bug.
- `total_entries_method` NULL or `bare-count`, or `figures_source_url` NULL → **class A**, non-zero exit. The selector cannot have emitted one; if it did, something bypassed the query and nothing may ship.

#### No warn-and-render flag

A flag that defaults to warn-and-render until the columns are backfilled is **refused**. An unstamped `total_entries` may be a sold count, a per-person cap, or a neighbouring comp's number (`lib/parse.mjs:151-155`; `qa-fix.mjs:5`; a live row at 99, below `plausibleEntries`' own floor of 100 at `lib/parse.mjs:149`) — all of which understate the denominator and show better-than-real chances, CAP 8.20/8.21. CAP 3.7 requires evidence held **before** publication. A flag that publishes an unevidenced odds claim is not a staged rollout, it is the breach — and it is the `AUTO_PUBLISH`-shaped switch §10.8 itself warns gets left on.

#### The scope collision is resolved by narrowing the exclusion, not by staging the gate

§12.3's "Aggregator / scraper accuracy work" exclusion means exactly four things: which pages are fetched, which draws are selected for the site, how categories are classified, how operators are scored. Recording provenance about a figure the scraper already reads changes none of those — it is a derivation over work already done, the same boundary §12.5 R9 draws for Stage B asset normalisation. Schema and parser work that a render gate depends on is therefore **in scope**, as a blocking Stage 0 in §12.4, ahead of Stage A.

#### Stage 0 — the complete, bounded dependency list

Nothing else is added to it.

| | Item |
|---|---|
| 0a | Migration: the three columns, the `CHECK` constraint on `total_entries_method`, and a btree index on `figures_checked_at` (the new query predicate). |
| 0b | `extractEntries` (`lib/parse.mjs:155`) returns `{ value, method }` instead of a bare number — five value-returning sites (tier 0, tier 1, tier 1b, tier 2, tier 3). The `??` chain at `:724-729` maps branches to methods; branches (b) and (c) are `strict:true` so they are always `labelled-cap`. |
| 0c | `run.mjs` writes all three columns on **every** observation, including the `no-correction` branch. |
| 0d | `manager/draw-update.mjs`'s `ALLOWED` set at `:20` gains the three columns, with `total_entries_method` validated against the enum in the same place and the same way `category_source` already is at `:24-32`. Without this every agent-corrected row is permanently ineligible. |
| 0e | `qa-fix.mjs` sets `total_entries_method='manual'` on rows it patches. |
| 0f | `draws.free_entry_route` — column only, enum `postal | online-free | none-stated | unknown`, default `unknown`, no parser work, **not** a render blocker (§10.2). |
| 0g | `time_defaulted boolean`, plus removal of the four silent `20:00` substitutions at `lib/parse.mjs:21`, `:350`, `:391`, `:398`. A fabrication fix, not accuracy work (§10.3). |
| 0h | Backfill: leave `total_entries_method` NULL on every existing row. **Do not guess** a method for a value whose path was never recorded — a guessed `labelled-cap` is a false provenance claim, which is worse than none. One full daily sweep re-stamps every reachable live draw. |

**0c is the one a builder will miss.** Verified: `run.mjs:358-368` handles `plan.kind === "skip"` with `plan.reason === "no-correction"` by logging and `continue`-ing at `:368`, writing nothing. A stable, correct cap that the parser re-confirms every day would therefore never have its `figures_checked_at` moved, would cross 48h on day three, and would silently remove itself from the eligible pool. The symptom — the deck shrinking over a week for no visible reason — would look like inventory decay, not a missing write. A no-change observation must still PATCH `figures_checked_at` and `figures_source_url`.

**Explicitly not in Stage 0, and therefore not blocking:** `closes_at_kind` / `closes_at_source` and the widening of the two-fetch agreement to compare time of day (§10.3 — the clock does not ship, so they buy nothing); and `operators.instagram_handle` across 60 operators (nothing refuses to render without it; the operator name is already selected and the handle lives in the caption, not the frame).

#### One stamp per asset, and where it renders

The evidence made visible. **Exactly one rendered stamp per asset** — a second restatement anywhere is an unpermitted string under §10.6a. The wording law: `read from` is the only permitted verb, the timestamp is mandatory, and `verified` is forbidden.

Two deterministic forms, both sourced from `min(figures_checked_at)` across the deck's draws, rendered Europe/London, in JetBrains Mono 700 at the face and weight the dated-stamp slot already uses on each surface:

| Form | String | Glyphs | Width, Mono 700 | Renders in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Long | `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` | 34 | 693.6px @34 · **897.6px @44** | Story band 1 |
| Short | `READ 09:04` | 10 | 204.0px @34 · **264.0px @44** | Reel and Reel-cover top-rail right slot; **carousel masthead Slot B**; the cover's dateline (§5.4), composed into §10.6a 1.2's string |

**A slot's free measure, not the bare track, is the fit test.** At a measured 0.600em the long form fits a *bare* 950px chrome track at either size, and the build steps down one step on overflow and fails if neither fits — but a bare track only exists where no second slot shares the row. The carousel masthead is the case that proves it. Slot A is `PRIZEDRAWSDAILY`, Inter 700 44px at +0.08em = 480.5px, ending at x 545.5, so Slot B's real measure is 1015 − (65 + 480.5 + 24) = **445.5px**, not 950. The long form right-aligned to x 1015 begins at x 321.4 and overlaps Slot A by **224.1px** — a §5.2 build stop, and because Slot B is suppressed only on slide 1 it would fire on slides 2–10 of every deck. The step-down escape does not exist either: `--fs-micro` 34px is already T3's lowest legal step for this slot. **Slot B therefore carries the SHORT form**, which begins at x 811.0 and clears Slot A by **265.5px**. The short form is licensed on a still by this section's own rule — it is permitted wherever the surface's alt text carries the full sentence, which is every surface under §10.7. The long form keeps Story band 1, which has no second slot and which §7.2 measures at 897.6px against 950 — **52.4px** of headroom, re-checked on this same occupancy rule and unaffected. This closes §5.2's open question: §5.2 supplies the measurement, this section makes the assignment.

**The cover is the one still that carries the short form, and it does not double-stamp.** §5.2 suppresses masthead Slot B on slide 1 — a glyph there would sit inside the profile-grid keep-out — and moves the stamp into §5.4's dateline, which already carries the day's date; that is why the short form rather than the long one goes there. The composed dateline `THU 18 SEP 2026 · READ 09:04` is 28 glyphs = **571.2px at `--fs-micro`**, inside the 895px well with 323.8px to spare. One asset, one stamp.

**Three sections must take these strings, and one clearance moves materially.** §5.2 currently publishes `CHECKED 18 SEP 09:00` (20 glyphs, 528.0px @44), §6.3 publishes `CHECKED 09:00` (13 glyphs, 343.2px @44) and derives its rail right-slot occupancy from it, and §7.2's settled band-1 row quotes `CHECKED 09:00 · WED 17 SEP` (26 glyphs, 686.4px @44) and derives 263.6px of headroom from it. All three take §10.4's forms — §5.2 and §7.2 the long form, §6.3 the short — and re-derive. The consequences, measured:

- **Story band 1.** The long form is 897.6px at 44px on §7.2's 950px track, leaving **52.4px** of headroom rather than 263.6px. Band 1's 55px height is a 44/50 line box plus 5px of slack and does not move, so §7.2's five-band sum of 883px is untouched. §7.1 withdrew the category word from the Story rail on the old headroom; it stays withdrawn, now by a far larger margin.
- **Reel top rail.** The short form is 79.2px narrower than `CHECKED 09:00`. Right-aligned to x 1015 its left edge is x 751.0, against mark slot M's right edge at x 655 — a right-hand clearance of **96.0px**, up from 16.8px, which was fractionally inside §8.3's 16px suppression threshold. **This does not rescue M.** The Lane C ruling measures the wordmark at Bricolage 800 = 418.35px before tracking, ending at x ≥ 483.35 against M's left edge at x 435, a clearance of **−48.35px**. M suppresses on the left regardless of what the right-hand slot does, and §8.3 must state that conclusion rather than carry the old estimate.

**The stamp does not become a fourth conditions-band line, and the arithmetic against it has strengthened.** It cannot share a line with the T&Cs pointer: measured, `FULL T&CS AT THECOLLECTORSCLUBCOMPETITIONS.COM` alone is **992.9px at 34px** in Inter 600, already over 950, and the long stamp beside it takes the line to roughly **1,690px** — an overflow of about 740px, not a near miss. But the dispositive constraint is height. A fourth line costs 45px, and §6 and §7 funded the band's 145px from deletions with no slack left:

- **The Reel.** §6.3's expanded chrome is 116 + 285 + 145 = **546px of 1920 = 28.438%**, against its assertable ceiling `chrome_area ≤ 29%` = 556.8px — **10.8px of headroom**, and a photograph floor of 71.563%. A 190px band takes chrome to 591px = **30.781%**, over the ceiling by 1.781pp = 34.2px. (These are §6.3's constants on its 285px insert card, quoted not owned; the earlier pair, 533px / 27.76% / 72.24%, was computed on §10.2's superseded 272px card and is retired here. If §6.3's Row C grows again, the chrome figure grows and this refusal only gets stronger.)
- **The Story.** §7.2's five bands sum to 55 + 145 + 273 + 245 + 145 = 863, plus four 5px gutters = **883 exactly**, which is Safe Box A's height. (Those five heights are §7.2's, cited here for the proof; §10 owns none of them.) There is no slack at all: a 190px band 5 gives 928px against 883, over by the full 45px.

The existing dated-stamp slot on each surface costs nothing and already exists. That is why the stamp lives there and the band stays at three lines.

**The full sentence lives in alt text, which has no space budget.** `honesty.mjs:31-37` appends to every draw-carrying asset's alt text: `Ticket cap read from <registrable domain of figures_source_url> at <HH:mm>, <D MMM YYYY>.` Bare registrable domain, never a full URL, never a link. The short form is permitted only on a surface whose alt text carries this sentence — which is every surface, per §10.7. CAP 3.7 requires evidence **held**, not displayed adjacently, so the display position is editorial; one place beats two, and the machine-readable place beats both.

#### One live mislabel this gate must fix

`honesty.mjs`'s header comment (`:2-3`) states that `total_prize_value` is gross ticket revenue (entries × price), not prize worth. Confirmed by direct query: in every sampled row `total_prize_value` equals `ticket_price × total_entries` to the penny — e.g. `0.02 × 299,999 = 5,999.98`, stored as `5999.98`. There is no honest alternative field: the `prize_value` column exists but is **null on every row sampled**, so the database holds no figure for what a prize is actually worth. `capValue()` (`honesty.mjs:19-23`) caps the revenue figure at the operator's own stated cash alternative *where one parses*; `carousel/tests/honesty.test.mjs:34` confirms the documented behaviour that with no cash alternative "revenue stands". `build.mjs:135` then passes that sum into the intro slide and `render.mjs:139` renders it as `${value} IN PRIZES`. A ticket-revenue figure labelled "IN PRIZES" is precisely the shape the ASA upheld against Amazing Giveaways Ltd in 2025 (could not fund the prize on tickets sold). The gate makes the label impossible: **a `capValue` sum may only carry ticket-revenue-derived wording, never "in prizes" or any synonym.** This rule is unchanged and is not negotiable.

#### The sell-out qualifier

`total_entries` is a cap, so an odds figure derived from it is the odds **at full sell-out** and may never render as an unqualified present-tense fact. The requirement stands; **the wording is §10.6a's**, and the conditional now travels inside the claim's own text run rather than as a separately-sized qualifier line. §10.5 rule 1's old ratio test went with it.

---

### 10.5 G4 — The emphasis rule

**Why.** CAP guidance, verbatim: *"Promoters should ensure that the page design, layout or format of the promotion is not misleading. Promoters should not embolden or otherwise emphasise claims to create an overall impression that is not true."* Type size, weight, colour and position are a compliance surface, not styling.

**Current state (verified).** The template emphasises exactly the wrong things:

```js
// render.mjs:67
<div class="closes"><b>${esc(d.closes)}</b>${d.odds ? ` · ${esc(d.odds)}` : ""}</div>
```

`.closes` is 33px (`styles.css:358`); `.prize` is 98px (`styles.css:346`). The odds figure — the one datum no operator publishes and the whole honesty proposition — renders at **0.34×** the prize name, as a trailing fragment after a middot, with no element of its own. Worse, `styles.css:360` sets `.closes b { color: var(--hot); font-weight: 700; }`, putting the deadline in the hot accent while the odds stays plain white: the design literally emphasises urgency over probability, and does so with the one CSS declaration in that block. The Reel repeats it — `urgeChip()` (`reel-template.mjs:473-476`) prefixes the deadline with a `⚠` hazard glyph at `:475`, which is emphasis applied to a commercial closing date.

**The gate.** Three machine-checkable rules, asserted at the DOM stage against computed styles, on nodes carrying `data-pdd-claim="odds"`.

**1. The conditional travels inside the claim.** No figure on any surface carries a qualifier in different type. Every conditional sets in the same text run, at the same size, weight, colour and opacity, as the claim it conditions. Asserted as: no descendant of a `data-pdd-claim="odds"` node has a computed `font-size`, `font-weight`, `color` or `opacity` differing from the node's own.

This replaces the old "qualifier renders at ≥50% of its figure" ratio, which is **deleted**. The ratio was unbuildable in both directions: at a hero-size figure it demands a qualifier so large that `IF ALL 4,500,000 TICKETS SELL` overruns the band by hundreds of pixels; keeping the qualifier at legend size fails the ratio instead. Putting the conditional inside the claim's own run (`Odds at sell-out: 1 in 699.`) dissolves the conflict: **the ratio now has nothing to measure, by construction**, and CAP's emphasis guidance is satisfied structurally rather than numerically. §3.5's T4 adjacency rule governs the figure-and-label lockup where one is used.

**2. The odds figure is a co-equal claim, not a fragment.** Odds is not a qualifier of the prize; it is a co-equal claim about the same offer, with its own element and its own type step. Asserted as two comparisons, neither of which publishes a number of its own:

- the odds-figure node's computed `font-size` equals the resolved value of §3.5's `--fs-figure`; and
- it is **greater than or equal to** the prize-name node's computed `font-size` on the same frame.

This is deliberately written against §3.5's token rather than a literal, because a DOM assertion holding a hard-coded pixel floor is exactly how a gate comes to fail every legitimate render on day one. §3.5 owns the hero-figure floor and the scale; §10.5 asserts conformance to it. The second comparison is the rule that carries the CAP argument and the Recommendation-Guidelines "adds material value" argument, and §3.5's T1 guarantees it by construction (the prize name's largest step is below `--fs-figure`), so the assertion cannot produce a false positive once the templates land. The 0.34 ratio at `render.mjs:67` is what it replaces.

**3. Colour is emphasis.** Palette semantics are enforced, not conventional. Caution red `#B3202C` only on a deadline, and never on rail blue (§10.2: 1.80:1). Signal amber `#FFC53D` for chrome and closing state only. Verdict green `#0F6B45` and mint `#E6F2EA` only on **a figure whose row satisfied §10.4's eligibility predicate** — that is the definition of a checked fact, replacing the deleted evidence triple. (Green on mint computes to 5.69:1, so the pairing is legible at the sizes in play; legibility was never the constraint on it — meaning is.) The gate reads computed `color` on every claim element and fails on any mismatch; verdict green touching an unevidenced figure is a hard fail, because the whole point of that colour is that it means "we checked".

Rule 3 is why the DOM stage exists. A refactor that moves the odds into a green span is a compliance regression, and only computed style catches it.

**Rule 3 has an unresolved conflict and a hard ordering dependency.** §5.13 specifies a Trust Score chip — `PDD 4.2` in ink on mint with a green border — and §5.4 sets the cover proof line's figures in green including a deck count. Neither is a figure on a row with a `figures_checked_at`; both are PDD's own computed assessments. As written, rule 3 fails every draw slide and every cover. The colour semantics are §3.2's to set, not §10's, and there are two honest outcomes: §3.2 widens the green rule to admit PDD's own evidenced assessments and defines what evidence a Trust Score must carry, or §5.4 and §5.13 restyle in ink and meta grey. **G4 rule 3 must not be enabled until one of those lands** — the same ordering discipline §10.2 applies to the scene module, and for the same reason: a gate that hard-fails every asset on day one for a reason the operator reads as a false positive gets bypassed, and a bypassed gate is worse than no gate.

**G4's tone baselines must be re-derived before calibration.** §8's four still scene-region areas moved with the gutter (cover 51.73%, draw 16.57%, count 21.10%, closing 77.78% unchanged). Every §8.4 ceiling is a percentage of its region, so no threshold moves — but G4's tone baselines are per-region means, and comparing a new region against an old baseline on the first run is a false positive waiting to happen.

---

### 10.6a The permitted-wording table for odds copy

**§10 is the normative owner of this table.** It is a CAP 8.20/8.21 and 3.7 artefact spanning four surfaces, and no surface section has authority over the others; §10 already owns the gate module, the four enforcement stages and the failure classes, so the table and its enforcement sit in one place. §4.8 keeps the CAP reasoning and cites this subsection. Every other section calls `oddsCopy.*()` and contains no odds literal of its own.

**What this subsection owns is the strings. It owns no geometry and no vertical budget at all.** Band width, ceiling, row count, band height, block heights, the E2 module total, surface assignment and every type size belong to §4.4, §4.7, §4.8, §7.2 and §3.5. The earlier "Device vertical budget" block carried here — the 812px / 809px sums and the "1350 − 812 = 538px left for photo" line — is **deleted outright**; it restated §4.4's count-slide budget against a 150px figure and a provenance row that no longer exist. Type is named by §3.5 token, never by literal: the eyebrow sets at `--fs-label` (Inter 600), the figure at `--fs-figure` (JetBrains Mono 700), the annotation at `--fs-label` (JetBrains Mono 700), the legend at `--fs-body` (Inter 400).

#### Part 1 — the table

**1.0 The governing shape.** Every conditional travels inside the same text run, at the same size, weight, colour and opacity, as the claim it conditions (§10.5 rule 1). The hero figure is therefore never an odds claim — it is the bare, directly-evidenced ticket cap. `format.mjs:53`'s `oddsLabel()` is retired from every rendered surface and replaced by `oddsCopy.capFigure(n) = Number(n).toLocaleString("en-GB")`.

**1.1 The odds device — one module, one set of strings, four surfaces.**

| Slot | Exact rendered string | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Eyebrow | `TICKET CAP` | 10 glyphs. 264.2px at Inter 600 44px bare; 299.4px with §4.8's 0.08em tracking |
| Hero figure | the bare cap, en-GB grouped: `699` / `9,999` / `4,500,000` | Tabular. Glyph budget is §3.5's T4 (≤9). Beyond T4 the build does not shrink the figure — the draw is dropped (class B) |
| Conditional — E2's third row, **every surface** | `1 IN {cap} AT SELL-OUT` | One line. Worst case `1 IN 4,500,000 AT SELL-OUT` = **619.8px** at Inter 600 44px, measured; 330.2px spare on the 950px track, 275.2px on the 895px well |
