| Annotation (clipped state only) | **`{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED`** | Right-aligned to x 960 in §4.8's own 50px row. See the note below |
| Legend, full state, 3 declared lines | L1 `Each dot is one ticket.` · L2 `Odds at sell-out: 1 in {cap}.` · L3 `We do not know which ticket wins.` | Measured against §4.4's band; build fails on overflow |
| Legend, clipped state, 2 declared lines | L1 `Each dot is one ticket.` · L2 `Odds at sell-out: 1 in {cap}.` | as above |

Within this table only `{cap}` and `{shown}` are interpolated. No other token in any 1.1 string is variable.

**The annotation, and why `SHOWN` was struck.** `{shown}` is §4.7's ceiling, en-GB grouped, always the literal-by-derivation `1,440` (5 glyphs); `{cap}` is `draws.total_entries` en-GB grouped, at most 9 glyphs by §3.5's T4. The string's fixed cost is 23 glyphs, so its bounded worst case is 23 + 9 = **32 glyphs = 844.8px**, inside §4.8's measured 33-glyph / 871.2px slot at every legal cap. Measured, at JetBrains Mono 700's exact 26.4px per glyph at 44px:

| Cap | String | Glyphs | Width | Slot 871.2px |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,441 (shortest clipped) | `1,440 OF 1,441 · NONE MARKED` | 28 | 739.2px | 132.0px spare |
| 9,999 (§4.2's median) | `1,440 OF 9,999 · NONE MARKED` | 28 | 739.2px | 132.0px spare |
| 13,995 | `1,440 OF 13,995 · NONE MARKED` | 29 | 765.6px | 105.6px spare |
| 4,500,000 (measured maximum) | `1,440 OF 4,500,000 · NONE MARKED` | 32 | 844.8px | 26.4px spare |

The previous form, `{shown} OF {cap} SHOWN · NONE MARKED`, is dead at both ends: 34 glyphs = **897.6px** at the median cap, over the slot by 26.4px, and 38 glyphs = **1,003.2px** at the maximum. The word `SHOWN` costs six glyphs the slot does not have. Since §4.2 measures the clipped sheet as the device's default appearance — roughly three days in four, and every draw on a car-draws day — that string guaranteed a class-A build failure on the ordinary run. **The gate now cannot fire on legitimate inventory, and that is a proof rather than a sample**: the only variable is `{cap}`, T4 caps it at 9 glyphs, and a 10-glyph cap (≥10,000,000) drops the draw at the figure node before the annotation is composed.

What is given up is the explicit not-shown count; the reader must subtract. §4.9's clipped alt text keeps it in full and becomes its sole normative home, and the clipped legend's L2 carries the true denominator in running copy at a larger step directly beneath the row. The row is **mandatory** whenever the sheet is clipped: if it cannot be composed, the draw is dropped (class B), never the row.

**The Story carries the same module, stacked.** There is no side-by-side Story variant and no separate numeral-lockup qualifier string. E2 is one module taking no surface parameter: eyebrow, figure, conditional, each its own row, rendered on the carousel draw slide, the count slide, the Reel and the Story alike. Its rows, heights and y-ranges on the Story are §7.2's band 4; on the carousel and Reel they are §4.4's. The retired `{cap} TICKETS MAX · ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT` slot had no consumer left once E2 became uniform, and it sat one word away from a string §10.6a bans by name.

**Why `NONE MARKED` and not a colour-naming clause.** It is encoding-agnostic — it stays true whether the device's marker is a green dot, and it stays true on §8's still surfaces where the per-category accent is dropped. A string that names a colour is a string that becomes false when a surface's palette changes.

**1.2 The cover.**

| Slot | Exact rendered string |
|---|---|
| Dateline | `THU 18 SEP 2026 · READ 09:04` (§10.4's short stamp form; 571.2px at `--fs-micro`) |
| Proof line | `8 draws closing within 5 days. Lowest ticket cap of the 8: 699.` — `8` from `drawsRendered` (§5.11), `5` from the real max days-to-close in the selection, `699` from the real minimum cap |
| Headline — `question` | `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?` — one permitted form, no long/short pair |
| Headline — `price-anchor` | long `{n} DRAWS. FROM {price} A TICKET.` / short `{n} DRAWS. FROM {price}.` |
| Headline — `deadline` | long `THREE OF THESE CLOSE {day}.` / short `THREE CLOSE {day}.`, rendering as `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUN.` — `{day}` is the three-letter uppercase weekday `closesLabel()` already emits (`format.mjs:46`), never a full weekday name and never a clock (§10.3) |
| Headline — `absurd-comparison` | long `{cashAlt} FOR A {price} TICKET.` / short `{cashAlt} FOR {price}.` — runs only where `cashAlt()` parses, else falls back to `price-anchor` and logs `absurd-comparison→price-anchor` |

**The cover's permitted interpolations are `{n}`, `{day}`, `{days}`, `{minCap}`, `{price}` and `{cashAlt}`** — numbers, number-derived labels and the day token only, never a free-text string parameter, consistent with L1's no-string-parameter rule. (The stricter "only `{cap}` and `{shown}`" sentence is scoped to the 1.1 device table, where it is true.)

**The `question` arm has one form and it carries a figure.** `{n}` is interpolated from `drawsRendered` (§5.11), never a literal; `oddsCopy.headline('question', form, facts)` ignores `form`, and `carousel_posts.hook_archetype` logs `question:only`. The reason is §10.6's rewritten mechanic predicate 3, and the reason there is only one form is arithmetic: `HOW MANY` measures 869.70px of the 895px well on its own and `TICKETS?` 683.70px, so each takes a whole line box, and the only two-figure line that would fit — the bare `8 · 699` at 500.55px — reads as "8 draws have 699 tickets", attaching one draw's cap to the whole deck. (`8 DRAWS. 699` is 1,065.15px and does not fit at all.) A fitting string exists and an honest one does not, which is why the predicate moved rather than the table.

**The `deadline` arm's day token is three letters, and that is a measurement, not a house style.** At `--fs-hero` the full weekday names do not survive the 895px well: `WEDNESDAY.` is ten glyphs and measures **1,012.35px**, overflowing the well outright by 117.35px, while `THURSDAY.` (857.85px) and `SATURDAY.` (855.15px) are nine glyphs, over the eight-glyph authoring cap below. Worse, with any full name the long form never renders — `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUNDAY.` greedy-wraps to **four** line boxes (721.50 / 484.65 / 481.35 / 676.80), because `CLOSE SUNDAY.` is 1,191.6px — and §5.5 hard-fails a four-box headline. With the three-letter token the long form renders on five days a week (`THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUN.` = 721.50 / 484.65 / 879.75, three boxes; likewise TUE, THU, FRI, SAT); on MON and WED it still needs four boxes, because `CLOSE WED.` is 903.3px, 8.3px over the well, so §5.5's long→short rule takes `THREE CLOSE WED.` at three boxes (489.15 / 481.35 / 388.50). Nothing fails the build, and the fallback is counted (§10.8) rather than silent.

**The proof line fits the 895px well and improves.** 63 glyphs at Inter 600 48px = 1,445.1px = **1.61 measured lines** on §3.5's 895px content well, so two line boxes with 344.9px of the second line unused. (It was measured against an 888px track and is unchanged in wording; only its margin improves.) The degraded fallback `8 draws closing within 5 days.` is 700.4px, one line.

**The headline word cap is EIGHT glyphs at `--fs-hero`, and it is measured.** §3.4's measured Bricolage 800 uppercase advance is **0.674038em**, so a mean glyph at 150px is 101.11px: eight glyphs is 808.8px ≤ 895, nine is 909.9px > 895. The earlier figures — ten glyphs, and the nine derived from a 0.6573em advance — are both retired; ten overflowed even the old 930px well, so it was an error the narrower well merely exposed.

**The cap binds exactly one thing, and it is why the day token is three letters.** Measured per word at Bricolage 800 150px, the longest words in the table are `TICKETS?` (8 glyphs, **683.70px**), `SUNDAY.` (7, 676.80px), `£52,000` (7, 625.20px), `TICKET.` (7, 559.05px) and `DRAWS.` (6, 602.40px) — every one inside 895px, the worst with 211.3px of slack. The only word any arm could otherwise emit that breaks the cap is a full weekday name, and `WEDNESDAY.` breaks the well as well as the cap. The earlier claim that "the cap rejects nothing that exists" was true only of the table's frozen example day.

**The binding constraint is not a word but a line box, and it is tighter than the cap suggests.** Greedy-wrapped on the 895px well with real advances, every permitted form lands inside §5.5's three-box gate, but two lines are close:

| Form | Line boxes | Widest box | Slack on 895 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `8 DRAWS. FROM 79p A TICKET.` (`price-anchor` long) | 735.00 / **892.50** / 559.05 | `FROM 79p A` | **2.5px** |
| `8 DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?` (`question`, one form) | 735.00 / **869.70** / 683.70 | `HOW MANY` | **25.3px** |
| `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUN.` (`deadline` long) | 721.50 / 484.65 / **879.75** | `CLOSE SUN.` | 15.25px |
| `£52,000 FOR A 79p TICKET.` (`absurd-comparison` long) | 625.20 / 749.25 / 559.05 | `FOR A 79p` | 145.75px |
| `8 DRAWS. FROM 79p.` (`price-anchor` short) | 735.00 / 790.05 | `FROM 79p.` | 104.95px |
| `THREE CLOSE WED.` (`deadline` short) | 489.15 / 481.35 / 388.50 | `CLOSE` | 413.65px |
| `£52,000 FOR £2.99.` (`absurd-comparison` short) | 625.20 / 808.20 | `FOR £2.99.` | 86.80px |

2.5px is not a margin on an advance sum. The `price-anchor` long form should be expected to fail §5.3's measured fit at render and fall back to its short form; above a £1 ticket price it does not reach the measurement at all, because `8 DRAWS. FROM £2.99 A TICKET.` greedy-wraps to four boxes. That is §5.5's long→short mechanism working rather than a defect — but it means the published long forms are the exception on two of the four arms, which is why §10.8 counts the fallback. Digit advances, previously unmeasured, are **0.6005em** in Bricolage 800 — narrower than uppercase — which is why `8 DRAWS.` is the shortest of the question form's three lines rather than the longest, and why the form holds at every legal deck size (`4 DRAWS.` 731.55px, `5 DRAWS.` 728.10px).

**`Lowest ticket cap of the 8` is the only comparative permitted anywhere in the system**, on the cover only, because its evidence is the eight slides that follow. It is a comparative about a *cap* — arithmetic and checkable — not about *odds quality*, and its scope token (`of the 8`) is mandatory and interpolated from `drawsRendered`. Both counts in this string are digits rather than words, deliberately: the scope token must be a digit so the reader can count the slides against it, and a word and a digit for the same quantity in one sentence reads as two facts.

**1.2b Two standing strings that assert a cadence, moved under the allow-list.**

Two rendered strings claimed a checking frequency the spec's own evidence contradicts, and no predicate caught either. `Every UK draw we track, checked and dated daily.` (§5.10's closing sub-line) and `UK PRIZE DRAWS, CHECKED DAILY` (§6.3's Reel sign-off strapline) both assert *daily*, while §10.4 sets a 48-hour window precisely because daily is not achieved and §1.4 records the pipeline 76 days dark. This is the third appearance of the defect §1.5 A11 logged against `global.series.slotLine` ("every night · 7pm UK", `config.json:10`, verified). Both strings therefore move into `oddsCopy`, into the frozen fixture, and into the permitted table:

| Slot | Exact rendered string | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Closing-slide sub-line (§5.10) | `Read from each operator's own page, and dated.` | 1,112.6px at Inter 400 48px — **31.0px narrower** than the string it replaces (1,143.6px) and setting in the same two measured line boxes on the 950px track, so no geometry moves |
| Reel sign-off strapline (§6.3) | `PRIZE DRAWS, READ AND DATED` | 884.9px at Bricolage 700 56px, 895.9px at Bricolage 800 56px, 716.5px at Inter 600 44px — inside 950px at **every** step §6.3 might choose, and narrower than the 930.1px it replaces |

Both state a method rather than a frequency, and both use §10.4's permitted verb, so the stamp and the standing copy speak with one voice. The strapline also drops `UK`, for two reasons that are not taste: at the incumbent's 56px Bricolage setting every `DAILY`-free variant retaining `UK` overflows (`UK PRIZE DRAWS, READ AND DATED` = 977.0px at Bricolage 700 56px), and §10.2 has already deleted `UK ONLY` from every asset as an unevidenced territory claim, PDD storing no territory field. The handle and the domain carry the territory signal without asserting it.

**1.3 The banned strings, by name.**

Retired from the odds module: `YOUR ODDS AT THE CAP`, `699 TICKETS MAX · YOUR ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT`, `9,999 TICKETS MAX · YOUR ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT`, `{cap} TICKETS MAX · ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT`, `one dot = one ticket · one of them wins`, `green mark shown at minimum width — the true share is smaller`, and the 34-glyph annotation `{shown} OF {cap} SHOWN · NONE MARKED`.

Retired from the cover: `Shortest odds 1 in 699`, `SHORTEST ODDS TODAY?`, `WHOSE ODDS ARE SHORTEST TODAY?`, `SHORTEST TICKET CAP OF THE SIX BELOW — 1 IN 599`, `Every odds figure checked against the operator's own cap`, **`HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?`** and **`HOW MANY TICKETS?`** — both banned because they carry no verified figure on the frame itself, and because the arm has one permitted form. *The earlier justification that the long one "greedy-wraps to four line boxes and is unrenderable" is withdrawn: measured on the 895px well it wraps to three boxes (869.70 / 619.95 / **891.15**), the last 3.85px inside the measure. That came from a nine-glyph capacity derived from a mean advance. It is banned for the figure, not for the geometry — and the 3.85px is a reminder that the mean flatters some strings as readily as it condemns others.*

Retired from the `deadline` arm: the full weekday names. `WEDNESDAY.` is 1,012.35px at `--fs-hero`, over the 895px well by 117.35px; `THURSDAY.` and `SATURDAY.` are nine glyphs, over the eight-glyph cap; and with any full name the long form takes four line boxes. The arm interpolates `{day}` as the three-letter form and nothing else.

Retired as standing cadence claims: `Every UK draw we track, checked and dated daily.`, `UK PRIZE DRAWS, CHECKED DAILY`, `EVERY LIVE UK DRAW, CHECKED DAILY`, and `every night · 7pm UK`.

Retired as a separately-sized qualifier line: `IF ALL 13,995 TICKETS SELL`.

Retired from the mockup: `Your odds` (`merged.mjs:83`), `1 is yours` (`merged.mjs:45`), `Best odds tonight` (`merged.mjs:107`).

Retired from the Reel: `ODDS · 1 IN` as a label.

Retired from config: the six `hook` constants at `config.json:20/26/32/38/44/50`, and the `"WIN BIG"` fallback hook hard-coded at `carousel/config.mjs:15`. **The physical removal is §8.7's**, performed in the same commit as its `theme` and `particles` deletions rather than separately; §10.6a states only that the strings are banned.

**And a structural consequence: there is no permitted wording for a clamped proportional bar.** §10.5 rule 1 forbids an undisclosed clamp and no disclosure string is permitted, so the bar cannot ship in any form. It is deleted, not relabelled. The reason is arithmetic rather than taste: a rail clamped at `max(2px, track/cap)` crosses over at a cap in the low hundreds, so essentially every live draw renders the identical minimum mark, and a 1-in-599 draw and a 1-in-4,500,000 draw produce the same picture. A 34px line admitting the graphic is wrong does not discharge CAP's page-design rule.

**Why "your odds" is not a wording preference.** `total_entries` is a property of the draw. A viewer's odds depend on how many tickets they hold and are undefined at zero. `YOUR ODDS AT THE CAP` is therefore false for every viewer who has not bought exactly one ticket; under CAP 8.21 it implies the reader is already in the draw, and under 8.20 it converts a published cap into a personal probability claim. It currently ships as the standard sub-label on every draw slide.

**Why "TODAY" cannot be evidenced (CAP 3.7).** The selection pool is `pickBestCategory` picking one category, then `select.mjs:20` truncating at 300 rows (verified) from the in-window set, out of the enterable inventory, out of a UK universe PDD has never enumerated. A superlative at hero size claims a comparison over that universe. Even "shortest in this category today" fails, because 300 rows is a majority but not all of the window. The only scope PDD holds documentary evidence for, before publication, is the post itself.

**1.4 Alt text** (`honesty.mjs:31-37` → `out/alt.json`) carries the statements the creative has no room for, including §10.4's full provenance sentence, the clipped state's explicit not-shown count, and the untruncated prize title (§10.7). It is generated from the same module and is subject to the same predicates.

#### Part 2 — what enforces it

**L1 — allow-list by construction (CI stage, the primary control).** New module `carousel/odds-copy.mjs`, the single source of every string in Part 1. It exports a frozen object of template functions taking numbers, a validated hostname and the day token only — `capFigure(n)`, `eyebrow()`, `conditional(cap)`, `legendFull(cap)`, `legendClipped(cap)`, `annotation(shown, cap)`, `proofLine(n, days, minCap)`, `headline(archetype, form, facts)`, `stampLong(t)`, `stampShort(t)`, `closingSubLine()`, `signOffStrapline()`. **No parameter of any of these functions may be a free-text string that reaches the output**, the two exceptions being a validated hostname and `{day}`, which is constrained to the seven three-letter weekday tokens. `render.mjs`, `reel-template.mjs`, `story.mjs` and §8's scene module call `oddsCopy.*()` and contain no odds literals.

Three CI gates, all cheap, all of which would have caught every string in Part 1.3:

1. **`carousel/tests/odds-copy.test.mjs`** asserts the exported table equals a frozen expected-string fixture, character for character, at every boundary cap. Changing a permitted string requires changing a reviewed fixture. The fixture additionally asserts `annotation(1440, cap)` character-for-character **and its rendered width in glyphs** at the boundary caps 1,441 / 9,999 / 13,995 / 4,500,000, with a standing assertion that no annotation output exceeds 33 glyphs, so no future wording revision can reintroduce a build-failing string. It also asserts that the clipped legend is exactly its two declared lines — because the annotation's defence against being misread as a sell-through figure is the legend's `Each dot is one ticket.` sitting immediately beneath it, and a later legend edit must not orphan it silently. Finally it asserts the greedy wrap of every headline form on the 895px well at all seven `{day}` values and at the fixture's price set, and fails on any form whose **short** version needs a fourth line box.
2. **A repository grep gate**: no file under `carousel/` other than `odds-copy.mjs` and its test may contain, in a string literal, any of `ODDS`, `1 IN`, `TICKET CAP`, `SELL-OUT`, `TICKETS MAX` (case-insensitive).
3. **`carousel/tests/allowlist-conformance.test.mjs`** — the structural fix, and the one that makes this class of conflict impossible rather than merely corrected. Every string `oddsCopy` can emit, across the fixture's boundary fact-sets (n = `DRAWS_MIN`…8; caps 99 / 699 / 1,440 / 9,999 / 4,500,000; prices 79p / £2.99 / £12.50; days 1…7; `{day}` MON…SUN), is run through **every** L2/L4 predicate — `secondPerson`, `unboundedComparative`, `cadenceOrCoverage`, mechanics 1–3, `bannedPhrases` — in the same unit the renderer will present it in. An allow-listed string that any predicate rejects fails the **test job**. After this, an allow-list entry and a predicate can never again disagree in production; they disagree in CI, which is where the previous round's build-failing `question` headline should have surfaced.

**L2 — MODEL stage (`compliance.mjs` G5).** Runs at §10.1's existing chokepoints. Applies to every string in the asset model, **including the generated cover headline**, which is model data under §5.5 and is the largest element on the slide. Predicates are word-class, not phrase lists — §10.6.

**L3 — DOM stage: identity check, not a lint.** For every node carrying `data-pdd-claim="odds"`, assert `normalizeWhitespace(node.textContent) === ` the exact string the model emitted. Exact equality has no false negatives and catches CSS `content:` injection, `text-transform`, and a refactor that splits a run — all of which a regex over the DOM would miss. The DOM stage keeps its geometry, size and colour job otherwise; it is not given the wording job.

**L4 — PUBLISH stage.** Covers the model-authored caption; see §10.7 for what the hash binding can and cannot enforce today.

**The explicit answer to the question this table was written for:** yes, enforcement covers generated cover headlines as well as captions. Headlines are covered three times now — allow-list at L1, conformance at L1 gate 3, predicate at L2 — and captions at L4. Headlines get the stronger control precisely because they render at hero size and cannot be retracted from a published image.

**Why an allow-list and not the deny-list §4.8 specified.** A deny-list cannot enumerate second-person framings: `Your odds`, `your chances`, `you have a 1 in`, `1 is yours` is four of an unbounded set, and PDD's own archived caption already shipped `better odds than most raffles you'll scroll past all week` — two violations, zero deny-list hits. Meanwhile every string in Part 1 is a *constant*, so the cheap control is that it cannot be written. `config.json:13` has exactly one consumer in the whole repository (`brief.mjs:11`, verified, which prints it into a Markdown briefing); a control defined in editable JSON and read only by a briefing is not a control.

---

### 10.6 G5 — Wording bans, and the ban on gambling furniture

**Why.** CAP 8.20/8.21: must not exaggerate the chances of winning or imply consumers are luckier than they are. CAP 8.22 and DMCC 2024 for false urgency. And the categorisation point: PDD is **not** under CAP Section 16 (Gambling) or 17 (Lotteries), so gambling furniture is both inaccurate and re-categorises PDD in the viewer's mind.

**The deny-list is a backstop, not the mechanism.** §10.6a's allow-list is the primary control for every string that is a constant. A string blocklist cannot govern a generator explicitly instructed to vary its wording each day — and that instruction is in the repository, verbatim, at `brief.mjs:24`: *"One send-CTA, fresh wording each day (never verbatim-repeat…)"*. Fresh wording defeats string matching by construction. So `global.bannedPhrases` is promoted from a briefing input to an enforced deny-list at the L2 and L4 stages only, over the one surface that is genuinely generated: the caption, plus the cover headline the archetype generator produces. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries.

**Provenance: the word classes and additions below are design judgement derived from the cited rules and the teardown's confirmed clichés. This is not a legal review and must not be presented as one.**

#### Word-class predicates (L2 and L4)

**`secondPerson(s)`** — `/\b(you|your|yours|you're|youre|u|yer)\b/i` → class A. PDD's own voice never needs the second person on an asset.

*Carve-out, because it is a real hole:* `cleanTitle()` output — an operator's prize title — is exempt, since operators write titles like "Build Your Own PC". But a title matching `/\byour\b.{0,30}\b(odds|chance|win|ticket)\b/i` drops the draw to a backup (class B), and §5.12's cleaning contract carries the rule.

**`unboundedComparative(s)`** — any of `/\b(best|better|worst|shortest|longest|lowest|highest|greatest|top|cheapest|biggest|smallest|easiest|likeliest)\b/i` present **and** no scope token from the closed set `{here, on this card, in this post, of the N}` present in the same string → class A. Also class A: any of those words within 40 characters of `/\bodds\b|\b1 in\b|\bchance/i` plus an unbounded scope token `/\b(today|tonight|anywhere|in the uk|ever|of the day|right now|all week)\b/i`.

**`cadenceOrCoverage(s)` — new, and it closes a defect this document has now logged three times.** Any of `/\b(daily|always|nightly|24\/7|round the clock)\b/i` in PDD's own voice → class A, with **no carve-out**: these assert a frequency PDD does not achieve, and §10.4's 48-hour window exists because it does not. Any of `/\b(every|all)\b/i` → class A **unless** immediately bound by a figure interpolated from the run's verified-facts table in the same sentence (`all 8`, `every one of the 8`), exactly as `unboundedComparative` is bound by its scope token. It applies in captions as well as on assets, with no relaxation: `global.series.slotLine`'s "every night · 7pm UK" was config, not caption, and it was false within days of being written.

**Three live strings fail this predicate today, and all three are removed in the same pass.** Verified: `honesty.mjs:36`'s CTA alt text `See every live UK prize draw at prizedrawsdaily.co.uk` and `caption.mjs:32` / `:33`'s `👉 See every live UK draw: https://prizedrawsdaily.co.uk` each carry an unbound `every` about PDD's own coverage — the same claim as the strapline, in the two places nobody looks. They are rewritten to name the site rather than quantify it (`See the live UK prize draws at prizedrawsdaily.co.uk`), which the predicate passes and which asserts nothing PDD cannot show.

**Gate check, on the ordinary run.** The class fires on zero permitted strings. `Each dot is one ticket.`, `Read from each operator's own page, and dated.` and `Enter · terms · each operator's own site.` all use *each*, which is deliberately not in the class — *each* distributes over a named set and asserts no frequency or exhaustiveness. Nothing else in §10.6a's table contains a class word. The two rendered strings that did are replaced in §10.6a 1.2b, and gate 3 of the CI conformance test is what proves it stays that way.

#### Mechanic predicates (L2 and L4)

A deny-list cannot express these, and each is the rule that actually bites on generated copy:

1. **No imperative directed at the reader's social graph.** A part-of-speech check on the leading verb of any sentence: `share`, `send`, `tag`, `comment`, `vote`, `react`, `double tap` and their inflections, in imperative position → class A. This is a mechanic ban, not a phrase list, so a novel phrasing of the same ask still fails. (It fires on `brief.mjs:24`'s own send-CTA instruction, which is the point: the instruction is removed in the same pass.)
2. **No numbered reference without its referent named in the same sentence.** `"number 3"`, `"the second one"`, `"slide 4"` with no noun phrase naming what it is → class A. A carousel caption that indexes a slide the viewer has not reached is an unresolvable reference.
3. **Two-figure test, evidence-unit scoped.** Fires on any rendered text **unit** whose text **contains** `?` — contains, not ends with, so a headline cannot evade by trailing a full stop. The unit must carry at least two figures with **distinct fact keys** from the run's verified-facts table. Class A on failure.

   A "figure" is a maximal match of `/[£$]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?[pk%]?/` in the unit's text whose normalised value equals the string form of a value in `facts`. Word-numbers ("THREE", "EIGHT") never count — which is why §10.6a's `deadline` form `THREE OF THESE CLOSE SUN.` is untouched: it carries no `?` and no digit, and the rule does not fire on it.

   `facts` is frozen at the MODEL stage, written to `selection.json` and printed in full by `brief.mjs`: `drawsRendered` (§5.11) · `caps[]` (every deck cap) · `prices[]` (every deck `ticket_price` as `priceLabel()` renders it) · `daysToClose[]` (every deck days-to-close). **Distinct keys** means two matches drawn from two differently-named facts; two caps do not satisfy it.

   **The unit, by surface:**
   - cover headline → the cover slide's model, `normalizeWhitespace(headline + " " + proofLine)`. The proof line is a fixed, mandatory block rendered directly beneath the headline (§5.4) and is generated, never authored.
   - any other rendered string → that frame's own model text.
   - caption, FB caption, alt text → the single sentence containing the `?` — **unchanged**, because a caption sentence has no adjacent rendered evidence.

   The unit differs by surface because the evidence does. This is §7.10's own principle made machine-checkable: *a permissible question is one whose answer is in the post; an impermissible one is a question whose answer is only in the reader.* **No string is exempt because it is allow-listed** — an exemption keyed on "emitted by `oddsCopy.headline()`" would auto-exempt every future allow-list entry, which is how a gate rots.

**What the predicate still catches**, and what it cost. It still catches every caption sentence containing `?` with fewer than two distinct-key figures — including PDD's own archived, verified violation `Which would you pick?` (zero figures, class A); any generated caption question implying a flattering answer with nothing to check; and a cover regression in which the headline carries `?` while the proof line is absent, empty or figure-less, which is the exact failure the rule was written for. It no longer fires on a question whose evidenced answer is rendered immediately beneath it.

**Confirmed on the common case.** On a `question` day the unit is `8 DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS? 8 draws closing within 5 days. Lowest ticket cap of the 8: 699.` → keys {`drawsRendered`, `daysToClose`, `caps`} = 3 ≥ 2. Pass. On the stated fallback proof line `8 draws closing within 5 days.` → 2 keys. Pass. At the degraded floor `5 draws closing within 1 day.` → 2 keys. Pass. On the other three archetypes no `?` is present and the rule does not fire. **The gate fires on zero legitimate runs. The old rule hard-failed roughly 91 of them a year**, because `plan.mjs:71` rotates `dayOfYear % 4` and §10.8 makes a §10.6 hit class A — non-zero exit, no PNG, no MP4, no `publish.json`.

**`brief.mjs` must print the run's verified-facts table and predicate 3 in full**, alongside the Part 1 table it already prints, so the caption author generates questions that carry figures rather than discovering the rule at L4.

#### The class table

| Class | Banned in PDD's own voice | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Chance exaggeration** | the eight existing `config.json:13` phrases, plus `secondPerson` and `unboundedComparative` as word classes rather than literals | 8.20 / 8.21 |
| **False urgency** | "last chance", "final tickets", "selling fast", "almost gone", "nearly sold out", "ending soon" | 8.22 / DMCC 2024. "X tickets left" can **never** be true in PDD's data: `README.md:43-44` records that sold/remaining counts are vetoed at parse time, so PDD holds no remaining-ticket figure at all. This ban is provable from the data model, not merely cautious. |
| **Unevidenced cadence or coverage** | `daily`, `always`, `nightly`, `24/7`, `round the clock`; and `every` / `all` unbound by an interpolated figure | 3.7. The claim is about PDD, and §10.4's 48-hour window is the evidence that contradicts it. |
| **Gambling furniture** | `PLAY RESPONSIBLY`, `BeGambleAware`, `GambleAware`, "gamble", "bet", "stake", "punt", "odds-on", "jackpot", "sweepstakes", "lottery" | Section 8, not 16/17. **"odds" itself stays** — it is the proposition. "lottery" is permitted only inside an operator's registered name. |
| **American tells** | "$", "WIN BIG", stacked exclamation marks, MM/DD dates, AM/PM clocks | Not a code rule; the teardown's register findings. Enforced for brand consistency, listed here because the L2/L4 predicate is one mechanism. |

**The caption carve-out.** Second person is permitted in caption prose ("follow so you don't miss tomorrow's") but **not** within 60 characters of an odds token (`odds`, `1 in`, `chance`, `ticket cap`, `win`). Captions are conversational and assets are not; the distinction is the proximity rule, not the surface. `cadenceOrCoverage` gets no such carve-out.

**`PLAY RESPONSIBLY` is on every asset PDD ships, in nine places, not the seven a casual grep finds** (two are lower-case and one is a third copy of the video footer): `render.mjs:69`, `:122`, `:157`, `:172`; `reel-template.mjs:789`; **`reel.mjs:105`**; `story.mjs:155`; `caption.mjs:35` (`18+ · UK only · Play responsibly`); and `brief.mjs:26`, which instructs the caption model to produce it. All nine verified in-session. Every instance is removed.

**The American-tells row indicts PDD's own config twice, and the second indictment has now been discharged by another section.** `config.json:12` sets `global.fixedHashtags` to `["#prizedrawsdaily", "#ukcompetition", "#winbig"]` (verified), and `caption.mjs:17` and `:34` append it to every caption. `#winbig` is the "WIN BIG" tell in hashtag form and must be replaced; the teardown also found hashtags roughly irrelevant to reach (2.6pp spread, 65% of carousels used none), so dropping it costs nothing measurable. Separately, `carousel/config.mjs:15` hard-codes `hook: "WIN BIG"` into the `catCfg()` fallback. **When that was measured it was the default headline for `sports-outdoors` and `home-garden`, 147 live draws, because neither slug had a `config.json` entry. §8.7's migration closes that path twice over** — it authors both entries and it deletes the `hook` key from the schema entirely, so the fallback hook has no consumer left. The string stays banned by name under §10.6a 1.3; the claim that it is "the default headline for two of PDD's categories" is a statement about the pre-migration state and must not be carried forward as a present-tense fact.

**The age and territory marks are handled in §10.2**, not here: `18+` folds into the band's L3 as a pointer to the operator's terms, and `UK ONLY` is deleted outright because PDD stores no territory field. §10.6's job is to enforce their absence from captions and alt text as well — `honesty.mjs:33,35,36` and `caption.mjs:19,20,35` all carry them today. `story.mjs:152`'s on-frame `LINK IN BIO` goes in the same pass (§10.2).

**Under-18s** (CAP 1.3 social responsibility, 8.8 special care; 16.3.12's "strong appeal" test does not formally bind PDD but the design is built as if it did). No cartoon characters, mascots, game-like or toy-like treatments. **This subsection is the one that performs the removal** of the three devices and their CSS, so that no other section deletes them a second time at a different point in the sequence:

- `confettiHtml()` — `render.mjs:47-59`, called with 24 pieces on the intro (`render.mjs:145`) and 20 on the CTA (`render.mjs:164`).
- the particle fields — `particlesHtml()` at `render.mjs:30-42` and `particleField()` at `reel-template.mjs:480`, types `embers | golddust | fireflies | holo`, **including the `.p-*` rule blocks in `styles.css`** (`:258`, `:261`, `:264`, `:267`) — which is what actually removes them from video, because `reel-template.mjs:47` lifts exactly those four blocks by name into the Reel's stylesheet. (The `particles` key itself leaves `config.json` under §8.7, not here.)
- the `.stamp` rosette — CSS at `reel-template.mjs:90-97`, markup helper `stampHtml()` at `:98`, slot at `:320-323`: a 430px circular disc with a 10px `--gold-2` border, a radial-gradient highlight, a second expanding `.stamp-ring`, and `transform: rotate(-8deg)`. It is simultaneously a confirmed category cliché (gold foil rosettes, red starbursts) and a toy-like device.

The `--gold-*` token block itself is **not** §10.6's to delete; it belongs to §3.8, and §5.2's deferral must point at §3.8 rather than leaving the handoff orphaned. The devices go here; the tokens go there; the config keys go to §8.7; nobody deletes anything twice.

**Emoji as layout furniture** is banned in rendered assets and captions: `🏆` (`render.mjs:149`), `📌` (`render.mjs:170`), `⚠` (`reel-template.mjs:475`), `⏳` (`reel-template.mjs:681`), `👇` (`caption.mjs:14`, `:15`, `:32`), `🎯` (`caption.mjs:29`), `👉` (`caption.mjs:32`, `:33`). The `⚠` is the worst — a hazard glyph doing emphasis work on a commercial deadline, which is §10.5's problem as much as this one.

---

### 10.7 What must be preserved, and what binds the publisher

Two existing behaviours are genuine E-E-A-T assets and survive with their semantics unchanged. Both are upgraded from silent to accountable.

**The cash-alternative cap (`honesty.mjs:19-23`).** `capValue()` caps a draw's claimable value at the operator's own stated cash alternative, with the `alt != null && alt > 0` guard that stops a `"£0"` parse artefact from zeroing a legitimate figure. This maps directly to the Raffle House rulings (2019, upheld twice: the cash substitute was "not a reasonable equivalent") and must never be relaxed — the operator's own number is the honest ceiling. Its **six** tests in `carousel/tests/honesty.test.mjs` are the regression contract, including the 2026-07-02 incident guard at `:41-50` (`valueLine v2 uses per-draw capped sum`: capped sum `£141,000+`, not `£222,000+`).

The one change: `valueLine()` returns `""` when the total falls below the per-category bar (`honesty.mjs:27`, `total < catCfg(slug).valueLineMin || total < 1000`), and `build.mjs:135` passes that empty string into a slide field that simply does not render (`render.mjs:139`). The outcome is right and the mechanism is wrong — it is a silent suppression. Under the new scheme it emits a named, counted class-C event naming the real configured bar, e.g. `value-line suppressed: capped sum £900 below collectibles bar £8,000`. **The `valueLineMin` values themselves are §8.7's** — it is the sole normative owner of the `config.json` category schema and of all eight per-category entries — and §10.7 no longer enumerates them.

**The unconditional-suppression case is closed, and this section's earlier statement of it must not be carried forward.** `carousel/config.mjs:8-11` sets `FALLBACK.valueLineMin = Infinity`, and `carousel/tests/honesty.test.mjs:13` asserts the behaviour explicitly (`unknown → Infinity bar → never`). When that was measured, `sports-outdoors` and `home-garden` — 147 live draws — had no `config.json` entry, so their value line was permanently suppressed at any prize total, silently, and nobody had chosen it. §8.7 closes it: both categories are now authored with real bars, `catCfg` no longer merges FALLBACK into a configured entry, and `pickBestCategory` skips any slug absent from `CFG.categories` altogether. The unconfigured path therefore survives only for a slug that can no longer win a deck. The class-C event keeps both forms — `no valueLineMin configured for <slug> — value line suppressed unconditionally` alongside the named-bar form — because a log must distinguish a threshold decision from a missing threshold, and because the honest record of *why* the second form exists is that it was reachable in production for 147 draws.

**Per-slide alt text (`out/alt.json`).** Written at `build.mjs:161` from `altTexts()` (`honesty.mjs:31-37`) and consumed at `publish.mjs:171`. It survives, with four changes. First, it extends to the formats that currently have none — the Reel cover and the Story. Second, it carries §10.4's full provenance sentence, which is what licenses the short stamp form on the Reel and on the cover. Third, **it carries the untruncated `cleanTitle()` output on every draw-carrying asset**, so a prize name truncated on-frame — which §6.5's Reel budget does to over half of live inventory at the measured median title of 26 glyphs — never loses the record. Fourth, this line is deleted:

```js
// publish.mjs:171
const altTexts = await Bun.file(`${OUT}/alt.json`).json().catch(() => []);
```

A missing or unparseable `alt.json` currently publishes silently with no alt text at all. That becomes a hard fail. (The `18+` strings inside `altTexts()` at `:33`, `:35` and `:36` are rewritten per §10.2 and §10.6, and `:36`'s unbound `every` goes with them.)

#### The PUBLISH gate binds the publisher only as far as a control actually exists

`publish.json` is **not** what reaches the platform. An agent session reads it and calls Composio tools, and §7.5 documents that agent already choosing a different tool than the runbook specified, producing five to seven separate posts with the caption attached as a self-comment. Nothing today gates what the agent actually sends: it can edit the caption, drop the alt array, or post a different asset, and `COMPLIANCE.json` will still read pass.

The previous specification closed this with three additions and then said "without (2) the gate is advisory" — while §7.5 establishes that neither the multi-photo tool name it selects nor `FACEBOOK_UPLOAD_PHOTOS_BATCH` appears anywhere in the repository, and that the tool is chosen by an agent reading prose. So "the posting step" is a model reading a runbook: precisely the control class §10.6a rejects by name when it dismisses `bannedPhrases` as "a control defined in editable JSON, read only by a briefing". A class-A failure whose trigger nothing can evaluate is worse than no class at all, because it makes the gate table read as stronger than the pipeline is. The control is therefore split into four named parts with honest enforcement status:

| | Control | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | `publish.mjs` writes a **SHA-256 of each cleared artefact** — `CAPTION.txt`, `CAPTION_FALLBACK.txt`, `FB_CAPTION.txt` and the serialised `alt.json` array — into `publish.json`, alongside the strings themselves. | **Ships now.** A file write with an enforcement point that exists. It is a record, not a gate. |
| **P2** | The posting step **re-hashes what it is about to post** and refuses on mismatch; a mismatch is class A, nothing is posted, the run is recorded as failed at PUBLISH. | **Specified and dormant**, exactly as §10.8's class D is dormant because no clock ships. It has no evaluator until P3 exists and must not be listed as an enforced control until then. |
| **P3** | A first-party posting step: a Bun script that reads `publish.json`, re-hashes, and calls the Graph API directly with a stored token. | **Not in v1 and not §10's to cost.** It is a genuine addition to §12.2's Facebook line and belongs in that budget. P2 activates on the same commit. |
| **P4** | A **post-publish reconciliation** re-reads the live media's caption through the Graph API, flags any divergence, and records the posted hash in `carousel_posts` (§11). The forbidden tools are named in the payload, as §7.5 proposes. | **Ships now, as detection.** It finds divergence after the fact; it prevents nothing. |

§10.1's PUBLISH row and §10.8's class-A entry are restated accordingly: today the PUBLISH stage enforces the caption and alt-text *predicates* over the files `publish.mjs` writes, and detects — but cannot prevent — an agent posting something else. That is a weaker claim than the previous text made, and it is the true one. The route to the stronger claim is P3, it is one script, and naming it is how it gets built rather than assumed.

---

### 10.8 How each gate fails — loudly, never silently

Four failure classes, in descending severity. Every one writes a named line to stderr in the existing `✗` / `⚠` convention (`publish.mjs:47` is the precedent) and a structured record to a new **`out/COMPLIANCE.json`**, with a human-readable **`out/COMPLIANCE.txt`** beside it.

| Class | Behaviour | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| **A — HARD FAIL** | Non-zero exit. No PNG or MP4 written, nothing uploaded, no `publish.json`. | Any §10.2 band line absent, below 38px, opacity below 0.92, on a non-opaque background, overflowing its measured track, or outside `surface.safe` / inside `surface.keepOut`; the band's line count ≠ 3. **On a `DRAW_CARRYING` role only: the prize-name element absent, empty, below §3.5's `--fs-lead`, overflowing its measured track, or outside `surface.safe` / inside `surface.keepOut`.** `prize-name-on-deck-asset` (a prize-name node present on a deck-level role). `role-mismatch` (the `data-pdd-role` attribute disagreeing with the role the caller passed). `post-carries-no-prize-name: <format>`. Missing or unparseable `alt.json`. A wording ban hit in PDD's own voice (§10.6), including **a rendered unit containing `?` carrying fewer than two distinct-key figures from the run's verified-facts table (§10.6 predicate 3)**. Verdict green on a figure whose row did not satisfy §10.4's predicate. `total_entries_method` NULL or `bare-count` at MODEL stage. A headline whose **short** form still needs a fourth line box (§5.5's own gate, recorded here). `deck-underfilled: category <slug> supplied <n> of <DRAWS_MIN>`. An empty selection pool. |
| **B — DRAW DROP** | The offending draw is removed and a backup promoted; when backups are exhausted the deck shrinks one draw at a time. | `figures_checked_at` stale at build time (§10.4). `entry_url` null. `draw_date` missing or unparseable. `ticket_price` null or ≤ 0. `grand_prize` and `cleanTitle()` both empty. A prize title matching the second-person odds pattern (§10.6). A cap above §3.5's T4 glyph budget — which is also the condition under which §10.6a's annotation could not be composed, so the draw is dropped and the row never is. Title residue (§5.12 rule 9), image class (§9.6) and slide-2 image quality (§5.6 Delta 3) resolve here too. |
| **C — SLOT COLLAPSE** | One figure does not render; its layout slot closes up. Named and counted. | An unparseable cash alternative; a value line below the category bar, or suppressed because no bar is configured. **Nothing else.** |
| **D — DOWNGRADE** | The clock becomes a date chip, one rung down §10.3's ladder. Named and counted. | Dormant in v1: no clock ships, so no run can produce a class-D event. The class is retained for the release that enables it. |

**A caption hash mismatch is a dormant class-A trigger, not a live one.** It sits beside class D in the same posture and for the same reason: the condition is specified and nothing in the pipeline can evaluate it until §10.7's P3 lands. It is listed here so that the commit which adds P3 knows exactly what to switch on, and it is excluded from the live class-A set so that the gate table does not overstate what runs.

**Provenance can no longer reach class C.** The class-C row for a stale odds figure is deleted (§10.4). An odds figure never collapses its slot, because a draw without evidence is never selected. This is the single change that makes the first run possible: previously every figure was class C on day one, the escalation ceiling fired, and nothing published.

**`entry_url` null is class B, not class A.** Measured today against the live DB (`ilnegxrsalmzpljotgpe`): **0 of 1,792 `status=active` rows have a null `entry_url`**, so the path is currently unreachable — and it is a per-row, recoverable condition, which is the definition of class B. `entry_url` *is* in `REQUIRED_FIELDS` (`gate.mjs:10-11`), but that list is env-overridable (`process.env.REQUIRED_FIELDS || …`) and only binds rows written through the scrape-time gate, so absence is possible in principle.

**Class B is cheap because the machinery already exists and is unused.** `plan.mjs:69` slices backup draws out of the category pool and `plan.mjs:75` writes them into `selection.json`; `fetchimg.mjs:170` already pre-fetches their photographs from `[...sel.draws, ...(sel.backups || [])]`. Verified: those two files are the only readers of `sel.backups` in the whole pipeline — **`build.mjs` never substitutes one**. This gate is the first consumer. The backup *count* is §5.11's constant and is not restated here.

#### Counted records that are not failures

| Record | Written when | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `prize-name-truncated: <role> <slug> <n>→<m> glyphs` | §5.7's fitting ladder or §6.5's Row B budget truncates a title at a word boundary | **none** — counted in `COMPLIANCE.json`, never a failure. The untruncated title is in `out/alt.json` (§10.7). This is the measurement that tells anyone how bad the Reel's 22-glyph budget is against the measured median title of 26. |
| `headline-long→short: <archetype> <token>` | §5.5's fit rule takes the short form because the long one needs a fourth line box or overflows a line | **none** — counted. It is the measurement of how often the published long forms actually render: `deadline` falls back on MON and WED, and `price-anchor` falls back at any ticket price above £1, so a run of short-form days is expected behaviour and not a regression to hunt. |
| `absurd-comparison→price-anchor` | `cashAlt()` does not parse | none |
| `deck-short (pool truncated)` | a short deck on a day `select.mjs` returned exactly 300 rows | none |

#### Drops are resolved in one pass, against the deck, not against the reasons

Four mechanisms swap draws out of one deck — §10.4 provenance staleness, §10.8's class-B data fields, §5.12 rule 9's title residue, and §9.6's image class — and a priority order between them is the wrong fix, because whichever runs first wins and the rest escalate. Instead: **the MODEL stage evaluates every draw against every class-B condition in one pass, producing the set of failing draws; promotion and shrinking then happen once, against that set.** A draw failing three conditions consumes one backup, not three. The record in `COMPLIANCE.json` lists every condition each dropped draw failed, in the fixed order provenance → data fields → title residue → image class → slide-2 quality, so the log is stable and diffable.

#### Degradation is one draw at a time, and the floor is §5.11's

Class-B exhaustion no longer escalates straight to class A. The order of recourse is: promote a backup, up to §5.11's `BACKUPS`; then shrink the deck by one draw; repeat. Class A fires only when `drawsRendered < DRAWS_MIN`. A seven-draw deck of evidenced draws is strictly better than no post, and §2.6's S1 continuity criterion is protected by the ladder rather than by refusing to fail. The backup count and the floor are §5.11's constants and are not restated here; the old "three backups is the hard ceiling" sentence is deleted along with the fixed number it carried.

#### The class-C ceiling is a proportion

**`collapsed > floor(0.4 × drawsRendered)` escalates the run to class A.** Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines exclude "unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value", and the research identifies this as the single most important constraint on the whole project, because a daily auto-generated carousel of other operators' photographs and prize data is directly exposed to it. The added value must be *visibly on the slide*. A deck that collapsed its way to zero differentiated data is not a compliant deck that shipped; it is an ineligible deck that should not have.

The proportion is a faithful generalisation, not a recalibration: at the old five-draw deck `floor(0.4 × 5) = 2`, i.e. escalate at three or more, which is arithmetically identical to the sentence it replaces. Nothing measures whether 40% is the right threshold at any deck size, and no such measurement is obtainable — carousel children have no per-slide insights in the Graph API.

#### Silent failures deleted by name

Each currently converts a compliance problem into a plausible-looking asset:

| Location | Current behaviour | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `honesty.mjs:27` | `return ""` — value line vanishes with no record | class C, named and counted |
| `publish.mjs:171` | `.catch(() => [])` — publishes with no alt text | class A |
| `story.mjs:125` | `draw.draw_date \|\| nowIso` — renders a frozen `00:00:00` clock | class B |
| `reel-template.mjs:750` | `closeIso ?? now + DEFAULT_LEFT_MS` — renders an **invented** ticking `03:47:22` | class B |
| `plan.mjs:41` | `process.exit(0)` on an empty pool — a no-publish day indistinguishable from success | class A, named, non-zero exit |
| `run.mjs:358-368` | `no-correction` → `continue`, no PATCH — a stable correct cap silently ages out of eligibility | Stage 0 item 0c: PATCH `figures_checked_at` and `figures_source_url` on every observation |

#### The record

`out/COMPLIANCE.json` and `out/COMPLIANCE.txt` are written on **pass** as well as fail, so a run with the gates disabled is distinguishable from a run that passed them. Both carry `drawsPlanned`, `drawsRendered`, `backupsUsed` and `poolTruncated` in every case, so a degraded deck is distinguishable from a full one in the same file.

`out/COMPLIANCE.txt` names the gate, the stage (`ci` / `model` / `dom` / `publish`), the asset, its role, the field and the stored value that failed — so the failure is a work item, in the same way `README.md:25-26` describes the aggregator's draft hold list doubling as "the parser's to-do list". On a passing run it requires no human read; it is a machine artefact that exists so a later question has an answer. Only a class-A run demands attention, and a class-A run has already stopped. A gate whose output is only an exit code gets switched off the first time it is inconvenient — and this pipeline already has the switch: `AUTO_PUBLISH` is opt-in and honoured only by the daily Action (`README.md:29-31`), so the precedent for an env var that turns off a safety behaviour is established.

---

### Decisions this section commits to

- Compliance moves into a new pure module `carousel/compliance.mjs`, shaped like the ROOT-level `gate.mjs`: `{ ok, violations[] }` per gate, combined `{ pass, stage, violations[] }`. It is also the single authoring site for `DRAW_CARRYING = {count, draw, reel-card, story}`.
- Gates are enforced at FOUR stages: CI (the odds-copy fixture, the allow-list conformance test and the repository grep gate), MODEL (`build.mjs:156`, `reel.mjs:236`, `story.mjs:247`, plus the post-level field-5 count), DOM (stills between `render.mjs:191` and `:195`; video between `capture.mjs:21` and `:22` on three sampled frames **per role run**), and PUBLISH (between `publish.mjs:172` and `:173`).
- §10.2 is the sole normative owner of the conditions band, of `data-pdd-role` and of `DRAW_CARRYING`; §10.4 of the evidence and provenance contract; §10.6a of the permitted wording for odds copy. §10 owns no geometry outside the band, no type scale, no track width, no gutter, no ceiling, no block height, no deck size and no `config.json` value, and restates none of them.
- The band sets on ONE track — §3.5's 950px chrome track, x 65 … 1015, Meta Safe Box A's width on both canvases. The three-candidate hedge (940 / 950 / 952) is retired; 952px at x 64…1016 was 1px outside Box A and 940px was the retired 70px gutter.
- L2 and L3 set in **Inter 400**, not Inter 500, because §3.4 retires that weight and §3.8 deletes the file. All eight L2/L3 widths are re-measured at 400 and published. The claim that the band was "renderable as written" in Inter 500 was false against the delivered §3.8 and is withdrawn.
- Measured against 950px: draw L1 889.1px (60.9 slack), draw L2 891.6px (58.4), draw L3 915.0px (35.0), deck L1 928.0px (**22.0 — the binding case**), deck L2 716.7px, deck L3 863.2px. Lines with under 40px of slack fall from three to **two** — draw L3 at 35.0px and deck L1 at 22.0px. Fit is MEASURED at render, never counted in characters.
- 44px still does not fit at Inter 400: L2 1,032.4px and L3's worst state 1,059.4px against 950. 38px remains a named exception to §3.5's scale and a design judgement, not a legibility standard.
- Sentence case on L2 is load-bearing: the same string uppercased is 1,141.2px at Inter 400, **28.0% wider**, and fits no track.
- **CAP 8.17 field 5 is scoped by role, not by surface or canvas.** Every frame declares one of eight `data-pdd-role` values through the same four call sites that already write `data-type` / `data-theme` (verified). G1-P runs on `DRAW_CARRYING` roles only, with a single floor — §3.5's `--fs-lead` token — because all four draw-carrying surfaces resolve to the same step. On a deck-level role the assertion does not run, and a prize-name node present there is itself class A.
- The band's variant, L1's amber caution state, L2's host identity check and L3's four-state machine are all selected by `DRAW_CARRYING`, replacing a prose surface list that omitted `reel-open` and the whole of `reel-cover-9x16`.
- A post-level MODEL gate asserts at least one draw-carrying asset per publish format carries a non-empty prize name, and exactly `drawsRendered` on the carousel. It is what catches a mislabelled role, and it is not optional.
- The G1 per-line assertions are scoped to `[data-pdd-band] > [data-pdd-band-line]` with `count === 3`. Unscoped, `fontSize >= 38px` fails the masthead Slot B stamp and §5.4's cover dateline — both at 34px — on every still, every day.
- `--rail-meta` `#B9C6D6` renders on every asset and has no definition anywhere in the repository (grepped). §3.7 must add it; §10.2 quotes the hex only to measure 6.87:1 against rail blue.
- A category word cannot go in deck L1: measured, `10 CAR DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM £129.99` is 1,018.0px and the tech form 1,287.0px, against 950. The friendly case fits, which is the trap.
- No HH:MM:SS clock ships in v1 on any surface, and neither does a stated time of day. `reel-template.mjs:750`'s invented ticking 03:47:22 from a test sentinel is deleted; `story.mjs:125`'s `|| nowIso` is deleted; the parser stops substituting `20:00` at all four sites and records `time_defaulted`.
- The evidence model is THREE ROW-SCOPED COLUMNS following the shipped `category_source` precedent; the method enum excludes `operator-api` and includes `derived-sum` and `operator-pattern`; the window is 48 hours; enforcement is a SELECTION PREDICATE in `fetchEndingSoon`, not a render gate.
- ONE rendered stamp per asset, in the dated-stamp slot each surface already has — and on the cover that slot is §5.4's dateline, because §5.2 suppresses masthead Slot B on slide 1; the composed dateline is 571.2px at `--fs-micro`. §5.2, §6.3 and §7.2 take §10.4's forms and re-derive: Story band 1's headroom falls from 263.6px to **52.4px** (897.6px of 950) with no height change, and the Reel's right-hand mark-slot clearance rises from 16.8px to 96.0px — which does **not** rescue mark slot M, dead on the left by 48.35px.
- The stamp is not a fourth band line. On the Reel a 190px band takes chrome to 591/1920 = **30.781%**, past §6.3's 29% ceiling by 34.2px; on the Story the five bands sum to 883 exactly and a fourth line overruns Box A by the full 45px. (§6.3's 546px / 28.438% / 71.563% supersede the 533px / 27.76% / 72.24% set computed on the retired 272px card.)
- **§10.6a's annotation becomes `{shown} OF {cap} · NONE MARKED`.** Fixed cost 23 glyphs, bounded worst case 32 = 844.8px inside §4.8's measured 33-glyph slot at every legal cap. The 34-glyph form overflowed by 26.4px at the median cap and by 132.0px at the maximum, and §4.2 makes the clipped state the default, so it guaranteed a class-A failure on the ordinary run. The reader must now subtract; §4.9's alt text is the sole home of the not-shown count.
- **E2 is one module with one set of strings on all four surfaces**, taking no surface parameter: eyebrow, figure, conditional. The separate two-line Reel conditional, the side-by-side Story conditional and the `{cap} TICKETS MAX · ODDS IF IT SELLS OUT` numeral-lockup qualifier are all deleted. `1 IN 4,500,000 AT SELL-OUT` measures 619.8px at Inter 600 44px.
- §10.6a publishes **no vertical budget and no type literal**. The 812/809px device budget and the "538px left for photo" line are deleted; type is named by §3.5 token throughout.
- **§10.6 mechanic predicate 3 becomes evidence-unit scoped**: it fires on any unit *containing* `?` and requires two DISTINCT-KEY figures, with the cover's unit defined as headline + proof line. No string is exempt for being allow-listed. The old rule hard-failed roughly 91 legitimate runs a year; the new one fires on zero.
- The `question` arm has ONE permitted form, `{n} DRAWS. HOW MANY TICKETS?`, logged `question:only`, and it renders three line boxes at every legal deck size. Both previous forms are banned by name for carrying no verified figure — and the claim that `HOW MANY TICKETS ARE THERE?` also wrapped to four line boxes is **withdrawn**: measured, it wraps to three, the last box 3.85px inside the well. It is banned for the figure, not the geometry.
- **The `deadline` arm interpolates `{day}` as the three-letter weekday `closesLabel()` already emits.** Full weekday names are banned: `WEDNESDAY.` is 1,012.35px at `--fs-hero`, over the 895px well by 117.35px, and with any full name the long form takes four line boxes.
- The headline word cap is **EIGHT glyphs at `--fs-hero`**, from §3.4's measured 0.674038em. Ten and nine are both retired. The cap binds exactly one thing — the day token — and the real constraint is the measured line box: `FROM 79p A` at **892.50px of 895px (2.5px)** on the `price-anchor` long form, then `HOW MANY` at 869.70px (25.3px). Bricolage 800 digits are measured at 0.6005em, closing a previously-unmeasured gap.
- A THIRD CI gate, `allowlist-conformance.test.mjs`, runs every emittable string through every predicate in the unit the renderer will present it in, and greedy-wraps every headline form at all seven day tokens. An allow-list entry and a predicate can never again disagree in production.
- A new `cadenceOrCoverage` predicate bans `daily`, `always`, `nightly`, `24/7` outright and `every` / `all` unless bound by an interpolated figure. It fires on zero permitted strings and on three live ones (`honesty.mjs:36`, `caption.mjs:32`, `:33`), which are rewritten in the same pass. The two rendered cadence claims move into `oddsCopy`: §5.10's sub-line becomes `Read from each operator's own page, and dated.` (31.0px narrower, same two line boxes) and §6.3's strapline becomes `PRIZE DRAWS, READ AND DATED` (inside 950px at every candidate step, unlike every `UK`-retaining variant).
- **The PUBLISH hash control is split into four named parts and honestly labelled.** P1 (write the hashes) and P4 (post-publish Graph reconciliation) ship as a record and as detection. P2 (re-hash and refuse) is **dormant**, like class D, because §7.5 establishes there is no posting step in code to evaluate it. P3, a first-party Bun posting step calling the Graph API, is the prerequisite and belongs in §12.2's budget. A class-A trigger nothing can evaluate is not listed as enforced.
- `out/alt.json` extends to the Reel cover and Story, carries §10.4's full provenance sentence and the UNTRUNCATED `cleanTitle()` output, and `publish.mjs:171`'s `.catch(() => [])` is deleted.
- `prize-name-truncated` and `headline-long→short` are counted, non-failing records — the only measurements of what the Reel's 22-glyph budget and the cover's line-box ceiling actually cost.
- The `valueLineMin` values are §8.7's and are no longer enumerated here. The unconditional-suppression path that affected 147 draws is closed by §8.7's migration; the class-C event keeps both wordings so a log can distinguish a threshold decision from a missing threshold.
- `PLAY RESPONSIBLY` is removed from all NINE locations (verified). `#winbig` leaves `fixedHashtags`. The `hook: "WIN BIG"` fallback stays banned by name, but §8.7 performs the removal and the "default headline for two categories" claim is a pre-migration fact, not a present one.
- §10.6 PERFORMS the removal of `confettiHtml()`, the particle fields (including the `.p-*` blocks in `styles.css:258-268`, which `reel-template.mjs:47` lifts by name) and the `.stamp` rosette. The `--gold-*` tokens are §3.8's and the `particles` config key is §8.7's.
- Class B drops are resolved in ONE PASS against the deck; class-B exhaustion enters §5.11's one-draw shrink and reaches class A only below `DRAWS_MIN`; the class-C ceiling is `collapsed > floor(0.4 × drawsRendered)`.

### Open questions

- **Is a neutral free-entry pointer enough?** `draws.free_entry_route` will read `unknown` on 100% of inventory on day one. The L3 string neither asserts nor denies a route, which satisfies CAP 3.7 — but if the ASA's view is that an unknown route means the draw cannot be posted at all, all 883 enterable draws fail at once and no geometry helps.
- **Does PDD have a stated 18+ listing policy?** Nothing in the codebase applies an age filter. If PDD does operate one, the honest fix is a claim about PDD rather than about the operator, and L3's wording changes accordingly.
- **Does the restart sequence sweep before it renders?** The selection predicate matches zero rows until Stage 0's first full sweep lands, so the first restart run produces a named class-A empty-pool record rather than a deck. §12.4's Stage 0 exit criterion is the only place that ordering can live.
- **Who builds P3?** The first-party posting step is one Bun script, and until it exists §10.7's P2 is dormant and the strongest real control over what reaches the platform is after-the-fact detection. It is a §12.2 line item and nobody has claimed it.
- **Does `progress-bar` belong on the renderable side of the method enum?** `lib/parse.mjs:151-155` names tiers 2 and 3 as the stranger's-cap leak path, and a stranger's cap does not drift, so `lib/verify.mjs:77-79`'s no-drift check would not catch it. Stage 0 must report the operator distribution before the allow-list locks.
- **Who resolves the verdict-green conflict** — §3.2 widening the rule, or §5.4/§5.13 restyling? G4 rule 3 cannot be enabled until one of them does, and G4's per-region tone baselines must also be re-derived against §8's moved region areas before the gate is calibrated.
- **How often does an operator's `website_url` differ in registrable domain from its `entry_url`?** The one-host rule is unmeasured and it is a cheap query that should run before G1 ships.
- **Does the `price-anchor` long form ever render?** Its binding line is 2.5px inside the well on an advance sum at 79p and does not fit at all above £1, so the short form may be the only one anyone ever sees. §10.8's `headline-long→short` counter answers it after one week of runs; if the answer is "never", the long form should be deleted rather than left in the table as decoration.
- **§12 owns the operator time budget; these are §10's line items in it.** Recurring: class-A triage of `COMPLIANCE.txt` (per incident, unbounded, and the class most likely to arrive on a bad day), Stage 0 backfill verification (once, then on schema change), and P4's post-publish reconciliation review (daily, only when it flags). §10 cannot put minutes on any of them without a run, and will not invent them. If §12.7's ceiling is breached, the step §10 would cut first is P4's review — it is detection, not prevention, and the record survives whether or not anyone reads it.
- **Does the DOM stage need every video frame?** Three samples per role run is specified, and a moving element can leave `surface.safe` between samples. Full-frame checking adds a `page.evaluate` to a loop already running one per frame at `capture.mjs:21`, against the hard five-minute budget at `:20`.
- **Is `total_entries` a contractual hard cap or an operator target?** If an operator can raise the cap mid-sale, an at-sell-out conditional is not a defensible ceiling and §10.6a's wording needs revisiting. (`README.md:25-27` treats a `total_entries` that moves between runs as a stock counter and never publishes it — which addresses drift between runs but not a cap raised after publication.)

### Risks

- **The band consumes real estate on every surface at once.** 168px of 1350 on the carousel (12.4%) and 145px of 1920 on both video canvases, on top of the standing chrome each surface already carries, pushing the asset toward Instagram's "majority text" demotion signal — the same guideline the odds hierarchy is meant to satisfy. The two constraints pull against each other and the balance is unproven.
- **38px is 13.7 CSS px on a 390px-wide phone.** That is below a conventional body floor and below §3.5's 44px video floor. It is defensible for repeating standing chrome and it is 2.0× today's 19px still footer, but it is a legibility concession made to fit, and it should be eyeballed on a real handset before it is locked.
- **Every width in this section is an advance sum, not a rendered line.** fontTools gives the sum of glyph advances from the bundled woff2; it does not model shaping, kerning pairs, hinting or the browser's own rounding. **Deck L1 at 22.0px of slack is the tightest band line, with draw L3 at 35.0px the only other one inside 40px** — the move to Inter 400 and the single 950px track removed the third. Deck L1 is also the line whose worst case depends on an unknown maximum ticket price, and the documented ` A TICKET` → `/TICKET` shortening buys 32.4px and then the build fails.
- **The tightest measured line in the whole section is a headline, at 2.5px.** `FROM 79p A` is 892.50px of the 895px well on the `price-anchor` long form. On an advance sum that is inside the tolerance of shaping, so the long form should be expected to fall back at render; §5.5's mechanism handles it and §10.8 counts it, but nobody has rendered it. The eight-glyph word cap behind these numbers is a mean-derived authoring constraint, and §3.4 is explicit that a mean describes no real word — §5.3's measured-fit rule at render is the only gate.
- **The cover runs at its tightest legal vertical on question days.** §5.4's own arithmetic puts a three-line headline's start at y 244, leaving 47px of air below the dateline against 197px at two lines and 347px at one; the `question` arm always renders three boxes, so roughly 91 days a year the cover sits at the tightest arrangement §5.4 permits. Legal, and nobody has eyeballed it. (Those are §5.4's figures, cited; §10 owns no vertical.)
- **The annotation's worst-case margin is 26.4px — exactly one glyph.** At the measured maximum cap of 4,500,000 the string is 32 of 33 glyphs. If §3.5's content well ever drops below 844.8px, or if §4.7's ceiling grows past 9,999 so `{shown}` takes a sixth glyph, every figure in that table must be re-measured. And the shortened string opens a misreading: `1,440 OF 9,999` with no verb could be read as a sell-through figure, which would be a fabricated fact and a §10.6 deny-list class. The mitigations are contextual — the eyebrow and cap figure above, the legend's `Each dot is one ticket.` below — and the CI fixture now asserts that legend so the annotation is never orphaned. **Nobody has tested that reading on a real viewer.**
- **The role attribute is a new single point of failure and it fails quiet in one direction.** If a renderer emits the wrong role, `role-mismatch` catches a disagreement with the caller — but the caller and the attribute are written in the same commit by the same hand, so they will usually be wrong together. A `draw` slide mislabelled `cover` would skip G1-P entirely and publish with no prize name, silently. The two-sided rule closes half of that; the post-level count gate closes the other half, which is why it is not garnish.
- **The closing slide and the Reel sign-off still discharge field 5 post-wide, not on the frame.** §5.6 records that Instagram re-serves slide 2 cold, so it re-serves non-first children generally, and a viewer can meet the closing slide alone carrying `8 DRAWS IN THIS POST · TICKETS FROM 79p` and no prize nature. The cover is covered by its board and the count slide by its prize name; the closing slide is the one genuine hole, and the only two fills available are a category word in deck L1 (measured dead above, by 68.0px) or a fourth band line (measured dead above, by 34.2px of chrome). If a reviewer rejects post-wide discharge, the cheapest honest fix is to give the closing slide the cover's board.
- **The wording deny-list is design judgement, not a legal review.** Shipping it as a "compliance gate" risks creating false confidence that a passing run is a compliant run — and `out/COMPLIANCE.json` being written on pass makes that false confidence easier to point at. The allow-list in §10.6a is stronger, but it governs only the constants.
- **Predicate 3's weaker gate is a real trade, not a free one.** A headline question is now evidenced by a sibling element rather than by itself. If a future edit deletes, empties or de-figures the proof line, the question becomes bare rhetoric — the rule catches that, but only because the proof line is in the same model. Any surface that ever renders a `?` without an adjacent generated facts line reverts to sentence scope by default, and nobody has checked that the Reel, Story and FB templates never acquire one. The conformance test is also only as good as its enumerated fact-sets: a predicate that fires on some unenumerated real value still reaches the daily build, and nobody owns extending the fixture when inventory changes.
- **Excluding the band's characters from §6.5's read budget is a design judgement**, and the single assumption in this section most likely to be wrong. If the ASA's view is that a significant condition must be readable within the hold a viewer actually gets on a Reel card, three 38px lines of changing values do not clear it, the hold must lengthen, and §6.4's resolved bed table collapses. The alternative — counting the host as a fifth field — provably pushes every bed past 16.0s and kills the Reel.
- **One-host rule, unmeasured.** Where an operator's `website_url` has a different registrable domain from its `entry_url`, L2 names only the entry host and therefore points at terms that may sit elsewhere. Nothing in this session queried how often the two diverge.
- **G1 has a hard ordering dependency on the shared scene module, and G4 rule 3 has one on the green-colour decision.** If either gate ships first, the DOM stage hard-fails every asset every day for a reason that looks like a false positive, and the likeliest response is an env-var bypass — the exact death this section is written to prevent. `AUTO_PUBLISH` already establishes the pattern.
- **The PUBLISH gate is now honestly weaker than it read before.** P2 is dormant and P4 detects rather than prevents, so between today and P3 an agent can post an uncleared caption and the run will be recorded as passing until the reconciliation flags it. That was already true; the previous text obscured it behind a class-A row with no evaluator. Naming it does not fix it.
- **Category diversity, not deck starvation, is what the selection predicate costs.** `pickBestCategory` scores only eligible rows and the largest category alone can fill a deck at heavy attrition. What may not survive is rotation: the `avoidCategory` penalty halves yesterday's category (`select.mjs:42`), and if attrition lands unevenly — the datacenter-403 operators are not randomly distributed across categories — the deck can oscillate between two categories for weeks.
- **The `bare-count` share is genuinely unknown** and cannot be measured until Stage 0 item 0b ships. It is structurally bounded — two of the five `??` branches are `strict:true` and can never produce tier 3 — but the bound is not a number.
- **The stamp is true about the figure and silent about its correctness.** `READ FROM OPERATORS 09:04 · 17 SEP` says PDD read something at a time. It does not say the number is a cap, and a `progress-bar` row wears the same stamp as an `operator-pattern` one. The method column makes that distinction machine-checkable but never viewer-visible.
- **Computed-style emphasis checks are brittle.** Rule 1's "no descendant differs" assertion is stricter than the ratio it replaces and will trip on legitimate markup that wraps a number in a span for tabular alignment. Expect pressure to add exceptions, and exceptions are how gates die.
- **Removing `PLAY RESPONSIBLY` is correct on categorisation grounds** but there is no evidence either way on how viewers read its absence; some may read a prize-draw post with no responsible-play line as less trustworthy rather than more accurately categorised.
- **The 10.4% substituted-time measurement is a lower bound on one half of the problem, not a rate**, and the 1,000-row sample is the first rows PostgREST returned unordered from 1,792 `status=active` rows, only 883 of which are enterable. It over-represents historical parses and may not describe the set the carousel selects from.
- **The DOM stage adds a Playwright `evaluate` per slide plus eighteen sampled video frames** to a pipeline that already waits on fonts and images, against `capture.mjs:20`'s hard five-minute budget. The tightest sampling window is 140.74ms, on elegant.mp3's one-beat sign-off run; any section that lengthens the row-swap past 200ms or the collapse past 270ms closes it.
- **Retiring confetti, particles and the rosette removes most of the current visual motion budget from the Reel** at the same time as the countdown clock is disabled outright. Arm C in particular is a countdown scene with a rosette; with both gone it may have no scene left. That is a content problem this section creates and does not solve.
- **The whole odds-copy table is blocked on data that does not exist.** Not one permitted string may render until Stage 0 ships the three columns and one sweep backfills them. Until then the honest state is that the odds device does not render at all. This settlement makes the default clipped state *renderable*; it does not make it *lawful to render*.
