- Adding four API pulls plus a derived pass to a daily trigger multiplies the Composio call volume; if rate limits or a connection lapse cause partial days, the 95% G1 coverage bar fails for instrumentation reasons rather than design ones, and there is no retry policy specified here.
- The §2.6 reconciliation deletes S5's decision rule without replacing it. Nothing now sets any expectation for interactions per deck, which is honest under §11.5 but leaves the spec with no answer to 'how many likes should a good deck get' — because there isn't one at this account size.

---

### Decisions
- Kept the rewrite substantially intact: registry compliance is clean (no restatement of type, geometry, deck size, band or wording; every borrowed value is a reference to §3.5, §4, §5.11, §8, §10.2 or §10.6a), and all six claimed fixes are genuinely present in the text.
- Re-queried Supabase ilnegxrsalmzpljotgpe live (95 metric rows, 12 post rows) and re-derived every MEASURED figure. All of §11.1's numbers, including the corrected fb_reactions median of 0.5 and every printed sorted vector, reproduce exactly.
- Corrected the Story claim, which contradicted the section's own data: 'publishes a Story most days' is the design (DAILY.md:3, :117-120), but exactly one Story row exists across five publishing days, and DAILY.md:118-120 documents a 'story skipped' fallback for a Graph API that may reject STORIES on this Creator account. Also corrected the citation from publish.mjs:202-209 to the write-ahead row at :202-208 plus the supervised publish step in DAILY.md.
- Corrected a fabricated reassurance in §11.4: the claim that §10.6a's retirement of the six config hook constants would make hookLabel() 'throw rather than quietly substitute'. Verified format.mjs:72 is `catCfg(slug).hook || `WIN ${catLabel(name)}`` and config.mjs:15 supplies its own 'WIN BIG', so the retirement substitutes silently. Replaced with a stated requirement to delete hookLabel() and the d.hook render path, and a matching risk entry.
- Corrected the §11.9 degradation arithmetic: 8 skip-rate-only readings at ~30s is 4 minutes plus the same 2 minutes of mandatory filing = ~6 minutes per sitting and ~24 minutes per block, not the ~5 and ~22 published. The earlier figure had dropped the filing line from the degraded sitting. Flagged the correction in the text so it is not silently re-introduced.
- Added a verified defect the findings did not ask for: the pipeline's only fb_video post (2120805272190159, the PRIMARY Facebook action per DAILY.md:124-128) has no metric row, while a different object id carries metrics on the same date. B9's coverage is now measured against carousel_posts.fb_post_id rather than against the page-posts pull, with a matching open question and risk.
- Restored value the rewrite had dropped: the CAP 8.22 / DMCC Act 2024 reason a `deadline` headline may never render a clock (now a reference to §10.3, not a restatement); §2.6 S3's metric-key caveat (entry.name || "reach", insights.mjs:40), absorbed into A1 with the measured confirmation that all 15 stored rows key as `reach`; and the registry's point that Eden's breakout-vs-own-median is doubly uncomputable for PDD because 12 post rows give no own-median.
- Added an 'unmatched platform objects' block to §11.8. Both directions are populated today (19 unmatched IG ids, 7 unmatched FB objects, 1 unmeasured fb_video, 1 unmeasured Story) and pooling strangers is exactly how the likes baseline was nearly 2x wrong.
- Softened one hardened number: A1's target is now '10x, at the top of DAILY.md:171's 5-10x doctrine' rather than '10x, matching the doctrine' — DAILY.md states a range, not a point.
- Noted that DAILY.md:172 still records 49 followers against the profile's ~66, so the provenance of the live figure is explicit rather than the two sources silently disagreeing.

### Open questions
- Why does FACEBOOK_GET_PAGE_POSTS return an object id on 2026-07-03 that is not the fb_video id the pipeline stored? If the pull does not return video posts, fb_reach for the primary Facebook action needs a different call and B9's coverage bar cannot be met as written.
- Does Composio expose an Instagram per-media insights action at all, and a Story-insights action? The first blocks the whole denominator mandate and B1-B4; the second decides whether B10 exists. Neither is documented in carousel/INSIGHTS.md:21-48.
- Exact Graph API field spellings for saved, shares, views, profile_visits, follows and the two reel watch-time fields remain unverified against the live API version.
- Where is the design spec cited at carousel/DAILY.md:149 for the 76-123/day Reels reach figure? It is not in this repo and no stored reach row exceeds 13.
- Does Instagram cap retention on in-app post insights? §11.2's fortnightly batching and §11.9's budget both assume it does not.
- What is cashAlt()'s real parse rate against live inventory? It sets the absurd-comparison substitution rate and therefore whether the experiment starts at four arms or three.

### Risks
- The archetype defect can recur in disguise: hookLabel()'s own `||` fallback survives the config-constant retirement, so unless the d.hook render path is deleted the cover ships a category constant while carousel_posts logs a template id that never rendered. cover_headline is the only detector and it is diagnostic, not a gate.
- Facebook is measured through an id space that does not match the pipeline's — 7 of 10 stored objects are strangers and the fb_video post is absent — so a pooled FB figure can read healthy while the format Facebook leads with is entirely unmeasured.
- B10's denominator is unstable as well as expiring: Stories are not reliably published today (one row in five days) and DAILY.md documents a skip path, so a coverage percentage over 'published Stories' may be computed over a near-empty set.
- Everything in §11.7 is inert until publishing resumes; 76 days dark and n=6 on the only per-post series mean the day-56 multiples could be met or missed by chance.
- The carousel_metrics primary-key migration must land in two places at once (state-schema.sql:20-27 and the on_conflict string at state.mjs:70) on a live production table; changing one silently reverts to last-write-wins.
- §11.9's 50-minute ceiling is §11's alone and is only meaningful once §12 totals it against §9.7, §10.8 and the daily caption; §2.7's central argument still rests on an unfinished sum.

**Decisions this section commits to**

- Only one class of edit was needed: the §10.6a template-id examples. §11 now cites `question:only` (C8's single permitted question form) instead of the retired `question:short`, and points at §10.6a as the owner of the id set rather than implying a long/short pair exists.
- No arithmetic in §11 was invalidated: every MEASURED figure (medians, the 16.0x denominator ratio, the 28-day block, the 48/50-minute budget, the ~24-minute degraded block) is derived from PDD's own database and operator minutes, not from any geometry, type or wording value the settlements moved.
- §11's references to §5.11 (deck constant), §4 (odds-device surface assignment), §10.2 (conditions band) and §10.3 (no clock on a deadline headline) are pointers with no restated values, so the C1/C2/C3+C5/C4/C9 and §8 settlements pass through §11 untouched.

**Open questions**

- C8 renames the question arm's logged id to `question:only`; §11.4's `archetype_requested` vs emitted-template comparison assumes the emitted id is always `<archetype>:<form>`. If §10.6a's single-form arms drop the suffix entirely, the substitution-detection rule needs the archetype part parsed from an id that may have no colon.
- C9 introduces `data-pdd-role` and a post-level prize-name gate as class-A violations. §11.2's `gate_violations` jsonb currently enumerates only L2/L4 predicates; whether the new class-A codes (`role-mismatch`, `prize-name-on-deck-asset`, `post-carries-no-prize-name`) and the counted `prize-name-truncated` record should also land in that column is §10.8's call, not §11's.
- C4 adds sports-outdoors and home-garden to config.json, taking the live category count to eight. §11.4's stratification note still says '6 configured categories (8 on the live site)'; that parenthetical is a pointer to §1/§8.7's roster rather than a §11 value, so it was left alone — but it should be re-read once §8.7's migration lands.

**Risks**

- The `question:only` fix is a cross-section coupling: if §10.6a's id scheme changes again, §11.2's column doc, §11.4's experiment-key rule and §11's decisions list all carry the example and would drift together. §11 states no id of its own beyond the example, which limits the damage to illustrative text.
- §11 is the only section that would detect a §10.6a wording revision silently breaking the archetype series, and its detector (`cover_headline`) is explicitly diagnostic, not a gate.

## 12. Scope, sequencing, risks and open questions

## 12. Scope, sequencing, risks and open questions

This section fixes the boundary of the work, argues an order for it, counts what it costs an operator, and states honestly where it could fail. It does not schedule anything — the implementation plan is a separate artefact.

It also owns nothing that any other section owns. Where a decision has a named owner elsewhere in this spec, this section cites it and states no value of its own: the type scale, the gutter and both tracks are §3.5's; the type stack and the face-deletion schedule are §3.4's and §3.8's; the odds band geometry and the count-slide budget are §4.4's; the ceiling and the above-ceiling encoding are §4.7's; the permitted odds wording is §10.6a's; the conditions band, its variants and the `data-pdd-role` enum are §10.2's; the evidence and provenance contract is §10.4's; the deck size is §5.11's; per-category identity, its surfaces and its ink budgets are §8's; the `config.json` category schema and its gate are §8.7's. This section carries no sizes, no hexes, no band heights, no ceilings and no deck digits of its own. Restating them is how the earlier draft of this document acquired four incompatible dot grids and three incompatible field lists.

One class of number is the exception and it is now three items, all quoted rather than set: §6.1's Derived Safe Box A rect and §5.1's 3:4 crop inset appear in §12.4 solely to state a **measured position of code that exists today** — a live breach in the Reel's case, a latent one in the still's — and §12.7's minutes table transcludes §9.8's and §11.9's own line items so that a total exists. None of the three is a value this section may change, and if an owner moves one, the arithmetic here moves with it. Measurements of the repository itself — line numbers, file counts, byte sizes on disk — are not owned values and are not covered by this rule; they are evidence, and they are dated.

Every code claim below was re-verified against `~/pdd-aggregator` on 2026-09-17. Where the earlier digest and the repository disagreed, the repository won, and the correction is marked ⚠.

### 12.1 The decision already taken

The visual direction is settled and is not reopened by this spec.

The user selected **"The Verdict + The Board's chrome"** from three rendered options: newsprint editorial ground with rail-blue standing chrome bands, Bricolage Grotesque display, Inter body, JetBrains Mono for every figure, one restrained accent set. The rejected alternatives were "The Board" and "The Late Board"; the latter survives only as a possible sub-register for dark live formats and sits in the category's most crowded territory, so reviving it requires a new decision, not a preference. §3 is the normative owner of the token set that direction became, and that set has since grown by addition (§8 adds a scene tone; §3.2's unfilled-dot value is retired in §8's favour) — read §3 and §8 for what ships, not this paragraph.

Everything downstream of that choice — the odds dot grid as the signature device, the light ground, the mono figures, the chrome bands — is a constraint on this spec, not a proposal within it. Reviewers should raise execution objections, not direction objections.

⚠ **The font gap in the approved direction is now closed, in the opposite direction to the earlier draft.** Verified in-session: `carousel/assets/fonts/` holds 17 woff2 files and `carousel/fonts.mjs` registers all 17 in its `FACES` array (entries at `:5–22`), base64-inlined into every rendered document at `fonts.mjs:31` whether the face is used or not — by all four renderers (`render.mjs:7`, `reel.mjs:66`, `reel-template.mjs:38`, `story.mjs:27`). Of JetBrains Mono, **only `jetbrains-mono-latin-700-normal.woff2` is bundled**, and Cabin is absent. The earlier draft made acquiring JetBrains Mono 400 and 500 a scope item. It is not one: every consumer in the reconciled spec sets mono at 700 (§3.5 assigns the faces per step; §7.2 changes its dateline from 500 to 700 for exactly this reason), and no ruling anywhere in this spec consumes an unbundled weight. **Acquiring fonts leaves scope; deleting them enters it.**

⚠ **The deletion list is eleven faces, not the nine this section previously published, and the count is §3.4's.** §3.4 owns the stack and §3.8 owns the deletion schedule; the end state is **six retained faces**, which is the normative count, and §12 states no other. The earlier nine — Anton, Bungee, Fraunces, Oswald 500/600/700, Playfair Display 700 italic and 800, Space Grotesk — excluded **Bricolage Grotesque 400 and Inter 500**, which §3.4's stack does not carry and §3.8 schedules out. ⚠ **Corrected figure, measured from the directory listing:** the eleven retired faces are **195,020 bytes ≈ 190 KB** of woff2, inlined as roughly **254 KB** of base64 (×4/3) into every page on all four surfaces — not the 148,384 bytes ≈ 145 KB / ≈193 KB this section published against the nine-face list, and not the 168 KB / 224 KB the draft before it published against nothing. §3.8's two-tier schedule governs the order, and the tier figures below are §3.8's, quoted: four faces are already unreachable and leave `FACES` and `assets/fonts/` now (93,104 bytes), and seven leave with their consumers (101,916 bytes), the latter in the same commit as the `[data-theme]` blocks §8.7's migration deletes.

**One dependency runs the other way and is recorded rather than decided here.** Inter 500 is on the deletion list because §3.4 retired the weight, and §3.4 states the consequence itself: §10.2's conditions band sets its sentence-case lines at 500 today and must restate them at Inter 400. The band is the one element the ASA position makes non-negotiable, so the ordering is strict — §10.2 restates the weight and re-measures its own worst-case lines, or the face stays in the bundle and §3.4/§3.8 say so. §12 may not delete a face a rendered surface still names, and it will not carry the deletion as settled until §10.2's weight is. The scope consequence is a single subtraction on the same directory listing: if the face is retained, the retired set is ten faces and 170,748 bytes, and §3.8's first tier loses Inter 500's 24,272. It is carried as **Q15** so that it cannot be settled by silence.

**Corrections this section established, and where they now live.** These are binding. They are listed here because §12 is where they were established, not because §12 can edit the sections that carry them — and, per the round-2 finding, ⚠ **all three have since landed in their home sections; this section no longer asserts that any sibling still repeats the error**, because an instruction to fix something already fixed sends a builder to the wrong file and spends the credibility of the MEASURED claims around it:

- The Socialinsider carousel-versus-reel figure is **views**, not reach (§12.4, Stage C). §11.5's mandate 5 and §11.6's trap 1 make the distinction load-bearing: views are replay-inflated, reach is not, and this spec's success criteria are reach-denominated. §1.2 and §2.4 as delivered both read "out-view" and both carry the qualifier.
- **Nothing in the current Reel is fully inside Box A.** The digest's "everything except `.pcard` is outside the safe box" overstates `.pcard`'s compliance. §2.4 as delivered states the corrected form, with the breach deltas attributed to §12.4.
- The price pill's profile-grid hazard is **latent, not live** — §5.1 verified that slide 1 is always the intro, so it has never rendered under Instagram's multi-image indicator. §1.5 A4 as delivered is headed "Latent, not live". ⚠ One detail of this section's own statement of it was loose and is corrected: `.pill` is emitted at **two** sites, `render.mjs:62` inside `textOverlay()` and `render.mjs:114` in the typographic fallback (`.rank` mirrors them at `:63` and `:115`) — the same two-function pattern as the odds fragment below, not one.

The HH:MM:SS flip clock does not ship in the first implementation (§10.3), so `closes_at_kind`, `closes_at_source` and the widened two-fetch time agreement are not dependencies of anything here. And, per §12.1, acquiring JetBrains Mono 400 and 500.

Two existing behaviours are explicitly **preserved**, not rebuilt: ⚠ the cash-alternative value cap in `honesty.mjs:19–23` (`capValue()`, which floors the claimed value at the operator's own stated cash alternative and guards against a `£0` parse artefact) — the draft conflated this with `valueLine()` at `:25–29`, which is a different function — and the per-slide alt text in `honesty.mjs:31–38`, which §4.9 and §10.6a extend rather than replace, because alt text has no space budget and is where the full provenance sentence now lives. Both are genuine E-E-A-T assets and both must survive the rework intact.

### 12.3 Explicitly out of scope

| Out of scope | Why, and where it belongs |
|---|---|
| **The website redesign** | `draw-discovery-hub` is a separate repository with its own design register. Social templates must not wait on it, and must not assume it. The shared surface between them is the brand system, not the layout |
| **Aggregator / scraper accuracy work — narrowed to exactly four things** | Out of scope means: **which pages are fetched, which draws are selected for the site, how categories are classified, and how operators are scored.** Those are a live programme with its own daily routine and its own release cadence. Nothing else is covered by this exclusion. In particular, **recording provenance about a figure the scraper already reads is a derivation over work already done and is IN scope** — it changes none of the four, and it is the same boundary R9 draws for asset normalisation. The earlier draft's "this spec consumes the inventory as it finds it" is retained only for inventory *content* — the digest's 17 Sep 2026 snapshot found 899 enterable draws, all carrying an `image_url` and a `total_entries` ticket cap, and this spec changes none of that (and `select.mjs:18` already filters on `image_url=not.is.null` regardless) — but it does **not** apply to inventory *metadata*, and it may not be cited against Stage 0. The count itself is a snapshot; see R13 |
| **Backlinks, SEO and GEO** | Off-page work, guide CTR, AI-citation assets and Search Console are separate programmes. The only overlap this spec touches is the `seoKeyword` string already carried per category in `config.json` (and consumed by `honesty.mjs:32` for alt text), which it passes through unchanged |
| **Facebook Groups strategy** | The research verdict is that the real UK comping audience lives in Facebook Groups and that the largest, SuperLucky's Lucky Learners at roughly 23,000 members, bans competition links outright while welcoming scam warnings and win stories. That is a community and editorial play requiring a human posting by hand under their own name. It is not a template problem, and nothing in this spec should be justified by it |
| **Trial Reels A/B rig** | Unavailable: a professional account needs 200 followers (help.instagram.com/1013292530224018, OFFICIAL) and @prizedrawsdaily is at roughly 66 |
| **Instagram library music** | Closed by construction. The Content Publishing API for Reels has no parameter to attach library music, so audio must be baked into the MP4. The current arrangement — Pixabay beds, precomputed BPM and `firstBeatOffsetMs`, always muxed, `assertVideoContract` hard-failing without an AAC stream — is correct and stays |
| **A bespoke Facebook content format** | Facebook gets a mirror, not a design. §7.5 and §7.7 own the mirror's shape |
| **Any per-slide drop-off strategy** | Carousel children have no individual insights in the Graph API. There is no per-slide, swipe, exit-rate or completion metric, in the API or the app. Any proposal resting on one is resting on a metric that does not exist |

**Explicitly not blocking, so that Stage 0 stays bounded.** `operators.instagram_handle` across 60 operators: nothing refuses to render without it, the operator *name* is already selected by `select.mjs:14`, and the handle lives in the caption rather than the frame (§5.13). `closes_at_kind` and `closes_at_source`: the flip clock does not ship in v1, and §10.3's date-only ladder rungs need no new column. `draws.free_entry_route`: a column with a default and no parser work, never a render failure (§10.2). None of these three may be used as a reason to delay anything.

One handoff, logged rather than solved: `prizedrawsdaily.co.uk/category/cash` returned a 404 during the 17 Sep 2026 crawl. That is a site matter and belongs to whoever owns `draw-discovery-hub`.

### 12.4 Sequencing: what gates what

The ordering argument rests on one distinction. **A gate** is work that, if done later, forces earlier work to be redone. **A multiplier** is work that, if done later, means earlier work was tuned against the wrong input. A gate outranks a multiplier, and both outrank surface work.

**Stage 0 — the evidence and provenance columns. Blocking, and ahead of everything.**

Five gates in this spec depend on data that does not exist. §10.4's eligibility predicate, §10.6a's permitted odds strings, §10.2's band stamp, §4.9's alt text and §4.7's device all read provenance that no column holds today. **Until Stage 0 ships, the honest state is that the odds device does not render at all** — and the odds device is the added value that Stage C argues is a distribution-eligibility requirement, so nothing downstream is worth building first. The rulings that have since closed the device's own geometry and its clipped-state wording change nothing here and say so in their own words: making the default state renderable does not make it lawful to render.

The list is complete and bounded. Nothing is added to it.

- **0a.** Migration: `draws.figures_source_url` (text), `draws.figures_checked_at` (timestamptz, distinct from `updated_at`), `draws.total_entries_method` (text, CHECK-constrained to §10.4's enum), plus a btree index on `figures_checked_at`, which becomes a query predicate. Where other sections write `total_entries_source_url` and `total_entries_checked_at`, **§10.4's names govern**; they are the same two columns.
- **0b.** `extractEntries` (verified at `lib/parse.mjs:155`) returns `{ value, method }` instead of a bare number — five return sites. The `??` chain at `:725–729` maps branches to methods; the two `strict: true` branches (`:726`, `:727`) can only ever produce §10.4's labelled-cap value, and the `ltyCap` branch at `:687`, selected at `:728`, is the one §4.9's draft enum had no value for.
- **0c.** `run.mjs` writes all three columns on **every** observation, including the `no-correction` branch. ⚠ **This is the one a builder will miss.** Verified: the `plan.kind === "skip"` branch opens at `run.mjs:358`, logs a refused read at `:362` and `continue`s at `:368` without a PATCH, so a stable, correct, re-confirmed ticket cap would never have its `figures_checked_at` moved, would cross §10.4's freshness window, and would silently delete itself from the eligible pool. The symptom is a deck shrinking over a week for no visible reason, which reads as inventory decay rather than a missing write.
- **0d.** `manager/draw-update.mjs`'s `ALLOWED` set (verified at `:20`) gains the three columns, with `total_entries_method` validated in the same place and the same way `category_source` already is — ⚠ the enum constant and its guard are at `:29–33`, not `:30–31`, and the comment above them at `:24–28` states exactly why an unvalidated value becomes an opaque 400. Without this, every agent-corrected row is permanently ineligible.
- **0e.** `qa-fix.mjs` (verified, repo root) sets the manual method on rows it patches.
- **0f.** `draws.free_entry_route` — column only, §10.2's enum, default `unknown`, no parser work, not a render blocker.
- **0g.** `time_defaulted` boolean, and stop the four silent 20:00 substitutions — verified at `lib/parse.mjs:21`, `:350`, `:391` and `:398`. This is a fabrication fix, not accuracy work, and it sits inside the narrowed boundary for the same reason 0a–0e do.
- **0h.** Backfill: leave `total_entries_method` NULL on every existing row. **Do not guess a method for a value whose path was never recorded** — a guessed provenance claim is worse than none, which is Q12's own standard. One full daily sweep re-stamps every reachable live draw.

**Exit criterion, and it is a gate not a report.** After one full daily sweep, at least three distinct categories must each retain §5.11's `drawsPerDeck` eligible draws in the `fetchEndingSoon(7, 1)` payload, and the measured share of rows whose method is non-renderable must be reported. If it fails, Stage A does not start. The share is genuinely unknown today and cannot be measured until 0b ships.

**Stage A — the shared scene module (§8). The first gate on design work.**

The three renderers build their CSS by regex-scraping `styles.css` with `/(?:^|\n)\s*(?::root|\[data-theme="[^"]+"\])\s*\{[^}]*\}/g` — `:root{...}` and `[data-theme="x"]{...}` blocks only. This is not an accident; the comment at `reel-template.mjs:41–43` says the descendant rules are intentionally skipped. The consequence is already visible in the repository today, and it is worse than the digest states as a hypothetical:

| Rule | File:line | Effect dropped from Reel + Story |
|---|---|---|
| `[data-theme="luxury"] .card` | `styles.css:77` | hairline gold frame |
| `[data-theme="luxury"] .intro-kicker, … .feat-kicker` | `styles.css:78` | italic, 2px tracking |
| `[data-theme="luxury"] .slide::after` | `styles.css:79` | 4% film grain |
| `[data-theme="collect"] .card::after` | `styles.css:145` | holo sheen sweep |
| `[data-theme="tech"] .techgrid` | `styles.css:279` | scanline grid overlay |
| `[data-theme="tech"] .hl` | `styles.css:281` | chromatic split |
| `[data-theme="tech"] .closes, .feat-closes, .intro-sub` | `styles.css:282` | the mono spec-sheet data line |

Every one of these has a selector with ` .something ` before the brace. Every one renders on the carousel today and is silently dropped from the Reel and the Story. Per-category structural divergence is not a future risk; it is the current state of three of the six configured themes.

⚠ **The three scrapers are also not identical to each other**, which the digest does not say. `reel-template.mjs` runs a *second* `matchAll` at line 47 that additionally lifts the parameterised particle skeletons `.p-embers|.p-golddust|.p-fireflies|.p-holo`; `story.mjs:31` and `reel.mjs:69` run only the token pass. So the Reel already inherits one class of structure that the Story does not. The replacement module must be a single import with one behaviour, and the implementer must not assume "port the regex three times" is a faithful translation — it is currently two different behaviours wearing the same comment.

This is why Stage A precedes all design work, and specifically why the user's own brief cannot be met without it. The brief asks for a looping scene in the background for sports. A scene is structure, not a token. Authored in `styles.css` under the current architecture it would appear on the carousel and vanish from the two surfaces where it can actually loop. Per-category work started before the module exists is either thrown away or shipped broken on two of four surfaces.

**Stage B — asset normalisation at ingest (§9). The multiplier.**

It is not a gate — the scene module can be built against today's assets — but it improves every downstream surface simultaneously: the carousel draw slide, the Reel's photograph under the insert chrome, the Story, and every tile of the Facebook album. It also removes the *reason* several existing decorative layers exist. The current codebase compensates for uncontrolled input in three places, all verified:

1. The only asset gate is a 500px longest-edge floor — ⚠ `minDimOk(path, min = 500)` at `imgcheck.mjs:33–38` (not `:33–39`, and not `:33–37`), which returns `true` on an unrecognised format and defers to the render gate.
2. Fit is chosen by a runtime heuristic (`render.mjs:75–79`, commented "contain = show the WHOLE product uncropped … cover = fill the card"), keyed off a per-draw `framePhotoContain` flag.
3. A blurred, scaled, saturated copy of the image is used as its own background — `.backdrop img` at `styles.css:287` (`scale(1.75) blur(48px) saturate(1.6)`) and `.card .cbg img` at `styles.css:313` (`scale(1.5) blur(40px) saturate(1.6)`).

That blurred-self backdrop exists because incoming assets are not uniform. Normalise the input and the compensation becomes unnecessary — which matters beyond aesthetics, because Instagram's own ranking guidance (about.instagram.com, 31 May 2023, OFFICIAL) makes reels "less visible" when they are "majority text" or carry borders, and the defence is a dominant photograph. Every ruling in this spec that protects a photograph well is spending layout on that defence; Stage B is what makes the spend worth anything.

Known mockup weakness (c) — clean product shots sitting beside loud operator marketing collages, a darts collage next to a gold iPhone tile — is this problem rendered. The cover thumbnail strip that displayed it is deleted by §5.4, but deleting the display does not fix the input: the same mismatch now lands on consecutive draw slides and on the album's tiles, where it is larger. It cannot be solved in layout.

Placing B after A rather than before is a judgement call, and the reasoning is that A's cost of being late is rework, while B's cost of being late is retuning. If the team disagrees, running them in parallel is defensible: they touch different files and share no state.

**Two measurements inside Stage B gate decisions outside it.** First, §9's usable-yield measurement — how many candidates per category per run survive §9's Class A and Class B floors — must complete **before §5.11's deck-size constant is locked**, because the pool bar is `drawsPerDeck + BACKUPS` usable candidates in one category, §9's own floors are geometry-derived rather than corpus-calibrated, and if the yield is below the bar the deck runs short every day while the config says otherwise. ⚠ The gate is weaker than it reads, and the round-2 finding is right about why: §5.11 has already authored its constant, so this gates *unlocking* a number that is already in the config rather than *choosing* one. §12 states no deck digit and will not author a smaller one — but the gate only bites if the authored value is treated as provisional until the yield lands, and §5.11 is the section that has to say so. Second, both selector fixes (§12.2, `select.mjs:40` and §8.7's unconfigured-slug guard) must ship **before any deck-size change**, because without them the pipeline can silently return a three-draw deck at any configured size, or hand a deck to a category with no config entry at all, and raising the number would ship those failures under a spec that reads as if they could not happen.

**Stage C — the still carousel.**

First among surfaces, because at this account size the carousel is the primary growth surface, not the reel. MEASURED, Socialinsider, 35M posts across 447,613 accounts, Jan–Dec 2025: at the 1–5K follower band, **median views** are carousel 993, reel 580, image 417. ⚠ That is a views figure, not a reach figure — 993 ÷ 580 = 1.71, so the carousel *out-views* the reel by roughly 1.7×, and the advantage holds in every band. Do not restate it as reach.

This is also where the single most important constraint in the project lands. Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines (help.instagram.com/313829416281232, OFFICIAL) exclude "unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source with only minor, immaterial edits, without adding material value", and the Guidelines are held to a higher standard than Community Standards. A daily automated post of other operators' photographs and prize data is directly exposed. The added value — odds, ticket cap, closing date, comparison — must be visibly on the slide. Today the odds are set at 33px (`.closes`, `styles.css:358`) against a 98px prize name (`.prize`, `styles.css:346`, dropping to 72px at `.prize.long`, `:352`), roughly one third the size of the datum every competitor also shows. Verified across `styles.css`: 18 of 28 `font-size` declarations are ≤46px. Fixing that hierarchy is a distribution-eligibility requirement, not a preference, and it is the reason Stage C cannot be deferred behind the video work.

**Three things land in the same commit as the template rewrite, not after it.** §3.5's `assertTypeContract()` gate — because a type gate authored against templates that have not been moved onto the scale fails 100% of legitimate renders, and a gate that fails on day one is removed on day two; landing it with the rewrite is what makes it pass on run one. `carousel/odds-copy.mjs` and its frozen-fixture test — because the first rendered odds string must come from the allow-list, not be retro-fitted to it. And the CI grep gate that forbids odds literals elsewhere under `carousel/`, because it is the cheap control that would have caught all three of the wording findings this spec was audited for. The two gate files §12.2 adds — the allow-list conformance test and the rewritten `config.test.mjs` — land here for the same reason: a gate authored after the thing it governs is a gate authored around it.

Two further constraints belong to this stage because they are geometric and cheap to get wrong. Mosseri (Oct 2024, OFFICIAL) states that where a viewer does not swipe, Instagram "will often give that carousel a second chance and automatically move to that second piece of media" — so slide 2 must be independently intelligible, carrying the brand mark and category context on its own; §5.6 makes that slide load-bearing rather than incidental. And the profile grid centre-crops to 3:4: on a 1080-wide upload the kept width is 1350 × 3/4 = 1012.5px, so the crop takes (1080 − 1012.5) ÷ 2 = 33.75px from each side, and it reserves roughly a 180×180px clear zone top-right where Instagram draws its own multi-image icon. **§5.1 owns the crop and the resulting side-margin headroom; those numbers are cited here, not set here**, and the earlier draft's derivation of a "≥64px side-margin floor" from them is withdrawn — the gutter is §3.5's, it now has one value on every canvas, and every side margin and track width in §5 is published as a derivation of it rather than as an independent measurement. The price pill currently sits at `top:52px; right:50px` (`.pill`, `styles.css:328`) — directly under that icon. ⚠ Per §5.1 that is a latent hazard rather than a live defect: `.pill` is emitted only at `render.mjs:62` and `:114`, both draw-slide branches, and `build.mjs:150` puts the intro first, so it has never rendered under the indicator.

**Stage D — Reel and Story on the shared module.**

After C, because the Reel's data card is the carousel's draw slide in motion. Designing the motion grammar around an unsettled static layout means authoring the expand-hold-collapse timing twice. Stage D is now smaller than the earlier draft assumed: the Reel's dot-grid slot and the Story's proportional bar are deleted, so both surfaces carry the numeral lockup §4.7 specifies and neither re-specifies an encoding.

The safe-area rebuild is unavoidable and severe. Measured against Meta's own 9:16 diagram (facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490, diagram asset version timestamp 10 Feb 2026, edge-detected by §6.1), **§6.1's** Derived Safe Box A is x 65..1015 by y 269..1152 — a rect §3.5's gutter ruling has since confirmed rather than moved, since the chrome track and Box A's width are now the same constant, so the breach arithmetic below stands unchanged. Verified positions in `reel-template.mjs`:

| Element | Declaration | Line | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.pbar` | `top:0; height:10px` | 367 | y 0..10 |
| `.urgechip` | `top:64px` | 371 | y 64 |
| `.pcard` | `left:64px; right:64px; top:240px; height:950px` | 178 | x 64..1016, y 240..1190 |
| `.cd-pill` | `top:1470px` | 403 | y 1470 |
| `.kickline` | `bottom:330px` | 259 | ends y 1590 |
| `.tblock` | `bottom:300px` | 289 | ends y 1620 |
| `.lower3` | `bottom:200px` | 293 | ends y 1720 |
| `.rfoot` | `bottom:36px` | 394 | y 1884 |

⚠ The digest's phrasing — "everything except `.pcard` is outside the safe box" — overstates `.pcard`'s compliance. `.pcard` is the only element that *substantially* overlaps Box A, but it too breaches it on all four edges: 269 − 240 = 29px over the top, 1190 − 1152 = 38px under the bottom, and 1px outside each side margin (64 < 65; 1016 > 1015). Nothing in the current Reel is fully inside Box A. The price, the deadline, the CTA, the handle and the compliance footer have all been rendering underneath Instagram's own interface. Separately, 10 of the 24 `font-size` declarations in `reel-template.mjs` are below the floor §3.5 sets for a video canvas (24, 24, 27, 27, 30, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37). The insert chrome must be authored inside Box A from its first frame rather than nudged into it afterwards.

**Stage E — instrumentation. Not a surface and not a sequential stage, but a precondition on the first live post.**

It touches no render code — `insights.mjs` is a separate ingest path — so it runs in parallel with 0 to D and its letter denotes priority, not position. It must complete before the first post of the new format goes out, because the moment that post ships, the only comparison available is a 76-day-old set of twelve rows. It must also record §5.11's rendered draw count per post, or a series that silently mixes full and degraded decks cannot be read at all. What is available now and is the priority: the retention chart and skip rate on normal posts, read by hand in the app. What is not available: Trial Reels (see §12.3), and anything per-slide (see §12.3).

One measurement rule belongs here and is a design constraint, not a preference. Instagram's own definitions (help.instagram.com/202865988324236, OFFICIAL) count Views as "starts to play or replay", include replays in Watch time, and compute Average watch time as watch time including replays divided by *initial* views. A seamless loop therefore inflates views, watch time and average watch time without inflating reach. §6.8 ships a build assertion that frame 0 and the final frame are the same picture, so **the Reel does loop**, and it may therefore only be judged on accounts reached and skip rate. Against a MEASURED baseline of 65.50% skip within the first three seconds at the 1–5K tier (Socialinsider, 140K reels, Jan–Jun 2026), that is the number that carries information.

**Stage F — Facebook. Last, and deliberately small.**

It is last because it is blocked on a user action nobody in the pipeline can perform (see Q1), and because the ceiling is low enough that ordering it earlier would buy almost nothing. MEASURED: Buffer, 52M+ posts, updated 13 Sep 2026, median reach per post in the 0–1K follower tier is **30**. Instagram out-reaches and out-engages Facebook at every measured page size on the same content (3.20% vs 1.25% overall; 6.65% vs 4.35% at the 1–5K tier). The scope is: publish the Page, set a username, move the post path onto the tool §7.5 names, carry the photo array and the forbidden-tool list in `publish.json` rather than in prose, complete the `fb_photo` → `fb_album` rename across the eleven sites listed in §12.2, bind the caption files by hash per §10.7 so the publish gate is not theatre, and check again in 60 days.

One thing this stage must **not** do is build the `child_attachments` carousel. Every card requires a link, which makes it a link post — the worst-performing organic format measured (0.05% engagement rate, roughly 200 views against roughly 1,125 for a photo; Socialinsider, 25M posts). The 4:5 assets already rendered are Meta's own recommended Facebook feed ratio, so nothing needs re-cutting.

### 12.5 Risks

**R1 — The format is genre-unprecedented, and the failure would be invisible.**
No UK operator or aggregator runs a daily multi-draw roundup carousel (observed directly, agent-driven headless browsing of every profile in the category, 17 Sep 2026). In this genre a carousel means more angles of one prize. The closest template match found anywhere is Wowcher's "Wow Week" — dated, named, week-long daily roundup, three deals per post. Being unprecedented is simultaneously the comprehension risk and the only uncontested position available. The sharp edge is that we cannot diagnose it: with no per-slide, swipe or completion metric in existence, a comprehension failure and a reach failure produce identical data.

**R2 — The light direction is unproven in this category.**
The evidence for it is absence: no UK prize-draw brand, operator or directory owns warm paper white with black type and one restrained accent. Absence is a positioning argument, not a performance argument. It may be unoccupied because it does not work in a feed optimised for saturated thumbnails, and we have no pre-launch way to find out — the A/B rig that would answer it needs 200 followers and we have roughly 66. Note also that "light cannot be mistaken for an operator, because operators need dark to make glow work" is the research's own reasoning, and it is a judgement about viewer inference, not a measurement.

**R3 — Nothing in this spec has been rendered at the geometry that will ship, and the thumbnail question is still open.**
The odds device was proven at 1 in 699 on a fractional-cell CSS mockup at full size. §4.4's geometry is not that geometry, and §4.7's ceiling and above-ceiling encoding have never been rendered at all. What has changed since the earlier draft is the scope of the caveat, not its force: the rulings that closed the gutter, the count-slide column, the Story's band table, the scene geometry and the clipped-state annotation each carry the same sentence in their own words — nothing at this geometry has been rendered — so this is a spec-wide condition rather than a property of one device. On the profile grid the same asset is centre-cropped to 3:4 and JPEG-recompressed by Instagram, at which point a single marked dot among hundreds of neutral ones is a feature of a very small number of pixels. The fallback half of this risk is closed — §4.7 owns the above-ceiling encoding and is the single normative source for it — but the compression half is not, and the honest position is that the device must be eyeballed at feed size, at profile-grid size and after a real encode before anything about it is treated as proven.

**R4 — There is no warm baseline to measure against.**
The pipeline last published on 2026-07-03; today is 2026-09-17. That is 76 days dark. The entire history in `carousel_posts` is 12 rows spanning 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-03, produced by the old format, at a different follower count, under a ranking regime that has since published at least one new system card (Reels Chaining, updated 11 Nov 2025). Any before-and-after claim across that gap is confounded on at least four axes. The honest consequence is that the first four to six weeks of the new format *establish* a baseline rather than test a hypothesis, and the spec should not promise otherwise.

**R5 — The originality regime could still catch the format.**
The design answer to the Recommendation Guidelines exposure is to put the added value visibly on the slide, which is what Stage C does. That is our reading of the policy applied to a classifier we cannot inspect. The underlying fact does not change: the format repurposes another party's photograph every single day, automatically. Adding odds, a ticket cap, a closing date and a comparison is a strong argument that material value was added; it is not a guarantee that a classifier agrees, and there is no design-level appeal.

**R6 — The account may already be suppressed, and we would not be able to tell.**
Engagement bait is demoted at account level for repeat offenders, and a daily automated poster is exactly that profile. Two of PDD's own past captions are exposed: "Which would you pick?" (comment solicitation) and "#1 is unreal" (sensationalist withholding). If any demotion is in force, the rework will be judged against a suppressed account, and it will look like the design failed.

**R7 — Replacing the token-scraper is a change to a load-bearing seam with no visual regression net.**
The regex appears in three files, was written deliberately, and — per Stage A — already behaves differently in two of them. `carousel/tests/` holds 17 `.mjs` test files (plus `fixtures/` and `tmp/`), including `render.test.mjs`, `story.test.mjs` and `reeltemplate.test.mjs`, but they are unit tests, not pixel comparisons. A shared scene module can pass every existing test and still change what four renderers actually draw. ⚠ The suite's blind spot is demonstrable rather than theoretical: `config.test.mjs:5` enumerates six category slugs by hand, so the two missing categories this spec exists partly to add could never have failed it, and §8.7's rewrite replaces the enumeration with a derivation for exactly that reason. The prior for this is established in this codebase: a parser change with green unit tests once altered the draw date on 12 of 111 live pages. §8.7 makes the migration a single commit across all four surfaces, which is correct and which also means there is no partial rollback.

**R8 — Two commercially-shaped numbers sit under the carousel-length argument.**
Eden's slide-count finding (655,385 carousels, 12,159 creators, Aug 2025–Aug 2026: 3 slides 23.4% breakout, rising to 32.1% at 14 and plateauing around 18–20) comes from a vendor that sells a carousel generator, and breakout-versus-own-median may simply be measuring effort. The direction is credible; the magnitude is soft, and it must not be restated as a hard threshold anywhere downstream — including under §5.11's deck-size constant, which takes only the densest step of that curve and declines the largest one. ⚠ The round-2 finding presses this further and it is recorded rather than resolved here: the constant is already authored in the config, every downstream line item in §9, §11 and §12.7 is sized off it, and the metric the curve is denominated in is one §5.11 itself says PDD can never compute. §12 cannot author a smaller number without taking a value it does not own; what it can say is that the gate in Stage B is only real if the authored value is provisional until §9's yield lands. The widely repeated "5–8 slides is optimal" has no source at all and is not used here. Similarly, Metricool's +108% reach from mentions (24.36M posts, 375,118 accounts, Jan–Feb 2026 vs 2025) is correlational, and the adjacent hashtag finding (−31.70% views) is explicitly flagged as weak accounts spamming tags rather than tags causing harm.

**R9 — Two workstreams now sit on the boundary §12.3 draws, and the deeper one is new.**
Stage B was always the thin case: normalisation at ingest touches the scraper's image path (`fetchimg.mjs`, `imgcheck.mjs`) rather than the render path, in the same repository as the daily scraping routine. Stage 0 goes further in — `lib/parse.mjs`, `run.mjs`, `manager/draw-update.mjs` and `qa-fix.mjs` are the aggregator's core, not its edge. The narrowing in §12.3 is what makes that lawful, and the rule it rests on must be enforced deliberately rather than assumed: **this spec may derive over work the aggregator already does, and may not change which pages are fetched, which draws are selected for the site, how categories are classified or how operators are scored.** The practical exposure is release cadence, not correctness — a social-template change now lands in a repository with a daily routine and an owner who is not this spec. ⚠ §8.7's config gate adds a second-order version of the same exposure: once the category key set is asserted against `lib/parse.mjs`'s taxonomy, the scraper can no longer add a category without the social pipeline's config catching up in the same change, and somebody will meet that on a red build.

**R10 — The pipeline did not go dark because the design was wrong, and redesign may not restart it.**
Runs on 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-14 built complete decks — slides, authored `CAPTION.txt`, `FB_CAPTION.txt` — and produced no `publish.json` and no state rows. They were abandoned at the publish step, not crashed, and Composio connections for both Instagram and Facebook are active. The failure mode was operator attention, not template quality. A rework that assumes the format was the blocker inherits the same unaddressed dependency: the publish step still requires a human-supervised agent session per `DAILY.md`. Q11's cadence answer must account for this or the new format goes dark the same way. Stage 0 lengthens the runway before the first post, which makes this worse rather than better. §12.7 now prices the gate rather than only naming it, which is the minimum this risk was owed.

**R11 — The layout collision is resolved on paper, and the paper is tight.**
The earlier form of this risk was that the type floor and the requirement that all significant conditions appear in the material might be arithmetically incompatible on one slide. It has been resolved rather than left open: §3.5 owns the scale, the gutter and both tracks, §10.2 owns the conditions band and its field list, §4.4 owns the odds device's geometry and the count-slide column, §4.7 owns the ceiling, and §5.7 owns the slide assembly that has to hold them. ⚠ Two of the aggravating conditions this section previously named are discharged and must not be restated: the gutter and the tracks no longer differ between rulings — there is one owner, one value on every canvas, and every coordinate downstream is published as a derivation with its sum beside it — and the odds figure's type step is no longer contested per surface, since the still, the Reel and the Story now take one step from one module. Both were settled without a single edit to this section, and the reason is the discipline in the preamble: §12 published neither number, so there was nothing here to correct. What has not changed is the margin. The rulings that closed it record their own slack in single-digit and low-double-digit pixels; the draw slide's column closes with none at all, with the photograph as the flex residual, so the next element added there is paid for out of the photograph; and no render has ever been made at any of these numbers. Any section that later adds one element to a slide breaks an arithmetic it did not write, and the failure will surface as a build refusal on a legitimate draw rather than as a design discussion.

**R12 — Per-category identity is still the largest line in scope and the least evidenced.**
Nothing in the digest says per-category visual identity moves reach, views, skip rate or follows; it is in scope because the user asked for it, which is a legitimate reason but not an evidential one. §8 has reduced the matrix — the still surface carries a reduced treatment, and at least one scene (`house-draws`) is dormant against inventory that does not exist today — but it has not made the case measurable, and §8's own gate set is uncalibrated by its own admission. The risk is unchanged in shape: it consumes the majority of build effort while the two changes with actual policy or measurement behind them — the odds hierarchy (distribution eligibility) and asset normalisation (the majority-text defence) — are the ones that carry the outcome. If effort has to be cut, it should still be cut here first, by shipping the shared register and the per-category tokens and deferring the distinct scenes.

**R13 — The inventory figures do not reconcile, and the habit is the problem.**
⚠ There are now three counts in play, not two. The digest states 899 enterable draws and separately lists seven categories summing to 897; several rulings elsewhere in this spec compute against 880. Nobody has reconciled the three, and the gaps are immaterial to the design but material to the habit: these numbers were taken as one-off samples, they move daily, and §5.11 re-measured its own in-window pool in the same session and corrected two of its own published figures as a result. Nothing in the templates may hardcode a count, no figure in this spec is a standing fact, and a section quoting one must say which sample it came from.

**R14 — The eligible pool after Stage 0 is unmeasured, and two decisions wait on it.**
§10.4's predicate removes every draw without fresh, method-stamped provenance from selection. Deck size survives easily on the largest categories, but two things do not follow from that: the share of rows whose extraction method is non-renderable is unknown until 0b ships, and the operators that fail intermittently are not randomly distributed across categories — the documented datacenter-refusal class is operator-shaped. The consequence is a rotation risk rather than a starvation risk: the deck can oscillate between two large categories for weeks while the thin ones never qualify. Stage 0's exit criterion measures this; nothing in the spec prevents it.

**R15 — Every floor in this spec is currently unenforced in code.**
`select.mjs:40` pins the category adequacy bar at three draws regardless of the configured deck size, and `slice(0, n)` returns short without an error. So the "never publishes below" floor this spec has carried in one form or another since the first draft has never existed outside prose. It is cheap to fix and it must be fixed before the deck size changes, because raising the number without it ships silent three-draw decks under a document that says otherwise. The same line is why §8.7's unconfigured-slug guard is not optional garnish: `select.mjs:41`'s `enough * 1e12` term dominates the score, so an unconfigured bucket clears the same bar on count alone.

**R16 — The operator budget in §12.7 is a total of two owners' measurements and three of this section's estimates, plus a fourth bound that sits outside the total.**
Only §9.8's four minutes and §11.9's forty-eight per block come from sections that reasoned about them, and §9 says plainly that its figure is arithmetic on a sheet that has not been built. The caption read, the composite QA pass and the publish approval are estimates this section authored to make a total exist, against a routine whose own documentation says the daily job is "basically approve"; the class-A allowance is a fourth, and it is bounded rather than measured. If the estimates are 50% low the ceiling is breached on day one, and the failure mode is not a red build — it is the same silent abandonment that produced the 76 dark days. The budget's value is that it can now be falsified by one week of honest timing; nobody has done that week.

### 12.6 Open questions

Six remain open. Nine are closed by ruling and are listed below them with the section that closed each, so that cross-references to the original numbers still resolve.

**Q1 — Is the Facebook Page unpublished, and if so, why?**
The `is_published:false` reading (1 follower, zero engagement across 29 sampled days, no vanity username, last post 3 Jul 2026) came from an agent reading the live Page through Composio and was **not independently verified**. The user must confirm it in Meta Business Suite, and must establish which of two very different things happened: they never published it, or Meta unpublished it. The second would be an enforcement signal against the account cluster and would change the risk assessment for Instagram too. This is a user action; nothing in the pipeline can perform it.

**Q3 — Does non-uniform reel pacing beat a flat card rhythm?**
Named in the brief as the single most testable question: fast cuts on photo-only beats and held frames on number beats, against a constant per-card rhythm. It cannot be settled from the digest. Trial Reels is unavailable below 200 followers, and the Reels Chaining system card (transparency.meta.com, updated 11 Nov 2025) discloses that watch duration is judged **relative to peer reels of similar length** — so varying pacing without varying length is the clean test, but it has to be read off the retention chart by hand. §6.4's length cohorts are built on that finding; what remains unanswered is whether the pacing variation inside a cohort does anything.

**Q9 — Is the operator tagged on a draw we have rated poorly?**
Tagging the operator in every draw slide and caption is the recommendation, on a MEASURED but correlational finding of +108% reach and +167% comments for accounts under 2K followers. It collides directly with unoccupied territory #3 — naming a loser — which no brand in this category has ever done and which is one of PDD's clearest openings. Tag on every draw, or only where the verdict is not negative? Note that the mechanism is no longer blocked: §10.4's ruling removes `operators.instagram_handle` from the blocking-dependency framing, the operator name is already selected at `select.mjs:14`, and the handle lives in the caption. This is now purely an editorial decision, owned by §5.13 and §7.10.

**Q11 — At what cadence does publishing resume, and who presses publish?**
Straight back to daily after 76 days dark, or a ramp? A daily automated poster is the exact profile Meta's engagement-bait enforcement targets at account level (R6), and a cold restart at full cadence is also the configuration under which the June Facebook regression fired seven posts in one second. The second half of the question is the one R10 raises: the publish step is a supervised agent session per `DAILY.md`, and it is where the pipeline stopped twice in July without erroring. Any cadence answer that does not name who or what performs that step is answering half the question. Stage 0 pushes the first post further out, which makes the answer more urgent, not less. §12.7 now prices that step and the four around it, so the cadence answer has to be given against a stated daily total rather than against "basically approve".

**Q14 — Which categories survive the eligibility predicate week after week?**
Raised by R14. §10.4's selection predicate and §5.11's pool bar interact with `pickBestCategory`'s `avoidCategory` rotation penalty (`select.mjs:42`, a 0.5 multiplier) and the seven-day slug exclusion. If provenance attrition lands unevenly across categories — and the refusal class that causes it is operator-shaped, not random — the deck can run the same one or two categories for weeks while the eight scenes §8 builds go unseen. Stage 0's exit criterion measures the first week of it; nobody owns what happens if the answer is "two".

**Q15 — Does §10.2 restate the conditions band's sentence-case lines at Inter 400, or does Inter 500 stay in the bundle?**
New, and raised by §12.1. §3.4 retires the weight and §3.8 schedules the file out in its first tier; §10.2 still specifies 500 and measured its worst-case lines in it. The direction is safe — 400 is narrower than 500, so every published fit gets slacker, not tighter — but the published numbers are wrong either way, and one of two sections has to move. This question exists because §12 will not delete a face a rendered surface still names, and because a deletion list is exactly the kind of thing that gets treated as settled by silence. The answer changes a §12.2 scope item and one subtraction in §12.1; it is not §12's to give, and §12 will carry the deletion as conditional until it is given.

**Closed by ruling.**

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| Q2 — album or single hero photo? | Closed: the multi-photo feed post §7.5 names, with the array and the forbidden-tool list carried in `publish.json`. §12.2's Facebook line reads "album" and §7.5's decision is no longer provisional. §7.7 owns the photo count and its composition |
| Q4 — the dot grid's fallback above the ceiling? | Closed: **§4.7 owns the ceiling and the above-ceiling encoding on every surface.** The rejected candidates stay rejected there, and §5.8, §7.2 and §8.5 each delete their own competing version |
| Q5 — does `house-draws` survive? | Closed: §8.5 assigns it a scene and it stays dormant against future inventory. The font half of the question is closed by §3.4/§3.8 — Bungee is retired with the other ten faces regardless |
| Q6 — the two unthemed categories and the authoritative taxonomy | Closed: §8.5 builds against the eight categories declared at `lib/parse.mjs:9`, and §8.7's migration authors both missing entries, retires the fallback merge and asserts the key set against that taxonomy, so `config.json`'s six-entry list cannot drift again |

### 12.7 The operator time budget

§2.7 rejects a daily on-camera presenter partly on effort, and makes that argument conditional: it holds only if the rest of the document counts its own manual minutes. It then names the requirement and hands it here — a per-day and per-week operator time budget, itemised by step, with a stated ceiling. Two sections have already filed their line items expecting a total (§9.8, §11.9) and three recurring steps had never been costed by anyone. This is the total. It is the only place in the spec where a figure is added up across sections, and §12 authors only the estimates marked as its own; the rest are transclusions, and if an owner changes a line item the total moves with it.

| Step | Owner of the figure | Cadence | Operator minutes | Approval gate? |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Tier-3 image sheet — one row per fetched draw, master beside its rejected raws | §9.8 | daily | ≤4 | No |
| Caption read-and-approve — both captions, against `brief.mjs`'s facts table | §12 (authored here, unmeasured) | daily | ≤3 | No |
| Composite QA of the rendered assets, excluding the image sheet — slides, reel keyframes, story | §12 (authored here, unmeasured) | daily | ≤4 | No |
| Publish approval — trigger, composite preview, the OK | §12 (authored here, unmeasured) | daily | ≤1 | **Yes** |
| Weekly report read | §11.9 | weekly | 3 | No |
| Channel-B transcription sitting and screenshot filing | §11.9 | fortnightly | ≤18 | No |
| Class-A compliance triage | §10.8 owns the class; the bound below is §12's, unmeasured | exception only | 0 on a passing run | The run has already stopped |

**The sum.** Daily steps: 4 + 3 + 4 + 1 = **12 minutes a day**. §11's block: 4 report reads (4 × 3 = 12) + 2 sittings (2 × 18 = 36) = 48 minutes per 28 days = **1.71 a day amortised**. Total **13.7 minutes a day**; per week, 12 × 7 = 84, plus 3 for the report and 9 for half a sitting = **96 minutes**; per 28-day block, 336 + 48 = **384 minutes** — six hours and twenty-four minutes, a little *under* six and a half hours. One note on the transclusion: §11 commits to a ceiling of 50 minutes a block against the 48 its own line items sum to, and those two minutes of headroom are §11's. They are not spent here and they are not counted here.

**The ceiling this section commits to: 15 operator-minutes per day, 105 per week, 420 per 28-day block.** The headroom is 1.3 minutes a day, roughly 9%, and it is deliberately thin: a ceiling with slack in it is not a control, and the cost of being wrong in this document is measured in dark days rather than in pixels. The figure is a judgement, not a measurement, and R16 says so.

**Class A is outside the ceiling, and bounded rather than unbounded.** A class-A run has already stopped, so there is nothing to approve and no publication to supervise; the cost is diagnosis. It is budgeted at **≤15 minutes per incident, at most one incident in any seven days**. Beyond that the rule is not "spend more minutes" — a gate firing twice a week on legitimate inventory is a spec defect, billed to the section that owns the gate, and publishing stops until it is fixed. That is the same standard §10.8 applies to itself, stated as a number so it cannot be absorbed quietly by whoever is holding the trigger.

**One-off costs, named so they are never amortised into the daily figure to make it look smaller:** Stage 0's backfill verification and its exit-criterion read, the Facebook Page publication and username (Q1, a user action nobody in the pipeline can perform), and the first read of §9's usable-yield measurement. These are real and they are not recurring, and a budget that quietly spreads them across 28 days is lying in the direction that killed this pipeline once already.

**The cut order, fixed in advance so it is not improvised under pressure.** If the measured total breaches the ceiling:

1. **§5.11's deck size comes down first.** It is the only line that scales with a number a config file holds — §9.8's sheet is `N + ⌈N/2⌉` rows at roughly twenty seconds each — and §12.4 already gates that constant on a measurement that has not been taken. Cutting here costs slides, not evidence.
2. **The caption is accepted as generated unless a gate fires.** §10.6a's allow-list and the L2/L4 predicates are the control on that string; a human re-reading copy a predicate has already cleared is duplicated work, and it is the estimate most likely to be over-spent because it is the one that feels like editing.
3. **§8's advisory gate output stops being read daily.** §8 says its own thresholds are uncalibrated; a daily minute spent on an advisory number nobody can act on is the cheapest minute in the table to stop spending.
4. **§11's sitting degrades last, to the skip-rate-only form §11.9 has already specified** (~6 minutes a sitting, ~24 a block). Measurement is what tells anyone whether any of the rest of this worked, and it is surrendered last on that ground alone.

**Two things are never cut: the publish approval and the class-A triage.** The first is the gate, and automating it away is a different decision belonging to Q11, not a saving. The second is the only step that exists because something is wrong.

⚠ **One proposed cut is declined.** The round-2 finding suggests cutting §9's Tier 2 — the two probabilistic semantic checks — before cutting measurement. It does not belong on this list: Tier 2 costs machine time, not operator minutes, and removing it moves the failures it catches onto the Tier-3 sheet, which is a human step. Cutting it would raise the number it was proposed to lower. §9's Tier 2 is a cost to §9's runtime budget and should be argued there, not here.

**Decisions this section commits to**

- The section is sound in substance: all five round-2 findings are discharged, every settlement touching §12 is applied, and §12 still publishes no gutter, no track, no band height, no ceiling and no deck digit. It is returned substantially unchanged, with five corrections.
- ARITHMETIC DEFECT FIXED — §12.7 stated 384 minutes as 'a little over six and a half hours'. 384 ÷ 60 = 6.4 = six hours twenty-four minutes, which is a little UNDER six and a half. Every other sum in the section re-derives exactly: 4+3+4+1=12/day; 4×3+2×18=48/block; 48÷28=1.71; 12+1.71=13.7; 12×7+3+9=96/week; 336+48=384/block; ceiling 15/105/420 with 1.3 min ≈ 8.6% headroom.
- CLAIMED CHANGE THAT WAS NOT IN THE TEXT — the Inter 500 dependency was said to have been 'added as an open question so it cannot be settled by silence', but §12.6 carried only Q1/Q3/Q9/Q11/Q14 and no such question. Added Q15 (does §10.2 restate at Inter 400, or does Inter 500 stay bundled) and changed the count from 'Five remain open' to 'Six'. The nine closed questions are unchanged, so every existing cross-reference still resolves.
- OWNERSHIP HUNT (the defect that survived two rounds) — three residual leaks closed, none of them a geometry value. (a) The preamble licensed its three quoted numbers as stating 'a measured breach of code that exists today', but §5.1's crop inset is used for the .pill case, which §12 itself calls latent and NOT a breach; reworded to 'measured position of code'. (b) The preamble's exception list did not cover the font byte figures, which are the fourth class of number in the section; added one sentence saying repository measurements (line numbers, file counts, byte sizes) are evidence, not owned values — and attributed the two tier figures (93,104 / 101,916) explicitly to §3.8, which owns the schedule. (c) §12.7's class-A row named §10.8 as the owner of a minutes bound §12 actually authored; the cell now separates the class (§10.8) from the bound (§12, unmeasured), and R16 counts it as a fourth estimate sitting outside the total.
- THE FONT DEPENDENCY MADE CONCRETE — §12.1 asserted the deletion is conditional on §10.2's weight but left the scope consequence unstated. Added the single subtraction it implies (195,020 − 24,272 = 170,748 bytes, ten faces, and §3.8's first tier loses the same 24,272), so a reader can price the conditional without recomputing it. Both figures are arithmetic on the directory listing already quoted in the paragraph, not new §3.8 values.
- R11 MADE TRUE TO ITS OWN CLAIM — the change log said §12's no-numbers discipline is what let the gutter settlement pass without editing this section, but the text never said so. Added one clause to R11: both aggravating conditions were discharged without a single edit here because §12 published neither number.
- TRANSCLUSION HONESTY — §12.7 summed §11's line items to 48/block while §11.9's own committed ceiling is 50. Added one sentence stating the difference and that the two minutes of headroom stay with §11, so the table cannot be read as a misquotation of §11's ceiling.

**Open questions**

- Q15 is new and is §10.2's to answer, not §12's: the conditions band's sentence-case lines are specified at Inter 500, a weight §3.4 retires and §3.8 deletes in its first tier. Until it is answered, §12.1's eleven-face / 195,020-byte deletion is conditional and §12.2's 'Dead CSS and orphaned fonts' scope row is one face short of final.
- §11.9's committed ceiling (50 minutes a block) and the sum of its own published line items (48) differ by two minutes. I have recorded the difference rather than resolved it — if §11.9 means the 50 to include a step it has not itemised, §12.7's total is two minutes low per block and the daily figure moves by 0.07.
- The three §12-authored estimates in §12.7 (caption read ≤3, composite QA ≤4, publish approval ≤1) have never been timed. One week of honest timing falsifies or confirms the 15-minute ceiling; nobody has been assigned that week, and R16 says so rather than hiding it.
- The digest's inventory counts still do not reconcile (899 vs 897 vs the 880 several rulings compute against). R13 records this as a habit problem rather than a design problem; it remains unreconciled and no section owns reconciling it.

**Risks**

- §12.6 now carries six open questions instead of five. If a sibling section cross-references 'the five open questions in §12.6' by count rather than by number, that reference is now stale. The Q-numbers themselves are untouched (Q1, Q3, Q9, Q11, Q14 plus the new Q15), and the nine closed rows are unchanged, so every reference by number still resolves.
- Q15 hands a live dependency to §10.2 in a spec round that has already closed. If §10.2 is not reopened, the deletion list ships eleven faces on §3.8's authority alone while §10.2 still names Inter 500 in a rendered surface — which is exactly the state §12.1 says it will not carry as settled. The failure is quiet: the build renders, the band sets in a fallback weight, and §10.2's measured slack figures (as little as 13.0px on one track) were taken in the face that is gone.
- §12.7's ceiling is 9% above its own total and every figure inside it is either unmeasured or transcluded. If the three authored estimates are 50% low, the ceiling is breached on day one and the failure mode is silent abandonment at the publish gate — the same mode that produced the 76 dark days — not a red build.
- I verified every code claim in this section against ~/pdd-aggregator read-only on 2026-09-17 and all of them hold (select.mjs:32/:40/:41/:42, config.mjs:8-11/:15/:16, parse.mjs:9/:155/:687/:725-729/:21/:350/:391/:398, run.mjs:358/:362/:368, draw-update.mjs:20/:24-33, fonts.mjs FACES :5-22 and :31 with all four consumers, 17 test files, config.test.mjs:5, the eleven fb_photo sites, the five FACEBOOK_CREATE_PHOTO_POST sites, the seven dropped descendant rules, glass at 8abc72e dated 2026-08-26, 18 of 28 and 10 of 24 font-size counts). They are a snapshot of one commit; any of them can go stale the next time the aggregator's daily routine lands a change, and the section's own ⚠ convention is what carries that caveat forward.
- The 899/897/880 inventory spread is unresolved and R13 keeps it visible rather than picking one. Anyone who reads the 899 as a standing fact will size Stage 0's exit criterion against a number that moves daily.
